review_text:
Was able to try this place out during their soft opening and I had a great experience from the get go! Has a well thought out design to the space and has quite a good amount of seats, whether its at the bar or tables with groups (I would limit the groups to 4-6 max). Front and back of the house were totally putting out their best effort.

I got to try one of their cocktails at the bar, The Orient, which is a gin based drink and it was pretty tasty! They have a pretty good list of cocktails and also Hitachino Beer on DRAFT! If you have any know how of more craft Japanese beer, they're usually quite hard to find and usually in bottles. So its super dope to find draft here! =]

Sat down with a couple of my buddies and the waitress walked through every aspect of the menu, answering any questions we had. We ended up getting a few appetizers and noodles to share. For starters we got the grilled duck breast, spicy tuna cones, eel and tamago roll, and the tatsuta FRIED CHICKEN! The chicken was really awesome. Super tender and juicy inside and the accompanying purple sauce was so so good! 

For our main course we had the sizzling sukiyaki udon, salmon chirashi bowl, a deluxe curry udon, and the cold mentai caviar udon. Loved the presentation and the choice of dishes they use. They made the dishes look amazing and pop out at you! So you get to eat with your eyes first, then your mouth. 

The mentai I didn't think I would like but the roe isn't overpowering and the dish is overall very balanced. If you can, try it with the thinner noodles it'll taste better. The sizzling sukiyaki was pretty dope, its sweet and salty and hearty and all awesome. The curry was really good actually and noodles were extra silky with the curry sauce on it. Plus the katsu and tempura shrimps were light and tasty and disappeared very fast haha. I'm not a fan of salmon so I can't comment but I thought the rice was top notch! Soft and a hint of sweetness from the vinegar. So if you're hesitant of ordering a rice dish, don't be! It'll probably taste like heaven. 

We closed off with a sorbet medley of mango, lychee, and lemon. All 3 were very refreshing, awesome, and complimentary to one another. They had ran out of the chocolate cake, which goes to show how popular it was. Not to mention some of the staff had it as their personal favorite. 

Loved my time here! Would totally come back when they officially open. My dining experience was great and its a good change from the more street, izakaya style. Also unlike other more fine Japanese restaurants it won't cost you everything you own. Its priced quite fairly for the experience and the quality of the food. I really hope they do well!

Soft opening in the old Union Square Cafe spot. 
Officially open tomorrow for dinner.

Very extensive menu (many appetizers, including sashimi & rolls, and many varieties of udon, don, and cold noodles).
Most of the items reasonably priced.

Favorite appetizers:  Tatsuta fried chicken, ribeye steak, and the spicy tuna tartare cones. Try to order as many appetizers here. Most impressed with the appetizers.

Udons (nice break from all the salty, greasy ramens popular in the city these days): 
Curry deluxe udon - in a nice curry broth, but the stars were the donkatsu & shrimp tempura on top. 
Tsurutontan deluxe udon- really enjoyed the broth in this one. Nice touch of sweetness from the aburaage (fried tofu skin). Comes w/ excellent shrimp & vegetable tempura.
The noodle is not the nice, chewy texture like Raku's though, which I prefer more; More on the soft side here.

Many thanks to Chris for the excellent service.

: 8 calendars

What the 3 previous reviews said - like I'll have what they're having!!
YES
I look forward to working my way down the menu.
I like the thick udon noodles they offer and the broth is just right.
I had the tuna waffle cones- beautifully presented .
 Spices and  herbs were perfect. Somehow I had been thinking tuna as sashimi but this was totally rad.
The staff is very professional,gracious, and thorough.
The decor is exceptional .
Welcome to the Nabe .

The food is great, service is great.


Being it is their grand opening , it is a bit overwhelming for both the floor and kitchen staffs. But they are able to keep the services level well. 

Their Asian infusion cocktail are good but a bit too Asian favorite. It is a bit of trying to be Asian too much and leaving out the idea of a good cocktail, I would say if the cocktail menu have one or two drinks that's more classic or less citrusy (Asian influence) it might be better, every drinks have a bit of fruit of citrus in it.

After waiting for an hour, finally got a seat, the hour was well spent at the bar, trying their cocktail and get to know the bartenders (Frankie and Andrew) they are awesome. 

Food come out fairly fast and the presentation is total at par with the price. 

I got the uni appetizer, they didn't provide the soy sauce or salt but it come with sweet soy jelly with help bring out the uni sweetness a very nice touch. 

The wagyu sushi is simple and melt in your mouse, serve with truffle salt, which I do use it on the uni to bring out the sweetness a bit more.

And I tried their mentaiko udon and it is totally awesome, first you can't really find anywhere in NYC that serve mentaiko and second they did it right , it isn't too salty and too fishy. Well a balance.

Visited during grand opening day! The average wait time is around 90 mins(they told us), but we didn't get to our seat until 2 hours later. The staff was very polite and nice to greet us, but they can do much better in their seating assignment. 

The appetizer was very okay, we have spicy tuna cone, like typical spicy tuna with avocado wrapped with crispy wonton skin ($12, I think was little over price, should be $8-$10 range), definitely a mediocre appetizer. Crispy fried chicken was also very okay, only 6 pieces ($11) dollar, chicken was very juicy and tender, but again, didn't surprise me. 

Now, comes to the main character of the night, Udon! That's what they famous about! I gotta said udon was meet my expectation, definitely the best udon that I had so far in NYC area. We had tempura Deluxe, curry deluxe , and creme deluxe. They all tasted so good! The broth was amazingly delicious! That will become the only reason than I want to come back to try another one! The bowl looks gigantic, but the portion was very normal size!

Dessert! The worst part on the menu, only three choice, we got water cake, very simple, nothing special. 

Overall, it was a good Japanese udon speciality restaurant, but defiantly not worth 2 hours of waiting( luckily they do accept reservation request after their grand opening date, so call ahead to book your table). It was little pricy, I think the reasonable price for a bowl of udon is around $15.

I was here on 8/29 at the grand opening. Doors opened at 5 pm. I got there at 5:30 to put my name and number down. The wait was about a 30-45 min wait. That wasn't too bad. My friend and I got a drink at the bar while we wait for our table. He got a Sapporo draft and I got a ginger beer. Staff was attentive and polite. We got to sit down at our table and looked at the menu. There were so many choices for appetizers and udon dishes. I had a hard time deciding because everything sounds amazing and delicious.

For appetizers, we got the tatsuta fried chicken and smashing cucumber salad. For udon, I settled on the curry beef and my friend picked the recommended, Tsurutontan deluxe. 

The fried chicken isn't fried fried. It was very juicy and tender. The tartar sauce gives the chicken more flavor but I felt like I could eat the chicken without the sauce. The smashing cucumber salad is pretty much sliced cucumbers with sesame sauce. We really like this appetizer because it was light and refreshing. This appetizer is perfect on a hot day.

The udon comes in a giant bowl. At first I was a little intimated because I was halfway full from the two appetizers. But once you peek inside the bowl, it's really not a lot. There's not a whole lot of noodles but it was just the right amount for me considering I was halfway full. I opt for the thick noodles. I like smaller noodles for ramen. There are bits of beef cubes and the curry soup was thick. Their curry is the sweet kind. My friend tried my curry soup and he said it tastes like the curry from go go curry. I was able to finish my curry udon and my friend also finished his tsurutontan deluxe. He would have preferred more udon noodles. Our server, who was knowledgeable, mentioned that more noodles could be added to the bowl, free of charge. So if you are someone who wants more noodles, you can request! 

We were so full that we didn't have room for dessert. We will definitely come back to try other appetizers and udon dishes. I'm definitely bringing my friends here! I love noodles especially noodles in soup. I love ramen, udon soup and soba in soup. the broth is what makes the dish! 

Also, you can always order a bunch of appetizers and share the udon dish instead of getting your own.

I went here on opening day and waited a bit more than two hours to be seated, granted it was opening night. The staff were so apologetic and provided exceptional service. Our server Kristen was really nice and gave great recommendations. She knew what she was talking about instead of "everything here is good". 

My sister and I got the spicy tuna cone which was so good. There is a avocado on the inside, which neither of knew about so that was a nice surprise. This is great for sharing. 

I ordered the sukiyaki udon, which was really good. It was on the sweet side, as sukiyaki is. Nothing overwhelming. Sukiyaki is a sweet soy flavor, more sweet and umami than salty. Order the thick noodles with hot dishes! :) 

My sister ordered the TsuruTonTan Deluxe, which she really enjoyed. The tofu kitsune was a bit overwhelming in sweetness but I hear that they will be changing the dish a bit to accommodate to US tastes. The dish was dashi based. 

Overall, the place is great. Service is great. The environment is professional and clean, and great lighting for photos! :)

Everything was absolutely amazing! For appetizers, we had the spicy tuna cone, duck breast and fried chicken with tartar sauce. I think the duck breast was my favorite! So flavorful, especially when you dip it in the wasabi. 

For the udon, I had the clay pot one under the ever-popular section. The udon was definitely the highlight of the dish. Bouncy; cooked perfectly. 
 
The food, the service and the decor.. Amazing!!!

Great drinks , I tried Tokyo mule and lychee drink . Both of them was really good .
We ordered sukiyaki udon and cream mentaiko udon (cold) and it was just ok. 
I expected more.
I also tried supicy tuna appetizer which was more like Latin than Japanese .
They are famous in Tokyo and I'm Japanese but quality of main food udon wasn't anything special .
Bar also didn't have any chairs so I waited for my friend for hour just standing around ...
Staff were very friendly and service was great . Clean bathroom .
Also if you leave food , you can't take it home as they don't have take home containers.

Delicious ramen! Great selection! Chic decor, spacious area and nice food. Finally there is a potential alternative to my all time favorite Ootoya, still need to come back and check the consistency though.

The beef buns are filled with sukiyaki beef, which is less oily than a pork bun. The flavor is still nice and the meat is juicy.

Thick Udon noodles was great! Got the one with tempura shrimp and veggies. There was a gigantic piece of fried tofu on top of the noodles and they placed the tempura on top of the tofu. This way the tempura was still crispy when served! Very thoughtful. The noodle toppings also include eggs and beef. 

My friends got curry deluxe which was also great! 

Wanna come back and try more things on the menu.

We got there at 5:45pm and was told the wait was 45mins to 1 hour. So we put our name and phone number down. After 1 hour, still no text message, so we came back to the store and was told there was another 30 mins or so wait. After 30 mins, there were still 15 more tables before us. So we left with empty and angry stomach. I understand this place is new. But you could have just told us about the 2 hour wait. Why telling a lie?! People around me were angry too. Don't bother coming back again!
None of their dishes disappoint me so far! Highly recommend. And they also have a fancy bar inside.

Got there at 5:40 pm and was told the wait was about 30 min for 2 people. Guess what? The time we were actually seated was 7:00 pm. I understand that the restaurant is new and needs time to get used to the new computer system, but an hour's difference in estimate??? Isn't it ridiculously wrong???

The food was pleasant and delicious. My friend and I shared the Seared Salmon Sashimi ($14). I got myself the Tofu Burrata ($7), large thick-noodle Uni Udon ($24, and if you upgrade from normal to large, there is NO EXTRA charge), and the Water Cake ($8) for dessert. My friend tried the normal-size thick-noodle style Mentaiko Caviar Creme Udon ($17).

The Seared Salmon Sashimi was really tasty. The salmon was slightly seared and marinated in oil and special soy sauce. The salmon meat was fatty, tender, thick , and fresh, and was topped with salmon roe and fried garlic crunches. The only thing I would suggest changing is that there should be less oil, because the fish itself is rich in oil and extra oil, although tasted light, did not add to any flavor.

Then came my Tofu Burrata. Very, very rich tofu taste and thick, dense, and soft texture.  If you add a hint of the sea salt that came with the tofu, you will experience a different but interesting taste. 

The Uni Udon was so good! Very strong uni flavor. The noodles were completely saturated in creamy uni sauce and I felt my mouth was full of uni fragrance. For uni lovers, this is a must-try! And the noodles just had the right texture, kinda chewy but not overly hard. The uni cream sauce went very well with the shredded Shiso leaves and seaweed, making the dish more flavorful. But the portion was really small. I upgraded to big size and still it was the portion of a normal size to me. 

I also tried a little bit of my friend's Mentaiko Caviar Creme Udon and I loved it, too. Creamy, rich, and flavorful. The creme sauce makes the noodles softer (just a little) than the uni one. I just love anything made from mentaiko and uni!

The Water Cake (was once a hype at Smorgasburg but I didn't try it there) itself has no flavor but purely is a water jelly, or I'd say, the texture was softer and more watery than jelly. It came with Kinoko power, sweet-and-salty syrup, and a scoop of vanilla ice cream. I recommend adding the syrup and Kinoko power to the vanilla ice cream, because they are the best match! I also like adding the syrup to the water cake, creating a simply sweet flavor. I tried to eat the water cake with the ice cream, but no chemistry was created in my mouth (LOL). It was fun to try out different ways of eating this dessert and the nice thing is it was overall not very sweet or sugary.

Aside from the long wait, the service was a bit slow. We waited for 5-10 minutes between each course and our server forgot to check out our bill. But it was their first week and so many people went there dining, it is understandable that they were all in a flurry. I really would like to go back and try all their noodles and donburi (rice bowls), but I have to hold onto myself because this place is indeed pricy.

I was a regular at Tsurutontan in Roppongi. Now it's here! I was super excited and visited on the opening night. The udon and the broth tasted exactly the same. As a fan, I will be returning here often.

What was I expecting?

A little history of Tsurutontan from the perspective of a person who is a fan of theirs.

I have been to the Roppongi branch and the original in Osaka. 

The main things that I gather from going here were the portions. 

They are huge and that's relative to the size of the dish as well. 

It was one of the most moving experiences I have had with food in a long time. Rich flavor that warms the heart.

When I heard about Tsurutontan coming to New York City, I was beyond excited that my mouth was watering at the thought of those delicious Udon noodles. 

I wanted to believe that it could capture the same Japanese sensibilities and concepts that I respected. 

Unfortunately, it was not the same.

The service was impeccable; that is without question.

It did not carry the same vibe of the original. It was more for the younger crowd and it had the fast-paced New York mentality with nu jazz echoing through the speakers.

The  other problem is the portions were not the same. 

Maybe its localization or whatever. I can give a little bit of leeway to that but it was not the same.

I will give it another shot but the fact is I might have to live with the fact that to get the true Tsurutontan experience, I might have to take a 14-hour flight to the home of those noodles. 

Better luck next time~!
Holy sh!t so good. I can't wait to back and try everything on the menu. Excellent service and phenomenal food! Worth the wait

Tsurutontan tsurutontan tsurutontan! (now try saying that 5 times fast!)
Heard about this place from a friend as we were walking nearby, and we decided to check it out- it is a chain restaurant that originated from Osaka, and has made its grand debut in New York in late August!
I had read reviews about the long wait- we were quoted 1.5 hour by the hostess, but got the text that our table was ready in 45 minutes- no complaints there!
Interior is beautiful, very extravagant yet tasteful- you'll walk by the bar/counter area, and there are two levels open for seating.
My friend got the Tempura udon (tempura on the side- one of the veggies was enoki mushroom, i've never seen that before!) and I got the Mentaiko Ankake udon. The Mentaiko Ankake is an egg gravy with bits of mentaiko cooked in, served atop udon with a small mound of fresh raw mentaiko on top. Delicious and extremely filling! The gravy was very rich and satisfying, I strongly recommend. You could really taste the difference in udon, the texture was unlike any I've ever had before.
I look forward to stopping by again and trying their other dishes.

I don't usually write reviews, but my recent experience at Tsurutontan....

First off, the only reason why I'm giving them 2 stars is because of the food; the food wasn't bad but then again, a restaurant needs to focus on hospitality and clearly, they didn't succeed in that regard. 

My girlfriend and I were sat in a spot where there was a strong current of AC. We asked the waitress about switching over to a seat without the draft and she was nice enough to let us know that she will accommodate us. But, I do realize that the restaurant was busy and she probably forgot, therefore another party was seated at a spot where the waitress was going to seat us. After calling her again, she said sorry and went to get a gentleman who was in a suit.

We told the gentleman the same situation and all he told us was that every seat in the restaurant has the same draft from the AC. Unless he is a structural engineer by trade, I really cannot stand by the comment that he made. Clearly, all seats are not made equal. Not only did he not accommodate us by not switching tables, he gave us attitude for bringing up the situation. 

When asked if all the seats are the same again, with a fake smile, all he was able to muster up was a, "basically." After that comment, i was brewing up with anger and I asked verbatim, "You want us to suck it up and just eat with the cold air blasting my face?" And all he said was, sorry with a fake smile and just left us. I gave in because we already waited an hour for this dinner.

I wanted to test the gentleman's theory that all the seats were the same. I went to the other seats and tested out the AC. To my surprise, there was NO current at all. OMG, that guy isn't a structural engineer. Well, I went to a nice Japanese hostess and told her about our situation. She automatically helped us and put us at that seat. 

Lastly, before we left, there was another couple who were seated in the same seats that we were seated before. They, as well, requested to switch seats because the draft was way too strong.  

All I can say was, the guy really soured our experience at Tsurutontan. For those of you who are heading over to Tsurutontan, and get seated at that particular seat. You guys will know what I'm talking about. Otherwise, enjoy the food. I liked the Uni Udon.

Waited for more than an hour to get in. Then we had to wait for almost an hr for our food. I think they messed up our order in the back. Offered complimentary dessert, but it was only sorbet not the dessert on the menu. Definitely not worth the wait.
I ordered a TsuruTonTan Deluxe. It was soooooo delicious. It was totally worthy for waiting one and a half hours~ Amazingly good.

I love udon noodles, but udon hasn't received as much love as ramen (at least not yet in NYC). So, I was so happy to see more restaurants dedicated to udon noodles open. 

I stopped by with a friend around 6:45pm and was told that there will be a 1 and 1/2 hour wait without a reservation. We opted to stop by Breads Bakery (across the street) to kill some time since the lobby was packed with people waiting. I recommend people to do so. We returned at around 8:30pm, hoping that there is a slight chance that we would be seated earlier. However, we ended waiting until 9pm for a table (45 minutes longer than the expected amount of time). 

Now onto the menu, there were so many options for the noodles. You can choose from traditional broths to curry based or creme based broths. My friend and I decided to share the Tsuruton Creme Deluxe and the Tsurutanton Deluxe. I preferred the Tsurutanton Deluxe. The creme one was good, but I prefer a lighter broth. 

It was worth it. I thought the portions were just right, but you can add more noodles to your soup free of charge. It is definitely on the pricier side. Despite the wait, I have to commend the service. The staff were friendly, courteous, and helpful. There seemed to be some miscommunication amongst different staff members though. It was the first week of opening, so I don't think it would be a common occurrence.

I was fortunate to come here before 6pm one night and lucky me... no wait!

Tsurutontan is an establishment that people are familiar with in Japan and they decided to open up their first shop in the USA by Union Square!  This place is decently sized and I think there was a lot of hype in the first week as I heard there were crazy waits.  There is good reason though, as I feel the food is great.

The ambiance and feel of this place was delightful, coupled with the very nice and attentive servers here.  She even was promoting how nice the menu looked (which yes, it did look very well done)!  There were so many choices of appetizers and different types of udon (hot, cold, traditional, and unique styles), along with some rice bowls if you are actually not feeling udon (but you really SHOULD try the udon, as its KNOWN for it!). Anyways, after careful deliberation, I decided to go for what was apparently their most popular dish, the cold Uni Udon.  When I ordered this, you have the option to get the "large" order, which to be honest, is still a very manageable size.

Upon receiving my bowl, I have to say that this was one of the best bowls of udon I ever had in the United States.  I felt there was just the right amount of sea urchin and flavor in it.  What really won me over was a very simple ingredient, the sesame seeds, as it provided a nice mixture of taste.  The udon noodles themselves were prepared very well with the right amount of texture.  This definitely is illustrated by the fact that the udon is prepared in-house.  

Maybe I tried their best dish here?!? Who knows, I would have to come back here and try some other bowls of udon... but with how good the Uni Udon is... that will be hard to actually follow-through on that idea.

I loved Tsurutontan in Roppongi.
But NY Tsurutontan was a bit disappointing.
Udon noodle was too hard compared with Tokyo.
Waiting time was too long.
Good things is the pricing is quite reasonable.

We came around 5:20, and by six the place was totally filled.

We shared two appetizers and both got large udons.

Tatsuta fried chicken: the meat was juicy but not the juiciest nor crispiest fried chicken i have had. good but not great. the sayce was a very bright pink but tasted quite average.

Grilled duck: this was the best duck i have had in new york!! the meat was so tender with just a small amount of fat.

Truffle cream udon: the soup was creamy but balanced by a chicken stock base so it was not too rich. although we got a large size for both udons, this one turned out larger than we expected and we struggled to finish. there was definitely a mushroom flavor but not much truffle.

Uni Udon: a refreshing cold udon. the large size for this udon was actually pretty manageable. i wish there were more pieces of uni though.

Overall, the udon was very fresh and there was a wide range of both traditional and more creative flavors. I'm not sure if the udon tastes twice as good as udon west though. Even Raku, with noodles imported from Japan, is cheaper. The creative flavors (and duck) here are definitely worth a try though.

I had the Duck tsuke udon and creamy spicy shrimp tempura with the green tea crepe cake. 

The appetizer and udon are both great, though the shrimp aren't really spicy at all to me. The broth for the udon was a little sweet, but not too much. 

The crepe cake is from lady m bakery actually, and was as good as I'd expect coming from there.

The service, presentation, and atmosphere are great as well. For what you're getting it's if anything under priced.

First time trying this place, everything was pretty good, definitely will come back and try something else on the menu. 

Overall, I gave 4 stars for this place. Food was pretty good, especially the appetizers, they were AMAZING! But the udon was bit of a disappointment. I mean they were good, but slightly off from my expectation. And it's free to add extra noodles, and they offer two types of udon. 

I should probably try their cold noodles or a lighter broth next time, and leave more room for their appetizers!

My friend and I arrived around 4:45 pm on a Saturday. We waited outside. They opened around 5:10 and there were about 20 people waiting in the line outside the restaurant. They didn't have a good seat management system. It took them probably 2 minutes to assign a seat for a party of 2. They took information such as name, phone number before they arranged a seat. 
We were the fourth party in line. The server took us downstairs. We sit in the middle. The seats were weird. You sit next to your friend, not face to face. Even if there were plenty of booth seats, they still had people sit in the middle seats. I just don't get it why they don't give more comfortable seats. I could see the people sitting in front of me, who were totally strangers. And I had to listen to them talking and talking and talking and talking "Asians are blah blah blah". It was really unpleasant. 
I ordered caviar udon, my friend ordered the tempura udon. They were both good. The server asked if we would like our noodles be thin or thick. I like that. 
When we checked out and was leaving, there were about 8 people waiting. But there were still a lot of seats in the restaurant. 
Food was good but the overall experience was meh.
Food is very good service sucks! It took 30 minutes to bring two bowls of udon, we were starving the while
Tried the sukiyaki udon and found it to be mediocre and far too sweet. Very underwhelming for the price. I've had cheaper and far tastier udon around Union Square. I would not recommend this place.

The appetizers i must say were awesome!!!! Must get the waygu beef, shishito peppers and truffle sashimi roll. But the udon was very disappointing. My friend got the uni udon and I got the beef udon.  We were definitely expecting better. 
Water cake (raindrop) was delicious.

Tried this the first week they were open. Since we went at opening which is 5:30 I believe we didn't have to wait. The dumplings were nothing special. We also tried the ordered maguro uni sauce roll. Tuna didn't taste too fresh. Didn't taste or see any uni sauce. Onto the noodles. We ordered the kitsune udon, mentaiko caviar creme udon, and the tsurutontan deluxe. The bowl that came out is huge! Also you get to choose how any grams noodles you want either regular or large (all the same price). The noodle texture was nice and my mentaiko creme udon wasn't heavy which one would think when you see "creme". I think overall it was a decent experience but they are working out the kinks. Wasn't too impressed with the apps but the udon was decent. On the pricy side for udon. Not sure if I will be back though.
Grilled duck great for appetizer and tradition udon noodle soup was delicious. Cute modern atmosphere and great prompt service. Can't wait to go back and try other dishes on the menu.

I lived in Japan. This place sucks. Food is ok. But wait time from when you order to when you eat is endless. Service is very bad - not even a tiny bit Japanese.  Skip it for many better options in the city.

Why did I not know about this place before . This is one of the best udon places in the city. Me and my friend got the tsurutontan special and the sundubu udon. Both of them were exceptionally good. And the best part is, you can add extra noodles for free. This will be my second home during winter. The cocktails, omg are so on point and all the staffs are friendly and attentive. Lastly don't forget to get the water drop cake.

Big disappointment!

I went there on Sunday 2 weeks ago. Got there at 5:10pm and the line was 45 minutes wait so I left. Went back again last night. 

Service was attentive but the food need to improve. We had
 
- Creamy spicy shrimp tempura. We had 4 appertizers and it was the best one. I wish there was little bit more sauce on it. 
- Rib eye steak. There were tendons in most of our steak. Taste was not bad. 
- Grilled duck breast. Really nothing special.
- Seared salmon sashimi. Again, it was ok. 


- Tsuruton curry deluxe. I wish there was more curry favor in the soup. It was kind of bland. The udon noodles were average. I had a lot higher expectation but it really disappointed me. 
- Tsuruton tempura deluxe. The rice was wet. The rice stick together. 
- Uni pasta. There were 3 small pieces of uni in the bowl and it looks different from the pictures

We also ordered a bottle of sparkling champagne$44. It was good. 

At the end of dinner. We got a free water cake. It was good too. 

The bill was $198 and we paid $235 for 4 people. 

I'm not going back again!

Hands down the best noodle I've ever had! The customer service was great. It's a bit crowded so the noise level is above average for such an elegant place, but that's a very minor detail. I got there at 6:15 on a Wednesday and there was no wait for two people. We got the duck breast and uni and caviar for appetizer then the sukiyaki udon and beef udon. When I reached the bottom of my bowl all I could think of was "why do all good things come to an end..." Can't wait to go back and try more of their udon and other food! The staff are very friendly and attentive as well.

Ordered Sukiyaki Udon, Tatsuta Fried Chicken, and Tempura Udon

Tatsuta Fried Chicken was really meh, the sauce was a weird pink color and not tasty, the chicken was thigh meat but somehow dry. Where da moisture at? 

35 minutes after we ordered, the Udons finally arrived. Wat zee fk? I mean sure the waiter warned us that it'll take 25 minutes but do you guys literally grow the wheat and mill it?

Sukiyaki Udon had a broth similar to simple syrup. 50% sugar and 50% water. If you want diabeetus, you come here and get this. If you no want dyebitis, stay the hell away. I also heard from my friend the Deluxe Ramen has a super sweet broth too, in addition to the super amai Aburaage. Get these at your own risk, though your cavities might thank you later. 

Tempura Udon was fine. I mean, the noodles were supposed to be hand made but it hasd a familiar doughy kinda chew, not unlike supermarket freezer udon. Honestly I wouldn't be surprised if they took that 35 minutes to run to the Japanese market near NYU to buy frozen Udon. More than enough time to make it back according to Google Maps.

Did I mention the Tempura was cold? I mean sure, in Japan, the shopping street vendors sell cold Tempura so it's not unheard of. But this is not a fking shopping street now is it? WHERE MY HOT OIL AT BRUH, DO YOU EVEN HEAT LAMP? Hell, is it that hard to time the Tempura to be ready at the same time as the Udon? Do you even Kaizen? 

Bill came out to be $60 with 18% tip. We Are Never Ever Coming Back Together. Save your money and go to Sunrise Mart instead.

Love this place!
This is probably the coolest noodle shop in the world! The bar is also cool and I don't feel like I m in the Udon shop haha. I had mentaiko caviar Udon with poached egg and loved it.

Will def come back!

TsuruTonTan's interior is gorgeous and the waitstaff are so friendly, kind and perfect at explaining menu items. The tofu burrata was very smooth, made well and delicate, almost like the homemade tofu I remember from childhood. Sushi was fresh and tasty as mentioned by my friend. The mixed drinks are good as well. It's definitely classy and beautiful inside, especially for being an imported chain.

a lot of hype. liked the space and the diverse menu, but the food itself was quite up to scratch. the fried chicken is very tender and good. the caviar appetizer is also very good. but the udons are hit of miss - the thick noodles are not al dente and the broth lacks character. raku is still the best by far.

this place also has a long way to go to work out their service and order management. one udon came out 15 minutes later than the others.

Very underwhelming. Honestly, it would have been the same to get udon from the mediocre Asian take-out place near our apartment in Hell's Kitchen.

Started with the spicy tuna tartare cones. They were served wedged into this basin of rice which honestly turns me off a bit. They must reuse those and how many people have shoved their fingers into it like my husband did? Oh well, I'm Asian and I will eat it of course....but still....anyway, they were good. Nothing special but a solid appetizer. The tartare was a nice texture and the bottom had puréed avocado (not a puréed baby food texture to be clear - a nice adult purée).

We also got the duck and it was probably the highlight of our meal. Juicy, tender, lovely sauce, served with a lime wedge and wasabi. Tried the tofu burrata as a last minute decision...it was kind of heavy in texture but tasteless at the same time. Do NOT order as interesting as it sounds.

Ordered the Nebayaki udon and curry katsu udon as our main dishes. True to our waitress' description, the Nebayaki came piping hot. I found the soup base too sweet and it was reaaaaaaaalllly scalding - even for me and I drink cups of boiling hot water every day. I accidentally flicked the noodle a tiny bit and the soup felt like it was melting the skin on my face. The curry was very thick although it did not taste as heavy as it looked (even though it was definitely on the heavier side). It was like eating a katsu don with udon instead of rice. Couldn't recommend either dish.

We finished with the water cake otherwise known as the famous raindrop cake. You pour brown sugar and soy powder over it and it comes with a side of vanilla ice cream. Best part was the ice cream...looks really cool but I didn't care for it at all. It didn't even meet my low expectations. It was kind of like a grass jelly texture and the toppings were the only thing that gave it flavor. 

Ambience was nice. I really liked the decor and the lighting of the general part of the room. They had this long table in the middle where they seated parties of 2 side by side which I thought was a little strange. But the wood slanted curtain they had was neat (you'll see what I mean when you're there). We were seated in a really weird corner booth that had such low lighting, we had to do the old person thing and take out our phone flashlights to decipher the menu. The ceiling was super low and made me in my 5"3 frame feel like a giant!! I liked our waitress, she was cute and tried to be really helpful. Finally, toilet paper was really soft. That was the most impressive thing of the evening!

We went there at 5pm and saw a line in front of the restaurant already. Luckily the place itself was pretty big, we were seated as soon as they were opened. The ambience is really nice and all staff are all friendly and efficient.

We ordered two drinks and the bun for starter. The bun was so so. But the cocktails were great. For food, I ordered a cold uni udon and my boyfriend ordered the curry katsu udon. We both got the large bowl with thick udon. I   the cold udon a lot, it's very al dente with great flavor. My boyfriend liked his as well, but think katsu hama are better. Overall, we will come back again.

Great food and ambience.
Drink menu is really fun and cocktails are tasty!

Heard that they are opening lunch soon and can't wait to get Uni udon for my lunch!

We visited here on Saturday. We got here at four thirty to get a good spot in line before it opened. Once we got in, we were seated quickly. The ambiance here was very relax and we loved the music that was playing. Our waitress was very friendly and gave us a great selection of recommendations.

We started with the Fried Chicken, Grilled Duck, Sashimi and Tempura Shrimp. The fried chicken was nice and crispy and served with a tangy tarter sauce. The grilled duck was tender and succulent. Sashimi was okay and the Tempura shrimp was nice big pieces that were fried very well.

For my entree, I got the Mentako Caviar Udon. They can upgrade any entree to a large size, though it kind of feels like the bowl is bigger not the portion. The noodles were nice and chewy. The sauce was nice and creamy and with the caviar had nice saltiness to it. I also tried the Uni Udon which was also delicious. It could have used more sauce but the bites of Uni in it complemented it very well.

We finished with the water cake which pretty much looks cool but has no taste without the toppings.

I will be coming back here for sure. I noticed as I was leaving at seven that there wasn't a line anymore.

PLACE IS BOMBBBBBBBBB.

They only take reservations at 5pm or after 9pm. I've had ressies both times I've been here but have always seen lots of empty seats. First time was at 10pm, second at 9pm.

I've had the uni udon, the tsurutontan deluxe, and the curry. All amazing. I'd have to warn that the uni udon is VERY uni-tasting, some of my gals who love uni couldn't stomach the entire thing. I'd recommend sharing an uni and a regular with a friend. The namesake udon is SOOOO good - nice chewy thick noodles with a hint of sweetness in the broth. I've also had the wagyu beef sushi (just fine) and the tuna tartare cones (delish!)

They offer regular or large portion (1.5x regular) for the same price! The only caveat is that you cannot doggybag anything. But the Asian side of me ALWAYS goes for the large. You should, too! :)

So my friend warned me before we came here that I would be a changed man after eating the Udon at this place. We had to wait on a line to enter for about 15 min before we could enter. Once we were seated, a waitress took our order immediately. I ordered the Mentai Kamatama Udon (cold noodle with egg, caviar and spicy sauce $17) and my friend ordered the Kitsune Udon (hot noodle, decent amount of broth and tofu $14). Whats really cool is that the small and large portions cost the same. My meal was so bomb awesome that I was tempted to order another meal to go. I'm typing this review while waiting on a short line to go back in.

Food was extremely underwhelming.  Udon in broth was soggy and everything was very salty.  My entree came late- others in my party were finishing theirs. Space feels very corporate with harsh overhead lighting.  Music is loud and electronic. On a positive note the waitstaff is friendly. 



Edwin, thank you for the response.

I think the initial craze has died down (thankfully) and now the rest of us can enjoy udon without a crazy long wait. For a table of 5, we were seated immediately around 6:30pm on a Thursday. 

The interior is actually nice, more like momosan and ippudo, but dark (I was tempted to use my flashlight to read the menu). The appetizers we ordered were surprisingly good. I recommend the tatsuta fried chicken - perfectly fried little nuggets of chicken with a normal tasting pink sauce just like the picture. The seared salmon sashimi was also very good. Now onto the noodles... these bowls are massive, I was speechless when they brought them over. The regular portion of udon is definitely filling enough, and opt for the thick noodles. The sukiyaki udon was too sweet for my taste, but if they just added some broth to it I think it would've been perfect. The nabeyaki udon was less overwhelming in terms of sugar/salt content, and I loved that it had a bit of everything. The mentaiko caviar creme is pretty formidable to take down, but there's no denying that it's delicious (how could cream and caviar noodles not be?). 

Definitely worth revisiting when you're in the mood for good udon, but probably not worth waiting over 30 minutes for fast-casual type food. (Btw I see they use resy but the time slots are weird atm)

Really glad we checked this spot out, had a very chic/upscale vibe to it as soon as we walked-in. Heard the place gets pretty busy with it being relatively new but we must've beat the dinner-rush, got sat immediately. 

Ordered:



Sukiyaki Beef Buns - Liked it but I think I was mentally expecting something similar to a pork bun. 

Sukiyaki Udon - Wife ordered this and glad she did, I don't have a sweet tooth and this broth is sweet. Perfect to share but I think a full bowl of it would've been too sweet for me

Uni Udon - If you like Uni then get this, the noodles are sooooo good and they give you a satisfying amount of Uni. 

Spicy Tuna Tartare Cone - Everyone around us was ordering this and we were so curious so we had to order after our meal, guess this counted as dessert? Good app to try, interesting avocado purée underneath.

Well, I've never been this angry with a restaurant before. It's not about the taste of their food, it's about their no to go policy. The food there is oddly expensive, my friend and I spent more than 100 dollars for two small appetizers and two bowls of udon noodle. They refused to let us take our leftovers to go. I was totally surprised by that. I mean we already paid 100 dollars for our orders, and we can't decide how we gonna eat them? Their answer to this policy is the noodle will not taste the same tomorrow. Well, it is not their concern. My point is, customers pay money to buy food, they should be able to pack it and take it home. Not forced to throw it away when they can't finish it at the moment because some arrogant ridiculous reason.

This place is definitely worth the hype! 
I had a really great time and I loved everything about my experience at the restaurant (the service, the food, the interior designing, the ambience)!! 

To start, my friend and I walked in without a reservation on a Wednesday evening at around 6:30-7:00pm. We were offered seats at the counter but my friend wanted to sit at a table so the hostess (or manager) checked for us. Lucky us, a table had just opened up so we got sat immediately. Not to mention, the area in which we were seated had only four tables so it was semi-private. 

My friend and I had each ordered a cocktail. He had the Rosie Lychee ($13) and I had the Kyoto Imperial ($14). I'm not sure if we made the wrong choices but they were nothing special. As a matter of fact, the sparkling wine in my drink was so overpowering, I couldn't taste anything else.

For appetizers, we got the Uni & Caviar ($18) and the Ribeye Steak ($19). 
- The steak was pretty small for its price but IT WAS SO GOOD!!, especially if you eat it with the daikon and ponzu sauce. It's a must get! 
- The Uni & Caviar came after the steak, which I felt stole the spotlight but nonetheless, it was another great appetizer. I really loved the daishi soy gelee, which was kind of like a soy sauce jelly. It pulled the whole dish together. If you're not fond of caviar, you might want to pass on this appetizer because they do give you a generous amount of caviar. 

For entrees, we got the Sukiyaki Udon ($19) and the Uni Udon ($24). Since we shared both entrees, we upgraded the dishes for a larger portion of noodles -- FREE OF CHARGE!! 
- I forgot what the broth was, but the Sukiyaki Udon was served in a sweet broth with thick noodles. Since I never drink my soup, I didn't think it was that sweet. My friend, on the other hand, drank a whole bowl of the soup and he thought it was very sweet so I suppose you should drink in moderation (haha). It was still a great dish. I would recommend this if you don't want something too heavy. 
- The Uni Udon, a cold dish served with thin noodles, was not too enjoyable. My friend and I, both avid uni lovers, did not enjoy the dish. The uni taste was too overwhelming... The dish was a little more bearable with the shiso but I would've liked A LOT of shiso to enjoy the noodles... As tempting as "Uni Udon" sounds, I would not recommend this dish. 

Just as a disclaimer, although I loved everything about my experience here, I didn't mean they were perfect. There were certainly things they could work on, such as the order of dishes being served or the taste of certain dishes, but considering how they're new, they were forgivable mistakes. Not to mention, the staff were all very professional and they made an effort to ensure their customers were having a wonderful time. That means a lot to me.

I can't wait to be back to explore more of their menu!

Been here 2 times in 2 weeks! This place is the real deal udon spot. I dare to say it is  the best in NYC. Tastes just like the udon I experienced in Japan. Light but flavorful broth, perfectly cooked noodles and ton of variations. The menu is HUGE! I will be back many more times to sample everything. Highly recommended!

The food was great, but the service was outstanding! Our server was excellent as well as all of the other staff that came by throughout the meal.

The spicy tuna cones were delicious, and very thoughtfully crafted. The avocado inside was layered so you could taste all of the ingredients in every bite. The breaded and fried pork cutlet in the udon we got was really good!

Not a bad experience overall. Udon is good but not exceptional. We order the deluxe udon ( beef, tempura and fried tofu in it) and kimchi jjichae udon. Service is attentive and efficient.

My main problem is wait time. I tried to book two times before. They told me it's a two hours wait. This time I think the hype is kinda over. So I was told 40 min wait. We waited in the bar area where you can see the dinning area. It is 50% empty. I talked with the staff. They said the customers were in their way to the spot...I hope they are not faking their popularity.

This is that type of place that you only need to try once.
Taste was good. The large portion was like in a basin! But that's fine for my hungry tummy. Beef bun was good. The sauce tasted just like the pork bun sauce from ippudo.
Bestest! Reasonable,  great service.  Whet here for my birthday I could have picked anywhere and was really happy.  I'll be back soon.  One comment.  Could use more Nigori on the menu

Never been a big fan of udon's, but wanted to check this place out with all the hype. Service was fine, and the ambience was pretty cool. Good portions, there was a ton of udon noodle! But the quality of it was not mind blowing by any means. (tasted like most udon noodle i've had in the past) Overall, overpriced and underwhelming. Probably won't be back again anytime soon.

Food was delicious and masterfully presented. The service was excellent!  Kudos to our server Kyle who was very knowledgeable and professional.  We followed his recommendations from appetizer to dessert and were extremely satisfied.  Will definitely be back, well done!

Based on my best friend's hype about this place I decided to try it out and was definitely impressed! As a big udon lover I couldn't wait to try an udon specialty house. The wait time for a Monday night dinner was 20 minutes but we were told by the hostess that the wait time is usually an hour so we would recommend making reservations for weekend nights.

The quality of the restaurant was beyond my expectation. Great service with very knowledgeable servers and great interior design. The concept of the restaurant and the decor went hand in hand very well and marketing was excellent. 

However what really blown me away was their entrees! To start my boyfriend and I shared  spicy tuna tartare cone $12 and ribeye steak $19. Although the tuna tartare cone was bit lackluster for my taste as only the top part of the cone is filled and the rest is hollow the ribeye steak was excellent! It was unique and cooked to perfect medium rare, it paired very well with their house sauce that came on the side. 

Next came our entrees I had the mentaiko caviar creme udon and it was out of this world! The perfect creamy texture and slightly sweet and salty taste complimented the udon noodles very well. The udon were cooked to perfection and the presentation was very impressive. My boyfriend had the shrimp tempura udon that he also enjoyed but we couldn't really find it to be much different then any other udon. If you are planning on coming here definitely go for the unique udon dishes as they for sure would not disappoint! My new favorite udon craving restaurant would definitely come back!

I saw a post somewhere online about this place opening and I knew I had to try it. The results are in, and they're positive. Came here for the dinner rush without reservations but the wait time was only about 30 minutes (not bad when you are hungry at that hour). Though narrow at first, it opens up to more seating and eating space on a top floor and in the back.  The decor is interesting with the weird hay ball looking walls and the chopped up jeans on the other side.
But the important part is of course the food.  I got the curry udon large (free noodle upgrade) and my friend got the sukiyaki.  The curry sauce was thick and flavorful. And the noodles silky and perfectly thick. The tempura in the udon was well coated and had the right crunch with just the right amount of seasoning. It wasn't oily at all. Surprisingly I did eat every last drop,  but had the biggest belly ache ever (over eating). Would totally do it again!

Went twice, disappointed twice.

First time, arrived early for a table of 2 and decided to order a cocktail at the seated bar (which was completely empty). Before I even got my drink, I was told I couldn't sit here and had to stand near the waiting area with my $15 cocktail.

Second time, put our name down for a table of 3 but had to change to 2 because a friend couldn't make it. Was told we would only have to wait a little bit more for a table, but never got a call back. Only when we went back to the hostess did they notice they forgot to call us and blamed us for changing our party size instead of apologizing. Ended up waiting another 15 minutes while they seated several parties ahead of us only to sit at the bar even though there were plenty of tables.

Best udon ever. They have thin and thick udon -- both were AMAZING. 

Get the:
1) Uni udon - cold, goes well with thin udon, and they give a big chunk of uni
2) Sukiyaki udon - legit sukiyaki & broth, goes well with thick udon 
3) Wagyu with uni (appetizer) - perfect combo! 
4) Non-alcoholic Lychee Mojito - SOOOOOOOOO GOOOOOOOD 

We also got shishito peppers, salmon with ikura over rice, and those were good but not mindblowing. My non-alcoholic mango skinny piña colada tasted alcoholic, which was ok. 

I'll be back fo sho. Need to make a reservation in advance though! We walked in at 5PM on a Thursday night* when they opened and still had to wait. 

*Yes I came home and wrote this review because it was just so damn good.
Definitely the food is excellent here, just be warm the curry is a little heavy as my waiter warn me. But overall the food here won't disappoint you.

Go early. Avoid the lines. Delicious udon and tuna cones!  This place did not disappoint.  Udon was NOT greasy.  Never paid that much for udon but it was delish so...very friendly staff and extremely attentive.

the portion size is HUGE.  you can also have a extra half order of udon ON THE HOUSE.  don't be greedy like we were, share your bowl!  For appetizers, we ordered the fried chicken & cucumbers (totally refreshing).  Hot tea is on the house, phew.  get the thin noodles.  curry deluxe, seriously delicious.  skip the water drop dessert, although the ice cream was good the water drop tasted like... water.  We rolled out completely stuff.

Very good place for udon. Friendly staff. Huge place but still has pretty long wait.
Recommended: shrimp tempura, sukiyaki udon, tsurutontan deluxe

1. Ambience was the catch of the restaurant. The setting are different and unique. 

2. The host were pleasant, servers were well trained with menu and manager (Nathaniel) was attentive. 

3. Food were mediocre. 
Portion for side dishes were too small. I had uni and & caviar dish that cost $18. Which I think it is not worth ordering. Basically a bite size. Ribeye steak was too much fat and too salty at the 1st time but Nathaniel offered to make another new order. It was better. I would not order side dishes again. 

Beef udon was in good portion and nice presentation. Nothing spectacular about it but my daughter loved it. I will order mentaiko dishes next time. 

4. Beverage 
THE ONI WITHIN- I didn't taste shiso in the infused sake. I am a big fan of shiso leaf. A little disappointing. 
MYSTIC FALLS- same that tasted fruity and floral aroma. Touched the note and perfect for uni. 

5. Price
Average upscale price for noodle dish but overpriced for side dishes. 

6. Service
The host were pleasantly polite. Xuenie was well trained with menu. Great service and not overbearing. Nathaniel (manager) was attentive to guest and did the right moved in making a new order after the comments. 

7. Do not like the Japanese size of restroom. Expect nice bidet. But not important. 

8. Loved the exterior and interior of the restaurant. Well used of every inch of the space!

*why only 3 star- portion for side dish, the food & drink that I tried did not WOW me. I usually will only give 2 star. However, I liked the ambience, service and my company.

This place is amazing!

I arrived with a party of three at 7:00 for dinner. However, one of our party members was late, so we did have to wait until she had arrived to be seated, which is completely understandable to me. We got lucky and there was no wait when we did complete at 7:25ish. 

The restaurant is huge, I think somewhere close to 150+ seats! Ambience is nice, the decor is great, very Japanese. 

Our server for the night was Felix (very attractive :P). He was super attentive, came over to take our drink orders first, but being as we were hungry little pigs, we ordered everything on the spot.

Drinks:
Sauvignon Blanc
Kirin (they don't have draft Kirin, so we settled for a bottle) 
Non alcoholic mango pina colada - I liked it! Not overpoweringly sweet.

Appetizers:
Grilled duck - OMG. This duck is amazing. I highly recommend. It's only a few slices, but so nicely prepared. I'm salivating just thinking about it.
Sukiyaki beef sushi rolls - nothing to write home about. I think the sauce was a little too heavy.

UDON! Felix explained that no matter whether we ordered a small or large size, it was the same price. SO COOL! Of course we all ordered the large. And lemme tell you, it is LARGE. None of us finished, unfortunately.

Uni creme udon : I did not try this, but I'm told it's very good.
Tsurutontan deluxe : I have to start by saying I'm not a huge fan of udon noodles, so I settled for thin noodles. I actually liked it! The noodles aren't as chewy as thick udon, so yay! It came with a thin slab of tofu, which was slightly sweet, sukiyaki beef mixed with egg, and tempura. For an udon place, Tsurutontan's tempura is surprisingly good. TWO THUMBS UP! The broth was amazing. Not too salty at all. 

Dessert: 
Sorbet trio - The scoops were melting into each other by the time it got to us, so eh. The lychee was my favorite. It had pieces of real lychee embedded!
Chocolate cake with vanilla ice cream - a little dry on the cake.
Raindrop cake - Okay, I've been making fun of this thing every time I see it on Facebook, but I take it all back. It's the perfect dessert after a big ol' meal. The kinako powder gives it a nice nutty kick, and the sugar is not too sweet, so it doesn't feel too heavy after you eat. My favorite out of all three desserts.

It came out to about 65 a person, so not too shabby, considering we ordered so much!

Food, service, and ambience were all really good. Our waiter came by to take our orders after giving us a moment to look over the menu, the bus boys kept our cups of ice water full, and they brought the food out pretty quickly. I was about to order the original sukiyaki udon dish but the waiter explained that the broth is a bit sweet, and that if you don't like that to go with the sizzling sukiyaki udon instead. I was very happy with that suggestion because it came out in a hot stone pot and was delicious. We also had the wagyu beef, sukiyaki beef buns, tuna tartare, and tofu barrata for appetizers. The tofu barrata is actually no longer made with olive oil but with soy sauce. The soy sauce and dollop of wasabi made me think I was eating sushi for a second but you can really taste the soy bean in the tofu. The wagyu beef was a bite full of delight, which I can eat all night long if I were made of money.

A nice change from all the ramen shops this restaurant focuses on udon. Enjoyed the sukiyaki udon.  Fried chicken appetizer was meh. The spicy tuna cone appetizer was good. Water cake was..good to try once..  Seemed to be a lot of people waiting despite seeing several tables open throughout the night. Not sure that they have the seating and wait times worked out yet.

I'd give this place 5* for the food 3* for service and a -1* for the hostess who greeted us on Sunday nights.  I went there two Sundays in a row and both times I was greeted with this unpleasant excuse for a HOSTESS who's better fit working the counter at McDonald's.  

SUNDAY NIGHT CLOSING HOSTESS IS AWFUL 

Some Japanese exports are pulled off well (Ootoya on 18th st) Tsurutonton feels like they are tying too hard to be what it's not.  It feels like it's the Apple Bees of Udon,  and that's a shame because the food is good.   The staff gives off this impersonal attitude that you would expect from a major American chain restaurant.  Not rude but working off a manual.   The menu is too big and unfocused,  filled with picutures.  

If anyone from the management reads this please respond with a comment to know at least ur Yelp is being run properly.    I'm sure the Japanese head quarters won't be happy to hear about the negative experience guests are having

No wonder why people encounter long wait times. The quality of the food is top notch. There is a lot of space inside but for some reason they only take reservations for 5pm and after 9pm. I was so surprised but made a reservation for 10pm. Came early around 9:30 and had to wait 10 minutes to be seated. Although, I noticed some people walked in without reservation and were seated before us. As we were seated, i saw so many open tables available so I'm not sure what the wait is for. The interior of the restaurant is phenomenal. I loved the jean wall, very Japanese. 

For appetizer we had the spicy tuna cones. Delicious, especially with some type of green guac like thing in the middle. 

For drinks we had their take on a negroni and tokyo mule. It wasn't mind-blowing but it was pretty tasty. 

For dinner we had the mushroom egg udon and cold soy dipping udon. Both with extra noodles. We thought the portions looked small in pictures but boy were we wrong. The display is very fancy and lavish. Felt very special. The hot udon came is a ginormous bowl (large than 3 hands flat) and the cold udon rested on a pretty bowl of ice. Taste wise, udon was so fresh and the broth was really simple and clean. I couldn't finish my udon, only half. But my boyfriend finished his, including the soy broth!! 

I will definitely be back again, hopefully seating is managed better. This was such a satisfying meal. Great meal for a cold night in the city!

The Itami hot sake was nice. Food was good, thought the karage was decent. The wagyu was nice but nothing unique. I did enjoy the uni udon, noodles were al dente and the sauce was an uni paste, very excellent. Would definitely come back to try other dishes. Very nice decor and seating. We did come right at 5pm on a Sunday and there was a 30 minute wait.

Highly recommend but they don't take reservations. Got here around 5:30pm on a saturday and there was a wait....your entire party has to be present to be seated. 

We grabbed some beers by the bar while we waited. 

Once we were seated about an hr later...I recommend the tuna tartare and duck apps. The uni caviar is not that great. For my meal I got the truffle udon - thin noodles (you can pick thin or thick). Delicious!!! 

I liked this place a lot and I think this is worth the wait!

Update: I went to the site again and they take reservations online

Second update: I came back and got the uni udon- OMG BEST THING EVER- I got it cold with thin noodles. You can get it hot/cold with thin/thick noodles. Decent amount of uni!!!

I love udon and was especially excited to try this place after hearing that they offer cold udon. Our server was attentive, explained the menu to us, and explained the level of sweetness of some dishes we were debating between, absolutely loved him.
I ordered the uni udon with large udon. The uni was fresh but i found the udon to be a firmer than what i am used to, maybe because it is a cold thick udon dish. the dish overall was very fishy, something im not used to but it was overwhelming.
I had a chance to try the curry katsu udon and the spicy soondubu udon as well. All 3 of their udon dishes are super different. The katsu was nicely fried and the curry was flavorful and saucy. The spicy soondubu udon came with sukiyaki, no tofu, had a nice kick and flavorful broth. I liked both of these hot udon more than my uni udon but all these udons are in different categories and can't really be compared with each other.
For appetizers, we had the sukiyaki beef buns, chefs sashimi salad, and grilled duck breast. The sukiyaki beef buns was my favorite, even though the buns, itself, were cold when brought out. It would totally win my table over if they warmed the buns before serving. The sashimi was fresh, there were 4 slices of each fish. The grilled duck breast was delicious but the wasabi served with it had no kick, doesn't make a difference if you eat it with or without the wasabi.

For drinks i had the orient and mama colada. The orient kicked me in the throat, it was strong but i loved it. Mama colada was mildly sweet but taste like most pina coladas.
Food was decent but it took 45 minutes for our udon to be served. The soup itself was good but I would not go back if I had to wait for this long.

After two visits in two weeks I think I'm not gonna go back for a while. The food is nice albeit some dishes are better than others and deserves three stars. The service is definitely sub par. 

I really enjoyed the food the first visit. The creamy spicy shrimp tempura was big, deliciously well fried and indeed creamy. The tsurutontan deluxe was even bigger. Its broth was both sweet and savory. The udon was just a bit chewy as it should. The amount of meat was incredible. 

The food was so good that I decided to go back the following week. Bad idea. Nearly everything we ordered that night was bad or ill conceived. The tatsuya fried chicken was so dry that even dipping it into the tartar sauce couldn't save it. The seared wagyu sushi was mediocre and reminded me of a slice of roast beef hastily pressed on some rice. Why they made their uni udon their signature dish is a mystery to me. The flavour is not bad but the dish is unbalanced proportion wise. A few pieces of sea urchin were placed on a top of a large amount of thin udon. This dish would gain to be served with less noodle as an appetizer. The only nice dish of the night was the spicy soondubu jigae udon. The broth had some punch and we really enjoyed it. 

Service was bad and racially insensitive. First I don't know why they do not open all sections of the restaurant. Is it because it was still a soft opening (but really still 2-3 weeks later?) or do they want to create a sense of hype having patrons wait for 45 minutes or an hour?

When we got seated at the bar squeezed between other people I noticed a table for two that was empty and will remain empty for another 15 minutes. Why not offer your customers the option to decide where to sit?

Our waitress recommended all those dishes we didn't like. She also made a racially insensitive comment. Nothing really bad but totally insensitive. 

Overall the staff from the maître d' to the waiters is too inexperienced to provide a customer worthy service. Disappointing. 

Will I come back? Only when my udon craving is unbearable
Whom would I recommend this to? Solo eaters who would just come for a quick bowl of udon.

Really enjoyed the udon, both my uni udon and my mother's sukiyaki udon. Had a variety of appetizers as well (tatsuta age, shishito, sushi roll) all tasty and decent portions.

Larger size upgrade is free, but they don't allow you to take home any leftover food.

Service was good; waiter was really nice.

For dessert got the lady m crepe. Yummy!
Also got the water cake. It was a nice experience but didn't have much flavor (other than water) without the syrup and kinako powder.

If you love noodles, this is a MUST. It's only been opened for a few weeks but I've already been here twice w/ 2 different friends!

First off, the udon is FRESH. The noodles are so soft that they break apart on your mouth. Get your slurping game on! Amongst the dishes, my fav was the caviar udon. Get thinner noodles if you go w/ the cold dishes & thicker ones if you're aiming for hot. And large or regular comes as the same price so bring in a hungry stomach!

If you love sashimi, go for the salmon & ikura don. Instagrammable & delicious!

I loved the touch of bonito flakes on the shishito peppers. Yum!

And if you want something different, try the seared wagyu sushi. Yeah, you read that right. Whaaaaaaaaaat?! :P

Service is also on point. Props to the waiters & management.

Awesome decor as well.

Make reservations if you can!

I had hamachi carpaccio, uni udon, and deluxe udon. Udons come in either regular or large size and thin or thick noodle. Regular and large are same price (idk how...). I ordered thick noodle because i think udon noodle has to be thick lol. Their noodle was phenomenal! I haven't had better udon noodle anywhere else. Highly recommended. Carpaccio was very good as well. Very refreshing and perfect to cleanse palate before entree!

Not gonna lie but I walked in here with low expectations since most reviewers said the service here was meh but boy was I BLOWN AWAY! (in a good way of course)

I work a block away from here so came promptly at 5:10 PM with a boyfriend.  There was a line to get seated but it went rather quickly.  Don't let the store front fool you... it's abnormally big inside the restaurant!  They have a left side seating that's HUGE and an upstairs as well!

We had the pleasure of having MARCO as our host/waiter and he was beyond AMAZING.  He explained quickly to us that there are two different types of noodles (exchangeable), two different size to an order - can upgrade to large at no extra price and no takeout option.  My boyfriend and I ordered the following:

Spicy Tuna Tartare Cone ($12): HIGHLY RECOMMEND this as an appetizer.  It comes in 4 cones filled with tuna tartare, avocado puree and purple shiso.  This was super tasty and I love how the cone adds an extra crunch to the tuna!

Uni Udon ($24): fresh uni, shiso, nori and uni dashi sauce with thick udon noodles.  By far, the freshest uni in New York I've ever encountered!!!!  The uni MELTS right in my mouth.  It is such a great combo with the udon when you mix them together.  I love love love this dish and some may say $24 is really expensive for a bowl of noodles but this uni is WORTH IT!

Caviar Udon ($16): spicy mentaiko, caviar sauce with thick udon noodles.  This was super tasty as well!  Definitely not too heavy.

Water Cake ($8): got this as a dessert and it was surprisingly good!  This came with a a powder and syrup as the topping and also ice cream as a small side.  Super refreshing and light!

I also wanted to point out that Marco gave us two extra empty bowls so my boyfriend and I can exchange our udon orders - we thought this was super sweet and thoughtful of him! 

Overall, I had a super positive experience and would definitely come by again to try the other items on their menu.

FYI - my udon order took almost 30 mins to arrive but that only means their quality is beyond great!

I've been to Tsurutontan in Japan before, and the food at this new NYC location is just as good. Very happy that I'll have convenient access to awesome udon now. 

I believe there were 3 sizes in Japan, but only a small and large in NYC. No biggie, because both cost the same. The noodles are definitely fresh and the broth varieties are delicious, grouped by clear, curry/creamy, and cold. Big fan of the sukiyaki udon and the curry deluxe. The ingredients and toppings were prepared well. The apps were also delicious. Loved one of the specials -- wagyu beef with uni and truffle oil sushi.

The decor at Tsurutontan is pretty sleek, with both tables, bars, and benches and plenty of space. Pretty sweet venue.

Some logistical things still needs a bit of work. Came in as a party of two and put our names down to be seated. Saw another party of two come in after us wait less then we did and get seated before us. Saw one more party of two come and the front desk said they could be seated right away. We finally stepped and told the staff that we had been waiting 30 mins and our names were taken.

There are already so many ramen restaurants in NYC, so I'm glad there's an exciting new udon place now.

I've gotten the sukiyaki and uni udons, and my husband's tried the TsuRuTonTan Deluxe and nabeyaki.  The sukiyaki was exactly how I imagined it; the broth was slightly sweet, and it was overall very flavorful.  The uni was a bit disappointing; there was barely any uni.  My husband enjoyed the deluxe, and the nabeyaki was light (I liked it, but he thought it was a bit bland).  I also had a spoonful of the curry from a friend's dish, and that was flavorful...I would be interested in ordering that for myself as we head into winter.  

Update: recently tried the soondubu, which comes in a sizzling pot; another great winter item.  Also ordered the tempura (nothing special) and a sushi and crab sushi roll (pretty good except it came very slowly...after our noodles).

I like how you can pick thin or thick noodles (I think thin makes sense for cold noodles or saucy noodles, and thick for heartier broths).  Regular and large-sized portions are also the same price, which is good news for big eaters, but I thought the regular size was plenty.

My Japanese friend recommended this homemade udon place. The udon can refill for free as long as you can finish. The Uni and caviar with sushi rice taste amazing! My friend ordered the creamy udon, it taste rich and creamy. The udon I ordered taste normal, it is traditional soy sauce and bonito soup baSed. I personally don't like the thick udon so I think what I order is ok. I will go for thin udon next time because the thick udon is too much for me. The server also recommend me the uni top up on the beef, I would try to try it next time! 

Also, I wanna try the uni cold udon next time with thin udon~ The water ball dessert is made from the seaweed, and the topping comes with soy bean powder and black sugar. It is unique.

Hot, new udon spot took over the old Union Square Café space. Another Japanese chain opens up in NYC, yay for us! Upon arrival, I was impressed with their décor and high beat music. The bar is wide and there is a big dining area. My friends arrived just a minute before 6:00 pm and they are packed. Reservations are recommended through Resy on their webpage. 

For appetizers, we shared the Tatsuta Fried Chicken, Shishito Peppers, and the Sea and Truffle Sushi Roll. Tatsuta Fried Chicken, it was acceptable but was a bit chewy and dry. It seems like it was pre-fried since it came out so quickly and it was not crispy. Shishito Peppers, this was a nice snack to start with, nothing bad about it but nothing special as well. Sea and Truffle Sushi Roll was probably my favorite - combination of tuna, salmon, and yellowtail fish. Truffle Oil flavor was strong and pronounced. This was good.

For udon, we tried the Spicy Soondubu Jigae, Sukiyaki, and the TsuruTonTan Deluxe. To be straight to the point, the udon noodles were really soft and had a nice chew. That is their strength. Their broths, I was not really a fan of because all three were on the sweet side to me. Spicy Soondubu Jigae, this is a fusion of Korean and Japanese. I did expect this to spicy with kimchi flavor like Korean soondubu jigae. Only compliment about this dish was the pork, it was good. Sukiyaki was very sweet and I was not a fan. TsuruTonTan Deluxe, I asked the tempura to be on the side since I would not like my broth to be oily. The broth had eggs, seaweed, beef, and fishcake for flavor. It is more on the homemade side so I actually liked this dish the most. I would have definitely ask for salt though.

I have never been to their Japan chains before so I would not be able to comment about their similarities or differences. Overall, I did not dislike it but I did not love it either.

We came for the first time on a Sunday night and were surprised that there wasn't a wait at all. We were seated on the second floor, which was much more quiet and secluded. Our server, James came by to check on us frequently, and the service was really great! Towards the end, a manager came by to ask how our experience was, which I thought was very thoughtful. 
For first timers, the server takes the time to explain the menu and make some great recommendations. The wagyu sashimi was heavenly for an appetizer. Mushroom egg drop udon was light but flavorful. Last but not least, the water cake is a must-try for dessert. The water cake itself is a jiggly clear jello ball that doesn't have much taste on it's own. It comes with brown sugar syrup, slightly sweetened soy bean powder, as well as a scoop of ice cream. The flavors are well balance, and I love the fact that it wasn't overly sweet. 
Overall, our experience was wonderful! We'll definitely come back another time to try their signature curry udon.

I've been looking forward to coming to Tsurutontan for weeks but shied away due to the absolutely ludicrous wait times. I managed to get in late on a weekday evening with only a thirty minute wait. I tried the cold uni udon and the mentaiko caviar cream. The cream udon wasn't what I expected but it was deliciously though heavy. The pairing of flavors really came out well and their udon is really great. The uni udon I liked less but the noodles were definitely the stars. I would definitely come back to try other options.

Came here on a Wednesday night and there was already a long wait. I tried the wagyu as my appetizer and it was delicious. My favorite dish was of course the udon. The regular sized udon comes in a bowl that's probably 2-3 times the size of your head. However, the amount of noodles is not that much. The plus side is that you can upgrade to large while you order at the same price. I didn't really like the seating because if you're not a group of 3 or more, they seat you across a bunch of strangers which is kind of weird.

My friends and I came here right when they opened on a Thursday and had no problem being seated. Our waiter was very nice. He explained how the menu was organized and recommended us to get the thick udon with the hot dishes and the thin udon with the cold dishes. My friend and I decided to share the Mentaiko Creme Udon (hot) and the Uni Udon (cold). 

Mentaiko Creme Udon: I was really looking forward to trying this as I had something similar in Tokyo. However, I felt that the creme sauce overpowered the mentaiko. I wish there was either more mentaiko or less creme sauce. Also, the thick udon was a little too soft for my liking. 

Uni Udon: This was the real winner! The uni taste really came through. Also, the thin udon had a nice chew to them. I will definitely come back for this! 

You can upgrade to a larger portion of udon noodles free of charge. However, large looked pretty average so I'm not sure what regular would look like. I would just say always ask for the large and don't bother with a regular. 

We decided to end the night with the raindrop cake. After seeing photos of it all over instagram during the summer, I had to finally try it. While the "cake" itself doesn't taste like anything...I mean it's jellied water, it does have a very pleasant texture that works really well with the syrup and the soybean flour. The vanilla ice cream on the side is an added bonus.  

The menu is extensive. The staff is great. The ambiance is on point. I can't wait to come back and try the other items on the menu!

Best udon I ever had in NYC! I walked in around 5:30pm on a Friday and had to wait about 20 mins for a party of two. The ambience of this place is very unique and the staff was very helpful on suggestions! Loved how this place served everything with huge bowls and utensils. I had the Wagyu Shabu Udon while my boyfriend ordered the Truffle Creme with Mushroom. I thought mine was better while he insisted his was... but overall you can't go wrong because they were both yummy. Remember to always get a large (extra noodles) because it's the same price as a small!!

This place was awesome!! We didn't make a reservation on a Friday night and had to wait 40 minute for a table... but no one seemed to want to hang out at the bar so we were able to make ourselves comfortable and waste time with a bottle of dragon god sake and were seated in no time. We split the truffle & sea appetizer and then I had the uni udon and my BF had the Sukiyaki special. We both were obsessed with everything we ate. I am going through a crazy sea urchin phase though - unless you are going through the same my uni udon dish may not be for you. We finished with a water cake. It was way better than the boring jello I was expecting (probably because of the toppings that we drown the jello in).
