Everything was great here, I 100% recommend this place for any slightly adventurous eater

I heard about it from my friend who tried it when she visited Japan.  
I went there this evening with my friend, I ordered one of recommended "Suikyaki Udon" (beef, egg, vegetable with soup) which was just okay to me, and appetizer "Seared Salmon sashimi" which was tasty!  I will go there again to try other Udon noodle with creamy soup or the Don.

The restaurant is spacious and service is friendly but can be better of introducing food to customers.  Overall, I have no big compliance there, only a minor thing that my portion of udon noodle was so little compared to other people who ordered same size with mine.  Also, I heard people can refilled udon noodle at the one in Japan so I asked the server if it is the case, and he said mine was the large size already so could not fill up (are you kidding me?! yes, the size of bowl is large but not the amount of noodle =_=).  I guess I will see if it is the same when I go there again.

The drink menu has good varieties of cocktails, beer, wine and sake.  The dessert menu only has 3 choices and none of them are interested to me.

a great addition to the upcoming nyc winter scene 
upstairs has a cute loft area great for hosting party ( 10ish ppl) and downstairs has two sections, rather spacious.

the appetizers are great for sharing~ tuna roll is nice and easy to eat while fried chicken is on the bland side you'll have to eat with the sauce. 
the curry and cream udon dishes will be rather heavy and good for sharing.
sukiyaki udon is truly "sukiyaki"(on the sweet side) so if you are expecting a pure dashi broth it'll be a surprise. 

the decoration is artsy and ambiance great, may be a little noisy though.

4/5 because it's a little pricier than your usual udon. The tsurutontan Udon is $23 and the uni Udon is $24. The bowls are pretty big. A bit confusing cuhs a reg size and large size is the same price? So they ask if you want a larger portion or not for free. We also got the uni wagyu sushi as an appetizer which we all rly loved a lot!! Cept it's 2 pieces for $23. But that was especially yummy and worth it. 

Went in on Sunday night with a party of 4. Had to wait around 30 min which wasn't too bad. They also seated us at a big booth table which was nice.

Servers are all great and really nice! We got some hot tea after our meal as well. I'll def come back to this spot !

Delicious!!

The reason why I took out a star was because of the lack of communication between the waiter and us.  We were debating about getting the wagyu beef appetizer and the waiter told us they can certainly add a piece since the order typically only comes with 2 pieces and we had 3 people.  He also told us there was a special going on with the wagyu beef that includes the uni.  So we assumed it would roughly be about the same price as the original plus that extra piece.  The original app was $13.  They charged us $35 for the appetizer - that's basically TRIPLE the price.  We were expecting maybe $20 or even 25 but certainly not 3x the price listed.  I mean, the appetizer was phenomenal but would have liked to be more informed especially since the price was such a large jump.

Other stuff we ordered:
- shishito peppers.  this wasn't as blistered as the ones I usually find but it was quite nice and came with a yummy sauce
- tsurutontan deluxe udon.  This was what I got with the large size (no extra cost!) and with thick udon. It was HUGE.  The whole bowl was probably the size of my midsection.  It was crazy big with a large amount of toppings from the tofu skin to eggs to a ton of tempura.  My only qualm was that there was too much tempura that made the dish go from delicious dashi to more oily.  My friend recommend that I do the nabe next time so there won't be any tempura.  My friend actually had to finish the rest for me cause it honestly too much tempura/toppings
- uni udon.   My friend got this in the large size with thin udon and the picture in the menu was a little misleading.  It looked more creamy then what the actual dish was.  Also, there was only 3 pieces of uni on top.  My friend said it was good but had expected a little more.  He also recommended it more for summer rather than winter since it's a cold dish
- shrimp tempura udon.  My other friend got this one also in large with thick udon.  He thought it was delicious as well.  This was more of the traditional one since it was pretty much dashi broth with udon with shrimp tempura on the side.  Nothing too crazy.  Just a good noodle soup for the upcoming winter months

My friend who ordered the uni udon is already planning on coming here like once a week because it's a good deal if you get the large size and I'm already eyeing the curry udon...

Dope.

Came on a Sunday night in a party of four at 7PM, we waited under our estimated 30 minutes. The interior reverberates a very spacious, smart casual setting. 

10/10, would order again:
Shishito Peppers - topped with bonito flakes and a side of yuzu kosho (has a bit of a kick)
Uni Wagyu Sashimi - on sushi rice, with dashi gelee and truffle salt 
Uni Udon - cold, option of thin or thick noodles, complimentary extra udon 

Our waiter was knowledgeable of the menu, checked in with us regularly. I am definitely coming back to try the other dishes.

I guess you will have to eat with the right person to get the full taste of this place - today my friend was very helpful and offered to wait in the line as I was still busy at work. We met around 645-ish and were seated promptly, thanks to her wait upfront.

Upon opening the huge menu, I already lost my mind on what to order, as I heard that every dish was spot-on that you simply cannot miss. Trying to make the best out of it, we went with those "recommended" dishes, and never got disappointed, fortunately. 

The uni sushi was definitely a bomb - how can you go wrong with the two most tasty raw food and combine them with sushi rice? For udon, we followed our waitress's advice - cold went with thin noodles while hot went with thicker ones. It turned out that both of us enjoyed the hot broth more, while still gave credit to the uni, perfectly marinated itself with the soup base. We opted for the water cake as dessert - this is probably the most popular one on their menu, even though I did not quite get the hype of this flavorless, jelly-type of cake, I had to admit that the green tea ice cream played a very good supporting role here. Would suggest trying the matcha crepe cake instead.

Bill came down around 45 bucks pp, quite a bargain given the lots of things we shared and the fame of this place back in Tokyo. This is probably the top udon place in the city, well done!

Udon was good 
Had sukiyaki udon  
It was good.. noodle texture wise i am not so sure.. maybe because its fresh udon? Maybe it suppose to taste that way.. 
it was good

Where has this place been all my life! The best udon creations by far in NYC. 

This place is known for its udon creations and they make sure that udon is the best. The restaurant is very spacious and can accommodate large parties and a lot of guests however due to such high demand for their awesome udon the wait can pick up. luckily we went early on a Wednesday night and the wait was quick. The space is dark but you feels cozy and dimmly lit so it's intimate but still comfortable to see everything. The wait staff is super friendly and explains everything on the menu of needed. They are very nice and the manager even walked to our table to check on us ever so often. The water cups were never empty. 

For the food I ordered the recommended appetizers: seared salmon with salmon roe and grain. Super delicious. The salmon is seared very lightly and the flavor was great. We also ordered the spicy salmon cones. A large amount of perfectly chopped spicy salmon packed into crunchy wonton skin shaped into cones. You can eat a whole bunch bc their that good. 

For my main course I ordered udon of course but the Curry Udon Deluxe: you have the option of getting thin or thick udon noodles (ask your server for the best type of noodle for your specific dish; mine was thick udon) the noodles come in a huge portion in a gigantic bowl. The curry was the best Japanese curry I've ever had. Not too salty and simply umami. It comes with shrimp tempura, pork katsu (fried pork cutlet), and tender beef slices. This dish was just amazing. It is a must try when you come here. The Katsu was tender and moist, the tempura stays crunchy even in the udon, and the beef slices just melt in your mouth. 

This location is highly recommended to fulfill your udon dreams. 

Tip: you can ask for extra udon with no extra charge.

Prices may seem a little steep for a bowl of udon but it is totally worth it! We arrived on a Wednesday night and we got seated pretty quickly once our whole party arrived. We ordered the spicy tuna tartare cones, uni wagyu sushi, wagyu udon, uni udon, and tsuruton creme deluxe. 

The spicy tuna tartare cones had a kick of guacamole in the end. Never had spicy tuna with guac but it works! The uni wagyu sushi was a special and I'm so glad they told us about it. It was literally heaven in my mouth! If it wasn't so pricey ($23 for two pieces) we would've ordered more. 

The udon came with two sizes (regular and large) and two different types of noodles (thin and thick). They suggested thin noodles for the cold noodle options and thick noodles for hot broth. No extra charge for a large? Yes please! The wagyu udon was also a special. It's pretty much the sukiyaki udon but with wagyu beef instead. My friends really enjoyed it but I prefer salty broth over sweet. The uni udon was pretty disappointing. It could've used a little more uni and the noodles itself did not have much taste. I did love the texture of the thin noodles over the thick noodles though. The tsuruton creme deluxe was my favorite. The broth was flavorful and creamy without being overly thick. 

My friend also ordered a tokyo mule which was delicious! Wish I got one myself.

I came here on a Friday night with my boyfriend and no reservation. There was quite a few people waiting outside already and the inside was packed. We were told a waiting time of half an hour so we sat at the bar and enjoyed a couple of drinks.  I ordered the Rosie Lychee Martini and it was delectable. My bf ordered a Tokyo Mule but it was too diluted with ice and rather weak.  
We got seated promptly at the 30 minute mark and we were excited by the menu's visual layout.  We eventually ordered the Uni Udon and the Beef Sukiyaki Udon.  The waitress recommended to have the Uni Udon with their thin udon noodles as there is an option of thick or thin udon.  They also offer large sized portions of every noodle dish at no extra cost! The food came out rather quickly to our surprise so that's a huge plus! 
The Uni Udon was well beyond my expectations. The Uni was fresh and the udon noodles were the perfect texture with the right amount of bounce. The Uni and sauce coated the noodles with this delicious goodness.  It was also a cold noodle dish so it was quite refreshing! 
My boyfriend's Beef Sukiyaki Udon was also great! It was extremely sweet and savory with thick chewy noodles.  The slices of beef were soft, thin and packed with flavor.  
This restaurant lives up to its hype, I definitely recommend it.

This place is all hype.  Don't get me wrong the food was good, but do not wait on long lines.  Wait at most 30 minutes and that's it.  Before coming here, I read the hostess had a tendency to make people wait for their table regardless of the fact that there were multiple empty tables.  This same exact thing happened to me.  I got there around 645pm on a warm Tuesday evening.  The main seating area had multiple tables, probably 1/2 empty, open.  Yet, we were still quoted a 20 minute wait.  I don't know if management is doing this on purpose to make it look like they are a very busy and popular establishment or what.  

We finally got seated and I am not a fan of the setup of the seats in the middle.  You can't even see your dining partner since you are seated next to each other.  Aesthetically, it looks nice, but practically, it is not.  We had a very pushy server along with some pushy busboys.  I felt we were rushed to order and also rushed to leave since they kept coming to check if we were done.  This was all the while half the restaurant was still empty since there were several empty tables.  I don't get what the rush was?

On to the food:

Seared salmon sashimi $14 - this was good, but not great.  It was a pretty standard seared salmon dish that lacked taste.  You can get a very similar dish at Gyu Kaku for much much less.  Skip this and get something more filling, like a bowl of udon instead.

Mentaiko Caviar Udon $16 - this was surprisingly very delicious!  I was a little scared of the caviar and afraid it would be too fishy for me, but it was delicious!  I loved the saltiness and it paired very well with the udon.  The description noted this dish is spicy, but it really isn't.  So you are safe and can order this.  Definitely get the large, but I recommend sharing the large with a friend.  After a while, the caviar can become a bit overwhelming so you'll want to change up the flavor with another flavor of udon.

Tsuruton Curry Deluxe $23 - this was a bowl of perfection.  It had all of my favorite Japanese foods - udon, pork cutlet (fried just right with the perfect amount of breading), shrimp tempura (you really can't go wrong with shrimp tempura.  this was delish!), beef short plate (yum) and the delicious curry flavor!  If you like any of the ingredients on its own and you enjoy curry, then you should order this.  Oh, and don't forget to order the large.  The large size is the same price!  

That said, I enjoyed my food, but it's not a place I will go back to.  I think I am more of a ramen girl and ramen + the broth is something I long for.  The flavors of the udon here just aren't that special.  These are flavors you can get at most authentic Japanese restaurants so this place isn't special enough for me to make the trip to, much less wait on long lines and pay high prices.  Ramen on the other hand, each place makes their broth differently, something you can't get anywhere.  Hope this helps!

We came here with a group of 4 people. We came right when the store opened and there was a small line before they were open for business. I had the US Wagyu Shabu Curry with thick udon. Tried the Tsuruton Salad. Contains Mentaiko caviar dressing and crispy udon. Also had Uni & Caviar, Truffle Creme with mushrooms, Uni Udon (cold noodle dish) and Tsurutontan Deluxe.

Out of all the dishes, I preferred the Tsurutontan deluxe the best. It felt to have the best balance between noodle and soup. Their broth reminded me of one of the broths I tried in Japan at the Udon Museum. It was a great educational experience and this place does udon justice. The tempura was light and crisp. Shrimp wasn't over cooked. The other dishes were very sauce/soup heavy and it felt to be too much. There is no extra charge if you order the large portion of the noodles. I thought it was a strange concept but it works. 

The bowls they serve the meal in is HUGE!! I asked one of the staff members where they got their bowls from and he said they got them imported from Japan. 

The staff was extremely helpful and always checking in to see if everything is okay with the meal. 

From the salad, I liked the crispy udon. Overall the dish was good but I preferred others. I have never tried a cold udon noodle dish and I wasn't that impressed with it. The uni was alright, not sweet enough but there were no sand in it. The truffle creme was too heavy on the cream sauce and flavors weren't balanced.

Overall, I would recommend this place and would definitely come back here again.

I never thought udon could be that good! This place sets new standards for udon! We came here for my girlfriend's sisters birthday and it was a great choice! My girlfriend had originally sent screenshots telling me she wanted to come here so we decided to make the trip. The decor in the restaurant is japanese like and makes me feel like i'm in japan. The food is delicious, we basically tried everything on the menu and nothing was dissapointing. So i'd definitely recommend this place to anyone that's looking to try something different than just ramen.

It's a trending new Udon spot that opened up in the old Union Square Cafe location. The decor is great and the location is very spacious, but the restaurant is new, so go early before the lines get long. Overall, I thought my meal was just OK, the first indicator of how the meal would turn out was was the lack of Asian staff. It's a Japanese restaurant, but both hosts and 90% of the waiters were all non Asian??? Yes, this matters to me since it shows that this is Americanized Asian food that caters to non Asians. I think it would be odd as well if I went to an Italian restaurant and most of the staff was Asian. So I had asked my Caucasian waiter if the Udon dish I was about to order was too sweet, he replied, "It was not, it was balanced." It was not balanced, it was too sweet...

The food:

Sea & Truffle- Tuna, Salmon, Yellowtail with Truffle Oil. I will be the first to scoff at rolls at Japanese places but this roll wasn't bad. It was Americanized but the truffle oil was pretty interesting.

Tatsuta Fried Chicken- Shibazuke Tartar Sauce. Easily one of the more interesting dishes we had that night. The dish is usually a no brainer since who doesn't love fried chicken? But, unfortunately, there were flaws in the dish. First, the chicken was oddly chewy and stringy, the overall flavor was good and it wasn't oily but the chewy and stringy part really killed the dish for me. The sauce had a very interesting color and tasted like Kewpie mayo tartar, it was OK.

Shishito Pepper- Bonito Flake & Yuzu Kosho. The peppers were just OK, they were kinda too straightforward, they just tasted like peppers without much else. The Yuzu Kosho was too aggressive and tart for me.

Spicy Soondubu Jigae Udon- Beef Short Plate, Vegetable & Spicy Broth in Stone Pot. This was a recommendation from the waiter and it was the Udon I liked the best of the three. And yes, I know this is a Korean dish but it wasn't half bad. The dish did have a little heat which was nice but this was too sweet and not balanced as my waiter suggested it was. I did, however, really liked the beef short plate and the shiitakes.

Tsurutontan Deluxe- Shrimp & Vegetable Tempura, Beef Short Plate, Kitsune, egg dropped. This was the dish I was most excited to try since it seemed the most traditional, it was just OK. I did like how homey the dish came off but it also felt like something you feed to little kids after school. I also thought this dish was too sweet. 

Sukiyaki Don- Beef Short Plate, Onsen Egg & Vegetables. This was my least favorite Udon, it was so incredibly sweet. The only bright spot, it did have a somewhat homemade taste.

I went there on Saturday night. 
Love the decor and beautiful large noodle bowl.
Food was delicious.
Great udon, great ambience and nice service. Noodles are a little overcooked. Udon could be more chewy.

Came here on a Friday night for a table of 4 and the approximate wait was 45 mins to an hour. However if you wait inside they may bump you up the list. After 20 minutes of waiting, the hostess asked what name we were under and bumped us to the top.

The decor is very modern and trendy, definitely not your usual udon setting!

I ordered the sukiyaki udon - the noodles were good and the egg was poached perfectly, but the soup was quite sweet. Sukiyaki is generally on the sweeter side, but the ingredients are only cooked in the broth, dipped in raw egg and then consumed. However as a soup I felt that it was a bit too sweet to drink.

My friend had the curry deluxe udon and she said was good, but quite heavy. She had most of it but couldn't finish all of it. 

We also randomly had patron shots which were surprisingly very smooth and easy to drink.

There is a variety of hot/cold udon dishes to pick from so I wouldn't mind coming back to try some of the others!
The food was "okay" but the waiter was annoying, seriously annoying.

Earlier last month, a friend suggested this relatively new trendy Udon place for a Saturday night dinner for a group of 7. She tried to call for reservations but the best time they could give her was 9:30pm. We decided to take our chances anyway and walk in for an early dinner at 6pm instead since we've heard that the place is pretty big.

Upon arrival, while polite, the hostess seemed overwhelmed and obviously new at managing tables. We waited a while outside, but later noted that there seemed to be available open tables scattered throughout the huge restaurant, which seemed to go on forever with high ceilings and long tables.

When we were finally directed to a table, we got a server who was extremely friendly and helpful. He offered recommendations from the menu and warned us of certain udon dishes that were more on the sweet side. He explained that there would be two udon choices (thin or thick) and the option to get your order as a large portion at no additional cost.

For appetizers, we tried the Tatsuta Fried Chicken ($11) with its bright lavender colored Shibazuke tartar sauce - tasty, but asides from the sauce's color, nothing too special. We also got the Seared Salmon Sashimi ($14) which had 6 pieces and was flavorful. 

For our entrees, I chose the Tsurutontan Deluxe ($23), figuring I couldn't go too wrong with what seems like one of its signature. Unfortunately, the broth was just too sweet for my taste even though to be fair, the waiter did warn that this was one of the sweeter tasting udon dishes due to the kitsune. The rest of the dish was just a mixing pot of egg, beef and tempura and I didn't enjoy it enough to finish it. 

I liked my other friends' dishes more: the Uni Udon ($24) is cold but refreshing with creamy uni and the curry udons were warm and savory. 

Two friends got the Water Cake ($8) at the end for dessert, which made for cute photos but otherwise tasted exactly like tasteless gelatin without dunking it in the accompanying syrup and powder. Gimmicky dish to try once.

All in all, our waiter was great and the dishes were okay, either hits or misses. I would come back to try another udon if I had the chance. 3.5 stars.

Heard goood things about this place so decided to check it out. Party of 2, we were seated at the counter in about 15 mins so not bad! The interior design is really nice, the place feels very clean and modern. Service was excellent as well. 

Food: We got two noodle bowls, the Curry Deluxe and the Sukiyaki Deluxe. I liked how you can choose different types of noodles, we got one thin and one thick and they were both delicious! Probably some of the best udon noodles I've ever had, they were very soft yet chewy, much much better than the typical udon shop. The curry ramen was good, it had beef chunks as well as pork cutlet and shrimp tempura. The curry could've used a bit more kick and spice, also a bad thing about fried stuff is that they get soggy quickly so eat those first! The Sukiyaki udon was good, the broth was sweet and salty, which complimented the curry well. It came with Enoki mushrooms, cabbage, poached egg, and regular mushrooms along with the beef, and was tasty as well. It would be better if they were served a bit hotter. 

In summary, great new udon joint and definitely will be back to try more of their massive menu!

My god the truffle udon special was to die for. Unlimited truffles! Pure bliss

We came with a group of 6 and ordered a bit of everything. The tuna tartare cones and shrimp appetizers were good but the real shining star were the noodles.

Our server recommended the sizzling sukiyaki udon and it was 1000% the best one. The truffle cream was like an Alfredo and the Curry Udon was an interesting thick flavorful sauce. Most classic was the Duck Udon but I'd still go with the sizzling every time.

4 stars only because the lights were flickering at our table and the server was difficult to understand and spoke awkwardly quietly.

I've been waiting to try this place since the day they opened but haven't gotten a chance until now. The food was good but sadly, I wasn't blown away. 

Spicy tuna tartare cone ($12)- I am usually not a big fan of spicy tuna but these worked well inside the crispy cone and avocado puree and displayed in such a cute fashion. 

Wagyu sushi ($13)- poor quality in wagyu beef. It didn't give the usual melt in your mouth effect like I would expect it to. However, the sushi rice underneath had a good flavor and just the right hint of vinegar.

Shishito peppers ($8) light appetizer. The sauce compliments the peppers well. 

Fried chicken ($11)- good batter for the fried chicken. They use dark meat which I like. The tartar sauce was very unique although I couldn't pinpoint what it tasted like. Don't think it's worth the price though.

When you order your udon, they let you choose between the regular size bowl of udon or the larger size portion. They are both the same price but if you choose the larger size, you are not allowed to take anything home if you do not finish it. You are also given a choice of thick or thin udon. I decided to try the Mentaiko caviar cold udon ($16), which was recommended to me by one of my friends. I enjoyed the flavor of my bowl of udon and the texture of the udon was very unique. I chose the thick noodles although they recommend the thinner noodles for cold udon. The strands are noticeably thicker than the normal udon you are accustom to, which created a different experience for eating udon. Although, I liked my noodles, after a while, since I was eating the same thing over and over, I got a bit bored of it. I need some more variety. The portions are pretty large and by the end, I struggled to finish everything! 

I didn't appreciate that I felt a bit rushed while eating. They kept coming around to take the plates/bowls away when we were still eating. Also, they placed the check down before we had the chance to ask for it.

This was my first time here. I loved every moment. The ambiance and the food. I had the shrimp tempura udon. It was very good but it could have used one more shrimp. I got two shrimps and the rest was vegetables. I had the fried chicken which was good. The tartar sauce through me off but it was tasty. The shrimp dumplings were spot on and the green peppers were delicious. I will definitely be back to try other selections from there menu.

I strolled in on a Wednesday afternoon with a friend at about 5:30pm for an early dinner and we were seated right away. By the time we left at about 7:30pm, there was a line out the door. So definitely make reservations or come early if you don't want to wait! 

The menu is a large fold-out filled with a large assortment of Japanese dishes on top of their signature udon dishes. I quite like that the menu includes pictures of the food as I am a very visual eater - looking at how a dish will look really helps me make my decision. 

We decided to split their Spicy Tuna Tartare Cone ($12) with avocado puree and purple shiso. The cones were presented very nicely - super cute and very picture-ready. The cones were crispy and crunchy and the tuna was just the right about of spicy. I kind of wish they had mixed the avocado puree in with the tuna tartare so it wasn't just tartare on the top and a glop of avocado on the bottom. 

We both wanted to try their Uni Udon ($24) so we ended up getting two of them - I got mine with the big noodles and she got hers with the thin noodles. The dish features fresh uni, shiso, nori, and uni dashi sauce. You can opt for the small portion or the large portion - prices are the same either way. I opted for the large portion and it was a lot of udon. When the dish first comes, it looks like very little food but it's really all an illusion! The bowl is so big that it makes the portion size look small. In fact, there is a lot of udon in all the dishes and I almost didn't finish! The uni sauce was fragrant and intense - but not overly so. It tasted very fresh - not fishy at all. 

Since we're twinnies, we both also had their Kyoto Imperial Cocktail ($14), which contains Complices de Loire Sparkling Wine, Pear Nectar, and Ginger liqueur. I really enjoyed the cocktail! They actually have a very extensive wine, sake, and cocktail list so be sure to give it a look if you want a drink with your meal. 

We finished our meal with their Water Cake with Vanilla Ice Cream. I've had water cake before at Senya, so I came in with an expectation on how it would taste (basically nothing!). The addition of the vanilla ice cream was a nice touch and helped give the otherwise tasteless "cake" some sweetness. I don't think I'll have another water cake again - anywhere. Next time, I'm interested in trying their other green tea desserts. 

Service was attentive and we never felt rushed, despite the fact that there was a huge line of people waiting outside. I can definitely see myself returning for more udon dishes as it's getting cold in NYC and perfect udon weather!

Good stuff. 
Get the larger size bowl.  i wish they would let you know that there are two different sizes up front.  I had to inquire about getting extra noodles on the side for my son when the server said we can just get a larger bowl at no charge.

Honestly, I didn't think the noodles here were that much better than frozen udon you can get yourself from the market, but the service and ambience here is pretty nice.  I think it is worth a visit if you're a noodle fan, but be prepared to spend some $$$

I've tried the restaurant twice now. The first visit obviously made a positive impression (wanted to tried more dishes) for me to tried the restaurant again, but after the second time around, I'm not sure I would go out of my way to eat here again. Both times, I came pretty early and avoided the long wait that people talk about here.  

Here are my thoughts regarding the dishes I've tried:
Spicy tuna cone: presentation is adorable. It will probably take two bites or more to finish one but I did not like that the tuna (on the top) and the avocado (bottom half) are separate and cannot be tasted together. 
Sashimi salad - I liked the fish and the dressing. This one was my favorite dish. 
Oyako Don - you get bits and pieces of chicken but overall, it felt slimy (egg yoke) and too sweet for my taste. 
Sukiyaki Don - with thin udon. It was good at first, but I quickly got sick for the sweet broth. 
Tsuruton curry deluxe - with thick noodle. I ordered the large option. It was so huge. I was so excited! It was topped with tempura and katsu. The glutton in me had to order the large (since you don't have to pay extra), but it was way too heavy for me to even finish 1/2 of it. Again, the curry was too sweet for my taste. 
Green tea Mille Crepe cake - comes with a side of green tea icecream and whipped cream. Did not disappoint. 

The service was great, portions are generous (free upgrade to large), decor is nice, and location is convenient, but I personally found the food overall too sweet (I emphasize here my personal preference).

Good food, but pricey. I ate better tasting food at a fraction of the price.  The atmosphere is very relaxing and the interior of the restaurant is quite a sight to behold. It reminds me of the traditional noodle shops from the far east. The fried chicken appetizer was very good and the best thing on the menu. I guess this place is worth a shot if you are willing to spend the extra money.

At any given time there is an intimidatingly long line of people waiting outside (and the inside). However Tsurutontan has an enormous interior spacing without too too much wait you will surely get a table with an impeccable service. 

Loves:
Spicy cod with onsen egg udon (cold)
Salmon salad udon (cold)

Misses:
Curry udon (hot)
Tempura cold udon (cold with dip)

So far I really like half of the udon dishes and the other half felt like a miss. The loves and the untried ones will keep me coming back for more but the wait and the inconsistency are pushing me away. Otherwise the price, the service, the beautiful large Japanese plates and bowls, decor, space, and location are impeccable. Despite the popular demand I never felt rushed once I am seated. The waiter/waitress were always super friendly and how can you not love the presentation? I get to crush my own sesame seeds for the tempura set! 

Surely the waiter will also tell you know that you can get the LARGE set at the same price as the regular / small :) also get the skinny or thin udon and you would be pleasantly surprised! The standard thick udon you can get anywhere but the thin version is chewy but delicate and smooth but never saggy and it absorbs more flavor without picking up too much sauce (does this make sense?)

I have yet to try the creamy udon, which I know they smell wonderful and heavenly, as I always cast my envious gaze over at my neighbors' udon. I look forward to add to my list of loves!

Great ambience. I had uni cold udon with thin noodles, which is great but could get tired after awhile. Interesting taste for people who would like to be adventurous. But, I did not feel quite satisfied with the amount of uni. I'm expecting a little bit more since I am paying 24$.

As a huge fan of udon, I had to come try this place once I heard about it!

FOOD
SPICY TUNA CONE - Crispy nacho cone filled with spicy tuna and avocado at the end. The spicy tuna was not your typical mayo spicy tuna, but more of a finely chopped tuna tartare with creamy avocado to end the note. It was fun and playful, a definite must try.

SEARED SALMON SASHIMI - Lightly seared salmon topped with salmon roe and crunchy bits. I was not a fan of it because of the strong fish aftertaste, but my SO really enjoyed it as it was a big explosion of flavor for him. For me, it is a miss.

UDON - For first-timers, they have two sizes of bowls of udon (regular and deluxe) and they both charge the same price as listed on the menu. The difference is extra udon noodles, not extra toppings. One thing they emphasize is no take-outs for items you do not finish. So order only as much as you can eat. They also have two types of noodles - thick and thin. They suggest thick noodles with the hot dishes and thin noodles for the cold dishes.

SUKIYAKI UDON - Thin slices of meat with an onsen egg. The soup has a sweeter note and reminds me of gyudon with the thin slices of meat. The onsen egg is cold and not yolky at all, a little disappointing. The best part were the udon noodles, perfectly cooked with that chewiness I love. I would expect nothing less. For references, I ordered a regular for myself and was happily fulled. 

TSURUTON CURRY DELUXE - Chicken tonkatsu with shrimp tempura in curry. The curry is the traditional Japanese curry, but I would like to emphasize it's not curry broth. The curry was delicious, not spicy at all. However, it was super thick and each time I would try to grab the udon noodles, they would break. The tonkatsu and shrimp tempura were your typical Japanese food, nothing noteworthy. My boyfriend ordered a large and he was also happily fulled.

SERVICE 
Our waitress was very informative as we were first-timers. She went through the different options and explained the restaurant's practices. However, it went downhill from there. Our appetizers arrived promptly, but the udon entrees took way too long. We saw other tables having the same issue as far as two guests had the bowls and one was still waiting 15 minutes as she watched her friends eat their udon. As impressive as it was when they present us our udon bowls (they were huge!), we were waiting around too long. For references, the dining room was still full at 9:00pm and does not die down until 10:30pm. 

TIP FOR RESERVATION
You make the reservations through their website. Like OpenTable, they show the times that are available. If you do not see the time you want, you can have them notify you if anyone cancels or a time slot opens up. Also, they text you a reminder of your reservation and you can notify them through the same text if you may be running late. We were seated promptly after we arrive. 

I would probably return to this restaurant because I LOVE UDON, but I would give it some time for the restaurant to get into flow of things.

The atmosphere of this place was great. Great lighting and lots of seating. Quite crowded on Friday night, but worth going to! The portions were huge at a fair price and many options to choose from. There are also no pork based soups, which was a huge positive for my friend and I. The actual udon was nothing life changing, but this restaurant is definitely a great place to take a date or a friend!
Great location. Nice decor. Attentive staff on a moderately busy night. Bad beer pouring-- so much head. Tasty food.

Environment is very nice, dim light, modern designs for udon, they use A huge bowl for it!!!!!! And big portion also. They have two option of udon, thick and thin. I personally prefer thin one, so I don't feel bad for eating so much carbs, but I would recommend people to choose the thick one if u like chewy noodles. I love uni so much, so I order the uni udon, but it didn't reach my expectation. Hm. For the appetizer, I order the sukiyaki bun( hm normal, Baohaus is better and cheaper), and then the tofu!!!( must order! So good love it!). Yah. And also they offer lady m cake. Not sure cuz I eat it so often, so I found it normal.

Guys, the bowls here are comically large. Like... large to the point where it barely fits on the table kind of large. Depending on what dish you get though, the serving size can be absolutely massive, so I'm not complaining. We came here for my gf's birthday dinner and had a party of 14-16, which were comfortably seated in the upstairs area (would definitely recommend this spot for birthday dinners). Food was amazing and service was very pleasant. If I lived closer, I'd order one dish of whatever every night simply for takeout as each serving is more than enough for two!

Lets be real: udon does not get much love. It has been ramen this, ramen that for years, while simpler, healthier udon is ignored and left to be a side at mediocre sushi restaurants. But Tsurutontan is changing that! All the reviews had me terrified of a long wait, but at lunch time there was no wait at all. 

Tsurutontan hails from Osaka, where udon is revered just as much as it's fattier brother ramen. And for those that thought udon was light, think again. Udon at Tsurutontan comes in variety of different ways: hot, cold, thick, thin, large, larger... And the broths also very as well. 

Servings here are massive, gargantuan, ginormous. When they ask if you if you want the normal or large size, the normal is more than enough for two so I do not know why anyone would opt for the large, unless your planning to take it home for another meal. A friend and I shared two udons, the spicy soondubu jigae udon and the shrimp tempura udon. The spicy udon reminded me a lot of a ramen in terms of its richness. It was quite spicy! The udon with shrimp tempura was clean and soothing and reminded me of the classic udon flavors that I am accustomed to. 

Prices are fantastic, especially considering the portions. Service was a bit odd and impersonal and I did not like that they brought the two dishes out five minutes apart. 

They are taking the art of udon very seriously and for that it is worth trying.

Good flavored noodles, although a bit on the pricier end.

A friend and I stopped by on a Friday evening with a reservation for 5:45, and we were out within an hour. Given the high level of popularity, there seems to be a high emphasis on efficiency, which is good in terms of getting your food but might cause your drinks to come back after your appetizers (which is basically what happened). We split the spicy tuna cone and the wagyu beef over rice starters, the latter of which was tasty and tender and the former was more standard and nothing amazing. We had the beef noodle soup and the uni udon, both of which were quite good. My friend found the uni udon a bit too cold, probably making it a bit more of a summery dish, but the flavor of both were nice and the noodles pretty good.

I don't think I'd wait over an hour to eat here (when we left, a table for two was an hour and a half wait), but if you make a reservation, it's a decent meal.

While having my udon, I overheard 2 girls sitting right in front of me telling the waitress that they spotted flies in their bowls (both of them). So I started to feel concerned and try to see if I'm free from the buggy. Unfortunately, I also spotted a fly in my bowl, and right after I told the waitress, I found another one (so lucky I feel I can win the lottery). The manager came by and explained immediately which I think it makes me feel a bit better? They offered me another fresh bowl but I said no cause I already lost my appetite. Apparently it was a right decision because the girls just caught another fly in their "fresh" one. The way they managed this is fine -- they took the buggy udon off the bill and offered a free dessert. But I think I will never step in this restaurant again.

So glad that this place made its way to NYC!!! Their first inferential location!  I came here on a Friday night for dinner with 2 of my girl friends. The wait was a bit faster than expected, we waited for about an hour and got seated. 

They have quite a few of the crafted drinks which I find to be pretty good. I had the sake infused cocktail with st Germaine and some other stuff- it was very refreshing.

We started with spicy tuna roll as the app. If came in a crispy roll that looks almost like an ice cream cone. It was probably my fave compared to the main dish! 

For the main I had the sukiyaki udon. And one of my other friends has the uni udon. They all came in humongous bowls FYI! The sukiyaki one was good. More on the sweet side. Udon noodles were all not soggy and more firm. Which I like a lot. Also you are able to pick the type of udon you like.  Skinny or thick. we all had the thick ones. The uni udon was good as well. Not fishy at all and very fresh. The ambience is also good. And considering the fact that they are very busy we did not feel rushed at all. Overall it was a great experience and I would def come back to try more of their other stuff!!

Very delicious.

The chicken appetizer was VERY good. dark meat chicken very well cooked. Tender, juicy. Wasn't a huge fan of the tartar sauce but that was just a personal preference.

The spicy tuna cone appetizer was also good, but I thought the tuna did not taste as fresh as I wouldve wanted. Sort of tasted like fishy cheap spicy tuna rolls you get delivered.

Noodles... LOVED the sizzling sukiyaki Udon (thick noodles)... so so delicious! My favorite for sure.

The caviar udon was good, very different and interesting, but I likely won't order again. I was happy that I had tried it finally but not my favorite cup of tea.


The wait wasnt bad.. about 30 minutes

If I could eat udon for the rest of my life, I would. If I could eat Tsurutontan for the rest of my life, I also would. This place is sooooooo delicious!

I came on Sunday night around 6:50PM with my boyfriend. The waitress told us the wait would be 45 minutes, but we ended up only waiting for about 30 minutes. 5 minutes after we came in, 4-5 groups of people came in so we just beat the dinner rush.

Our waitress wasn't horrible, but she wasn't very welcoming either. From previous reviews and friends accounts of this place, I expected our waitress to help us out with our order, but she barely spoke to us.

My boyfriend got the Nippon Old Fashioned for drinks, and we ordered the Spicy Tuna Tartare Cone, Tsurutontan Deluxe, and Tsurutontan Curry Deluxe. 

Nippon Old Fashioned ($15): very strong and worth the price! i'm not a fan of old fashions, but my boyfriend really enjoyed it.

Spicy Tuna Tartare Cone ($12): AMAZING APPETIZER! It comes with four cones filled with tuna tartare, avocado puree, and purple shiso. The tune and avocado is layered so you have both with each bite you take. The cone is really crunchy and complimented the tuna tartare really well.

Tsurutontan Deluxe ($23): I really enjoyed this one. It is packed with ingredients and the broth is light but flavorful. There's a hint of sweetness in the broth, which I really enjoyed. The noodles are cooked perfectly too - soft but with a nice chew to it.

Tsurutontan Curry Deluxe ($23): LOVE LOVE LOVE SO MUCH. The curry is very flavorful and saucy, pork katsu is fried to perfection - crispy skin while keeping the pork juicy. The beef short plate is also delicious. I would rate this dish a 9.5/10, if they make it a little spicy it would definitely be 10/10.

For all noodle dishes, you can request for extra noodles at NO EXTRA COST! The only thing is you can't take it to-go, so you either finish your food and leave some to waste. We ordered extra noodles for both. My boyfriend was determined to finish his (and did) but he was definitely overstuffed at the end. I didn't finish mine, and I feel like I didn't even touch the extra noodles.

I know I'm definitely going to be eating here very often. This place is amazinggggggg.

Stopped in here on a Saturday night.  There was a 45 minute wait which was cool.  They will take your number and let you cruise around before they text you when the table is ready.  Only annoying thing, when we got back to sit, the place was maybe half full, which sucked.  But, the food was fantastic.  The fried chicken appetizer was the winner of all the apps we got.  The udon is amazing too.  Be ready to eat, the portions are massive.  If you get the "large" it means large and you will be stuffed.  

Pretty expensive but walked out happy and did I mention full!!

I love noodles, and with it being sweater weather, it's prime noodle soup season. That being said, Japanese noodle soups, or food in general, aren't typically known for their large (read: American) portions so they're never quiiiite large enough to satisfy me. I came here with those expectations, but oh man, was I pleasantly surprised.

The bowls here are massive. I was a little concerned that it was part optical illusion and that the bowl sizes were only meant to trick you into thinking you were getting a lot, but after eating my noodles, I was convinced otherwise. You can even order a large order at no extra cost. So yeah, I ordered a large sukiyaki udon, which was delicious. Yum yum yum. Broth was unlike other udon and ramen broths I've had and the beef was very flavorful. I also tasted my friend's truffle creme with mushroom, which was really good but a bit too rich for such a large bowl.

Aside from the udon, the place is surprisingly large. There are multiple levels and various types of seating for different groups, so intimate and large group dinners would work here. If you're hungry for noodles and lots of it, make a trip here.

I love this place! I have been here way too many times in the past two months and have had a pleasant experience every time. Short/no wait times, friendly and attentive staff, tasty food.

There are two types of Udon noodles you can get. Both options include a "free upgrade" to a large size of noodles:
- Thick noodles: This is probably the udon noodle you're used to seeing.
- Thin noodles: Get this and definitely ask for the upgrade to large! Tip: you can ask for noodles after you get your food if you don't get the big portion to begin with - this will also prevent the noodles from getting soggy. (I was told I can do this but I've been told by another Yelper otherwise so...)

Must gets include:
- Spicy Tuna Tartare Cones: So good and surprisingly fulling.
- Beef Udon ($16): A classic you can't go wrong with.
- Sizzling Sukiyaki Udon ($18): Not much meat in this dish but very filling, even the regular size. You can only get the thick noodles with this dish.
- Rosie Lychee ($13): I could drink like ten of these.

Other items I've tried:
- US Wagyu Shabu Udon ($19): Good but nothing spectacular.
- Mentaiko Ankake Udon ($17): Kind of like a seafood egg drop soup.
- Sukiyaki Udon ($19): A little too salty for me but still flavorful. 
- Uni Udon ($24): Cold dish with a really overpowering seafood taste.
- The Oni Within ($13) - Pass, pass, pass.

We sat all the way out of the way upstairs in an isolated little table with access only to our very awkward waiter.  Appetizers were serviceable if not memorable (tuna cones and uni/salmon roe dish).  My creamy mushroom udon was frankly gross - it was like a bowl of cream with an odd taste to it.  The regular udon soup broth my friend ordered was pretty flavorless, and the curry we tried, to share, was sickly sweet.  Also, when we asked to take our leftovers to go (I figured I could zsush it up at home to make it taste better since I'd barely eaten) we were told that the restaurant didn't allow leftovers because of something with bacteria?  Not even sure what that meant except that maybe we were to expect food poisoning? Fine if that's your policy, but then say it on the menu or to people when they're ordering - especially if two people are ordering three dishes, you need to let diners know.

This chain is from Tokyo. I went to the one in roponggi and now the one in union square area. The serve big bowls of udon. Uní fans would like the uní udon. Sukiyaki udon is a well balanced one with beef, veggies, and mushrooms. Check out the photos. This is reasonably priced, though pricier than ramen. Not much of a wait as they have a lot of seating. Note the large portion and regular portion are the same price.

Second review!
There are four of us and we made a 6pm reservation but had to wait about 20-25 minutes for our seats. They apologized but I was a little annoyed. For appetizers, we went with the Tsurutontan fried chicken. I liked the tartar sauce. We also had the duck breasts, which was ok, and the sea and truffle roll. I ordered the Truffle Cream & Mushroom and the pork cutlet on the side. Both were yummy with the udon being very heavy due to a cream base. Others at the table had the Tsurutontan deluxe, which looked like a good deal, uni pasta, and the kaisen don. I was told that the kaisen don was meh at best, with the deluxe being pretty good. Someone also ordered the poached egg tempura, which we were all curious. I was told it's interesting but not worth ordering again. 
Again, good food but the wait is always quite ridiculous.

Delicious udon! Yes, it's pricey however I upgraded to large size udon free of charge. It's stated on the menu. Two large udon is sufficient for three people. I love the decor. The tables are spaced out, so no over crowding and elbow touching. I had the deluxe udon and creme deluxe. Recommend if you get a creme base broth to go for thin noodle to avoid over-richness. My friends and I came here for lunch with reservation so no problem getting seated right away.

Yum. Yum. Yum. Yummy. Yum. 
Came here with my boyfriend and my sister for her 16th birthday and could not have been more pleased. The food was so yummy and the service was excellent. We were tempted to each order large size bowls since we were so hungry but the waiter advised against it, and luckily we listened because the servings are pretty satisfying, especially if youre planning to order appetizers, which you definitely should. We ordered dessert at the end and the server came out with a candle and sang happy birthday to my sister. I didn't even think he remembered! We certainly did not expect it but it was so nice that he did that. 

-wouldn't really recommend the desserts though, cept the green tea cake.

I was excited to try Tsurutontan, but the major disclaimer here is that I don't think I'm an udon fan; I'm more into rich broths, thin noodles and tender meat (like at Pye Boat Noodles or at ramen joints). 

Luckily, my friend made reservations; it looked super crowded, so I'm not sure how long the wait would've been otherwise. That said, we still had to wait a little; there was some confusion because we were originally expecting more people, but some people dropped out. Not sure if we had to wait because we were unclear, but they eventually seated us after 20 minutes without the complete party. 

I shared the wagyu beef udon and the uni udon with Raymond, and I thought the portions were moderate, bordering on small. Well, the uni bowl was definitely small; there were a few scant pieces of uni, some noodles and a light uni broth that was not as tasty as the actual uni. If I hadn't ordered wagyu beef, I wouldn't have known that the beef was any more tender than it was supposed to be; there were also only very scant portions of beef and I thought it was very mediocre. I was not really a fan of the wagyu beef udon overall and I looked over at my friend's deluxe bowl with envy. 

Service is mediocre; the waitress didn't really communicate clearly that there were different bowl sizes until Raymond asked how big the portion was. She said that there was a medium and a large one, and the large one just comes with more noodles - not more uni/other stuff. She didn't communicate this to the other people at my table, though, and automatically gave them large portions, which I thought was kind of weird because this isn't indicated on the menu at all. 

Overall, I would go elsewhere if I were in Union Square or craving noodles. It's not bad, and it's probably quite good if you like udon. I guess now I know I don't.

Let's start off with the positive -- when you walk in, the restaurant actually smells like dashi (broth).  And indeed the soup stock is delicious, and not overly salted as can often be the case when stock for udon or soba is mass produced.  The nabeyaki udon had a generous amount of meat, shrimp and vegetables, but it arrived in a bowl of broth so hot that even when ladelled into a smaller bowl, that bowl became too hot to hold.

And that created the first serious problem -- because the broth was too hot, the noodles were terribly overcooked and soggy.  I had ordered the traditional udon, thick noodles that need to be served slightly al dente.  Tsurutontan also offers thinner noodles, but I had not ordered them.  I was with a friend, and she ordered the thin ones while I ordered the thicker ones.  

When mine arrived, the wait staff assured me they were the "correct" ones, but this was impossible, since my friend and I both were looking at identical dishes.  Only when they brought me some thick noodles, which were al dente, to replace some of the soggy ones I had, did I realize that indeed I had been served the wrong dish.   I said so to my waitress but she made no attempt whatsoever to adjust this.  She only advised me that I could have as much thick udon as I liked, but she made sure to remind me that the restaurant's policy was to not allow customers to take food home. I find this very odd -- once you have been served food you are paying for, as far as I am concerned, it is yours and it is you who decides what to do with it.  

I could have pushed for an entire new dish as they had served me the wrong one, but I was with a friend and had no intention of embarrassing her. This dish was $20, though ordinarily it would cost $13 or so.  No apology, nothing.  Giving additional noodles is merely a way to overcharge.

And the wait staff needs a lot of work, they are very young and very inexperienced.  Once they clear away your dishes, at some point they should ask you if you are ready for your check.  And once they bring you the check, they might make some attempt -- within the space of 15 minutes -- to collect it.  It is also very strange for a Japanese restaurant to have no Japanese staff, at least not in the front of the house.

One can see why the prices are high.  The restaurant is enormous, with loud music suggesting it wants to be a club of some sort,-- it is named Tsurutontan Brasserie.  It is not a Brasserie really but it does needs lots of clientele to support a place of this size.  But an udon-ya is not an upscale restaurant, udon is a light meal, and a huge, fancy restaurant will only work if the udon is overpriced....and if management skimps on staff.  

I say, head to Sobaya, much better all around or to Udon West.

Umm... yum!!! 

I came for lunch with a friend and ordered the Tsurutontan Deluxe. It was served in a massive ceramic bowl that funnels the warm humid broth air directly up at you. The noodles have a deliciously fresh chewy tenderness that I couldn't stop eating.  Loved that this dish had little bits of egg floating in the broth. Quite the experience! 

Highly recommended on a cold crisp day when you want a comforting bowl of soup to fill and warm you up. Just deducted one star as the service was quite slow- it took us around 20 mins to get our Udon , and our waitstaff never refilled water or checked on us to make sure we were enjoying the food. Possibly they are still working through some kinks in the service.

We liked the fried chicken. Not too crazy about the tofu burrata. Sukiyaki was good. Like how the udon was chewy. My uni udon was cold noodle which didn't fit me well. Not going to order that next time. Curry udon was so so. I like curry with texture but this one was just a layer of mushy stuff. 

Their best part is the ambient and the giant udon bowls.  Cool place to chill with friends. 

We had a little episode as we texted the place ahead to let them know we were being 30 min late on our rsvp. No response. So we totally expected everything to be ok. However the md was not going to honor the rsvp when we arrived. Although she eventually gave in and gave us a table right away. So no hard feelings this time.

Takeaways:

--The people here are really really nice and just great about explaining the dauntingly vast and varied menu. 

--The large portion soups are for some reason the same price as the regular portion and can feed two. They give you extra bowls and spoons.

--The thick udon noodles are chewy and slurpable and quite good.

--The salad comes with this absolutely divine spicy tobiko dressing that you must try.

Came to this place for the first time. I had a first date, shes Japanese so she picked this place. 
- Romantic, yes. But the way the tables are set for couples is very awkward. You dont face each other, its more build like a family outdoor party. Your body faces foward and in order to talk to her, your head has to be turned all the time. I think i got a neck cramp afterwards. They do have facing tables but those are for a group of four. 
-  Appetisers and fantastic! It felt like i was back in japan years ago. We order the meat. 
- food. She picked for for and she ordered some kind of noodles soup. Now they have a regular size and a big size. Same price ( which i think is wrong, but that's just me i guess). When i ask how big the waiter just said its a decent size. So i went for it. When it came it was huge! I couldnt finished the entire thing. Now i been around the world and seen poverty. I hate wasting food. Since this place doesnt have take home bags i had to throw away all that food. That pissed me off. That was $20 into the garbage. 
- the waiter was very nice. He deserved the $20 tip. 

Would i come back? ....... Maybe. I rather have Vietnamese take out....

Delicious udon noodles near Union Square. Reasonably priced, huge portions, and great vibe. 

We got the Nabeyaki and Sukiyaki Udon bowls (both pictured). They were both excellent. In particular, the Sukiyaki was sweet in a very subtle, pleasant way. The portion sizes were humongous. They serve their udon in these huge bowls and with oversized soup spoons. You look ridiculous trying to eat it, but in a good way. Side note - you can ask for extra noodles (aka the large size) in your broth for the same price, but you aren't allowed to take anything home. 

We were most excited about the raindrop/water cake dessert. This is a gelatinous dessert shaped like a giant drop of water, and served with some sweet syrup, powder that was maybe sesame powder, and some ice cream on the side. Taste-wise, the actual raindrop only has a very faint sweet taste, but it's definitely novel and a lot of fun. And, if you're like me and missed it at Smorgasburg this year, it's a great way to try it without standing in line for it. 

Last random note - It might not seem like it, but I think this is actually a great place for young kids. Even though the decor/atmosphere is very dark, modern, and steel-y, the space is large and everyone was very accommodating of my friend who had a baby/stroller and I noticed that someone else with a young child got similar awesome treatment.

Raku is much better.  The noodles even though made fresh, didn't taste fresh.  There was way too much going on in the recommended deluxe and sukiyaki udon.  Portion sizes are big, but outside of that the taste was just alright.

Beautiful place with delicious food. 

Food:
Anago and tamago sushi - good
Uni udon - delicious
Sukiyaki udon  - very good; on the sweeter side
Green mille crepe cake from Lady M with green tea ice cream - delicious as always

This place is just YES YES YES! Some of the best udon I have ever had. Inside is super chic and pretty big. Very modern setting. Their udon is all hand made and you can definitely taste it. Their udon noodles are SUPER chewy and tastes fresh.

We ordered:
Spicy Tuna Cone: So delicious, fresh tuna and has guac inside. Crunchy and tasty
Tsurutontan Créme Deluxe: Very creamy and delicious. Udon was amazzzzzzzing. This is one of their recommended dishes
Uni Udon: SO GOOD! The best I ever had in the USA. I have tried various uni udon in SF and LA and it does not compare. Recommend using thin udon. It's so fresh and creamy, thinking about it makes me hungry!

I would definitely come here again when I am back in NY, no doubt.

I usually don't go for udon amongst other types of noodles because they're really filling and they get really mushy and disintegrate when they're soaked in broth for too long. However, this place changed my opinion of udon.

We made a reservation on a Thursday night for when it opened for dinner and were seated right away. The staff were friendly and helpful. Our waiter explained how the menu was organized and recommended that we get the thick udon for hot broth and thin for cold udon. Every item on the menu looked mouthwatering. In the end, we went with the Mentaiko Caviar Creme Udon with thick noodles and Uni Udon with thin noodles, with extra servings of udon for both (it's free!). 

Uni Udon - delicious! The uni was fresh and creamy. The thin noodles were chewy while the uni melted in my mouth. Make sure to give it a good mix first so every strand of noodle is coated with some uni. 

Mentaiko Caviar Creme Udon - this was tasty as well even though it wasn't what I expected. There was a big scoop of mentaiko however the taste was overpowered by the creme sauce. Nonetheless, the cream sauce itself still tasted really nice and the thick udon was soft and chewy. If you want more of the mentaiko flavor, I would recommend trying the Mentai Caviar Udon (cold) instead with an onsen egg - I had something similar in Japan and it was delicious!

We ended the night with the Raindrop Cake. I've seen it all of social media so I was excited that I finally got to try it. The cake itself is like regular jello but topped with soy flour and black sugar syrup, and paired with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. The dessert tasted nice, but the excitement really stops at the fact that it's clear and it jiggles. I'm glad I got to try it though.

Overall, the restaurant ambiance, food, and service were great. I would definitely come back to try the other items on their menu!

Great service! Some amazing dishes. Some just ok. 
A bunch of friends and I shared a few and enjoyed some more than others. 
The wait was non existent because i came before dinner started at 5. I don't believe it's worth a wait... the waiter was amazing in explaining dishes to us. But during our dinner the kitchen sent about 3-4 dishes that we didn't order. We kept sending them back. Looks like they have some organizing to do... 
wagyu beef with uni sashimi. I literally could have just eaten that all night. That was one of the dishes we got another plate of. And while tempted to just take it. I couldn't do it... karma... 
loved the thick and thin noodle choices and suggestions. 
the fried chicken with the mysterious pink/purple sauce. Pretty good!
Uni and salmon roe sashimi... ok... can skip
Still best homemade udon place was in Hawaii... but since that's a little far... this place will have to do...
Udons we got one with mentai and poached egg. The best one of the night. 
Uni udon was ok. 
And the sukeyaki beef udon. Friend got this. Was soooooo sweet. We couldn't do it. 
But the wagyu beef and uni sashimi... i'll be back for you.

But that raindrop dessert thing? Yeah. I don't get the hype...

The udon is so yummy here. I've been a couple times and tried these hot variations: the creme deluxe, curry wagyu, sukiyaki and spicy soondobu jigae. The server recommended think noodles for the hot udon so I went with it. These noodles are like tasty blank canvases that takes on different flavors of color, depending on which broth you choose. 

One thing that did not score the last star was the standardization you can taste from a chain. If you have had udon from Raku you would know what I am talking about. It could be all in my head but nonetheless, very delicious udon and I will be back!
Went here for the first time this October, and absolutely loved their noodles! Great beef buns too.

Came here with a friend on a weekday for an early dinner. The restaurant actually houses a good number of tables, but quickly filled up by 7:30. 

We started with a special appetizer that the waiter recommended - the wagyu beef, which was wrapped over uni. Highly recommended. It was perhaps the best part of the meal. 

In terms of the main course, my friend got the cold mentaiko caviar udon with thin noodles and I got the mentaiko caviar cream udon with thick noodles. The cold noodles were delicious and quite refreshing. I would recommend the cold noodles with thin noodles. The hot udon was very rich and creamy, but not as heavy as I expected. I did have a little trouble finishing the entire bowl. 

The restaurant also offers items in two sizes - regular and large - at the same price! We both ordered regular sizes which was perfect, but if you are feeling ambitious and hungry, definitely go for the larger size.

I came here for dinner last night with a friend. We started with the tempura shrimp which was very tasty and two hot teas (the hot tea is free and very good)! For dinner we shared a deluxe beef Udon. It was tasty but nothing spectacular. The ambiance is GREAT. They sat us at the booth since the table wait was significantly longer. Eating at the booth was fine. A little difficult to concentrate on our conversation with everything going on around us but fine. I can see myself coming here alone for lunch or dinner and enjoying the booth seating. The staff is very friendly. We ended the night with a water cake for dessert. I'd seen photos of water cake on instagram for a place in LA and was thrilled that this place served it. It's definitely something everyone should try and I would order again.  Overall, great experience. Minus one star for the food not being a little more special.

I thought my curry deluxe udon was excellent. The most important part of a bowl of udon is the noodle itself and theirs are soft and delightfully springy. The curry was pretty solid with the slices of beef actually being the highlight over the entire katsu cutlet and two shrimp tempura. Also for some reason the large and regular are the same price (it's just more noodles not more toppings).

I can't do 5 stars because at $25 for my bowl, that's a lot to spend on udon (which in most places is $8-14). While they do give you quite a bit and the quality is solid, it's still a tough proposition. That being said, I'll probably go back. Also, I don't really dig the hip but too loud music. If i wanted to go to the club, I'd go to the club.
This place is amazing. It was so fresh and clean. The booths were very spacious. I really enjoyed the decor and the food is amazing as well.

I was really looking forward to this place since I heard really good things, some friend even claim this as the best Udon place in the city. I walked out of there feeling a little cheated. 

Reservation was not easy to get, but they do accept walk-ins so if you get here early enough, there should be no problem. 

We ordered the Tsurutontan Deluxe and Creme Deluxe, as well as fried chicken and sukiyaki bun as appetizers. Fried chicken was tender and juicy, don't let the odd color-ed sauce scare you, it actually tasted pretty yummy. Sukiyaki bun was a fail, meat was dry and chewy, and it's lacking some serious sauce. I ended up dipping the bun in the fried chicken sauce, which made it ten times better. 

Now come to the udon. If you are thinking of getting anything creme deluxe, just know that there's no broth. It's more like some heavy cream than soup. There's chicken/salmon/caviar in my creme deluxe, so you'd think the cream base would taste good. Noooo, it was VERY bland, not sure if it's the intention? Noodle was good, but without a flavorful base, it's just bleh. On the other hand, my husband's Tsurutonta Deluxe was actually pretty yummy, broth was light but flavorful. I ended up eating his because I just couldn't stand the tasteless creamy noodle in my bowl. 

I was thinking about giving it a two star, but bumped it up to three because of our nice waitress and almost everyone working there was very friendly. That still doesn't change the fact the food was inconsistent. This place is what I'd call a prototypical "overrated" restaurant.

This is like the ippudo for udon I feel. The interior is more modern and relatively big for a New York restaurant. If you don't have a reservation, be prepared to wait. I would say that it's worth the wait though! 

The food is delicious! I came with my cousins and we had the uni cold noodles and a creamy truffle mushroom one. I actually don't recommend the uni one since there's not a lot of uni in there and the flavor is quite bland. The cream based one on the other hand is delicious! I thought it would be super heavy but not at all! The bowls also come in regular or large size...for the same price. The difference is that you get a little more noodles in the large.

Definitely will come again!
Absolutely loved it. Had party of five ordered 4 different dishes- everyone loved their dish - had uni cavier, sea and truffle spicy soondubu and tsurutontan loved them all favorite was the soondubu

Such a disappointment..... This review is about the mushroom creme udon... NO truffle in the dish at all (probably truffle oil???) and really tiny bit of mushrooms only! Really, like nothing stands out in this dish. And the thin udon was a bit too soft, not firm:(  A waste of money and time :(

I came here with my friends after watching a movie a few blocks down. We got here around 8pm on a weekday so no there were no reservations taken. The wait wasn't too bad -- only about 5-10 minutes long. We were taken to the dining area, which is on a slightly lower level (the ceilings are kind of low).

Service - Our server, Marco, was incredible! He was extremely sweet and friendly. He gave us detailed descriptions and recommendations and helped us piece together a marvelous meal with dishes that complement one another.

Food - Oh man, where do I start! Every bite was like heaven, from the appetizers to the main entrees to even the drinks! Since this IS a udon joint, ordering a bowl of udon is a must! They have hot udons and cold udons. They come in two sizes (regular and large), both of which are the same price. The only caveat is that you cannot take leftovers home. So make sure you pace yourself well so that you don't try to stuff the last bites in your mouth because you don't want to waste the amazing food!

Truffle Creme with Mushroom - This is a warm udon in a mushroom truffle broth that is very creamy and rich, slightly sweet, and extremely delicious. I can't even begin to describe how good this is. All I can say is to make sure you order this dish!

Tsuruton Curry Deluxe - Shrimp, tempura, pork cutlet, and beet in a light curry broth. Even though I'm normally not a big curry fan, I found the soup to be so creamy and really good!

Uni & Caviar - For $18, you get a decent portion of uni and ikura over rice with some kind of jello broth. It's pretty fresh and definitely recommended for uni lovers!

Tatsuta Fried Chicken - This dish was also very good. I like how it comes with a pink/purple tartar sauce, which I found rather unique.

The drinks are also yummy!

Came here with the Beau on Saturday at around 2pm. We were told there was around 15 min to 30 min wait so we gave the hostess our name and number and walked around in the open market. We didn't have to wait too long and we received our text message saying our table was ready within 20 min. We were seated promptly and we ordered the tsurutontan deluxe and the  creamy mushroom udon. We both got large bowls with thick noodles. The food I would give a 4, and the service a 3.5. My bf's udon came out close to 15 min before mine did, and he definitely eats way faster than I do, and if he waited for mine, his bowl would have gone cold. They may need to work on getting the bowls out closer together as it seemed like most other tables had the same issue. I would definitely recommend the tsurutontan deluxe udon, but not so much the creamy mushroom. I really wanted to like it, but the broth was more of a sauce, and it was way too thick, not rich in flavor, and unimpressive. I would come back to try their other udons, though.

Beautiful, cool place to dazzle out-of-towners, and solid choice for a first date, as the place certainly looks impressive, and you'll be likely sitting alongside your date. Prices aren't cheap by any means, and for that price you can get a tastier bowl of ramen almost anywhere else in the city.

Udon is not ramen, though: if you're expecting the same kind of rich broth and explosion of flavor, you'll be disappointed.

We came here without a reservation during lunchtime on a Sunday. The place was definitely very busy, but the line moves quickly, and we barely had the time to order drinks at the bar that our table was ready.

We tried the Tsurutontan Deluxe and the Oyako Don with chicken. First of all, the udon noodles are really good: thick and chewy, a real pleasure to eat. Moreover, most of the dishes come in huuuuge bowls the size of a small sink; as beautiful as they are impressive. The broth of both dishes was pretty mild; the tempura in the Tsurutontan Deluxe was good, and I certaily suggest to take it out of the bowl and put the various pieces on a side dish unless you like your tempura soggy. The chicken in both dishes was very bland, and in retrospect I would probably get the Okayo Don with salmon instead of chicken. Overall, outside the noodles, there was nothing particularly striking with these dishes.

Service was good; attentive and fast despite the place being very busy.

This place has a hip, cool ambiance that would be good for a winter date night that won't break the bank.  The concept of huge bowls and sharing is always fun and festive.  They also have a pretty decent cocktail and whiskey selection for a reasonable price.

The food here is just okay - nothing is really exceptional except the classic udon noodles.  
-Veggie tempura udon was awesome.  Tempura is sooooooooo crispy and light.
-Spicy tuna cones are a cool concept, but they're just okay.
-Don't go for any of the uni dishes - they charge up the wazoo for ity bity portions.  The uni pasta is basically a giant bowl of flavorless noodles topped with 2 tiny piece of mediocre uni.
-Sukiyaki udon was way too sweet - pass.
-Other reviews say the large portion is free, but their menu says that they up charge $5 for extra noodles.  Maybe they changed?

Service is prompt and friendly.  All in all, good if you just want udon noodles and nice ambiance.  If you are looking for really good Japanese food, go elsewhere.

My dear fellow udon fanatics- this is what we've been waiting for!! A restaurant that specializes in udon with great appetizers will always make me come back for more. 
Their menu offers sooo many special udons to choose from and to make me go crazier, they offer super-sized upgrade for free. Of course, you cannot take it home after and yes, one of my friends tried to ask for a take out box and another yes, they adamantly refused. 
So far I've tried curry udon, tsukiyaki udon and mentaiko caviar udon. My personal favorite is mentaiko caviar udon! It is absolutely delicious. The dish is so flavorful and even though it's cream based udon, you will never get sick of the taste. For me, tsukiyaki udon didn't appeal to me at all because of its excessive sweetness. Curry udon is also very good but it would never top mentaiko udon, so go with that!
As for appetizers, I tried their rolls and spicy tuna cones and both are excellent. You really can't go wrong in this place except tsukiyaki udon. 
Price is a bit steep but worth.

An absolutely great place if you like udon noodles.  Very cool vibe and friendly, efficient staff.  We were greeted as soon as we walked in the door.

The food: curry udon was quite good.  The curry broth wasn't too thick, but had enough consistency to let you know that it was Japanese based curry.  The noodles were slightly al dente, which I like.  Be careful with the curry broth though - it will splatter and get on your clothes.  Ordered the spicy tuna cone for an appetizer.  It was very good, although a bit pricey for what it was.

Service: very friendly and quick.  A very nice and pretty lady named Nancy came by to make sure that we were being taken care of.  Excellent overall - kudos to the staff.

Value: for what you get, this is a good value.  You can probably go somewhere a bit more divey to get udon noodles, but given the ambiance and quality here, this place represents a good value for the noodles.  The appetizers may be a bit less of a value when considering the portion size, but are unique enough that you will want to try it out.

Stopped in for lunch today and was certainly underwhelmed by the udon.  The space is quite chic and cool... I was a many time visitor to Union Sq Café so it was interesting to see the space in its new clothes.  Started with shisito peppers, pretty good standard fare.  I had the Nabeyaki udon and my companion the chicken udon.  I found the broth to be less than spectacular.  The noodles were fine but nothing I'd go out of my way for.  The chicken in my soup was overboiled like it had been in the pot for way too many hours.  In the end nothing so special.

After happening upon Pete Wells' review in the NYT, my wife and I decided to make an impulse stop for dinner here last weekend once we finished wandering through the holiday market in Union Square. Even though we got there shortly before opening time for dinner (5 PM), there was already a decent line building. Capacity isn't really much of an issue - this is where Union Square Cafe used to be located - but it does fill up quite fast, so much so that by the time we left, there were a decent amount of folks waiting at the front for a seat.
