The decor has a much more cosmopolitan feel to it, and with contemporary pop/electronic music blaring in the background, you won't mistake this for a NYC institution (yet). We ended up sitting in the dining area slightly below ground level, and the layout is tables all around, with a center area that is divided up into 2 seats per party - a very handy way of making it easy for couples to sit together in a relatively space-efficient manner. Service was generally solid overall, although we had to ask to get a spoon for the broth.

My main gripe about the food here, simply put, is that the prices aren't justified, and perhaps that's a function of the rent (and why Danny Meyer moved out). $25 for a bowl of noodles just seems overdone...I used to think Ippudo and its $15-16 ramens were expensive, but this definitely takes the cake. The bowls themselves looks quite big as well, but the amount of noodles you get - along with the amount of broth - isn't necessarily a larger quantity. The nice thing is that you can order a larger portion of noodles for free (which my wife did), but it still didn't make it feel like it was a $20-25 bowl of udon. She had the wagyu shabu udon, which in all fairness was quite good - the thin slices of meat cooked in the light broth were quite delicious, and the large udon was good for soaking in the flavors as well. I went with the uni udon, which is cold and served without any broth. It's pretty good overall, even if I felt the amount of uni served on top was a bit on the light side. The sesame seeds add a nice crunchy texture to each bite, but given the overall price (this is one of the more expensive ones) - I didn't think it was worth it. I really did enjoy the ribeye appetizer; the steak is cooked exceptionally well on its own and has great flavoring, with some rich yuzu ponzu sauce on the side to dab it in. Very good but still overpriced ($20 for 7-8 small slices of meat).

The food here is good, as is the udon and the appetizers. I come back and visit again purely on the merits of the food (the drinks, maybe less so; my cocktail 'Autumn in Osaka' was poorly executed), but the price simply feels like the store is out to make a buck than deliver you a homey Japanese meal. While I would come back, it's definitely less frequently than I would visit a Japanese noodle spot like Totto.

Great decor, contemporary Japanese.
There was a line of about 10 people before it opened at 5:00. We found out they take reservations so next time we'll call ahead.
We ordered a special of spicy & sour udon which was delicious on a cold evening.
We ordered a cucumber salad, a beer & 2 bowls of udon and it came to $70 with tip. Very expensive. We spent 8 years in Japan & I can't recall udon this expensive. However, this place has taken Udon to a higher, deliciously creative level.

Yum yum yum! 
The avid noodle lover (especially udon) that I am has been nagging me to come here for the longest time ever!
Arrived just after 12pm on a Saturday afternoon and was pleasantly surprised that there was virtually 0 wait time! 
Once seated, the menu graciously splayed in front of us, dilemma set in with the numerous deliciously appealing udon options. After much deliberation (and hard life choices to make) settled on the sukiyaki udon. 
There was a slight lag in our orders getting to the table but our waitress kept us happily and thoroughly informed. But let me tell you the noodles were worth the wait! Large steaming bowls of piping hot udon larger than my hand (and face!) 
The bowls are deceivingly large, but not in a bad way. It`ll fill you up with the perfect amount; you won't leave hungry. 
Will definitely come back to try their cream udon!

Had dinner reservations and was seated within 10 mins. Had spicy shrimp tempura. It was delicious. Ordered the large kitsune udon. Simply flavorful and delicious. Reminds me of my time in Japan. Only thing is I feel like I need a high chair to eat the large udon dish. Definitely a must try.
Walked out after having 2 sips of cold Udon I had to wait 30 minutes for because the waiter was too busy on his phone or flirting with another waitress. USC would be disappointed

Came here for a friend's birthday with a group of 15 and service was fantastic. The waiters were all very attentive and pleasant. I ordered the beef curry udon. I went for a larger udon but definitely should've gone for a regular because there was so much food. Shed a tear because it was so good but I just couldn't finish it all. Will definitely be coming back!

Can noodles ever get four stars?  Maybe not. But this is close. S really a 3 1/2. Busy, intense udon temple and gracious wait staff (thank you Sabrina). Huge portions will allow you to split and half price of the not too expensive experience.

yummmmmmmmmmmmy! I really want to give this 4 1/2 stars given a couple of caveats below, but if I'm thinking of the food at the forefront (as a good yelper should), this one's a keeper.

We just went and I'm already plotting my return. One of the top 5 noodle experiences we've had, and after a summer in Japan and a visit to every noodle haven in NYC, I feel amply qualified in that declaration :) The sizzling sukiyaki thick udon is just heavenly. Super umaminess with a deep, deep soul. The texture of the udon was spectacular. Gosh that was a great bowl.  

Two issues that I feel I must report which were sufficiently problematic to warrant a star removal: cocktails were really meh. My lychee cocktail tasted like a bar of soap in my grandmother's bathroom. It was way too heavy on the rosewater. My husband's gin and ginger beer number was really blah.  

Our server was lovely but they took a TREMENDOUS liberty with the whole "enjoy the plates as they come out because we serve things as they are ready!" line.  My husband and I shared my entire steaming hot, slow to eat bowl before someone came over and said - oh! I should check on the other dishes. My husband's came out promptly after (curry udon, very very good if you are a fan of the style - wish they would leave the tempura on the side so as not to get soggy in the kitchen before it makes it to the table) and my kids came out 10 minutes AFTER THAT. No, no, no. You do not bring the kids meal 30 minutes after the grownups have gotten theirs.  That is seriously bad form, and I could tell this was not intentional.  

We also had to ask for forks, extra bowls etc. for our kids which, I get it, this place isn't intended for children, but kids exist so they should help parents out and encourage our visit by making that extra efforts. Ours were not the only little ones there, and it would be a benefit to the other patrons if you could time the kids dishes better, ask about forks and other components, maybe provide some version of minor kid entertainment like crayons and a placemat (we brought our own things, but given the 30 minute wait for them to get their food, we went through all we had while we were trying to eat our own meal - thus the reason most places bring the kids stuff out first - it makes it far easier for adults to enjoy their meal if the kids have already been served).

I also wish they would simply consider a kids portion of anything on the menu. Our kids split a dish but the bowl was the size of a sink, making it really difficult for them to fight for space on the small table. My daughter spilled an entire bowl of warm broth in her lap because the bowl was perched on the edge of the table given the huge shared bowl.  Again, I understand this place isn't intended for kids and that their restaurants in Japan likely don't make such accommodations, but why not make it easier for everyone? I promise you will earn the loyalty of locals if you do make them feel welcome to come with or without kids.

That said, do not miss a trip to this ridiculously good udon place.  Make a reservation, even for lunch. We booked that morning and were sat within 5 minutes. Walkins were waiting 30-40 minutes at 1:45 pm.

I'd rate this place about a 4, similar to what market value has it. My friend was raving about this place and how great it is so considering there wasn't much of a wait, we decided to try it out. Firstly, the interior decor is just fantastic. High ceilings, open bar with very intricate architecture. I remember the ambiance just 

Onto the food, I wasn't blown away. I started off with the shishito peppers, fried chicken, spicy tuna tartare cone and wagyu sushi. Not JUST me, I'm not THAT fat... I was with 4 people. Yes, I have friends. My favorite was the shishito peppers, it was just a great light appetizer that had these flakes on top which were savory; peppers not too spicy but some had a good kick. There's this very sour sauce that contrasts quite well with the texture and heat of the peppers. The Spicy Tuna TarTare Cone, my second favorite, was tasty, It was served in a box with uncooked rice, I decor thing, and the spicy tuna itself was pretty decadent. However, I thought the cone was a bit too oily and it wasn't as 'crispy' as I expected? It's acceptable but it's very brittle. The Wagyu sushi tasted like a thin piece of beef, nothing special. Fried chicken was good, pretty tender, but wasn't crazy about the pink sauce. 

I ordered the Tsurutontan Deluxe. When ordering Udon, you get to option to choose between regular and large, no price difference. You're also given the option between thin and thick udon noodles. I got the large, duh, and got the thick udon. I didn't think much of the dish, and it seems to be their special? I liked the texture of the udon, the dish tasted very 'basic.' Wasn't much unique flavor and I got sick of the dish about a quarter-way in. Wish there was some heat option or something else to give it a bit more 'oomph.'

All in all, I think this place is great to try out. The decor and ambiance are really fantastic. The food I think could be better - it's definitely "American-ized" to be tasty for the majority of people so I'm sure other people really would enjoy this. Worth noting, you cannot take your udon to go if you don't finish! Definitely come through and check it out for yourself.

Absolutely amazing udon place. The restaurant has nice decor, each table is somewhat in its own little "section" of the restaurant. The staff are all very friendly and eager to help. 

As an appetizer, I had the smashed cucumber salad (? not entirely sure of the name) and it was delicious. As a cucumber lover myself, I enjoyed the sauce and sesame seeds. I also had the cauliflower tempura, which was very good. I really liked the grated parmesan on top of the cauliflower, it added a saltiness to the dish. We also ordered the peppers, which I found to be a little plain (in flavor) but delicious all the same. 

For the main course, I ordered the Vegetable Tempura Udon with thick noodles. Warning, the udon bowls are large and do look extremely intimidating, but the portion itself is average size. The noodles were the perfect firmness and length, it was very easy to pick up and eat. The tempura was a little too oily for my liking (however I'm not a huge fan of tempura), and I enjoyed the eggplant tempura the most. 

Overall I had a wonderful experience at this restaurant and will come again when I'm in town!

Heard about Tsurutontan through an article in the NYT. It was recommended.
We had a reservation.
Space is big, and we thought the interior design was very good.
Our waitress was very attentive and on top of her game.
We shared some appetizers: spicy tuna roll, shishito peppers and the beef buns. I would give the appetizers 4 stars. Slightly underwhelmed by the spicy tuna roll.
Then we had the noodles. My friend ordered the cream and truffle, and I had the Sukiyaki (beef plate).
Both were excellent. The udon was the right consistency and the brith was flavorful.
Overall very good dinner at a good price.
Would definitely go back

Great service and udon at the new Japans Udon shop in the old Union Square Cafe space. Tried some of the cocktails. I particularly loved the Osaka Sunrise. I ordered the Duck udon with extra noodles (there's no extra charge). Delish.  Service was friendly and accommodating.

Oh man, where do I start.  I am so glad my friend Claire introduced me to this udon brasserie because it literally has become one of my go-to places for udon.  It is a very large space, but it can get quite crowded so I do recommend a reservation if possible.  I did eat at another udon joint just days earlier, and there is definitely a difference between the two.  Truthfully, it depends on the mood you are in.  Tsurutontan is your special, deluxe, fusion-not-fusion type of decadent udon.  It isn't the type of udon that you can find in your average izakaya since they elevate it in both serving style and type.  For one, they not only have your traditional type udon served in dashi broth, they have a slightly richer broth that is "flavored" dashi.  Then they totally explode your mind with creme-based udon, curry-based udon, and then cold udon.  #mindblown . They make all the noodle from scratch at the beginning of the day and for health purposes, you cannot take any of the extra noodles or dishes home.  Bring an appetite or let it go people.  There is a plus for those who have the stomach space: you can get an XL portion with more udon noodles (but again, you cannot take it back).  The normal serving is already pretty hefty, especially for light to moderate eaters like myself.  I did have a guy-friend come into town and he was pretty stuffed after a regular portion.  This sits a little heavier especially if you order a creme-based or curry sauce as well.  The thing I have managed to indulge in include:

-  wagyu beef sushi with fresh Cali uni
-  creme deluxe udon
-  curry deluxe udon
-  uni cold udon

This is from two visits to this restaurant hence the three udon dishes.

Wagyu Beef with Uni sushi appetizer: initially on my first visit, this was a special.  On the second visit here, it was so good I added the uni since it wasn't offered as a special.

PROS:
- melts in your mouth: literally the fat and richness of wagyu beef is the best that I've had
- the combination with fresh uni is unbelievable.  This alone kicks it up to five stars.
- whatever little jelly cube they put on top, it adds that extra burst of richness to the bite that goes all over your mouth.  
CONS: 
-for the price, it's a slight stab to the wallet, especially as an appetizer.  I want to say it's like $10 for the sushi and an additional $10 for the uni add-on?  For the flavor, it's out of this world and I think my friend Carlos would say it's worth it.

---------

Creme Deluxe Udon

PROS:
- super filling: definitely shareable
- good flavor: not overwhelmingly cheesy like a lot of sauces can get but there is definitely a distinct cheese flavor meaning they didn't skimp out on it
- goes well with the udon: as a lighter type of noodle but still with a smooth surface, it holds enough sauce but isn't overwhelmingly heavy

CONS:
- almost too heavy and rich: we couldn't eat anything else after this dish because it was so heavy.
- too much sauce compared to the other ingredients such as the shrimp and meat - would also prefer some more vegetables.

--------

Curry Deluxe Udon

PROS:
- also super filling, very shareable as well
- great for curry lovers, sauce was even and no chunks of roux noted
- good amount of sauce to toppings ratio
- the katsu was ON POINT: not too dry and not overly burnt or overcaked with panko

CONS:
- very rich: eat this last before any lighter types of dishes such as classic udon or even the cold udon dishes

--------

Uni Udon

PROS:
- nice and light, no heavy sauces
- good uni and seafood flavor: you have to like seafood and definitely love uni though
- doesn't sit so heavily after the meal is over
- uses thin udon noodles so that it is able to soak the sauce a little better
- more fresh uni on top!

CONS:
- The uni is slightly more firm than the Hokkaido uni I've had at some top notch sushi restaurants: this makes it slightly harder to break up and mix evenly in the udon.  It's doable, but just requires a little more work and still yet not quite evenly displaced.  

I would totally come back just for the Uni Udon truthfully.  I definitely prefer lighter dishes over heavier dishes but I can see myself coming here on a super cold day and getting a cream based udon, but it'd definitely have to be with someone because there's no way I can finish something like this by myself.  I'm totally a fan.  The wagyu beef and uni sliders sold me with the uni udon.  Definitely check them out!

While I was sad to see Union Square Cafe have to vacate this location, I was excited to try to this new udon place.  When it first opened it sounded like there were crazy lines, so I didn't really want to go and have to wait forever, so I held out a bit, and then went on a weekday for lunch.  You can make a reservation on Resy, so the day before I was able to get a reservation for 2 at 1 o'clock.  The bones of USC are still there you can tell, but the decor is completely different.  The place wasn't packed when we got there, but throughout the meal the room we were in really filled up. 

We were seated at this long communal table in the middle of the room, but it was kind of sectioned off, so it was good for parties of two.  We were seated next to each other and on the side there was another group. There was something dividing the two sides of the table, so it wasn't really too bad. You could see what the other people were eating (I like to see what people are having) but you didn't feel like you were sitting with them. The menu was pretty big, with options of noodles, hot or cold, with or without soup, appetizers, and there looked to be some sushi options.  We browsed the menu, full of pictures, and decided to start with spicy tuna tartare cones, and I got the sizzling sukiyaki udon which the waitress informed me didn't come in a broth and was just noodles.  I thought about it and decided to still order it.  You get the options of thinner or thicker noodles, and we asked which they suggested and they said thicker, so we went with that.  I forgot exactly what my dad got, but his came with broth, and the bowl was huge!  All the bowls are pretty big, but the ones that come in broth look ginormous.  The only issue though is that they don't let you take home leftovers, so don't go in thinking you take the rest of it with you to go.  

The spicy tuna cones came and they were pretty good. The bottom of the cone is filled with avocado, which I'm super picky about, so I didn't eat the entire thing, but the tuna was really good.  Then my big bowl of udon came, and it was very good!  It was a cold rainy day, so pretty much the perfect food for that. I think I finished it all, but if not I came pretty close. We didn't look at the dessert menu (breads is across the street!) since we were pretty full after our meal.   

Overall I enjoyed it.  The service was pretty good, we didn't have a wait, and the food was good. I definitely plan on coming back this winter!

Two main points:

1) On a Saturday evening, we were told it was going to be an hour wait. After an hour we followed up patiently - the response from the hostess was "it will be around 5 minutes, do you mind closing out your tab at the bar?".  We reply, "ok, great in agreement and we are just standing right there".  
After 20 minutes, we follow up and the hostess' response in a condescending tone, "it's a Saturday night, you're the next table, it will be 5 minutes".  Poor response and a dialogue begins. 

2) Arriving at our table of 4, our waiter takes our orders of drinks, 3 appetizers and 4 entrees all at the same time (as we saw the menu while we were waiting).  
The entrees arrived earlier than expected - that is where anything resembling service ended.
The entrees begin arriving after 10 minutes so we inquire about the missing appetizers - the waiter was unapologetic and said there was no record of the order.  Very disappointing.

I am/was a regular and the udon dishes are generally good and cater to most tastes.  After we asked to see the manager, he apologized and gave a couple of free desserts but I don't think this was adequate - we still never got the appetizers (never offered but it was far too late).  Extremely poor service from start-finish.
AMAZING! Pricey but quality and ambience make it worth it. Authentic and extremely delicious udon noodles

I took one star off because of their customer service & wait time. 

Came here on a Saturday night around 6pm. It was very busy with lots of people waiting. The hostess told us that it was a 30-45 minute wait, which we were ok with because I was very excited to try this place. We were seated after an hour. 

After ordering dinner, my friend ordered a soda and I asked for just water. The waitress came very quickly with the soda but didn't bring my water. I reminded her about it. I finally got my water 15 minutes later after reminding the waitress two more times. The food took awhile as well. We received the udon approximately 40 minutes after we ordered.

I ordered the Tsurutontan Deluxe while my friend ordered the Sukiyaki Udon. They were both very tasty. LOve Love LoVe the Udon noodles!!! Love that it has that springy resistance thing going on with each bite. And the bowls are far generous portions (I think 2 people can share one bowl and be satisfied). And I'm definitely a sucker for noodles so despite the long wait... I might come back to try the other choices on the menu.

After seeing pictures of giant bowls of udon, 
I had to go try.
I went twice before writing this review and I plan to go back many more times in the future.

My favorite is the spicy tuna appetizer 
and the cold uni udon.

There may be quite a line if you arrive during lunch or dinner peak time, so be sure to make a reservation if you plan on being there during the peak hour!

I guess I'm confused by the place. Don't get me wrong, the decor is gorgeous, or server was a doll, and the food was good. But I don't know why I ended up paying that much for a bowl of udon.

I llike udon more than ramen, so I it's not that I don't like the dish itself...but I couldn't really discern why I was paying this much more for a bowl. I got the Tsurutontan Deluxe which left me confused. Maybe I'd have a different view of the place if I ordered something else (my friend ordered the Nabeyaki Udon which was $4 cheaper and more up my alley), or if another friend hadn't talked it up. But I couldn't taste what made the broth so special (sorry chefs, I'm sure you put a lot of time into it!). The noodles too, were cooked just a bit too long for my liking.

I'm sure (at least I hope!), the quality here is much higher than most places that serve udon...but like...udon is cheap. If you're going to charge me more than two times the normal price of udon, I need more than what was given.

I learned about this place through work. Once I saw uni on the menu I knew I had to try it.

Came here on a Friday night at 6:30 and was told the wait would be 45 mins to an hour. One hour later they told me 10 more mins. I waited 20 before I asked again how much longer. They seated us quickly but there were a lot of seats available upon walking inside. I am guessing it's for reservations. But really not cool that I had to wait so long.

We started with the Tatsuta Fried Chicken as an appetizer. My boyfriend had the Sukiyaki udon. The broth was good. I ordered the uni udon which comes cold. You have the option of a regular bowl, or a larger bowl which comes with extra noodles for the same price for all udon dishes. Clearly I ordered the large bowl for $24! There is also the choice of thick or thin noodles. I love cold noodles in general, so that mixed with uni, it was yummy. I just wish there was more uni. However, I walked out super full. Was it good? Yes. Would I come back purposely to try other udon dishes? Probably not. There are so many more delicious places in St. Marks!

Good food but still working out the logistical kinks. 

Was here for a large group dinner. They seated us in the back, no problem. 

Ambience: pretty 

The food: four stars. Had the Tsurutontan deluxe. Great broth. Minus a star that everyone's food came out before mine, then telling me that they ran out of thin noodles and had to make them from scratch (but plus a star for making them from scratch) then exceeding my expectations by providing me the thin noodles. 

For apps, we had the edemame (I didn't try), the shishito peppers (I got one pepper because it was a large party but it was good) and the spicy tuna cones (good).

The water cake tastes like clear agar jelly. The toppings taste good. Overall it is worth having a bite of just for the experience. 

They have complementary tea but they again told me they had to make it from scratch. But then the tea appeared. I could tell the waitress was really trying.

I enjoyed my meal when i came for the first time but then the second time I was somehow disappointed.
First time i got the mental caviar udon, it felt refreshing and flavor was good, but I didn't like the fact that I had to pay for an egg. 
second time i got the tsurutontan deluxe from the dash stock section and it was so not impressive, it was one of their "best seller" too. overall everything was just saggy, totally failing on texture and they added way too much udon.

First of all I loved the ambiance of the restaurant. The server couldn't have been more helpful and since it was my first time she helped me place my order. I had the caviar udon which was unreal. I brought two friends here from Caalifonrnia and they were so impressed. I have been back twice and each time thrilled with both the physical space and the food.  Highly recommend!

This place is mediocre at best. Expect a long wait -- put your name down and get a text when your table is ready. My husband and I had dinner here last night -- we were seated at the worst table in the restaurant -- we were joking that the owners must've been like "let's just squeeze in one more..." since the 2 person table was upstairs, in the back, and placed immediately in front of a kitchen space -- which meant that my husband and i were actually apologizing for being in the way of the waitstaff who were running back and forth between the kitchen and the rest of the restaurant ... 

Had a rose lychee cocktail to start which was nice. We ordered 1 appetizer and 2 entrees -- all of which were dumped on the table at the same time! Since the entree bowls are enormous (HUGE) even for regular portion orders (not sure if they have even larger dishes for large portions) -- having everything on the table at once made it impossible to enjoy the appetizer (uni caviar dish) -- which we ended up just shoveling down in order to get rid of the plate. The udon was good -- but nothing special. If you're in the mood for a lot of udon -- this place is fine.

Uhmmm the food is not bad. For udon it's considered very overpriced, but the portion they serve sorta make up to it.

Pros: large selection of innovative udon dishes, nice interior. Food is above average.

Cons: portion was way too big for one person, and they do not let you do take-out. Really feel like a waste as I couldn't even finish half of the bowl. Would suggest their every single dish for sharing only.

Spicy Tuna Tartar Cone ($12): very good!
Tatsuta Fried Chicken ($11): so so.
Sizzling Sukiyaki Udon ($17): not bad but nothing special.
Tsurutontan Deluxe ($23): a lot of food but my friend said it's nothing special, gigantic bowl.
Tsuruton Curry Deluxe ($23): a lot a lot of food, came with tempura shrimp, pork, sliced beef, beef chunk. Very generous but again, way too much food...

Not sure if I will come back here.

Tsurutontan has fully lived up to the hype of its debut a few months ago. 

I had spicy salmon (or tuna) tartar cone which is a good starter. 

Slurp away as you would with a good udon and a deliciously sharp yet dense soup. 

Beware a size portion ladies! Lol you will probably shock once you see the size of bowl. 

Dessert is limited but I go with water drop something with peanut powder ( I guess) It's simply good as a finishing dish.

Summary
Brand new noodle shop in a modern, clean, chic space.  Choices and portions galore.  Can't wait to come back! 

The Food
Udon!  So many different ways!  My best advice is to ask the server to point you in the right direction.

The Service
Standard fare.  Nothing to complain about.  The server was very helpful in pointing us in the right direction.

The Atmosphere
Cool.  Chic.  Modern.  Very Japan.

I gave in to the hype. This udon restaurant is conveniently located in Union Square. When I arrived for my Friday 7PM reservation I heard the wait was already 1.5 hours. I am glad I was able to make reservations through the Resy app because I do not think this restaurant warrants such a long wait. Their udon bowls come in two sizes - regular or large for the same price, the difference is the amount of noodles you receive. The fat kid in us opted for the large bowl. Between the two of us we ordered the salmon garlic appetizer, two bowls of udon - the sukiyaki and curry deluxe and two Kirin's. My favorite udon spot of all time is Marugame Monzo in LA where you can taste the bounce of freshness in each strand of noodle. In NY, I recommend Raku's udon noodles over Tsurutonton. Overall 3 stars, I have had much better meals for $120.  

I highly recommend ordering 1 large bowl of udon to share between two people and sharing a bunch of apps.

I had a very nice evening, the food was really satisfying and the service was great.  I really enjoy having a choice extra large my noodles without any extra charge.  Very nice atmosphere, decors and staffs.  Please advise that reservation is a must otherwise there's always a long line. 

The only downside is that they should add a baby changing table in the restroom, so it can accommodate mothers when they need to change their babies.

Udon is ok. Bonito broth is not smoky enough. Very large portions. You won't be able to eat all of it. If you're a girl order one order and share with another girl. There are no to go boxes. Oh and get the Fried chicken! The best!

The udon version of Wagamama without the variety & vision in the old Union Square Cafe space. It's amateur hour here.
Decor- long, modern, sleek
Computer seating system borders on ridiculous. Like Wagamama they keep you waiting at the front. It doesn't feel welcoming. More on that later.
Food wise; this is the Rolls Royce of udon
Housemade noodles make it a fine Winter concoction.
Ate:Truffle creme w/ mushroom $17
Very fine udon, but upon leaving and seeing all the empty seats made me furious, when they sat me at the bar and had me wait for the stool.

Amateur hour indeed. If you know anything about What it means to eat Japanese noodles, you will be wildly disappointed. Decor is overzealous, service was laughable and the bill, steep. Probably could be a good noodle shop but somehow the pretense ruins the care for "hand stretched" noodles.

I came here with 3 friends on a Wednesday night at 7. We were told the wait was 45 minutes and we would be texted, so we went to a bar down the block. After 40 minutes we received no text so we went back. We inquired about our spot and were told we would be next. 50 minutes went by, we checked back twice and all they said was that we're next. Then, an hour and a half after we originally came in, someone asked us our name again, and realized our spot had been marked as "cancelled" because no one responded to the text. We never received a text. We didn't receive an apology. Also, one of my friends was VERY clearly pregnant but they also never offered a seat during this hour and a half.  The food wasn't good enough to compensate this service. There are three hostesses, hire at least one that knows how to do his/her job!

The hype was worth it. I got the tsurutontan special udon with the thick noodles, my friend got the cold uni udon. Both were great! For the appetizer we got the fried chicken which was a bit salty for my taste though.

This is now my FAV Udon location in New York!!

It has a very friendly and intimate vibe (great for a casual date spot), is well priced and extremely tasty. The menu is expansive and has many great options. We ordered Sukiyaki Udon (hint of a sweet taste 9/10), Wagyu Sushi (My fav of the meal), Uni and Caviar (Fresh and as expected to be therefore good) and Uni Udon (8/10). 

Definitely will return!

I've never experienced a long wait that was actually enjoyable until I came to Tsurutontan. The staff here is so nice and so helpful! 

  The bar is very trendy and welcoming. The bartender knows how to make some wonderful cocktails! 

 After we were seated, we were helped immediately and given great suggestions for meals. I had seen some pretty delicious photos of Uni udon and I really wanted to try that, but it was such a cold night that I wanted a warm noodle dish. The server helped me decide on the truffle udon with Uni on the side. The manager came out and shaved fresh truffles into the dish! It was everything you're imagining and more!!

  My friends also really enjoyed their meals. I can't wait to go back and enjoy that truffle udon again.

Is your dream eating a bowl of noodles larger than your head? If so, Tsurutonton is the place to make that dream a reality! 

Tsurutonton was decorated for dates- dark mood lighting, trendy decor, well-dressed waiters and waitresses. 

I was taken aback by the ~$20+ prices of the udon, which I used to make for like $1-2 from a frozen jumbo pack from Costco, but with a bite, I was in pure bliss! For the same price, you can choose either a small or large (head sized bowl) which makes it perfect after a long stressful day that necessitates some carboloading! The Sukiyaki udon was spot on- just the right amount of sweet and savory, with a good medley of veggie and meat. Wagyu beef udon also really hit the spot- they were generous with healthy cuts of tender beef. I do believe for the price, however, both the udons could have more toppings, especially those of traditional udons like enoki mushrooms, fish cake, tofu, etc.

The shrimp dumplings are delicious!

Got the sukiyaki udon both times I've gone! The broth is so tasty! And I think I now like udon noodles in my soup over ramen. It is veryyy filling so come hungry. 

The water cake for dessert looks interesting to try as well. 

Definitely recommend coming here!

Long story short Tsurutontan is not as gimmicky as I thought it might be.

I went to Tsurutontan with my mom, who was down for a hip place, but I still hesitated for a bit afraid how those $20 udons might not please her. But when we walked in we were told the wait will be 15 minutes. Just 15, on a FRIDAY NOON. We're going in for sure, duh!

I gave in to the hype and ordered the Wagyu Shabu Udon. The 3 dollar difference between this and the regular beef shabu udon is evident. While the cut of the beef they served was razor-thin and that definitely affected the texture, with a warm bowl of fresh udon like that, delicious beef nevertheless, and really refreshing soup, I'm sold.

Now while udon is this store's main emphasis, I think their rice is pretty good too - and accompanied with a bowl of, surprise surprise, udon. The udon that came with it was nothing special but since it had nothing fancy, it was an easy way to determine how much of this place was just fluff, and how much their food actually worked. (Hint: it worked.)

And I came to like their rice - the portion is much larger, and like I stated, it came with another side udon - all at just around the same price. Not to mention it is also pretty good, enough so that I think despite both a burden on the wallet, the rice was actually good enough to fulfill both my lunch and dinner needs when I don't want to have all three meals.

But then again, if I justified $20 for a bowl of udon as a good deal, I would've been smacked probably even by the servers. Take pride in the fact that you're privileged enough to eat the same kind of food at a nicer atmosphere and not feel burdened by the price.
Highly recommend. Waygu beef sushi melts in your mouth and uni udon was peffectly made. The wait was a bit long so it's better to reserve in advance. Service was great as well.
Food was great, but the service needs to improve a bit. No water/spoons and waiter forgot a drink order. 4.5 stars.

Probably should have listened to our friend when he said it's nothing special and no need to try!  The place is nicely decorated and it was busy that they gave up our table when we made it by the 15 minutes grace period!  The food is so not to par and it's so disappointing they would call this Japanese food...wonder if real Japanese owns it or it's just another fad!

Came with my friend for the first time and went back just days later. It is literally THAT good. The udon is on point and in New York I haven't had udon that I have loved...until now.  

The location is where the Union Square Cafe used to be. When you walk in, you notice the nice modern decor, you also notice the somewhat different type of seating. There is a middle wall of seats where there is a bamboo partition that separates what feels like a giant table made into a bar. These are kind of partitioned out so it is seating for two side by side. The bamboo partition forms a wall so another couple can sit across from you without you feeling like you are eating together. There are also booths for two or four or more. They annoyingly put the chopsticks not on something that holds chopsticks for real, but a small smooth black rock. Pretty, but the chopsticks are constantly falling off that thing even when the wait staff are trying to set the table. But no worries. Once the chopsticks are in your hand, they won't leave your hand. 

The menu is extensive. Noodle soups, fried noodles, cream soup noodles, appetizers, and all with so many amazing choices.  

You can choose between thick noodles and thin noodles. They also let you have a choice between regular or large portion of noodles for free. My suggestion is to always go for the thick and if you are super hungry, do the extra noodles.  If you aren't, don't. The extra noodles soak up sauce and soup from your dish and you aren't allowed to take it home.  I am a big fan of the sukiyaki udon and the uni udon. My friend tried the truffle cream udon and it was delicious. Another friend had the stone bowl dry sukiyaki. It was also amazing. The flavors of these dishes are always perfect and this is all comfort food to the max. 

I will definitely be a regular here.
Food is great. Don't bother making a reservation though, you'll end up waiting for an hour plus and the staff will be totally unapologetic.

The Udon was delicious the atmosphere is great and very kind staff.  Nice chill music.  Busy place but only about 20 min wait for two.  Only thing I'd say is the large bowl I got (same price as regular which is also huge) was piping hot when I got it.  Really needed to wait a bit before I could start but it was outrageously delicious.

Pretty good udon. Fresh noodles. Uni udon is good. Pricey but good. Waiter forgot my paper napkins to discard my gum, not sure if he really forgot, but I was pretty clear that I needed paper napkins. I would still come occasionally. Opt for the extra noodles! Good choice of udon to choose from.

Came here for dinner on a Sunday after many great reviews about the place and it did not disappoint. I really liked the modern yet japanese styled decor of the place. They had a nice bar area but we were led to the left where there were stairs to a lower second part of the restaurant that was a more quiet space for dining. We were seated at this long table that was separate by this wall made out of alternating pieces of wood and space, so that you could still see the guests on the other side of the wall.

We both decided to go with the Tsuyaki bowl, which was one of the best sellers. Our food came out after 15 minutes in these HUGE clay bowls. I thought that had meant that it was just for show and there wasn't a lot of food but it had a decent amount of udon noodles and toppings in it. The broth was pretty good though a bit too salty. It had thin slices of beef, enoki mushrooms and various vegetables inside which were delicious soaked in the full flavors of the broth. 

***ALSO, you can add extra udon noodles at no extra charge!

At $20, it might be on the pricier side for udon, but it was worth it!

Been to this place three times. I've tried the uni udon, mentaiko udon as well as the sukiyaki udon. All three were extremely good. I've also tried the wagyu sushi, which literally melts in your mouth. 

The one critique I have is that their thick udon was too thick for my liking. Although I normally prefer thick udon, I tried a bite of my friends and found it way too doughy. I would definitely recommend this place, but would recommend to order the thin udon instead!

A must visit place when I am in NY.

Such a beautiful place, the food is superior, and service is excellent.

I am hungry just thinking about this place. Best Udon I've ever had.

This new popular Japanese noodle spot has been a hit since it opened. There always a line unless you have reservations which I recommend. Now does it live up to the expectations?

Cold December day is perfect for at least for me a comforting warm bowl of noodle soup. We finally got a lunch time reservation that worked for everyone one. We had a 2:15pm time slot. Arrived promptly waiting in the modern stylish interior. The spacious dining has two sections the larger room and smaller part with bar seating. The staff was quick to greet and we had to wait for a few minutes before beginning seated.

What we got was the very large niche table that would probably seat for 6 six people. Nice and roomy! Our friendly waitress was quick to come over got our drinks and food. It was like clockwork machine. We went with the Tsurutontan Deluxe and the Nabeyaki Udon. For the same price you can get the large and well when they said large they meant large!  

To start we tried the Sukiyaki buns, fried chicken and the Shishito peppers. The starters came out quick! The buns were light and fluffy with the meat had a nice sweetness to it with the crunch on the cucumbers. The peppers in a light soy sauce and bonito flakes with a spicy dipping sauce was tender but I wished it was slightly more charred. The fried chicken had a great crunchy exterior, tender interior but I didn't like the purple mayo glop on top. I rather it be on the on the side and if you chose to dip it.

But here is it all about the Udon noodles. Freshly made I'm told. The thick rice noodles were firm without begin water logged. The large is enormous and comes with and equally enormous spoon. We looked like kids in a huge booth with a huge bowl with a huge spoon. The broth was light and flavorful. Not too salty. The deluxe pretty much had everything in the bowl you can imagine. The Nabeyaki was a bit more simpler with fish cake, straw mushrooms and a fillet of fish that I thought added a perfect saltiness of the fish to the soup. 

Lastly, we decided to try the infamous raindrop jello dessert. Wasn't quite sure what to make of it but I'd say it was a good ending. The flavorless clear ball is sweeten with accompanied toasted sesame and glaze with ice cream. It isn't t over sweet like most Western desserts so I liked the balance.

I'm not Udon expert as I'm can be perfectly happy with those one you find at the Asian markets but this was good. It was satisfying. Was it more expensive...yes but you are paying for the service, attention to detail and the space of course. You're eating here than you kind of expecting it so not sure why people complain about the price. If you want it cheap buy the refrigerated ones and make it at home. 

The service was on point and our waitress checked on us appropriately without too much. I'd recommend if for two people order a large with several appetizers is more than plenty or 2 large noodle for 4 people.

I love ramen noodles, and I constantly go to Ippudo for a steaming bowl of noodles and broth. I stumbled on this place which is in the location of the Union Square Care. They serve the thicker, creamier udon noodles, and on my first mouth full I was blown away! The creamy caviar udon noodles are to die for, and the sizzling sukiyaki dish is another revelations. There service is good, and I have now gone so many times that the hostess at the door knows my name. I'm sure I'll be back for many a visit in the future.

Applaud the effort to bring popular don/udon offerings to 
USW and kudos for catchy large bowls; definitely a conversation piece. 

While the food was good, it certainly wasn't amazing. Clean buildout and attentive staff earn the 4th star. Food is 3.5 stars

Hoping they can give Ootoya a run for their money soon.

/ THE SPACE:
The place looks smaller than it actually is -- the bar space is long and thin, but there's a room off-shooting the bar that's quite large, and a space upstairs for some larger parties. The space for waiting is kept to the front, which makes your experience upon sitting nice and quiet.

/ THE WAIT:
We made reservations early, but most of the people who came in without reservations were seated within 20 or so minutes. If you're a small party, you can get away with sitting at the bar.

/ THE SERVICE:
The service was fast and attentive -- we asked for a billion additional spoons and bowls since we were sharing a lot of the noodles and they happily obliged. We also had a birthday cake we wanted to eat and they gave us plates, spoons, etc., for a tiny plating fee (around $4/person).

/ THE MENU + OUR PLAN:
When you order, your options are:
(1) SMALL/LARGE - I think they're the same price. You'd be inclined to just order a large but (1) the bowls are huge and (2) they don't pack leftovers for you.
(2) THICK/THIN noodles (we asked our waitress what she preferred and she was great with her advice. Although I prefer thick noodles usually since I like the chewiness and bounciness).
(3) There's also a seasonal menu with some sushi/sashimi and udons, which we happily ordered from.


We ended up sharing some bowls as 'appetizers' and I thought that worked out really well, as it gave us the opportunity to try a bunch of noodles without slurping up a big bowl of each one. We then each had our own -- which I could barely finish because the bowls are HUGE. The pictures do not do them justice. 

/ WE GOT:
UDON:
RUBY RED CARBONARA - Delicious. Well, it basically tastes like carbonara so I'd get it for the wow factor more than anything else. Also not as pink and pepto bismol-y as the picture looks.
WAGYU SUKIYAKI UDON - Light and flavorful -- the broth is sweeter than most.
TRUFFLE CREME WITH CRAB + MUSHROOM - HEAVY but delicious. I'd recommend sharing this, as the person in our party who got this couldn't finish the whole thing.
WAGYU SHABU CURRY -- Rich and perfect for winter. The wagyu in it was definitely worth it, it also comes with extra chunks of meat from the curry.
TSURUTONTAN DELUXE -- has egg and shrimp tempura in it, if you're looking for noodles with a ton of toppings (also comes with fried shishito leaves, I think). 

For another appetizer, we also got the seared salmon sashimi, which was delicious and a nice break from the 900 gallons of broth we were going to drink. Next time I return, I'll take a more in depth look at their sushi menu.

Unreal place... here's a bit from my writeup...

"Flavor? Oh hell yeah. I had the Sukiyaki for lunch. The waitress asked if I wanted thin or fat noodles. Pro tip: ask for extra fat. She just nodded with that wink cool kids give you and shuffled off. In a few minutes before me was presented a beautiful bowl, the kind you would buy your girlfriend for a birthday if you were planing on staying together with her. Inside was sizzling, yo, SIZZLING noodles in thick sauce. scattered pieces of tender meat, woodsy mushrooms, bright scallions, and were those perfectly caramelized onions like they hijacked an In-and-Out burger? Yeah, yeah they were."

check out the whole review here my friends: https://cineclast.com/2016/12/15/eat-me-tsuru-tontan-udon-nyc/

Their udon is delicious! Ate there twice and tried the Tsurutontan udon and uni udon. The uni udon was good but it wasn't amazing. The broth and udon of the hot udon - tsurutontan - is amazing and it's just perfect for a cold winter day/night. My friend also enjoyed the hot udon more. Also, their rolls aren't really that great. It's an udon restaurant...just stick to the udon. Sea & truffle roll is the only one worth trying.
A good noodle shop with good decoration. The food is just so so. I had their don which comes with a small udon. The rice is sticky and the don is not as good as I expect.

Heard of this place a long time ago. Finally checked it out today. Glad I came here.

My friend and I came in at 6ish, when the wait time was 20-30 mins. You can put your name and cell number down but they'll ring you when your table is ready. 

The menu has plenty of dishes to choose from: appetizer in cold or hot, classic udon in clear soup, in richer soup, and in most rich and creamy soup. Udon noodle has two options-thin and thick. I prefer the thin as it is more flavorful. Another highlight is you can upgrade your udon portion size to large and for free. And dessert menu is limited-only 4 choices. We ordered the crystal Japanese cake, which to me, is non-flavored jelly with syrup and ice cream. 

My friend and I ordered 1 appetizer, 2 udon, 1 dessert, and ended up paying $70+, including tax and tip.

Fix your quality control. Used to come here a lot and brought clients from out of town here. First time I came was only two months ago and ordered the same thing (#1 Deluxe), at the time one of the best things I've had in NY. Recently a client mentioned it was terrible and I would not believe it. Went myself just now and the same Udon I had loved was extremely undercooked and the egg drop was more like a fried egg. Left half the bowl unfinished. Embarassing. The branch in Roppongi would never be caught with this level of quality. Hopefully the truffle udon, uni udon and the sukiyaki udon is still as good as I remembered...

Nice servers, great decor with an emphasis on textures, rest of the menu hopefully still on point. Don't even care about the hour long wait times. If the udon which they proudly claim is homemade on the daily is THIS bad, happy to direct people elsewhere. Go to Raku in EV or any of the Udon West spots across town for a consistent, cheaper and frankly much better bowl of udon with no wait times.

came twice in a span of 8 days. the udon is DELICIOUS; the tsurotontan deluxe with extra udon is definitely enough to split between 2 people. their uni udon is also quite delicious if you like uni; this dish is cold though.

BUT, if you're in for a real treat.. look at their appetizer list..
my favorite item in this restaurant is actually their Seared Wagyu Sushi. imagine a thin fatty slice of beef blanketing a small mound of warm, sticky sushi rice. i've had beef sushi twice before; but this is on a whole new level of yum. GET IT

Came here for the third time last night! This place never disappoints. If you have a reservation, they definitely honor the time. I especially love that the restaurant sends you a half hour reminder of your reservation.

As for the food, the udon regular size and the large size portions cost the same. Go for the large size portion if you're really hungry! It's quite filling. The staff there are very friendly. I highly recommend this place.

Pretty long wait on a week night. The menu is extensive and everything looked so good. For appetizers, we had their daily special, uni wagyu beef sushi, which was good but not really a good deal for the price. For the entree I had the uni udon and the friend had shrimp tempura udon. Uni udon was lacking but all the udon with broth looked good.

My nickname as a child was "baby udon,' so I might be a little biased, but I personally think this is one of the best new NYC restaurants of 2016.

My boyfriend and I got the Tsurutontan Deluxe and the Sukiyaki Udon. This udon was without a doubt the best udon noodles I've had in NYC. They were springy and had their own flavor, while standing up to a delicious broth, as well as shrimp and beef. 

The broth itself was more mild than one would regularly get in ramen in NYC, while still being delicately flavorful. 

It did take a little while to get seated, but they texted us when our table was ready. The waitress was kind and patient, even though the restaurant was clearly super busy. While waiting for a table, I was able to sample their Negroni Giapponeria, which was one of the best Negronis I've had recently. The yuzu and campari went together incredibly well. 

Overall, we had a great time, and I can't wait to come back!
Another Japanese chain transplant. The food is reliable and good. Good for a lazy Sunday dinner but dont go out of your way.

Update

This place has really gone down.  The soup is less thick and rich.  I tried the "Hot and Sour" special "with eggplant" which was basically udon noodles in hot and sour soup with 3 small pieces of eggplant on top.  Tempura was very heavy and service was slow.  Portions are still HUGE though

This udon spot was eagerly anticipated for months, and as expected there were lines out the door to get in once it opened. Good news - they take online reservations! I chose it for a dinner with some out-of-town guests, and they were really impressed. First of all, we got a nice, cozy little u-shaped booth that shielded us from the loud music (courtesy of the in-house DJ... who knew udon spots put such a premium on their beatz??). The service was amazing from start to finish - it wasn't long since they first opened their doors and I think they really wanted all the feedback they could get and wanted to impress their diners. Which they did! 

The menu is huge and can be overwhelming, but luckily there are lots of photos which is always helpful. This is the first American location (I think they mentioned there are like 12 in Japan), so as expected some of the descriptions don't use perfect English but you get the idea pretty easily. If you're not feeling udon there are plenty of other options, like tempura or donburi bowls. But I went with Tsurutontan Deluxe, which turns out to be an even more huge serving than their other huge bowls of ramen! Not that I was complaining. I gobbled those noodles, shrimp and veggie tempura, beef, chicken, and yummy broth right up. It's $24 for that bowl so not cheap, but this thing is HUGE and will absolutely fill you up. 

It's a fun environment whether you're grabbing an everyday meal or having a bit more of a special occasion. The decor is beautiful and, again, the service was impeccable. Highly recommend!

All I can say to people who are wondering if they should go: BELIEVE the HYPE. 

After seeing the NY Times and Eater NY rain praise down on Tsurutontan and then hearing all my friends say the same, I had some high expectations. We went as group of 5 on a busy weekend night and were told it would be a substantial wait. However, the restaurant did have a texting service that would let you know when your table was ready so we got to spend the time shopping around Union Sq. 

As we walked to our table, I noticed how beautifully and tastefully decorated the restaurant was - perfect for dates or entertaining friends or family from out of town. Our server was attentive, thoughtful, and helped us quite a bit in navigating their enormous menu. We ordered the Tatsuta fried chicken and the Spicy Creamy Shrimp Tempura as appetizers - both of which were outstanding. The pink sauce of the friend chicken is a little jarring but deliciously tangy with a light herbal background and the spicy sesame sauce paired with the microgreens for the shrimp made the perfect bite. I ended up with the curry katsu udon, which came in an enormous bowl, and the portions are definitely enough to fill anyone up. The noodles come in large and regular size but the big difference seems to just be the amount of noodles you get. Dessert was less impressive but still interesting and satisfying. We got the raindrop cake and the Lady M Green Tea Crepe Cake. The raindrop cake was a little gimmicky for what is basically a clear, round ball of agar with syrup but cleansing and interesting to self-assemble. Lady M, of course, needs no introduction. Overall, it's a little pricier than I would traditionally spend for an udon dinner but it is 100% worth the money and a beautiful experience.

All in all, I have made Tsurutotan a part of my regular rotation for places to bring friends/family...or to just splurge on myself a little.

I went to master cabbie i had the best service ever from the day i start Fatima Ais the director helped me with every thing i need it go go to her for your Tlc license you will get every thing you need fatima your are the best god blessd you and bless master cabbie

Delicious, flavorful food. I had the classic beef Udon (don't remember what it's called) but it was so tasty, although I wish it had had more vegetables. The dumpling appetizer was amazing too. Edamame, surprisingly, was the only disappointment - it's so basic, you'd expect it to be a good, simple starter, but ours was mushy and flavorless. Still, the food was terrific. My biggest complaint is the fact that they refuse to send you home with leftovers. What is that about?! The portions are huge, and not cheap - why wouldn't they want to save food? Whatever, seems pretentious, and it means I probably won't go back because each meal out is usually two meals for me. Still, overall a good experience.

Can't pronounce the name of the restaurant, but they do have some amazing udon. Came here around 1pm on a Wednesday and there was a short wait of about 15 min. We ordered some drinks and the sukiyaki udon and the curry udon. They offer a large portion for the same price, so of course we opted for that. The only thing is that you can't take home any leftovers. 

The place itself was very modern and and simple. There is a large communal bench/table and some tables scattered along the perimeter. There was also a second floor, but didn't go check that out.  

The food itself is really flavorful with lots of toppings. My noodles came out a tad bit mushier than I'd like (I always prefer noodles with a bite to it). Maybe next time I'll opt for the thin udon noodles. The little pieces of meat in there were slightly sweet which was a nice contrast. Other than that, everything was really good. The curry noodles was more filling and heavier, but still very tasty. Aside from the traditional soup and curry, there were also creme based and cold noodles. A bit of everything for everyone.

The drinks are also very good. Their menu is actually very extensive and offers a Japanese spin on some classics.

The food is average udon; the price is a splurge for what you get, but the service is impeccable.

The store front is rather narrow, but this restaurant runs deep and has a second floor of seating, so it's actually rather spacious. We came for Sunday lunch and only had to wait 15 min. We were definitely relegated to the back, on a rickety table closest to the kitchen because we were extremely casual (it was a celebratory post-finals meal). The servers tried to even out our table, but there were other patrons so they weren't going to down a table. If you're not incredibly hungry, skip the appetizer because the portion sizes are huge. They offer you the option of adding more noodles for the same price, but be reasonable with how hungry you are and pass. Will definitely come back again if the craving hits!

Love this place! Glad to have a higher end, quality udon place in NYC.

I went for the first time and got the cauliflower tempura, tofu burrata, and kitsune udon. The cauliflower tempura was delicious if not interesting (tons of shaved parmesan on it), the tofu burrata I could pass on (literally just tasted like whipped tofu and soy sauce), and the kitsune udon was the star. I got the thick noodles and the large portion for the same price. My eyes were bigger than my stomach but it was delicious. Noodles were soft, but not mushy, broth was flavorful without being too salty/briny/overpowering and tofu was perfect. A quality bowl of noodles that left me satisfied. Probably more expensive than it should be, but comparable to what you'd pay for a good bowl of ramen in NYC anyway.

Second time I came, I had the tatsuta fried chicken and the katsu curry udon. The fried chicken was good, not great (lightly battered and fried, most of the flavor came from the overwhelming amount of purple mayo sauce that was on it) and I was pleasantly surprised that the katsu curry udon comes with katsu pork and beef. Also delicious, but it's definitely more "gravy" than it is soup. Like a thick curry gravy that's not exactly drinkable. It was also heavier than I thought it would be (I ordered the large again, like an idiot).

The most recent time I came I think I refined my order. I split an order of the spicy tuna tartare cones and had the large kitsune udon. That was enough to make me feel full but not exploding.

Ever since this place opened, I've been craving udon nonstop. I think everyone should come out and enjoy this place at least once. Also, a small perk is being able to make a reservation.

ATMOSPHERE:
Casual dining with a large table area downstairs, the chairs are benches that seat 2! You can also make reservations online. My boyfriend & I came on a Thursday night at around 7:00, and there was barely a wait. SHOUT OUT to our server, Annie, who was super nice and helpful with guiding us through the menu and giving recommendations!

FOOD ORDERED:
Spicy Tuna Tartare Cone - Yummy & interesting! Definitely worth trying!

Tsurutontan Deluxe - Great soup base, and thick classic udon noodles!

Uni Udon - Got it with the thin noodles, and it was like a flavorful explosion of the ocean! It doesn't look like much (because it's so simple) but it definitely packs a flavorful punch! 

Chocolate Cake (forgot the name!) - Classic and yummy!

COMMENTS:
Overall lovely atmosphere, kind service, and fresh flavors!

Overpriced dishes with ok service. I had high expectations because I loved the udon noodles that I had in Tokyo. Sever skipped me to take order from another customer after me.  He didn't even tell me about noodle options that I was supposed to be told.  But I may go back for their another chance for them.

We went for lunch; the food is great and the service also but there is ABSOLUTELY NO JUSTIFICATION for a restaurant to ask you to bring YOUR OWN TUPPERWARE to pack up left overs. How is it possible they do not have containers to pack your food? The manager's answer was: we expect our customers to bring their own. It is ridiculous and with all the restaurant options in the city they've lost me as a customer.

a bit on the pricey side ...

but ambiance is great and

i'd say share a bowl only cuz its quite large for me at least (got the Tsurotontan deluxe) - broth is good

and spicy tuna cones (appetizer) were great!
Can't believe how big the bowl is and the amount of food they give you.  Taste good and the service is fast.

Overall decent food but think it's a bit pricy and portion is too big. (Expect 30+minutes wait and $30+pp even if you don't drink).

We got curry katsu udon and the uni cold udon for share. The curry katsu udon is savory and delicious. The thick noodles absorbed the curry sauce really well too. The uni udon is a bit too cold and light in flavors. 

Don't think I'll wait over an hour for this place again. Prefer Raku over this place.

3 stars. Beautiful location, tasty udon yet un-traditional and 'chain-like'. 

I'm conflicted about Tsurutontan. Loved it the first time, fell out of love the second. My initial reactions were most likely similar to those of many others: 

-Large and beautifully decorated venue by Union Square (very easily accessible)
-HUGE, beautiful bowls
-Takes reservations, (which I highly recommend taking advantage of as it allows you to skip the line)
-Noodles in big healthy portions

Perhaps I'm being pessimistic after eating here again but I really think the food is slightly "chain-like". There is nothing special about their noodles, it honestly feels a little mass-produced and the broth flavors are heavy-handed. 

I would not rule out Tsurutontan if it's your first time (I would even go as far to say try the uni); however, I don't think it's worth the wait and I definitely don't think the food is special enough to warrant a revisit.

Best udon noodles in NYC! Usually takes 20 - 30 mins wait time to be seated, very cool interior decor but not too comfortable for sitting (unless you sit by the bar, otherwise there is only a bench to sit on. Oh well a lot of ramen places are like this too...)

Appetizers are in the fair price range compare to other NYC Japanese restaurants. Their spicy tuna cone is a must try!

They are a little pricey for a bowl of udon, but proportion is very generous. Not to mention that you can upgrade for extra noodles without additional charges. This is the best udon noodles in the city. Their cream soup is also amazing, perfect match with the noodles! Love!!!
Those oodles of noodles! Those bowls! The service is efficient and the place is minimalistic. A perfect destination for a wintry day.

Long wait for the entree. The sukiyaki udon was plain. Was hoping for mind blowing authentic Japanese, but it's just average. The kaisen don was small, and had scales on my salmon. Ootoya is better for overall food. Abuiya Kinnosuke blues this place away. Disappointing...

Met up with a few friends around 5:30pm and it was already starting to get packed. The venue is pretty big and the decor is really nice. The bowls for the udon were pretty huge with giant ladle spoons. The portions however did not match the size of bowls but it was definitely sufficient. Overall, really good but on the pricey side.

Summary: Easy to get in for weekday lunch but super overpriced for a lackluster bowl of udon. Repeat visit unlikely. Definitely not worth the wait. 

Process: Got here at 11:40am on Tuesday (12/27) and was first in line for lunch service. I thought with the wait times noted in the Yelp reviews there would already be a line. Even by the time they opened at noon there were still only about ten people around. Easy to be seated but all parties do need to be there. 

Food: We ordered the popular deluxe and nabeyaki in large sizes. It's clear that the noodles are handmade with its springiness which was definitely a plus but I can't justify paying $27 for udon that's just well made and nothing special. I guess they can charge whatever price they want since there's no competition in the city (RIP onya my go to udon spot) and you do get a very large serving (like everybody else noted, both sizes are the same price and massive) but there's really nothing special about their udon. The broth is well done as the restaurant hails from Osaka where they're known for their subtle but deep flavored broths. If it were 40% cheaper I would be a repeat customer but I could easily make this at home for about $5. The shichimi spice is nothing special and tastes like grocery store shichimi. 

Service: Really attentive and friendly staff.

Food was solid, but not too memorable. My girlfriend and I had dinner there last night. The wait wasn't long which was nice. Service was excellent. We ordered all of their "Top Sellers" as listed on their menu and a couple other fellow yelper favorited dishes. While the food was good, not one dish had me craving to go back for more. They had an uni and caviar appetizer which was probably the bite we had. The udon soups were just okay. Drinks were tasty, but on the pricey side.

I was so hoping this would be a more delicious and convenient replacement for Raku but alas, it was not meant to be.

Friend and I came here on a Wednesday night at 6 and were greeted with a ~15 minute wait (not too bad), though the place was packed by the time we left around 7:30. While we waited at the bar, I ordered a Tokyo Mule and he ordered a virgin Lychee Mojito - both were delicious.

We were seated at the communal bar, kind of awkwardly close to the couple right across from us. Since it was freezing outside, I abandoned my original plan and ordered the spicy soondubu jigae udon soup (thick noodles, small with an extra serving of noodles on the side) and my friend got the sizzling sukiyaki udon, minus the beef.

Vegetarians beware - that was basically the only warm vegetarian option on the menu as all of the broths are made with bonito (fish) flakes and all the curries are made with beef. Though I'm a die hard carnivore myself, it is disappointing that there's not a dedicated vegetarian option on the menu like at so many other noodle shops.

Luckily, my friend loved his dish. I was underwhelmed with mine - the noodles lacked the springiness that I've loved at Raku, and the broth was way too sweet (I can only imagine how sweet the plain dashi broth is, since this was based on that with some other add-ins). Serving sizes were enormous though, as other reviewers noted, and you can upgrade to the large noodles for free.

Dessert was the water cake, which was a refreshing (aka tasteless) and a fun way to end the meal. 

Decent bowl of noodles overall, but not worth the wait or the price. I'll stick to schlepping out to Raku for now or Udon West for my quick fix.
so good.  udon noodles are cooked perfectly.  so far, have had the mentai udon, uni udon, tatsuta fried chicken, beef sukiyaki udon and the tempura udon.  all of it was good.

We came here as part of a 10-person birthday group. Had a really great experience! Each bowl of noodle soup was really fun to watch coming up to the table in the super giant bowls. I would skip the appetizers (very small portions) and go right ahead to the noodle.

I think we got an udon with beef - I can't remember which one - but it was a crowd favorite. Tender, flavorful slices of beef in a broth that was perfect. A fun place to visit and great central location.

Came here for dinner with a friend. When we walked in I was surprised by the size of the restaurant. It's very big and immediately smelled delicious! We split the fried chicken, which was good, but I would definitely try the appetizers if I were to eat here again. My friend got a spicy udon bowl (don't remember the name) with thick noodles and it tasted amazing! I got the uni udon, which was very good, but the uni flavor is quite strong so keep that in mind if you are to order it. Overall, great udon and we left very very full. The size of those bowls is no joke!

All the bowls are gigantic sized, food was good. We ordered to much as always. The downside to this big portion family style restaurant is they have a no leftover takeout policy. A downer because I'm Chinese, nothing goes to waste! Luv the decor and atmosphere.

This review isn't commenting on the food, but rather an unpleasant and strange experience I had here. At some point during my dinner, a server accidentally spilled a plate full of soy sauce and sashimi bits down the inside of my wool coat and the back of my sweater. The server was extremely apologetic about it, and spent a good deal of her time trying to get the soy sauce out using club soda. She even blow dried it to make sure it was dry since it's 35 deg outside and I need a coat. I really am not angry at the server - accidents happen. 

Unfortunately, my coat still has soy sauce stains all over the inside, the back, the collar, and the sleeves - and it absolutely reeks of fish juice. The stench is so unbearable that I ended up having to cancel my plans with my friends for the rest of the night so that I could go home and shower. This wasn't like getting water or wine spilled on you. It is absolutely one of the most repugnant smell combinations and there is also some weird sticky residue on the coat. Too bad my only choice was to wear this coat all the way home or freeze. 

After I paid my bill and was about to leave, I did ask the manager to pay for my dry cleaning. She offered to reimburse me if I get the coat dry cleaned and then hand deliver the actual bill to the restaurant as soon as possible. Well....I don't really consider this to be an adequate response. Considering that it will already take some amount of my time for me to bring this coat to the dry cleaners, having to then travel all the way to union square to show them proof of the ~$30 bill is obviously not going to be time or cost effective for me to do. I will probably end up eating the dry cleaning cost myself and I will have to rethink ever eating at Tsurutontan again.

My first impressions of Tsurotontan did not exceed any sort of expectations. It was along the lines of what I was expecting. Though I have to say the restaurant itself is a large and nice looking space with two floors, but only one bathroom(?). We came here with a 5P reservation for a Friday night. I highly recommend a reservation instead of a walk in if you aren't looking for a half hour to hour minimum wait. As soon as we got to the restaurant at 4:45P, there was already a line forming at the door. They open at 5P for dinner, but don't bother trying to come in before 5P even with a reservation because they won't let you wait inside (even if their doors are already open).

We ordered the Tatsuta fried chicken with house made tartar sauce and some edamame to start. I had the regular size Tsurotontan Deluxe ($24), while my bf had the regular size Wagyu Sukiyaki udon. For drinks, Hitachino White Ale on draft, a light Japanese beer. Firstly, the udon is a nicely presented dish, but the portion sizes are ridiculous. Instead of being comforting, it was overwhelming. This might be the one of very few times I will complain about oversized portions. They have between a regular and large size, and a regular bowl can feed two people, if not one and a half people. It is a tad too much, and I only got halfway through. Otherwise, the flavor was underwhelming. There was nothing that particularly stood out in this dish other than the size of it. The Deluxe was disappointingly mild, bordering on quite bland, even with all the shrimp tempura, beef, and chicken in it. The chicken maybe did not even need to be in this dish. The Wagyu sukiyaki is the complete opposite as it is much too sweet. The Tatsuta chicken was stringy, and I didn't care for the extra amounts of sauce. The edamame was ordinary. The appetizers, udons, and two beers, came to a bill of over $100. We were pretty underwhelmed by the meal, so we are not certain if it would be worth coming back to try other dishes considering the price.

Tsurotontan could be better. The extravagant portion sizes still leaves much to be desired. The menu offers a wide array of options, especially for udon, but I feel less inclined to try them when compared to my usual udon spots. It is worth a shot at least once regardless, but I don't think Tsurotontan is replacing Raku or Udon West for my udon crave.

Things to keep in mind: the best thing you can do is get the optional larger size of udon and share it with someone else and get some extra apps.

The Tsuru Deluxe was delicious. The broth was amazing. The egg and beef was so satisfying and comforting. The tempura placed atop the soup stayed crispy for the most part. I like that they half fried the seaweed. Very nice touch.

Service was also great and would love to visit again!

Wygyu beef sushi is a must have!  I will go back again and again for that!  I know I should come here for udon, but their appetizers are so delicious!!!!

I love this place so much!!!!!

This restaurant is amazingggg!! I love noodles and this place does not disappoint! The Spicy Tuna Tartare cone was a light but delicious appetizer! Had guacamole and spicy Tuna Tartare in a crunchy outer cone. The fried chicken was also really good plus the purple mayo that they put on it is a nice addition. I got the truffle oil mushroom and crab Udon. I got the large portion even though it is the same price which is awesome! Only thing is that if you can't finish, you can't take it to go since the consistency of the Udon can change and make you sick later if you take it to go. Which is fine since I finished every last bite. The large bowl is humongous though and I was afraid that I wouldn't finish even though I consider myself a big ester. Service was great and speedy and the restaurant had a nice atmosphere. Great date spot or just a dinner outing with friends! I highly recommend this Udon noodle place. They have so many options! My Udon choice was excellent! Creamy and filling and satisfying to the last bite!

This was one of my favorite restaurants on this trip to NYC. I had done some research and wanted to check it out, so I met my relative here for lunch. It is very close to Union Square -- you can see it while standing outside.

The restaurant gets packed fast, so go early. There were three of us and we ordered several udon and a couple of appetizers to share. You also get the feel of eating in an upscale restaurant with the attentive service. Managers were stopping by the table making sure we were enjoying the food.

The cucumber salad is delicious!

I ordered the cold udon with mountain yam and uni.... OMG the texture of the udon is out of this world. It's chewy and so perfectly al dente there are no words to describe it.

The hot udon is a fraction less chewy. I think the hot broth continues the cooking process so the udon becomes softer, but it still possess a good chew. If I had eaten the hot udon first, I wouldn't have given it a second thought, but when compared to the cold, there is a slight difference.

The bowls are ginormous which allows for really great broth to noodle ratio. We also had the Tsurutontan udon and the chicken udon, both with great broth.

I highly recommend this place.

My friend and I arrived at 5:45 on a Friday evening. There was no wait - great! The restaurant was pretty much empty and we could chat without shouting - great! But the hostess sat us in a dining bar with our backs facing the bar/entrance area when there were clearly other preferable seats available. I understand that we did not have reservations but this was a little extreme. 

Prior to dining, our waiter warned us that he could not package our leftovers to-go in order to preserve the flavor and integrity of the noodles. I thought this was strange. Clearly, if we were dining in, we would have the full experience. As someone who likes to give her leftovers to hundreds of people on the street looking for their next meal, I thought this concept was wasteful and selfish. Especially since we have a huge food waste problem in this country. I also asked the waiter if they have tea and what kind. When I asked him to explain the notes of the tea more, he was a little dumbfounded and I had to explain myself again. Maybe this was a communication error on my part. 

We both ordered hot udon dishes. The noodles were great and the broth was rich in flavor. I was satisfied at the end of the meal. A little pricey for what it's worth so I won't be dining here often, but it is worth a trip to try. 

At the end of our meal, we waited about 10-15 mins for the waiter to offer us a dessert menu or to check on our dining experience but he never showed. We ended up asking another person in the wait staff for our check. By this time, the restaurant was getting busy.
