If they would have been more attentive, they could seat us in a more preferable place and turned the tables over faster for their guests with reservations.

While this isn't my favorite udon place (see review for Raku), I still enjoy coming here. There's a wide variety of options on the menu and options for either thin or thick udon (although for me, thick is the only way to go).

There are also options for regular or large portions without any additional cost for the large. This is a good option if you want to share a large and try a lot of appetizers/small bites. The only caveat is that you can't do takeout, which I don't have a huge gripe with. Why would you want to take a soggy bowl of leftover udon, anyway?

The first time I came here, I had the mentaiko cream udon, which was delicious. While creamy, it wasn't overwhelming or too heavy, and had just enough of a "brothy" consistency to it to make me feel like I'm still slurping a bowl of hot udon. The next time I came, I had the Tsurutontan special, which was a bowl of hot udon with tempura shrimp, some veggies, beef, chicken, and egg. The broth was very savory and well-seasoned; not too salty. Noodles are also chewy.

The host(esse)s and servers have all been very friendly and welcoming. Service was excellent.

It looks like it gets crowded easily but I've gotten lucky both times to be seated within 15 minutes of arrival. The space is large, and although I've read other reviews stating that they were not seated promptly despite it not being crowded, I haven't encountered that problem.

Awful! THE WORST dining experience of our lives! This restaurant does not even deserve a star! 

We felt unwelcome from the start! We had a reservation on 1/4/2017 for 5:30pm. We arrived at 4:45pm and was told off by the discourteous hostesses whose backs were turned while they told us to come back at 5pm. Fine, so we walked around a bit and came back at 5. When we walked in at 5 the same hostesses still had their backs turned while we requested to be seated earlier. The rude hostess said fine in disgust and seated us. She carelessly flung the menus on our table and walked off. Mind you we had a lot of luggage with us and never once were we asked if they could take care of  our coats and set aside our belongings. While we were looking at the menus 2 more guests had arrived. Contrary to the service we received, the hostess gladly asked if she could take their coats and seated them right beside us in an EMPTY restaurant. So we were forced to move our luggage which we placed right next to us somewhere else. How on earth does that make any sense?! It was outrageous when the hostess sat those guests right next to us in an EMPTY RESTAURANT! We were incredibly discontent and frustrated not only because we were trying to order food, which we never got to place because the employees were too busy jabbering away, we were also treated so poorly! It felt like we were in a high school cafeteria, which is such a shame because this place had so much potential. 

Horrible service, horrible staff, horrid hospitality. We walked out and never ordered and will never come back. It's such a great location and seemingly expensive budget by the looks of the restaurant. It's really such a shame...NY is the Mecca of hospitality and dining experience and Tsurutonton is definitely not it!

For an out of towners like myself this place is great! Price point is good. Honestly most resto in NYC that I went to, an entree would cost around $20-$30, for casual dining. This one is definitely worth to visit for that price point. Definitely one of the best ambience and menu selections. Also, the restaurant is a reputable chain from Japan.

As far as food, definitely get the Spicy Tuna & Avocado cones for appetizer. The presentation and flavor makes a good experience :)

We got here when it opened at noon so there was no wait. Upon walking in, the first thing I noticed was the decor. I mean, this place was beautiful inside for a place that's serving udon. It looked more like a high end restaurant. In front of the main entrance is the bar and behind that, was a small space with some tables in the back. You turn slightly left and that was the main dining area with tables and some counter seatings. This place was a lot bigger than I thought. 

Food: we ordered the tsurotontan deluxe for $23. You can add more noodles for free of charge, but the toppings and soup doesn't change if you get more noodles. You can also pick between thin and thick noodles, but the thin is recommended for the cold noodles and usually not the hot because it absorbs the soup too quickly. We stuck with the thick ones and no regrets. The soup base for the tsurotontan was very clean and light. I actually really enjoyed it. It comes in an overly sized big bowl and they give you a huge spoon to drink the soup with the noodles. The tsurotontan wasn't too heavy which I liked. Another good thing about it was it had a mix of everything. It had seafood, veggies, meat. We also order the tuna tartare cone. I thought that appetizer was OK. I didn't taste too much of the tuna since the guac and the cone flavor over powered the tuna tartare. Overall, I will definitely come back to try other things. They offer different things like don buri rice bowls, thicker udon bases like curry or creams. They even had an uni udon that I was really tempted to order. The uni is very fresh right from California, which is supposed to be really good. It was difficult to select which ones I wanted to try. I will definitely come back to try others! Also, our server Anderson was awesome. He was very thorough and knowledgeable about the menu! I also loved how the menu had pictures and they labeled which was "top seller." Made it just a TAD easier to pick.

So the food for this place was actually great and very tasty but no one informed us that we couldn't take the remaining leftovers. There were three of us and we were stuffed even with the normal portion. For the price of the place you'd think that considering we paid for the food we should be able take it when we leave. We had the option of either stuffing ourselves or leaving half our meal wasted. Initially recommended this place to friends coming to NYC for visits but now retracted it. If you come here order the extra portion and share.

I feel bad as I've heard good things about this place. The restaurant is big and spacious with a welcoming feeling, but sadly that was the only good thing. I suppose I am fairly picky about udon as I just visited the udon capital of Japan. 

We came as a group of 5 for Saturday lunch, and were seated quickly. The restaurant wasn't even half full, but our water glasses were constantly empty and they never refilled our tea. By comparison, Ootoya, a similar price point casual restaurant, always refills tea and water efficiently even when they are packed. I have to say this was not a pot of tea but just the basic free hot tea they offer... which is pretty standard in these types of Asian restaurants. 

We got sukiyaki udon (both soup and sizzling) and the nabeyaki udon. I can't attest to the sukiyaki udon as I didn't taste them, but my nabeyaki udon noodles were extremely overlooked and soggy with no bite to them. They were so bad I sent it back after the first taste, although they tried to argue that the noodles will continue to get cooked as it was in hot broth (why don't they undertook the noodles a bit then). They did send me a new one, but the noodles were even soggier. I ate the toppings and left hungry. The thing is, it only took them 5 minutes to bring me a new udon, but it was even worse. I think it takes around 6-7 minutes to cook udon (estimate based on the thickness of their noodles) so I think they pre cooked the noodles and just left them standing or something ... 

The soup base and the toppings were good, but the udon itself was terrible. And I think the most important part of eating udon is the udon... so sadly, I don't think I will return. Raku nearby has good homemade udon and is slightly cheaper.

Great new udon place in New York!! 
Ambience: great ambience - much larger than I would expect and have many seats. One suggestion though: would be more convenient if there are coat hangers / bag hangers. 
Food: solid udon!! The portion is huge! We got the curry udon and the sukiyaki udon - both are very tasty. You can also pick thick or thin udon noodle, with free extra noodle. (That's why the price is justifiable.) 
Service: very nice and welcoming, but a little bit slow sometimes. 
Waiting: you can take a number and they will message you when the table is gonna be ready. We waited for almost an hour.

New place that opened up in union square area - decided to come by to check it out. Luckily there was no wait for the counter area seating, but it's funny how all their tables are completely booked at 5:30p (the restaurant is actually pretty massive).

+ You can order a regular size or the larger size (i.e. extra noodles) for no additional cost - good for those who like eating more noodles/carbs

- They actually have a policy of NO TAKEOUT. Therefore, if you don't finish eating, then it's all leftovers. I'd suggest ordering a large noodle dish to share and an appetizer between two people - unless you're with a huge eater (like me...I ate my entire large-portion alone...surprised myself)

Food: Ordered the Sizzling Sukiyaki Udon - was not craving a soup-based dish, so this is the one to order for a stir fried noodle dish with beef and a poached egg in a stone pot. There was nothing outstanding about the dish itself - could do with a bit more beef (and I believe I somehow had a piece of chicken land in mine as well...that was weird).

My friend ordered the Nabeyaki Udon - this was subpar. The broth was flavorless, the tempura shrimp was in the soup when served (so was soggy by then). There is also two thin slices of eel and a few veggies. Overall, disappointed that there weren't much toppings in this dish (versus the photo on the menu).

Service: highly attentive

Ambience/Decor: very cute - there's a wall of ropes that look like a noodle-ocean

Menu: MASSIVE - tons of options. All customizable - as long as you see the ingredient, you can add it to your dish.

To try in the future: the uni udon. However, this is a cold dish, so I'm not sure how I feel about that. I have had uni pasta in the past that were all hot dishes, so curious why this is cold. Will potentially give it a try in the future, but that's only if someone else wants to go.

I'd probably give this place 3 1/2 stars if I'm being honest. I've been wanting to try it for awhile and we finally decided to come on a random weekday night. Without a reservation, we probably waited 15-20 min? Not horrible. They have a little waiting area which at least makes it more comfortable. The place is very sleek looking and I still can't quite understand how a small and large bowl are the same price, but the value is excellent! The udon was definitely good, though as an udon lover, I don't think it was great. That being said, this was a solid choice to enjoy a casual dinner.

Housed in the space previously occupied by the original Union Square Cafe, Tsurutontan opened up to no small amount of fanfare in 2016. The restaurant has had a successful history in Japan and with the launch of its first location in the United States, they seem to have accumulated a similar amount of success. Thankfully, it's much easier to get inside and seated these days than when they first initially opened, as waits of upwards of 1-2 hours were the norm.

I was able to visit on a weekday afternoon for lunch with a friend, and given the off-time, we were able to be seated quickly in the main dining room. The space is beautifully done and spacious, and while some of the arrangements were a little peculiar (some seats are typical two-tops, while we were seated side by side in the center of the room), it's very much a comfortable ambiance that isn't overly formal.

As for the food - the star here is definitely the udon, and while I can only speak to a handful of bowls, I can certainly vouch for the quality of the noodles. Tsurotontan gives guests the option to choose one of two varieties in each bowl, and my personal preferences lies with the larger, thicker udon noodles over the thinner ones. They have a satisfying chew and bounce to them that are characteristic of the noodle, and I find that they don't swell up as easily or quickly as the thinner ones. Also, for the similarly-minded carb lovers, each bowl can be ordered with an additional half serving of noodles at no charge; it's pretty much a no-brainer... and if you're watching your carbs / calories / weight, why are you in a noodle restaurant to begin with?

For Uni lovers, an order of the famed Uni Udon is definitely worth the splurge. It is the most expensive dish on the menu, but for good reason; a luxurious portion of creamy udon plated over a portion of udon noodles, nori, and a touch of dashi will disappear in mere minutes. The Sukiyaki was also simply prepared, but well done; the broth was lightly sweetened, and the thin slices of beef were cooked to just the right tenderness. And for those looking for a more indulgent bowl, the Mushroom Truffle Crème Udon will make for a delicious bowl to share. The truffle notes aren't too overpowering, and the cream broth is an ideal balance of earthy, creamy, and umami flavors.

Prices on average are fairly reasonable, especially given the area, and now that it's feasible to get a table without making a reservation weeks in advance, I'd say it's fair to add Tsurutontan into the regular dinner rotation.

Came here twice already and thought the food was pretty good! I like the fact that there is a large selection of udon dishes compare to the typical nabeyaki that you get a Japanese restaurant. We all really liked the sukiyaki udon. Very tasted. The mushroom truffle was delicious as well. You can either order the regular portion or the large portion for the same price. We also like the apps. Fried chicken was good and the rolls. You definitely need to make reservations ahead of time because it gets filled up fast. Service was also very good. Would come back here again!

I really loved their uni udon! Probably one of the best udon places in NYC. If you are a uni lover, this definitely is the place you have to check out! Also, there usually is a long line during dinner time (arnd 7 ish) on the weekend so I recommend you to go for early dinner:)

If only no stars had been an option!
Me and my husband always meet for dinner Friday nights in the Union Square area after work, and we could have gone to one of our favorite places like Casa Mono and Bar Jamon on Irving Place, or the lovely ABC Cocina, the amazing Tarallucci e Vino, Craftbar, Blue Water Grill or Barn Joo in the immediate area. All beloved places to meet and gather with friends and make great memories. Establishments that always makes you feel welcome and never disappoints with great food and drinks. But we made the enormous mistake and ventured to Tsuru Ton Tan. We may have been there for an hour and it wasn't so bad until we were told to leave before we were done with dessert and drinks after having spent $150 in the counter area seating, because they needed the "table". Their website advertises "forgotten elegance", "a place for everyone to gather" along with "great hospitality and service", because "they strive to create a pleasurable experience for their guests". All fluff! Clearly these people don't want repeat customers or wish to be a neighborhood joint. And we will make sure colleges and friends know what this establishment is all about; get you in and get you out. We will never set foot in this pretense establishment ever again. Should you be jonesing for Japanese food, there are plenty and far better restaurants in the area that would more than welcome your business. What a humiliation, waste of time and money!


Reply to manager:
Rushed is not just something we "felt" Sir. "Politely" asking guests to pay up and leave is nothing but a rude gesture and someone believing this is good practice in the restaurant business should perhaps not be training the Maître D'?
I apologize for loosing my cool.

I think this place is definitely more on the trendy end.

My friend and I love Japanese food, so we were eager to try this.  We came with another friend and got slammed with an hour wait but muscled through it with mediocre nachos and overpriced guac so we could try it out.  Looking back, I'm not sure if it was worth it..

Firstly, the bartenders need some more experience.  I ordered their Pimm's Ginger, and it's hard to fuck up that drink.  Something was off in mine, however, and I had to struggle to finish it.  It tasted like a sour ginger ale gone wrong, with little to no alcohol.  Fail.

I ordered the chicken udon, and it was underwhelming.  I liked the broth and thick noodles, but the chicken was thick and tough, and not at all enjoyable to chew through.  It was just your standard bowl of udon that you could buy in bulk at a packaged price in your local Asian supermarket.

In fact, I think I'll stick to that instead.  No desire to spend upwards of $20 on a bowl of udon.

Had a great experience here!! The food was so delicious and extremely filling. At first, I was overwhelmed by the variety of options we had! There were the classic udon, the udon with curry, hot stir fried udon, and even cold udon! After much deliberation, my friend and I decided to go with the classic deluxe and the wagyu beef curry! Needless to say, they were both so delicious, especially the curry one!! Also- they let you upgrade your noodle portion to a large one without an extra charge which is great if you had a huge appetite. My friend and I ended up leaving a lot behind but it was delicious!! But be careful when you order cause they don't let you take leftovers home!! We also had the sashimi salad WHICH WAS DELICIOUS!!  Must have!! And two glasses of sake, overall a great dinner with great ambience ~~
It was fine. Nothing special. Found the food to be pretty bland. Also, they move you through the meal like you're on an assembly line.

Tsuru Ton Tan in Roppongi was my go-to last lunch any time I traveled to Tokyo on business, so I was thrilled to hear it opened in NYC.

TLDR, the udon is great, what they do with it is hit or miss, and definitely not a Japanese experience. 

I'd go back for the udon because it's the best (only?) place for Japanese udon here, loved the cold uni udon and couldn't eat cold mentaiko udon - will be selective about choices. Definitely get thick noodles.

I had the uni cold udon -- it would have been a tragedy to mess that one up, you're getting $24 of uni plus udon. Creamy sauce at bottom with nice chunks.

Mentaiko udon did have a good amount of mentaiko, but the sauce was super mayo-y, overwhelmingly so, and I was sad not to be able to have more than one taste, the mayo was so strong (full disclosure, mayo is my kryptonite - but it also shouldn't taste like that, and doesn't in Japan). $16.

Also, they have this "large for no charge" -- actually in Japan they tell you one "tama" (ball of udon) or two are same price, but here, the large is not two tama-worth, and pretty standard size. Two large udons wasn't too much for two petite women.

One strange side note - we asked for tea at the end and they served us an un-drinkable houjicha -- way oversteeped, have never experienced anything like it :/

It was a 30 min wait for late lunch, and looks like you can make a reservation if you call two hours in advance

Bar only serves drinks and appetizers (no udon)

My ratings on Udon places in NY would go like this:

1. Raku
2. Udon West
3. Tsuruotontan

I got the curry deluxe udon here and found the broth too thick. The texture of the noodles were a bit quick to turn mushy even though they were cut thicker than normal.  We also started with the sukiyaki beef buns which could have been executed better. Pretty obvious they were pre-made and were being kept somewhere because by the time they came, they were at room temperature (cold).

Overall, it wasn't too bad but not worth the premium prices they are charging.

Alright guys.... I love UDON! Udon is an important part of a balanced diet. :) My fave to start with is the  SPICY TUNA TARTARE CONE, which has avocadoe puree and purple shiso. For udon, the two I liked the most was the WAGYU SHABU UDON and the MENTAIKO CAVIER CREME DELUXE. Both delicious are perfect in the cold weather. Will definitely go back when I'm in NY again for work. ENJOY!

Fantastic food. I'd definitely get everything with Uni. The uni noodles are the number one way to go. Appetizers are questionable, but I don't need to tell you that because Pete Wells already did.

Uni noodles, and get yourself a reservation, you'll need it!

Loving the fat noodles here :D This place is more of a lunch place for me. I feel like there are more options during lunch (I could be wrong). The menu with pictures make everything look so good!! This is evil. I had such a hard time choosing. 

Eventually I got the sizzling sukiyaki with fat udon. You can get the large portion with no extra cost. That's what I did and the bowl was huge!! It was really yummy. I love the sweet soy sauce taste yum. My cousin got the truffle creme with mushroom. The truffle wasn't too overpowering and the soup wasn't too thick. I like it but I like mine better lol. They don't let you take home any leftovers because of quality control. We all know that's bs. They don't want you to order a large portion and take the remaining back hehe. 

The price may be higher than normal but I think it's justified by the quantity and quality. Definitely go for the thick udon!!

The dishes were just meh and didn't reach the status of being a good bowl of udon. Although the restaurant is nice and modern the service and food left something to be desired. I had heard that the service was really awful but gave the restaurant the benefit of the doubt. The service ended up being horrible, the servers at this restaurant could ruin even the best food experience. Too bad since the concept is actually cool. If you want good udon go to Raku in the east village.

If you're looking for a good bowl of ramen, this will be your spot. I came to try the new udon spot in town and it was slightly underwhelming compared to the reviews I read and the hype. 

I came with my best friend and tried the tuna tartare, which was good, but nothing too special. Then I ordered the uni udon and she ordered the creme deluxe. The uni udon was simple and refreshing but too plain for my liking. The creme deluxe was so good, I wish I ordered that. 

I think the food is overpriced for but you get, and if I were given the choice, I would definitely get something else unless I'm craving udon.

The food is good as always, I had no problem with that. We were asked to wait because we had one person missing that came late, which is fine, that's their policy to only seat full parties. But once we were seated, the waitress did not come to check on us for at least 5 minutes, I had to waive down the bus boy 3 times to ask when our waitress can take our order, he just said that she's busy (taking other people's orders) and will be with us right away. After another few minutes, they finally sent another waiter to our table, saying that our waitress is too busy. 

The service was not good on this visit, yes I get it they are busy (then hire more people!). Our waitress basically just brought us the spoons for the noodle soups, water, and bowls. By the time we got our check, another waitress had taken over the shift. I'm paying 15% tip for bringing us spoons, water and bowls? I enjoy the food here, but the service on busy nights is somewhat chaotic, you can't let people who've already been waiting more than half hour to be seated to wait another 10 minutes before your waitress even comes by to say hi, and your customer needs to waive down your bus boy 3 times to get their attention, that's not acceptable, period!!!

Such a fan of this place and can't wait to come back and try other things on the menu. Came here with my friend on a friday night with no reservations and was quoted a 45 min wait. The waiting area was up front and it was huge. There was quite a lot of people waiting and i didn't feel cramped up at all. There was also a bar up front where you can grab a drink while waiting for a table. 45 min came by quick and my name was called. The host said there are bar seats available and if we wanted to sit there. We told him it wasn't a problem and was seated right away. We were given our menu and ordered right away. We ordered the buns, sushi (salmon and snowcrab roll) and the curry deluxe udon. The buns came first. It was 2 for 10$. Something i wouldn't get again. It came out a bit cold  and the flavor was lacking. Next came the sushi and boy was that goood. I wanted another roll but 18$ for one roll was kinda steep. The udon took pretty long. We were done with our drinks and apps. When it finally came you can smell the aroma just bursting out of the bowl. The bowl was hugeeeee. Twice the size of the hands. The udon didn't have much favor. Next time i'll make sure to go with the thin noodle. The thick udon was just too much. Cant wait to come back. I'll make sure to make reservations next time.

Overall rating:
Food: 8/10
Decor: 10/10 
Pricing:7/10 
Service: 7/10

Delicious Udon! Can't go wrong with the quality of the food and the cocktails are delicious too. Can get very crowded - hard to get in without a reservation even for lunch. Staff still seems to be learning the ups and downs of working since a new place - but very satisfied and will definitely go here regularly. Can't beat that tempura udon!

We had a reservation at 8.45 and at 9.20 we had to leave Bc we weren't getting our table. After asking the host 3 times, all she said was that there were people with reservations even earlier and that she didn't know when we could be sat. Very disappointing and frustrating for a party of 6 in NYC a Friday night.

Came here for lunch, seemed like a good option in Union square for a warm winter meal.
We were seated in the lower section, and we were the only people in the whole room (at 2:30pm, prime lunch time!) which is never a good sign..

Ordered several appetizers including the shisito peppers, tuna tacos and the shrimp dumplings to share. Dumplings were the best out of all of them. 
For main I ordered Kaisen Don which came with a small bowl of udon noodles on the side. Fish quality wasn't very good so I did not eat much of the bowl, but the udon noodles were better then the main so I ended up eating those instead.

I was visiting my sister in New York and she made a reservation for us here about a week earlier! Once we got there, we were seated right away, right by the windows, where it was pretty spacious, but not as pretty as the other areas of the restaurant. I ordered the Sukiyaki Udon and got to try the Tsurutontan Deluxe, Tsuruton Creme Deluxe. There were two size options, regular size and large size, which were priced the same. They said that the only difference was that there would be more udon noodles for the large. I was first nervous that it would be too much food but it wasn't! I liked the presentation: the HUGE udon bowls, HUGE spoons, and the chopsticks that were placed on a single rock. They also gave complimentary oolong tea, which was nice.

The food here is amazing!! You can't go wrong with any of the noodles. The sukiyaki noodles have a sweet, clear broth, juicy and tender beef slices, and perfectly cooked udon noodles. I've been here three times, and haven't had a dish that's disappointed me yet!! My favorite is the soondoobu udon and the uni udon - give them a try! They also offer extra udon at no additional charge, but they do not offer takeaway so eat what you can!

The wait can get quite long, so be sure to make a reservation in advance!

I'm obsessed!! I love Udon and this place, taste so good, amazing!! I can't wait to go back again, it's big and comfortable to sit down too, friendly stuffs, it's not cheap for Udon but I think it is worth paying for here!

I just came back from lunch here today and we sat on the 2nd floor. People have been raving about this place to me but never had an opportunity to try until now. I'm also not a big fan of udon so didn't care too much for it. But because of this place, I grew to love it. First my husband and I started off with their spicy tuna cones and they were delicious. It had guacamole in it which made it extra tasty. For entree, I ate the sukiyaki udon and my husband got the tsurutontan deluxe. My sukiyaki one came with beef, egg and veggies and my husband's had everything from beef, chicken, shrimp tempura to assorted vegetable tempura. Both of ours came in big bowls. We also had wonderful service. I would definitely go back again and try their other udons.

If I can give a negative star, I would totally do it. I did not get a chance to sit down to try their food. but I had an awful experience with their services and arrangement. We were a group of 10 and we knew it can be difficult to get a table for our group. so we called and asked how long is the wait. they said it may take about 30 mins and max 45 mins. not too bad. so we went there and waited for 1.5 hours!!!!!!!!!!!!! (and still couldn't get a table) we talked to the waiter and all they kept telling us the other table is not ready yet and as soon as they leave, they can get us seated. 

the point is, why did u tell me it takes max 45 mins and end up making us wait for more than 1.5 hrs!!! why can't they manage the seats better? everyone around us and customers who even came in later than us already got their seats and we WERE STILL STANDING AND WAITING. ( we waited from 7:30-9 and all of us were really hungry) 

we even talked to the manager and they didn't seem to feel sorry about their poor management and arrangement, especially the tall girl with black curly hairs. This girl did not apologize AT ALL and gave us an attitude. 

Totally unacceptable !!!!

Rude service.   Place is empty and you are seated directly next to another close table. Yes they move you and then seat another couple on top of you, who then ask to be moved this continues throughout the meal.  Food is delicious
Udon noodles were great and so were the portion sizes. Wasn't a fan of the broth. Prices are a little high - I was in Tokyo and had better udon for $4-6.

Really enjoy the noodles here. I've been here quite a few times... wasn't satisfied with hostess service this time at all, sad to say. I thought the hostess was rude to customers - she dragged on wait times (yes, it can be hard to tell but her answers were was basically I don't know / I'm not sure, in the two times I asked), she didn't even look at me (and all the other customers) when I was (they were) talking to her / seemed disengaged and didn't care at all. Her tone was mildly annoyed from what I can tell and it was quite a displeasing experience since I've had positive experiences with the hostess on my previous visits. This won't turn me away from coming back here since the food and wait staff are awesome. Maybe the business should hire more friendly and polite hostesses.

On the other hand, our waiter, Kyle, was awesome. He made sure we had everything we needed, before we even asked for it. He checked in with us to make sure the meal was good and up to our expectations. This was a sharp contrast in customer service.

Stumbled upon this ramen joint after doing some yelping. The reviews looked good so we decided to try it for dinner. Once we entered we weren't warmly greeted and quoted a 30-45 minute wait time or could be less as per the hostess with bright red lipstick. We waited in the area for some time and I feel like they really waited to seat us until we waited the full 45 minutes. I can understand if it was busy, but when I went downstairs to use the restroom there were many seats available. There was also an empty booth and empty stools. I don't understand why you would make two people wait the 45 minutes, when one you have available seating. I can understand why you wouldn't seat 2 people in a booth, but in those single chairs? Those two hostess girls weren't very friendly and just chatted with each other. 
When it came our turn to be seated, they put us in those single bar stool chairs! Common, you couldn't have done that earlier. Also they put us right next to a couple, which I usually don't mind but there was no body else being seated at the bar stools. 

When it came time to ordering, we both ordered a bowl of udon and shared the spicy tuna cones. The appetizer came out pretty quickly and tasted pretty good. There were four spicy tuna cones in a crispy shell with an avocado puree at the tip. The udon can be thick or thin in thickness and regular or large in size. The price is the same for both. The portions are big for a regular as I couldn't finish it. However, they do not allow any to-go boxes. 

Overall experience was Meh. The hostesses really irked me.

Even though this is an udon place, I actually enjoy their apps more than their udon. The seared wagyu sushi with uni is SO delicious. Not cheap, but definitely worth it. I also enjoy the gobo and guacamole immensely. The spicy tuna tartare cone and tatsuta fried chicken are both decent. The only thing I would not order again is the "Uni and Caviar." While pretty to take a picture of, the taste is nothing special.

For the udon, it's always dilemma for me deciding on hot or cold. The borth is definitely better in the hot udon, but the noodle texture is definitely better in the cold udon...The uni udon was just okay for me. While I love uni, the broth did not have enough flavor. I like the broth of the sukiyaki udon a lot, but the noodles were too soft. Meh.

But even if this is not my favorite udon place, I'll keep coming back for the apps.
Great udon. Although udon is not my favorite noodle. Lots of options, just to tempt me to come back and try more plates on the menu. Service is very courteous.

A lot of people are on the waiting list. And a lot of tables are ready. But they kept people waiting. They called people not by the list. I wasn't the last one on the list, but I was the last one to be seated. 

Food was ok. Hope they can raise the level of their service.

There is a big problem here.  First of all, when we arrived on a Monday night,  they told us that we would have to wait because there were no tables and they had 100 reservations for that night.  There were empty tables then and during our meal. Lots of them.  And some remained empty from the time of our arrival until our departure.   They just wanted us to sit at the bar and spend money.  Second, and I have NEVER seen anything like this.   Both small and large portions cost the same and you are not allowed to bring any leftovers home.  This is really outrageous.  People who run this restaurant listen up:   this is New York City. We don't do things this way.  Finally, while the udon soup was delicious and beautifully presented, my soup had 1 small  piece of fish and 1 teeny piece of chicken.  Are  you kidding me?  The prices look good, but when you consider that you are basically getting a bowl of soup and noodles for $20 plus, that is really outrageous.  I would love to love this place.  But their M O  is really poor.

Three reasons you'll continue to see most Japanese folks at Raku and even Udon West despite Tsurutontan's entrance into the NY market: price point, service, simplicity. 

Sure, Tsurutontan is swanky and their bowls are on point. Their noodles are noticeably freshly made too. But Udon West is cheaper, its service kinder and quicker, and its options simpler. Plus they allow takeout teehee. Easy choice for me to make.
I was so disappointed.....the katsu curry udon....the katsu was too dry i couldn't even chewed.....i was so sad.....u guys has to make it better....

Save your money and buy the frozen udon. I had the curry udon and it was terrible. If youre interested in this dish, do yourself a favor and just buy the frozen udon and the pre-made japanese curry sauce. Btw, terrible service.
Delicious Udon made in house. First time there and tried fried chicken, tofu burrata, sizzling sukiyaki Udon that is brothless, and nabeyaki udon. Excellent service. Look forward to returning.

The hype was not real..for the uni udon, I honestly think you can skip this dish and save yourself the money. 

For everything else, Tsurotontan has got it DOWN. Their udons come in these wonderfully ginormous ceramic bowls. Just order different kinds of udon with your friends and just share them! 

My absolute favorite was the sukiyaki udon -so savory, sweet and slurp-y. 

Definitely a great spot to dine at with friends!

We made a reservation for 8 but still ended up waiting around for a good 30 minutes anyway. Even after we were seated the service was so slow. I was so hungry I couldn't bear it.

The decor inside is really cute but the tables inside seemed a little too high.

I started off with the spicy tuna cones. It was good but nothing that blew my mind. I thought we got jipped when I realized after one bite there was no more tuna left but only avocado. But then I realized halfway there was another level of tuna yay!

We ordered the wagyu suki yaki udon and the curry udon. The suki yaki was a little sweet but still good. I liked the curry one better with the donkatsu and shrimp tempura in it.

I love my mules so I ordered the Tokyo Mule. They put cucumber in it and I don't really like cucumbers but it was a good drink.
Ok the wait was long but!!! The uni udon from the cold section is amazing!! All the udons are awesome!!

KenScale: 8.0/10

New York City already has a ton of ramen shops but you don't often see a place that focuses on udon, another popular Japanese noodle dish characterized by thicker noodles and broths with more moderate flavor compared to ramen. When a popular chain in Japan decided to open its first U.S. outpost in the space that previously had the acclaimed Union Square Café (which has since moved to another location), I was somewhat intrigued. I've always been more of a ramen person than an udon person since I preferred thinner noodles and liked the flavor of ramen broth a bit more, but in the case of Tsurutontan, this chain also offered a lot of unique dishes such as the signature one with mentaiko (salted roe used frequently in Japanese cuisine) caviar, all in humongous bowls. Since the shop opened last summer, though, it had been constantly packed with crowds so I was waiting for the hype to die down in order to avoid waiting for hours outside. I think that time has finally come; I was able to book a table in early Saturday dinner time online about only a couple of days in advance. So did this place live up to the hype? My girlfriend and I overall liked the experience here and the udon dishes that I had tried were certainly delicious.

What immediately caught our eyes on the visit was how large the range of udon selections is on the menu. You'll see more standard ones with beef, chicken, duck or shrimp tempura, or other more adventurous selections that employ sukiyaki or curry style. I even saw dishes that had truffle crème or chicken parm! Obviously, it's important to know what you're eating from this vast menu, and we were glad that both of our dishes were a success. The signature mentaiko udon with egg dropped broth was a perfect antidote to a chilly winter; I really enjoyed the aromatic broth that had nice balance of flavor without any hint of overpowering seasoning. My girlfriend thoroughly enjoyed the curry deluxe udon dish as well, served with shrimp tempura, pork cutlet and beef inside the delicious curry that also wasn't overly heavy or salty to our delight. In addition, the firmness of noodles for both dishes was more or less spot on. Even though the size of each bowl looked pretty intimidating at first, I'm happy to report and my girlfriend and I nearly finished the entire thing! We also had some starters before the udons came in but I wouldn't recommend stuffing yourselves with these. Cucumber salad and sukiyaki beef buns were serviceable but I found the seared salmon sashimi with ikura caviar, garlic chips, chives and ponzu to be a little too citrusy for my taste.  

As noted above, getting a reservation at Tsurutontan has become more manageable, and you'll even have a much better chance than last year in snagging a walk-in spot (there is a large communal table at the subterranean area of the restaurant). It's a typical Japanese casual food joint atmosphere like Ippudo. A glass of beer or a small bottle of hot sake should be a great complement to your meal. Lately, Manhattan has seen a lot of influx from popular food chains in Asia, and I find Tsurutontan to be a welcome addition to the scene with its unique offerings of udon dishes.

Really enjoyed the appetizers (uni and caviar and spicy shrimp tempura- didn't taste spicy though). The udon was delicious, but it was udon. Like everyone else, my friend said the sukiyaki udon tasted a bit too sweet. Regular sized bowls was more than enough for us. Very nice atmosphere, great service and an overall very pleasant experience.

So I stumbled upon this place while trying to find a place to go for dinner with my girlfriend. She loves udon so I figured why not try the place that took over where Union Square Cafe used to be.

This restaurant is beautiful, the venue is done so tastefully and it feels very comfortable. It is on the pricier side for sure but so are all the specialist ramen shops in NYC. It's nice to see a place that excels in udon, even better that they're from Japan.

We got the spicy tuna tartar cones which were excellent. The wonton cone broke so delicately and mixed with the spicy tuna and micro greens. It's expensive, $3 per cone but really good. We also tried the grilled duck breast which came with fresh wasabi and lemon.

On to the noodles. I think it's awesome that you can pick the thinner udon and the nice fat ones too. I tried the creme deluxe which I thought was cool, I had never seen this sort of broth before. She got the uni udon with the ikura. 

The creme broth was delicious and complimented the wide noodles perfectly. There was chicken, roe, shrimp and salmon in mine. The uni one was good but I barely got to try any. I asked her if she wanted to switch and she said "no" in between slurps. Mission accomplished.

On a side note, I overheard someone ordering a soondubu jigae udon - I need to come back and try this.

I was a bit disappointed with Tsurutontan. The inside is beautiful. Like wow. And the waiters are super friendly.

I really like spicy food, and I immediately went for the spciy soondubu jigae udon which has beef, vegetables, and spicy broth. Except it wasn't spicy. It just looked spicy. In fact, there wasn't much flavor at all. And it was pretty pricey. I was disappointed.

the food was great! portions are ginormous...bring an appetite!
-----------------------
went back to tsurutontan and had really terrible service. walked in around 7PM and our server Kyle did not check up on us, or our order, never gave us water, had to grab his attention every single time. we waited 40 mins for our appetizer then another 40 for our udons to come out. i saw 3 tables in front of me and next to our seats, coming, eating and leaving.

good was great but downgrading my review to a 3stars bc of the terrible, terrible service.

I think the food is generally quite strong (the hot apps I love!). But a noodle shop should be evaluated on the strength and consistency of its noodles, right?

Been here twice now and the consistency was off.  First time the udon was perfect - chewy with bite, like and Italian al dente.  Second time they were too soft, as if soggy or soaked for 5 minutes too long.


Note that any noodle dish can be ordered regular or large at no extra charge, the extras cannot be taken home however.

My standouts udons -  the cold mentaiko and uni udons.

First,  the interior is gorgeous and the staff were extremely nice and friendly.  I ordered a Mentaiko Caviar udon and wasn't sure how I felt about cold noodles at first but there's something very soothing and satisfying about it. It was a little salty for me, but the flavor was still great. I will be back to try out the other udon on the menu.

It's really unclear whether people come for the food or the Instagram opportunities.

For me, the appetizers were the best part of the meal. The beef buns were good, but the tofu burrata was AMAZING.

For the udon, we ordered both the uni udon and the caviar udon. I'm a big fan of uni, but to be honest, the uni udon just wasn't quite flavorful enough for me or it felt like it was missing an ingredient. The caviar udon was excellent.

I thought this restaurant had a nice ambiance going on. It seemed like a place I would have gone to meet up for drinks or a date.

I came here with my friend who had suggested this place for dinner. We made a reservation, and I totally recommend doing this because this place gets filled up really fast after a certain time!

I am a boring udon person and am looking for specific udon flavor profiles, so sadly I did not try the crazy caviar udon or anything. If I do, it might change my review, but for now it'll stay.

One of my favorite udon is Kitsune, the one with the giant piece of tofu in the bowl. I got it and thought it was decent but nothing special and thus a bit overpriced. The bowl was about $14. I did order the large for no extra charge and got a lot of noodles.

I think the broth was missing something, some pizazz that I usually look for in udon. I also didn't find the broth to be that hot either. I like my soups hot despite it posing extreme danger to my mouth. 

We also ordered the water cake. This was fun... But not worth a reoccurring purchase. It's cool to look at, I mean translucent orb on your table, sure why not! I was a bit disappointed with the flavor. Alone, it tasted like flavorless jello. The bean curd powder and the Japanese maple syrup didn't enhance it that much. I actually thought the maple syrup was not tasty (you should have seen my WTF IS THIS face). There was something incredibly off putting about it. But don't take my word for it! The ice cream on the side was tasty though.

Service was good. 

I really wanted to give this place a 3.5 rating but wasn't super keen on returning anytime soon. If I do try other flavors and find it better, then I could update accordingly.
I ordered Sukiyaki udon. Taste was ok, but a little bit oily. And when the broth getting colder, the taste became more salty. But the udon was very good.

I was really looking forward to eating here udon reading other reviews and I really wanted to like this place. I have had more than a fair share of udon in my life and I have been to many places both in Japan and in NYC. 

I believe this place is a good place to bring people to if they want to have solid Japanese food and they prefer having a variety of dishes centering Udon. 

I got a Shrimp kakiage udon since I love kakiage in general (when it is a good one). Udon and soup were 'good' (not good enough for me to pay that much, though). However, the kakiage was unnecessarily big and it did not have enough shrimp for it to be called 'shrimp' kakiage. I believe that if you want to serve such a big kakiage which was shaped like a square, it has to be very good. Since it was not (mostly just shredded vegetables soaking up vegetable oils and not much other textures to it, with the middle being mushy because of the shape), I could only eat half of it (I felt sick after eating it).  

I would probably still go back and order something else if the dishes were in the same price range they offer in Japan. I understand everything here has to be more expensive, but I would happily pay that much if it were better. Udon served Raku in East Village are priced quite similarly but I am OK paying that much for Udon at Raku. So if you just want to get some good udon in soup, I would recommend going to Raku instead. 

Again, I do think this place is still a good place to come and bring people to if you can find your favorite dishes here. But I still recommend avoiding Shrimp Kakiage.

Their food was great and filling. Loved that it came in big bowls because I always have trouble eating udon since it goes all over the place.. but with big bowls, everything stays in the big bowl. 

Service was great, they kept checking up on us to see if we needed anything! We made reservations so seating was quick. Would definitely come back again to fulfill an udon craving!

yea noodles!!

beautiful restaurant with a comfortable atmosphere~ the novelty hasn't died down for me yet~ still looking forward to my next visit to tsurutontan!  

it took me a while to try the 2 mentaiko udon dishes to write this review!  first, i am a HUGE fan of mentaiko! anything mentaiko i just have to try! my first visit, i had the mentaiko in egg drop broth.  it was good! not entirely what i expected but i still enjoyed it!  i was not super accustomed to the heavy flavor in the clear udon broth and tsurutontan definitely delivered a very rich and savory one!  the 2nd time, i got the creamy mentaiko udon.  this was definitely not traditional.  in fact, it was hardly japanese lol despite that, i absolutely loved it!  once i tasted the silky white soup, it instantly reminded me of the french signature dish, waterzooi.  and i would not be surprised if that's where the inspiration came from.  the broth was easy on the palate but it was no doubt umami packed! sweet aroma from the onions enveloped the subtle hint from the sea.  it pairs great with fish fillets like they have on the menu with salmon and shrimp!  rather than mixing the meitaiko into the soup, i left it where it was and just picked a tiny dab each time onto my spoonful of udon maximizing the raw mentaiko flavor. really yummm! every slurp was different yet the same.  a quick absence from slurping mentaiko let me appreciated the soup a little more.  pulling up the noodles that kept the mentaiko ball afloat covered in an abundance of the mini roes added an extra unami kick.  to simply put it, it was just a great bowl of noodles!

we also ordered the karaage (fried chicken) starter.  i was so intrigued by their pink tartar sauce and just had to try for myself!  made from shibazuke (pickled eggplant?) giving it the natural exotic hue.  the tartar sauce was lighter and creamier than the store bought ones.  the crunch in the dipping sauce was created with a plethora of chopped chives and something else(?) very unique! the dark meat chicken was fried in the typical izakya style leaving it very juicy.  i wished they gave us a lemon slice tho.  it was delicious but i would've loved some zest with it lol.  overall, very nicely done.  

the only thing i have to complain about tsurutontan is the price lol  it's unfortunate that it won't be a place i can dine at all the time but that'll keep me "waku waku" (excited with the glitter eyes) looking forward to the seldom visits.

tips: 1) make a ressie online to cut down on the wait~ 2) always order a large bowl of noodles b/c it's at no additional charge!! 

Happy slurping!

What a great deal of udon in the most ginormous bowl ever! Prepare yourself, either starve for the day and come to binge or order a couple appetizers then share a bowl of udon with someone. So great to have this place in NYC~ tons of crazy good for under 20 bucks!!

Thoroughly impressed with this place.

WAIT: Made reservations the day of (Monday) and got a 6:30 pm reservation.  By 7pm the place was pretty packed so make sure to make a reservation.  The inside dining area isn't huge so you could be waiting some time.

ATMOSPHERE: Hip music, low lighting, trendy/japanese minimalist wooden decor and overall trendy.  There are communal tables that face each other with this artsy piece in the middle to semi-block the view of the person in front.  

FOOD: They have a pretty extensive menu and appetizers.  What was cool was they have a little indication if it's a best seller.  They have 2 portion sizes and 2 types of udon.  Thin or thick, they recommend thick for the soups and thin for the cold noodles.  They also have a larger portion of udon for NO EXTRA COST! So crazy, why wouldn't you get the larger portion?!

SUKIYAKI STIR FRIED UDON - I love stir fried udon and it's hard to come by so this was a no brainer for me.  I think it was around $18 so a little more expensive than your typical bowl of udon, but I guess you're paying for atmosphere and quality.  The larger portion was definitely enough for 1 person and I was a little stuffed towards the end.  It comes with shredded beef (very tender and juicy), mushrooms, a poached egg, and some little napa cabbage.  The thick udon pieces were pretty chewy and fresh, but as good as the ones we had in Japan but pretty good.  There is a little bit of broth on the bottom that is fairly oily, but the rest of the dish was dry.

BEEF UDON - my husband got the larger portion and it comes in this HUGE bowl, very cool.  They also give you big spoons to eat out of.  The beef broth wasn't as flavorful as the sukiyaki broth but it had a light flavor.  It was still very tasty.

Overall, definitely recommend coming here if you like udon and have a little extra money to spend.  Come on a date night or a nice night out and enjoy yourself.

I was completely taken aback by the sheer size of the bowls of Udon that is served.  I am pretty sure that despite it being delicious my bowl of beef Udon was one of the Wonders of the World just from its hulking size.  

We started with salmon and snow crab roll for 16 dollars.  It was slightly pricey for only 8 pieces of sushi, but the mastery of flavors in this little roll were amazing.  The combination of sweet and salty was incredible.
The Udon was gigantic, but the beef Udon was a little plain and I think I would try one of the deluxe bowls.

All together it was a good Udon place for the area and I would recommend the sushi appetizers.

I have never seen such huge bowls of noodles before! Giant bowl and super thick udon noodles. I came here twice, first for dinner about a month after they opened and second time more recently for lunch. 

First time around there was a line at 5PM and lunch was not offered yet. Very trendy decor and attentive service. We ordered the Sukiyaki Udon and the Tsuruton Curry Deluxe, upgraded both of course. They gave us these big spoons (or shall I call them ladles?), but that did not prepare for how big our eyes got when the bowls were put in front of us. The noodles were chewy and we could barely finish both bowls! 

Second time around I came here for a work lunch. We ordered: 

Spicy tuna tartare cones - Crispy cone with a smooth avocado puree inside. Not very spicy nor  overfilled with spicy mayo (like spicy tuna rolls) 

Tofu Burrata - This did not look like the tofu in the menu. The tofu itself had the texture of flan and kind of looked like it too! It wasn't bad, but I guess I was expecting a little more when you call it burrata. 

Steamed Shrimp Dumplings - Thin dumpling skin with a nice plump shrimpy filling. 

Maguro Zuke Don (Soy marinated bigeye tuna, onsen egg on sushi rice) with a small udon - Smooth, slightly salty slices of tuna that melts in your mouth! I think I had two sips of broth and one or two strands of udon since I could barely eat after the tuna and rice. I definitely think two could share this set. 

Udon bowls are pricier than normal but given the amount of food, totally worth it. I would be back to try out the other udon noodles and seeing my friend's faces when the bowls come out!

This is the first time we visit this newly open Japanese Udon restaurant. We are impressed for their food and Udon noodle soup . We will be back to explore other new dishes. The sever is excellent ++++++++.

Decor is beautiful, trendy, hip. Make reservations or youll wait in line.

They have a pretty descent dinner menu, love their Nabeyaki and Chicken Udon Bowls are great! The white truffle oil as an add-on for $2, not bad!

Quaint hidden noodle and sushi spot in union square. First off, I love the ambience with an underground vibe. We started with some delicious sake and a sushi roll. The waiter knew his stuff and walked us through the whole menu keeping my diet restrictions in mind. He stayed with us until we truly understood everything the menu has to offer. The fish is super fresh which is the most important part of a tasty sushi dish. The ramen seems delicious but unfortunately we ordered a bowl where the broth was too sweet. I loved the thick noodles, but couldn't handle the sugary broth. The waiter was nice enough to take it off the bill. Great service, good menu, perfect date night spot.

Tofu Burrata, seared salmon w garlic chips, uni caviar - spectacular! The sizzling sukiyaki is hands down the favorite dish of the nite! The curry and Waygu udon are also winners -  the uni udon - is cold and not my fave (too fishy) but the house salad and famous chicken are both noteworthy.  For drinks - grab the Tokyo Mule and Lychee Rose. If ur looking for an alternative to ramen to brave this NYC winter - this joint hits the spot! I'm a fan and will definitely be back.

Tsurutontan is a trendy Japanese restaurant. it serves a variety of udon noodle courses from traditional Sukiyaki udon to frenchy Truffule Creme udon. I have eaten here 3 times and they never let me down. My fav. is cold noodle- Mentaikamatama udon.

It was a rainy day and the place is pretty huge, so we did not have to wait at all to be seated when we arrived here for dinner on a Sunday evening. Instead of the classic sukiyaki udon, our server highly recommended the spicy soondubu jigae udon and the sizzling sukiyaki udon. The uni udon caught my eye too, but I decided to give the sizzling sukiyaki udon a go. What I like about this place is that in addition to the traditional thick udon noodles, they also offer thin udon noodles! You also get to pick between regular or large serving (no difference in price). The sizzling sukiyaki udon was served in a hot stone pot with a mountain of udon, a raw egg yolk, beef slices, shimeji mushroom, onion and leeks. Definitely unconventional but tasty.. Albeit a little oily. Even with a regular portion, I couldn't finish my noodles. I was expecting more vegetables though (just like what you'd get in the sukiyaki with broth).

Oh, they also tell you upfront that they don't do takeaways. So do take note!

Maybe I should go back and give them another try? 
Nah, it's okay. To me, this please is too fancy, and I think the portion is way too big for a bowl of Udon. 

*Don't take my words too serious, I'm more like a classic-Udon person.

Loved the limited time hot and sour udon. If you are a fan of hot and sour soup, this is the right choice for you. The spicy tuna cones are overpriced in my opinion, but quite tasty.

Waited for around 45 minutes for a seat on a saturday night around 8pm. The waiting area around the bar is pretty roomy. 

Compared to udon west, the price point is about double, but the quality is also better. If you just want a quick meal, this is not the place for you since the udon takes a while to be served.

This place is worth a try. They have such a wide variety of udon and was very tasty. The service was great and they were attentive. I wanted to try everything but 6 of us shared 4 udon, one rice dish, 3 apps and 2 deserts and I was still hungry but again the food was really good. They had thick and thin and the thick ones were really thick but you should try both thickness. The presentation was very pretty in huge bowls. I would definitely come back here again!

Reservations online
Great portions
Amazing udon (some people say its too firm to be authentic but you know what ITS BETTER THIS WAY). 

Service is great!
Appetizers might be a little pricey but the udon is amazing

This place was a little ridiculous.  The menu is  huge although it is a plus they had glossy attractive pictures but they had so many labeled with top sellers, it is a little overwhelming. The portions like everyone has mentioned in their reviews, are in fact ginormous and probably can feed a whole clan of guatemalan relatives.  If you want to know why Americans are overweight, then this is the place for you. Prices are in the $$ range but it is probably a good deal for the LARGE amount of food you are getting, but then again, can you really finish it all? Plus, they make it super easy for to size up and get more noodles!! but remember, doesn't matter how LARGE the trough of noodles is, you CANNOT take any of it home.  What a waste of noodles.  The point is, the food is decent and you can get your noodle/udon fix here, but the novelty of the portions are a little crazy.  The food is good is definitely good for the value- aka a goo deal. There have also rolls and sushi options, if you get overwhelmed- maybe just get one of the many top sellers!!?

When I first heard Tsurutontan opened in the former Danny Meyer location, I was curious to try their udon. Especially, because I heard it is their first location in United States. Most Japanese restaurants trending are ramen places, however this restaurant takes another approach and specializes in udon. Personally, I love noodles and it is one of my guilty pleasures. I went with a couple of friends and the moment we got there, it was a line waiting for dinner to open. The interior design is fascinating, the modern take and simplicity makes it unique. I love the idea of serving their udon in enormous bowls with spoons. I tried the Uni Udon, which is considered their best seller, it was great. The creamy texture, savory and the Uni balanced well with the udon.  For appetizers, the Tatsuta Fried Chicken and Ribeye Steak were perfect, they were the best. 

Also, I love the fact the menu has a variety of udons to choose from, makes it hard to decide what to eat! If you like, I would recommend ordering different udons to share for the table. I will be coming back again!

Love this place!! Have had a number of things - udon, a don rice bowl, the tuna tartar, shishito... everything has been delicious! Definitely make a reservation if you can - the wait can be long but with a res they sit you pretty quickly. It's a little loud, but that's the only complaint I have!

3 1/2

tuna tartare cones were cute and tasty. Better than expected, but on the pricier side for what it is.

got the deluxe. It was decent-good. Worth returning? Not sure.

Definitely worth a visit! The restaurant itself is beautifully decorated.  The menu is quite intensive - it took us longer than normal to make an actual decision on what to get since everything looked so good!  Our waiter was also very helpful and forewarned us that the portions were on the larger side so we had no surprised when we ordered our meal.  I ended up with a udon dish while my friend had ordered curry. All in all - a great meal and a place I highly recommend to friends and family in the area.

The dashi broth was flavorless, and the giant bowls/spoons were cumbersome to use. My companions similarly unimpressed with their meals. It was ~$100 for 3 for lunch, and we only had water to drink. I would not return.

I really did not want to like this place because of the ridiculous long wait!!! But I am here to report it is awesome!!! 
Finally my friends and I got to the restaurant closer to 9 pm on a Tuesday so luckily there was no wait. We decided to order three different udon dishes to try. They have this weird policy where you can upgrade the noodle portion for a dollar more. We couldn't resist the temptation so we decided to go to Large for all our dishes.

Uni Udon - small uni on top but still was delicious. It was a cold noodle dish. I did not think i would like cold udon dish with Uni bc it was winter and I was craving something warm but it turned out really amazing

Sukiyaki Udon - tbh for my taste, it was little too sweet. But it was still super tasty. Not my favorite but my friends were really enjoying it. 

Soondubu udon - as a korean, I have to say it was not the best soondubu but I don't think it was trying to be. The taste was just right for what it was trying to do. It went so well with udon noodles. If you are a spicy food lover, a must try.

3.5 Stars

I've been to Tsurutontan about five times now and while their noodles aren't the greatest, I find myself coming back for the satisfying soup, comfortable atmosphere, and convenient location.

I really love a good bowl of noodles and I can't think of any other place in NYC that focuses on udon. Really good udon is supposed to be slippery with a lovely chewy texture. Unfortunately, the noodles here aren't like that - they seem to be missing the delightful texture and slipperiness. The noodles taste rather dull and flat. Though the advertisement on the wall says "made in-house", it tastes like refrigerated udon.

I do enjoy the udon soup though which I always drink all of - a wonderful combination of kombu and dashi flavor. I tend to get the Tsurutontan Deluxe ($24) - I love the shrimp tempura and tempura breading that softens in the soup. The beaten egg white with thin slices of beef also tastes good. 

I've also tried their sushi rolls, most recently the salmon one. Pretty good. 

I like the atmosphere here, it's designed in a way that feels cozy, comfortable, casual, yet intimate. Of course, the food is overpriced...20+ dollars for a bowl of udon is ridiculous!

Just ok. I love Uni and I was beyond excited to have the Uni noodle. It was good but nothing amazing. Need a little bit of salt. Share a bunch of appetizers. The shisito pepper were just fine. Fried chicken was also fine. The most disappointing dish was the sashimi dish. It was as not worth $26. There was just 9 thinly sliced pieces of fish and the dressing was too much even though I asked to be light on the dressing. Overall it was just ok. I would not go back. Staff was nice but if the food is just ok I'm just going to go back Edie silly when it's expensive.

I have been here a couple of times. This place definitely is one of the best udon places in NYC. Really cool thing about this place is that you can get a huge portion (at least the bowl itself is huge) of udon for no extra charge. So, make sure to get large udon instead of the regular. Their cold uni udon is particularly good. I think all the other hot udons are great. Price is very reasonable as well. One thing to know in advance is that you would want to make a reservation before you go because although the place is spacious, the seats fill up very quickly and the line is usually quite long. Great udon place!
Wow what a cool place. Food comes fast and furious! Portions are rather large. Wait stuff is awesome , and atmosphere is extra star! So happy to have a new place on union sq !

Excellent. Must eat. 

Make a reservation! We came here on a weekday lunch and it was packed. Took a few minutes to get seated with reservation. Service was excellent. Friendly knowledgeable staff. Our meal was served fast. Delicious noodles.

We went here at 10:30PM on a warm Saturday night. There was no waiting line as many seats were available. 
The ambience was chic and enjoyable, modern yet not overwhelming. It had a meticulously lit interior with stylish wall decorations. The furnitures and kitchenwares were artistically selected, paired well together to create a whole contemporary fine dining look. 
Appetizers were all great. Udon can be a bit miss and hit. Service was friendly and attentive. The water cake dessert was very fun to look at but not so impressive on the taste. 
Overall given the environment, food, service, price, I had a wonderful experience here.

Waited over 15 minutes for our table despite making reservations.  Good thing we didn't have any other plans.

Most of the food was excellent.  Our group shared the Sukiyaki Beef Buns, Cauliflower Tempura, and Creamy Shrimp Tempura starters which we all enjoyed.  For my entree I ordered the Sizzling Sukiyaki Udon.  I'm not sure why it's called 'Sizzling', but it was delicious regardless.  Others enjoyed the regular Sukiyaki Udon and the Mentaiko Anake Udon; however, those who tried the Katsu Don found the pork extremely salty.

Our server was friendly and attentive and happily took the time to explain the difference in rice grades that account for the varying prices among their sake selection.

Overall it was a good experience, delay in seating notwithstanding, and we'd definitely try it again.

I've heard great things about this place and waited a few months before I decided to try it. Was seated immediately and ordered the grilled duck breast, mushroom udon, tsurutonton deluxe udon, wagyu sushi and the seared salmon sashimi. The udon was not bad but I did not think it was amazing. I didn't like that they included an egg in it because by the time it got to the table it was overcooked in the broth. Was also not a fan of the random ingredients in the broth such as the overcooked chicken and the soggy tempura. The grilled duck breast lacked flavor but was cooked to a nice temperature. The seared salmon was below average, not a fan of the sauce. The best was the wagyu sushi, sorta pricy but it has a nice clean flavor.

Would come back again to try other appetizers and just order one udon for the table because the portion was HUGE

A bit underwhelming really.  The aesthetic inside is nice, but there is a lot of waiting.  This was actually the second time we tried to go after not being able to hack the long wait time the first time. 

Appetizers of sushi and tempura at the bar was nice while we waited for a table.  Although we did not try them, the cocktails looked strong and well made.

Again, waited a long time from order to eat.  Food was clean and tasty however.  Unfortunately there was not much choice for non-meat broth udon.  I would not recommend the tofu udon.  Eel sushi was nice and sweet, but the salmon and crab was kind of bland.  One highlight was the tuna tartare cones, would recommend.  

Overall, there are better Japanese options for the price and atmosphere. 

Sumiko 69

Absolutely loved this Place... the food, the decor, the staff, the ambiance. Couldn't get better. The staff is so attentive and they really care about your dine-in experience. Came here on a Friday night with my bf and we were treated so well. We ordered apps, main courses, drinks, and dessert.. and let me tell you... everything was AMAZING. Can't wait to go back!
Great ambience. But overpriced for overcooked UDON.

For Fridays and Saturdays, I would suggest making a reservation a couple of days ahead especially during prime dining hours. We saw a couple of families getting turn away since they were all booked that night. We were promptly seated and our friendly server did a good job with explaining everything since it was our first time. We ordered the following:

1. Tatsuta Fried Chicken - Average in flavor and tenderness. Didn't care for their purple dipping sauce. 
2. Sea & Truffle Sushi Roll - My favorite dish of the night. The truffle oil and nuts made the dish unique and tasty. 
3. Salmon & Snow Crab Sushi Roll - Good but didn't taste the spice at all in their spicy sauce
4. Seared US Wagyu Sushi - Underwhelm and was a little too greasy for me. 
5. Cucumber Salad - $7 bucks is expensive for a tiny thing of cucumbers even when it tasted good. 
6. Sukiyaki Udon - Enjoyed the thin udon noodles. Broth was slightly too sweet for me. 
7. Wagyu Shabu Udon - I enjoyed the clear fish broth better than the Sukiyaki. 
8. Water Cake - The "water" gelatin is flavorless so you have to pour the Kinako powder and syrup over it. Vanilla ice cream served with it. Not my cup of tea since I didn't care for the kinako powder.

We ordered the large portion size for both udon orders and split between 4 people. It was plenty since we had so many appetizers too.

Me and my wife just went here over the weekend.  We had just came back from our honeymoon in japan in October and we were craving something that reminded us of our time there.  we heard about this place and man does it deliver!  The udon noodles were cooked to perfection and the accompanying meat was tender and full of flavor, and who can for get the broth, the broth tasted like it was stewed for hours.  It was the perfect meal for a cold winters day!!! we would definitely come back and recommend this place to my friends

Katsu don was a bit salty but overall it was ok. I would ask if they could make the katsu son less salty next time though... Atmosphere is great and everything else is good. However, they don't have take our boxes, I guess it's a Japanese culture thing
Great food, fast service, cute ambiance! Book reservation though it gets packed!

Their signature dish, Uni Udon, was not impressed, although the dish was very creative. It is too heavy to finish this dish alone, as I felt a little sick at the end of dinner.  Daikon Hamachi was awesome. Beef was just right. Very pricy but beautiful restauran

Wow, I love TsuruTonTan! Where do I even start??

I love the modern decor of the restaurant. It made me think it might be an expensive place, it is not. I found the prices quite reasonable for what you actually get.

They serve their noodles in these hilariously large bowls. I was worried that the place is only popular because it was a gimmicky thing to do, but my worries disspiated once I took my first bite...it was very delicious!

I ordered the Nabeyaki Udon - it was jammed packed with accompaniments. It's got two shrimp tempuras, soft boiled egg, chicken, enoki mushroom, shiitake mushroom, napa cabbage, sea eel and a slice of scallop (?). All of this is simmered in a delicious, comforting broth. The udon noodles were nice and chewy, just the way I like it! It was perfect. Totally reasonable for $20 (lunch price)

My friend ordered the cold mentai-kamatama udon. There is a huge portion of spicy fish caviar and you're supposed to mix the soft boiled egg with it along with the udon. The udon in the cold dish is even chewier (in the nice way!), and I love that this tasted light yet delicious. Although I have to say my friend was totally jealous of my dish!

Oh, and this place gives extra noodles for free! How awesome is that?? We both got extra noodles and managed to finish everything.

If you don't want to wait, there is a convenient app that lets you make reservations. I did not have to wait at all.
Great service, great food! I ordered the sukiyaki udon and the size is huge. The restaurant is a must try in Tokyo!
Came here a couple of times; the ambiance is great but the food is overhyped. I got curry udon and it was ok.

Ugh there were at least 15 - 20 seats available and they didn't seat us. No place is that good! Left for somewhere else after waiting at the bar for 30 minutes - staring at empty seats. I understand there is a waitlist but the bar eating area was open and 5 tables available which I counted on the way to the bathroom . Ended up going to a ramen place a couple of blocks away.

Ok! Went to Empire Cake last night and came on Yelp and gave a raving review! We r heading home tomorrow, so we headed back to Empire Cake for another party for the taste buds! This time we got the Carrot Cake cupcakes!!!  They were moist, tasty and the perfect amount of sweet! Do you know how most times the cream cheese frosting is way to sweet and u need to wipe half of it off in order to eat it? Not Empire's! Your gonna wanna scrap and lick every bit of this frosting up! Hubby said it was the best carrot cake cupcakes he ever had. YUMMMY!!!! To everything!

This restaurant is in the old Union Square Cafe space and it was weird seeing it reimagined as a Japanese noodle shop. Having said that, the food was very good and the noodles were excellent. The cold uni udon noddle was full of umami and you can get a large order (double noodles but normal amount of broth) for the same price as a regular order. The spicy tuna tartar cones were crunchy but could use a little more spice. The uni caviar dish was excellent as was the duck breast. There is a huge menu so definitely worth a couple of trips to try everything.

Liked the food but I did not like the price. Most of the top seller udon dishes are around the $20s range for basically broth and noodles. And I don't like that you can't take leftovers home (I believe that if you paid for it then its yours). 

The food: I got the tsuruton creme deluxe for $24 (I got the large which was the same price as the regular size). It had a creme based broth full of flavor. It had mentaiko caviar which added some interest to the broth when I mixed it in and got some crunch in each sip. It also included some shrimp, salmon, and chicken. The salmon and shrimp weren't bad, but the chicken was too hard and bland (I think if it had been soft it could have soaked up the sauce and had been more flavorful). Also chicken is a cheap ingredient so it really has to be extra flavorful for it to be worth it. I appreciated the fresh dill on top, it may not be much but I personally love the smell of fresh dill. 

The decor: the restaurant was an intersection of modern and cultural. It was quite big and the ceiling was high. There were multiple types of seating arrangements. 

The service: friendly and attentive. We waited for seating for about 15-20 min on Wednesday evening.

Yum! To start, my table shared the spicy tuna cones, which I loved! For my main dish, I originally wanted to have the beef sukiyaki udon, but the waitress told me that it was a sweet dish. I was craving something more on the savory side so I decided to go with the sizzling beef sukiyaki udon instead. I'm really happy she told me that because what I ended up eating was amazing down to the very last bite. 

My reasons for deducting that star: my $8 non-alcoholic lychee mojito was more than 50% ice, my party of 7 was there before our reservation and they still didn't have our table ready, so we had to wait ~15-20 minutes before sitting, the bathroom could afford to be bigger, and one of my biggest pet peeve of all: watered down/diluted soap -___-

Still. would highly recommend as I will be returning - just make sure to make a reservation.

Set in a chic, trendy space, this place will wow you with the choices of ramen and stir fry's. We had the mega ramen bowls with the "big" udon noodles. They were delicious. Up size to a large bowl for the same price.The service was spot on and very attentive. Would return again for another lunch or dinner.

This place has really cool ambiance and vibes but for a place that's supposedly known for udon, I think they missed the mark. I think they're much stronger in their appetizers because everything we ordered (shishito peppers, fried chicken with tartar sauce, grilled duck breast, sea truffle oil rolls, tuna and avocado cones) were all pretty delicious. But the Sukiyaki Udon bowl (main entree) was just alright. The sweet broth threw me off a bit and after a few slurps, I was already full. I also felt like they didn't really mix the ingredients well enough and didn't put too much thought into how things would taste. It would be better if it were a bit more savory. And oh yeah the bowls are larger than life. Didn't really see the purpose of having a huge bowl that's twice the size of your head when portion wise it's more or less the same for a normal bowl.
