If you really want noodles or ramen, you're better off going elsewhere with much cheaper price and better tasting noodles.

3.5 if I could.

the ambience and décor in this restaurant is pretty spectacular.
did not have to wait long to be seated. the drinks at the bar were pretty good and the bartender was friendly. our waiter, Anderson, was amazing. he went through the entire menu in detail but in a quick and straight forward manner.
he provides great advice in regards to what you may or may not like.
I thought the spicy tuna cones were a bit underwhelming especially after reading the reviews on yelp. the udon itself was okay.
the bowls are huge but don't be too alarmed, its only filled about half way. the menu is extremely extensive and perhaps I just choose the wrong soup base, but my broth was really sweet. at over 20 dollars for the top sellers, I was just a bit underwhelmed overall.
would probably return to try different things on the menu.

Impossible to pronounce the name of this place... but solid, creative comfort food option in Union Square! Unlike a typical ramen joint because they have so many more options than just broth. The portions are huge (each dish comes with free extra noodles) so I would definitely recommend sharing with your party.

We enjoyed the spicy tuna cones a lot and ordered 3 ramens for the 4 of us (which was more than enough): Uni udon, Sukiyaki udon and beef broth udon. Very carb heavy but pretty good blends of flavor. I liked the uni udon the best.

Would definitely come back here in the winter if only it weren't so hard to get a reservation at a normal time!

I'm going to be heading to Japan in April so figured I may as well try some Udon noodles beforehand, and I am happy that I chose this spot near union square to sample them!
Came with a group of 4 at 9 pm on a Friday night and it was packed inside, a surprisingly large interior with wooden tables and Japanese decor throughout, in a stylish and sophisticated way. 
We all started with some Sapporo beer, then split two appetizers. The spicy tuna tartare cones packed a little kick, but were pretty small. The creamy spicy shrimp tempura was a solid secondary choice and was a bit larger. 

The waitress was very informative and explained the menu, which was almost slightly overwhelming with the amount of Udon plates. I ultimately settled on the sukiyaki udon- Beef short plate with onsen egg and vegetables. The waitress informed me the broth the Udon noodles came in would be sweet, and we also had the choice of extra noodles for the same price, but the regular bowl was MORE then enough. It arrived piping hot and the extra-thicke noodles went down perfectly with the beef strips. You can really tell that they cook it in house as the noodles are a nice texture. They don't let you take it to go, so make sure you bring a hearty appetite! There is no question I will be returning here, as I am slowly learning there is more to Japanese food then just sushi and chicken teriyaki.

We were really excited to try an udon place after having some amazing stuff in Japan. The cold lime udon was disappointing. The texture of the thin noodles were great! Unfortunately, the cold broth was not right. It was the same dashi broth they use but even with the lime slices, there's barely any citrus/sour taste. We also ordered the kakiage thick udon. The broth taste was great, but the temperature was like warm. It wasn't hot enough when it came out. The tempura was also disappointing. It tasted like old oil and wasn't fresh. Overall, this place needs to make a better effort.

Sweet & thick noodles with great ambiance! (with a catch - pricey for what it is)

Came here with a friend at 8pm on a Monday night, there was a 30 minute wait. No problem! Lots of shopping in the area to take up the time. The interior of the restaurant is very nice, not too dark or loud. We were seated at a bench, across from another pair (I was hesitant at first..) but there is a divider in between so no awkward eye contact! It was a little difficult to get into the seat, but comfortable once we were sitting. 

The waitress did a great job explaining the menu to us. You can get extra noodles free of charge, but no take out. She emphasized that most of the items on the menu are quite sweet. 

To start off, we ordered the anago and tamago sushi roll. It was great, has a melt-in-your-mouth vibe. I ended up getting the sizzling sukiyaki udon (no broth) with thick noodles.  It comes out (obviously) sizzling in a stone pot, with the thinly sliced beef being my favorite part. Second favorite? The thick and soft noodles. The sizzling sukiyaki has a similar flavor to the broth udon (my friend got the sukiyaki udon with broth), a mix of sweet and salty. If anything, it was a little too salty for my taste. Towards the end, I had to rehydrate due to the saltiness. I was satisfied with the amount of food, I didn't get extra noodles. If you don't get an appetizer or arrive starving then supersize it!

This is my to-go udon spot in the city. The lines can be vicious but luckily union square is nearby where you can keep yourself busy during the wait. I've gotten a few udons and a donburi. The udon is pretty phenomenal. It comes out in a large dish (though it's definitely an illusion because it isn't as big as you'd think). The presentation of the food at Tsurutontan is beautiful. The food is very fresh and comes out quickly. 

Definitely get the fried chicken as the appetizer - the sauce it pairs with is amazing and the chicken is so tender. My only complaint with the food is that the udons can be very salty, especially the creme based udons. Service here is always great.

I was in NYC and I stayed at the W hotel which was down the street from this location. I woke up and was pretty hungry so I decided to look for a good place to eat. I wasn't feel well from the cold, and needed something warm and savory. I found this place on yelp and decided to give it a try. I came here, got seated immediately, and was given a menu. The server came up to me and asked if I had been there before and went over the basics. She told me there's 2 sizes, large and regular. The large is extra noodle at no additional price. You also also have the choice of thick or thin noodle. The catch is, you cannot take your leftover togo. I ended up ordering their most popular udon which was 25 bucks!!! I got a large, and it came with 2 shrimp tempera, some veggie tempera. The tempera was pretty good, but once you let it sit too long, it becomes soggy in the soup. The soup was also okay, nothing special, nor worth 25 bucks. I didn't finish the entire bowl, but I still say, order the large, because you'll probably want more after the regular size one. I enjoyed this location, but you have to flag someone down to get you some tea, or assistance. This isn't something you must go to, except they do serve their udon in huge and I mean BIGGER THAN YOUR FACE bowls!! 

value 2.5/5
taste 2.5/5
service 2.5/5

Was super excited to go to this restaurant as a lover of udon - but trust me, its alll just hype. Ordered the hot and sour udon and the caviar udon: BOTH SALTY AF. The steamed shrimp dumplings were the only highlight of the meal. Save your money and go some place else.

Good spot for udon. As a lot of reviewers have stated, the decor is noteworthy; very modern and sleek. I liked the large open design of the restaurant, but it feels a bit sectioned off with the upstairs, downstairs, and smaller dining area by the women's bathroom. 

The menu is pretty extensive but I was there for the udon, so I ordered the sukiyaki and my friend ordered the creamy truffle udon. The bowls were GINORMOUS when they arrived, which was fun! As I said to my friend, I felt like I was sneaking a bite of a giant's dinner. We were offered the option to upgrade our noodles free of charge, but I knew I wouldn't finish it so I chose not to.

The sukiyaki was definitely on the sweeter side, as other reviewers have mentioned. I loved the veggies in my bowl, and the beef was so soft and tender. Major plus! I tried some of the creamy truffle udon broth and it is so rich! But tasty and a different take on traditional udon. I liked it, the truffle taste was distinctly there.

Good thing I opted not to supersize my noodle portion, because I did not finish my udon and when I requested to bring it home, I was told I couldn't. Bummer, didn't realize that was the case and it's unfortunate since all that noodle and broth just went to waste.

Overall had a good doing experience, I would return to try some of the other udon options. The apps also looked appetizing, but that's for another day.

Tsuru Ton Tan is the much hyped about Japanese udon restaurant chain just off of Union Square. The space is beautiful and modern, with several sectioned off dining rooms with different artistic flourishes. I love that the smaller dining rooms cut down on the bouncing sound that is common in larger restaurants and probably enables them to serve small groups together if you reserve far enough in advance. The bar is a bit smaller than I would expect, but hopefully you're like me and really here for noodle goodness. I've been twice already and I can tell you that they are still hot and it can be hard to get a reservation for prime dinner time unless you reserve a few days before. The online reservation system is good and seems to leave a good amount of buffer. When I showed up early for a reservation, they were happy to seat me early. 

The menu is pretty exhaustive when it comes to udon, with traditional, cold, and more fusion udon options. They also have appetizers, sushi, and donburi, if rice is more your style. Udon can be ordered as regular sized or large, and unless you're starving, the regular is large enough for most people. The first time I came, I had the nabeyaki udon (a traditional staple on many Japanese menus) and husband had the spicy soondobu jigae udon, which is udon with a traditional Korean tofu stew. The nabeyaki udon was solid, and if you're looking for a traditional udon that isn't as large, its a good option. The soondobu udon was really really good and I totally had food envy. The second time, I had the TsuruTonTan deluxe where I really liked the beef, tempura shrimp and vegetables, and the egg drop. The quality of the udon is good, but for some reason I am not a fan of the chicken - I think it just doesn't have enough fat. I do like the appetizer fried chicken though, and I think the smashed cucumber salad is a tasty and refreshing dish. 

Service is excellent, checking in frequently, ensuring we had full water and tea cups. We did not have a long wait for our noodles, but both my visits were Wednesdays at 8 pm and the place wasn't full. I didn't see any opening jitters or mishaps, they seem to have everything running pretty smoothly. The bar can be a little more hiccupy, as there are not enough seats or bartenders and the staff require you to close out your tab before they seat you at a table. Restrooms are accessible and clean.

The only gripe I have with TsuruTonTan is that the prices are more indicative of the location and upscale look rather than the selectivity of the meal. Entrees range from $15 to $25, appetizers are $10-$20, with most dishes being at the top of the range. Additional toppings are $2-$4 for basic ingredients, although upsizing to the large udon is free.  College food this is not - you're encouraged to get drinks and really spend time here, so the prices do match. Considering the prices at Ippudo on the other side of the park at $15 per ramen bowl and $10-$15 appetizers, TsuruTonTan is definitely trying to keep the clientele on the high end for something that I consider comfort food.
I don't like here, because their waiters will customers to wait for several minutes intentionally, even when they're seats available

All the noodle bowls can be upgraded to a large with extra noodles at regular price. I got the uni creme udon with thick noodles. It was amazing and I would recommend. The appetizers were mediocre, have had better at other places.

I came here for the first time with a friend. First, we started with Sukiyaki buns. Delicious appetizer, and great to share. Then, we ordered the US Wagyu Shabu Udon and Uni Creme Udon for entree. Both were superb and delicious. We finished off our meal with Water Cake, which was a joy to eat. I would highly recommend, and would return for another fantastic experience.

Tsurutanton did not live up to the hype for me. When it just opened, my husband immediately pointed the place out to me since I am a noodle lover and especially an udon fan. My husband had tried this chain in Japan before and liked it. And since it's from Japan, it has to be good right? I.e. Ippudo down the street.

So after months of waiting for the initial hype to die down, we finally went one night to try it. The location is convenient right in Union Square. I was surprised at how big the restaurant was, definitely not the usual small Japanese shop. There's a bar area and a separate dining area. Also the place is very nicely decorated and upscale (unlike the original shop in Osaka). And you'll find this reflected in the price!

Udon came in a awesome huge bowl which did not do a good job at keeping the temperature in. My broth and udon were barely warm. The udon was good but the broth was mediocre - nothing special. Oh yeah, my bowl was $25. 

Even though the drinks were good, the service attentive, I would not return unless someone wants to  take me out. Even then, it'll just be for the atmosphere and the drinks. My friend actually treated my husband and me to that first meal since it was my birthday; and even though it was free, the noodle was still unsatisfying. And I love free food!

Came here with a few friends on a Friday night around 6pm. Definitely make a reservation because it was pretty packed when we got there. Ordered the fried chicken appetizer and we each ordered a udon. For the udon you can choose regular or large at no extra cost and you can also choose thin or thick. Generally they said thin noodles for the cold dishes and thick for the hot ones. 

Udon prices ranged from $17-$24. They all come in big bowls which imo is just a gimmick and made it hard to eat. I ordered the mentaiko udon (cold) and it wasn't something I enjoyed personally. The fried chicken was pretty good, soft and the sauce was good. We also ordered drinks each and they are really strong which is good for some and bad for others. 

Now the reason for three stars, one is that the chicken came right away when our waiter put in the order meaning that it wasn't fresh. You can't fry chicken in 1 minute. I'm not exaggerating. Let's put this in perspective, our waiter was still taking our order when our appetizer came out, and we were a party of 3. It's not like it takes a long time to take our order. 

Another reason is the take out option. You are only allowed to take out your leftover food but not order take out. Makes me question the owners because you can just order another bowl and then just ask to get a container to take it to go. They have a safety concern over raw foods but what about sushi restaurants? They do take out all the time. It doesn't make sense. 

Anyway, would I come back? Probably since my boyfriend wants to try this place. Maybe my second visit will be a bit better.

I was really excited when I saw this open up and have been waiting to go but was disappointed by the food (maybe because I had high expectations). I ordered the curry udon and my friend ordered the tan tan udon. The katsu curry udon was nothing spectacular and it came just warm. Would have appreciated if it was hotter. The katsu could have been cooked better since the outer fried layer separated from the meat. I did appreciate that the udon was cooked just right. The decor and service made you feel like you were in a hotel. Would give this 3.5 stars, but not on my list of favorite Japanese spots.

A great noodle restaurant that takes their noodles seriously. The service is prompt, helpful, and courteous. Th dashi broth is light and refreshing, and I would definitely come back to try their other noodle dishes. The Wagyu beef is awesome and the duck breast is cooked tenderly. Give this place a shot, it is priced just above an average ramen restaurant.

There's always something magical when you walk into an establishment and your immediate reaction is toward the decor and ambiance of a restaurant. Let's just say when I walked in, I knew instantly I was in for a treat. The restaurant is very modern, upscale and impressive. The layout exuded warmth, and beauty.

Immediately we were seated and the vibe felt great. The menu offered many choices of appetizers and it's main course -- udon. I ended up ordering their sweet uni udon and it was delicious! The mild flavored uni was silky and fresh, while the cream sauce that came along with it helped hit the right note.  As for the texture of my udon, it was al-dente and very yummy!

I would definitely come back here again and would recommend this higher end udon place if you're nearby. Though with so much competition, it might be a while before they see me again since the price here is quite high.

I give Tsurutontan 3 starts because my experience was not too great primarily due to my choice to try something new. I like to try new dishes, i like curry and I like udon but I did not enjoy my curry udon. I would not recommend it. While I thought the presentation of my dish was spectacular, I was a little shocked about the price. A friend who joined me and has gotten around to eating a lot of Japanese food concurred that it was not worth the price.

I came here with a buddy I haven't seen in a while, and we miraculously both chose this place to catch up (of all places in NYC). First, I was impressed at the interior, the various patterns and themes weaved into this udon restaurant adds to its character.

We ordered a ton of food and I got the uni udon, served cold. It was ridiculously good and the portion sizes are right up my alley (Go big or go home). My friend got the curry udon, which looked amazing and I'll likely get it next time. 

While the prices could be considered on the higher side I believe the amount and quality of food balances it out. I'd be back next time for the curry udon

Upgrade your udon to the large size no matter what. 

What I tried:
-Spicy Tuna Tartare Cone: Was not spicy at all, coming from someone who likes mild spice. It wasn't that good because it lacked flavor. The cone is essential for the texture but, I would not get this again. 
-Shishito Peppers: Aren't 1 in 10 shishito peppers spicy? Well, 7 of the 10 peppers that came to the table were SUPER spicy. My tongue was on fire and turned numb. If you like that, order this. 
-Sizzling Sukiyaki Udon: It comes with udon (duh), raw egg, beef, mushrooms and, scallions all in a stone pot. Be sure to mix everything around and if you listen carefully, the udon continues to cook in the pot, making sizzling sounds. If you don't eat it fast enough, udon stuck on the bottom will have crisped and you can enjoy the crispy and chewy texture of their udon.
-Duck Udon: The duck breast was cooked perfectly, but too bad it only comes with 5 thin pieces. The soup is sweeter than my liking, but I couldn't stop myself from drinking it. 
-Katsu Curry: I'm not a huge fan of curry to begin with, but I thought this would change my mine. Nope. The pork cutlet is better on it's own. 
-Water Cake: This was a good refreshing dessert to end the meal. The burnt sugar syrup definitely added flavor to the water cake. 

I'll be coming back for more sizzling udon and I think I'll give their uni and wagyu sushi a try.

Had lunch and dinner here. Got the truffle mushroom udon both times and shared. It's incredibly delicious. I also have had the tuna tartar cones which are very tasty and the guise appetizer. I love the decor of this place. The wall of boro is so beautiful and unique. I ordered a hot pot dish for my boyfriend which he loved. I also ordered the cold uni udon which was good but needed more uni flavor. 
This is a great place for lunch. Be warned that they don't let you take leftovers. Unfortunately.

Update: I could tell the difference between reservation/getting called by the text and just walking in. Even if I couldn't, 30 minutes wait vs. 10 minutes was frustrating enough. I wouldn't have eaten here if I needed to wait for 30 minutes. Also I'm not Japanese and I haven't been to Japan either, so I can't say about the authenticity. If it is authentic Japanese food, it is definitely really different from the mainstream traditional Japanese food (as I said, the food isn't bad). One more point to add, this is a pretty big restaurant but they have extremely limited restrooms. There was literally a line for the bathroom. 

The food was not bad. I had a frustrating experience though, which definitely impacted my appetite. I came in by myself and was told it was 10 minutes wait. I ended up waiting for 30 minutes, for a seat at the counter. People who came after me were seated before me. If I wasn't so lazy, I would've gone to East Village for authentic Japanese food. This place is like Americanized fusion Japanese food. But I would give this place a second chance if I'm in the neighborhood.

We certainly haven't had better udon- the only comparable restaurant is probably Marukame in Hawaii (but you have to go to Hawaii and this place is right here). From top to bottom this place is as good as it gets.

Ambiance - 5 stars for their stylish and compartmentalized dining rooms (with questionable but interesting wall coverings) that make dining feel more intimate.

Service - 4.5 stars since they were exactly 10 minutes late taking us to our table after we had made a reservation (but that's because they were crazy busy on a Wednesday night) but otherwise spot-on.

Drinks - 5 stars for my perfectly made "Nippon" Old-fashioned ('cause I'm old fashioned).

Food - 10 stars for tasty kaarage and perfect pork belly apps and truly top notch curry and wagyu sukiyaki udon.

Value - 5 stars... too much food for not that much money (note: get the small- whatever you do, get the small)

Can't wait to return...

Absolutely delicious! They have a wide range of choices to choose from. If you come during lunch time (noon-3pm), there's basically no wait at all. Dinner is a lot busier but the service is really fast. On their lunch menu they give you an option of choosing a lunch set. For $3 more you get a bowl of rice with a topping of either mentaiko, beef or fried chicken. I had the tan tan udon which I thought was okay. The soup was on the thicker side. I was more of a fan of their uni creme udon and mentaiko udons. Just like their dinner menu, you can choose a large or small bowl along with the type of udon you want.

Great udon place that is more of a Japanese-American fusion udon. They offer their noodles in a regular and a large size, for the same price. The only difference between these two sizes is the amount of noodles - the amount of toppings and stuff is the same. They had a number of flavors, ranging from what you would expect at a Japanese place, like curry chicken, to slightly odd ones, like soondubu (okay, I've seen places with both Korean and Japanese food), to ones you'd never expect, like truffle cream and caviar udon. I had the nabeyaki udon in a large size, and have to say that it was delicious. Was the perfect amount of hearty and warming for the winter, and the large portion more than filled me up.

Udon is one of my favorite comfort foods, and this place has all kinds of udon base you can choose from. They offer bar portion udon and regular portion udon... for the same price, so why not go for the big guy? My favorite one was the cream deluxe, I forgot what's in it, but all I could remember is the taste of the smooth and flavorful soup. I could probably eat three bowls of that. 

We also ordered the curry one, which was meh, something didn't taste right to me. We also got the uni udon (served cold) and the salmon over rice. The uni was alright, I was hoping that the udon would have a hint of the uni taste, but nope, it was just uni on top of udon, nothing special. 

The service was great, the waiter took good care of us. Even though it was really packed during lunch hours, the staff didn't rush us out. Make sure you make a reservation.

It's a pretty nice place to eat at. The place is huge, but it fills up pretty quickly. Good pricing. But tbh I don't understand what the hype was. Like it definitely would have satisfied my udon cravings, but I don't think I would have waited for hours to dine here *Advice: make a reservation!

Upon ordering your udon entree, you can choose between small/large bowl and thick/thin noodles. Our waitress said thick noodles are recommended for hot udon entrees, and thin noodles are recommended for cold udon entrees. As for the size, I got the large bowl and was super full by the time I finished. The bowl was literally humongous. It's a nice gimmick haha

I got the US Wagyu and Mushroom Sukiyaki (large, thick noodles). It was a little sweeter than I imagined/wanted it to be, but I still ate the whole thing cause it was yummy :) My boyfriend got the TsuruTonTan Deluxe and I thought it was pretty flavorful. *Advice: mix everything before eating, I think the true flavor is at the bottom of the bowl. The Spicy Tuna Tartare Cones were pretty solid, but a bit oily. The Wagyu sushi was just ok, don't think I would order it again.

I heard one of the employees speaking very rudely/ condescendingly to other employee. The food was great ! However, witnessing the interaction put a bad taste in our mouths. The food is great and you can't really find elsewhere in NYC and our waitress was very attentive!

so delicious!
They don't do take outs so be sure to only order as much as you can eat. Now, having said that, you can choose to have a regular amount of noodles or a large portion. The cold uni udon is really rich and creamy.  Super great service. It does get packed so make a reservation

The udon is serve in a large bowl, just like the way that I remenber when I visited Japan last summer.  I like the cozy feeling of the environment.  The fried chicken was soft,  believe it or not,  it's the fried chicken that I said is soft and crispy.  The duck is good,  not too oily.  It's a good environment for two!  :)

New hot restaurant that everyone is raving about on Instagram, so I decided to give it a try. My first impression is, not too shabby~
Tsurutontan is located conveniently close to the Union Square station, so if you can't get a table here, you have plenty of dining options nearby.

The price per bowl is very high, but the portion is big enough to be shared by two. Menu is huge including many Japanese fusion style appetizers and different flavors of udon noodle. Since there are so many options, it made me want to go back again in the future to try everything.
I recommend for a group of two, order one appetizer and one noodle to share.

The appetizer spicy tuna tartare cone was very fresh with just the right amount of crispiness and spices. We had the Tsurutontan deluxe and Mentaiko caviar creme udon, both are delicious and HUGE!

I recommend coming for lunch to avoid the wait. 

Tips:
+ order the large portion (extra noodle) with no extra charge
Absolutely has an awesome atmosphere! Tuna Tartare in little cones are bursting with flavors serving as an ultimate palate cleanser before you dive into their huge bowls of noodle greatness!!

This place was really disappointing. Ive been too lazy to post reviews but was very compelled in this case so that you can save yourself a bad overpriced meal. The aps were mediocre. The udon looks cool (mainly because of the funky bowls) but tastes average at best. I got the tsurutontan deluxe udon and the pork was cut in huge pieces and tasted off. I'm 99.9% positive this gave me mild food poisoning. The green tea cake is good (afterall it's from lady m) but the portion is ridiculously small. The water cake thing is worse than hospital jello. It's essentially flavorless jello and you're supposed to mix it up with some word syrup and some sort of flavor powder. The end result is one of the worst things I've ever eaten, not exaggerating in the slightest.

I had high hopes and was excited to try this place. 

I've been to this location when it was Union Square Cafe. The layout remains unchanged, the real difference is the decor. This place apparently is very popular, and I'm glad that we decided to make a reservation at the last minute, since even as early as 6 pm they already have people waiting.

I had to order the Uni Udon, being a fan of uni and reading the yelp reviews. My friend ordered a Sukiyaki Beef Udon. I don't really understand how the regular and the large bowl would be the same price, but in any case, I went with large (which I never usually order). The bowls were comically huge and the portions were hefty as well. It would be fair to say you could probably even share one for two people if so inclined.

For the Uni Udon, I ordered the thin noodles. I liked how chewy and substantial the noodles were, and the texture was great. The udon came cold with uni, nori and dashi. It was good but I found it a bit lacking in flavor, despite having a good amount of uni on top of it. Also tried my friend's sukiyaki udon and yikes! It was so sweet, practically sugary. Not really my cup of tea. 

The menu is extensive and I'd be willing to come here again, but I wouldn't order either of the ones my friend and I had.
The menu is overpriced. The food is like just okay so I guess I won't be eating here again. Very nice renovation tho... I miss the Union Square Cafe which used to be here.

The serving size is outrageous. I tried the original udon bowl and the curry udon bowl. Both were delicious. If you come with a group you can share a bunch of different dishes. Otherwise good luck finishing one bowl on your own. Sad you can't take out any leftovers, but I've accepted this.
Love all the choices!! So many options- I really loved the skinny noodles in spicy pork broth. Also added the tempura egg. Get double noodles for the same price!!!

The decor is cozy. It's definitely a nice place to have a group dinner. When we sat down, our waiter introduce the menu to us. Apparently you can get thin or thick udon noodles. I got the matcha over the moon drink as recommended by the waiter. It's definitely a girly drink which I like. It might seem like a weird combination but it actually taste good. For appertizer, I got the tuna cone. The cone was crispy, tuna had a spicy kick and the avacado at the bottom of the cone made it freshing. For the entree, the udon noodle was awesome. It wasn't too creamy and it still maintain the udon flavor. The curry delux was super filling. It got so much meat. I didn't even notice there were cubes of beef in the curry soup base. As for the curry, it wasn't over power. They put enough curry for you to taste it but not too thick that you couldn't enjoy the broth. Overall, I enjoyed my dinning experience at the restaurant and can't wait to return to try the other dishes on the menu.

Really tasty Udon.  Service was prompt and nice.  Absolutely recommend the sizzling udon with egg yolk and shishito peppers app.  

They have Sapporo Black, which can be tough to find as well.

A nice place and the portions are huge if you get the large size for the top sellers. Tried the Mentaiko cold udon (small noodles) and the Sukiyaki udon (hot). Both were good. I liked the chewiness and refreshing taste of the Mentaiko udon. The broth was good for the Sukiyaki udon, although for my tastebuds a tad bit too sweet. I got the Sukiyaki buns for an appetizer - it was okay, tasted like a burger. Would recommend to try at least once. They have many types of udon so I'd probably come back to try other types.

My group ordered the seared salmon sashimi, fried chicken, and himachi for appetizers. The salmon was probably my favorite appetizer. The fried garlic is nice and crunchy which is a great contrast against the soft, tender salmon. The sauce also had a good amount of acid which cut the sweetness of it. The taste of the daikon on the himachi reminded me of an asian pear. It was pretty good but I don't know if I would get it again. The fried chicken was nothing memorable. It tasted like fried chicken that you can get from most places in ktown.

I ordered the uni creme udon. The broth was sweet and rich. The noodles were perfectly cooked and just the right amount of chewy. The caviar added a nice crunch to each bite. I knocked off a star because the uni was kind of fishy. If I'm paying that much extra for a little bit if uni, it should be very fresh. The broth of the tan tan udon is great too. It has a salty sesame taste with a little bit of spice. I just don't like how the top of it is drowned in chili oil. It makes it unappealing the drink the rest of the broth at the end. The portions for the large are substantial and will definitely fill you up.

The service is terrific here. Our server was attentive and was knowledgable about everything on the menu. He also never let our water glasses get empty (my true test of good service).

This is not the cheapest place to get a bowl of udon in the city, but the quality is great. They had a huge selection of dishes and I will definitely be back to try their other broths!

WELP. If you've tried Raku, you really won't enjoy this one. 

Dined in for lunch with a friend in hopes to try the large portions of udon that others seemed to really dig on Yelp and Instagram. Boy oh boy was I disappointed. The noodles aren't as chewy and they taste like the frozen kind you buy from h-mart or from Assi. A bit of a disappointment. The broth isn't anything extraordinary, it's whatever. The dish, if you get the large, is huge in portion although I kinda ate all of mine. 

The highlight of our meal was the seared salmon sashimi that was lightly seared and had some sort of ponzu sauce that went well with the salmon. 

Would not recommend for udon, what a disappointment.
I would give 3.5. Uni crème udon - good. Small amount of uni and tobiko caviar. Creamy broth with a hint of sea. Chewy thick udon. Super large bowl and spoon.

Excellent food. The staffs are friendly and funny. They love to have a conversation with you. A good place to hang out with friends, they have a huge bar. I suggest get some appetizer and share a bowl of noodles and rice.

The noodles are great. Great consistency. Great broth. No upcharge for extra large portion? Awesome. Service was very good, and they take reservations. 

Dessert portions are quite small though. The match cake slice is ~half of what you'd expect at a Lady M. Not a big deal though. Can get a bit pricey depending on how much you order. 3 bowls of udon, 3 drinks, 2 desserts came out to ~$160 including tip. But still a satisfying meal.

Having eaten at this restaurant at the Haneda airport, I can tell you that the quality is very similar. The restaurant itself is fairly large, and tables usually turn around quickly.

Between two people, we shared a large udon noodle and sushi roll. We sat at the shared seating located in the middle of the room, so the table space was quite tight. It's nice to have a bit of a barrier from the other side of the table from the decor that split the table in half lengthwise. 

Tips: 1) There is no price difference between regular and large. 2) Choose either thick or thin udon noodles. 3) If you get a dish with tempura, ask for the tempura on the side, separate from the broth.

TSURUTONTAN DELUXE: essentially a mix of all the proteins and seafood. There was a limited amount of beef and chicken, but my biggest gripe is that the tempura shrimp and veggies are placed on top of the soup. By the time the bowl arrives to your table, the tempura is almost thoroughly soggy. Seems like a waste of perfectly good tempura...

SALMON & SNOW CRAB ROLL: 8 pieces; good flavoring of lightly seared salmon and snow crab salad as the main stuffing. I tasted a bit of a garlic aftertaste but I'm not certain the dish actually has any. There was also a bit of a crunch..again not sure if that was intentional or not but it seemed like there might have been small pieces of snow crab cartilage. 

Overall, an OK experience. A little underwhelming.

Noodles are a must!! There's an udon menu and a sushi menu, but the place specializes in udon, so that should be a no brainer. 

The noodles are perfectly spongy and come in comically large portions. I had the uni udon, which had a generous amount of uni and was served with a creamy broth. It's a hot dish, but I'm also curious to try their cold udon dishes...Maybe when I come back in the summer. 

The restaurant is large, but I would still recommend making a reservation. It was very busy even when we arrived for our res at 5:45 on a Saturday.

Great ambiance! A great place to get dinner with friends. The food is very authentic and the udon noodles are to die for. The menu has so many different concoctions of udon that it's hard to come here just one time because you want to try them all! From truffle udon to chili paste, this place has it all. The appetizers were particularly delicious too. We ordered the tuna tartare cones. Very addicting. The udon bowls themselves were very surprising when they served us because of how HUGE the bowls were. You definitely have to come here on an empty stomach. Udon noodles are the new ramen.
I love this place. I dont think I've had anything bad here so far... I'm trying to work my way to try everything on the menu [:

Wow!  This place was a real surprise!  From the service to the food quality, everything was on point!  The reservation host was a bit of a snob.  I tried to make a reservation over the phone for the same day and they didn't have anything at the time I wanted but they said they have more tables available for walk ins?  So we gave it a try. We still had to wait a bit (15 mins or so) and we took the bench table seating which actually was pretty cool.  We were sitting among over customers and the experience was quite nice! Our waitress was so nice with helping with the food selections and her recommendations.  I wish I got her name because she was a part of the enjoyable experience. I ordered the spicy noodle dish (don't recall name) and my wife ordered the chicken katsu noodle dish.  Both were delish and our apps - Grilled Duck - just delightful.  The desert topped it off!  It wasn't on the menu but once again, our lovely waitress recommended so we went with this banana inspired dish - so light and tasty.  

Thanks for a wonderful evening!  Hope to come back soon!
Fantastic selection of noodle soup bowls, and even rice dishes and other additions. There is something for everyone here.
Massive portion sizes! My new favorite udon restaurant in NYC. Make sure to make a reservation because they fill up fast!

Service: 4 stars
Food: 2 stars
No wait at lunch time and happily surprised! This restaurant is fairly big with multiple dining areas, however I think the wait can be pretty long during dinner still.

They have an EXTENSIVE menu of all different kinds of broths: traditional/dashi, curry, cream, cold noodles. They also have a lot of appetizers to choose from.
Since we already had a dessert place in mind, my friend and I decided to share one bowl of udon and an appetizer.

I definitely suggest getting the extra noodles (FO FREEE) if you're going to share, or if you're hungry. It was the perfect amount of food for the both of us. 
We got the chicken ramen, which was very bland. Chicken cubes were very dry and the udon itself was not that impressive. The noodles weren't that chewy, and I guess I was just expecting a little more for the price.
However, this is just for the chicken udon. I would go back to try the other varieties only during lunch though. Wouldn't wait for it. 

We got the hot oil seared salmon appetizer, which again was not impressive. I just wasn't a fan of the taste. But by no means was the quality compromised. 

Again, I'd want to try their other udon choices, but it wouldn't be my first choice udon restaurant.

Great udon noodle soup with various types of broth and meat. If you find the creamy broth too heavy, the clear broth is also very delicious with a rich taste. They also have multiple curry udon options if you enjoy a bit spices. 

Note: You can ask for extra noodles for no additional cost, but no take-out (ie you have to finish while eating there).

Unreal. Tokyo Mule was my favorite drink. The tuna cones were an awesome bar snack, tuna was super fresh. The sukiyaki noodle bowl with the raw egg was the best noodle dish I've ever had. Service was great too.

I want to give this place 6 stars for the best meal I had all weekend.

I bookmarked this place on yelp since we'd be attending a convention nearby. There can be a wait if you don't have a reservation,  so in the future, I may opt for that. It has several levels,  and we sat upstairs in a cool nook that overlooked the activity downstairs.

Their udon noodles are made in house, and you can absolutely tell from the quality in taste. It costs the same to have extra noodles, so come hungry and say YES when they ask.

We started with the chicken appetizer, which came crispy, not greasy, and in an amazing zesty chili sauce. Oh my goodness.

My husband had a spicy creamy udon broth with minced meat, and I opted vegetable tempura. Mine was great, but oh man that spicy cream broth in my husband's bowl rocked our world. It wasn't horrifically spicy. The kind that creeps up, but brings serious flavor behind it.

Beware: they tempura a poached egg, which I didn't know until I took a bite and it poured down my lap :( 

Service was wonderful. Someone came by to ask how the meal was, chatted about how we were visiting. For as high end as the place is, I thought the prices were very worth it. My husband and I are making sure reservations here are a must the next time we're in the area.

Food is okay. It comes in GIGANTIC portions. They will ask you if you want the regular or the large portion. Unless you are starving, just order the regular. The location is pretty good and the atmosphere isn't bad, but the waitstaff is problematic. I had made a reservation for lunch for two a few days prior to my coming to the restaurant. When I arrived, the restaurant was empty and the waitress sat me right by the window, next to the cold air. When I asked if I could get a better seat (I HAD made a reservation), the waitress said they were completely booked and because I didn't have a reservation there was nothing she could do. Note that at no point did she ask if I had a reservation, assuming I was without one. Further note that the restaurant was almost completely empty. It is frustrating to mistreated by an establishment when you are going to be giving them money. Between the service and the slop sized portions, I won't be returning. Please spend your money elsewhere.

Good food. Loved the spicy tuna cones. The smashed cucumber salad was good but way too expensive for about 7 pieces of cucumber give or take. 

Now onto the udon....the curry udon was delicious. The noodles were perfect. I liked the option of "super sizing" it for free but the regular portion was more than enough for me. 

Would definitely return. (Their cocktails are also very good)

A trendy, hip and spacious Japanese restaurant situated in Union Square with a variety of food options to choose from. Besides that, let's not forget that you can actually opt for large orders without extra cost!

We came here for dinner on a Saturday night, which we regrettable realized we should have made reservations for. The wait took approximately an hour.

We had ordered the uni creme udon, the tsurutontan deluxe as well as my favorite of all the spicy tuna tartare cone. They offered the option of either getting thick or thin udon and we went for the thick, which was good but super filling since we also got the large. The tsurutontan deluxe was a bit lacking in flavor, and essentially tasted like hot pot. 

Overall, I would still come back but to try other things on the menu.

This place was really good. I was brought upstairs (had no idea there was an upstairs) and atmosphere was great. The food was presented well. The noodle bowl was covered before given. 

Drinks were really good. Tried the Tokyo mule and the matcha cocktail (forgot the name).... but awesome.

Wednesday night, no reservations made, waiter 40 minutes for dinner. It was well worth it. The broths were so rich and distinct from each other. We all had the thick noodle because it's more chewy.

Tip: when they ask regular or large: LARGE
It's the same price, we asked why, they said no reason

So if you can't finish, you can take leftovers home.
Because they don't allow take out. 
Or two people can share one large noodle and order some appetizers.

Dessert: chocolate cake is rich and delicious
Rain drop cake is tasteless but fun to eat if you like jello
The decor is modern, while the bench seat brings you two closer. Big selection of hot and cold udons as well as appetizers. The beef was not super tasty, and overall the udon bowl was fairly plain.

Very disappointing. In Japan they are famous for their cheap and fast udon. Although they make the udon on site, the actual udon tastes worse than frozen udon. Their udon has no koshi in it and tastes like udon flour. It splits clean when you bite into it. I guess this would be a matter of preference.

The presentation is great, it comes in a big bowl like most places now. But after trying 8 udons with a group of Japanese people, every dish tasted terrible. The curry udon is hands down the worst curry udon I have ever had, plus there was almost no beef in it. The sukiyaki udon which seems to be popular only tasted like sesame oil and was way too oily and tasted almost nothing like sukiyaki except for the ingredients. The cold uni udon almost tasted nothing like uni. They made it into a sauce by blending it and left no actual pieces of uni. Such a waste.
Also their tatsutage is karaage. This is misleading and annoying because a lot of places do this. If you're a Japanese establishment you should get this right.

Although the presentation and interior are great, the food is terrible. I would not go back again. This is all hype because it's from Japan. I would give it a year or two unless they actually hire Japanese people. If you want to eat really good and authentic udon try Raku instead.

P.s.- they only have two bathrooms for the whole place so expect a line. They should probably have a waitlist for t

Great udon! I've been a long time fan of udon but NYC has been more of a ramen country for the last several years. So when I learned that Tsurutontan opened at the old Union Square Café space I knew I had to check it out. I visited on a week night and there was no wait to dine solo at the bar. I ordered the nabeyaki udon. It was delicious! And wow, what a portion! I'm glad I came hungry. Next time, and there will be a next time I want to come back with a friend so I can try other things. I'm definitely eager to try their modern offerings.

This has become my favorite restaurant. I love everything I've tried so far. By far my favorite is the wagyu and mushroom udon. The noodles are so fresh and delicious and the broth is flavorful and yummy. The waiters take the time to explain the menu and the food comes quickly (although they don't rush you out if you linger which is nice). Love love this place!

Delicious! I love udon and these noodles did not disappoint. I tried the sukiyaki udon with no broth. This is more of a fried udon type dish and it was delicious, not too dry, loaded with veggies and meat. M had the tan tan udon, which was actually really spicy. The broth was also a little too oily for my taste, but the noodles were nice and chewy. I also want to try the tuna cones and some of their sushi. Will definitely be back.

The decor is pretty funny - the idea is that you are in the soup bowl. There are large ropes on the walls to signify the noodles and sheets hanging from the ceiling to mimic the steam. It's well-lit and clean. I've had the curry udon and the oyako don. The curry broth was tasty and the udon noodles are chewy and savory. The rice bowl was everything I was craving for brunch: eggy, savory, tangy, meaty and filling. The only negative thing is that they don't let you bring home any food even though they give you ridiculous portions. I very rarely crave udon over ramen but would return on the next cold day that I get a hankering for something hearty and chewy.
Delicious udon noodle with generous portion. You can order small or large portion depending on how much udon you would like to consume. Enjoyed their warm dish more than cold dishes

Maybe it's just me but I didn't think this place was amazing like some others. I had the US Wagyu & mushroom sukiyaki. I knew it came with sweet broth but it was too sweet. The tsurutontan udon was definitely better but I still didn't think it was worth $24. 

When I first got there one of the hostess was not welcoming at all. She had this attitude that I did not appreciate at all. I was asking her a question and she was either not paying attention or pretended she didn't know what I was saying. I had to break down my words to her. 

If you bring a cake there, they charge a $3 serving fee per person.

Bookmarked this place when I had udon at another restaurant in the LES and heard this place was good.  (Was curious to see how Tsuru Ton Tan's udon compared).  Union Square Farmer Market days are a good opportunity to try neighborhood eateries.  TTT is located in the former Union Square Cafe venue and is spacious.  Ordered a katsudon (fried breaded pork cutlet with egg over rice) which comes with a small bowl of plain dashi brothed udon.  My bf got the large Tsuru Ton Tan which has a piece of katsu, 2 shrimp tempura, beef and chicken and a small bowl of fried garlic over rice.  We both thought there was ample food but you pay for it, $18 and 24 respectively.  This is lunch and more food and pricier than your normal noodle shop.  The lunch set gives you a lot but most of them are in the $20 range.  I also have to comment that the thick udon was really thick and not that much different in texture from the packaged kind you make at home.  (The homemade kind at the other LES udon place was chewier and not so thick).  You have your choice of a thinner noodle but we wanted to try the more traditional size first.  My katsudon was a little bland.  The umami  taste was lacking.  All in all, it satisfied but $60+ it was not a quick bowl of noodles. We weren't wowed.

Service was good and engaging.  Our server knew her stuff and walked us through the options which was helpful.

Big portion and the best texture udon noodles- they are so soft and chewy. Curry and spicy udons had great flavors but made me drink lots of water after- little too heavy salt. But i will be def coming back for many more shabu udon bowls.

Very very mediocre udon for the price you pay. Now before you think I am a hater of some sort, let me tell you that 1) I am Japanese 2) and have had udon from various locations in Japan including the well known Kagawa prefecture.

Yes I may be hyper critical. But for a place that specializes in udon, one would expect you to perfect the art of udon.

Most of the appetizers aren't authentic Japanese so I skipped it, except the tofu. It was okay but I know that the Japanese supermarkets have similar quality tofu for less than half the price. 

For udon I had the simple cold one and the truffles one. Honestly I think if you're going to judge how good a Japanese noodle place is, whether it's soba or udon, you need to have it simple and cold. That's the best way to see the texture and how firm it is, etc. First if all, the regular portion for the cold is too small, even for a Japanese person. It is smaller than what you get in the stand in places at the stations in Tokyo. Second of all, the udon was not properly chilled. Everyone knows it's best to firm up udon with ice water after you boil it. That's what gives it is unique chewy texture. They obviously didn't do that as it came out room temperature or slightly warmer on a huge bowl of ice. (Usually you don't put it on an ice bowl in Japan as it is usually cold enough, unless you're serving something like somen) The sauce was way too sweet as well. 
The truffles one smelled great but that was the extent it went. The cream soup it was in was too watery so it didn't mix well with the udon. ( needs to be thicker to mix in like a carbonara) I can honestly say I can make better udon with the dry udon they sell at the Japanese grocery stores.

Service was fine, not bad actually pretty good. She was courteous and always filled up my tea so I think the one star would be for her. 

Again hugely disappointed considering if us a Japanese chain, since so many of its companions have done so successfully. 

If you're a non Japanese who wants a cool hip Japanese fusion experience go for it. But for authenticity, it seriously lacks.

We arrived at around 5:30 and were able to beat the dinner rush. No wait at all for a party of 3. The place looks very nice and upscale. We were seated at a table in the corner next to the window so I was a littler worried that we would be neglected but the service was actually attentive for the most part. I also liked how our waiter took the time to explain the menu items to us. Ultimately, we decided to share 2 udon noodles (with extra noodles at no extra cost) and 1 appetizer. We got the spicy tuna tartare cones, katsu curry udon with thin noodles, and wagyu/mushroom sukiyaki udon with thick noodles. We all agreed that we liked the katsu curry udon more. The curry was very flavorful and the katsu remained crispy despite having been soaked in the curry. It probably would've tasted better with thick noodles but I enjoyed the thin noodles too. As for the sukiyaki, it has a very fragrant mushroom soup taste to it with a hint of sweetness. Not bad but the curry katsu was definitely the winner. The spicy tuna tartare cones were a lot smaller than I had expected them to be...Also they only fill half the cone with spicy tuna and the other half is just guac...Had to get it since it's one of their more popular appetizers but probably won't get it again.

The udon noodles here definitely aren't your typical prepackaged ones. Very nice texture and delicious taste. Prices are kind of high but bear in mind the type of environment you're dining in. This is a very trendy place right now and I can see why. The udon is tasty, the decor is very attractive, and the service is great. I would definitely recommend this restaurant for a more upscale place for a date or get together.

Tsurutontan NY $20+ for non tasty udon no thanks. The braised pork belly was not good. The pork bun was not good, the tempura calamari was not good. My overall experience, terrible. Given a table and said I had to finish in 45 minute, because they need the table back in 45 minutes how awesome is that! (sarcasm) Please do your self a favor go to your closest supermarket buy a $2 dollar pack of instant udon cut up some eggs and pork throw it in there, I can assure you, you'd feel so much better about yourself and what life has to offer =)

Went to this place on a Sunday morning cuz we wanted to break away from our usually routine of Udon West and Raku. I ordered the sukiyaki wagyu udon with thick noodles ($24) and my boyfriend got the shrimp tempura udon with thin noodles ($17). The server suggested that the wagyu beef would be served medium rare and so I asked to have it served rare. 

So this is how it turned out: 

There was no wagyu beef in my udon. There was a lot of well done eye round. Being Vietnamese, I definitely know my beef cuts and it definitely wasn't a tough piece of wagyu. It was eye round beef!!! 

The noodles were too thick and undercooked. I've never had anything sukiyaki that sweet before -- it tasted like a dessert. 

The manager came out and said he would bring the wagyu beef on the side. The meat didn't come out until we were almost done with our food. What's the point?? 

My boyfriend's shrimp tempura was average. The broth isn't as good as Udon West given that it's twice as expensive. 

I didn't even finish the food because it was so yucky tasting. And I didn't wanna toss a big fuss cuz my bf was visiting from out of town and didn't wanna ruin our energy for the rest of the day but I want to put in the time to write this review. 

Service was terrible. The server was having a mental break down and didn't know what to do besides coming back to us 5x times asking if everything is ok. Of course it's not ok. The food was disgusting and I just spoke to your manager. Even the manager didn't understand half of the issue and didn't even try to make an effort to fix it. The meat came out at the end of our meal. We didn't have to go to a udon restaurant if this 5 slices of raw beef was what we wanted to eat. We wanted to see how your kitchen incorporates it together into your udon! 

This place is a scam. If you are really looking for good authentic udon, there r other places in st marks where you can get great food for half the price. We will never go back. I don't understand how they could stay in business selling such terrible food. 

Yuck!

I came here for dinner when I was in NYC.  The ambiance and place itself is really nice and pretty interior.  The udon itself was average in my opinion.  I got the sukiyaki udon and the texture was similar to other udon places I've had.  The sukiyaki was pretty good but I felt the price for what I was paying was not the quality I was receiving.  The bowls are huge too! Just an average udon place in my opinion! Take the train, the stop is right there at Union Square!

The reason why i wanted to try this place was because two of my friends who did not know each other came here for dinner on the same night and both decided to snapchat me the same pictures of the tuna cones. I thought what a coincidence, this place must be good if they are both raving about it. However i was pretty disappointed since the food was okay and the sukiyaki wagyu udon wasn't as great as i thought it would be. The broth was way too sweet and it felt like i was eating dessert and the wagyu felt like it had been in the hot broth for so long that it came tough. To be honest my boyfriend and i both thought the wagyu tasted a bit like over cooked thin sliced beef in hotpot. I think i will come back to try other dishes but definitely not worth the hour long wait during rush hours.

I have been here three times now and I leave impressed every single time.  I remember when TsuruTonTan was close to opening and was getting a lot of hype due to it being a very popular udon restaurant in Japan.  I was there on opening night and have brought guests with me for two other dinners and left extremely satisfied every single time.

TsuruTonTan accomplishes something completely unexpected.  Most people think of udon as a very simple dish of dashi broth and noodle.  But TsuruTonTan makes you realize that there is a huge difference in the quality of dashi, in fresh-made noodles, and in the variety of preparations.  The attention to detail is unparalleled here and the quality is evident in every single bite.

My first time here, I had the cold udon with karaage and an onsen egg.  You can choose between thick or thin noodles and they recommend the thin for the cold broth options, so I trusted them.  The dish was perfection.  The noodles had great chew and the thin noodles added a difference to the texture that I have never experienced before.  The onsen egg was great as well.  It was the perfect dish to order on a hot humid August day.

My next two times I ordered the exact same thing.  The Uni cream udon with thick noodles.  Yes, the creamy udon has been done before, but it is done here with exquisite finesse.  At other places, I never order creamy udon soups, especially creamy uni udon, because it is often too creamy and rich to really appreciate any one component of the dish.  Here, I've ordered it twice.  The cream is light and well-balanced with the uni.  The noodles are, of course, always perfect.  The uni contributing the fresh taste of the ocean.  The seafood stock base giving depth to the dish.  It arrives looking like a work of art and tastes just as good as it looks.

Service here is very good.  On opening night, I ordered a San Pellegrino and it was poured into the cup for me, only for the waiter to realize that there was a small crack in this brand new glass.  He immediately took away the glass and the opened San Pellegrino, replaced it with a new glass and new bottle, and comped the item.

If I had to come up with a complaint about TsuruTonTan, it would be that the appetizers are just okay.  They're tasty and there's a large selection, but they are expensive for the portion provided and don't wow in any way.  Instead, what I do for appetizer is to order a couple of the cold udon soup options with thin noodles for the table to share.  And then we all get hot noodles for our entree.

If I had one wish for the place, it would be that they would start an udon tasting menu.  They could definitely put out a menu with a progressive tasting of different udon dishes.  Start with one of their tuna tartare cones as an amuse bouche, move on to a sashimi salad, then some tempura, then a cold udon, followed by a hot dashi udon, then an uni cream udon, then a curry udon, then the sizzling sukiyaki udon (once they figure out how to make it less sweet), some sort of green tea ice cream, and finishing with the water cake.  I would gladly order this.  Bonus points if they set up a chef's table and serve the tasting menu there.

TsuruTonTan has become one of my favorite restaurants in Manhattan.  If I did not live 75 minutes away by train, I would eat here much more often.

Tsurutontan located near Union Square is a new entry to the restaurant field. They come swiftly with their unique and fresh take on Udon. The place is big and can accommodate a large group even without reservations. I came to this place three times which left me full and satisfied.This place does not hold back when it comes to the udon as the portion sizes come in these giant bowls. They will give a large one for no additional cost just remember to ask after ordering.

Spicy Tuna Tartare Cone: This is a must get if you love sushi. They present it in a wooden box and shape in these little cones are filled with spicy tuna and avocado puree. A delightful experience and a good way to start a meal. I could easily down 10 of these but a tad expensive for that.

Grilled Duck Breast: I personally love duck but it has to be done correctly. Overcooking it would give a chewy texture that no one wants. The duck is drizzled with a white ginger soy which pairs nicely with it. The duck was tender and pack full of flavor. This is a must get and I get it every time I go.

Tatsuta Fried Chicken: Reminds me of Karaage and is served in most japanese restaurants. They did add a unique taste with the shibazuka tartar sauce but this is not something I would order again as it does not stand out like the others.

Pon Dumplings: Made with udon dough instead of the traditional dumpling skin. However, taste is mediocre and nothing special about this besides the shape. I would skip this in favor of other appetizers.

On to the main dishes where Tsurutontan is known for:

Sukiyaki Udon: I love the udon texture but the broth was way too sweet for my taste. I felt half way through it I was eating something similar to a dessert. I would not recommend this as I felt the sweetness overpowers everything.

Duck Udon: The duck fit perfectly in this dish as the broth was a clear dashi broth so nothing overpowered the udon and the duck. This was my favorite one and I would recommend it to anyone who want something simple and light.

Tan Tan Udon: A spicy udon with ground pork and chili oil. If you love spicy food, this is the one to get. There is a similarity to Dan Dan Noodles but maybe its just the name. The udon is a great vehicle to carry the flavor or the chili oil and the sesame broth they used. My family personally loved this one.

Tsuruton Curry Deluxe: I personally think curry and udon were made for each other. Udon is good at carrying thick sauces or broth and what a better sauce then a curry broth. I also love Japanese curry and wow was this good. A bite of the crispy pork katsu with the udon is like a taste of heaven. This also comes with Shrimp Tempura and Beef Short Plate.

Overall, I love this place. I am a big fan of quality food when coupled with decent portions. A lot of food allows others to share in the enjoyment and nothing is better than that.

Honestly I didn't see what all the hype is all about. It's a busy restaurant. I'll have to say that service is great here but I was hoping for more of a wow with the udon noodles. My brother and I ordered the sashimi salad to start and shared both a large duck noodle and tan tan udon. The duck udon was tasty and it reminded me of a Thai gang juerd soup.  As for the tan tan, I ordered it bc it said it was a top seller. That was my least favorite dish. I couldn't find myself to like it. The broth was too creamy for me like a curry broth. I'm not a huge fan of curry and creamy noodle soup. I also couldn't explain why I didn't like the texture of the noodle as well. I've had many homemade udon noodles. Had plenty of udon in japan. Tried some fresh made udon noodles in hawaii and that was bomb. But this place I can skip. I don't like waiting so long just for noodles. My brother enjoys this place along with his friends but he did warn me about the tan tan and knew I wouldn't like it. But I got sold on the picture and top seller sales pitch. Next time, I'll stick to what I like and know.

Came here with two girls and the food here is awesome. We ordered a Grilled Duck breast, Uni with Wagyu Beef, Chu-toro Blue Fin Tuna, Sea & Truffle Roll, Creamy Uni Udon, Mentaiko Caviar Udon and a Mushroom Truffle Creme Udon. 

Grilled Duck Breast - this is very flavorful and not dry at all. The duck breast was cooked perfectly and it was delicious, highly recommend ordering this as appetizer to share with friends.

Uni with Wagyu Beef - this is absolutely AWSOME, it is so delicious. The Wagyu beef melts in your mouth with a tint of sea salt with rice. This is a must get if you like Uni. I absolutely love this. A order comes in two piece but they give you an option to add an extra piece if you have a party of three.

Chu-toro Blue Fin Tuna - this is on their daily special menu and comes in three pieces. You can choose to get sashimi or sushi and we chose sushi. The tuna is good but in my opinion it is nothing special. 

Sea & Truffle Roll - this is a roll mixed with tuna, salmon and yellowtail with truffle oil. My friend highly recommended this and it turn out to be delicious. If you love truffle, this should be your go-to roll. You can smell the scent of truffle before you eat it and with a little wasabi, the roll is perfect.


Creamy Uni Udon - the noodles here come in two size, when you place the order the waiter will ask if you want regular size or large. Both sizes are the same price and the only difference is the large size have more noodles. Next the waiter will ask you what type of noodles and they have two types, thin or thick. We ordered a large size with thin noodle. The broth is very creamy and I love the taste. Out of the three Udon I tried here, this is my favorite one.

Mushroom Truffle Creme Udon - we ordered a large size with thick noodle for this noodle. This is also a creamy broth just like the creamy Uni Udon. The truffle taste is not overpowering at all but the Udon was a little soggy when we got to it. The soup base is not bad but not my favorite either. 

Mentaiko Caviar Udon -  this is a cold noodle and the waiter suggest getting the thin noodle for cold noodle so we ordered a regular thin noodle. They gave a lot of mentaiko caviar on top of the Udon for you to mixed the caviars with the cold Udon together. The mentaiko caviars made the udon a little too salty in my opinion. I couldn't eat a lot of this because it got too salty and one point. 

We thought we ordered too much food for three girls but at the end we finished everything because everything was so good. Definitely make a reservation before going there. We made a reservation and all of us arrived At least 30 minutes before our reservation time but we end up getting seated 15 minutes after our reservation time. It is very busy and crowded in this restaurant because this restaurant have awesome food. Certain food is a bit pricey compare to their other food but it is worth it because all the food have certain levels of qualities here. 

Will definitely come back to try more dishes and recommend this place to my friends.

This place never lets me down. It can get busy since it's on the trendier side, but the udon to me is worth the wait. I've tried some of the fancier dishes but I always come back to the plain beef udon. The broth is savory but not too rich, the noodles are bouncy and never soggy. It's perfect in its simplicity. My husband loves the curry udon and I've definitely been tempted by the creamy uni udon, but I'm not sure I'm ready to stray from the plain beef just yet!

I saw the pics really good, actually food there are pretty. But the udon is not as good as I expected. Sauce and soup are good, but the noodle itself is just average. But you can notice that the price is not average lol.

Slurping has been the latest eating habit and no one is around to judge or tell you otherwise anymore! In the Japanese culture, it is essential to make sure you eat its stable noodles, with the loudest slurps to show your enjoyment! When you think about Japanese noodles, what pops up into your mind first? Ramen? Soba? Udon? Well of all three, Udon noodles seem to be hidden in the dark abyss as its opponents (Ramen & Soba) propel into popularity.

If you love Udon noodles or like me, never really cared too much about, this place will make open your eyes like you never before. The size of the menu is ginormous and one absolute great thing about it is there are pictures!! The menu is section off between the appetizer on two sides and Udon heaven on the inside of the pamphlet-like menu. It separates the cold from the hot Udon noodles. Now onto the food, to keep it long story short. Everything I ordered was ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS and I will be counting down the days to come back and try the other stuff on the menu! This restaurant definitely brings Udon noodles to a completely different level of cloud 9. 


Appetizer:
-Uni And Caviar (Must try at least once!)
-Spicy Tuna Tartare cones (Must try at least once!)

Udon noodles: 
-Uni Udon (cold) - Uni melts in your mouth and noodles are  flavored perfectly to accentuate the Uni. The sesame seeds and 
-Sukiyaki Udon (hot) - The broth is perfect for a cold day with thin noodles and

It's very easy to find the place, you can see the name when you walk to 16th street. Everyone needs to be present in order to get a table, otherwise you have to wait.

The environment is really peaceful and not noisy at all. Staffs are welcoming and friendly. They gave good recommendations for food and drinks. The only thing is that they always came and checked if we had finished eating. Maybe it was late and they wanted to wash dishes early. I understood that, but it made us a bit uncomfortable. 

Appetizer: We ordered tuna cones as appetizer, and it was sooo good!

Udon: We ordered regular size of Dandan udon and Sukiyaki noodle. The bowl was huge! The broth of Dandan noodle is yummy! Sukiyaki noodle is sweet. They gave us free noodles to add.

Drink: We got oni within, lychee rose, and lychee mojito(no alcohol). I love the lychee rose! Lychee mojito tastes like soda.

Dessert: Green tea ice cream is a must try. 

Overall I love the place.

My boyfriend and I are regulars here, and for good reason! The menu is diverse in options and we order different dishes every time.  They always are phenomenal with their beef sukiyaki, the fried chicken appetizer.

Whoa!

Very impressed with the food there. The serving size was really impressive, I would say go with a group and share is better than dining alone because you'd get to try different noodle dishes and have stomach room to order the other dishes on the menu as well.

Love their fried chicken and the mysterious purple mayonnaise based sauce.

the only great thing about this restaurant is the bowl is big. It is good for people who like to take a picture and post to the social media. For the taste, it is average in the us, and far away from the Japanese standard. 

Worthy to try. Not worthy to wait

Love this place. The kimchi udon is great. Don't get too ambitious and ask for the large portion though (regular and large are the same price). Or you won't have any space in your stomach for the dessert.

Had the most gigantic bowl of beef sukiyaki udon here! And the crazy thing was that it was the same price as the smaller size...what?! Obviously I got the large and slurped all of it right up. The udon was thick and chewy and soaked up the slightly sweet flavor of the broth. My only complaint was that they could have added more meat.

My boyfriend ordered the tanin beef don and loved it. I tried a bit and thought it was a tad too creamy and bland. It was good, but my udon was definitely better. 

For our appetizer we got the tofu burrata out of sheer curiosity. It was so interesting! It was very creamy and formed that i thought it would be. Definitely not the texture of burrata haha but more like a soymilk flavored creme brûlée.

Will be back regularly to get my udon fix!

Unlike Ramen , it is so hard to find a restaurant which serves authentic and  good Udon. Many of them serve defrosted Udon which tends to be too soft for my liking. 
Finally, I found a good authentic Udon here. I am really happy.

I know it may not sound right. But this udon is one of my favorite udon in the world. Obviously their udon is not traditional one; however their food is the fusion of the western and the Japanese style. The soup of mine is like the taste of paste, however i can tell they are udon. Very impressive.  This store will definitely to be one of my favorite restaurant.

I was rushed when I ate here, so I didn't get as much of a taste as I would have like. It's on the pricey side for Udon for sure. And I was thrown off completely by the fact the large and small sizes were the same price? That's asking for people to waste food...

The one other thing I'll say is that when the waiter asks you "Have you been here before? Do you want help with the menu?" Just say you're good. I made the mistake and had what felt like a 20min lesson on the very extensive menu. And he didn't even get to the end of it...I had to cut him off.

Not sure if my taste buds were off at my visit, but everything tasted slightly too salty for my liking.

Kuro Buta Pork Kakuni ($15 USD)
Braised pork belly, hardboiled egg, shishito  and daikon. The pork belly were well braised, the meat was really soft and tender. The hardboiled egg was nothing special, being at a Japanese restaurant I would have expected it to be more of a runny soft boiled egg instead. The sauce was pretty salty though.

The bowl of noodles here are bigger than my face! One interesting thing was they said you can ask for normal or extra noodles for your bowl, but there is no additional cost if you ask for extra noodles. Then really, who would want to have less noodles? You also have the option of choosing thick or thin udon.
Sukiyaki Udon ($24 USD)
Beef short plate. onsen egg and vegetables in a sweet sukiyaki broth. The broth is supposed to be sweet, for some reason I felt like the more you eat it, it ends up tasting really salty which made me not wanting to eat too much of it. There were lots of ingredients though which was good. I actually felt that there were more beef and vegetables than udon. The texture of the udon was good though - thick and slightly chewy. 
Tsuruton Curry Deluxe ($24 USD)
Shrimp tempura, pork cutlet, and beef short plate in Japanese curry broth. To me, the curry taste wasn't too strong but I found it still tasty. The soup was slightly thicker, which I felt went well with the texture of the udon acting like a curry sauce to go with it. The cutlet pork and shrimp tempura were served inside the soup so the breaded fried layer lost its crispiness and was soggy. Probably would have been better if they served the fried food on the side instead.

I dined at Tsurutontan for a friend's birthday about a month ago and had a good time.  So when my sister asked for a fun spot to celebrate her promotion, I recommended we come here.  She made a 6:15pm reservation and arrived early checking in with the male host.  At around 6:15pm our entire party was present and we informed the host the same.  He told us they needed about 10 minutes to set up the table.  Ten minutes rolled by and we were still not seated so we checked in again.  This time the host informed us that the previous party was just wrapping up and that we would be seated soon.  Meanwhile, small and large parties were getting seated while we continued to wait.  When we checked in once more, we received a curt response, eye rolls and a shaking of the head - completely unprofessional.  We were finally seated 45 minutes after our reservation time.  A female host called out for our party and asked if we were all present.  YES, WE HAVE ALL BEEN HERE SINCE 6:15PM!  A manager eventually came out and while he apologized, he did not provide an explanation on the delay but instead offered to bring out our food quickly and comped our apps.

I am a firm believer in making a reservation especially in New York City and waiting a bit give or take the usual 15 minute grace window.  However, a 45 minute wait time with a reservation is not reasonable.  Furthermore, the unprofessional attitudes from the hosting staff is unacceptable.  I  will not be coming back here anytime soon.  You can find better udons elsewhere with courteous service.

Tsurutontan is most well know for their ginormous bowls of ramen. What is even more amazing is that the regular is the same price as the large. The only major difference is the amount of noodles you will have in your ramen bowl. 

FOOD:
Dining with 4 friends, I was able to sample a few different udon this restaurant offers. 

Spicy Tuna Tartare Cone. This was alright for me. It's plated in a box with uncooked rice, it was super cute. It was a creamy tuna consistency with smashed avocado served in a cone. No wow factor for me. 

Snowcrab Roll. Okay, this may not be the name, but it's one of the bestsellers. This roll gave me life! I would have loved to have more!

I personally ordered the Uni Creamy Udon. Uni reeled me in and WOW. The uni tasted fresh and went so well with the creamy broth. Be advised, creamy is the operative word here It was CREAMY and borderline too heavy. Nonetheless, I enjoyed every bit of it. 

The Sukiyaki beef udon. They will warn you, this is on the sweet end and they are not lying. SO overpowering. I would be okay with a few good sips, but a bowl would be too much for my liking. Beef was great!
