The Seafood tempura udon. The broth is much lighter than the other udon bowls, which is surely preferred. Surprisingly with all the tempura in the broth, it was not that oily. I would definitely get this for next time!

The Spicy tan tan ramen with pork. It didn't have a kick as it name would suggest. The broth seemed like it had a lot of oil and left a peanut after taste flavor. Not a fan. We ordered a sukiyaki beef on the side. Even without the broth, the meat itself was soooo sweet. But, the texture and fatty beef combined got me hooked.

The restaurant has a wonderful ambiance, extensive menu, with a great drink menu. The food was good, but I would love to try other udon options. I would recommend this joint and would come back. The prices are worth the really big portions. The service had no hiccups, I could not complain.

I've been excited to try this place for a while and despite the mediocre reviews that I've read on this page, I decided I'd try it out myself, only to find out that those reviews had hit the nail right on the head. 

The restaurant is extremely large which is great, because it's always hard to find such a big venue in the city. The prices are reasonable, especially when you think of how much food you're actually getting. They said that the large vs. regular serving of noodles cost the same, but my friends had told me the regular size in itself was already so huge, and they were right. The noodles are also definitely thicker than the udon noodles I'm used to so that's another factor into the dish being so filling. 

How did the food taste? It's pretty much what you've been reading in the reviews. Overly sweet. We ordered the Wagyu Shabu Udon which was okay, not the best, but not horrible. We also shared the Spicy Soondoboo Jigae Udon, which was overly sweet for being a spicy dish. It had the essence of a soondoboo jigae, but with a whole bunch of sugar added to it and I don't believe the stew itself traditionally has any sugar added to it. 

I will say the only up-side to this place is that I'm sure this place is great for large groups, which is perfect because they also have a lot of different options to choose from. Just beware when ordering some of the brothy udons.

Pricy spot but I LOVE the atmosphere so that makes up for pricing. The staff is always friendly and on top of everything. I always get the Uni Creamy Udon and keep it to myself because it is soon delicious! Overall I highly recommend this spot to anyone and everyone.

I eat by myself quite often trying new restaurants. Tsurutonton was on my list: 

This place is has a modern ambience with a bar area with lots of seating and dining areas on the other side of its wall. 

They were very professional, offering to have my coat hanged and my violin stored away while I sat down. You get a number with the coat check and it's free!

I ordered the uni creme udon thick noodles. I tell you it came in an interestingly large bowl with a lid that they lifted for me. 

A good amount of uni topped the noodles with lots of mentaiko. The only thing was I think I expected was a thick creamy uni noodles but this was definitely mixed with uni cream and chicken broth. So if you're searching for a creamy thick udon soup, this isn't it. 

However this spot is good for single eaters or with groups of friends. I plan on coming back to try the other things on the menu that equally look unique!

Good noodles, but I wouldn't recommend their uni dishes. Maybe it's not the season, but I felt you could get much higher quality uni at that price.

Would come back if I had a hankering for noodles near Union Square but would likely lean towards trying a new place instead.

I like the variety of dishes and atmosphere. I had the tantan noodle, which had mild spicy and cream base soup. They served in huge bowl and big portions of noodle & soup. You have choice of large or regular and there is no extra charge for the size up :) my only complain is that servers were not responsive, slow, and confused. I don't think they were trained, although I can see they were trying. Food wise: good experience

Ok so ramen for me is simple really -well flavored broth and fresh ingredients. I have to say not in love with their broth. BUT there is a but here- please try the spicy tuna and avocado cones appetizer. Really just perfect hence the rating!

absolutely delicious, huge portions - best to share

Great apetizers
faboulous noodles
original, modern ambiance - great design, music, very nice and helpfull service

Nice and wise menu: accompagned by photos of dishes

Came here for a weekday lunch without reservations.  It was great; we were able to get a table without problems.  The décor was beautiful with restaurant divided into different areas.  Under our servers recommendation, I ordered the wagyu with mushrooms udon instead of the sukiyaki udon because he said the sukiyaki was on a sweeter side so I'm glad I did the wagyu with mushroom one.  It was still a little sweet but just the right amount for me.  The udon noodles are cooked to perfection.  Al dente style just how I like it.

Would love to come back for dinner and enjoy their cocktail menu.

Im not a typical noodle fan, but definitely love the way this place cook their udon noodles. Amazing taste, wonder appetizer. Specially the soup of the noddle, is delicious. Definitely recommend to everyone.

my girlfriend and I stopped by on Sunday evening around 9pm.  

The receptionist was a little frigid asking "if we had a reservation", which prompted me to look around and see a lot of empty tables.  They seated us in a interesting seating area, please see the picture.  I didn't mind, but with plenty of room in the restaurant, they (not sure who does the seating, I am assuming the receptionist) kept seating people right in front of us...which was kind of annoying if I'm honest.  It's hard to describe the seating, so I will post a picture.

Our waitress Valentina was great!  She explained the extensive menu (i have a picture of my girlfriend perusing the menu) in great detail, thank you!!

As far as the food goes, I thought it was wonderful.  Perhaps 5 stars, if the seating situation was better...

We started off with a Spicy Tuna Tartare Cone ($12) which was very niiiicce!  It comes 4 in an order, but I wished that there were like 8 in an order, haha!  I really like them!  Just the right amount of spiciness and the crunch from the cone is wonderful!

One interesting fact is that they have 2 sizes for the Udon, but they charge the same.  One is a regular size and the other is a larger size with more noodles...duh!! We both got the larger sizes haha!  Definitely do it if you plan to share your bowls!

She had the Tan Tan Udon, which comes with a spicy and creamy sesame broth, ground pork and chilly oil!! ($20).  It had a nutty flavor, more creamy than broth...if you are in the mood for broth, then maybe this is not for you.  But as far as flavor and texture, I give this a thumbs up!

I had the Hot and Sour Udon ($20), comes with thinly sliced beef, eggplant, mushroom in an egg drop broth!  YUUUUMMMMM!  I really liked my broth and the flavor.  Right balance of spicy and sour, this is not like your Chinese resto Hot and Sour soup, very different.  Every ingredient blends well together, I ate my entire bowl!! If you're in the mood for good broth, this is the one for you!

PRO TIP:  he noodles in the udon is way long, so probably need to cut it in half to make a nice bite sized spoonful!  The spoon that they give you is GINORMOUS, you requested a smaller spoon which is the normal sized spoon, haha! 

We finished the meal with 2 desserts.  We had the Banana Mille Feuille from Lady M, I never had it before.  I thought is was ok, not great.  Tasted a little like banana pudding from a cupcake vendor.  I probably wouldn't get it again.  Finally we had Lychee Sorbet, which was a nice finish to cleanse the palate.

All in all, the food is great, very good in fact.  The ambiance is probably too nice for a Udon restaurant, but they are calling it a Brasserie, so it's nice!  I didn't like our seating, but it's my opinion.    

I would definitely go back to try the other Udons!

ENJOY!

The food here is okay....
we got the uni udon and duck udon
the soap base here isnt amazing which is the key to a good udon dish
the uni was drowned in this super creamy thick sauce that i'm not even sure what i was supposed to taste
bar staff are nice and friendly

The two of us were seated right away on a Tuesday early evening (around 6). The interior is pretty swanky and hip and really enjoyed the mood the dimmed lights created. 

As soon as we sat down, the server fired off his recommendations and most popular dishes with a detailed description of each. It was pretty impressive. We ordered one appetizer to share (pork belly) and two udon dishes. I wasn't too thrilled that the udon came at the same time as the appetizer, as I wanted to take my time and enjoy the delicious pork belly with my beer and sake. 

I ordered the Uni Creme Udon and the creamy broth was delectable. My gf ordered the Sizzling Sukiyaki Udon. I tried a bite and it was slightly on the heavy side accompanied by mild sweetness. Don't get me wrong, it was delicious but without chasing it down with some sake, it is one of those greasy dishes that you would get tired of easily. Overall, this is a great place to try at least once or twice. But if you're on a budget and want to impress your lady/beau on your first date, do your math before making the reservation.

All the appetizers are tasty. Highly recommend the tuna cone and beef. Noodle bowl is HUGE, literally! It would be a good idea to share a big bowl with one or two other friends. Tantan noodle was not very authentic - instead of spicy, it was sweet. The signature curry dulex was pretty good. Service was great. Price - a bit expensive for a noodle place.

This place is amazing if you want to try authentic Japanese Udon noodle! 
The Uni pasta is great with the cold thin noodle! 
The squid tempura (calamari?) is great too!!

We were able to get a table for 2 on Resy a few days out and still change the time the night of the Friday reservation.  I'm not sure they do anything between 6:15 and 8:45 online - they may reserve those for walk-ins only?  I think there was no wait for smaller parties for walk ins at 8:45pm.

It's actually a pretty big space, and it's very modern / non traditional, but the restaurant is originally from Japan.  

This was dinner #2 for us, so we could only eat so much. The actual bowls for the soup udons are huge.  Udons come in small and large - same price - the only difference is the amount of noodles. 

- Smashed cucumbers: great texture - clean and crisp, flavorful but not overly heavy miso sesame dressing. However, there were only around 10 small pieces for $7, which I thought was on the expensive side 
- Sizzling sukiyaki udon: sukiyaki beef, onions, and mushrooms but without all the soup. I had read the soup was overly sweet. Even just the dry ingredients were on the sweet side, but adding red pepper and breaking the raw egg yolk helped a lot to balance the flavor and add richness. The noodles didn't get an amazing char in the bowl, but they were still quite good 
- Tempura udon: the broth was clean and proper. The tempura was too oily for me. The onions, shiso leaf, nori were all quite greasy. The shrimp was pretty good 

Overall, it was pretty filling.  We were curious about some of the desserts like the Mille crepe and another sphere shaped dessert, but we really couldn't eat anymore. 

Service was very polite, and they were good about water refills and checking in. Food also comes out pretty quickly. 

I think it's interesting to check out. Compared to what we had in Japan, it was much more expensive (not surprisingly), but the stuff was definitely one of the better udons I've had in the US.
Loved the chewiness of the udon. The uni was also very fresh and tasty. The big bowls make for awesome Instagram pictures

Probably the priciest udon you'll ever have in New York but they are also the biggest bowl of udon I have ever seen in my life. And they are delicious too! Unlike those places that serve big but not so yummy udon. You can even ask for a larger portion (1 1/2 times more noodles than the regular portion) Been three times already and have not been disappointed all three times.

The service is great too. Each time they were very friendly. The last time I went, I went with a large group with a reservation and had changed the time and group size 5 times, but they accommodated us without any attitude or complaints. We did have to wait 20 minutes past our reservation time, but it seemed like that was out of their control with customers not leaving.. And we did have a big group.

Definitely make a reservation before you go, especially in the fall/winter.

Went to tsurutontan udon noodle place for the second time yesterday.  It's good enough to be a repeat visit type place in my opinion!  The draw is that it's a restaurant dedicated to udon noodles--the thicker cousin of ramen noodles.  Indubitably there's more udon noodle dish varieties here than at any other nyc restaurant.  There's soupy udon, cold udon, hot udon, spicy udon , dry udon, sweet udon etc.  there's also rice based don dishes.     The best sellers here include both cold & hot sea urchin or uni udon noodles.  Both of which i have tried--both are satisfying to this sea urchin megafan.  

On this visit we were a group of 4 adults & one baby & we ordered hot uni creme udon, duck udon, sizzling sukiyaki udon & spicy tantan udon plus as part of lunch special you can add of for $3 extra a small rice bowl with either soy garlic fried chicken/or mentaiko cod roe rice or sukiyaki beef rice--we did 2 bowls of soy garlic fried chicken rice as it was highly recommended by our server.  

As for kids: note there's no kids menus but as the option to order large vs regular size noodles with your order at no extra charge is there it's easy to share your meal with a small kid.  There are booster seats but no high chairs & no changing table in bathroom.  

My favorites this visit were hot uni creme udon & sukiyaki udon!
The noodles are good, just good. The space and the presentation are fun but something about this place feels gimmicky

Lovely ambiance and ample seating for solo diners at the bar! I was impressed by the extensive menu options: basic dashi Udon, creme Udon, cold Udon, rice bowls, sushi, sashimi, etc. I ordered the large uni creme Udon with thick noodles as recommended by the waitress (thick noodles for creme based and dashi based udon). The size of the bowl blew me away, but I had no problems finishing every drop and still had space for dessert. Back to the uni creme udon I ordered - it was mediocre at best. The uni didn't taste very creamy and fresh and the ebiko was lost in the pool of soup. The soup... Was so diluted it doesn't qualify as creme. More like dashi soup (I could taste the dashi) that looks like creme. The only saving grace was that the large costed the same as small and that filled up my tummy for the most part. I definitely won't return for the uni, but am excited to try other dishes on the menu!

Came here for lunch when it first opened.

The udon was overdone. Period, end of story. If you can't get udon texture right as an udon place... no.

The location and decor is cool but what happened to the noodles? Frozen noodles are better and chewier than this mess. 

Just got back from Japan and this fails in comparison, (as with most foreign country to US transplants), but for it to be subpar to frozen Korean noodles for $4.99 a pack of 5, is sad. The broth in the Tsurutontan Deluxe Udon was good in the sense that it had a very "homemade" taste but nothing to pay money for. Sukiyaki Udon, same thing, also very sweet.

People, Sukiyaki broth is made with Soy Sauce, Sugar, Mirin, Sake, and Dashi Broth (you can get instant ones for $5). Not hard, so definitely not worth paying $24 for a bowl each if you can do better or similar at home.

Shiso martini was watery and had an odd aftertaste... yes, I use shiso in cooking a lot and it was sigh

Disappointing. Overhyped by the location/decor/japanophiles? Will not be returning.

It's easy to make a reservation online using Resy. I made one about a week in advance for 6:30pm on a Monday. They don't seat you until full party is there, but you can wait at the bar. I ordered a Tokyo Mule while waiting and it tastes like a regular moscow mule. I couldn't taste the Yuzu.

Tofu Burrata - Very smooth tofu. It reminds me of the silken tofu my grandma used to give us with congee. There is no burrata in this dish.

Udon Pon Dumplings - The waitress said it this was dough only, but it actually had vegetables inside. It tastes like a pan-fried vegetable dumpling. 

Mentaiko Ankake Udon with thick noodles - I ordered this for my entree and really enjoyed it. The broth was a delicious and savory eggy broth. Mentaiko is salty, so I took a first few bites to get the fishy flavor and then mixed it with the broth. I chose the thick noodles because it has more of a chew, but they are more filling. The regular is huge! I thought it was a large at first. You definitely don't need a large. Or I don't at least. Two people can even eat the regular size.

Uni Udon with thin noodles - My friend ordered the large portion with thin noodles, which was about the same as the regular thick noodle portion. Or it could be my soup made my order seem larger. I liked the thin noodles better. They were softer, but still chewy. I would probably go for that next time. The uni isn't the best quality, but the whole dish tasted as I expected. Just uni mixed in with noodles. There was nothing surprising there.

I've heard some mixed reviews from several of my friends who went, but I really enjoyed what I ordered.

I think I've stumbled into heaven on earth. When people ask me what my favorite food is, I always say noodle soup (I don't specify because I don't discriminate). BUT if we want to get specific, I prefer thick noodles over thin noodles because they're more fun to eat and chew. So what better place to indulge my noodle obsession?!

The menu here is endless (it seems), hot noodle soup, cold noodle soup, stir fry noodles, etc. I ordered the wagyu ramen because it was listed as a favorite. When the server came to take our orders, she told us that extra noodles were FREE. Um, excuse me, what? *Falls deeper in love* I also asked for hot sauce for my soup, and she said it was going to be $1 (I said ok, to which my ATL friend said, oh you have that New York money now lol).

I do recommend mixing the soup to make sure the distribution of flavor doesn't sink to the bottom, but of course this was delicious! The noodles were perfectly done. If udon noodles are overcooked, they break and become mushy and it's not pretty. The broth was flavorful and not overbearing of soy sauce, which I find is the issue with most Japanese places that serve udon. 

Try to make a reservation if you can or just come really late at night at 9pm like me to avoid the wait!

Tsurutontan has excellent food and a great atmosphere. I've brought my mother here when she was visiting from Korea, and she thoroughly enjoyed it. Judging from the many doe-eyed couples that surrounded us, it's probably a good date spot. Of course, I have no boyfriend and no potential suitors, so I can't really confirm this.

We ordered the salmon & snoe crab roll, the Tsurutontan deluxe udon, the uni crème udon, and the water cake. The roll was excellent (not too sweet), and both udons were hearty. I ordered the uni crème udon--while it was expectedly heavy, I couldn't stop eating it. So delicious! I should probably note that even the "regular" portion was generous--I can't imagine how much food you'd get if you ordered the large.

Okay now for the criticism. The water cake is literally tasteless--you're paying $8 for flavorless jello that you top with a bit of unsweetened misugaru, honey, and vanilla ice cream. If I were to make the water cake myself, I'd eliminate the toppings and rather infuse something sweet with the gelatin to make it more dynamic.

But besides the cake, great restaurant!
The moment when a waiter asks:"Is this enough?", we all know that we'll never come back.

I've heard wonderful things about Tsurutontan, so my boyfriend and I decided to try it. I went once around 7pm and I was quoted a 2 hour wait, so I decided not to stay since I was really hungry. I tried back a week later at 5:30 pm and was given a table right away. 

Atmosphere and service -
The atmosphere was great. They have a separate single tables by the walls and one long communal table in the middle. Even though it was one long communal table, I was still able to feel private with the help of a divider up to the ceiling in the middle of the table. The service as wonderful. The server was very helpful with the menu and drinks. The food came out very fast and very presentable. 

Food
The spicy tuna tartare cone (one of their more popular item on the menu). It was great. It tasted very fresh and interesting with the crunchy cone. It also had smashed avocado inside, underneath the tuna. 

We ordered the Uni-Toro-Caviar sushi on the sushi menu just because we love uni, toro and caviar. When it's put together, PLEASE GIVE ME! It was 2pcs for $31 which I felt was a little pricey, but why not? :p When I ate it, it was oh my god.. The combination was great together. Everything was so fresh and I was overwhelmed. It was amazing.

The shrimp dumpling was okay. We only ordered it because my boyfriend loves to eat any form of dumplings everywhere he goes. My boyfriend really liked it and I thought it was kind of basic. It had garlic, chili oil, cilantro and ponzu sauce. It actually tasted like a szechuan dumpling.

For main course, we ordered Mentaiko Caviar Udon with Uni. I loved it so much. It comes cold and the uni is served on a small dish on the side. I just dumped it into the udon and ate it together. It was very flavorful, but my boyfriend felt it was a little overwhelming after a few bites. The udon was cooked perfectly (to my liking). It was not overcooked where it was mushy and not undercooked where it was too hard. The udon was firm and had a good bite to it.

We also got the uni creme udon. I liked it, but it lacked a bit of flavor for me (after eating the mentaiko caviar udon). My boyfriend didn't like it much, so I ended up switching with him. It came with a warm soup and udon with uni on top. The uni tasted fresh and the soup was a bit more on the heavier side. It was pretty creamy, but I was fine with it. 

I will definitely come back with reservations. I can't wait to try the other things on the menu. :)

Full disclaimer: I usually prefer lighter broth Japanese noodles (whether it's ramen or udon) so of course this being my first time trying Tsurutontan, I went for the basic chicken broth as I believe that is the way to taste and judge the real flavor of these noodle bowls!

The menu is quite extensive, with an overload of noodles to choose from, complete with appetizers as well. However, we were here for a quick lunch so only tried 2 noodles and a side of rice ($3 extra to make it a lunch set). The Tsurutontan Deluxe and chicken udon both tasted very authentic - the dashi broth was not overly salty (you can actually drink it! unlike some ramen soups..) and there was an abundance of meat (an assortment of tempura and a healthy portion of chicken thigh pieces in the chicken udon). There was no picture of the side of soy garlic fried chicken rice so what came out was a bit unexpected. But the 3-4 chucks of garlic fried were very flavorful and the rice drizzled with some kimchi flavored sauce. What's even nicer is that "large" portion of noodles is free so no reason to go with "regular" size! But the bowl was so big that I could not finish all of the noodles...

Onto the ambiance - definitely chic and a bit trendy, but not in an uninviting and unfriendly way. However, you can tell that the interior is a bit run down and could really use a new coat of paint (especially in the ladies room....), hopefully management will spruce up the place soon. There was also an old musty smell away from the dining room so I would have given a 3-star if ambiance was more important to me... but overall, enjoyed this place!
Worth the wait specially the sour and spicy udon! Parents loved it!

definitely go with the THICK NOODLES (not that there is anything wrong w the thin noodles) but the thick noodles are "al dente"  & yet still tender w the right chewiness
whenever i have the option of spicy soup...i will opt for it.....& yes i absolutely LOOOOVE the Tan Tan Udon (it's a giant bowl of spicy nutty/sesame soupy broth w tiny bits of minced pork dancing in the broth with the thick noodle activity) HAPPY HAPPY HOT HOT (in temeparture and spicyness...) excellent soup., Great for a cold gloomy rainy type of day.... spicy level i would say 8/10...it's spicy...but i like spicy ...so maybe others would rate ot 10/10... 
i also loooved the spicy soondubu Jigae (i had it w the thin noodles....i think because the noodles are thin it expands at a quicker rate and absorbs the broth...i am a fan of broth...so next time i would prob. opt for the thicker noodles so there is more broth left in the soondubu....nevertheless... still delicious and 8/10 spicy level)
infact thinking about these bowls...i want to get some NOW
spicy tuna tartar in cones are super cute and delicious too... it's almsot like a cone taco ceviche tartar?!?!?! 
and the tempura is my weakness... i love crunchy crispy fried stuff
the side sauce  it comes with is warm! which is an excellent touch. now i feel like every other place i've gotten tempura has ripped w off w the cold sauce ...i should know the sauce name by now...i think it's some sort of soy... anyway
again DELICIOUS
i HAD A GREAT EXPERIENCE HERE
forget it....I'm running there now...

Pleasantly surprised. Went with no expectations but was probably one of the more memorable udon I've had in NYC. Even beats Raku! Portions are generous but a steep price for just noodles. I would still come back again because the broth was so rich. (And the servers were really nice.)

I brought my family here for dinner on a week night and sat right down. Very cool layout and decor. The menu is easy to navigate with pictures and descriptions. We enjoyed the smashed cucumbers and the pickled vegetables (tsukemono) for appetizers. I had the nabeyaki udon and my son had the sukiyaki udon. The noodles themselves were consistent and pretty long and perfectly cooked. The flavor of my nabeyaki was excellent. I wasn't able to taste my son's udon because he finished before I got a chance. Definitely one of the best nabeyaki udons I've tasted. It is also one of the most expensive bowls of udon I've eaten. But I guess if you're eating in a place like NYC, it's to be expected. The service was friendly and attentive but there seemed to be a little forgetfulness about refilling our green tea. All in all a great meal. It is easy to see how this restaurant has earned high ratings on Yelp!

キレイ、新しい、
席空いてるのに何故ここ？

I usually go to this restaurant in Tokyo.
Thats why i good to know price and service and how much volume ...
Then i wanted to try ny location. 
When we went there around 9pm .it already few familys and couples were there. 
But they gave us small space.. alot people walking behind us.. So noisy.. 
but when i watched that there were alot of empty table ...so bat feel and we were girls , not couple .and also wr have some shopping bags!...if there are empty seats , Please giving us 4 people seats!

This place was ALMOST really good. Three of us went on a night that was not terribly busy. Each of our orders came out at a different time. The wait staff was very nice, and kept coming by to apologize that not all the food was out yet, but I would have preferred if all 3 dishes had arrived in a way that let us eat together. By the time my udon arrived, everybody else at my table was almost finished :(

wasn't actually impressed with the food here.  went with a group for dinner and none of us were really impressed.  maybe we went on an off night, but my udon lacked flavor, so much so that i had to put my boyfriend's curry sauce into my bowl.  probably won't be back.

I love that you can get a large with no upcharge!

But I will say, the large is huge - and unless you slurp it down relatively quick, the noodles start to soak up the soup and get a bit chunky. 

We started with the sukiyaki buns, which I recommend :) 
The bun was soft, the meat was tender, the light sauce made it a great appetizer.
We also had the grilled duck breast to just try something different; it was okay, nothing to rave about. 

For the noodles, I went for curry because I was in the mood. I felt really heavy after a short-while, and I definitely should not have gone for a large... 

My friend got the deluxe and it was a lighter broth which I think is complementary for such a dense meal. I tried it, and thought it was really good! 

Perhaps I should have tried something more "special," but overall, quite a good place but personally I did not have a meal I felt was worth $100+ for 2.

So... after hearing rave reviews from multiple sources including close friends, what else is one to do. I've gotta verify with my own taste buds. See how sexy this place really is! But with high expectations there's always a fear of being let down... so here goes...

Ambiance is good and I avoided peak hours. I HATE long lines and waiting which I hear happens here a lot. The spacing was just a bit tight but enough that you don't feel cramped. I've been to places that pack your asses in like a chicken coup, this was not one of them. The design was nice, modern and clean. 7.5/10

Service was friendly and the waiter explained the menu and recommended dishes and specials to try. Wait staff came around to ask us about our meal once or twice and our glasses were constantly refilled when low. 8/10 

First dish- Soy Garlic Fried Tatsuta Chicken: damn tasty! Definitely hot. Very fresh. (Pro tip: burned the roof of my mouth. Not blaming them, I should've known better but I'm a fatass that loves fried chicken... go figure.) Incredibly juicy on the inside, felt like maybe it came from a pressure fryer or something. The outside was crunchy and there was a good balance/quantity of sauce in it that it didn't overwhelm, but had me soaking it up from the plate with my last few bites of chicken. 7.7/10

Sizzling Sukiyaki Udon: my wife had this. No worries, as always, I waited until she was slowing down to steal the last few bites (for the sake of this review of course!). That's one hearty dish. Seemed like a good mix of meat in there even at the end. Sauce was thick but not too salty, at least in my opinion (they call me sodium boy btw). Although I didn't get to have a lot, I'd still say this was a solid dish. Presentation came put sizzling and I'm betting the initial few bites of this bad boy would've been better than the last 1-2 bites I had. I'm giving this 7.8/10

Truffle Creme with Crab and Mushroom: this was my dish... and HOT DAMN was this satisfying. My fear going in was that they would biotch out on me and not give me what they advertised. To my relief they delivered! A generous portion of a good mix of ingredients. Usually, I eat and leave feeling "there wasn't enough XYZ... and too much udon or noodles", NOT the case here. Friggin solid, truffle (check), creme (check), crab (double check), and mushroom (drop the fracking mic). Truffle flavor was great, I hate the shuttle shit and I loathe if it's to overpowering, especially when it comes to truffles. You've gotta have balance on the truffle taste, they nailed it. Creme was thick enough to cling onto the udon but not so much so that im filling up on it. Tons of crab pieces in all bites (pro tip: if you can down this sonofabitch the best part is slurping the bottom of the bowl with all the good stuff laying at the bottom), and the mushrooms... oh boy these mushrooms,... different kinds and in a generous amount. The mushrooms btw, were not soaked but felt like they were individually prepared and added last. You just have to be a grilled mushroom fan to understand. But if I had one word to describe this dish it would be "distinct". You tasted everything individually and yet they all came together to make a wholesome happy dish. Best udon ever?,... No,... but damn is it up there. 8.6/10

Would I recommend this place? To sum up "I'm definitely coming back..."

The price may look pricy but it comes with a full plate. Really big serving and taste is very good. I thought I will not come back for it because it's a little expensive but if you share (girls) with your friends then you can manage to finish a bowl of noodle. 

Really like their appetizer like spicy salmon cup thing. Something you must try!!!
Generous amount of serving!i ordered the uni cold ramen. Noodle was perfect and sauce was delicious. A little light on the uni though.

The atmosphere was very nice and well kept. The restaurant was spacious and the servers were friendly and helpful. I went with a large group for a birthday celebration so it was the perfect venue. The udon came in large portions but I thought the texture of the noodles were standard. I ordered the Tan Tan udon. The broth was very thick and overall not that spicy but I still enjoyed it and the serving was generous.  My main reason for giving three stars was that  they charged us a $3/person plating fee for the cake we bought in. Since there were 13 of us there, the total plating fee ($39) added up to the price of two bowls of udon. The fee was completely unexpected since we were not notified until it was time for them to bring out the cake and there weren't any in-house desserts on the menu.
Great for a group, great food but just Okay service. All different kinda udon noodle, I don't really think it's authentic... more localized food but taste isn't so bad.

One of the best udon in U.S.  We went there on Wednesday night.  We didn't have reservation, so we were told to wait 30 min., but actual waiting time was less than that.  The menu has photos so it is easy to understand what we get.  Taste was so Japanese.  I will recommend this place to all real udon lovers!

It's actually a 3.7 star.
I came for week day and weekend lunch. 

Sizzling Sukiyaki Udon ($18) - an impact of the dish did not wow me as other dishes. It is mostly because the size of bowl. it was in a traditional Korean sizzling stone bowl, meaning it's in a smaller bowl than ridiculously humongous bowls that most other dishes are in. This sukiyaki was rather salty but the flavor was on point, delicious. I wish there was more portion of toppings, beef and Enoki mushrooms, that would matched the price. The Udon noodle was bouncy-chewy deliciousness and it was a filling dish.
 
Sukiyaki Udon ($20) - I would pick this one rather than the sizzling one. First, it comes in that huge bowl with all the traditional toppings for Sukiyaki and generous portion of broth, more like a soup here. 

Uni & US Wagyu Sushi ($22) - I expected more from this sushi. The combination is very similar to U.S. Kobe chuck flap & Uni on Nori seaweed at Takashi. The contrary to the menu picture of this dish, the beef was cooked, not raw. I picked up the entire thin sheet of beef and Uni placing in the center with sushi rice under and put in my mouth. I expected the explosion of flavors, like I got that from Takashi. It was a simply greasy flavor less sushi. It definitely screamed for acidity. We had some limes for San Pellegrino so I splashed the lime juice over it. It helped but I would not order it again. 

Cold Uni Udon ($24) - knowing Mentaiko Udon would be so good and I make it at home, I opted for something a bit more decadent, Uni. Bonito and Konbu dashi with fresh Uni in the sauce was really nice and enhanced the flavor of Uni. I wish the quality of Uni was better. 

The thinner Sanuki udon noodle used in this this was a perfect choice, more flavor of the sauce be entwined and achieving much needed flavor in a one bite. The portion in a huge bowl looked sad comparing to other dishes but it was a good portion for lunch.

Tsuruton Curry Deluxe ($24) - if you like thick Japanese curry, you might enjoy this dish. The thick noodle goes so well with this curry. If I may, I found the portion to be too much and most of noodle dishes are not shareable in design, unfortunately. 

Desserts: 
Green Tea Crepe cake from lady M ($8) - you know it is good and it was. It also came with a scoop of ice cream or whipped cream.

I think it was called "Water Ball" ($8). It has a shape of ball and it is clear like water in a bowl. It is " Mizu Yokan". It's a Japanese jelly that's made of agar and it is sweet. Dark sauce that came on a tiny cup was molasses consistency and flavor sauce. This dark sauce is made of sugar cane. Pouring over the ball was fun to watch. The dark color covering the surface of the ball like something you see in sci-fi movie. Finishing with the sweet soy powder on top of it gave a nice texture and extra sweetness. But over all outcome was light, very Japanese.

If I come back, I will get simple Sukiyaki Udon. That truly satisfied my Japanese craving.

PS
I've been to the original one in Roppongi Tokyo. My friend, Mari, has helped the image of the restaurant as a visual aspect of the original restaurant, choosing the bowls and utensils as well -- but I find those bowls to be unessesary too big. I had my very first raw horse meat sushi at that restaurant -- it was not my choice. It was unmemorable and that would be my first and last.
This place is opposite my school and I crave to go there everyday! Their combination of udon noodles with chicken parmesan is so good! I love the place.

Good food. However, be careful. Last time I was here, they added an additional $12 to the tip. So hold on to your receipts, because there are some waiters at this restaurant that steal from the customers.

One of my favorite discoveries as of late. I recommend the tuna cones, the salmon ikura sushi, the snow crab sushi, and the creme roe udon with thin noodles (because they pick up more of the sauce! 

I've also had the curry udon before which was really good. The spicy tan tan noodle was good but less special because it feels more common. 

Also, big props for their policy of holding tables for 15 mins!

Pretty tasty, but pricey. Apparently TsuruTonTan hails from Japan and this location is their first international location. The amount of variety on the menu here is pretty ridiculous. There is so much to choose from. 

I had US Wagyu Shabu udon and my friend had the tan tan udon. They give you a large portion of noodle upgrade for free. I'm not that impressed with that gesture as the minimum you are going to pay here for a bowl of udon is about $18. I also ordered the salmon and ikura roll for $10. 

Both udons here were pretty good. I liked my US Wagyu Shabu udon more. The broth was light but had depth. It wasn't too salty. The meat was plentiful and extremely tender. I only tasted my friend's broth and it was average, but not spectacular. It kind of tasted a bit like Frank's red hot sauce for hot wings, which I'm not sure is a positive when it comes to authentic udon. Don't get me wrong, I like hot wings, so it still tasted pretty decent...just probably not authentic. The noodle portion for both were plentiful and had good texture.

My salmon and ikura roll was good, but nothing super special. It was pretty standard tasting. Service was pretty decent and we got a bar seat right away here. I imagine this place gets pretty packed though. However, it was raining the day we went and before the dinner rush, so probably why we didn't have any trouble getting seated here. 

Overall, I think this is a good place to take visitors for authentic udon. It's pretty unique because they offer so much variety that other udon shops don't offer. The price is the major negative and is mostly why I had to dock at least a star.

Pricey but yummy. I ordered the tan tan udon and enjoyed the broth more than the noodles themselves. Found that the noodles were a bit lackluster in their texture, and they could be more bouncy and fresh. The smashed cucumber appetizer was so good though. The seasoning on it was amazing. However, the portion size is small and for the price, not that great of a value, 

What stands out about this place is of course the massive bowls. Def fun to eat out of and take pictures with~ 

Food: 4/5
Ambiance: 5/5
Service: 5/5
Value 3.5/5
I've been here five times now and every time has been exceptional. The food is delicious - creamy uni, cold uni, and kaisen don are my favorites. Also the service it fantastic!! I love this place!

A little bit pricey for Udon noodle. But good quality and good portion. 
Authentic but unique Udon place. 
Will come back. But of course Tokyo is better.

I am a big fan of this place! Everything is amazing. Udon are good price and delicious, pretty big portion! You won't get such a good quality udon like here anywhere in NY. 
The service is great too. There are always friendly. Amazing hospitality. I love this place!!
Udon here was cooked perfectly but broth was just OK. On the expensive side but definitely some of the best udon I've had in NYC. The raindrop cake was delicious too!

We've been here for lunch. I ordered veggie tempra with noodles plus $3 sukiyaki beef rice. It was so great. My friend ordered yamakake cold udon with $3 spicy mentaico rice. These are both lunch special. I highly recommend you should plus $3 and order sukiyaki beef rice or garlic fried chicken with rice or spicy mentaico rice. These $3 options are really good and big potion. Whatever if you couldn't finish you can take home. For lunch time we took a reservation but actually I didn't need it. The place is big!
Just moved here from Tokyo and can honestly say that this place is as good as it gets. Delicious food, huge portions and excellent service.

Loved this place! The food was delicious and the service was great! Our server was attentive, coming to check on us multiple times, explaining the menu and answering any questions we had. 
My favorite thing the whole night was the Spicy Tuna Tartare Cones! And I believe it usually comes 4 an order but we were a table of 5 and our server allowed us to order 5 instead of having to buy 2 orders of 4, since the restaurant/kitchen wasn't busy, although on busy nights, we were warned that they usually don't do it.
The Uni Creme Udon was delicious and the soup wasn't as thick/heavy as I expected it to be and it had a deep seafood flavor. The Sukiyaki Udon was too sweet for my taste, I could only have one sip of the soup before it was too much. The US Wagyu Shabu tasted a little like pho soup base, it was good although I probably wouldn't order it either in the future as it was kind of plain. The Tsurutontan Deluxe was my favorite soup base out of the ones I tried. It wasn't a regular udon/soy sauce tasting soup, it was deep and made you want to keep sipping and slurping. The udon noodles were thick and bouncy and made you want to slurp, delicious!!
I would definitely come back :) 

P.S. the bowls are enormous, our server brought the first bowl of udon and I thought it was literally holding everyone's bowls inside of it or something!!! Also, they give you huge metal spoons and honestly my fingers got too tired to hold it as a regular spoon so I ended up holding it with my whole hand like a shovel.

Food, cocktails, atmosphere, service---all amazing!!

The bartender is a little bit on the cool side (a man of few words), but his Matcha cocktail was super tasty. The Tokyo Mule, albeit light-tasting at the first few sips, posed quite a punch afterwards in potency!!

Our udon selections were both amazing, albeit I much preferred the thin version of the udon to the standard thick version. Man I can eat that thin noodle for days ~~~~
Also the larger size that we ordered generated much more thin noodle than the thick version. I had to take my thin noodles to go, but def no complaints there.

My new neighborhood fave, I can't wait to return for another yummy meal.

Food was pretty good, giant bowls that are shareable. Noodles cooked perfectly, chewy yet soft. Wagyu with uni was yummy but nothing spectacular- but does look good on photo. Service was good and attentive during the meal. One annoyance was that they didn't allow outside drinks. They did offer to keep drinks in the fridge and later the manager offered our table of 7 people three complimentary dessert dishes. AND it was my first time trying Lady M Green Tea cake...omg, amazing!! That really earned this place the 4 stars. All in all a pretty trendy place.

You walk in and just keep walking. Don't let the outside deceive you, this joint is much larger than you may think. The communal tables work nicely and you don't feel as if you're intruding on someone else's life or their date....

Staff: "Would you like single or double udon noodles in your bowl? There's no additional charge for double noodles"

Me "what's the catch? Do you have take out boxes?"

Staff: "yes we have take out boxes if you don't order something raw"

Me "OK great, who wouldn't order double noodles? #FreeFood"

Staff "they all say that the first time...."

After you have this conversation with the staff you'll start seeing enormous bowls come out of the kitchen and wonder to yourself, man, is my bowl going to be that big?? Indeed your bowl will also be that large so long as you get a soup. 

Did you really need that large of a bowl? No probably not.
Did you intend to finish it? Definitely not
Was it worth it? Mildly. The udons are definitely something to order again and again, but unfortunately their broths lack depth and you'd be better off finding a ramen joint that serves udon noodles. Is that a thing? If not, someone should open that restaurant....
I liked my truffle creme with crab and mushroom. also had some of my friend's tan tan and liked it too.

Came around 6:30 PM on a Tuesday afternoon and the restaurant was half filled. My friend and I didn't make reservations but they were able to seat us immediately. There's a huge bar area upon entering and plenty of seating in the other rooms. We were seated in the corner away from the crowed, quiet and perfect for catching up. 

Their food and drink menu was so extensive, we had an extremely difficult time trying to decide. They have more traditional udons, curry udons, creme udons, and cold soba noodles. The waiter started off by explaining that all udons had a small and regular size for the same price. Only difference was the regular size has more broth and noodles. This is great for those who want smaller portions, so they have more stomach room to try more dishes. 

To start, we ordered the popular spicy tuna tartare cones ($12). The crunchy cone has avocado puree  between the layers of spicy tuna, topped with purple shiso, all on a bed of raw rice. The avocado complimented the spicy tuna very well. Overall a solid appetizer - fair for the price. 

For my entree, I ordered the uni creme udon ($24). This was my first time trying uni so I was really excited. I've heard so many great things for it so I had high expectations. But Tsurutontan did not disappoint. There was a huge chunk of uni on top of the udon. The broth was so flavorful and rich. It was the perfect texture, not too thick or too watery. The uni was so fresh and sweet, everything I imagined it to be. Everything was so delicious, I devoured the noodles and almost finished the broth. 

My fried ordered the Truffle Creme with Crab and Mushroom ($22). I've only had truffle fries so this was my first experience trying truffles with someone else. The broth was also creamy, but the so rich with truffle flavor. I loved my little sample, but it would've been too overwhelming for me if I had the entire bowl. 

Overall a great first experience here. The prices are higher than most, but for the city and the quality of the food, its definitely justifiable. The service was great, we stayed a bit longer than expected but we never felt rushed. Our glasses were always full, and they consistently checked in to ensure we were satisfied.

A friend from home recommended this place and it did not disappoint! Delicious and well portioned udon noodles. They have traditional, thick udon noodles and thin, yet still chewy udon noodles. With my friend we shared the hamachi appetizer but there are other ones I would want to try. For main, I got the sukiyaki udon with thin noodles and it was huge portion, scrumptious and so so good. The broth was sweet as sukiyaki should be, good amount of napa cabbage and Japanese mushrooms. I would definitely come back in the winter or on a cold day. 

Great service, clean, modern decorations, and great location near union station.

the ramen bowls are larger than my head!  wide variety on the menu.  great tastes!  the staff although young were kind and friendly to my family and i as newbies and tourists.  location is ideal for nyu students and pricing was fair for manhattan.  would def come back!
Came for the first time with high expectations. The food (seared salmon appetizer and the truffle mushroom udon) were both delicious. Would definitely come back and try something else on the menu!

Service 3/5 
Even with a reservation I've had to wait to be seated for at least ten minutes 2 of the 3 times I've visited this restaurant. Neither time has the hostess been the one updating our party, it was more of us checking in with her and feeling bad for asking when we had a reservation to start? 

The waiters are really great, though, so it's a shame the first impression of service doesn't align. Everyone seems to know the menu well, always asking if it's the table's first time at the restaurant, and explaining that the larger size comes at no extra charge, just more noodles. The food also comes out super quickly.

Food: 4/5
The duck udon here is my favorite. I've had beef udon too which was equally as flavorful. Loved the broth, I've ordered both the regular and large size and really the only difference is the noodles, so if you're hungrier order the large as the bowl's big but the portions aren't HUGE so don't be scared. 

I've also tried the Udon Pon as an appetizer, which was just okay. Sort of like a doughier breadier dumpling with less filling. Still good to try.

The fried chicken app (Soy Garlic Fried Tatsuta Chicken) is delicious! A great starter, super tasty and perfectly crisp, not too oily.

Ambiance: 5/5
The inside is super spacious and has multiple levels, like the mezz by the bar, a "downstairs" (just a couple of stairs that lead to another main seating area), and an upstairs too, I believe. The lighting and interiors of this place are definitely unique!

We had the roast duck with thin noodles and the spicy sesame oil udon with ground pork. The regular size on both were more than enough - happy we didn't order the large. The broth on the duck udon was basic but good, not too salty. The spicy sesame one was good and creamy but not overpowering. There was more than enough noodles for two people. Thinking we might share a bowl next time we go there. The place is posh, too - so that doesn't hurt. Made our reservation through Resy. Just wish my noodles were cheaper than the $ 20 average price at this place

6 of us went there with reservation for 7:30PM and we weren't seated until 8:30. The host lied that they had issue with their computers.  They comped us with the appetizers. But it ruined all my friends mood already the comp didn't really help.  

Udon: it feels like it's batch factory made that you can buy from supermarkets. It's soft and not tasty like the handmade ones. I would suggest Raku if you want tasty ramen.

Uni udon: the uni smells very fishy. It's definitely not fresh.

Everything great food in this store. it is same as really the store which in Japan I was like so excited 
I like Mentai ankake tamagotoji Udon.
Any dessert are all excellent!

I love a good udon noodle soup. Tsurutontan lived up to my expectations. 

I had the US Wayagu and Mushroom Sukiyaki Udon noodle soup. I got it with extra thick noodles and extra noodles. The soup broth was sweet and flavorful. The udon tasted fresh. The texture was bouncy and it soaks the broth really well. A well made bowl of udon. 

We also got the tuna tartare and the soy garlic fried chicken. The tuna tartare had a good crisp on the outside and soft delicious tuna on the inside. The soy garlic fried chicken was also yummy. Crispy chicken on the outside. Juicy and tender on the inside. 

For dessert we got the Water cake and Banana mille-feuille. The water cake was very unique You definitely need the sauce and crumbs topping to make it a flavorful cake. The banana mille-feuille was oh so heaven. Moist, creamy, and super delicious. 

Service was very friendly and our waiter explained the menu really well. 

Prices are bit overly expensive for udon, but I think it's worth it for well made udon.

Meh.  I thought this place was just ok.

Pretty extensive menu ranging from traditional to more unique options.  All their udons come in massive bowls.  I had the creamy uni, which was good but very rich - which I knew it would be, so that wasn't a surprise, but I would have liked a little more flavor/depth.  There was a tiny bit of shiso on top, which I liked, but other than that, it fell pretty flat, and I got sick of it pretty quickly.  The uni also didn't taste very fresh.  I ordered thin noodles and they gave me thick - I think this particular dish would have been better with thin, but I was eating with others so I didn't bother to ask them to swap it out and wait for a new dish.

Glad I tried it but I don't have a strong desire to come back anytime soon.

Came here with a friend - ordered the spicy tuna tartare cones, seated salmon sashimi appetizer, shrimp tempura udon, and matcha cake dessert. Everything was good, although what truly stood out and guarantees a future visit (with more people) were the cones - delightfully crisp and stuffed with fresh, flavorful tuna. Oddly enough, the salmon appetizer was rather disappointing - the sauce was good but didn't make the salmon itself taste better (in fact it covered up the taste that good salmon would have by itself) - and salmon is my favorite raw fish. ( ･･ ) It is a rare day when I prefer a tuna fish to a salmon one, especially to such an extent.

Really fantastic place. While I am sad that USQ Cafe closed its original location and made way for this spot, Tsurutontan does the location justice and offers a great menu with something for everyone! I've tried all the basic types of udon here (tip: always get the large size) and some of the appetizers and I haven't had anything that I thought was even a little bit flawed.

I really love the tuna cones as an appetizer in particular.

I'd definitely stick to the thicker noodles for most broths, but thinner ones for the cold udon. The thinner noodles tend to disintegrate in hot broth pretty quickly.
Love the food.  Good service and nice atmosphere.   Conveniently located in Union Square.

Biggest bowl for Udon I've ever had! The portion was huge and the uni cream Udon I tried was pretty good (after a while it started getting too creamy). The appetizer uni with wagyu beef sushi was good too (but the price was a bit high for only two pieces). Service was great. Ordered the water cake for dessert - interesting flavor. 

The reason for 4 stars was that my stomach felt a little weird after the meal... not sure if it was the uni or something else...

Really delicious udon! My friends are obsessed with the cold uni udon (and thin noodles) while I am more of a traditionalist and go with the dashi. The menu is a little confusing, but the wait staff is nice and will go over it with you. Portions are generous, and I was surprised by how much tempura they give you!!

The restaurant is ginormous, so it shouldn't be that bad of a wait to come dine. But you should really take advantage of the fact that they take reservations!

This didn't affect my rating but the music is really bad and almost gave me a panic attack lol

Came here with a friend for a quick dinner. We were seated immediately but at a horrible table location upstairs near the dishes so busboys kept flying past us in such a narrow way! We complained and were seated at another table right away thankfully. The hosts were very accommodating. 

We ordered the spicy tuna tartare cones which were delicious. There were only 4 and we only wished there were more!! 
Their portions for the udon along with the actual bowl are HUGE. Almost unnecessarily so but I guess you get the amount you pay for since it's $20! I got the tan tan udon (spicy broth) and I wouldn't recommend it. It got a little too much at the end so I couldn't finish it. I like more variety so I would want wagyu mushroom sugiyaki. 

Would come again and try other things off the menu!

After 3 or 4 visits and after having tried many different dishes I can say nothing beats the sizzling seafood and the sizzling sukiyaki udon here. There is much taste, it is hard to explain. Also, since there is no broth, the noodles gain a very unique texture - a little crusty but chewy on the inside.

The ones with broth are great as well. The broth smells incredible - but the sizzling ones are the real deal. 

While not cheap, it is nearly impossible to leave this place hungry. You can ask for a large portion of noodles for no extra charge. Great value for the quality and taste is simply delicious. On top of that, service is on point: courteous and attentive.

Super value lunch in the heart of Union Sq AND it was yummy. The basic veggies tempura was superb with a mix of enoki mushrooms, perfectly crisped, pumpkin, just right, shiso leaves, eggplant, and an amazing tempura soft egg. $16 is a steal. 

My first time here and did not realize the super size upgrade was free so I ordered the $3 rice bowl to supplement. The "big" udon bowl was practically shoulders width, while the "mini" rice bowl was equivalent to the size of my head. After the udon and tempura, I got through maybe 3 bites of the beef rice bowl before tearfully throwing in the towel and calling for the check, all while running through some crazy scenarios in my head of stuffing the whole bowl into my purse when no one is looking. To my surprise, the waitress offered to box it up for me even without me asking! It made a very exciting dinner.
Very good udon in an impressive space. Portions are big and food comes out very quickly. Highly recommend the Sizzling Sukiyaki Udon. Make reservations if possible, the wait can be long.

Been wanting to come here for so long! Finally got the chance today. I came with a group of 12 for a birthday at 12pm on a Sunday. They do take reservations if you're a big group. They gave us the whole upstairs which was nice as it felt like we had our own private room. Our server was super nice and funny, everyone loves him! He gave us a little lecture on the menu and how to order which was very helpful. For appetizers, I highly recommend the spicy tuna cones. So delicate and cute, almost too pretty to eat. I must say, it was my favorite dish there. The crunchy cone and guacamole that hides beneath the spicy tuna adds a nice touch. 

For entree I tried one of their best sellers on the menu, cold uni pasta dish. You have the option to get small or large for same price. The difference is the amount of noodles you get. You also have the option to choose thin or thick noodles. Also you can add $3 for a side bowl of rice with fried chicken, beef, or cod fish eggs. Pretty good deal if the bowl of noodles is not enough. The dishes are served in HUGE bowls with an oversized spoon. Very nice presentation of the food. 

I'm a huge fan of Uni, and I was pretty happy with my dish. I like that it was cold for a hot summer day, and it didn't feel heavy at all even though it's full of carbs! The thin noodles was very well cooked, and every bite just makes you want to take another bite. My boyfriend got the Tsurutontan deluxe, it was okay. Not anything special, and I had much better Udon. The broth is a bit on the sweeter side. 

I'm happy I finally got the chance to try this place, as I tried making reservations a few times and it never works out. They're always super booked. Although I must say my all time favorite Uni pasta place is still Sakamai. (You must try if you like Uni and pasta!) I'll definitely be back for those spicy tuna cones!

It's always pretty packed here and the wait takes ~an hour or so at night. Maybe I just have bad timing, but it seems to be so throughout the few times I actually tried getting in here. The decor of this restaurant is beautiful, a nice modernized asian feel. 

The dishes do get a little pricey. Most of the popular udons fall in a price range about $20. The udon was delicious though. I actually really wanted to try the uni udon that a lot of people have raved about, but unfortunately they were out of it for the night. I opted for the SIZZLING SUKIYAKI UDON, which was good but I don't really think it's worth the $20 I paid for it. It was flavorful, but a little on the sweeter side. It took me a while to adjust to the sweetness of this dish. The meal itself was satisfying, but I'm not really sure if it's worth. You can actually upgrade to a bigger size for free, but the normal size is actually huge to begin with.

omg so delicious. the best udon noodles i have ever had. i had the mentaiko caviar cold udon (thin udon) and it was so good! everyone else loved their picks. but the cold noodles are a must. definitely upgrade to a large for free.

Huge bowls of udon noodles that are chewy and delicious! Same price for a small or large bowl so go big and share some different ramens. We got one tsurutontan deluxe which has tempura and fashion broth, tan tan spicy udon and mushroom and crab cream. All delicious and different. The crab cream was all truffle and mushroom flavored. You don't even notice the crab at all. The tan tan has a thick soup and the right amount of heat- not too much. The dash broth is delicious but the tempura does come out soggy. 

Apps were delicious!! Seared salmon is a must get as were their caviar and uni! 

Go there now! Didn't have a reservation but only waited about 20 minutes Saturday early evening.

Went there for the first time because of their lovely decor and because I love udon. The waiter recommended sukiyaki udon and here's my five words review: 
too salty, too sweet, overpriced. 
I could barely finish it.

This review is strictly about reservation and management. Not food nor service (both are quite good). 

1. Since you have a reservation system, please ensure that people get seated on time. 

2. If you can't seat people on time for some reasons (which seems to be every single time I visit this place), at least have a queue system that let people who come in first (and been waiting for longer) to seat first. It's very annoying otherwise. 

3. If you can't estimate how fast tables will be cleared, don't allow for reservation.

Checked in on 6/30/17 for Lunch.

Overall experience was mixed.  Service was excellent, suggestive, and attentive.  Great decor.

Spicy Tuna Tartare Cone - Excellent!  Great presentation!

Soy Garlic Fried Tatsuta Chicken - Perfect crunch but but the sauce was on the sour side and that killed it for me.

Oyako Don - Not great.  Bland and rice to topping ratio was unbalanced.

Spicy Tan Tan Udon - Terrible!  Broth was way too thick and way too sour to be enjoyable.  Did not enjoy this dish at all.  It actually made our stomach hurt hours after. 

Would not go back again.

Overall, I'm a fan of this place. I've been three times; the first two times I enjoyed my food. But the third time I ordered the chicken udon and it was actively unappetizing. So some things on the menu are delicious, and others really aren't worth the $$$.

The service is also very hit or miss. The first time I went we had a very jovial waiter who interacted well with everyone. But the past couple of times, I've had an icy waiter who made me feel uncomfortable.

In sum, some of the food is tastey. But some is mediocre and the service is often strange.

Amazing udon noodles. The bowls they come in are bigger than your head and they have unlimited refills of noodles. Thing is you just can't take any leftovers home. But you will definitely leave full and satisfied. They have a large variety of different types of udon noodle bowls. Their donburi is also very good and comes with a side of udon noodles, though they are the basic udon noodles with the basic miso broth and no toppings. For appetizers, I suggest the tuna tartar. But definitely come here and try their udon noodles as you will not be disappointed.
Really great udon and a super cool restaurant inside - way bigger inside than it looks from the outside.

Wow what can I say?! Ordered the spicy Tan Tan noodles and asked for the large noodles. The flavor was out of control ! So tasty, appropriately rich, delicately spicy. Noodles were just incredible. Thickkkkk and al dente. Got the lunch set of soy garlic chicken rice. What a great deal! Rice was topped with fried chicken chunks that were to die for. Service was incredibly prompt and friendly. Eager to come back !

I've just found my favorite Japanese restaurant in NYC. The food was perfectly seasoned, creative and so well prepared. The servers were attentive and helpful, and never tried to up-sell us. We had went to Sushi Yasuda the day before, and as good as that was, this place was better! Shocking, I know! Definitely coming back for more.

My first experience with Tsurutontan was during their opening week, and quite frankly it was really disappointing but I didn't want to be quick to assume that they suck, and leave a negative Yelp review! Anyhow, I went back two weekends ago with a large party to celebrate a friend's birthday and decided to give it another shot. 

This time I ordered their cold udon- Tempura Zara Udon as my entree, crispy chicken and spicy tuna tartare cone as our appetizers. The assorted tempura was made really well. The batter was light, fluffy and the dipping sauce added a subtle sweetness and savoriness to the crunch without being too overpowering. The udon was placed under a cold bath and the presentation of my meal was made perfectly. They make their udon in-house daily so it's not your typical udon noodles. It was in fact really good. Crispy chicken and the spicy tartare cone was still delicious. I'm glad both times remained consistent. 

My only critique is the udon made with hot soup. My first time at Tsurutontan, I got the Tsurutontan Deluxe and I think because the noodle soup bowl were kept with a lid, the noodles got really soggy by the time it was served. I was extremely disappointed. I couldn't even finish it and only ate about 1/3 of my meal. In my opinion, not only is the soup base important but also the texture of the noodles. It's what makes the experience enjoyable. I remember a woman waitress asking for our feedback after our meal. I mentioned to her what I said about the soggy noodles, and she either didn't really mind that it was or that it probably wasn't a big of a deal to pay close attention to it to address it. During my friend's birthday weekend, I tried the curry udon noodle soup and the broth was really rich. I think if you're a curry lover you would like this. I also tasted the Deluxe again and this time the noodles were not entirely soggy like when I had it during their first opening week.

Overall I give Tsurutontan 4 stars - customer service deserves a 5, cleanliness of the restaurant is also a 5, food - I would say a 4. Please try to be more consistent with the udon noodle soup.

One of the best udon ever!!! They came with huuuuuge bowls, like, bigger than your head. We tried spicy tan tan, crime and sukiyaki. All was great. The noodles, oh I love the noodles. Five girls sharing three large bowls and i was so full I could barely walk. Would also recommend the fried udon(?) dumplings. The tofu appetizer tasted a bit weird to me though, texture too thick. Good service as well.

I assumed this place would just have a dozen udon options, but the menu is very extensive and they also serve other non-udon dishes like sushi/sashimi and various apps. I think I spent 15 minutes oscillating between getting the duck or creamy uni udon - but everyone raves about the uni, so I ended up succumbing to self-imposed peer pressure. 

Creamy uni udon comes (not pictured). Love the presentation in the huge bowls, and satisfyingly large soup spoons for optimal noodles-to-mouth experience. In another world, if I liked heavy & creamy broths, this would've been amazing. However, this was way too heavy for me...I could not stop eyeing my bf's cold udon with uni, scallops, and roe (pictured). He caught on, and generously gave me a couple bites of light yet flavorful goodness. The hot udon was thicker noodles, the cold was recommended the thinner kind. Both were al dente and had great consistency. 

Salmon sashimi was interesting because some parts were seared and others were not, so it ended up being this lukewarm dish. The sprinkled fried garlic pieces were a nice touch, though.

I have no doubt the other udons are amazing. Just a personal preference on the creaminess - will have to come back and go with my gut udon :-)

This place was pretty good, but not an exceptional noodles restaurant. There are a lot of smaller, more authentic udon noodles that are handmade, which make them have a chewier consistency. These noodles tasted as if they could have come out of a package. It's great that extra noodles are offered at no extra cost! 

I ordered the tan tan udon noodles, thick. Would not recommend the thin ones. The broth was good but a couple slurps in, became overwhelming. 

However, the decor and service are impeccable.

Love, love, love the big bowls of Udon. The most expensive I've ever paid for a bowl but worth it. I got the Deluxe and it had everything.! Chicken, beef, shrimp tempura, and even egg drop. Truly satisfying for someone who could never decide between beef, chicken etc. Very nice ambience, friendly staff, great food

Really enjoyed our dinner experience over the weekend. It seems like they do get very busy on the weekends, so I would recommend making reservations. Their portion sizes are pretty decent, and the quality of food is good. I was also very impressed by their excellent service. 

I ordered the vegetable udon. I think they only have 2 options for vegans - one cold udon or a hot bowl. The hot udon had the perfect broth (not too salty or bland. I also tried the shishito peppers (ask for this w/o the bonito flakes) and these were also very good. Peppers were not spicy at all. 

Great ambiance for a casual date night or dinner with bigger groups. I liked how they served Japanese beer & drinks.

Amazing! Shrimp dumplings on point-must order. Beer is perfectly cold, I mean perfectly. Spend more time on picking your udon, cuz they are good, but you need to know what you like. Great service and atmosphere. 5 stars.

One of two places recommended to me by a friend to try in New York -- I LOVE udon and think we have the best back home in LA.  So naturally, I had to come try the udon here.

Tsurutontan was easy to find, and I had managed to snag a table for two using Resy on a Saturday night.  The ambiance was fun and trendy.  We arrived a little early, but were seated at a long table separated with a divider in the middle. I ordered the kobe udon and an order of yellowtail nigiri (because we were curious about how sushi tastes in NY).  The udon was chewy and yummy, and the soup base was flavorful but not overly salty.  The yellowtail was pretty good, and we enjoyed our experience overall.  Our waiter was attentive, but not overly so. 

All in all, looking forward to coming back here when back in NY!
Love their fresh udon noodles.  I would definitely come here again on my next visit to NY.

Came here after searching for udon specialists in downtown Manhattan, and was glad that I did. Service was attentive and friendly. I ordered the tempura zaru udon with the soy garlic chicken rice lunch set. You get to choose between skinny or thick udon noodles. The one shown in the photo here is skinny udon. The noodle has a good chewy texture. The soy garlic chicken rice is delicious and is quite a big portion, and for an extra $3 it is good value for the money.

The first time I came to this place the "masculine" female who was taking down names at the front was incredibility rude with an attitude of "why are more people walking in?" I understand it is crowded but there is no need to make potential customers feel unwelcome. - we left as we didn't want to wait 2hrs.

Many months later we returned for lunch and were greeted by much friendlier staff and quickly seated ( I guess lunch time is the best time)
Our waitress was so friendly and took her time explaining everything.

I ordered the Spicy Tan Tan Udon ($22) as my main dish with regular noodles. The soup ended up being only giant noodles and a sprinkle of meat, no veggies no nothing, but broth. The broth was straight up sour! with a hint of peanut butter flavor. I requested some clear broth thinking it would help but it did not do a thing to improve the flavor. The waitress said the soup was like a 2 on the spicy scale, but holy cow it was burning my stomach after I left. 
The noodles also fill you up almost instantly. 

The appetizers were all very good though, especially the tuna cone which was more avocado then tuna but still very tasty!  

Its very expensive for what you get, I know the bowl is big but that doesn't justify the price if all your getting is udon noodles.

Would not be returning.

This is my go to spot to bring visitors to eat. It's hard to find Asian restaurants that are mid tier in pricing but still feel like you're getting your money's worth! Service was excellent (A+) and the place is pretty good for larger groups. You feel like you're at a 5 star restaurant with the level of service provided (this includes changing out small plates between appetizers and explaining the menu). When an error was made; the manager himself came to apologize (although we weren't mad or upset). Although it's known for its noodles - it's also great for sushi. Small plates and appetizers allow for a large variety of dishes to be ordered without you feeling like you only have the option of noodles. I highly recommend.

One of my favorite meals in NYC so far. I'd recommend ordering a variety of large udon bowls to share with the table.

We've only got the hot udons so far which were the Uni Creme Udon and Spicy Tan Tan Noodles. Both were so good and plenty to share with 3 people if you get the large bowls. For appetizers, I thought the fried chicken was ok but I liked their sukiyaki buns a lot.

They even sell Lady M's Mille Crêpes here! Made me so happy since I was dying to try their green tea flavor.
Wow. This place has it all tasty food and great service. I can't believe what I just ate it was something to behold. The shushito peppers and curry bowls are on the top of the list.

After bookmarking this restaurant for awhile now, I finally got the chance to check this restaurant out. 

I decided to make a reservation ahead of time around 5:00 pm on a Monday. Surprisingly, there was a lot of time slots to choose from. I made a reservation for 8:45pm. At around 8:15 pm, I recieved a text from the restaurant that I was due at Tsurutontan in 30 minutes. 

Location:
Conveniently located near the union square train stop, you can't miss it! 

Ambiance:
Once I walked into the restaurant, I was greeted right away and seated at my table. The restaurant is lightly dimmed and has a touch of Japanese culture in the decor and layout. The spacing between the tables is very comfortable for all parties. My server gave us a breakdown of the menu and what were the most popular dishes: creme uni and spicy tan tan. What's interesting about the menu is that they have things organized based on what's the top sellers and what's popular which makes ordering a little less overwhelming for first-timers! 

Food ordered:
**You can ask for large udon portion for no extra charge**

-Tuna tartare cones (4/5)
Interesting concept and full of flavor. However, if I came here again, I'd try the duck appetizer next.

-Creme Uni (4/5)
Very heavy creme but don't let that steer you away from trying this. They even give you a generous piece of uni that's placed on top of the udon. Greedy me always wants more uni.

-Spicy Tan Tan (5/5)
Every spoonful of the udon I had, I couldn't get over how amazing the broth was. It was so rich!! Don't let the word spicy scare you. It's a very light spicy in my opinion. 

The reason I gave this restaurant 4 stars was because of the service after we ordered the food. It was difficult at times to get the attention of the server whether it was to get more water, utensils, or to ask to look at the menu again.

With a reservation at 8:45 PM, thankfully we managed to dodge the 50 MINUTE WAIT that walk-ins were enduring. We were seated immediately and I noted that there were several empty tables in the back seating area. We were finally seated at a 4 person table although there were plenty of 2 seaters available. Seems a bit odd to make potential clients wait for close to an hr when adequate seating was available. 

Anyway onto the actual food itself, though the menu may try to distract you with vivid pictures of their many appetizers/small bites/ sushi, do not be lured in, my fellow astute Yelpers. The real treasure lies in the middle of the menu. 

The server will tell you the Tan Tan Udon and Uni cream are the most popular. Get the Large if you want more carbs, no real difference otherwise. 
Overall I felt that the Tan Tan was nothing special, lacked a depth of flavor (could only taste chili oil). There's a subtle difference between a dish having a spice kick and just being spicy for spiciness's sake. I don't think that difference was noted here.

Uni udon was good but nothing to write home about. While the soup broth did well with keeping the creamy flavor while not being super heavy on the stomach, it came off a bit bland.

3/5, willing to give this another try and revise the review.

If you are a fan of udon, this is the place to be. This is one of my favorite places to get noodles in the city and catch up with friends. I've probably been here at least 10 times in the past 5 months. The restaurant is spacious with plenty of seating - great for large groups. You can also make reservations in advanced. 

The menu is extensive, accompanied with photos of every dish. They have a wide range of udon choices, as well as Japanese appetizers and dishes. All the appetizers I've tried had been amazing. I definitely recommend the spicy tuna tartare cone ($12) - crispy cone with soft tasty tuna filling. For noodles, I always get the Spicy Soondubu Jigae ($20) because I love the spicy broth! I also enjoyed the Uni Crème Udon ($24) and Tan Tan Udon ($20). The Sukiyaki Udon broth is actually a bit too sweet for me, so my friend recommended getting the dry stone pot stir fried udon if you want beef (Sizziling Sukiyaki Udon $18). 

What blew my mind when I came here for the first time was how huge the bowls were. The bowl of udon is bigger than my head!
