There is also no extra charge if you order the large portion of the noodles. My kind of restaurant! Portions are huge. Every meal has been delicious and I will continue to come here regularly whenever I am in the mood for soup or noodles!
We enjoyed every dish that we ordered. Everything was flavorful and yummy! The service was on point. Our water glass was always full

Location: I would say it's in union square bound. This place, though seems to be small, has two connected dining areas. We were quickly greeted and sensed to a bar setting room to eat food. If you want a nice table, I guess waiting is necessary 

Food: of course, udon! I had uni creme udon. It's seafood base but but greasy at all. Udon is chewy with a huge portion. The soup with udon kept me eating and all of a sudden: I am too full to eat any more food. 

Price: very legit. Extra noodle with the same price. N everything is nice here 

Service: treat us like gods!

Love it ! Will come back

Previous reviews have mentioned two sizes for the udon; that combined with the pictures is enormous bowls of udon led me to believe that I would getting a huge amount of food to match the high prices. I didn't find this to be the case. I ordered the larger portion and shared an appetizer with my dining partner. Even so, after eating all the food, I was satisfied; but not completely full. We had the deluxe and duck udon and started our meal with one of their sushi dishes.

If I were to go back, I'd stick with the small plates and steer clear of the udon. Both udon bowls were ok; but not worth the price that they charge.

Went here during lunch on a Sunday afternoon, and only waited for 5 minutes without a reservation. Right next to Union Square, this noodle place feels like it was straight out from a five-star hotel in Tokyo. The only hint of inauthenticity was the American indie music playing in the background, from the likes of Tame Impala and Washed Out (my boyfriend really liked that bit).

As soon as we sat down we knew we chose the right place to have udon. You can see the giddy smiles spread across everybody's faces as the BIG BOWLS rolled out to their table. Our reaction was a mixture of excited and - yikes, we can't finish that! Thankfully the servers gave us an option: regular or large portions, and thick and thin udon noodles. You know they know their shitz when they give you two options for udon noodles.

The boyfriend ordered the curry katsu udon and I had the nabeyaki udon with their famous dashi broth. Both were on the pricey side, but I was glad to splurge given the quantity and quality of it. I was particularly crying tears of happiness - it had been a long time since I had authentic Japanese food.

His curry broth was super creamy with a tinge of sweetness. My dashi broth was amazing! It was like a bowl of infinite surprises. Chicken, unagi eel, perfectly poached egg, mushrooms, fish cakes, shrimp tempura...in between hot, hot, elastic hand-made udon. I'm thankful for the background music or else people across the table would probably hear my loud slurping.

The only complaint I have was that I prefer my shrimp tempura and katsu to be put separately in a different dish so it won't get soggy in the broth. But that's just a personal pet peeve of mine. 

Will definitely come back here with my friends during my next trip to the city. Hands down best meal ever over the weekend.

The place is alright. The service is decent and the food comes out at a decent time after ordering. I got wagyu beef noodles and it was good but nothing jumped at me when I had it. Wasn't thrilled about it but it tasted good. The sushi roll and sashimi are quite fresh and tasty on how it is made. It is a bit pricy for udon noodles in my opinion. Great environment and ambiance

I'm not a big fan of udon, but I must say, this place is certainly worth the bucks. I went with a party of 7 and everyone seemed to enjoy their food the same way I did. I ordered a tsurutontan hot & sour udon with thin noodles and it was absolutely delightful. 

The place is usually really packed, so make sure you reserve seats or go early. 

Tip: There's no price difference between a single or a double bowl. Slurp on :)

Came here last night with my fiance, and one of my girl friend's and her boyfriend. We did not make any reservation ahead of time, but were seated immediately. The ambiance is really welcoming. It's a nice place for a casual get together or if you want to take someone out on a date. Their menu is pretty easy to follow and the pictures are accurate to the entree listed. 

I got the Sukiyaki Udon with Spicy broth. My fiance got the Sizzling sukiyaki udon. My girl friend got the Tan tan udon and her boyfriend got Nabeyaki udon. We did not have a long wait to receive our food...I think it was a maximum of 20-25 min but we were all preoccupied on catching up and having small conversations. Once the food arrived, we could not wait to dig in. All of our udons were served in huge bowls. The main cutlery is obviously chopsticks but you can always opt out for a fork (which my friend's boyfriend did). They also give you a huge silver spoon, which you can use to hold your udon or the broth to sip. We honestly did not have any complains about our food. My spicy broth sukiyaki udon was beyond delicious, it definitely satisfied my craving. It was spicy, but not overly spicy where I could not enjoy the flavor. The beef were perfectly done. My fiance loved his sizzling sukiyaki, they were not cheap with their shrimp and there was enough sizzle and flavor. My friend's tan tan udon was the perfect hint of spice, and she said the pork was cooked well for her liking. Her boyfriend's nabeyaki udon was really good..he even took it to go so he could enjoy it later on at home. The prices are pretty reasonable, because of the quality of the food. My fiance also got a non-alcoholic lychee mojito, which was also delicious. 

Overall, I loved this place. The atmosphere is nice, the music is alright but it's not too loud where you cant have any conversation. The entire was super nice, and kept coming back to make sure we were okay. We were so full that we could not try anything on their dessert menu...however, we will definitely be coming back to this spot to try more things from their menu.

Gigantic bowls of udon! I've never experienced such a bowl but Tsurutontan Udon Noodle Brasserie has made experience it. 

Came here on a whim after my friend decided we should go here after a workout. Oh the decisions we make on an empty stomach. We didn't end up waiting long for a table and was seated side by side which was unusual but didn't really matter. The appetizer we chose of the many delicious-looking options was the braised pork belly with radishes, shishito peppers, and hardboiled eggs. That dish was a stunning piece of work because the pork fat melt in your mouth and the meat was juicy, succulent, and a sweet and savory flavor all working together with the other elements in the dish. 

For my gigantic bowl, I ordered the kakiage (mixed tempura) udon. What I didn't realize with the size upgrade which is the same price as a normal size is that the kakiage is humongous fried tempura nest full of vegetables and shrimp. In the picture on the menu it looked small but no, no, no, it arrived and big. It was a bit difficult to eat but it was so good especially dipped in the light dashi broth and the noodles. I couldn't finish all the noodles but they were so fresh and the texture had the perfect amount of bite. They sure get you with those portions! 

It does get loud inside especially when it's full. There are mixed seating options and it's very luxe cozy inside with the warm lighting and the dark wood. With many other appetizers and udon bowls to try on the menu, a repeat visit is a must and this Osaka-based chain is high on the list of must visits for a great bowl of noodles in the city. 

Happy eating and remember: Don't deny, satisfy!

Terrific food, location, ambiance, everything here at Tsurutontan is praiseworthy. A few minutes' walk from Union Square, I stumbled upon this place with a friend after a workout class and returned with another friend's family. Both times were excellent - practically no wait time to be seated at prime hours, and the downstairs space is large and inviting with unique decor.  The menu is a bit clunky as it's filled with photos and somewhat disorganized, but the server I had my second time dining had very in depth recommendations that were tailored to everyone's needs. 

The tofu 'burrata' is divine and the silkiest I have tasted in a long time. I also would recommend the uni creme noodles. The noodle thickness and broths are all interchangeable, as well as the additions to the dish you choose. The bowls are extremely large and filling, and you're likely to have some tasty leftovers if you choose to order the apps as well. I can't wait to bring more friends over to this spot -- besides the name pronunciation, you really can't go wrong here!

Hands down. THE BEST UDON PLACE EVER!!!!! Could you hear me? You got it? Mapped it?

Words can't describe how delicious this place was. If I was in New York one more weekend, I definitely would be hitting that spot again. Seriously!

The udon were just the right texture. Not too chewy, not too soft. I got the thin udon and it was amazing. I slurpped up the entire bowl of udon. And it wasn't a small bowl of udon. The bowl was huge. Look at all the yelp photos. The broth was delicious. Yuuuuummmmy!  the tartar cones were out of this world good. The cucumber appetizer was also crispy juicy. Vegetables should always taste as good as these cucumbers. 

What are you guys waiting for? Still sitting here reading my review? Go.

Saw this place on INSIDER and contrary to my surprise, the hype was pretty plausible. 

I came here with a friend on a saturday noon, 30 minutes right after it opened for lunch. We were seated pretty quickly even without a reservation and it seemed that this place was more spacious than it appeared to be from the outside. The interior design and concept was rather pleasant to look at with no doubt. 

My friend and I both ordered cold udon options for this hot summer season. I would have liked to try and order appetizers and all but this friend has a rather very small appetite. Its interesting because every udons come in reg or large size depending on how hungry you are. And theres no additional charge! They give free large size meaning more noodles. So you can definitely have more control over your portion. They also ask your noodle preference of thick or thin with recommendations of thin noodles for cold udons and thick for hot.

I ordered the tan tan udon which seemed to utilize pork and some oil soup base. The soup had a blend of spicy, sweet and sour. Yet it wasnt too overwhelming. I wouldnt mind trying this one again.
As for my friend, her mentaiko udon literally tasted like... mentaiko. Im not sure how to describe this flavor unless you yourself has tried or will try it. It gives off that refreshing seafood taste with no bitterness or fishyness. But this mentaiko udon was consistent and did not leave any heavy feelings after. Overall their udon noodles were soft and chewy each flavor/dish unique in their own tastes for soups and toppings.

The servers were all nice and attentive. They offer dessert options afterwards but dont push for you to get anything.

Four stars for the food. 

The first thing is that you should have a reservation, but my wife and I were able to get seated within 40minutes on a Wednesday night in the summer. If you make a reservation the whole party should arrive. 

The kuta buta (spelling error?) $15 is great we got one whole seasoned egg split in half two pieces of daikon (radish) and 5 pieces of tender pork belly. Melt in your mouth savory and sweet and worth a try. The fat might put off some people but trust me and have the whole bite. 

After it took a long time for our main course to come out. The waiter had apologized for the wait. It was very busy but took more than 30 minutes to come after the app. We saw three groups of two come after us, order after us and finish their food before we got our food. 

The noodles were good. My wife had the beef mushroom sukiyaki thick udon $24 and I had the uni cream with thick udon $24. I preferred the beef mushroom one because you actually had more to munch on mushrooms and beef while the uni had two pieces of uni and some small roe so basically you were eating plain udon. Don't get me wrong the creme soup was great with a possible hint of truffle oil but it was just lacking something to eat with texture. You can order extra serving of udon for free and we tried the thin udon but we prefer the thick udon. The waiter said that thin noodles are good for cold dishes. 

Waiting for table at 7:35pm to getting the check at 9:20 pm. After tax and tip it was 37 per person. 

Food 5/5
Service 5/5
Wait time for food 1/5 
Food/enjoyment-cost ratio 1/5 (yes the udon was better than frozen udon and the texture was great but wasn't worth 24 per bowl. Even with the extra noodles 75 dollars for two bowls of noodles and 5 pieces of pork I'm sorry. The cost didn't reflect the food. ) 

Try it if you never had good udon, but I don't think I'll come back because of the enjoyment over cost ratio is very low for my wife and I. Unless someone wants to try it I probably won't even think about this place again.

Now this is a place that stays in your mind. I went there two weeks ago for unagi cold udon and I'm still thinking about my meal there. Delicious and filling - and normally I dislike cold noodles. It was chewy, the taste just fills your mouth, neither too rich nor too bland. I also tried the uni cream udon which was good, but a little on the heavy side. 

The atmosphere here is pretty nice, a little dark but good for a date or grabbing a bite with friends. The only downsides were that we had to wait about 15 min despite having reservation, and the cost is a little on the pricey side.

I love it. I made a reservation for Tuesday night, it wasn't packed. Our waiter Kyle was wonderful and knowledgeable about the menu. He was also very patient (and cute... Boyfriend made fun of my for that). We started off with his recommendations, sea and truffle sushi and a large uni udon. Then we ordered another spicy one (large of course). It was very yummy. Throughout the whole night, Kyle was very helpful. So at the end of dinner, another waiter came and gave us our check. I was being careful and made sure it was Kyle's name documented on the check. We definitely wanted to make sure that our tip goes straight to him, but sadly it wasn't is name on the check. We let him know it wasn't his name, shook his hand, handed his too in cash. 

Management, please make sure that the tipping issue doesn't happen again. I hate to see a good worker not being compensated.

THIS IS A MUST TRY WHEN IN NYC!!!!

The udon comes in such a big bowl! They even upgrade the size for you for FREE. WHAT. I love you guys already.

The noodles were so delicious and soft. Very excellent texture, I can tell they are fresh and the soup was very flavorful. 

Service was super bomb, my server was very nice and checked up on us/refilled our water and just made us so happy. 

We didn't wait at all but we sat at the long table connected to the bar. It was a shared table which I didn't mind because we didn't have to wait! 

I can't wait until I go to NY again because I will definitely be eating here again!!!!

Our reservation was for 7 but arrived a little early at 6:40 but the host greeted us in and sat us right away. It was a fast paced moving restaurant. For appetizer i ordered silken tofu and spicy tuna tartare cone both were excellent. I asked for some wasabi and place a small amount on the tofu and it really taste great. For udon i got the curry deluxe and my girlfriend got the truffle creme with crab and mushroom. Curry deluxe was amazing no too salty and now too bland. As for hers it wasnt as good as the curry but still had that taste we were looking for. We def recommend the curry though

Went there as a group of 4 with a reservation and we couldn't sit at our table on time. But once I got food I could understand why people didn't want to leave! The noodles were AMAZING. Definitely would recommend to anyone looking for an awesome udon place in Manhattan :D

Best udon in the city! Two sizes: regular and large; both are the same price. Sometimes, there's a longer wait but arrive for an early dinner (5:30/6:00) and there's usually hardly a line. You can also make reservations online, but they want your credit card and you can only cancel up to 24 hours in advance. All fair.

Got the sizzling beef sukiyaki which is a dry pot udon and on the sweeter side. Partner got the ultimate curry and it was very filling; curry was surprisingly good, especially as broth for udon. 

Had the crepe cake from Lady M and the lychee dessert; Lady M cakes always good!! 

I love coming here just for the noodles. It's hard to describe exactly, but they have a great...mouthfeel? Very good noodles and great broth/sauces that show off the noodles.
This place is worth every penny. The noodles are fresh and delicious, the service is excellent and the ambiance is very nice. 100% coming back when I'm looking for another noodle fix.

Tsurutontan is a pretty large restaurant with a decent amount of seating. Although, I thought that their seating was kind of awkward and I did not like at all. My friend and I were seated at the large table and had to sit next to each other rather than across.

For food, it has a ton of udon options -- soup, curry, etc. They give an option for a regular size or a large size for the same price so there is no downside to ordering the large size. However, you are not allowed to takeaway any leftovers. You could always bring your own Tupperware (and suffer a life of eternal tackiness). 
The Tsurutontan deluxe udon was very filling and contained shrimp, chicken, beef, and veggies. The broth was not too salty. It was a solid dish. 

The hostess who seated us, the one with short brown hair with blonde tips, was not very friendly or helpful. She ignored us when we told her that the entire party arrived. She did not offer to check our jackets until they were in the way of other diners since we were sitting on benches. It would have been great to know that coat check was an option from the beginning, rather than her making us feel bad for throwing our jackets on the benches. Then it took us a solid eight minutes to grab her attention in order to retrieve our jackets. The unhelpful and seemingly rude front staff seemed out of sync with the rest of the staff because, in contrast, our server was friendly and helpful.

If there is a long wait to be seated, I say you're better off going to a different restaurant nearby.

Made a reservation at 7PM and they do not let you seated when you're early. The interior of the restaurant was very clean and modern. It had an upstairs and a lower level. There seatings looked very unique. Our waitress was very kind and attentive. She took her time to explain the menu as well as giving recommendations when asked. The appetizers came in fast. We had four appetizers the Soy Garlic Tatsuta Chicken,Spicy Tuna Tartare Cone, Seared US Waygu Sushi, and a Salmon and Ikura Roll.

Soy Garlic Tatsuta Chicken was crispy on the outside and tender in the inside. They were a bigger version of popcorn chicken. It was mixed with a chili sauce. It was pretty good but not sure if I will order as an appetizer again.

Spicy Tuna Tartare was one of my favorites out of the four. It came in a cone shape. Inside was spicy Tuna and smashed avocado. It was very delicious and I can see why many people order this!

Seared US Waygu Sushi was another favorite. I didn't think I would have enjoyed it so much since it didn't look fully cooked BUT it was very worth trying! It literally melts in your mouth!

The Salmon and Ikura roll was like a typical salmon sushi roll. Wasn't anything special but you can taste the freshness of the salmon.

As for udon, we ordered the Tan Tan with thick udon, Sukiyaki with thick udon, Tsurutontan Deluxe with thick udon and Tsuruton Curry Deluxe with thin udon. The regular and large sizes are the SAME PRICE! So we all went for the large size! The udon itself was very tender and chewy. 

Tan Tan Udon was a spicy soup base with tiny bits of meat. If you keep eating, it might get a bit spicy.

Sukiyaki was a clear broth noodle that contained among mushrooms and beef.

Tsurutontan Deluxe (my order) was very good! The soup base was clear and overall very tasty. It contains a lot of ingredients (mostly fried), beef, chicken and egg. Since it's all placed on the soup, expect the fried batter to be soggy. I rather eat it when it's crispy and not soggy.

Tsuruton Curry Deluxe came with a thick curry broth topped with shrimp tempura, pork cutlet and beef. It's was overall very good. 

These portions were huge but definitely worth coming here!

Went there for lunch with my family.  Place was comfortable and had a LA feel to it. Service was excellent and very attentive.  Sushi was fresh and excellent.  Udon with broth came in large bowls (upsize with no extra cost).  Udon without broth came in sizzling bowl which keep the meal hot at all times.  Wish the meat and seafood was enough to compliment the large amount of fat udon noodles.  Overall very good.

tl;dr Huge portions and really good noodles; my favorite udon spot in NYC.

I got the duck and meatball udon and split the beef brisket buns with a friend. The udon was a little pricey, but the portions are huge and they upgrade the size to large for free (not sure why the bowls aren't large by default?). I really enjoyed the noodles here. They were just chewy/thick enough (millennials read THICC), and the duck was cooked perfectly. If I had just gotten the udon alone I'd probably give the meal 5 stars.

I thought the buns were just average and the beef was a little dry. I'd pass on these if I came again but there were plenty of other appetizers that looked great.

I love this place and have regularly brought friends here who also love the soups. Who wouldnt love the fact that the bowls are gigantic and theres no price difference between the small and large? I personally was not a big fan of the sukiyaki because it was overwhelmingly sweet or the kimchi udon which was not even kimchi but rather plain cabbages and a weak soup base. I would highly highly recommend the duck and wagyu beef udons though as they are my absolute favorites!
Absolutely great udon. Loved it. The bowl is probably the biggest noodle bowl in NYC.

I've been coming here on a pretty regular basis for the past few months, either eating solo after grocery shopping at the greenmarket or bring my friends/family. Between all of these visits and guests, I've tried the uni creme (hot), truffle crab/mushroom creme, the sizzling plate tempura veg, and the duck, plus the tofu burrata app. The service is great, attentive, fast; most meals at least two servers have checked on me. I usually sit in the first dining room (with the bar) rather than the lower dining room (in the booths), and it is relatively quiet and peaceful. My favorite udon is the uni creme (hot) - it has so much umami that it tastes almost like mac and cheese. If anyone is concerned about it tasting/smelling fishy, I assure you it does not. The truffle crab creme is a close second, and is also full of umami thanks to the truffle oil/sauteed mushrooms. Both are rich (the uni is richer), and taste amazing with the thick noodles (always large portion of noodles. ALWAYS). I am not as enthused about their apps, and I find that healthwise and appetite-wise, just ordering the noodle main is enough to satisfy. That said, the tofu burrata was a poor choice to try and would not suggest for anyone who has access to silken tofu, soy sauce and bonito flakes. I thought it was like an actual burrata (some kind of creamy texture in the middle) but it was just a lump of fresh tofu. The tofu was fresh and delicious, but still. 
Having tried the duck udon in the clear broth, I think you get a better deal and a tastier meal going with a creme based broth. Once you have creme, you can't go back. I also found the duck broth didn't have any particularly strong duck flavor, which was disappointing. It was like a plain chicken noodle soup but subbed chicken meat for slices of duck (which were cooked perfectly). 
I took away one star because I do think it is pricey for udon. I took my parents out to Saturday lunch, and we ordered green tea, the tofu app, and 3 udons. The bill was $100 including tip, which is a lot considering we just had noodles!

Made a same day reservation for lunch on a Tuesday. We were 20 minutes early and got seated right away. It does get crowded though. I've tried making a Friday night reservation days in advance and they were out of reservations.

I had the curry deluxe udon. For the same price you can upgrade it to a large which is more noodles in the same sized bowl. Although I was pretty full with the regular size. The texture of the udon was good, not too soggy, and the curry was flavorful. My friends seemed to enjoy their meals too.

Staff was attentive, always checked up on us, and explained the menu in details to us.

The food was ahhmazing. Came here on Sunday evening and was seated immediately (nice use of space btw, I really liked the makeshift wall)

The order was the soy garlic chicken appetizer and two tsurutontan deluxe udon bowls. The portion size was HUGE esp after an appetizer; you can also opt for a larger portion (more noodles) at no extra cost.
But in the end, I couldn't finish my noodles despite how delicious it was. From the tempura shrimp and vegetables, the egg, the beef, the chicken, the addictive dashi broth, there was literally a party in the bowl. I would hands down order this again but with the tempura on the side so it doesn't get soggy. Can't wait to come back here again!

WOW!!! I dare you to name a better udon place that can beat their great service, variety, and restuarant size. It was my first time here and I will definitely be bringing back many friends for them to try and for me to try other udon soup flavors!

We (2 total) arrived at around 6:30 on a Tuesday and were seated right away. Our server, Annie, gave us a little time to look at the menu before coming over and explaining it to us. Throughout the meal, she was very attentive to check on how much water we had in our cups and if we were ok with our food. 

They have such a wide variety of soup flavors that choosing one was really hard!! I went with the deluxe and my friend with the Wagyu beeef udon. Both were delicious and very filling. We had an exhausting day of biking and walking around Manhattan and the regular size was enough for us, maybe because we had a lot of liquid throughout the day. But if it wasn't, free refills  on the noodles! There's also a choice of thick or thin udon; I don't think I've ever seen or heard of thin udon, but I'll be sure to try it next time.

By the time we left around 8PM, there was already a huge crowd waiting to be seated. So make sure you come early if you'd want to avoid a wait!

One downside of this place is that it might not be very comfortable if you are on the bigger side. A lot of their chairs are bar stools with small seats and they will fill up every chair so it's a bit crowded even without moving around and eating comfortably. They do have booths but those are for bigger parties of around 6.

Came here for lunch earlier today and I will say that I was quite impressed. For starters, I love that they offer free extra noodles to newcomers, (if I heard correctly ) and the staff here is very nice and friendly especially our waitress Annie, who explained everything thoroughly and was very helpful. I love the interior of this place as well it's very clean and very well set up; rather unique. 

Now getting to the food, I got the curry udon and my friends got the cream seafood udon and the sashimi (salmon) over rice. Firstly, I like that you can choose between thick and thin noodles, because you get more options. And secondly, the portions they offer you are crazily huge (bigger than your face! And maybe your friend's face... and their friend too...) I would definitely say you can share it with some people, especially if you're not the biggest eater. 

I enjoyed my meal quite a lot, the curry was very flavorful and had a nice smoothness to it. Also the tempura and the beef was really tasty. The beef was very tender and seasoned nicely and the pork and shrimp tempura was good as well. I wasn't the biggest fan of the creamy udon, mainly because seafood-based cream foods are not really my thing. Although the salmon was really good, it was really fresh.  The only thing iis udon is so damn hard to eat, it is one slippery ass noodle, it was still good though. Will definitely come back!

YUMMY YUMMY in my tummy. So good. I've been looking for a spot that can wow me like the way the flavors do in ramen and I finally found it! Only it is in udon form; which is a good change for once, since I have tried a many many ramen places before. They have an extensive menu and I am certain that you would find one that matches your taste palette! I also appreciate how they pictures along with the food item because it gives a much better visual. It kind of builds the excitement that come along with getting your food and makes it easier to decide what you want. They also tell you what the more popular choices are that usually people order. 

~There's an option for thin udon or regular udon
~Choice between large or small but it is the SAME PRICE

Things Ordered: 
Tsuruton Curry Deluxe ($24): shrimp tempura (2 of them), pork cutlet & beef short plate with regular udon. This was delicious! 10/10 would recommend. The curry was creamy and not  spicy with good consistency where the noodles can soak up the sauce. The pork cutlet is cooked like a tonkatsu just minus the sauce. It was moist and fried evenly. I would recommend this dish for all the curry lovers because it would not disappoint. Even if you're not like biggest curry fan, it is still yummy and worth trying.  

Tan Tan Udon ($20): Contains spicy creamy sesame broth, ground pork chili oil with regular udon. If you can't handle spicy I would avoid this dish! The spicy level according to the waiter is 7/10. The first initial 5 bites it is bearable but after a while, it gets gradually spicier. This was my least favorite out of all the things I tried and sadly it was my personal dish that I had chose. I couldn't finish the whole bowl and was also slightly disappointed since there wasn't much to my dish besides ground pork and the broth. But I guess what I am paying for in this dish, is the broth itself. In the broth the sesame flavor was definitely present and mixed very well with the chili oil. The bowl was literally glowing red like volcanic lava.  

Sizzling Sukiyaki Udon ($18): Contains stir fried udon with beef, vegetable & sweet soy in stone pot with regular udon. This is another awesome dish. If you are not in the mood for something that is soup/broth based but still want something saucy, try this one. It is one of the best stir fried udons I've had and you would not regret it. Just be careful when your dish initially arrives because it would be very hot from the pot.  

Uni Udon ($24): Contains fresh uni, shiso, nori & uni dashi sauce with thin udon. This is a light and simple dish but do not under estimate its simplicity. My family came here on a super humid day and my sister ordered this cold dish. When it tried it, it was super refreshing with lots of flavor coming from the uni and uni sauce. Personally if you are going to get a cold udon dish, I would pair it with thin udon noodles since it is chewier but not overwhelmingly thick. For thicker udons I would leave that for the more brothy/saucy dishes!

When I found out Japan's udon noodle chain had a New York location, I had to check it out. My friend and I met Monday at 7 PM for dinner and were immediately seated. Our server was super nice and took the time to explain everything on the menu, making sure to tell us what was popular and what his favorites were. Super helpful!

We shared the Sukiyaki Beef Buns, which were tasty. They were a tad oily, but the flavors were excellent. I then had the cold Uni Udon and my friend got the hot Duck Udon. They give you the option of the normal or large size for the same price, so we of course both got large. My Uni Udon was delicious! Super refreshing and light, with that creamy udon flavor. I didn't think it was that much food, but I quickly started getting full. By the end of the meal, I was stuffed. My friend's warm udon had nice flavors as well. But I'm all about the thin cold udon noodles. Yum. It's a little pricier than other noodle places, but definitely worth a splurge. Can't wait to come back!

I did get some mixed reviews about this place but I was getting tired of ramen so we came here for date night! The wait wasn't long, maybe 30 minutes. We sat at the bar and  had a drink with appetizers. We ordered the the duck and spicy tuna apps and they were great! I loved both. When we got to the table we ordered the sukiyaki udon. It was recommended by the waiter.. I didn't care for it. I preferred my husbands chicken over rice! That was delicious.

By far the largest bowl of udon I've ever had / seen in my life. 

Tsurutontan looks really trendy and hip on the inside-- their space is QUITE large for a New York udon restaurant, but I like it! It wasn't too loud and people weren't squished together like in other places. Obviously, it's not a traditional Japanese place, but it was a nice experience overall. 

The food: 
- Uni udon: was pretty good, but a little heavy. We got it with the thicker noodles, but I feel like it would've been better with the thin noodles instead. It just didn't taste the way I thought it would.. although it did come with a few pieces of uni on the top.... I'd stick with uni pasta over a uni soup thing any day. 

- I forget what it's called, but it was the standard one that was 1st on the menu lol. That was pretty good! It had a lot of flavor and tasted like the traditional udon that I love. We got that with the thin noodles... but... we should've gotten it with the thicker noodles. 

- spicy tuna cones were SUPER yummy!! I liked them a lot! 
- the chicken appetizer: pretty good, but I remember something was a little off about the flavor... maybe too salty?? Too sweet? I don't remember.. 

They give you A LOT of food (udon), with extra noodles being free! The small and regular sizes are the same price so, just get the larger size. We split the appetizers and the two bowls between three girls and we were stuffed.

I give it a 4 star because there was no service in the downstairs seating area. I had to constantly walk back upstairs to get service. Other than that, the food was great! The udon was very chewy and bouncy. If you're a fan of udon, this is the place to go to! They also have happy hour everyday but only at the bar area. The cocktails are $8 and you may not bring it to the table. The interior design is super chic and waiters were very accommodating. I will def come back again.
Average food with big portion, my uni noodle was too creamy. I would say its not worth the price.

Decided to try this place out with a few of my friends, since I saw this on insider and one of my friends recommended this place. We were greeted and seated very quickly. The interior of the restaurant was very sleek and simple, it gives off a very comfy feeling. They placed the menu on the table and our waitress greeted us and introduced herself to us too. She took the time to explain each item on the menu and her recommendations which was good. 

She said that thin noodles are usually placed with the cold udon dishes while the soupy ones are the thick udon. Also she told us if we wanted extra noodles and extra soup it's FREE. Which was a plus! 

My friends and I decided to do family style. So we ordered US Wagyu Shabu Udon (19), shrimp tempura (17) it came with a side of shrimp tempura, mushrooms that were fried, and last but not least we also got the sizzling sukiyaki udon (18). We decided to include a lunch set for two of the udon meals (you add $3 and you get a choice of soy garlic chicken rice, mentaiko spicy cod roe rice or sukiyaki beef rice) we got the soy garlic chicken rice and the mentaiko spicy cod roe. We also got extra noodles for our meal. 

The food came out pretty fast waited about 15 mins. The sizzling udon dish came out first, then the shrimp tempura and then the us Wagyu shabu dish. Don't forget to mix the egg in the sizzling pot of udon first. I tried the us Wagyu shabu udon first. The udon was delicious, the beef was pretty good, as for the soup it was okay. It looked very flavorful, but I didn't think it something that hit me like WOW, it was pretty good. The shrimp tempura udon, it was pretty good the soup based was straight forward & flavorful. The sizzling udon   was by far the most flavorful and my favorite. I would definitely recommend this dish. As for the 2 side dishes we ordered for our lunch we got the soy garlic fried chicken rice, the chicken was definitely very flavorful and yummy. The mentakio spicy cod roe with rice, the fish eggs itself was very salty, I didn't like it too much. Overall the service here was great! They came by to check on us a few times to see if we were okay and they also refilled our water countless of times. Definitely would recommend this place! 
Service 8.5 
Atmosphere 8
Food 8.5

I like it. I like it a lot. Once I ate here twice in one day and I still liked it. 

I like all the udon I've ever had here but I must say the mentaiko one can be a bit much/heavy for one person so I suggest you share. I always upgrade to a large (which you should as well since it's no charge) and try different things with friends. This is a great place for a summer dinner.

I hate sitting communal squeezed in between other people. But if ur an unlucky party of 2, that's what they'll give you.

Server was amazing. Food came out within 5 min of ordering, it was insane. Food was good. Water cake is def worth a try, just to say you've tried it. Very cool vibe inside. Highly recommend.

Big Big Bowls of Udon! 

I love uni and I love udon. This place was definitely on my list to try. Walked in one evening and got seated right away. The female staff that had helped us was warm and friendly but the male server we had was talking so low that I could barely hear him. Service was carried out in a laid back manner. 

The udon quality is superb. There is thin and thick you can choose from. Udon portions are offered at a regular size. You may upgrade to a larger portion at no extra cost. 

I started with the uni and seared wagyu sushi, soy garlic fried chicken, shishito peppers, and grilled duck breast. The sushi piece could use a sprinkle of sea salt. Other appetizers was just alright, not memorable. 

I was torn between the cold uni, uni cream, or truffle crab and mushroom. I went with the uni cream and I was not satisfied at all. The udon itself is amazing but the broth could use a lot of improvements. I was expecting rich and flavorful. The uni on top did not do any justice nor did it taste fresh. 

Overall, this place needs a lot of flavor, literally and figuratively.

It's a nice restaurant and everything on the menu looked good. I'd go again to try something new, but based on my dish I wouldn't add this to my list of favorites.

Decor is amazing, it's spacious, and the staff was friendly. We went at 5 on Friday and, not surprising, it was very empty. When we left though things had filled up and it looked like some people were waiting at the front for tables. 

Food was pretty good. I had the Yamakake Udon with tempura, very filling. It was a lot of food, but also a very consistent, same flavor. After my tempura was gone I couldn't finish just the noodles. My friends also got Udon dishes that were good. I think my favorite was the Mentaiko caviar Udon my friend got. Also it was a nice, smaller portion. 

For dessert I got the lychee one (I forget the name). Totally hit the spot. My friend got the water cake, which was definitely the most fun desert, but not a lot of flavor.

The bowl was huge. You can order extra noodles without being charged extra. I ordered the deluxe and the tempura was soggy due to it being in the broth for quite a bit. I thought the flavor was ok. I also tried the add on fish egg with rice for 3 dollars and it did not appeal to me. They have a good seating area.
The udon here was just okay. The broth was good and the condiments were good but the texture of the noodles weren't up to par. The service bumped it up to a 4 for me.

Variety of Uni dishes are great. 

The udon bowls are huge. But that's all it is. Huge bowls. Content inside the bowl is a different story. It's like buying a huge bag of chips realizing it's all air. 

However, it's really good. Tan tan had a nice spicy and sour kick to it. A lot of flavor and delicious. 

The sukiyaki sizzling bowl is a great option if you don't want broth. 

Tons of appetizers and other dishes to choose from. I had the shrimp dumplings and they were just okay. 

Huge menu with tasty options will leave your curious mind wanting to try them all.

Tsurutontan was such a great experience! I got the Duck Udon and it was pretty good. First time here and the customer service was spot on, we got in and seated under 2 minutes around 6pm-ish. Your choice of ice water or hot tea is completely complimentary and when you choose your preferred dish, there's no extra charge for the size that you want! What a deal! Definitely would come back!
Omgosh!!! This place is absolutely amazing. They have thick noodles in the biggest bowl I've ever seen. I can't wait to go back. Not bad for the price at all.

very good noodles and ok sushi.  order the extra large noodles and get any leftovers to go.  same price on extra large noodles or normal portions.  service is ok but keep in mind long wait times to get in.

After seeing this restaurant on Insider, my friends and I decided to try out this restaurant. We made a reservation for 1pm, but the restaurant wasn't very crowded when we arrived. The waiter was super friendly and explained the whole process. For our table of 3, the waiter suggested that we order 2 of the large udon bowls. 

We ordered the Beef Udon and the Curry Udon. We all preferred the Curry Udon. We were given small bowls with a large spoon. After having the Curry Udon, the Beef Udon tasted a bit bland and it was hard to taste the flavors. We all ended up taking the Udon from the beef broth and dipping it into the Curry broth. There isn't as much Udon in the bowl as we thought and I think the large bowl really affects your perception. The large spoon was a bit awkward to use and I would have probably preferred a normal soup spoon. The Udon was mediocre and we left feeling that we had paid to eat from a large bowl. 

Overall, the service was great but the Udon was average. I might come back if I'm in the area.

My friend and I came here for a girls dinner. The wait was a little long, but thankfully they have the text system. We were seated at the bar area and the waitress was very helpful. She explained the menu to us and also offered kind suggestions on getting thick udon noodles for the hot dishes and thin for the cold. 

We ordered the spicy tuna tartar cones and shrimp dumplings to start. The tuna cones were great, just the right level of crunch and spicy. One small critique my friend had was that she wished the avocado was incorporated better. It was kind of strange to get a bite of just avocado and then a bite of just tuna. The shrimp dumplings were amazingly seasoned. The flavor was just right, the shrimp to wrapper was very proportional.

I ordered the soondubu udon and my friend ordered the tan tan udon. We didn't exchange thoughts on the udon as we were both knee deep in udon (we went with the large). Our one comment was that the noodle was perfectly chewy and springy (if this description makes sense). I really enjoyed my soondubu udon, but wasn't in love with it. I think I was secretly hoping for it to become the seafood kimchi flavor I normally get at korean restaurants. In retrospect, I should have gotten a pork broth based udon as I was getting too fancy mixing and matching cuisines. 

The service was amazing, our waters were always filled and the the waitress was very polite.

Honestly, this place is hyped up just as much as Ippudo. The prices are around the same and some of the fancier udon dishes are 20+ for a bowl. Yeah, the small and large size are the same price but I have a feeling the only difference is the size of the bowl, not the amount of noodles or soup you get.

The service is up to standard. Kind and helpful waiters who go over the menu with you if it's your first time (like me). But, after we ordered, the food took some time to get to us which is one of the down sides to our experience at Tsurutontan. I ordered the Mentaiko Ankake Udon which had caviar + egg broth. My boyfriend ordered the Shrimp + Veggie Tempura Udon. We both opted for the thicker udon noodles which were firm and quite tasty. My broth was definitely more flavorful than the Tempura udon but I'm not sure this place lives up to the hype. 

I recommend this place to try out if you're ever in the area otherwise not somewhere I'd go out of my way to eat at again.

Really impressed by this place and the experience that you get. Inside is a chic and trendy restaurant that has a lavish modern feel to it. It's very hip with music pumping, modern decour, and ambiant lighting....almost makes you feel like you're in a club of sorts. Menu is awesome, and exactly how places should do menus, pictures for everything with good categorization. Staff is helpful and give good recommendations. The bowls they use are huge and gives you the impression that it's a gigantic amount of food for one person, however it's more than manageable. A cool feature of every dish is that they come in medium or large (only difference is quantity of noodles) at no extra cost either way. 

I was really drawn to the waygu entree, but there were so many directions I was pulled it was ridiculous. At first I thought I would for sure go with a spicy shrimp bowl that caught my eye, but then I gave some consideration to a seafood/enoki mushroom item, but ultimately I was swayed too much by the tender melt in your mouth beef I knew I was in for. The broth is extremely rich and would be warming on the coldest of days, but didn't taste too fatty or stout. The waygu was spot on, had a taste that I think is unique to waygu and definitely worth venturing a taste for how affordable it is (authentic waygu can go for as much as $45/ounce). Noodles were thick and tasty and were abundant in the soup, though I didn't feel like they cheaped out and only gave me noodles. Good meat to broth to noodle ratio.

The one draw back is this place can be a little pricy. For the one bowl it ran about $19, but I do think you get your money's worth for the phenomenal quality you get. Not too many places can give you legitimately tasty US waygu, and the meal is definitely an experience. If you've never had waygu, or you consider yourself a noodle connoisseur, definitely give this place a try at the very least.

The food was good, but service was atrocious.

I called ahead and made a reservation for 8:30, me and my party arrived on time and let the hostess know we'd arrived. Half an hour later and we're still waiting for our table. They kept telling us that the party before us was still in the process of paying. Yeah... a full 30 minutes to pay the bill, right. Aren't reservations made to NOT wait half an hour in line? Oh not to mention that parties that walked in after us were seated right away, but I digress... we did get our table.

So we get our table and start ordering. A couple of apps and four bowls of udon. Shouldn't be a problem for the kitchen right? Appetizers come, we eat, we're all smiles. Appetizers go and the waiting game starts. What kind of restaurant with a full kitchen staff takes OVER AN HOUR for four bowls of noodles? We try to call a couple servers to ask where our order is and they either shrug us off, ignoring us completely, or give a canned "you're order should be coming right up" while bringing hot bowls of noodles to diners who were seated AFTER us. 

I am a pretty patient guy but this was off the charts ridiculous. Never going back here nor am I ever recommending this place to anybody I know.
Great service and wide variety of noodles and other yummy foods. You can make a reservation online, which is awesome since the lines tend to be long.

Really cool spot in the city where You have options.

There is a lot of Ramen Spots
There is a lot of Pho Spots
There is a lot of Chinese noodle spots
BUT there is NOT A LOT OF UDON NOODLE SPOTS!


Tsurutontan Udon is located in Union square, pretty big location but regardless I recommend you to make Reservations,  it gets pretty packed during dinner time.

A group of us ordering and each which different dish we had the chance to experience it.  This successful restaurant has hit everyone's SPOT with their Udon with a choice of soup, sauce or with their specialized dishes.  and every Udon noodle order comes in a HUGE BOWL but is a regular size portion.  

TO be honest, is not RIDIC good that blows my mind, is more of a comfort food that warms my body and different from other restaurants.  Udon is not the BEST i've had.

Udon Udon Udon! Come with a big appetite because this place supplies big butt bowls of noodles. So good! I came here with a group of 4 on a Friday night and it was easy enough to make reservations a week beforehand. Service here was super friendly. It's easy to split the bowls or hoard them all for yourself. Get the large portion of udon if you are hungry because it is at no extra cost!

So for a group of 4, we got 5 large bowls of udon because we couldn't decide and I am sure glad we did. Everything was delicious. The udon itself was perfectly cooked, al dente to the way I like it. The soups they were accompanied by were just as good. We tried the curry, tan tan, uni crème, truffle crème and the Tsurotontan Deluxe. Depending on your palate, you really cannot go wrong with any of the choices. Personally, the curry deluxe and tsuortontan were my favorite. The curry was on the heavier side. Super flavorful with delicious tonkatsu. The tsuortontan was lighter in broth with an assortment of goodies inside including shrimp tempura and egg. As for the others, the tan tan had a good hit of spice to it. The uni crème and truffle creame were similar in consistency given its creamy base. The truffle definitely stood out in the soup. The uni crème was milder. 

Overall, great dinner experience. Casual and delicious!

This is the place to go for curry udon. It's delicious and it's HUGE. Both regular and large sizes are the same price and the large is very large. I came on an empty stomach and only ate half. Perfect for taking home to eat the next day!!!!!!!

If you like Udon, you're gonna love this place. They have tons of different options and flavors. It's a bit pricey, but you can get a large portion free of charge. So if you come hungry and do that, it's worth it!

Amazing, unique udon. I got the ikura uni udon and it was unlike any soup I've ever had. I also loved the lychee ricotta ice cream -- again, very unique and flavorful. Very friendly staff, too. I only gave this 4 stars because of the super long wait, and sort of high prices.

Ramen usually gets all the hype but udon deserves just as much love. Tsurutontan gives udon the love it deserves. 

Here's what you need to know:
1. Portions are OUT OF THIS WORLD. These bowls are huge. You can bob for apples in them, bathe a small child, or eat enough food to lock you into a food coma. I'm serious - these bowls are too large. In the best way possible.
2. The udon is worth it. The spicy tan tan noodles are my favorite but all bowls have a great amount of flavor and the right amount of toppings.
3. The appetizers and sushi are solid. There are a lot of trendy options that can be fill you up before you get to the udon.
4. The ambiance gives Tsurutontan the whole package. It's a cool spot to go to (and a great date spot). 
5. Service is all right. Sometimes it can be spot on but when the restaurant is really busy, it can be difficult to get someone's attention.

Tsurutontan is one of those places that's the total package. If you're looking for a solid spot in the Union Square area, it's definitely worth your time.

I ordered two sushi rolls: eel cucumber and tuna avocado. Both were great. My date had the duck udon. That was wonderful as well. If I had been hungrier, would have tried the mushroom udon too. Maybe next time.  Interior decor is excellent! Very noisy though!

When a restaurant is featured on Insider Food, you have to go and visit it. Tsurutontan was recently covered by Insider and I knew I had to check it out.

I made reservations for 6:30 on a Saturday and I'm glad I did. The restaurant had a ton of people and there was a wait for even parties of two.

I ordered the TanTan Udon and I really appreciated that my waiter told my group that a large bowl was the same price as a small. If you're on the fence, definitely go for the large! Overall the TanTan udon was delicious but wasn't as spicy as I thought it would be. You may not feel full at first but give it 20 minutes or so and you'll feel stuffed.

Knocking down a star because my table was charged $1.50 for chili paste. We didn't know that we would be charged for this since nobody told us. It was only after we asked for a second saucer of chili paste that a waiter was kind enough to inform us about this extra charge. 

Overall though, I would come back again to try other items on the menu.
The noodles are perfect. Hip interior. Everything was so savory and delicious. Great service. The bowls are reeeeeeaaaallly big!!!!!

Here is a Japanese noodle restaurant. They offers the same quality as Japan. If you ordered large serving, it would be same price. There are lots of appetizers and noodles on the menu.
I wanna go there again:)

Tsurutontan is a strong four star contender. While the food is certainly very well done and tasty, I can't help but shake the feeling that you're mostly paying for the restaurant's location and space. It's very beautiful, spacious and intimate inside, but at the end of the day... it's udon noodles. From my experience, udon noodles are typically priced at $12 or maybe $13 at most restaurants, so this is by far the most expensive udon I've ever had. My buddy and I came through for dinner before seeing a movie nearby.

We started off with the spicy tuna tar tar cones appetizer ($12), and then she got the tan tan udon ($20) and I got the duck udon ($18). The tar tar cones were DELICIOUS. Rich and creamy, the tuna and avocado complement each other to create edible silk. It also has a nice spicy kick to finish it off. The only problem is that there were only four cones; amount notwithstanding, this appetizer is a home run.

The udon noodles were also very nicely cooked. Since we ordered dishes with hot broth, our waitress recommended that we get the thicker noodles. The noodles were cooked perfectly and weren't over or underdone at all. My duck tasted like liver, which is fine with me, but some people may not like that. I would've been happy paying $15 for the dish, but $18 isn't terrible. My friend liked her tan tan noodles, too, but I think my duck udon was better.

As a last note, you have the option to order the noodles with either extra or normal portions. Both the extra and normal portions are the same price, so I really don't understand why anybody would get the normal portion. I ordered extra and I didn't feel like there was any more than a normal order at any given restaurant. True that the bowls are big, but like another reviewer mentioned, there wasn't an astounding amount of noodles included. Regardless, you're pretty much guaranteed to leave the restaurant full because of the soup.

I have been wanting to try out this spot for about a year since it took over the Old Union Square Cafe space. The decor of Tsurutontan is really nice. There is a long bar in the front and then there is a dining area in the back with a long shared table with sections cut of with hanging dividers and some separate tables for parties larger then two. The lighting is dim and they succeeded in making a fairly large restaurant seem intimate. 

Our server was very attentive, and well versed on the menu items. They took us through the different dishes, noodle varieties, flavors, etc. You can tell that management trains them to be well informed on what is being served here. It helps that the menu has pictures since there is a lot to choose from. 

The Shrimp Tempura Udon was perfect. The Udon comes in a big bowl with the tempura on the side. You can ask for a large portion of Udon and it will be the same price as the normal portion. Of course I got the large and they were perfectly cooked and tender. The type of noodle that once you start to eat it you cannot stop. The broth was also delicious. I am curious to try their other dishes, especially other Udons since I was impressed. 

The only downfall of this place is that it seems on the pricier side give the location and the decor. From what I have heard there are Udon places in the city that seem just as good and are more reasonably priced. But overall, this will be a good spot when fall and winter comes.

I had one of the spicy broth noodles and it was amazing. Huge large portions very tasty broth! Would def go back. We got water cake also for desert. I wouldn't order that again but it was very unique and if you hadn't tried it you should! Light and super different.

I was super excited to try this udon restaurant! I got the waygu and mushroom sukiyaki udon and my friend got the uni creme udon. You can choose a normal size or large size, large being with more noodles. Both came in the same size bowl. There is no price difference between the normal or large size. Given that aspect, we opted for the large size. You can also choose between thin or thick udon. I always ate thick udon my whole life so I got that option as well. 

The waygu was sooo tender and flavorful. Every bite was so amazing. The udon itself was chewy. The biggest downside was that the soup was lukewarm instead of hot. I think it stayed in the kitchen too long before being served to us. 

I would highly recommend to make a reservation as we went on a Wednesday night and it was super packed. I would definitely go back to try the other udon dishes!

Came here on a Sunday when they have great bar specials on food and drinks all day. I tried the soy garlic fried chicken and spicy tuna cones. The spicy tuna cones were also filled with guac and the combination of spicy tuna and guac went well together. The soy garlic fried chicken bites were mediocre. The sauce itself was flavorful but the fried chicken bites felt like they were originally frozen. Overall I enjoyed the food and  I plan on coming here again soon to try the udon!

Friendly services, clean space. Food was good but not great. Ordered the egg plant tempura, batter was too thick. Spicy tuna in cone shaped fried dough, presentation was pretty and tasted good. Uni with cold thin noodles, was enjoyable. I love uni, so I order an extra sashimi serving but the quality is not as good as the one the was with the noodle dish.
I would have given four stars, except the ladies room was smelly. Need attention to this area so to not ruin the dinning experience as a whole.
Delicious! Love the udon here. The large bowl is perfect for sharing. Definitely going back here.

Their dinner menu is on steroids. *Inserts arm emoji*

I'm gonna categorize this place under: Balls Gorgeous Inside, Deceptively Plain Outside. Every section has a different design, which keeps it quite exciting. They share a rustic appeal but the room I'm usually seated in has a long table in the middle to emulate a bar style for sitting. On the way to bathroom, I'm always distracted by a wall made entirely out of denim. Bathroom is a letdown; I usually get a kick out of a well thought out working closet but to have a wall made entirely out of a mirror but for me not to see myself while pooping? It's just inconsiderate.

Right now, my friend whom I went with is texting me "I'll finish those noodles one day... ONE DAY". It just dawned on me that I should always order Large simply because it's the same price and if I'm gonna end up taking it home anyways, I might as well be able to feed myself for the next two days. I mean, it'd better be a lot of noodles for $20+. Seriously, it's a lot of noodles. Like... don't bring a date here or else you'll lose her respect kinda noodles. :( I still remember the look of disappointment in her eyes so vividly.

ANYWHO, this review will probably forever be a work in progress because something always pops up that I'll wanna try next time. First I ordered the Spicy Miso. Then the Sukiyaki. Then the Curry Udon. It's a great place if you're the adventurous type. I'm an adventurous/drive myself into debt/fatass type of guy. Spicy Miso is their #1 but I ain't wit it. You get a lot of it but I was expecting a little more pizaz. Sukiyaki broth has a really sweet taste to it. I've never had sukiyaki before, is that how it's supposed to taste? It's neither bad nor good.

The curry udon on the other hand is king-- KING! Most places I find have the texture poorly executed. Maybe that's why it's sorta rare in the first place. But today I found myself drinking my meal instead of finishing the noodles.

To be continued

This is one of my favorite udon chain restaurants from Japan, that opened not too long ago in New York. 
The quality from the Japanese restaurants has remained constant with its New York counterpart. The service was pleasant and efficient, and it was easy to get a reservation.
I highly recommend the US wagyu and uni seared sushi.

Plus sides: No wait during lunch, decent happy hour, good service, good udon noodles

Cons: Salty broth, under cooked and bitter cabbage

My visit today during lunch was both amazing and disappointing. I ordered the Sukiyaki Udon with comes with enoki mushrooms, half a piece of mushroom, cabbage, beef and udon noodles. The beef was fatty and tender, the udon and mushrooms were cooked perfectly but the worst part of the ingredients was the under cooked and bitter AF cabbage :( I was on my lunch break and didn't have time to sent it back and get a new order so they weren't able to fix this but it's not going to deter me from going back. The udon noodles were the star of the show! I re-microwaved my leftovers in the office and the noodles weren't soggy. They were still perfect in texture. 

Looking forward to the next time I visit.

If you want Happy hour and Udon... forget it. Choose one or the other.

The noodles are great. I eat here for lunch often. 

Came in for Happy hour for the first time today. I was told I cannot order noodles at the bar. 

Ok. 

"Can I have Happy hour at my seat?" 

No. 

Asked to speak to Manager. Again. 

Manager Chris is rude. 

"Nope. Nothing we can do. It is the rule."

"?" So confused... 

I'll Happy hour somewhere else...

My aunt and I came with reservations around 5pm (late late lunch) on a Saturday. 

We ordered:
1. Soy garlic fried chicken
2. 2 bowls of tempura udon (large bowl)

The fried chicken was good. I wish that the sauce came separately as a dipping sauce. I don't like if my fried items become soggy and the sauce was not like a sticky Korean fried chicken sauce. It was more soy sauce-like and runny. 

I loved how the tempura arrived separately without needing to specify that I wanted my tempura on a different plate. There was a nice selection and everything came very crispy and hot. 

When ordering your udon, you get a choice of a normal bowl or a large bowl. There was no price difference between the normal or large bowl. With the large, you get more noodles I think. The bowls are HUGE, but the actual stuff in the bowls is a reasonable amount. The broth was a simple one, but very solid. The noodles were also cooked perfectly.

I would definitely come back for the udon. I may try a different appetizer next time.

Happy hour  ( from 7-10pm) includes a selections Of red/white wines, beers , cocktails and sake.  We waited approximately 30-45 mins without reservation on a Friday night. For appetizers, we ordered the crispy tuna tartare, and beef bun (both were not bad). For the udon , we ordered the large wagyu to share (two people). I loved the idea of the humongous bowl but you pay the same price as a regular bowl (you'll get more noodle ). the only thing I didn't like so much was the wagyu, it was a bit chewy.
Their uni udon and sukiyaki hot stone udon are good, but they are not too special. One thing I love about this place is that their waiters are hot :D

A regular spot for my boyfriend and I when it comes to dine in the city, they are making high value udon as a franchise restaurant, better than a lot more other restaurant I had tried in some other restaurant, the sushi is good too we usually have salmon and snow crab roll.  Waiters were well trained and always able to get a table without waiting with reservation. The down side would be they don't provide containers for left overs, so be careful not to order too much food and not able to bring them home afterwards.

This is the first location in the US for this Japanese noodle chain, and it did not disappoint. Went in hoping for some comfort food in the form of noodle soup, and a big bowl of that is exactly what they delivered.

The menu was huge but we ended up splitting one appetizer and getting a bowl of noodles each, which was more than enough for me.

Udon pon dumpling - The menu described this as a dumpling made of udon dough, so I was picturing a giant fried dough ball. What came instead was a deep fried dumpling where I guess the skin was made from udon dough but the insides were like eating shumai. Really nice flavor and the chili sauce it came with was excellent.

Chicken udon - The price for regular and large udon is the same, and they said the only difference was the large had more noodles. Since I was with someone who could finish the noodles if I got full, why wouldn't I get the large? The texture of the thick noodles was great, just the right amount of chewiness. The broth made with dashi stock was soothing and comforting with a such a nice flavor. We were there at the end of summer, but I could see this being especially nice in the winter.

Would definitely return. There is so much on the menu still to try!

Absolutely fantastic dinner with my family (with two aged 11 & 13).  We started with the Soy Garlic fried chicken and beef buns.  Dinner was Beef Udon, Duck Udon, Sashimi Udon, Oyako Don Rice bowl and the sizzling Sukiyaki Udon.  We really loved everything.  My only complaint is that mains did not all come out at the same time and so we were all waiting for everyone to have their dishes before eating (not sure if the lag was intentional as they have lots of sharing of dishes).  Next time, I will ask to have things come out together.  Portions are generous, you can size up the udon for no additional charge and can choose between the fat noodle or thin noodle.  
Service was really great.  Sabrina was our server and she was so helpful in guiding us through the menu, made suggestions and accommodations for anything we needed.  The manager, front of the house, bar, servers were all professional, friendly and attentive.  I look forward to dining here again!

Best udon in NYC! The wait can be long and they prices seem a little high but it's totally worth it. The portion sizes are huge so the price make sense. My favorite bowl is the sizzling sukiyaki udon. 2 people could probably share one bowl, or if you get your own which I usually do you'll leave nice and full.  Service was very slow my last visit, but overall from precious visits it's been ok.

What you need to know: 
- a massive restaurant with plenty of seating on two levels, though a reservation is still recommended 
- when ordering udon, you can pick between the thin or the thick noodles.  
- you can get a smaller or regular portion, but the price is the same (so get the regular size!! Duh.) 
- the menu is mammoth with lots of food options, it's not just udon noodles 
- accepts credit cards 
- the udon is freshly made 

What we ordered: 
- Hamachi Carpaccio price $13 - five thick slices of hamachi fish topped with grated daikon, avocado in a yuzu kosho sauce.  The fish is buttery and oily, it just melts and breaks upon on your tongue.  
- Uni Crème Udon $21 - I ordered this dish with thick noodles.  The noodles are in an uni crème broth and it is topped with tobiko caviar, julienned shiso and delicate uni.  The bowl that the noodles came in is seriously big enough to be a tub for an 8-month infant.  While the noodles tasted fresh, it didn't have much flavor and relied heavily on the broth and other ingredients for flavor.  It was a very satisfying meal and the portions are unbelievably large! 
- Shrimp Tempura Udon $17 - comes with shrimp and veggie tempura. The dashi broth is rich but tasted a tad too sweet for my preference.  Once again, the udon was good but needed the dashi broth for flavor.

I am super into this place! I came here on a Saturday around 2pm and expected it to be crazy crowded but was pleasantly surprised to find it quite slow, which was more than okay with me.  

I ordered the shrimp tempura udon and the waiter informed me that the larger size was the same price as the regular so of course I upgraded. It was 24$ which is very expensive for Udon noodle soup, but it was so worth it. The soup was HUGE and filled with so many yummy things. All sorts of tempura, beef, pork, rice cake, etc. 

I cant wait to come back and explore the menu further. One tip I would give is split the large udon noodle and get an additional appetizer. Neither my friend who ordered the same or I finished our soups.

I could literally eat here every weekend. I've come multiple times with friends (they have big enough tables to seat groups of up to 6 (maybe more but I haven't tried) and take reservations which is helpful. I've also come on my own and had a good experience (quick service, nice servers, and sitting at the bar area helps reduce the #foreveralone feels :p). 

As a note on ordering, you have to choose normal or large size and noodle (thin or thick). They rec thick for hot bowls/soups and thin for cold but you can do whatever you want. Historically they have not allowed folks to take home/away any leftovers, not sure if that's still a policy. 

I typically do the large size of the cold uni udon (thin noodles) and finish it every time, but honestly there are so many great options on the menu (my friends love the hot/sour, and I personally have tried 1) truffle creme - amazing, and 2) sukiyaki - liked it though felt it was sweeter than it need to be). I've also really enjoyed a number of their apps as well as their rice bowls (katsu don was solid; rice texture was great and dish was very flavorful). Can't go wrong!

A huge fan of Tsurutontan Udon Noodles Brasserie. I have been here three times now and each time has been glorious. I fell in love with the Deluxe Curry bowl and have not regretted a bite of it. The bowl is MASSIVE, the broth is not too thick, it comes with shrimp tempura and chicken katsu (I think it's chicken :)). I love the noodles, they are perfectly cooked and allow for you to slurp them all up, just be careful to not make a mess on yourself or your neighbor. I have come with groups of friends so make sure you plan ahead and either make a reservation or come as soon as they open, this place fills up QUICK.

I love udon noodles, so going to this place to get a giant bowl of udon noodles was the best thing ever. I got the wagyu mushroom sukiyaki udon, which was amazing. The noodles were perfect, the broth was sweet, but not too overpowering, and the meat was tasty as well. The next time I'm in NY I will definitely be returning for another bowl!

I love that they don't charge for a large! Beware it is a lot of noodles. The Asian in me couldn't say no to free noodles and struggled to finish. The restaurant is trendy and beautiful. I love how they a few different sections. Book reservations online to avoid waiting. 

Apps:
My favorite was the pork belly. It was well braised to the perfect soft and tender texture. The tuna tartare cones were super cute and actually pretty good, but a bit pricey for what you're getting. The grilled duck breast was tender and flavorful. The Tatsuta Fried Chicken was definitely unique. It comes with a pink shibazuka tartar sauce. It was good but nothing special.  

Udon:
Get thick udon for hot broth and thin for cold udon. I've tried the Deluxe and Sukiyaki one. If you're getting hot udon, I would suggest these. I like the light but flavorful broth. Everything was good. My friend got the curry udon, which was good but gets overwhelming mid dish. You're having curry soup. I'm usually more of thick noodles kind of girl but my friend wanted to try the Zaru udon so we got the cold thin ones. So yummy! I loved it almost more than the hot udon.

The Udon noodles here are amazing!!  We ordered the Tatsuta fried chicken, to start off with. Sauce and chicken were delicious. Then we moved on to the Udon soups... we ordered duck, Uni, chicken and the special. I was in love with the Uni Udon. It was such a pleasant surprise to taste it. It was as rich or as sweet as you would expect. Just amazing flavors! We order fat Udon with all the soups. Just cooked perfect. You can upgrade to a large portion for the same cost, which is a extra handful of noodles but the same both amount. Definitely worth doing for the picture opportunity even if you can't finish. Love the deco and vibe also. Can't wait to go back.

My number one favorite Udon place. 

Literally can't get tired of saying "look at this giant bowl!"
And I want to try every dishes here. Even the mentaiko ankake udon that I said "ewwww" to, and turns out to be amazingly delicious.

Deliciouuuussss udon!! So many flavorful choices!! The prices are atrocious but you get what you paid for ($20-26 for a bowl)! But if you ask for a large, the price doesn't change and they give you more noodles in the same gigantic bowl! Get ready for a gigantic bowl of delicious tasty soup in your face!! 

You can also choose a thin or thick udon noodle. I prefer the thick one but the thin is still thicker than a spaghetti noodle! So I liked both! I got to try the Wagyu and mushroom sukiyaki, the truffle cream with crab soup and uni broth. All were SO DELICIOUS!!! Each had so much broth that I liked it all but after awhile I could see the sukiyaki being too sweet and the cream soups being to rich. But i LOVE truffle flavor and the truffle soup was soooo truffle tasting! i loved it! This place was so great and gave us extra bowls so we could all order our own as well as try others. 
I hope to come back with a couple of friend to try their other broths! As a special they had cold noodles and hot soup options. They have tons of other option besides soup but that was all we happen to try. Tip: Reserve on the app before coming! We called to make a reservation of 8 and it was a good choice!

[occasion] - Saturday lunch date with my girlfriend 'C'. 

[Service] - the staff members are super friendly! our waiter(s) were super helpful with explaining the origin of Tsurutontan and what their specialties were. The menu is crazy large and I have never seen so many options for noodles in one spot, so it took us some time to narrow down our picks, so definitely ask for recommendations. 

[Space | Looks] - the restaurant is actually more spacious than it appears from the outside, but dimly lit and the interior is modern and stylish. Pretty good setting for a casual meal with a friend or even date night.  

[Food | Drinks] - 

FOOD  // 
[+] Duck Udon with Thin Noodles - clear meat broth with heavy, salty flavors and my friend chose thin noodles for her bowl. 

[+] Creamy Uni Udon with Thick Noodles - Definitely my type of udon, not your conventional clear broth, but a thick consistency of cream and milk-based soup. bits and pieces of salty uni is hidden within the noodles. loved it. 

[Recommendations] - You have the choice of picking between thin or thick udon noodles, depending on what you crave. Either way the portion sizes are RIDICULOUSLY large, which is what they're known for. Same price for regular vs. large portion! So if you're hungry, why not. 

[FINAL THOUGHTS] - Sooo many options and you can never really go wrong with a warm (gigantic) bowl of noods. Would definitely make the trip back if I'm back in big apple.

Oh man oh man, this menu is absurd. It has a lot of options and tons of udon!! I came with a group of 8 girls total. They were able to take reservations for us. The pricing on the menu looks expensive, but the bowl is huge. If you're a female that can't eat that much (cause it's a lot of noodles), I highly advise splitting with another person.  Apparently if you order size Large, it is the same price as a regular, they just give more udon noodles!  The service there was great. The waiter helped us decide what to eat and was very helpful with all the questions we had.  You can select thin or thick noodles, which my friend who had suggested the place recommended thick.  My girlfriends and I all of course tried each noodle dish. I would have to say my favorite is the duck soup. I love duck. It wasn't too strong, the broth wasn't salty, the duck was nice and chewy. The truffle soup was too heavy, cream was thick, the smell of it was too strong, but then again, I'm not a huge huge fan of truffle. It was definitely super rich. My friend and I shared the creamy uni udon. This was not too heavy and on the lighter side. Although the broth could add a little more flavoring in it.

Really enjoyed this restaraunt! They make the Udon noodles in house, and they're so delicious. We first started by order a few appetizers - we got the Shrimp dumplings, Crispy Eggplant, and Toro sashimi. All three dishes were amazing but my favorites were the Crispy Eggplants because it was EXTREMELY crispy and flavorful with the dipping sauce they provide, and the Toro sashimi because it was BEYOND fresh. 

I ordered the crab & mushroom Udon bowl, and my friend ordered the sizzling seafood udon bowl. Both of ours was so amazing. The Crab & Mushroom Udon bowl had a creme broth that had great flavors. It also came in the LARGEST bowl ever! My friend's sizzling seafood bowl was also really really really flavorful and definitely another great option. 

The portions are so huge, I practically took the whole thing home cause I couldn't finish it all. 

The only downfall to our visit was the waitress misheard us when we asked her to pack to-go boxes for both of our meals, and only packed mine while accidentally throwing out my friend's (and naturally we were upset as that was a lot of food).
