Luckily the manager came up to us as we were signing the bill to ask how our experience was, and my friend mentioned what happened - he was EXTREMELY nice and offered my friend another full bowl of what she ordered to take home with her. Definitely made up for our experience so not going to take off any stars for that. 

The prices are kind of high, but you're in NYC and I still find it worth it.

Definitely something to try!

Why am I just finding out about this place?? 
I went in a group of three for dinner, and when we were being brought to a table toward the back, every single server we passed by greeted us. Also, the interior is huge-- so many more seats than we thought there would be, and there is even an upper level with more seats. 

Our server was so friendly and helpful. She explained the menu to us, which has a ton of options. The food is pretty pricey--  $15+ for each kind of udon, with most of them hovering around $18-21. I suppose it's normal-ish for NYC...

I got the chicken udon, while my friends got the deluxe. Extra noodles are free, so of course we ordered the extra noodles. The bowls are massive, the udon was delicious, and the broth was flavorful. I feel like it'll be perfect during the winter when I am craving a hot soup. Overall, the service was amazing and the food was great! Will definitely be returning.
Great flavor. I thought I didn't like udon noddle just never had good udon noddle before! Highly recommend.

Amazing. Quality is on pointtttt. Udon was delicious, so was the sushi. Even the ice cream was good. You would think a restaurant that advertised for its udon would only be good for its udon... but the sashimi was FRESH. Definitely recommending this place!!!

Very nice interior, seating arrangement is mostly communal style long table with dividers between parties of 2. 

*US Wagyu Udon: I love this broth. It's dashi style, very light and refreshing. the Wagyu beef is also very tender and comes out a bit rare so it can soak and cook in the broth. 

*Salmon carpaccio: nothing special. I couldn't get that much of the torched salmon. The sauce is a bit overpowering making it salty. 

*Soy garlic fried chicken: breading is good but way too salty!

They do have a lot of variety in udon, ramen, donburi options with fun appetizers as well. Price is moderate. Main reason for 3 star is based on service. Service is spotty and it takes forever to get seated even if you made a reservation. Only one hostess for a big restaurant and she seemed overwhelmed. I've dined three times and waited until I wrote my review because I wanted to give it the benefit of the doubt service will improve upon subsequent visits. But I was wrong! Best for parties of 2-4.

Love this place! Great design & ambience, Excellent service and amazing food!!! Highly recommended! 
We ordered ButaKakuni, Sukiyaki Udon, Tantán cold Noddles and Water cake for dessert. Everything was amazingly good. 
We got a wonderful service from Caryn and Mario, they were exceptional.
I definitely come back!!! One of my favorite restaurants.

Beautiful space, pretty reasonable prices considering the high quality ingredients. We like the fried chicken and pork belly appetizers, the udon dumplings were not too exciting. I really enjoyed my funky udon noodle (went for the cold after hearing the creme version was super heavy) and my 2 piece toro sashimi was a great fancy side dish.

FOOD:  The Udon Noodles were fine. It's edible.  Slightly better than frozen Udon Noodles. 
I have had Udon noodles many times in Kagawa, Japan so I try not to nit pick here.  

SERVICE: Service wasn't terrible.  The host staff are not so friendly.  Our waiter was not terrible though. Wasn't really around often enough so we couldn't order more drinks.  

ATMOSPHERE: The place is new so it looks nice in general.  It felt nice to be in the space until we received the big tacky looking menus with a ton of pictures.  HELLO BIG CHAIN RESTAURANT.  As someone already mentioned, it feels like a Japanese version of a TGIF or AppleBees.  Hence the 3-star rating for a typical franchise place.  Not worth the time or money.   What a shame. I really wanted to like them.

Been twice and each time blew me away.  Service was amazing from the moment you walked in until the second you stepped out.  The udon was out of the world with lots of options, too many to choose from I got pork broth and the uni, the former was my favorite.  I loved all the apps, I got the snow crab sushi and it was delightful.  Would go back 100X

Free upgrade to large. I don't even eat a lot, but the fact that it's the same price for a medium or large udon just makes me love this place irrationally. And their large is LARGE. Like "bowls the size of your face" large. Usually my group of friends will get n/2 large udons and a couple appetizers and leave feeling satisfied and very happy. I'm also a ramen over udon person any day, but this is the one place in New York where I'll come just to eat udon.

Right off the bat: one star removed for the little fruit fly found in my soup. Didn't get a photo of it as it ruined my appetite, despite discovering it at the end of my meal. 

Other than that, this place is cool and has delicious udon noodle soup (perhaps it was the fruit fly flavor). 

The decor is gorgeous: vast, different feel in each section, cultural, elegant, chic, trendy - it's a pretty place! If you order noodles, you'll get your food in a giant bowl, giant spoon with regular sized chopsticks on a tiny pebble that you may or may not knock over by accident. 

Annie was a great waitress and extra helpful. Ordered the wagyu mushroom sukiyaki udon noodle ($24). It's a pricey, sweet dashi broth. It's not overwhelmingly sweet - just the right touch. Variety of mushroom including enoki and oyster, which is my favorite, however I originally thought there would be actual oyster in it, not realizing it was the mushroom they were referring to. There's also napa cabbage, wagyu beef(wish there was a bit more for the price) and loads of fresh, hand made udon. You can truly taste the difference of fresh noodles - divine. 

Wanted to try the fried chicken but didn't want the full appetizer so we ordered the side dish which is over rice for an extra $3. It's four pieces of nicely fried chicken, light bredding, which has a dash of spict sauce over it. It could have a bit more seasoning to it for flavor but guess that's the purpose of the spicy. 

Overall, good experience. Dead fruit fly in my soup really bothered me at the end. I did want to try the other dishes they had such as don buri and the sizzling hot plates but perhaps I'll wait a bit.

Let's start off with this place has very nice ambiance. The decor and atmosphere is great - HOWEVER the service was not nor was the food. The server forgot two things we ordered, and charged extra for chili sauce that was much needed on the tasteless dishes. Also the dishes came out all at different times. Would not come back.

I wasn't completely blown away by the udon here, but I must applaud their top-notch decor/ambience: cozy, intimate, and trendy. 

My friend and I both ordered bowls of udon in large (regular and large are both the same price) and shared a spicy tuna tartare cone appetizer. I picked the duck udon with thick noodles and my friend got the deluxe. The udon noodles were average and I would say comparable to the many frozen brands you can pick up at the market. Broth was flavorful, but lukewarm. That was a huge disappointment. Piping hot soup is an absolute must when it comes to soup noodles! My friend and I were also surprised by their portion sizes and did appreciate how they actually meant it when they called it "large". However, a part of me can't help but think that I would rather have smaller portions for lower prices. Rather than ordering a bowl of udon per person, I would highly recommend trying out several of their sides/appetizers and sharing one large bowl of udon.

1 star for good food. Negative stars for service. We were a group of 5 for lunch on Saturday. 

First our server took forever to take our order and put up his finger to tell us to wait. Then they brought out the wrong order TWICE. Then when one of us asked for a normal metal spoon in lieu of their soup spoons to eat the rice the server's help said there's no such thing and she proceeded to tell our server and they laughed at us from the corner. Then our server came back to "check in" with us acting like he didn't just laugh at us in my line of sight. He said there's no other spoon options. 

Few minutes later, the table next to us get 2 of the exact spoons we asked about. When we asked the server why we couldn't get those spoons he said he didn't know that's what we wanted. What do you mean you didn't know that a normal spoon is what we wanted......... he still refused to give us such spoon. 

A man in a suit kept walking back and forth looking at us and making us very uncomfortable. So I asked him if he was the GM and he said he was so I explained why we were upset. He looked at me blankly barely listening or caring and simply responded "I'll talk to him". No apologies- just walked away with no care in the world. 

After we paid another GM came out and said that guy was not the GM but that he was. What a mess!!! So he lied? 

As we were leaving all the staff stopped talking and stared at us. Word travels fast when you make fun of your customers in the open right?

4.4 stars.
Am here with friends for his bday lunch, we order tofu, fried chicken, and pork w/eggs, which is pretty much like Japanese local taste! Especially the fried chicken, it's awesome! Creamy uni iron is good too. :)

Been here two times; both on Happy Hour menu! I must say, everything tasted delicious except the soy fried chicken! The fried chicken is simply too salty, and reminded me of chinese food (General Tso Chicken). 

Other than that, I do highly recommend this place! I can't wait to go back, and try their regular menu. I heard great stuff about their Ramen too!

The uni and seared Wagyu beef was soooo yummy. 
Dyako Dan - was pretty good, the dashi broth is good. Still think udon west is better.
Tan tan udon- my waiter told me it was a 2-3 on the spicy scale (out of 10). Lies. At least a 4-5. I've had better tan tan udon, I would try something else next time. 
Uni udon, very creamy. Reminded me of a clam chowder. The uni quality is good here but I wouldn't get this again, felt it lacked in overall uni flavor

My friend invited me out to this Udon place because she says it's "authentic." So of course, being Japanese, I had to give it a try! She had the sizzling sukiyaki udon (yum!) and I got the creamy mentaiko udon (also yum!)

Pros:
- Very expansive menu so lots to choose from! They have pictures for every item so you don't get lost in all the wordy descriptions! It's all right there to choose from
- You get to upsize for FREE! When you order, they ask if you want a small or large at no extra cost. Basically, you just get double the portion of the udon noodles, but NOT the fixings.
- They take reservations
- Cute ambience! It's very modern/industrial/Japanese. Clean straight lines, exposed concrete, bamboo wood workings
- Very friendly staff! Our waiter was so warm and also so happy to help me with the menu since I was new. He also gave stellar recommendations.
-Happy hour ALL DAY! But only at the bar 

Cons:
- Pricey. This isn't what I'm used to since udon is traditionally supposed to be comfort food your mom whips you up really quick. However, for the portion, the culinary creativeness, as well as authentic traditional flavors, I don't mind the price at all! My bill ended up being $25 after tax and tip.
- Gets very crowded. Even with our reservation, we had to wait a bit. However, there seems to be quick turnarounds with the tables. Even though it gets busy, tables open up pretty quickly. However, it seemed like the bar was wide open.
- Not good for dates. The layout is very open, and as per New York, space is limited and you'll probably sit really close to another table. It's very loud so you'll end up yelling, which can get awkward when you have a couple to your left and a couple to your right, all yelling as well...

Overall, I think I had my fix after one visit. Don't get me wrong- the food was SO good and I had a pleasant experience... but I prefer quieter places to eat and enjoy my company.

Excellent service and very lively ambience. This was my second time coming here with a couple of friends and food was still good and they seated us right away for our reservation without any problems. Because we had ordered several appetizers before the meal it was quite filling and we couldn't finish the whole bowl but still very fresh and worth the wait!

Huge portion size and great tasting! What I love is the fact that you do not have to be limited to menu styles. You have choices between the noodles (thick or thin) and cold or hot. The prices are pretty reasonable in my opinion considering it's such an incredibly large portion (~$14+) I usually get very tingly when there is a lot of sodium or msg, but did not get a reaction this time. The spicy tuna tartare was so yummy! The tartare was in a deliciously crispy cone and presented in a cute salt box. The fish was fresh and just oh so yummy ($12 for 4). The Tsurutontan delux was $24 but it was so good! It's good for two meals if you have leftovers but it had so much in it. I would share this with another person honestly but again, delicious and hearty. Would definitely recommend

Tasty bang-for-your buck udon.

Came here for an early Saturday lunch with a friend (around 11am) and had no problem getting a seat.

We had the grilled duck breast appetizer to start which was well seasoned and juicy.

I had the chicken and shrimp tempura udon - large size. Tasty mild flavour and a generous serving size (I couldn't say no to a large when the price is the same as a regular!!)

We also had cocktails which were original, tasty and strong! 

Will be back to try the creamy and beef udons

The udon texture is outstanding - hard to describe...like a nice firm squishiness? I ordered the yamakake udon and the broth and egg were nicely seasoned together. It's a very large portion that will definitely fill you up.
Noodles are tender, broth delectable and sea urchin is out of this world earthy, fresh and a perfect pairing.  Goes well with sake.

My husband and I had a great experience here. They have an expansive and diverse menu, which is hard to come by with udon on the east coast. I had one of the spicy noodle soups and he had one of the more traditional udon bowls (sorry, don't recall exact names). We also ordered some tempura and sake. Everything was delicious and we left with extremely full bellies. Our server was so sweet and attentive. despite being somewhat large, I found the layout very romantic and cozy. My husband and I were side by side at one of the long tables that is divided in the middle. It felt very private even though we were really in the middle of the restaurant. Would definitely return here.

I really didn't know what I was expecting, but it was good! I ordered something off of the cold noodle menu, the one with the tempura fried assortment-- sorry I forget the name! I got the regular noodle and regular portion, and it was still a lot of food. Very family/casual atmosphere. I want to come back and try their other noodles and donburi

I came here when I was sick with lack of taste buds. Ordered Uni crème udon and the truffle crème with crab and mushroom. They come in big bowls and ladles were use as spoons. Even with my lack of taste buds the food was very good. The Uni was tasty without being fishy. My favorite is still the truffle crème. The atmosphere is very nice, can be a date place. Would try other stuff on the menu the next time I come back.

FREE UPGRADE TO BIGGER BOWL PEOPLE! The udon was worth waiting for. We had to wait over an hour to be seated (6 people) and another 30 minutes for the dish. We laughed hysterically when we saw the size of the bowl and were so happy that the restaurant charged no fee to upgrade to bigger bowl. I had prime beef udon ($19) . The meat was very soft and flavorful. I couldn't finish the bowl because the portion was simply too large (no kidding) Will definitely comeback!

Wow huge fan of this place. Ambience is hip and lively, and food is AMAZING. Definitely try the wagyu uni sushi - it's a bit pricey at $22, but so worth. The wagyu and uni just melt in your mouth. Also ordered the seared salmon and snow crab - fresh ingredients and perfect complementary flavours. Definitely get the udon of course - try the deluxe one, the egg mixed with dashi is so good. The noodles could have been a bit chewier, and I actually like Raku's noodles a bit more, but I think overall the flavours and soup at Tsurutontan is better. Will definitely be back to try their other foods!

Wow the ramen here was delicious. My boyfriend and I were in NY and decided to give this ramen place a try. We're fairly picky when it comes to Asian food but this place was amazing. 

Food + service + ambiance = A+

This place for me is like heaven. Udon is one of my favorite dishes ever, and this place offers so many kinds of udon in huge portions. I ordered the beef udon with egg and I finished it, but it was a struggle for me since the portion (a large is the same price as a regular) was bigger than the size of a basketball. So much food but so good! 

The noodles were perfectly chewy, the broth was super flavorful, the beef was tender. As someone who grew up in Tokyo, I was pleasantly surprised that this udon was so delicious.

Great service, spacious seating (2 floors!)/lots of privacy especially for a restaurant in the city. This is definitely a good place to catch up with friends, take a date, etc. as it has a nice atmosphere and not too loud to talk at the same time.
It tastes amazing and I love the texture of their noodles but unfortunately they use msg hence only 3 stars.  The decor is lovely and the wait staff are super friendly!

Love the food here but service is what's most outstanding. Our waiter James was extremely friendly and efficient.  He  check on us at a perfect time interval. Recommendations would be tuna tartar cone, caviar udon, truffle creme udon, lamb chop w spicy miso, scallop sushi and wagyu beef tartar. I would definitely go back again.

Udon is one of my ultimate comfort foods and I'm so glad I got to try this in my visit to NYC. The udon has the perfect consistency and the soup (I had the tan tan udon) was absolutely luscious. It was just the right amount of spicy so that you felt the kick, but could also pretty easily down the entire bowl. I didn't have to keep drowning the flavor out with water which is my usual peeve. The onsen/slow cooked egg was also lovely and was an excellent decisions as an add on for extra mmmmmm.

The atmosphere is also lovely, feeling cool and energized at the same time. I went with my sister, but I would take friends here, go on a date with someone if I was really interested here, EVERYONE. The wait time was less than 30 min and there was shopping to do in the area because they will text you when the table is ready.

I highly recommend this place :D Let it wrap your soul in happy!

I loved everything about my experience. 
The ambience is super hip and creative; it's a little bit dim inside but the walls are decorated with interesting patterns and textures. The restaurant is bigger than it looks from the outside. Once you squeeze past the narrow bar, there are more expansive dining areas.
The udon noodles were fantastic. We tried three kinds-- the duck udon (more of a traditional clear broth),  the hot and sour udon (loaded with mushrooms, ground beef, eggplant, etc.), the tan tan udon (with a spicy basil broth). The large and small portions are the same price, so why not get the large? We were all happily full after the meal. 
Everything is a bit pricey though. Expect to pay about $25/person per entree.

I am usually a fan of most asian soups - ramen, pho, shabu, etc. but after trying this place I've learned that I am not much of an udon person. Not that the meal was bad - I just don't think the type of broth is particularly my preference.

Their menu offers a ton of options from curry plates, cold and hot broth udon bowls, donburi plates and appetizers. I tried out the US Wagyu and Mushroom Sukiyaki broth which is supposed to be a little sweeter than the dashi (clear fish broth with a blend of soy sauce). It was filled with plenty of meat and mushrooms topped with a perfectly cooked egg.

We also ordered the spicy tuna tartare cone which tasted similar to a hand roll but in a crispy wonton like cone. At the bottom of the cone was an avocado paste/puree...great option for an appetizer!

The bowls come in either a regular size or large, which the only difference between the two is you'll get more noodles in the large. Also, you have the choice of choosing thin or thick noodles, which they recommend the thick for hot soup and thin for cold.

Service was fairly quick and our waiter checked on us often. The place was loud and dimly lit, but definitely had a trendy atmosphere. While everything was good, I just don't think udon is typically my choice of noodles/broth but if udon is your jam I think you'd be very pleased with their options here!

Wow was so happy to try this place! The udon noodles are so fresh and taste great and I love the broth! The decor is really nice but heads up that the place can get pretty noisy during dinner. I love that the both sizes, small and large, are the same price and you can always ask for more noodles without additional cost! You'll never leave this place any less than full :) 

It's really popular, so definitely worth putting down a reservation in advanced!

From the outside, I'm thinking this is going to be a typical noodle place but I was wrong. This is the fanciest noodle spot I've been into and the ambience is very modern and unique which I really like. I was skeptical about the Udon noodles cause I know a spot that serves really good udon noodles, but it was actually better than I thought. It's served on a massive bowl and they give you a huge spoon to eat with which I thought was funny. But I would definitely come here again and bring along my friends. It's a really nice noodle spot.

SOOO AMAZING!! 10/10 best udon I've had in NYC by a LANDSLIDE! It was so delicious and totally worth the cost. You get SO much noodles and the broth is so delicious. I got the duck noodles $18 and there was a good amount of duck and meatballs. It wasn't too salty so it was easy for me to finish the entire bowl. My friend got the wagyu udon $24. The wagyu beef was crazy good-- super soft and very sweet. His broth was a little too sweet for my taste and he said it left a sticky feeling on his mouth but still pretty good. Loved the udon! It was perfectly cooked and just the right amount of chewy. The raindrop cake was interesting. We didn't know what to expect. It was not very sweet but very good with the ice cream it came with. I liked the peanut crumbles but not a fan of the weird sticky syrup that we were supposed to pour on top. Our waitress (Valentina) was very sweet and attentive. So satisfied overall and will definitely be back soon!! Try to go before 7 if you don't have a reservation. Otherwise it gets VERY packed very fast.
Food here is average and pricey. I didn't like the truffle with crab & mushroom udon, the sauce tasted weird and was way too heavy.

I have been to Tsurutontan numerous times with our first time at their Roppongi location in Tokyo. It's usually very busy (every location in the world). We were so thrilled they opened in NYC. It's a bit pricy but it's the WHOLE package. 

Yesterday i went with my 7 month old and another mommy friend with her 10 month old. We made a reservation thru Resy, and were quickly seated at 2pm. It was emptier than usual since it wasn't peek time but still good amount of patrons. The servers seated us promptly and offered us water, we ordered, the food came and everyone was super helpful with moving things on the table so it would fit (our hands were full of babies so couldn't do much). They helped serve us our udon into smaller bowls and through the meal came back several times to help us. The servers were respectful (allowed us to breast feed and change nappies), kind, andn really working hard ot make sure all of the patrons had everything they needed to enjoy their meal. 

This is what going out to a restaurant SHOULD feel like. :) So glad you guys are here, you are much much appreciated! 

(forgot to mention how delicious the udons are, skinny, thick, regular, extra portion, whatever) my favorite is the Truffle creme with crab and mushroom.... YUM! 

Please add a changing table into one of your bathrooms! It would be so helpful!

Ok I'm probably biased because I love udon. NEVERTHELESS, I wish I could give this place more stars! I'm usually hard pressed for a solid 5 star review but this place was mind blowing.

Beginning with the service. We had an awesome waiter (shoutout to Andy) who knew the menu very well and actually engaged us in conversation- bonus points from the start. 

For the actual eating bit, we started out with a drink- the Matcha on the Moon. Not too sweet, subtle blend of flavors, delicious! We also got the Sea and Truffle appetizer, which was a great start. When they brought out the roll the aromatic truffle smell immediately followed. It was just a great time. The wasabi also tasted pretty fresh!

Now onto the best part: udon! My sister got the Uni Crème Udon, and I got the Truffle Crème with Crab and Mushroom. They were both so delicious, we couldn't pick which one we liked better. Usually I prefer lighter broths but the flavor of the broths were so phenomenal, I don't regret going with a heavier option. The flavors blended together seriously seamlessly, and the balance was to die for. You'd think an udon with Parmesan and truffle oil would really be too much, but it was the exact opposite, I couldn't get enough. Also, surprisingly, it wasn't as heavy as I'd expected. It was nowhere near pasty, and not even as heavy as a light chowder or bisque. Really just a great balance of everything. The noodles were also great- cooked perfectly! Not too hard, and just the right amount of chewy. I could go on and on about how great the food was but you get the point. The cherry on top of this magnificent cake is the fact that you can upgrade to a large bowl at no additional cost, no joke. 

Over all, I don't really have anything bad to say. The worst part about Tsurutontan is that if you crave it you'll have to make reservations in advance or anticipate a really long wait. Is it worth it? Totally.

A solid udon restaurant with udon bowls bigger than the size of your head. There are so many choices on the menu,  you would keep coming back because you want to try them all! There are different types of broths, classic, sweet, curry and you can also have your udon cold. They also give you an option of thick or thin noodles, however I've only had the thick because I love the texture of thick udon. Here's the best part: you can upgrade to the large, with more udon, FREE OF CHARGE!! 

Excited to go back and try every single item on their menu!!

got their best seller I believe called tan tan and my god was it delicious. Huge portions and they provide extra noodles at no additional cost, PLUS they're okay with people sharing. Instead of the ground pork I substituted it for duck for a charge of $6. Noodles Are made in house and you can definitely taste the quality. You're given two options: thick or thin noodles. I got thin and was extremely satisfied. 

Great atmosphere, loudish music, nice decor and clean restaurant all around. I'd come back if I lived here but sadly I don't.

I love udon and was excited to try this place! Their menu offers so many udon options it was so hard to pick just one! I chose a classic beef udon and my husband got the Tsuruton Creme Deluxe. We were curious to see what a creme broth would be like. We also got the Spicy Tuna Tartare Cones to start off with.  Also recommend to get the large portion, its free of charge! You get more udon noodles with it. We both got the thick noodles. 
When the udons came out, the portions were huge!! The creme broth by husband said tasted like clam chowder and the seafood/chicken were all cooked to perfection, everything melted in your mouth, my husband was a fan. The classic broth was great too, it did have a bit of a sweet flavor to it. I definitely want to come back to check out the other udons and the donburi dishes! They also offer Lady M desserts, but we were too full to try.

Really good udon! Comes very close to as eating it in Japan! Their prices are a bit high but you are paying for the fancy restaurant decor, and their noodles that are made in house. The portion size is lovely and you can pick between thick or thin udon noodles. I had ordered the sukiyaki soup based which was a bit salty for my taste and rather have the sukiyaki broth to be a bit sweeter but the soup still tasted yummy and flavorful. I would come back to try their dashi based broth.

My family and I enjoyed the Tsurutontan Deluxe noodles (with additional noodles at no extra cost) as our first meal and a bowl of rice with some beef (that costs only like $1 or something if you get it in additional to a meal like a noodle bowl). Will definitely come back to try other food!
Love love udon noodles and ramen/soup of really any kind. The broth here felt sickly sweet and had a strange taste. We ordered 3 different types and didn't like any of them. Wouldn't come back.

The tan tan udon is my favorite udon I've ever had. I'm not usually a huge fan of udon because of the clearer/lighter soups (I want soups that PUNCH ME IN THE FACE). But the tan tan udon's soup is super flavorful, but not heavy or too spicy so the soup is easy and nice to sip on. The udon noodles are doughy and chewy which is my favorite. Honestly I could've finished the entire dish, but just stopped because I have amazing self control. 

You can choose to get the larger or smaller size udon, but since it's the same price why would you get the smaller size??? You can also take the leftovers home, so it's really a no brainer. 

I actually wasn't going to write a review for this place, but it's been weeks since I've gone and I've been craving it incessantly since. Definitely a meal I remembered and am looking to repeat!

Sooo yummy! I'm from LA and I would liken this place to a fancier version of Marugame Monzo in Little Tokyo. I was visiting a friend and she suggested this place and it did not disappoint!

I got the cold uni udon with thin noodles and I actually really loved them! I was told the thick was better but I think I liked the thin ones more :) The uni was also sooo buttery and fresh and the sauce was delicious. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS. I tried my friends curry udon with thick noodles and the curry was delicious. Not too overpowering but very tasty. 

We did have to wait about an hour on a Saturday afternoon for a party of 4 but I thought it was worth it! The reason I'm docking a star is because the hostess wasn't very friendly or accommodating and acted as if we were bothering her. Which was weird because that's her job. Other than that, the service was great and I highly recommend!

We have been here a few times and it never disappoints us!  The bowls are huge, but we end up finishing.  Service is the best.  Kulthiwadi (aka Al) is our favorite server.  She's quick, attentive, and friendly.  She has great EQ. 

We recommend this restaurant.

I found the udon broth to be underwhelming. The udon noodles itself were a nice texture but the broth of the uni creme and waygu udon weren't that flavorful. My friends had the curry and spicy ground pork udon and those were a bit more flavorful. 

I guess I'm more of a ramen person where the tonkatsu broth is richer and saltier than udon broth.
Soo yummy!! tan tan udon is amazing best I ever had!! I'm in love in this place!!!

The facade is deceiving. From the outside it look like a small and simple japanese restaurant. And when we stepped-in... lo and behold! Its a one damn fancy and extraordinary japanese udon noodle house.

I was brought in here by a co-worker to co-celebrate mine and her birthday. I like the feel of the ambiance of this place. The interior design is something else, a mix of traditional and modern styling. 

The waiter approached our table, introduced himself and ask us politely if this is our first time in TsuruTonTan. Me, yup. She, nope. He then explained to us the food in their menu. Which one is spicy, which is not. What are the dish composed of, and how it will be served.

I always love udon and ramen but on this visit I went for a very simple beef udon noodle soup. Couple minutes later, here comes my udon... served in this huge (not exagerrating) bowl that resembles that of those modern bathroom vessel sink. I find it cool
though. 

First bite on the udon... I liked it! I think their
noodles are thicker compared to the other japanese restaurant I go to. The beef is good and overall the dish wasn't salty or has any overpowering taste.

I will definitely go back to TsurunTonTan in the near future and I highly recommend this place.

The appetizers tastes pretty good, but nothing special of the udon itself. There are some special flavor but not going well with noodles. Plus the portion is way too big. This is probably it's selling point but I see wasting food. I wouldn't go back for 2nd time.

Absolutely my favorite place in NYC right now. Before you even start eating, you'll know the place is good by the fact that you'll be completely surrounded by Japanese people who eat there on a regular basis. Fresh tastes, large portions and very reasonable  prices that I thought no longer existed in Manhattan. The best noodles you'll ever taste outside of Japan.

I have always been a noodle lover so naturally, I've been to Tsurutontan countless times. Every time I've been there, I had a good experience. I would recommend making a reservation for dinner because it tends to get really busy, but grabbing lunch shouldn't be a problem. As people have said, $20 for a bowl of udon is a bit on the pricier side, but it is totally worth it. I really like their truffle udon but its the hot and sour udon that keeps me coming back. I don't opt for the larger option even though it's the same price because the regular size is the perfect amount of food for me, but if you're really hungry or a guy, you may need to get the bigger bowl. I also love that the waiters are so attentive. Couldn't recommend it more!

They serve super yummy food in town. Every dish has a blend of Asian taste that makes it amazing. Mild sweetness, sour and drop of sesame oil makes me in loved to the store. Staff are very accommodating and I feel very at home. Highly recommended!

Udon comes in thick and thin, with my preference being thick, and regular and large size (same price).   The seasonal crab and mentai caviar ankake udon was very good with delicate flavors whereas the sizzling sukiyaki udon was a good contrast with robust flavors.  The bite size tuna tartare appetizer was also good.

Prices are not really worth the quality.

Three friends and I came in for dinner on a Tuesday night at 6:30. We didn't have to wait but the place is pretty big, and I'm not sure how busy it gets on a Friday/Saturday night. Service was quick - the food came out pretty quickly after we ordered. I went with the Uni Cream Udon in hot broth. There was one piece of uni on top in the middle, and that was pretty much it. The broth didn't really taste like udon, more like cream. In fact, it was a little too creamy and heavy. It should have been called 'creamy udon with a singular piece of uni on top' instead. It definitely wasn't worth the $24.

Their other menu items seemed pretty pricey as well and I'm not exactly sure why. It's not like Tsurutontan is fine dining. IMO, you can get the same quality for a lower price tag elsewhere.

$20 for Udon noodles that probably cost 50 cents? Well worth it 

Great vibe and awesome table settings. REAL polished rocks as chopstick holders (as seen in picture) and BIG metal spoons to complement their BIG a** bowls! 

I hate shrimp  as I think theyre like bugs and they clean the dirt off the ocean bottom. So shoutouts to my dude MARCO, #1 employee of the restaurant, for switching out my tempura shrimp with tempura chicken in my CURRY KATSU COMBO
The portions and the taste is the same as Japan! A bit more pricier but these are some damn good udon. And beautiful interior as well, as well as the Japanese style customer service was on point!

"How could i miss this place?" I kept asking myself over and over again after i had dinner at Tsurutontan. I could say that generally i am not a fan of udon but the skinny udon here was the best udon i have ever had! I also enjoyed the fancy water cake. It not only looked nice but also offered a variety of textures! Service here was terrific! I will definitely be back again!

Overall, a decent place if you're around the area and craving udon. It's a bit on the pricier end, with a dish being at least $20/bowl. But you can ask for the large size (vs. regular) and its the same price. The large bowl has more noodles, but the same amount of broth, veggies, meat, whatever you ordered. 

Inside is nicely decorated but a bit dim. They have pebbles as chopstick holders but the pebbles are really tiny so in my opinion, they don't really hold the chopsticks well. The bowl is really pretty though. 

I ordered the US wagyu and mushroom udon which was one of their top sellers. The broth was too sweet but the udon noodles were perfect. They had the perfect chewiness and texture and you mostly pay the high price for the great noodles. The bowl had a good amount of beef and mushrooms. 

p.s. They charge you $1.50 if you ask for spicy oil/garlic.

Not a fan of Udon but U Don Know about this place!  I thoroughly enjoyed the long thick chewy and doughy noodles. The noodles were so fresh and chewy, perfect to slurp with the warm smooth broth. 

I ordered the curry udon. Although I think the pork katsu and shrimp tempura lost some of its crunch in the broth, it was still very flavorful and just gave me all the more reason to eat it faster! I tried the wagyu udon also and I thought the broth was a tad on the sweeter side but the veggies were a nice texture element with the chewy noodles. 

I don't think I can eat udon anywhere else ever again...

The only udon place I know in the city is Udon West but I never been. Im not a big fan of udon but after coming here at Tsurutontan, I m loving it now! I came here twice, once for my friend's farewell dinner and second time, I brought my colleagues here and they enjoyed it!

There are so many udon options to choose from. I wanted to try them all! Kyle was a great waiter and very helpful. He recommened us couple of things and we love it!

We started with Spicy tuna tartare cones and sushi (forgot the name)! Spicy tuna tartare cones is a must to get, it is nice and crunchy.

We ordered US Wagyu Shabu Udon and Uni and Ikura Udon, both with regular thick udon. The udon is so chewy and fresh.  Love both of the udon. The beef is very tender and not too chewy, just perfect. I usually do not like the soup/broth but the broth was just light, flavorful and not  salty. You can ask for extra noodle with no extra charge. If you're feeling hungry, why not!!@!! 

I definitely will come back to try the curry udon and the donburi dishes. I will definitely bring more friends and recommend my friends here! Im a happy girl

Based on everyone's reviews, I was really excited to try the udon here. Unfortunately, it didn't live up to the hype for me. I went for my friend's birthday so I treated him to some lovely udon. Didn't make a reservation - went at 6:30PM and there were seats available. It was sort of hard to get in though. The wait staff was quick and friendly and explained everything when she found out it was our first time there. I ordered the duck udon and my friend ordered the sukiyaki udon. Before our noodles came, our wait staff bought out huge spoons for our humongous bowls. 

The wait time for food was okay. And having a bowl bowl to take photos of was definitely fun. My duck and meatball udon with an onsen egg was good. I liked the thick noodles paired with the duck. However, for my meal being almost $60, for 2 bowls of udon, I expected a little bit more.

Actually really loved this place! One of the best udon I've had! I went to Raku and some of my friends told me that Tsurutontan is so much better. I 100% agree! They have a variety of things on their menu including sushi, appetizers and different kinds of udon. The best part is that you can upgrade to the large bowl at no extra cost! I really wish I saved the picture to show how big it was, literally bigger than the size of my face haha. 

On to the food. Solid 4 stars. We shared the beef udon, the spicy tuna cones, sea & truffle and the salmon & snowcrab roll. Everything was pretty good! I'm not sure if the spicy tuna cones were worth the price but it was an interesting concept. The salmon & snowcrab roll hit the spot as well! The beef udon was light but I was sick so the broth was perfect for me. I would want to try the creme udon and carpaccio next time.

I'm giving the extra star because the service here is awesome - our waiter was very attentive. Although my friend was still not there by the time they had seats for us, the hosts in the front were really accommodating! We were able to be seated within 5 minutes.

I've been here a handful of times and every time i visit, whether I am with a large group or a smaller group, I always get great service and best of all delicious food! 

The noodles typically come in HUGE bowls and ginormous portions as well. There is an option for you to havethick or thin noodles (thick for hot soups and thin for cold noodles usually is the recommendation), also extra noodles at no extra charge too! The waiter will get you seated and explain to you which noodles are their popular ones and which one is their personal preference if you wish. This is awesome since the menu is has many many options for you. 
Their appetizers great for sharing like the tuna cones, fried chicken, and can't forget about the shishito peppers. Their drinks are also pretty good so I say give it a try!

LOVE this place!  the noodles are delicious and the portions are huge!  you can add extra noodles at no cost.  We tried the spicy tuna tartare cones and they were delicious.  Would definitely go again for their giant bowls of noodles.
One of the best meals I've ever had. The stone pot udon is amazing. It's what udon dreams are made of. Really great friendly staff as well!

Totally in love with this restaurant! I want to come back till I've had everything on the menu. The bar drinks are super inexpensive for NY and for the area. I highly recommend sitting there and grabbing a few drinks before having dinner or lunch. The noodle bowls are bigger than your head so go hungry!

It was a semi-cold night, and two friends wanted something warm and delicious. The pair of friends also wanted sushi so where else to go besides TUNB for the occasion? The sushi was delicious. However, the uni udon was a letdown. We both ordered the uni cream udon, hers was thick udon whereas mine was thin. The piece of uni was perfect but everything else in the bowl was sub-par, from soup flavor to noodle texture to pairing of the ingredients...it was not a bowl I'd reorder. I'll revisit but I will order another flavor of udon. And not the thin type. 

Oh, and one last thing before I submit this review: the waitress mistakenly added two drinks to my bill when we didn't order them. She rectified it after I informed her, but imagine those who don't normally review the bill before paying...

Dined here after book marking this place, and after a windy day venturing the city we were glad to have some soupy noodle goodness to warm us up!

We ordered the sukiyaki beef buns, spicy tempura prawns, US wagyu beef sukiyaki udon . . All dishes were delicious and very filling!
  Portions of the udon was very big! Probably the biggest bowl of udon I've ever had! And was generously filled with cabbage, udon, mushrooms. And wagyu beef! Broth resembles the traditional sukiyaki sweet broth that I love. Great stuff and highly recommend! 

Spicy tempura prawns, the batter was beautiful! Light and crispy however the prawns were over cooked for my liking but the sauce made up for the dryness which was nicely flavoured and good heat. The sukiyaki buns were very good, beef was drowned in the typical sukiyaki broth and leaked into the bun making the middle of the bun mushy and break apart but other than that it was a great way of eating!! 

A bit pricey but portion size and generosity of ingredients make us for it. I would definitely come back when I'm in NYC again
Awesome uni udon, and awesome waitress, server and host. The pork belly wasn't as tasty or tender as I thought; it wasn't completely warm- but overall udon

My friend and I waited for almost an hour to be seated, not because it was ridiculously busy, but because the hostess forgot to put my friend's name down, so by the time we got on the list, we were at the bottom of the waiting list. Although that hostess screwed up the beginning of our night, the food was great. My friend had the uni udon and she loved it. I ordered one of the spicy udons, and it was indeed spicy but sooooo good. For dessert, we order their Lady M cakes- red velvet and matcha crepe. I didn't like the red velvet- it tasted really dry and bitter. I loooved the matcha though.

Loved this place.  Great ambiance and quality foods!  My girlfriend went to this place 2 times in this past 2 months and we decided to let me try this place.  They had a professional seating system that would text us when the table was about to be ready. 

We were told to wait 30 minutes but luckily they were ready in 20 minutes. I had a hard choice choosing between the udon choices but ended up with the tsuruton curry deluxe and tsurutontan deluxe. Both of these are some of the restaurant's top sellers. 

We started with the spicy tuna tartare.  It was 4 tiny cones filled with spicy tuna and avocado. Don't let the size discourage you! It was really fresh tuna so it was worth to complement our udon meals. 

The udons were both so delicious since they had so items inside the bowls.  They offered 3 types of meats ranging from pork tonkatsu, shrimp tempura, sliced beef, and chicken. The cool thing about this place that I noticed was that they had a set price and it wouldn't matter if you chose regular size or large size. So I'd personally always choose LARGE!

One thing I have to criticize is that the chicken isn't as good.  I sorta wished they didn't include it all together.  It felt like it was a lower quality ingredients and should have not been included in the tsurutontan deluxe all together.  It lacked flavor and likely wasn't marinaded or enough.

Cute decor with delicious, mind-blowing food to match.  Large and regular bowls are the same price so why not get the large?  Both equally delicious.  Everything was made well.  The waitress was detailed in explaining the menu and each dish's subtle difference which was helpful for a first-timer.  Then there's the bar.  Creative drinks that were subtly strong and a great place to take in the amazing decor.  Would definitely recommend putting in a reservation ahead of time.

Easily the best udon in NYC.  Having lived in Japan, I'm a purist when it comes to good udon, so I always get cold udon, with simple toppings.  Can't speak to the more unusual udon dishes ... Which seem strange to me.  I also love how you have the option of getting large portion for no extra cost.  Definitely worth going out of your way to eat here.

I LOVE IT!!! Arguably my favorite restaurant in the city!

My friend introduced me to this restaurant and I loved it so much!! I was meeting up with a group a friends a few days later and came back with them! Tsurutontan offers classic udon broths, however, the really specialize in unique types of broths. My favorite is the Truffle Creme with Crab and Mushroom ($22) because it has such a flavorful taste and has a generous amount of crab and mushroom in it. The Hot and Sour Udon is another great choice when I want something spicer.

This place is always a great place if you have big, hungry stomaches to fill and satisfy. The wait time, especially for bigger groups, can get lengthy, so I would recommend making a reservation on their website.

-- 
taste / 5
aesthetics / 5
vibe / 5
service / 5
price for quality / 5
OVERALL / 5

I've seen this place so many times and was super excited to finally try it out! My friend and I had reservations for a Friday night; the host said that the wait would have been an hour without so calling in advance is definitely recommended!

Our server, James, was the absolute best. Friendly and kind, explaining every item on the menu thoroughly. It was almost to the point of excess but was appreciated nonetheless!

For food, my friend and I split a side of the Brussel sprouts. They were..... awful, to say the least. Cold and slimy, with an overpowering peanut sauce that made the whole mixture worse, not better. Our main courses were better - I got the Truffle Creme udon with crab and mushroom ($22) and my friend ordered the Tan Tan udon ($20). We both got the large order of the thick noodles, it's interesting that the prices are the same regardless of size.... I like (and hate) that it encourages you to eat more!

My udon was delicious. The broth was so creamy and rich, it tasted like liquid truffle cream and was absolutely perfect for the winter. If you're not into super heavy, heart-attack inducing broth, don't order it. But I am apparently! I unfortunately found a piece of hair in my soup which made the whole meal less enjoyable (otherwise this review would definitely be at least 4 stars). My friend thought the Tan Tan udon was mediocre, spicier than expected with a strange nutty taste reminiscent to that of the Brussel sprouts. Portion sizes were huge, though somehow we both managed to get through the majority of our bowls.

Overall, a generally positive experience here with a few mishaps. I'd like try out more of the menu in the future! My friend pointed out that the sizzling sukiyaki udon is some of the best she's had, so I'll have to come back for that!

Delicious and wonderful for large groups with a reservation and kids. Somewhat understanding and polite staff although individual requests were not accommodated. Skip the sushi and go straight for the noodle dishes.
Wish they didn't charge plating fee for birthday cupcakes. The uni creme udon, sukiyaki beef udon and truffle creme udon was awesome and everyone in the party enjoyed their dishes. 
Otherwise, amazing experience and tasty dishes all around. Huge space and nicely decorated.
Amazing udon with huge portions. The broth is flavorful and not too heavy or salty. The decor has a cool vibe and is perfect for smaller groups or dates.

Food here was so good! I'm a huge udon enthusiast and I really recommend this place~ 
There's so many options to choose from and the waiter was really informative about the menu. Best part about this place is that udon comes in two sizes, regular or large, for the same price!! I opted for large, of course. I warn you,  the bowl is REALLY huge. Next time I'm here, I think ill just get the regular size because it was difficult to finish.
The udon dish I ordered was great!! I think it was the most expensive dish on the menu though. No regrets. It was very flavorful and the broth was really good. The tofu was also really good, very soft. It melts in your mouth! Downside was I didnt really like the scallions/ginger that came with it.
All in all- great place, great food, wonderful service :)

We came on a Sunday night with reservations at 6:30 PM for a friends birthday, and the restaurant was pretty packed. So make reservations for large groups. The atmosphere was nice, you will enter to dim lights, nice decor and tables, We got seated and felt a little rushed to order. So I didn't really get to explore the menu and order Katsu curry. They have two types of noodles, thick or thin. I'm not a udon fan, so I ordered thin udon. The pork katsu was over fried in my opinion. I won't recommend getting the katsu curry. 

Overall,  this is a great location for large group. The service was mediocre. If you like udon, give this place a try.

Ooooh, how I wanted to love this place and how utterly disappointed I was...date night here was only 3 nights ago, so the memory is still fresh in my mind as I write this review. 

To start, we ordered the udon pon dumplings, duck meat balls, and crispy corn kakiage. While the udon dumpling and corn critter appetizers were pretty good, they were good in the way that you-can-never-go-wrong-with-fried kind of good. The duck meat balls tasted okay -- a little gamey and chalky, but the sauce seasoning was flavorful. So far, not bad..I'm still craving the udon to come. I LOVE udon and I'd heard so much about Tsurutontan that I was ready to believe that this specialty restaurant would be masterful at udon perfection. Unfortunately, not only was udon not perfected here, it was on the low end of the scale, as if it specialized in being the worst of udon creations. 

The first main dish I ordered --the uni creme udon -- was a huge FAIL. Let me add here that the photos you see on the menu are deceptive; the uni creme udon in the photo showed 4-5 pieces of uni. When the bowl came out, there was only ONE tiny uni placed in the middle. As for the creme broth, every time I brought my face down to the bowl and got a whiff of the cheesy creme, I felt instantly nauseated. There was simply TOO much creme. I still gave it a chance and took a  bite...only to be proven right that this was not the dish for me. So I had to order another, hoping that maybe if it wasn't creme-based, I might love it. This time, I ordered the Nabeyaki udon. While I waited for my Nabeyaki order, I tried a spoonful of my husband's beef udon. I was unimpressed with the flat, watery broth. It tasted like artificial beef flavoring. My husband said it tasted off to him as well. He felt the beef cut should really make the broth more flavorful, but it just didn't pack much flavor. Aside from the disappointing creme broth and beef broth flavors, the udon itself was also overcooked and soft, which made it floury in the mouth.

When my Nabeyaki udon arrived, I was hopeful for this third chance to be wowed. However, I was dismayed yet again. The presentation was not impressive, as I'm very familiar with Japanese aesthetic of food presentation, and this display felt like it missed the small but important details; the spoon was metal and very wide, and the portion was HUGE (this goes for all the three udon bowls ordered, by the way). The tempura shrimp arrived soggy, even though I didn't dunk it in the soup for the very reason I wanted it crispy. The broth flavoring felt like instant noodle flavoring (and not the good instant noodle, at that) that lacked the umami dashi broth flavor. The udon was soft and not chewy. I couldn't believe the claim that the udon was handmade.

The last gripe before I end this review: the prices are ridiculous. $24 for the uni udon, $20 for nabeyaki, $16 for the beef udon. While the udon portions may be huge, udon is nothing more than flour and water...still, I would have been okay with the prices if I felt the udon was worth it.

While I didn't enjoy my meal here, I'm glad I tried it so that I no longer need to wonder if it's any good. I've eaten amazing udon before, and for this restaurant to self-proclaim mastery of udon is a huge joke. For the people who rave about it, I advise you to try Raku or Soba-ya to truly understand how udon really should be done.

I finally came here with a friend because I heard so many good comments about it. It wasn't quite what I had expected. The interior walls had cool designs and there was another lower part of the restaurant filled with more seats and customers. The noodles come in a size regular or large. You should definitely get a large for your money's worth because the portion size is actually SOSO BIG; I got so full from eating just half of the bowl. I got the US Wagyu Shabu Udon, which was pretty decent, and the broth was so perfect for the chilly weather. Glad I finally got to taste this restaurant's udon!

Food: massive bowls of thick or thin udon noodles. You can choose to upgrade to large for free. Essentially the noodles are priced at $22-28 for a large bowl. I got the truffle creme with crab (4 small pieces) and mushroom. The soup was incredibly bland; I had to ask for salt on the side. It smelled amazing but the taste was completely different. I tasted my friend's tsurutontan deluxe bowl and it was just as bland. I've definitely had better udon elsewhere. 

Location: we came at 6pm on a Monday so it was fairly quiet. By the time we left around 7:30pm, there was a line outside. However there were still multiple empty tables. This place is huge. It's got a second floor that has two tables with 4-6 people at each. It would be a great place to have a private party (provided you like the food). 

Service: great! Very attentive.

Each popular restaurant must have at least one thing to attract attention. In Tsurutontan, it is the huge BOWL! It must be bigger than my head. 
I tried their top seller sukiyaki Udon which has less flavors than ramen. So I prefer this place design to their noodle

Surprisingly, this place was poppin at 6 pm on a Wednesday. My friend and I got seated right away at the counter and our lovely server ran through the menu highlights. I ordered the uni creme with thick udon noodles and she got the Korean hot broth also with thick noodles. 

The uni creme was delicious and not as thick of a broth as I had feared, and didn't evoke any lactose intolerant, ibs probs. There were two large chunks of uni and then some smaller bits but I'd always welcome more. Hers was just spicy enough with all the accruements- raw egg yolk, bulgogi, kimchi, etc. The regular size was plenty huge. I will definitely be back to try more apps, sushi and other udon.

I read wonderful reviews about this place so I was super excited to try, but unfortunately this place was just full of disappointment. First off, my friends and I made a reservation for 7:15 on a TUESDAY night. The waitress told us that they're cleaning the tables so it'll take them a couple minutes. Fast forward, we got to our seats at 7:55. God knows how a couple minutes turned into a 40 minute wait. We were quite upset but we were excited to eat. We ordered a few appetizers, which were delicious, hence the 2 stars. But udon was quite disappointing. It was lukewarm and the noodles were not chewy and tasty as we imagined it to be. We got creme uni udon, katsu udon, and chicken curry udon. Curry based udon were decent but still definitely not worth the hype. We ended up paying $43 each person, which would've been fine if the food was good, but quite over priced for the quality of the food and service.

The restaurant was definitely worth the hype. I thought it would be difficult to get into because it was on Insider, however it's very easy to make reservations! It looks like a place for dates with the dimmed lighting, but I think it's more for casual hang outs. The place is very loud because there is an open bar. As for the food, I think it was average, but the service made up for it. Waiters are constantly checking on you to make sure that you are happy with the food. I ordered the something with the deluxe, and by the time it came, the tempura was already beginning to be soggy. I'd like it better if they were to separate the noodles+broth and the tempura. IMO, crispy tempura tastes better than soggy. But nevertheless, the food was delicious.

Tsurutontan has been around for about a year, but it's taken me a long, long time to make it here. 

The space here is cavernous, but in a positive way. I like to think that I successfully blended into the background, since the setting is mostly dark and dimly lit. I obviously came here to eat udon, so that's what I ordered- however, the menu is pretty big, and they have a lot of other options here as well, so don't feel like just because you're here you'll be compelled to get udon. 

I believe I ordered a type of kitsune udon, while I also ordered a side of vegetable tempura on the side. The udon actually takes quite a long time to come out- maybe it was because there were a lot of people, but it also could just be because they're slow. I opted for the large size (you can get a small or large, i think) and was presented with this massive bowl. The amount of food in the bowl itself is much more modest, but the huge bowl I felt was a nice touch.

The tempura sauce here however was awful- I think it was some sort of eel sauce, but it was simultaneously bitter and sweet somehow- simply awful. I would perhaps order tempura again as a side, but would request it without the sauce. The problem with ordering on the side however, is that they're likely to bring it out first before you get your noodles, which means it might be cold by the time you get your main course. 

Overall a nice experience.
Ok place with good ambience, but if you are gonna call yourself an udon restaurant, then the udon dishes should be better than average. The cucumbers salad and sashimi are good though.
Good portion! Wagyu Shaun Udon is the best! It hits the right spot in the cold weather!

I left a 5 star review previously but i am changing that to a 1 star, 0 stars if i can. We asked for a regular table specifically because we had heavy jackets on and did not want to sit on a bench since there is no where to put them. We were asked to wait about 30 minutes. Fine...we will wait since that was what we requested for and wanted even though we were super hungry but we wanted to be more comfortable. After 40 minutes, they sat us at the bench, which we could have sat at when we first walked in and not have needed to want 40 minutes! We wanted to complain but we saw a table open up in front of us so we thought whatever, there is a table. We asked to switch and they asked if the matr'd knew! At that time the manager was right there, we told him what happened and he asked us to wait a little longer but by then we lost our appetite, left and walked right over to the better restaurants in union square.
The place is very clean and the food was good but the environment is very noisy and quite pricey for the portion size

LARGE portions for those who need to get their oodles on! Like bowls the size of your face. And more. For no extra charge! 

Be wary, the line is real on weeknights and weekends so highly recommend making a reservation. They're very good about seating if you do so. 

I've had their duck udon, sour and spicy udon, creamy mushroom udon, as well as their beef buns (appetizer) -meat is good but the fluff in bun is lacking- in different visits. This place fills the noods cravings and keeps me coming back for more!

I was thoroughly unimpressed with this place. That said, I should probably preface this review with a full disclosure: I am one of those people who don't believe that ramen/udon bowls are really all that different from a "fancied up" package of Nissin Cup Noodles. 

There were some pros though:

The drinks menu was extensive, and chock full of imported beers, whiskeys, and wines.
Next, the seating arrangement for couples was very unique (instead of small 2-person tables, they have a long bar table where couples sit side by side). The decor felt authentic.
Thirdly, you can ask for an XL order of Udon noodles (as opposed to the normal portion) completely free of charge. 

The cons:

I ordered the Tsurotontan Deluxe w/ Thick XL noodles ($22) and the 2 pc. Sukiyaki Beef Buns ($10). The beef buns were tasty, but too small. And the Tsurotontan Deluxe was totally bland, and didn't have enough of the "shrimp, beef, and vegetables" it was pictured having. 
Additionally, there was an unreasonably long wait to get seated.

Overall, this place just doesn't seem worth the price tag.

This is my favorite Japanese restaurant in Union Square. I was hesitant to try their udon noodles at first because thick noodles can be quite heavy (trying to trim my waistline). But I was surprised how lite and delicate it was. I love the fact you can upgrade to a large bowl with more noodles for the same price. I've been back a dozen times and everything on the menu is amazing. My favorite was the Hamachi carpaccio, Sea & Truffle roll, uni, ikura& crab don, wagyu shabu udon.  Also the Happy House drink specials are worth checking out. Special shout out to Edwin who is always  attentive and accommodating to our table.

**thin udon noodles are recommended for chilled udon dishes** 

It's not my first time dining at tsurutontan, and I have high expectations based on my previous visits. I was very disappointed yesterday because the texture of the thick udon  noodle for hot and cold dishes are way too different. I understand chilling cooked noodles immediately after cooking makes them really tender, but the chilled udon I had was chewy, way too chewy. It was tiring to eat. I then remembered the server recommended thick udon noodles for hot dishes and thin udon noodles for cold ones on my first visit. This was not my first visit so the server did not explain again and I was not expecting a different texture noodle for a different dish. It was just disappointing for me to have a unsatisfying udon dish from tsurutontan. 2 stars for my visit this time but giving 3 stars because I can see thin noodle would probably taste better for my dish. It's hard to say if I will risk ordering a chilled udon noodle again just to try it with thin noodles though.

waited over an hour to be seated. Ordered their mushroom and crab ramen. Would've liked to have more crab in the ramen, they were only a few small bites in the soup. The xlarge is the same price as the regular. So if you want to save some for later, order the xlarge. Appetizers were amazing, and the service once seated was great. I would give them a 5 but the front of the house hosts were not the best.

We came here as a large group, the service was fast, staff was very friendly and attentive. We had the best time ever here. Veggie noodle was the best with other side dishes, interior is also nice but there's potential to make it superior. 
Price is very reasonable, l highly recommend this place

You should make a reservation. Even with a reservation, it took us some time to be seated, but once that happened we received impeccable service.
It's difficult choosing from the enticing variety of udon concoctions (they're more progressive and modern than a traditional udon) like traditional to sweet sukiyaki to curry to creamy, ranging from $16 to $24 with either 260g or 390g of noodles for the same price.
I had the Wagyu mushroom sukiyaki udon ($24). The udon made in-house had a perfect chewy texture and drank in the flavor from the (somewhat overly sweet) broth. I'll believe them if they say my shaved beef steak was wagyu, but I can't actually tell. The fresh mushroom variety was all I could have hoped for. 
The beautiful ceramic bowls are comically large. The wall decor is also really interesting and visually stunning.

I've eaten here twice and both times I've been very satisfied with the service, price, quantity and quality. 

This past Friday night three of us showed up and they were able to seat us at the bar within about 20 minutes. They were very friendly and accommodating despite our lack of a reservation.

We had the shrimp dumplings, mushroom special and a spicy tuny roll as appetizers. The shrimp dumplings were good but not particularly memorable; the mushrooms and sushi roll were both excellent. 

We followed up with three noodle bowls: duck udon, wagyu curry and the sukiyaki. All three were delicious, though sadly none of us were able to finish our bowls since they are such generous proportions. 

I'm a big fan of the decor and atmosphere of the restaurant. The service was as noted, great; our server was very helpful in explaining how the menu was laid out and what to expect with each type of noodle dish. 

Overall a great experience and I definitely intend to visit more often!

Usually, I'm not a big fan of fushion Asian food because I think it usually ruins the authentic flavor of traditional Asian dishes. BUT to my surprise, I enjoyed the freshly made noodle (on a daily basis) at Tsurutontan and its ultra-modern decor and high ceilings. Service was also attentive, both from the waiter and the manager, who personally came to ask us about our dining experience at the end of our meal.

Now, onto the food. The gigantic portions were the most outstanding feature- not to mention that both regular and large were the same price! My date had beef sukiyaki udon, and said it was overly sweet, but he finished the large bowl regardless. I had udon soup with duck meat. Sliced duck meat soaked in udon broth was surprisingly chewy and delicious. It also came with some kind of meatballs, which went well with the hot broth. As for the noodles, they tasted fresh although it was a bit too chewy for my taste and didn't sit too well on my stomach. 

All in all, this place exceeded my expectations of fushion Japanese food restaurants. The sheer number of Asian diners during my visit proved my point!

MY NEW FAVORITE RESTAURANT IN NYC.

I love ramen/udon/soba and after trying this place out, Tsurutontan has become my new #1 noodle place in NY. Dishes are around $24 per bowl, but a medium and a large cost the same (so might as well get a large). I tried three different types of udons and my favorite one was the spicy dan dan udon (followed by the uni). The noodles are thick and chewy (they also have thin udon as an option) and everything just tastes very fresh, esp the cold uni which doesn't have a fishy flavor. 

Love the ambiance/atmosphere and the wait time was less than 15 minutes. Service was great. This is a cool place to bring visitors because they vouch that they have the largest bowls in all of NY.

MAKE RESERVATIONS! Thankfully we made a reservation because there was already a huge crowd by the door when it opened for lunch. 

My friend and I shared a bowl of the Tsurutontan Deluxe. We asked for extra noodles but I don't think we ever got any because our other friend had just the same amount of noodles as us and she did not order extra noodles. The soup was clear and refreshing and the noodles were delicious! My friend and I were content with our bowl of udon but I wouldn't recommend sharing if you're really hungry. The bowl may seem big but there's really not that much in there. 

The decor is great and the people are friendly. Would definitely come back to try their other udon bowls!

Yummy udon noodle place! Huge bowl for udon! Regular and large same price. We went there on Saturday around 2pm and we didn't have to wait. Udon noodles are handmade and taste so good!! Love this place !!!

Affordable and delicious noodles and ramen. It is easily located right at Union Square. The restaurant is beautiful and spacious. The service is quick and explains the menu well. There was three of us, we each got a bowl of noodles (with extra noodles) and two appetizers (beef buns and shishito peppers)!

Highly recommend it and great on a call winter night.

If you order any soup udon, the portion is HUGE. Free upgrade to large size where you get more noddles. Second time here. This time, we first got an order of spicy tuna cone appetizer. It was sooooo good. The cone is super crunchy and the tuna is perfectly blended with guacamole lying underneath. I ordered sizzling stir fried udon while my friend ordered soup based beef one(don't remember the exact name, but order anything is good!!!). I took off one star because although at first the dishes tasted incredibly delicious but toward the end, both of our dishes were a bit too salty. To the point I wanted to pour some hot water to dilute the taste so badly. But overall, the ambient is really nice and the service is very good. ( if you sit there for too long, the waiter may keep coming back to ask you if you're done with the dish. Which I totally understand because the place get very busy).

Make your reservations online! Avoid the long wait at the door for a table. Although the restaurant is much larger than expected, it is packed (and deservedly so). Came here with a group of 9 people, but while waiting for everyone, started drinking at the bar (where they do 7 days a week ALL DAY LONG happy hour that includes sapporo draft, wine, cocktails, and appetizers for a fraction of the price)

Our wonderful server explained the menu to us and told us that a regular size udon can be upgraded to a large AT NO ADDITIONAL COST. So we ended up ordering 6 large udons for people to share along with appetizers which ensured that our stomachs were full and happy, as well as our wallets! I enjoyed the curry udon and uni udon but the shining star in terms of portion and flavor, was the sizzling sukiyaki udon! Would highly recommend.

I tried the sizzling sukiyaki beef udon, it was very savory and tasty (comes with mushrooms too). My lovely girlfriend had the spicy tan tan udon which was also very good. Would recommend either of these bowls.

Best udon I've ever had!!! Portions are HUGE! Gigantic bowls with ladles instead of a spoon huge. 


Tuna cones - recommend. Tasty little bites as you wait for your udon. The cone is made of wonton. The spicy tuna tasted fresh and had whipped avocado as well. 

Uni udon - recommend. $24 and is their most expensive udon but so worth it. Broth was very creamy but not overwhelming. 

Curry udon - good. Typically curry have a strong taste and can be too salty however this had a great balance. The curry flavor wasn't too overwhelming and had a lot of flavors to it. 


If you're in the area definitely check this place out!

There were a lot of people waiting so be sure to make a reservation! 

I got the truffle creme udon, which did eventually get a little greasy near the end, but was still really good overall. It didn't come as hot as I wished it did (it was just warm), but the portion was really big. 

I would really want to come back again to try other udon flavors next time I visit.
I think this place has the best curry udon in the east coast. The noodle itself is very tasty as well!

This place has hugeeeee cold and hot noodles- you cam get large or regular for the same price! My biggest advice is sharing one or two noodle bowl and getting other stuff. I would definitely come again!

Other advice is get reservations! Theres usually a wait!

Yes, the udon is good here. Is it the best I've ever had? No. That title remains with Monzo Udon in LA. (I realize that Japan has much better offerings, but I've never been so I can't really speak on that).

My husband ordered the tsurutontan deluxe, I got the creamy uni udon, and we shared the spicy tuna cones. The tuna was probably the best thing we ate there - not sure how to feel about that since we came for the giant udon bowls. 

The tsurutontan deluxe was tasty. They gave a generous helping of seafood and the broth was flavorful but not too salty. 

Now for the creamy udon... I wanted to love it, but after a few bites, I found the taste to be somewhat unpleasant. The broth was waterier than what I was used to and I felt skimped out on the udon chunks. Once the uni was gone, it tasted like I was eating noodles in salty evaporated milk. I'd pass on this next time.
A must-try if you like noodles! The restaurant is spacious and trendy. The sashimi dishes and appetizers generally were pretty tasty and great for sharing.

Two words. In love. Food was so good, portion was HUGE. Service and interior decor was great. I have left overs and just devoured it for lunch.

I came around 9pm on a Monday night, no crowd at all. I got their most popular appetizer of the salmon tartare - comes with 4. DELICIOUS!! It's mixed with avocado and the cone it's served in adds a good crunch to it.

I also ordered the Uni creme udon, also amazing. The bowl was HUMUNGOUS. Seriously, if the bowl was clean, I could probably wear it as a hat. The spoon is also really big - I would describe it as a heavy ladle, heavy enough to make your arm sore after a few bites lol. All the udon orders come with extra noodles free of charge if you ask for it. They give you the option to choose thin or thick udon noodles as well. Uni itself is an acquired taste, so I would not recommend unless you're adventurous. My friend got the duck udon and that was really good too. 

I definitely want to come back to try their other udon dishes. By far my favorite udon spot *drool*
When they say large, they really mean LARGE. Huge portions and great udon. The interior is really nice inside and the staff are all friendly and attentive.

***Delicious items, Friendly staff, Reservation recommended*** 

There are so many items to try on the menu and quite frankly, they're all pretty delicious. I've been here several times and I recommend making a reservation as it does get crowded during normal lunch/dinner hours. For all udon items you have the option to get large or regular for the same price-I recommend coming with an empty stomach and getting the large. Also I recommend the fried chicken and tuna tartare appetizer-both equally delicious. Highly recommend checking this place out-you won't be disappointed!

Hailing from Japan, this modern udon chain has more than 10 restaurants with this Union Square location as the first and only one (so far) in the US. It stayed on my bookmark list from my last trip to Asia but now that it's in NY, I made it a point to join other noodle enthusiasts on the most chilly day of our stay in the city.

Yay for reservations, nay if you are late. We lost our table and it was only fair after being half an hour late. Thankfully the wait wasn't too long despite the crowd - this place was popping on a weekday lunch.

Feeling the lively vibe and loving the interior of wooden horizontal lines, we were led to our cozy table that didn't feel cramped despite the low ceiling in the dining area. Our jovial server helped us go through the menu, giving us tips such as: thick udon pairs well with hot broth while thin for chilled, and upgrading to a large bowl for more noodles has no extra charge. 

Spicy Tuna Tartar Cones ($9) to start with was not a bad choice. The presentation was cute, portion was enough to tease, and it was delicious. Going beyond that and ordering sushi would have been a bad idea. Let's stick to the specialty, shall we? 

Debating between the hot and cold Uni Udon ($24) was a struggle but the hot broth won which was apt for the weather. Fast forward to when my ginormous ceramic bowl of udon arrived, the pungent taste of fish broth stood out, so much so that it masked any uni flavor whatsoever. Our server apologized and took this out of our tab after seeing almost a full bowl untouched. The redeeming factor here was the Tsurutontan Deluxe ($24). Everything about it from the shrimp tempura, beef, chicken, seaweed, and egg to the mouthwatering dashi broth - it was glorious.
