The best part which is the most significant, every strand of udon noodle was slippery yet firm, very evident that it's handmade in-house. For that, I am sure to make this a sure stop each time I am in town.

This interior is beautiful, with dim lighting and wooden walls, feeling both modern and somehow very japanese (or at least to me). Unlike a traditional Japanese place that might only specialize in 1 type of dish, this restaurant serves mainly Udon dishes, but also serves Sushi, Katsudon, and many western meets eastern type appetizers. Additionally, they have Udon made with Dashi broth and other meat/vegetable based broths for those that don't like fishy tasting soup. Once you choose your Udon for the night, you can choose the usual thick style noodle OR a thinner almost "ramen" type noodle. Both are delicious. My personal preference are the thinner ones because they're a little easier to grasp with chopsticks and are just more satisfying to eat in one big chopstick-full. You can then choose the regular sized portion OR a large portion, which just means more noodles... and they are the same price... more noodles for the same price. Even if I wasn't a glutton, I wouldn't pass up that opportunity. Be warned though, that the large Udon serving is indeed very large. Don't ask me why or how I know this, but I was able to fit my whole head into this bowl...

Come hungry.

The interior is clean, service is good, and the wait hasn't been too bad. 

You get an option to get upgraded to a large portion for free! My all time fav is the mentaiko cream udon. The uni cream was alright. The lunch specials come with chicken karaage/rice so it was nice to share. 

The udon noodles are nothing special and the meal itself doesn't taste like the healthiest but it's flavorful and has just the right amount of cream.

Get a regular bowl of noodles and a large for the same price. I love the option, but not as much as I love the spicy tuna cones! They are always the highlight of my meal. 

Make reservations in advance, the whole party must be there before you are seated. My go to is definitely the curry udon. Supersize me please!

I have been holding back on sharing this hidden gem for a while.  TsuruTonTan Udon Noodle Brasserie has been in business over a year, and these Udon specialists are showing no signs of slowing down.  The Brasserie located near Union Square is the first location in the United States, but they currently have 13 locations in Japan.  Per a restaurant rep they have intentions of expanding to two more locations in NYC in the near future.


In NYC, Ramen and Udon noodle shops are about as common as McDonald's, and can be found in any neighborhood. TsuruTonTan sets themselves apart with providing their customers with a very diverse menu from your traditional Udon, creamy broth, and a curry broth.  Their noodles are made fresh and in house DAILY.  When ordering your entree you are given the choice of thin or thick noodles as well.  Prices ranges from $15 - $30 for these larger than life sized bowls of udon noodle soup.  Save room in your tummy because there is not a doggie bag option.  I am assuming it is because Udon is something meant to be eaten immediately after it is prepared.

TsuruTonTan happy hour is all day everyday!  There was not a typo with that last sentence, and I suggest you hop on board before they change this promotion.  Happy hour is only at the bar and includes some specialty cocktails, wine, beer, and appetizers as well.  Bar get packed around 6:30 so get there early to secure your seat at the bar.  This is great place to dine solo or with a large group because of the their setup in their dining room.

Some of  my favorites their obvious udon noodles, shrimp dumplings, and garlic soy chicken.

Great meal with the family. Big parties fit upstairs. The bowls are huge. My father in law's eyes lit up when he found out the large size was the se price as the regular bowl (more noodles). The fried chicken appetizer and shishito peppers were our favorites. We had all the top sellers and they're all a bit different but consistently good. Surprisingly the spicy soondubu was our favorite. The service is quick and attentive. Have been about three times a year and mostly when new friends and family come into town. Will be returning soon.

I came on a glowing recommendation and was looking forward to a hot bowl of noodles on a cool day. 

I opted for a regular-sized portion of the sukiyaki udon; it was marked a top seller and I like sukiyaki. Service was extremely quick (as in, I think I got my food within five minutes of ordering). The presentation was lovely; they bring your (extremely large) bowl to you covered and then uncover it in front of you. The noodles were just ok, though, a little too soft (I prefer a firmer, chewier udon). It may just have been the sukiyaki part, but the dish was too salty for my taste. The beef was a little on the tough side too. Truth be told, as big as the bowl is, there actually isn't /that/ much food inside. It's a healthy amount of food, but not a ridiculous amount.

I also was seated at the counter and was so confused. Was it ok to slurp my noodles? The decor is a touch too stylish, and my neighbors just weren't doing it. Plus, the spoon they give you is ginormous, so it's almost comical to be sipping broth out of it. So even though this place is Japanese, I felt there were some less than authentic details that took away from my experience.

4.5 stars

Came here for a quick bite on the recommendation of a friend. It did not disappoint!

Shared a large portion of the uni udon and it was fantastic. The noodles had a wonderful texture, and the broth was super creamy and rich, with a touch of a smoky flavor.

Will definitely be returning!

Definitely make reservations as this place gets packed! Good udon!

Ordered a bowl of the uni creme udon and Katsu curry udon, you can also get extra noodles for no charge.

The uni creme udon wad delicious. Although toppings are sparse in this bowl, the rich creamy uni flavor was good.

The Katsu was soft and crispy in the Katsu curry udon. The curry broth could be overwhelming with it's spices and thickness of broth, I would recommend to avoid this dish if you are not a huge fan of curry.

Used to be 5, but will have to give a 3 now.
Noodle itself is not bad, but one would expect a great noodle place should also have some accompanied greatness.

Uni cones ($19 for two) and hamachi carppacio had fishy smell. 
Fried chicken was really soggy.

My wagyu beef noodle soup was good with cabbage, mushroom, and egg, but the broth was way too salty.

May come back for one plate/bowl of noodles, but nothing more.

Really beautiful restaurant. Went on a Saturday afternoon. They said the wait would be 15 minutes . Once we were led to our seats we realized half the place was empty. Not sure why they made us wait then. There's good privacy if you're sitting in the middle communal style tables. I ordered the uni creme udon. Wasn't a huge fan of the flavor but the udon was delicious. It wasn't bad but a bit too overwhelming cream flavor. And hardly any uni or uni flavor. I also tried the curry udon with katsu and shrimp tempura. It was delicious! Came with lots of filling and great flavor. Decently priced. Our waitress was really friendly and helpful. Worth a try!

My love for the uni creme udon is so great that while there are a few menu items I don't love (I'll touch on those later), I'd give this place a 4.5. It's a bit unfair actually because I absolutely love uni and they do the uni creme don SO WELL. Firstly, the udon comes in their regular size and large size (at no additional cost), so I always get the large. It's definitely shareable between two people, which I would recommend and then getting an appetizer on top of that. The udon itself is thick, firm, and a nice chewy texture. But, let me just get to the broth of the uni creme don. It's heavy, creamy, and just plain HEAVENLY. If you're an uni lover like me, trust me, you'll love this udon bowl. It also comes with two generous piece of uni on top, which is relatively fresh and good quality for the price you're paying for it. My favorite part of this uni creme udon though is definitely the broth. It covers the udon so well and even though it's so heavy and thick, I don't get sick of it! I drink all of it to the very last drop and that's something I can say for very few bowls of noodles. 

As for appetizers, I usually get the tuna tartare cones. They're made of tuna tartare on top and then a whipped avocado creme on the bottom. They're aesthetically pleasing and also taste pretty good. I've also had their fried tatsuta chicken which is good as well and quite a large serving. However, there was one time where we found hair in this appetizer. They were quick to replace the dish with a new one, though. The one appetizer I really did not enjoy was the salmon & snow crab roll. It was so bad I actually spat it out after taking a bite. It had a strange aftertaste for me, but it could've very well been personal as my friend had no problem eating it. 

If you're looking to go during primetime for dinner, definitely make a reservation prior as it gets very busy! The atmosphere of the place is also pretty nice and they have a bar near the entrance if you want a drink while you're waiting. I see a lot of couples go here, so it'd be nice for a date night too.
Tasted like the one in Tokyo, great interior design, great service. Awesome portion size and the flavors were fantastic.
Great selection. big portions. Had sushi roll it was very good quality. Curry udon was flavorful definitely would return.

Great location.  Beautiful space.  Lots of tables, great for a large group as they do take reservation.

The menu is quite extensive with udon being their specialities.  If you fancy rice dishes, they're available as well.

We got the uni cold udon and it was great though I have to admit I am uni'ed out.  The udon was cooked al dente with some bounce.

It's moderately priced and service is good.  Do make a reservation as we saw a lot of people waiting for a table around the bar.

This is my favorite udon place in US and this is probably the only place in the world where I can finish the noodles. All these other places, you are there for the soup or topping or some combination, this place you are here for the noodle dipped in the soup! I ordered the creamy uni thin udon and it is AMAZING.

I used to think of udon as the healthy version of ramen. Where the latter's fatty broth and pork toppings leave me dizzy and drained, the former is usually lighter, simpler, and more restorative. Tsurutontan almost takes it as a mission to prove that udon can be just as decadent as its thinner-noodled peer.

We had tried to go on a weeknight, but were rebuffed with an hour long wait. Instead, we came in around 2 pm on a Sunday, and were told a half hour wait. After browsing the Union Square Holiday Market, we ended up getting a text 20 minutes later. Not too shabby...

The space is stunning and you can tell a lot of money was spent. Lots of unique wall hangings, a gorgeous bar, and multilevel spaces. We were surprised to see so many empty seats given the wait, but maybe they are trying to space out diners for the kitchen.

Your eyes will be far bigger than your belly here, partially because the udon bowls are massive and partially because you'll want everything. Deciding you want uni, for example, you'll next have to choose it in creamy udon, in cold udon, in donburi, or as a decadent appetizer. It took us a while to strategize. You'll also be tempted, given the high prices (most bowls are in the $20s) to just go all out.

I opted for the hot dashi Nabeyaki udon ($20), with chicken, mushroom, eel, egg, and shrimp tempura, for a little bit of everything. My boyfriend splurged on the cold Uni Ikura Hotate udon ($32), which as the name suggests comes with uni, salmon roe, and scallops, with shiso leaf strips on top. They came out maybe 15 minutes later. Both were impressive-looking.

I liked mine just fine. The thick noodles were not remarkable to me, the shrimp tempura and eel were especially good, and everything else was good. I'm not big on cold seafood soba, but the uni was very high quality. My boyfriend loved it. They are big, so come with an empty stomach or give yourself permission not to finish.

A lot of Yelpers try comparing this to Raku, but that's apples and oranges for me. Raku is tiny, clearly homemade noodles, lighter, minimalist, cheaper. Tsurutontan is bigger, more standardized, heavier, splashier, more expensive. One is a night in, the other is a night out. I prefer the former experience, as this meal left me feeling a bit overwhelmed and bloated, but Tsurutontan succeeds at what it's trying to do.

Service was great; I believe we had Christine, who was super enthusiastic. Reservations recommended.

Settle in for a heavy, slurpy meal.  You will literally be able to swim in the bowl of udon you're served at Tsurutontan.  You can even upgrade your bowl and add extra noodles at no extra cost!  

I ordered the vegan version of the sukiyaki udon with tofu.  The noodles were fat, chewy, and expertly seasoned.  They didn't really give off a homemade vibe, but I don't think that's what the ultra modern restaurant was going for.

I went on a Thursday evening and there was no wait.  

I'm definitely going back to try the mentaiko caviar cream dish and ALL of their donburi bowls.

Tsurutontan in Union Square is an American outpost of the popular Japanese noodle chain. The ingredients are actually shipped from Japan to maintain the same quality and experience. (I'm sure the occasional Japanese tourist would appreciate this fact.)

That being said, the noodles are amazing, if not also wholly authentic. The udon is thick, chewy and keeps its texture while soaking in its broth. I had ordered the sukiyaki both times I ate at Tsurutontan. It strikes good balance between savory and sweetness. However, I can attest that each of the broths have its own unique flavor while still being rich and deep. (There is a choice between thin and thick udon... pick thick.)

During my first time at Tsurutontan, I was taken aback at the menu. Many of the premier entrees were priced at 30 dollars. Nevertheless, you may order your entree to be regular size or large at the same price. They will add more noodles in for you at no extra charge! Regular should do for most people. (I would advise diners not to order large and expect to take the rest home for later. They did not pack food away at the time I went.)

The decor is elegantly designed, a more modern take of Asian architecture versus traditional Japanese characteristics. Still, clean and spacious. There is a small issue of space, concerning the restrooms. They are difficult to locate and for a restaurant of this size, I'd expect them to be proportionally larger as well. Due the overall popularity of the restaurant, it can a bit of a hassle at times.

Excellent food. Great location. Good for special occasions or even a date.

The caviar udon (the one without cream) is my absolute favorite. I've never had anything like that before.. I also tried the tsurutontan deluxe and beef udon. They're not bad but pretty generic. Ah this is making me crave the caviar udon...anyway the location is perfect, interiors are on point and the caviar udon was unforgettable.. what more can I say? Oh and don't forget to get extra noodles because I don't think they charge more so why not

Busy but spacious restaurant, steps west of Union Square. Modern interior, with lots of seating options on 2 floors. Most couples seat side by side, with a see through separation of wooden panels from the couples in front... a smart way to sit lots of people and yet give them some privacy. 

They allow reservations, so it's very convenient. You should definitely make one if you're planning dinner on prime time (or be prepared to wait, especially on weekends). 

We were warmly welcomed and immediately seated. The service throughout the evening was outstanding: since the menu is filled with yummy options, our waitress was very helpful in allowing us to order the right dishes. She was also very pleasant and patient. 

Soy garlic fried chicken: very tasty; it's mostly dark meat (luckily). 

Spicy tuna tartare cones: kinda pricy for the amount you get, but delicious.

Duck udon with truffle oil: the $2 extra for the truffle oil are beyond worth, because they nicely complement the broth; there's plenty of duck meat and duck meatballs; the broth is light and flavorful.
 
Tsurutontan Curry Deluxe: obviously, a much stronger broth, and still very good; it comes with meat and shrimp. 

We ordered large portions (same price as medium) of thick udon, which had the perfect texture. 

Overall, we had a very good meal, and left curious to try other dishes. I can't wait to go back.

such a delightfuL experience with a super courteous staff. Christian the manager was professional and went beyond the call of duty to make my evening with my girlfriend a special occasion. cheers to a staff that sets the stage for a wonderful and hospitable experience.

I love going to Tsuruton Tan for udon. In addition to many different types of broth to select from, the services are wonderful. The staffs have made us very comfortable and well taken care of. Food have never failed to please us in all of our 7 visits. The only regret is that there is no frequent diner program.

I cannot say enough good things about Tsurutontan. Our waitress Nicha was extremely knowledgeable in guiding us through the menu based on our preference and dietary restrictions. Christian the manager was charming and professional, touching base with us to check on our experience. The display of the food and flavor profiles were spot on. I would definitely recommend this restaurant.

Soooooo gooooood. We waited 30 min when we go there without reservation. Seating is tight and you might be sitting next to a stranger. Bit pricy for noodles but worth it. We got curry delux, dashi delux, sukiyaki, and wagyu one. Sukiyaki was the best out of those.

I came here for a birthday dinner. I was honestly overwhelmed by the menu. There were so many items on it that I would have been happy to order. I ended up ordering a few appetizers, the hamachi carpaccio and the seared salmon sashimi. Both were excellent. For the main course I opted for the Cold Uni Udon. I could have ended up with any number of entrees but settled for the Uni Udon. I had a few options for my udon, thick or thin noodles, large or regular. The large and regular are supposedly the same price, the difference being that the large offers more noodles. I went with the thick noodles, large and it was fantastic. The uni flavor was sweet and subtle. The noodles were great and the portion was more than enough. I had to take it home with me because there was no way I could have finished it in a sitting.

Overall, the food is amazing, the atmosphere is very nice. Definitely worth the visit.

On a Friday night this place is packed to the brim with people trying to get their udon fix. We ended up waiting an hour to get seated which isnt bad but I remember trying this place out when it first opened and not having a wait at all. Oh how times have changedddd 

I got the tsurutontan deluxe with thick noodles which basically has a little bit of everything. The broth was flavorful and the udon chewy perfection. All the added toppings tasted great and left me surprised every time i dipped my chopstick and ladle into the bowl.

My friend got the wagu and mushroom sukiyaki and although i didnt taste her's she really enjoyed it.

This is a trendy udon spot in Union Square. The quality is solid and I'm very impressed by the size of their udon bowls. You can order your udon in regular or large size but the price is the same. The large bowl comes with more noodles but the toppings and soup are the same. 

Recently I had the duck udon. The soup was delicious and the noodles were quite nice. However the duck was pretty bland and a bit overcooked. My wife had the tempura udon and that was much better. The tempura breading was great and they had a good variety of vegetables. 

One good thing about this place is that its quite large. You dont feel cramped here. Make reservations ahead of time though since it can get very crowded. 

Overall this is a solid udon spot and worth a visit.

First of all, the portions here are huge! (The interior of the restaurant is actually surprisingly large as well.. but back to the food.) 

When ordering, there are two options for customization: size and noodle width. A large portion costs the same as the regular portion but includes more noodles. For the noodle width, the hot udon are paired with the standard udon whereas the cold udon are paired with the thin udon. I've tried both and think they both have their charms--the thin udon is much chewier (in a naengmyeon kind of way, as opposed to undercooked, and I found it very delightful).

On my two visits, I tried: 

+ US Wagyu and Mushroom Sukiyaki ($24): I really enjoyed the first third of this but started finding the sukiyaki broth too sweet after that. But if a friend were to order this, I'd definitely want a bite!

+ Uni Ikura Hotate Udon ($32): This was definitely a splurge but boy, oh boy, it was heavenly. (Also, I justified my pricier entree with the fact that I didn't order any drinks!) This cold udon was topped with 5-6 pieces of plump uni, loads of ikura, and silky smooth scallops--all incredibly fresh and flavorful! The chewiness of the thin noodles and the savoriness of the dashi soy were also just perfect. This was definitely a crave-worthy dish! However... I think my enjoyment was heightened by the fact that I shared with my husband and got to balance my cold udon with some of his hot udon--the Tsurutontan Deluxe ($24). 

For the future, my first choice would be to go halfsies again to get that sweet variety: cold/hot broth, thick/thin noodles, and seafood/meat flavors. However, if I had to eat a whole bowl of only one type of noodles by myself (oh the horror!) I would probably order one with the hot, traditional dashi broth.

On the note of sharing, a large order could definitely feed two people of average hunger. I'm not sure if it's generally allowed but in our party of 10, one couple did choose to share a large and it was perfect for them.

We ended our meal by ordering a water cake ($8) to share for dessert. I objected to this because I had heard that it literally tasted like water and boasted only novelty and no deliciousness, but everyone else in our party wanted to try it out. To his credit, our waiter admitted that the water cake "doesn't really taste like anything" when we asked him about it. Well, ladies and gentlemen, I'm here to confirm that the water cake does not, in fact, taste like anything. Even the texture is not interesting like I had hoped--it's a pretty standard jello texture, as opposed to anything remotely mochi-like (which I thought maybe it'd be like because it's also know as mizu shingen mochi). It's served with sugar syrup, kinako (a roasted soybean flour), and a scoop of vanilla ice cream. Needless to say, I was not into it.. but at least now I can dissuade my next group of friends from ordering a water cake with more credibility!

Yum! Came here for a date night and left super full. Staff were friendly and attentive. 
 
soy garlic chicken - this was just ok
sea & truffle roll - wow, you can really taste the truffle in this roll - super delicious in my opinion
sukiyaki udon - by far my favorite
duck udon - Not enough duck flavor or we hoped for

Overall, yummy experience and i'll be back for more!

Let me start by saying, I'm a pretty busy guy with little time to engage and "review" my experiences. I don't need the attention. Yet this is one of the exceptions to my credo and was compelled to report.  

Setting the stage- Im walking in the light rain, it was a late,cold December evening in NYC and my cell battery life  including my back up battery were at practically @ zero. I had sporadic  means to navigate with GPS and I have been on the road for close to three weeks. I was missing my family ( missed Thanksgiving w/ family first time ever) so my soul was also a little drained.   My hunger was placed last in line to my frustration when I realized " man I need to regroup "  Being in Union Square, I need a spot to sit, drink a beer, warm up, charge my sh!t and paint a plan.   As I browsed the dark  cityscape I saw the key word "UDON" on a black awning.  The restaurants exterior optics looked very nice and knowing my daughters are big fans of Ramen and Udon I thought  charge up take some pics and tantalize them with my Udon dinner.   So I walked in with back pack, oversized umbrella and luggage in tow.  Since it was late I realized the restaurant was getting ready to close and I'm not " that guy" that walks in with a minute to spare and says " serve me now"     
I was warmly welcomed.  " don't worry about the time" said the host, "Let's get u a seat! " Trust me I didn't hesitate.  

Roshan, my server wasn't busy.  Again I was the only cat in his section.  I was expected to be rushed and didn't mind knowing the time.   I report to u that was not the case.  Roshan took his time explained all the wonderful options and I followed his advice with food selections.  I shared my phone situation and he was more than accommodating to get some juice into my dead devices. 

With food ordered I had some time to take in the decor. This place is "badass" as they say in my neighborhood. I was relishing on all the subtle details like a small pebble/stone to keep my chop sticks off the table.  Kool touch yet that was minor.  The lighting, fixtures, accent walls all of them modern and beyond appealing.   I kept thinking my fam would love this place!   

Food showed and it paralleled my expectations with three words "Awe" + "Some" + "Ness"  The Bowls were humongous!  Let's just say there is no way to do  a bowl haircut with these thing.  Too big! 

So now I'm in ZOD. (Zone Of Deliciousness )  not a word  coming out of my mouth.  It was all one way traffic baby! 

Then there comes Christian the manager to my table.  I was expecting the typical, "how are things"? what else can we get for u ? Etc...  again not the case.  Perhaps he saw the swing of my emotional state going from tattered traveler to hope in my immediate future. We just started talking.  He was being a human to another human and i needed it ! Got to know and appreciate this young man.  We talked about his upbringing, his accomplishments and drive. As an entrepreneur and business owner myself, guys like this are a rare breed and to reach these benchmarks at a young age, I was actually proud for him.  Christian explained the history of the restaurant, the short tenure in the US and I was flabbergasted that there was only 2.   Yup - Dos, 10-8=2.  I said u guys need to hurry your A$$es up.  The warm embrace from management down, the experience, the value, the ambiance! All of it adds up to Winner! 

So if Udon is your thing or not and in NYC , it's a must in my book.  You will thank me. Tell them Fernie Bourdain sent you!  And get to LA.  ( where I domicile) because I'm telling everyone.   So if I don't see u guys in Los Angeles, or better yet close to 90638, I'm withdrawing my write up.    Lol!    

Btw. I dined here twice this week. Almost 3.  U guys closed before I could get there. That should say something!

I had a double date here and we decided to come try this place as we heard the udon came in a really huge bowls.  First thing I notice is how nice the design and interior design was inside the restaurant.  It is very big and the wait is not bad.  

Service: The waitress came to us really quickly to get our order and they always refill the water because there was always this one waiter that constantly walked back and forth to check on all the customer.

Food: The udon I ordered was around $24 and yes they ask you for the size you would want.  The large comes in a really big bowl that I feel was really extra. 

Overview: It was good, but I feel the udon is a little pricey for the amount.  After I finished eating I was still kinda hungry.

A bit pricy but huge portions. Good thing you can share the dishes with friends. I always get deluxe udon and really enjoy having different options. Service feels a bit rushed but its a busy restauranf

Mmmm came here on a snowy day and was the perfect meal to warm us up. Our waiter was great and bet through about explaining the menu. We kept on seeing people come out with GIANT bowls of udon so figured we didn't need too many appetizers. Ended up with the duck udon and a side of tempura. Their presentation is so funny though because you get a huge bowl and a serving spoon instead of a soup spoon. Made it very cumbersome to eat but it was quite entertaining. I was surprised by the duck udon, very tender and not dry at all. I also had a matcha cocktail which was surprisingly light and great! Would come again for sure.

The best place in NYC to get fresh udon noodles!! 
The wait time was very fast. The decor and atmosphere is very nice as well as all employees that approached me.  Everyone all seems to love to work there and with each other.  The food was amazing except I can't give 5 stars because it was not a very Vegan friendly place.  I don't see myself coming back unless more veg options are introduced.  This place is really great can get crowded during lunch and dinner hours and definitely for the everyday carnivore. 

It was still nice that I was able to enjoy a nice dinner with a carnivore friend.  I was able to order the Grilled Organic Maitake Mushrooms and the Sizzling Sukiyaki Udon with Tofu. Both were amazing.  I wanted something with broth but they do not have broth made with veg so I had to settle for no broth Udon

I wanted to try this place since it was opened! I made reservations for 3 online. After everyone arrived on time, we still had to wait for 15 minutes to be seated. SAD! It was during the lunchtime and we were on tight schedule. Sigh.... the host showed some attribute after I asked her a few times.

The food was great, which made up the experience that I had with the host. We ordered the unicone from the seasonal menu to share. It was fun to eat. I had seafood chiage udon and got filled up. My husband got the Tsuruton curry deluxe, which tasted very good. My friend got the spicy tan tan udon. She seemed very enjoying it.

I don't think I've ever devoured a bowl of udon as fast as I did at Tsurutontan. I ordered the wagyu beef udon and added shrimp tempura for $2 each. You have the option to pick a regular or large portion, both for the same price. The only difference is that you get more noodles with a large portion. 

When I received my food, I was glad I ordered the regular portion because it was a pretty large bowl. The udon noodles were cooked to chewy perfection, beef was marinated to give the soup even more flavor and the broth was light and comforting. I enjoyed it very much and will definitely come back when I'm in New York again!

Noodle. So thick. So meaty. So juicy. UDON.

We started with a couple appetizers - the tuna tartare and fried chicken. The tuna tartare was elegantly served in cones standing on a bed of rice like flowers of deliciousness sprouting from a garden of flavor town. Every bite brought a new dimension. First the soft tuna, then the crispy cone, finally the creamy guacamole...it was like a rainbow of flavors descended on my palette and established a sprawling community. The fried chicken was no slouch either. Super moist on the inside and a heaping serving size perfect for sharing in larger groups.

Now..onto the main event. The UDON. The menu is large and the waitress did a great job of walking us through all the different options and various broth variants. I ordered the deluxe curry udon ($24) which comes with pork cutlets, shrimp tempura and beef. The meat quantity and flavor will give one the meat sweats. The broth is exquisitely crafted and as an Indian man, I am proud to attach the word 'curry' as its' descriptor. 

Pro Tip: The regular and large udon sizes are the same price so why not order the large (believe me, you'll discover capacity in your belly that you never knew existed after one bite of these tasty noodles).

My boyfriend and I went here on a random night of the week and it was packed, but we didn't have a reservation and it was late into the night, so we didn't mind the wait. 

We started off with their beef puns and some kind of pork and egg dish and both were sooo good. I mean, we were pretty starving but there was so much flavor in both of those apps, we didn't mind 

I ordered the spicy ramen and my boyfriend ordered a sweet tasting ramen and the spicy ramen tasted very peanut-y. I minded it at first because it was a new taste, but all in all, it was delicious. The portions are huuuuge, which is the reason why people go here I suppose. 

Well worth the wait and the price tag of these dishes aren't outrageous. I think they're actually pretty standard.

Tsurutontan was recommended to me as a restaurant I couldn't miss for amazing udon as I was travelling through NYC on holiday. I must say I am so grateful that she made sure I went because I can't image if I ever missed out! 

The first time I went I brought my mum after a long day of exploring the city. We were famished and just wanted a hot meal and anything delicious so we ordered the Tsurutontan deluxe and udon pon dumplings to share. The menu was huge but having the top sellers marked out was really helpful, as well as having the staff explain the good stuff. 

To our surprise the food came out super fast and we inhaled the whole meal. My mum (who is usually picky about restaurants) was so impressed with the flavours, noodles, everything! We had never tried anything like the udon dumplings and they were so simple, yet so tasty with the perfect amount of crisp!

Because the food was so amazing I had to make sure I went back to try something else before I left the city. This time I dine solo and order the Sukiyaki udon for a nice meal to end a long day. I came in late around 9:30pm and it was just starting to wind down for the day so I was able to enjoy the ambiance and to my delight, the music. I will admit that I geek out over restaurants that play good music that I am into, so I had to post a video on Instagram when dvsn was playing! 

On a food level the Sukiyaki udon was the perfect amount of sweet, the noodles just right and beef not too chewy. Then the egg just added to this bowl of amazing flavours. 

I couldn't leave without at least looking at the dessert menu, and so I believe it was the restaurant manager(?), Christian, that recommended the red velvet cake that they were trialling from a nearby bakery (I forgot the name). I am so glad I took his recommendation because I must say it was just the tip of the iceberg - absolutely delectable. 

Both of my experiences at Tsurutontan were 11/10 and I am still raving on about it to my family and friends back home in Sydney. I mentioned to Christian that there is nothing like this (at least that I know of... and I am a self proclaimed foodie) in the market here udon wise and if there were Tsurutontan in Australia it would absolutely blow up! I am also secretly wishing one opens up here so I don't have to wait until I visit NYC again to dine at this amazing spot.

I like this place alot! It has great udon noodles, really fun appetizers, and decent drink options.  Some of the soups are so rich in flavor and are very good--and you can extra a large size for the same price as a smaller one. 

My only complaints are that some of the seating arrangements are cramped and you have to sit next to the person you are dining with rather than across from them, and a couple of the soups have been a bit one note. But try a few, there are some real winners.

Probably the best udon place I've had in New York yet. Also love that I can make reservations here, which is so rare to see in asian restaurants. 

Been to Tsurutontan about four times now and after trying a couple of different flavors, I would recommend either the curry udon or the beef udon.

curry udon: the curry flavors are great although the broth can be on the slightly thicker side so it's hard to finish an entire bowl. but the curry udon is my usual go to.

beef udon: the broth is a bit sweet for my liking; however, the beef itself is so tender and such a joy to eat. for those with a sweeter tooth, this might be the winner for you!

My favorite udon noodle spot in NYC by far. This place will lure you in with its everyday, all hours happy hour (at the bar), cool vibes, and keep your taste bud happy with a wide selection of udon - those soft, chewy and delicate-flavored noddles. The sizzling sukiyaki and the mentaiko caviar udon bowls are two my personal favs.

Word to wise: try the Green Tea Crepe for dessert. It's bomb dot com. And, don't overlook their apps - the soy garlic fried chicken and grilled duck breast are amazing. 

Their staff is also super friendly. Christian, their assistant GM, was super helpful on a busy night. And, he also provided us with some great recommendations for our friend who was a first time diner.
Undoubtedly the largest bowl of Udon I've found. The extra noodles are probably not necessary. The food is good, but not quite the quality you'll find at Raku or even Udon West.

My waiter was great, but that was the only great thing about my experience. I went there on the coldest day of the year so far and they must have seated me by an open door because it was ice cold. I had to keep my coat on the whole time. They give you insanely, comically huge serving spoons to eat with, which is awkward and annoying. Why can't I just have a normal sized spoon. The udon was ok, but not with braving the ice cold conditions.

I was hunkering for a great bowl of Udon; this place did not disappoint! 

My girlfriend and I were looking for a great place for noodles. We both wanted something authentic but with a price range that didn't break the bank. We got the authentic right but the price could be a bit better. The portion size aligned with the price but I was hoping for man than three pieces of pork. That being said, the pork was extremely tender and complimented the delicate broth nicely. I wasn't sure if a ponzu infused broth would work with such contrasting taste like pork and tempura vegetables but to my amazement the combination was delicious.

The winner hands down was the spicy based soup my girlfriend got and I would suggest this dish in favor of my own. 

Would I come back?? Yes!! Make reservations!!

This place has a massive menu almost too many things to choose, We decided on a seasonal udon the Seafood Chigae Udon, with Shrimp, Scallops and clams.  Sadly we didn't get the big bowl with this but I can't blame them because it needs to be in a stone clay pot to keep it cooking!  The udon quickly absorbs the soup so eat it as you go! I thought it was the right about of spicyness and flavor, the seafood was nicely portioned.

We got Fresh scallops and Soy garlic chicken, the scallops were fresh and creamy and nicely priced!  The soy garlic chicken was nice and crispy and the sauce made it have a nice flavor that made you dip it back and wipe the plate clean!

I think this place is a nice hit, not too pricey but definitely need to take another visit.  I went during a sunday and there was a short wait for two, so plan ahead!

As always check my photos out and my IG Jliueats

Mildly overpriced, but they sort of make up for it with large portions and a modern ambiance! 

I tried the seafood chigae udon ($23) which came bubbling in a hot stone pot. Unfortunately, I think this caused my noodles to be a little over cooked. Some of them were falling apart so it was hard to pick them up. 

The soup had an amazing flavor, but it didn't actually come with a ton of seafood (or definitely not enough to justify a $23 price tag). Another annoying thing was that I asked if they could make it spicier, and they said they could give me more spicy paste for $1.50, but the "spicy paste" just turned out to be gochujang. $1.50 for a tablespoon of gochujang (which isn't even spicy) is insane! I don't understand why they couldn't have just given me some red pepper flakes or anything. 

To be fair the server was very nice and offered to swap it for a different kind of spicy paste, but the I tried some of the other kind since my coworker had ordered it and it was somehow even less spicy. So definitely save your money and don't bother trying to make it spicy. 

Enjoyable meal, but if I come again I'll be ordering a different dish for sure.

It was a freezing night in NY, and I was craving soup and carbs! I had a late dinner date, and remembered that a good friend had suggested Tsurutontan. I had the vegetable udon and my friend had the chicken, and it was the best udon I ever had outside of Japan!!

I always want Tsurutontan to be better. The udon is great, and great udon is a marvelous thing. Unfortunately, there's not that much else going for it. The service is always a bit off - a little supercilious, not so attentive, just not quite right. The non-udon dishes look great and, for that reason, are all the more disappointing when they fall far short of good. 

If you go to Tsurutontan with those expectations, it can still be very enjoyable. However, if you don't mind substituting ramen for udon (and don't mind waiting for over an hour), you're better off at Ippudo, which is a short walk away. If not, and you don't mind a slightly longer walk and have cash, Cocoron will not disappoint. Unfortunately, the same can't be said for Tsurutontan.
Grilled duck breast and corn appetizer was amazing!! Tan tan ramen was great, consistency of noodles on point. Always go for thick noodle!!!

West of Union Square, this gem was exactly what we were looking for - romantic, authentic and delicious!! We got lucky as walk-ins to get a table after a short 15 minute wait (happy hour at the bar makes the time go quickly - get your sushi there - half price!!)  (Lesson learned : make a reservation.) 

The noodles were crazy delicious. I ordered the Tsuroton For & Sour Noodle - it was egg based which made it even more hearty. It wasn't too spicy but had just enough of a kick to satisfy my craving. I opted for the thinner noodles and a sake to round out my meal. The bowl was as big as my head (portions are large!), so if you're up for sharing, I would recommend a few starters and sharing an udon dish. 

The food is excellent - just wish the price point was a bit lower.....but regardless, I WILL BE BACK!

Great ambiance and service is attentive and helpful in answering questions but most importantly, UDON NOODLES DONE RIGHT!! Not to mention the great variety in types of udon - so many to choose from, you're going to want to keep coming back for more.

To start you need to check out their Seasonal Menu so you don't miss any must-tries before they rotate them out. If you head over any time soon, try the Sea Jewels appetizer - uni, ikura, sturgeon caviar, poached
"Onsen" egg with soy gelee! It is as good as it sounds. So fresh and amazing mouth feels - get it while you can! We also got the Soy Garlic Fried Chicken and Udon Pon Dumpling appetizers! Both very good - the dumplings made out of udon dough were surprisingly tasty and had a nice balanced crisp to them.

Now, on to the main show: THE UDON! PRO TIP: Regular and normal size bowls are equal in price so get it if you dare but eater beware don't underestimate the sizes - regular is already pretty big. (Photo of myself for size reference.) Off the Seasonal menu, my mom got the Seafood Chigae Udon which was perfect for her because she loves soft tofu stew and this was a perfect mix. I got the Spicy Tan Tan Udon - this broth was beautiful, flavorful, creamy and just the right level of spice! Another great thing is COMBO LUNCH SETS! For $3 more you can choose from a variety of rice bowls to get on the side. Like mother like daughter, we both got the Mentaiko Spicy Cod Roe bowl on the side. This family loves that salty taste on rice.

My sister - who has been before and is the one who brought us here. She ordered the same udon that she got the last time she was there: Uni Creme Udon which consisted of uni, tobiko caviar, shiso leaf
in uni crème broth. One little taste and I understood why she re-ordered this again. That uni creme broth is FIIIIRE. Highly recommend.

The Boy doesn't love noodles in broth too much so he opted for the Oyako Don (chicken, onion, egg simmered with sweet dashi broth). Donburis come with a small bowl of udon as well which The Boy kindly let me eat after I devoured.

ALL IN ALL 10/10 WILL BE COMING AGAIN. Yom-yom-yom.

Great appetizers! We had the seasonal uni cones and the wagyu uni nigiri sushi. We had to send back the first wagyu since they had cooked the beef and it was illustrated raw on the menu, but the second time it came out of the kitchen perfect and delicious!

The udon itself was pretty normal by socal standards. We got a cream udon and a curry udon. The downside is that this run-of-the-mill udon was priced like some godly udon.

The cocktails were similarly good but a bit pricey. In my opinion this is a good place to come if you want to impress someone with restaurant trendiness but not necessarily with food quality. Or just come for the appetizers!

Options galore and generally tasty. Large open space and great service. The uni udon was interesting, but I wasn't as big a fan of cold noodles. The hot udon was pretty good though, and the appetizers were fantastic, especially the spicy tuna tartar cones. They also had a yuzu sauce that's super delicious. Overall very nice.

ordered sea urchin(uni)+scallop+salmon roe in cold udon, about 32 bucks+tax+tips.

outstanding fresh n sweet uni (ichiban quality), scallop.

salmon roe was excellent, a bit salty.

the udon was impressive springy, chewy, with right cold temperature, very delicious with sashimi grade seafood.

udon soup base is daishi (white raddish) soy sauce, cold, sweet, n tasty. :p (i emptied the bowl that kind of good)

**
arrived by 5pm walkin, no wait line, no rsvp.

**
service was fast. the server was very attentive, as soon as you finish, they are aware to clean up n provide u the bill, even if it is not being asked.
1 hr in total ... be seated ... browsing menu ... taking pictures ... food sharing ...bill.

**
server recommended 
thin noodle with cold soup.
thick noodle with hot soup.

asked for personal size bowl if u share the food with your friends.

We arrived about 5 minutes to 5PM which is when they open for dinner and there was already a line waiting. So I suggest to come early or make a reservation prior to coming. There is also a considerable wait (about 5-7 mins) between getting the menu and actually ordering food. However the food does come out fairly quickly, considering how busy the restaurant is. 

I ordered the DUCK UDON and it was pretty decent. The soup/broth was a little more on the saltier side and didn't have any taste of duck, which was kind of a disappointment; the broth doesn't have great depth in flavor so it is easy to get tired of. The udon noodles (we get to choose between thick or thin, I chose thin) were very good; they were just the right chewy-ness and softness. They ran out of meatballs so I only got duck; the duck was cooked well and had good flavor. The other topping in my udon was also disappointing as I only got one piece of it. 
There is no price difference in a small or large bowl so if you're very very hungry I suggest getting the large bowl since the small is already pretty big and filling. Each bowl is definitely on the pricier side. 

tldr;
food 4/5
service 3.5/5
atmosphere 4/5 (it's on the louder side)
interior 3.5/5 (the entire restaurant is pretty dark)

- one of the few places open for dinner on christmas eve
- 10-20 min wait
- may be my new go-to for udon
- the ambiance is very trendy, not what I'd normally go for when seeking comfort food but I'm sure it's worked into the price
- pricier than what I'd normally expect to pay for udon but for the size (XL same price as regular so you may as well indulge) it's reasonable 
- recommend: waygu shabu udon
- will return to try other options

After I walked around Union Sq Christmas Fair I was hungry and decided to go again. I ordered the same thing but this time I felt really disappointed. When it comes to noodles in soup, the broth must be the soul. The broth is fine but not hot enough.... And I ordered a larger portion which has no additional cost, but it comes out smaller than I had last time... When you charge so much for a bowl of noodles, I expect the quality should be up to standard.. Too bad it used to be one of my favourites, but now I'm sorry I'm not coming back....

This restaurant is totally overhyped you would pay 20 over dollars for an Uni creme udon but what you get is a piece of uni lying on the a bed of udon with the soup being just mushroom soup from a can product. The appetizer I tried was hamachi carpaccio which was really unique with the presentation and design matching its taste. Overall, it would be a good place to go during Christmas only since it is k e of the few restaurants open on that day. Not recommended or at least the Uni creme udon.

This place is awesome. Saw this on insider-new York so come to try it out

Service- 5 stars 
James knew that this is the first we are here so he went through the menu with us patiently and told us that there is free upgrade from regular to large size of any udon.  The rest (I meant every single one of them, they refill water without u requesting it, smile  of the staff are very polite and efficient as well. 

Food- 5 stars
We ordered the uni udon.  I'm not a uni person but saw their uni ikura hotake cold udon and the beef curry udon pix and decided to give it a try.  The uni udon is surprising good compared to what I had before.

Made reservations ahead of time for a Monday night. So glad we did because it was super packed and a large party stepped in right after we did. I've heard a lot about Tsurutontan and how the large bowls cost the same as the smaller ones so I was super excited to try it. 

The atmosphere is quite dim and the decor is very modern. But due to the dark lights, it was no easy feat to take instagram-worthy photos.

The service is quick and attentive. Our server was super nice and made sure to explain the menu and what the most popular dishes were. We ordered the infamous spicy tuna tartar cone and was not disappointed. The tuna was so fresh and the cone paired so well with it. I'm drooling just thinking about it. The avocado puree at the bottom balanced the tuna out really well. 

I ordered the US Wagyu Shabu Curry (of course, the large) and was surprised how large the bowl really is. The udon noodles have a good consistency but I didn't think they were too special. The curry and the beef were very flavorful.

They also have a large array of drinks. I had the Akatsuki Mango Sangria but felt it lacked a punch. Didn't really taste much of the Ryujin Sake.

Very nice and tasty, the place is beautiful and feels like a bar with really good food. Since we came for an early dinner it wasn't do crowded and the waiting list was 15 min. 
The udon balls are huge and the sushi was delicious.

The only reason I did not give 5 stars is because there is always a wait. With or without a reservation I have had to wait for a table (and I have been four times). The restaurant itself is very nice, chic and large and the service is good. The food however is the real star. The udon soups are good but I highly recommend the dry noodles (sizzling udons, the beef sukiyaki is my favorite). Everyone I have brought to eat here loves it and I am still going back despite the wait times which should indicate how good the food is.

I ordered the Sukiyaki Udon with large noodles (one of the Top Sellers on the menu) and it was about $20. 

First thing I usually taste before eating the noodles, is the soup. The soup for this bowl of udon was sweet and very flavorful. It also leaves a sweet and salty aftertaste, which can be a bit much. 

OH, and the udon noodles are made fresh daily which is great. Who doesn't love fresh noodz?

Everything was cool here, I think I just don't love Udon honestly!! The tuna wonton cones were the star of the meal! The Udon bowls are GINORMOUS and could truly be two meals. The only thing we didn't LOVE was sitting at that counter where you could see the people sitting across from you- a little weird.
The noodles are just cooked, chewy, al dente. The soup base is good, not heavy. I want to step on the appetizers, uni, They present it in the salt box, very cute.

Came here on a chilly winter Monday and it was a great call. It was crowded but we had a res and were seated right away. I had contemplated going healthy but before my brain could interject, my heart went ahead and ordered the sizzling sukiyaki udon. I kid you not, my order was out within five minutes and arrived with my water. That is speed folks. It was both hefty and decadent as heck and I went to town. Felt like a sumo wrestler after but so did my wallet, cause it was a cool $18. 

Would come again for sure but this is not a mind blowing meal and does have a fast food feel.

Excellent udon spot with a massive selection. There are plenty of non-udon options to choose from as well. Would recommend the duck udon for something a bit lighter, sukiyaki udon if you're craving something more flavorful.

I came here for lunch right at noon when it opened with one of my friends on a Thursday. Originally we were a party of 3 but one person was running late and we were hungry and didn't want to risk having to wait longer for a table so we just were seated in the lower level at the long table seating for 2. It was unfortunate that they were unable to accommodate for the guest that was running a bit late, but I guess that with the high volume of lunch rush they want to get people in and out. 

Sabrina was our server and she was extremely kind, knowledgeable and helpful! She really helped make our experience at Tsuru ton tan a great one. I ordered the tsurutontan deluxe which had a nice light but flavorful broth with egg, chicken, beef, and tempura in it. I fell in love with the udon and was probably the best one that I've ever had! My friend who has a different taste palette ordered the sukiyaki udon which has a sweeter and more savory broth flavor which I found a bit too sweet for me, but my friend enjoyed his a lot. They have a selection of Lady M desserts to serve, but we were running low on time since we had to catch a bus later in the afternoon. I would recommend making a reservation when planning coming here to ensure that you get a seat! The price point is more expensive for udon/noodles, but I would say that its definitely worth the taste and flavor.

It's a nice space and the staff is courteous, but it gets really crowded and they encourage a quick turnover. The food is served quickly and you're rushed along to get you out as quickly as possible.

If you want a leisurely dinner to chat with friends, this is not the place. They want you to just eat and get out. The food is fine. The fried chicken appetizer was good. Skip the tofu and Brussels sprouts. Both were not good. I had the duck ramen and it was ok. Nothing particularly good. They also give a choice of thick or thin noodles, which I liked because I prefer thinner udon.

Overall, it's ok for a quick bowl of udon. I probably wouldn't actively choose to come back unless a friend really wanted to come here.

I came here for dinner one Wednesday night with my girlfriend after work. They open at 5:00 PM and we arrived shortly after they opened. There was already a line for people to be seated when we arrived. From what 
I noticed, it is better to have a reservation. After a 10 minute wait, we were seated. Our server James was very courteous and took time to explain the menu to us since this was our first time here. We ordered a large sized Chicken Udon (thick noodle) and a regular sized Sizzling Sukiyaki Udon. The food came in almost no time at all. Both dishes were amazing! The chicken and the udon broth was delicious and the Sukiyaki Udon was very rich in flavor. Highly recommend this place, but just keep in mind that it can get packed really quickly.

First and foremost, exceptional atmosphere. Modern, romantic, but also good for groups and after work meal. Super friendly staff. Got seated quickly. Were lucky not to wait on a random wee night. Noodles are excellent and chewy (great thing) and they offer you extra free noodles if you want. Portions are big. Their top seller appetizer (soy garlic fried tatsua chicken) is so yummy. Got the chicken udon (in thick noodles) and US wagyu shabu curry which is amazing!!! The thin noodles, the flavor, the broth. the quality of the beef just perfect. 
I would go with thin noodles. 
I would go again

Long wait even with a reservation. It was also super packed on a regular weekday for dinner. This place is 3 floors. There's a basement, 1st, and 2nd floor level. Bowls and food portions were pretty big. If you order the soup udon, you can choose between the thick or thin and regular or large size. FYI, the regular and large size are the same price so don't settle for a regular size!

Came here for lunch with my friend.  Very busy - recommend reservation.  It's pretty cool that their large and regular portion noodles are the same price.  Bowls are HUGE.  Could not finish.

What we got:
Soy Garlic Fried Chicken Rice Bowl - THIS WAS DELICIOUS.  I could've eaten this for my meal.
Sukiyaki Udon with Thick Noodles Large Portion - This was okay and had a light broth.  My friend liked this a lot.
Spicy Tan Tan Udon with Thin Noodles Regular Portion - Didn't love this as a noodle soup.

Service:
It took a long time for the food to come out once we ordered but our water cups were filled during that time!

I'll have to admit, I came by this restaurant with a friend after seeing it being featured on Insider on Facebook. Lots of our friends kept getting tagged in the post so the video popped up on my newsfeed quite a lot. Even if I didn't see it as much, I still would have made this location a top food destination because I love noodle soups and who doesn't like the thick udon noodles? 

I dined on a Friday afternoon and there was a lot of people. We put our name down at the front and wait time was about 7 minutes. However this was somewhat a good thing because it gave us plenty of time to look over the menu and being as indecisive as we were, it greatly helped us come to a final decision by the time we got seated. 

Interior: When you first walk in, you notice the bar and the stool seating by the door is used as a waiting area. The restaurant didn't look too big but there was a downstairs component (and perhaps an upstairs as well?) The decorations incorporated many aspects of wood and seemed appropriate with the general vibe. We were seated downstairs and the table setup was a bit  unusual compared to what we're used to. For a table of 2, we sat next to each other rather than across. Across from us were strangers and there were wooden beams separating us so that was a bit awkward. The seats we were at were like benches with a short back. This made it very difficult to properly hang our coats on, especially longer coats, so mine dragged on the floor.  At the table they also had little pebbles that the chopsticks laid on. 

Food: I ordered the duck udon and my friend ordered one of the spicy udon options. Just as mentioned on insider, the udon was served in bowls larger than your head and the noodles were thick and chewy. When you order, you  have the option to choose thick or thin noodles, and extra noodles (the large size) would be no extra cost. Although the large bowl was overwhelming at first, after digging in, the bowl felt more manageable. We didn't get appetizers but the neighbors across from us did and the were beautifully presented. 

Service: We felt a bit rushed from the second we were seated to when we paid. But i guess this was understandable due to the high volume of customers. Our waitress was very patient when we made our final deliberation and helped us answer any questions we had and made sure we didn't have any allergies. They seemed to be very accommodating if anyone in your group did. One thing that was a bit uncomfortable was how the waiters would pop up behind us to check up on us. (This was because of the way the tables and chairs are arranged). It gave a few surprising jumps. 

Bathroom: neatly hidden behind sliding wooden doors on the basement level with 2 stalls and a sink. The inside is quite small so it's better to wait outside. It was a bit claustrophobic when people insisted on waiting inside. 

Overall, given the high volume of guests, everyone handled it very well and tried their best to ensure the comfort of each guest. The food was also very good and I loved the huge bowls. It was a bit loud so don't expect it to be super romantic. I'm definitely up to getting udon here again in the future and would love to try some of their appetizers as well.

Came here for dinner without reservations but my husband and I was there before 5pm. Once they open up for dinner, we were seated within 15 minutes so we were pretty lucky. The decor and setting is nice but the seats are a bit cramped. We were seated in the middle and the seats cannot be moved.

I got the uni creme and it was good, the creme base was delicious but not much uni. My husband got the Tsurutontan deluxe, the broth was very light which is good. We also got the spicy tuna tartare cone which was mediocre. Overall, I would go back!

Best place to go on a cold winter's day and need some hot comforting love.  If you are a fan of mushrooms, definitely recommend the truffle mushroom app special served on a bed of fried noodles.  It was oozing with umami truffle flavor.

For my main, I ordered the Sukiyaki udon with extra noodles.  Same price as regular amt of noodles, so why not.  Little did I know they would serve it in a massive bowl made for giants.  Literally felt like Alice in Wonderland.  Surprisingly I paced myself and nearly finished the whole damn bowl.

Even had room for dessert.  We went with the trendy "Water Cake" which was really just clear jello shaped like a bubble.  Literally felt like Emperor and his New Clothes. 

Did I feel good afterwards? No, since my stomach felt like it kept expanding and was going to burst. Literally felt like Violet in the Chocolate Factory.  Nevertheless, my grandmother would have been proud of me for finishing my plate.  

Gotta come early or else you will wait a very long time.  So prepare to come as an early bird at 5pm.

I came here for lunch on a cold weekday. Noodle soup really hit the spot on these types of days. I was seated promptly during lunch hours. Inside decor felt super Japanese, loved it (not that I've been). 

The highlight of this place were the service, big bowls, and unlimited noodles. Yea you read that right, UNLIMITED. Our server explained the menu and the different categories of broths we can get. Bowls were around ~$20 and came in a gigantic bowl but it was definitely the not as much food as the bowls made it look. They'll definitely still fill you up though. I had the spicy tan tan, which was very rich and creamy. There must be dairy in it because I felt gassy all day (lactose intolerant). 

Verdict: I'll come here again!

Yummy food, great ambiance, and attentive servers.
Ordered the Sukiyaki, which was extremely filling and delicious. You could taste the freshness of the noodles, which are handmade.

I saw pictures of the udon here and this cold weather makes for perfect noodle soup weather. Came right when they opened and we're seated immediately at a bench set up sitting side by side. It was cute but a bit cramped

The curry deluxe is amazing. A bit pricey at $24 a bowl, but it comes with udon (extra at no additional al cost!), katsu, shrimp tempura and some scallions. One thing I don't like is fresh Katsu in soup, since then it loses it's crispiness. However, it was all still delicious. The curry broth was very good, not too thick or spicy but just the right amount.

Came here on a nice frigid day (believe it was about 15 degrees) since it was the perfect day for something like udon. Also saw many people's pictures of the giant bowls of udon here. The interior is pretty nice with a mixture of bar type seating for two and tables. I believe you only get a table if you've made reservations. Since we just came, we got he bar seating. So their selling point is for the price, you get a choice of regular serving or extra large serving. I had the wagyu udon with extra large serving. The udon came within 10 minutes or so. It's a large bowl of udon with thinly sliced beef. The udon was pretty good, beef had good flavor. I tried the curry deluxe and it tasted a lot better than mine. If you're ever in a bind of what to get, get the curry deluxe. I'm not sure if my bowl contained the extra large serving because I was still hungry after my bowl, but it could be because I ate very fast as well. Overall, would definitely come again for their udon whether it's a frigid day or not.

The excitement for this place seems exaggerated. Be prepared to wait a long time if you want to accommodate a large party on a weekend night, and there's just not much waiting room inside.

The first thing you'll notice from the menu is that everything is PRICEY. The free-of-charge extra portion inside of a large, Instragram-able bowl should have balanced things out, but the beef udon (sold out of the duck udon by 7pm) is neither interesting nor impressive. Especially with other great choices for udon in the city, it's difficult to recommend shelling out your paycheck here.

I saw a video on Facebook of "Biggest Bowl of Udon in NYC" and I was pretty much sold. Then my cousin came here the night before, and told me it was a must. So I had pretty high expectations going in, especially going on a day when it was single digits outside, I wanted nothing more than a big hot bowl of noodle soup.

They highlight the fact that you can upgrade from a medium to a large for NO CHARGE. Any China-man's dream. BUT, you are still paying over $20 for a bowl of udon, granted it is twice as big as your face. 

I ordered the Pork Belly udon with mushroom tempura special. And my friend ordered the Sukiyaki udon, which came with beef, vegetables and a perfect soft cooked egg. We both obviously ordered the large, but both did not finish. It definitely hit the spot, the broth was delicious, noodles weren't too heavy, and they don't mess around when you order the large -- or maybe we're just weak. 

I will definitely be back to try the other udons (the uni-udon and tsuratontan deluxe in particular)!

Uni cream udon is to die for. Chewy noodles swim in a rich, umami-bomb of a broth. This is definitely a feast for your tastebuds (and the downfall of your waistline). The portion is plenty, but the ratio of actual uni to the gigantic bowl is almost laughable. I shared this with two other people since this was more a snack stop, but next time I'll definitely finish an order on my own.

Homemade udon outside of Union Square. Came here for dinner on a Thursday night at 8:30 and the wait was 30 minutes for seats at the bar so try to make a reservation if possible. 

Extensive menu with a ton of udon options, sushi, drinks, etc. Option of thin or thick udon noodles (I recommend thick ones). They have both hot and cold options. Btw, their portions/bowls are HUGE. Enough for two meals! I ordered the pork katsu curry ramen, the udon with caviar and their sushi with salmon in it. 
Tip: The large (which comes in the huge bowl) is the same price as the medium so get an upgrade and bring it home. 

Sushi is delicious and tastes fresh. The udon was chewy and not soggy at all! The broth is flavorful and not overwhelmingly salty. The caviar udon was light and refreshing. I would recommend all of these dishes! 

The menu is on the pricier side (more than $20 for a bowl of udon) but the portions of the udon kind of make up for it.

Great udon restaurant off union square with excellent attentive service. The tsurutontan deluxe is amazing, and they give you the free option of extra udon. I was extremely full by the end. 

My partner had the wagyu udon but we felt the wagyu had been overcooked while soaking in the broth. 

This, along with the relatively high price for similar udon places resulted in the one star being docked.

One of my favorite udon place .. the food is awesome and always have season selections! Definitely would recommend their soup based and creme based udon. Rice dish is okay not as good as udon.

Service could get lousy from time to time when it is busy.

I have been to this place twice and I did not have to wait very long for a seat both times. The first time I came here was on a weekend at around 2:30 pm and I waited for about 15 minutes before we got seats. The next time I came here it was on a Monday at around 6 pm and I did not need to wait for seats. This place does get fairly packed so I got lucky both times! 

The vibe of this place is great, it is a nice place for a bowl of noodles during a cold day. There is a good amount of seating so you do not feel cramp or too close to a stranger as you are eating. The menu is extremely extensive and I don't think that you can go wrong order from any of the recommended items. They have something for everyone from cold noodles, rice to their famous hot udon. The bowls of noodles are HUGE and you can upgrade to a bigger size for free which is a huge plus in my books. 
-Mentaiko Caviar Creme: This is the perfect dish for those of you who love creamy soup bases, the soup base was very creamy and thick and the flavors went amazing together. 
-Sukiyaki Udon: My first couple of bites, I loved this bowl of udon since it was super flavorful but the sweetness of the sukiyaki based soup got tiring after a while and I got sick of the flavor so I would only recommend this if you are a HUGE fan of sukiyaki. 
-US Wagyu Shabu Shabu Udon: This is hands down my favorite bowl of udon. The soup base was delicious, it was not too strongly flavored but yet it went delicious with the udon. 

This isn't my favorite place for udon, as I find that their udon is a bit too soft for my liking but it is still a great place for lunch or dinner. Their soup bases are amazing and the portion sizes are very large!

This was my first time here! The atmosphere was very loungey, upbeat, and dim. 

The waiter was extremely polite and generous. He gave a run down of the different types of broths in the udon bowls. From clean beef-based broths to a dense creme to spicy curry sauces. Before ordering, the waiter would ask whether you want a large bowl or a small bowl (tip: a small and large bowl means you want extra udon noodles at no additional charge). I would definitely recommend asking for a large udon bowl :)

I decided to order the Wagu Mushroom Sukiyaki udon bowl It consists of wagu beef, shimeji, oyster mushroom, enoki mushroom, cabbage, in sukiyaki broth. The soup is perfect for cold icy weather, and for warming up those hungry bellies. The udon noodles were not mushy or pasty. They were chewy and tasted fresh. The broth was not too salty, but had a sweet and beefy aroma :). After 10 minutes of endless noodle slurping, I ended up waddling out of the restaurant, with NO REGRETS.

For about $30 including tax and tip, this restaurant definitely earned its reputation for serving the biggest udon bowl in NYC!

Tsurutontan has the BIGGEST bowl of udon in NYC! I've been here three times now and I always order the creme uni udon which has got to be one of the best things I've ever eaten in my entire life.

Bold statement I know, but this udon is so delicious that I've had dreams about it. Heck, one time I was craving it so badly, I almost went downtown in the middle of finals to eat a bowl of this delicious uni udon and had to do some serious soul searching to remember to put my exams first. 

The creme uni udon is so rich and flavorful and it comes with nice thick udon noodles (which are all made in house!!) that you can slurp to your hearts content. There is a nice lump of uni in the middle of the bowl, and if there is anything I would want to have improved about this particular udon bowl, it would be that I want more uni! Always more uni, please. 

The broth is heavy because it is made with creme, and you probably won't be able to finish a single serving on your own (unless you are really hungry), but you can always take it home to enjoy it later. After all, the best things need to be savored multiple times, right? 

The best part about this udon bowl (and any of their bowls) is that you can ask for a larger portion with no added cost, so might as well go big or go home. 

In addition to the creme uni udon, I have also had the pleasure of trying some of their sushi rolls, and I've enjoyed them as well, but I do think the star is the udon bowls. 

There's nothing better than a warm, rich bowl of udon to bring you back to life especially during this very cold NYC winter, and the creme uni udon is exactly the udon bowl to do it.

It was ok. I wished I knew the portion was big enough for two. It is not an authentic Japanese cuisine, if that is what you are looking for. The drinks were kind of watered down. Initially, I felt that the service is super friendly, but I guess not enough coordination, so many of them keep coming back to our table to ask questions. Probably every 3-5 minutes! At the end, we were kind of taking our time and break from eating because of the big portion, and 3-4 waitresses come asking whether it is done. I felt kind of rushed, even when the restaurant wasn't full. Unfortunately, I kind of regret coming here and spending that much. :(
Great food and great atmosphere. Everyone in our group enjoyed their udon, and the bowls are simply enormous.

Few days ago in very cold evening I have met my friend and we decided to come here to eat some hot udon soup. The place was very busy when we came in. The hostess told us that table will be available in 20-30 minuets and we agreed to wait for it at the bar. After 25min we have been seated. Our seats was right across the main entrance to the dinning room. While we were having the meal we felt very strong wind when somebody were opening the door to the restaurant. It was very unpleasant. But it wasn't any other place to move. We order Udon tempura soup with thick noodles and Crab Udon Soup with thin noodles. Both small portions ( they were pretty big). You can choose big portion without extra charge. Mine soup wasn't hot enough but it had very good flavors, not spicy, perfect with tempura inside and on the side. The menu looks very interesting, will defiantly come back. Taking one star away for "cold" moments and warm soup.

I'm sort of conflicted on this place.  We arrived at Tsurutontan on a Wednesday night around 6:35 pm, ~10 minutes shy of our 6:45 pm reservation.  

The front of the house was simply chaotic.  Despite the fact that there really wasn't a large crowd, we had to literally fight our way to the hostess stand.  I attribute part of this chaos to the diners themselves... yes you, line jumper! Walk in the door, shout, and elbow your way to the front of the queue!  God awful etiquette.  That said, it's the hostesses job to maintain some level of order.  I mean, come'on!

Anyway, our table was not ready and we were offered a seat in the bar room at the long counter-top ledge across from the bar itself.  The hostess graciously informed us that Happy Hour prices did not apply to the main dining area, so we should take advantage of it (and handed us a drink menu).  So... when we looked through the drink menu and saw an $8 Sapporo draft and $11/$12 cocktails, we were kinda confused.  We saddled up to the bar and inquired about the drink specials.  Instead of reciting the drink specials, the bartender said "it's in the menu over there."  We apparently missed the plastic encased pop-up menu on the counter-top and assumed it would be in the menu the hostess had handed us.  Our table was ready before we could order a drink thanks to the confusion at the bar and we ended up paying double at our table.  So much for hospitality.

Before we head on to the meal, a quick shout out to our waitress.  She was warm, friendly, and took the time to explain the menu and answer our questions as first time diners.  Amazing service.  Anyway, onwards we go.

At the suggestion of the table next to us, we ordered the maitake mushrooms over small bed of fried noodles.  Absolutely incredible dish.  

For mains, we ordered Tan Tan Udon and Nabeyaki Udon.  Kind of crazy... you're offered the choice of a large or regular bowl of Udon at the same price... so we both chose the large bowl.  Nice touch.  The udon and broths were pretty solid.  The Tan Tan broth had the perfect amount of spice and the Nabeyaki broth was super clean and fresh tasting.  

That said, the food and service in totality did not meet our expectations.

Best place to go on a cold winter's day and need some hot comforting love. If you are a fan of mushrooms, definitely recommend the truffle mushroom app special served on a bed of fried noodles. It was oozing with umami truffle flavor.

I feel like I'm missing something about this place. I've been quite a few times with a variety of friends and family; they all love it, but everything I've ordered personally has been bland and disappointing. I wasn't particularly impressed by the uni udon, the duck udon, or the wagu beef appetizer, which all tasted sad and lacking flavor in bowls way too huge that felt like poor overcompensation. With each meal, and there have been several, I've looked around my table at smiling, satisfied faces and just felt... lost. It's all really just okay. At best.

To their credit, I think TsuroTonTan has a fantastic (and incredibly underrated) cocktail menu. Each time I've been here, my cocktail has been the saving grace of my entire dining experience. Seriously: for as disappointing as the food is, TsuroTonTan may have some of my favorite cocktails in this whole crazy city. I'd come back again just to sit at the bar... just maybe on a full stomach.

SERVICE HERE IS PHENOMENAL!! Our server was James and he provided us information on the types of udon to guide us through our decisions.

We had the spicy tuna tartare cones $12 which consisted of avocado purée, micro shiso, and wonton skin. They were so cute and delicious! For the udon, we shared a large portion of Tsuruton Curry Deluxe $24. We had big spoons to help ourselves to whatever we wanted from that giant udon bowl into our smaller bowls :)

The noodles here are amazing. They come in the biggest bowl I have ever seen! Can upgrade the size with extra noodles at no cost, but the original amount was more than enough for me. They do to-go boxes so don't fret if you can't finish, though noodles will get soggy when kept in broth. 
Though I felt it was a bit on the expensive side, the food and service were both great.

I ordered Fried chicken and 2 kinds Udon.
They are too salty so after eat it I should drink lot of water . 
Please think about it.
