This restaurant is one of those places where the indecisiveness kicks in for everyone -  it's so hard to decide which udon to get because everything on the menu looks so freaking good and it doesn't help that they have photos on their menu! But great tip - the "regular" and "large" size udons are actually the same price, so I'd recommend everyone in your group to order the large so that you can get a taste of each other's dishes. The line is usually insane at all hours, but they do take reservations on Resy for smaller groups.

By now, I've tried almost everything on their menu - all udons are pretty good; some are better than others but I think it is really a matter of personal preference. You can never really go wrong here. Today, I tried the Mentaiko Ankake Udon, which was basically udon noodles in egg drop soup. This was one of the lighter options as it had no meat in it, but definitely very flavorful and satisfying. I would go for this option if you are not too hungry and want something simpler.

From the numerous times I've been to this restaurant, I'd say my favorites are the Tan Tan Udon (if you want spicy), the Mentaiko Caviar Udon (if you want cold), Katsu Curry (if you want heavy). I would not recommend the Uni Udon - they really skimp on their uni. This restaurant is a good option for anyone that's craving a nice warm bowl of udon on a cold day. I'd say this place is more geared towards American customers than a traditional Japanese customer base (Raku in the East Village is a better option for authentic Japanese udon).

This place (whose name I cannot pronounce) excels at pairing udon with a wide range of Japanese food.  You can get everything from katsu, karaage, wagyu beef, sukiyaki, curry, duck, and more all mixed into an extra large bowl with an extra large portion of udon.  If you want to try something new, I would recommend the Truffle Creme and Crab Mushroom Udon which is a creamy white broth with crab and maitake mushrooms.  The udon texture is excellent and the food on top of the udon is what you would expect from a Japanese restaurant.  Not a fan of the karaage chicken and haven't tried the sushi.

Definitely consider coming in for lunch and adding a mini rice bowl for 3 dollars.  Though, it is probably not a good idea to eat both the extra udon and a rice bowl by yourself.

To recap, this place has excellent variety, big portions, and tastes amazing.  It's a bit pricey but you'll feel really really full for about 30 bucks.  Not recommended for low sodium or low carb diets and definitely doesn't have enough veges but great option for everyone else.

Overall a solid udon place BUT today was a bit disappointing...

My curry deluxe udon was missing green onions (see pic), and I saw the host check the bowl before he came to the table. He SHRUGGED and told the waiter to delivered it, which I hoped meant that he'd come back with the green onions later but nope I had to order it myself. Not the best service today.

Other than that, the food tasted great. We ordered the tuna tartare cones (has avocado, yum) and the vegetarian fried dumplings (very interesting flavor not sure I'd order it again).

Made reservations through their portal and it worked out well

Boy. Let me tell you. This restaurant is the restaurant of my dreams. The interior, the offering, the professionalism. I was in a whirlwind of awe and was glad to have been sat right away!

The beginning of our food journey went off to a little rough start. My boyfriend and I walked in and the host was about to seat us. However, a family of four came in after us and were being fussy when the hostess told them there was a wait. So for SOME reason, the hostess decided to seat them before us without informing us so it seemed that she was tending to them before us, even though we were there first. A simple communication could've cleared up the air. Having been a hostess for 3+ years, I was very critical and turned off by this.

Anyways, we were sat right away and were in awe of all the choices of udon. Our server was very attentive and very professional. I ordered the Truffle Mushroom Creme with Crab udon with thin noodles and my boyfriend got the Curry Deluxe udon with thin noodles. I love how you have the option to choose your noodle size.

Additionally, there are 2 sizes for udon and they're the same price. There's a regular and a large. The large just has more noodles, same amount of broth. If you have the appetite, I recommend getting a large. I got a regular because I knew I was eating a lot more that night.

Both udons were absolutely delectable and the bowls were HUGE! Even the regular size was amazing. The broths were so flavorful and delicious. But beware, this place does get pricey after tax and tip. But this place is definitely one of the restaurants that I MUST try every time I come to New York. There are so many other bowls that I wanted to try. Good job Tsurotontan. You guys are definitely one of my favorite restaurants.

First visit - Loved the service; Loved the food.  The waitress explained that I can get extra noodles for free and she recommended Beef Udon and Mentaiko Caviar Udon, which we got. It was super delicious. She refilled our water and served us constantly. Loved it.  My friend and I finished the noodles so fast; we even drank the entire soup from Beef udon. 5 stars for sure!!!

Second visit - I went with two friends who've never been there and sat at the bar. The bartender just left the menu in front of us and didn't ask or explain anything to us. We asked for water. We asked for plates. Bar was pretty empty when we sat there. We ordered Tsurotontan Udon, Sukiyaki Udon, and Mentaiko Caviar. 
- Tsurotontan Udon was delicious; the soup was perfect in flavor too (except we asked for tempura to be on the side, but it was still in the bowl, so it was super soggy). 
- Sukiyaki was super sweet and came out regular (even tho we ordered extra)
- Mentaiko Caivar Udon.... omg... had multiple hair wrapped in its udon noodles even before i got to mix it with the caivar. I usually take photos before I eat and the restaurant is dark, so if I didn't turn my flash on, I wouldn't have seen it. It had MULTIPLE HAIR wrapped in the noodles!!!!! GROSSS!!!! So I called the bartender and she said she will talk to manager, but I lost my appetite, so i said i don't want the noodles anymore. The bartender brought out a free dessert but it did not make up for the lost appetite. 1 star.... 

Bathroom rating - 4/5 (very clean)
Fair.  Decent. Huge place with impersonal bus terminal feel. Good quality standarized food.
It was a bit pricy for what you actually get.  In the duck udon it tasted very oily.  In the tempura shrimp it was soggy but the actual broth was good.  As for a onetime experience it is ok.

This is one of the best noodle places I have been to. My friends and I made reservations the night before and it was surprisingly very open. The place also has a 15 minute grace period for you to arrive just in case the people in your party are running late which ours were. They can only seat you once everyone has arrived.
First off the restaurant was really nice and modern. The food was very good and our waitress was very nice to walk us through the menu since it was our first time there. There were a lot of varieties such as hot or cold noodle dishes, curry or creme. We started off with the spicy tuna tartare cone which was very delicious. It was really light yet was filled with a generous layer of tuna and avocado. For our main dish, we all ordered different udon dishes. We had chicken, tsurutontan deluxe, uni creme, and wagyu udon. My dish was the uni creme and that broth was very rich in flavors. I couldn't stop sipping it with my udon noodles. The uni was really fresh but there was only a bit they put in dish. The only thing that bothered me was the scales? in dish. We all enjoyed the dishes a lot and there were a lot of flavors in each dish. The best part was that we could upgrade to large noodles for no additional cost. 
I will definitely be coming back to try the other dishes. I definitely recommend making reservations ahead of time since there can be a long wait.

First off, the name TsuruTonTan is creative af. Tsuru for the slurping sound while eating the udon, ton for the kneading/shaping of the udon, and tan for the sound of cutting the udon -- it's a perfect name for a place with udon that is artistically arousing. I love udon and this place offers such a great variety with or without broth, cold or hot, with thin or thick noodles, and boring size or FACE BASIN SIZE. They have equally great alcoholic and nonalcoholic drinks as well. People who don't like noodles fear not because they have a wide selection of appetizers and donburis for rice lovers. Their soy garlic chicken appetizer was tbh nothing special, but it was good. We had the sukiyaki udon with and without broth and a curry udon... all were good and it just felt super hearty and warm slurping a huge ass bowl of yummy soup and noodles. This is a place that you come back to because you want some nice udon that is either v traditional or deviated from basic broths and toppings, yet still authentic enough that it is consistent in flavor and texture. I mean I would come back for the face basin alone, but I'd like to try the different soup bases/toppings and temperatures.

I can say the fish is really fresh. The noodles are okay. Nothing special just the bowls are huge. I will come back for the sashimi but not the noodles. But the appetizer is really in a cone with fish. Anything fish related is really good. Definitely will come back here to try their sashimi. Come to try the noodles here at least once. It's a cool experience. Ambience is really cool.

I went to the restaurant with my husband in Union Square on last Friday. The woman who works there and look like a manager. She gave me bad service and judge us as not important costumer. She took us to the counter seats even the restaurant was just opened and empty. We asked for two people's table and she said it's all reserved. We were about to leave, then other waitress came to ask what happened? We said we don't like the table. She took us to upper level and there a lots of couple costumers and the tables were almost empty. Even she offered us the table, we didn't like the attitude of the woman manager. We left without ordering and we stopped and told the women manager how we didn't like the table situation and lied to us that table were all available. She didn't say sorry and she gave me weird look. The restaurant has no idea how to treat the costumer and do not judge we were Japanese. It's Supposed to be Japanese restaurant but it's not anymore. Sorry about the reputation.

Tsurutontan just killed the game for me bc this place was so freaking good and I'm sad it's so far away from me. I thought Marukame udon (in Hawaii) was the best thing ever, but this place definitely takes the cake. The waygu was so bomb! The restaurant itself is pretty small and they don't seat you unless your entire party is present.

Tsurutontan offers a variety of Japanese-inspired dishes in a contemporary digs. While Udon is their focus, I've equally enjoyed their small dishes and their cocktails. This is a solid option for good food and efficient service in the Union Square neighborhood.

SO many noodles in a giant bowl! Came here for a friends birthday and it was great! The interior is beautiful, the food and drinks are both great, the server was very nice and attentive. Will be back!
the portions are HUGE here! my favorite is the tan tan udon and the uni creme udon and my favorite starter is the soy garlic fried tatsuta chicken.

It's the perfect noodle place on a cold winter night. The portion sizes are very generous and they have so many options! I got my favorite shrimp tempura udon and almost could not finish the LadyM green tea crepe cake because it was so big. Make reservations early because you will wait over an hour on a Friday night. The interior is spacious & stylish. The original location is in Tokyo.
Fast service and perfect tempura. Had that with small udon noodles. Broth was flavorful and the price was good for the portion.

This place is a gem. 
The noodles are very unique and there are so many options to choose from. If this is your first time, you have to try the tan tan noodles. The flavor is incredible and the portions are generous (though it can be a bit pricey). 
The decor has an oriental vibe and it's pretty dope.

Best to make reservation and avoid average wait time of 30min - 1hour. 
For udon, they ask you if you want Large or Regular. Large basically means more noodles - both the same price. 

This place is good for large groups. Their second floor table was big enough for my group of 10. 

I tried the following items so far. 

Uni and Seared US Wagyu Sushi ($25)
Picture on the menu is misleading. Wagyu was cooked medium and uni didn't taste too fresh.

Spicy Tuna Tartare Cone ($12)
Tasty but thinner cone would have been better for more tartare flavor. 

US Wagyu Shabu Udon ($19)
I liked the simplicity of the broth. But didn't think it was extraordinary compared to other udon places in St Marks (ie Udon West). 

Sukiyaki Udon ($20)
Too sweet. This udon includes variety of toppings like greens, poached egg, mushroom and meat but the soup was way too sweet.

Came here for the second time. My first time was a while ago, but I remember we got the uni creamy udon (forgot the exact names of) and curry udon for my friend. I remember both of the dish being good so I came here today again with another friend. We got here around 12:30 pm on a Saturday. We got seated right away without waiting (probably because they open at 12 noon). We sat at a bar area, the server checked our coats. 
Ordered tan tan udon and sizzling suki yaki udon.
The server asked if you want thick or think noodles for the udon (got thick one for sukiyaki and think for tan tan) then he asks if you want regular or large size (same price) . We both got large. Didn't order appetizer because we knew how big the the portion would be. I saw this couple next to us sharing the large bowl.
Everything was pretty good for today's lunch. It's pricey for udon bowl to go over $20.
They have so many different kinds of food on their menu not just udon (I have attached the menu) that I would probably come back for it.

Massive (and kind of excessive? Lol) portions of noodles but it was really good and worth the semi hefty price tag, I mean it is New York City after all. You will not leave this place hungry at all.

 I got the hot and sour udon which was really good but not that spicy. My friends and I shared the dumpling appetizer which was delicious (but 11 dollars for 5?!) and the edamame (this was a cold dish however I felt it could be better if they came out steamed and hot, also needed a bit more salt for flavor). 

All in all a pleasant experience! Will come back for more.

Definitely worth the hype. I shared the Tsurutontan Deluxe with a friend along with the seared salmon and snow crab sushi roll. Everything tasted fresh and the broth was flavorful without being too heavy. I loved the chewy texture of the thick udon noodles. I can't wait until my next visit~
Great Udon and big portions!!! Come super hungry and be ready to eat! We tried the Udon with been sukiyaki and the stir fry Udon. They were all good.

I really liked my dinning experience here. I had the deluxe udon and it was amazing. Sizing up your udon is also free, but I didn't go for it since I don't eat a lot. My friends and I also ordered a sushi roll and the pork belly dish. Both dishes were so amazing. One of my friend ordered an uni cream udon while my other friend ordered a curry udon. I heard the uni cream udon was awesome but the curry udon was meh. The soup was too salty and thick. 

I really like my udon tho! Just wish it wasn't so expensive and difficult to get a table. I had reservation and still had to wait a good 20 min before getting seated. I would come back!

Oh Tsuru, you've slipped so much service wise since you first opened!

Back in the late summer / early fall, this place was great.  But that was when the crowds and waits were much smaller.

Each and every time we've come since then, the experience has gotten progressively worse.  And it completely bottomed out yesterday.

One of my biggest pet peeves is having to wait for a table even when you have a reservation.  And I thought yesterday's wait was excessive and could have been handled better. We had a 8:45 reservation and were not seated until 9:20.  When we checked in at the hostess area a couple of times, the staff was not particularly friendly and there were no sincere apologies about having to wait.

On the bright side, I admit the food here is still really good and tasty. So I cannot give it 1 star.

But the bad service didn't end once we got seated.  We ordered a round of drinks when our appetizers came and we didn't receive them until after we finished our meals. We timed it and it took a half hour. It was obvious that the waiter forgot about it, but he mumbled some bogus excuse.  And of course we were charged for them.

To top this all off, when the manager checked in with us at the end of our meal, he wasn't initially receptive to our complaints.  He made a comment that he had to "investigate" before he could remove that round of drinks from our bill.  

I'm sorry, but this is probably the first time I've experienced a manager not understanding and recognizing the customer is usually right. I think this properly sums of the kind of service we received all night.

All in all, 4 star food but 1 star service. We will not be back.

Between a 2 and a 3.  I know you all love this place, so hear me out.

One of my friends was in from out of town and wanted to go to Tsurutontan.  Making a reservation was easy.  I arrived a little early and I could not believe how packed this place was.  It was 19 degrees out, and I chose to wait outside instead of inside because of the sheer number of people packed into the tiny front room.  The entire waiting area was so jammed I felt like I couldn't breathe.  My friend arrived about 5 minutes late for our reservation (7:15).  We ended up being seated around 7:30.  

The dining area is much less crammed, although you are seated on these little fairly uncomfortable benches.  Our server greeted us right away, and she was great & attentive.  She went through the menu with us and pointed out some of the more popular items.

My friend ordered the duck udon ($18).  I hadn't been feeling well all day, so I chose to go with the decidedly plainer vegetable udon ($16).   That's a pricy bowl of noodle soup, even for those of us who are numb to NYC-sticker shock.  

My udon was relatively plain but had a nice underlying flavor to it.  The noodles were perfectly chewy.  I tried some of my friend's duck udon.  The duck was good and the meatballs were an interesting and well-thought out addition.  

I tried some of the tempura that my soup came with.  When I cut into it, I realized there were shrimp?  Now... here is what bothers me about this.  I have a family member who is extremely allergic to shrimp.  I explicitly asked for the vegetable udon which comes with veggie tempura.  Our server repeated it back to me.  But somehow I ended up with shrimp in my tempura?  I find this to be irresponsible and dangerous.  I actually like shrimp but this bothers me on a personal level.  

Also, I know the larger and smaller portion sizes are the same price, but I found that the smaller portion was smaller than my expectations.  I finished mine off easily and got a cookie on the way home.  

Our bill came out and I realize they had actually charged me for the shrimp udon ($17).  I'm not going to make a big fuss over a dollar but ... those with food allergies, beware.   

One other thing to note was that the bathroom was sort of gross.  Do with that information what you will. 

All in all, it's a shame because I actually thought the food was quite nice and our server was sweet, but the whole experience felt clunky and uncomfortable.

I'd give this place at least 4 stars if it weren't for the utterly ridiculous host/hostess experience.

This is a Japanese izakaya with emphasis on udon noodles, which are very good indeed: freshly made in-house daily and cooked in their own broth, either classic dashi or sukiyaki-style (sweeter) and served with quality toppings. Some of the appetizers we had were good -- soy garlic fried chicken, a roasted mushroom special -- while some (the sushi rolls) were just OK. 

The vibe of this place is buzzy fun lounge. Strangely, the food and drinks menus seem like they are from utterly different restaurants; the food menu is typical Japanese pub style, glossy with pictures of the dishes, while the drinks menu is sedate with just text, like it came from a restaurant in a suburban strip mall. But the serve is highly competent and solicitous, and your server can explain everything about the sakes they have (they should consider adding midsize carafes instead of just bottles and overpriced glasses).

Now for the host/hostess experience. The word I'd use to describe it ends in "show" and probably does not pass Yelp's editorial guidelines. We made a reservation for four on Resy for 7:45 on a Saturday night. When we got there -- on time -- the entrance and bar areas were jam-packed like a Tokyo subway car at rush hour. We had to elbow our way to the host/hostess stand, where we were told -- surprise, surprise -- that they were running behind. 

We had to wait three quarters of an hour for our table. During this time, I got a good look at the hostess display. Apparently they were backed up because there were five 4-tops with checks down but not leaving. I'm sorry, folks, but if that many parties "aren't leaving," it can't be because they are all hogs or drunk. This restaurant isn't managing its reservations well, which is borne out by the many other reviews here with the same complaint. They are taking reservations they shouldn't be taking, or underestimating time spent per meal. I don't think it's because the kitchen gets into the weeds at peak volume, because our food came out in a timely manner. Many of the people who jam-packed the foyer that night were walk-ins (who were told that the wait was 1-3/4 hrs), but I overheard at least a dozen parties being told that their reserved tables weren't ready.

This is still one of the best udon places in NYC because there isn't much competition. We still prefer Raku in the East Village, but since Raku is small and doesn't take reservations, it's not a realistic option on a Saturday night when it's freezing outside. But when Raku opens its second location in Soho, this place will have to up its front-of-house game.

This just might be my favorite restaurant in NYC! I've been probably close to 10 times and it never gets old. The udon here is better than the udon I ate in Tokyo. The sushi is great, but too expensive for the amount--stick to ordering the udon (the Waygu Udon is the best). And don't expect to walk right in at a typical eating hour: reservations are necessary.

Finally writing my first review this year! Unfortunately, it's not a good one. 

I came by with a friend to check this place out after hearing about it a while ago, it was during lunch over the weekend and everything started out fine. We were greeted by the ladies at the door when we walked in. It wasn't too busy that time around 12:20ish and there were 3 other groups waiting for seats. I mentioned we have a party of 3, but one of my friends was still on the way and asked about the wait time. They said it would to take 20-30 minutes to get seated. I told them that was fine and asked to put my name on the list. 

My other friend came after 35 minutes and when I went to ask about our seats, the response I got back was that we actually have to wait another 20-30 minutes since our full party just got here. I was so disappointed to hear that. It seemed like they moved our name to the bottom of the list and we basically wasted the first 30 minutes waiting there. I was starving by that time.... :(

After waiting for about an hour, we eventually got our seats. I noticed there were empty seats for bigger groups and just wished they gave us those seats to share! (I wouldn't mind! I was just soooo hungry!) They also don't serve food at the bar, we tried.

Now moving onto the food, you can choose regular portion or get large for the same price on their noodles and there's also a thick or thin option. I asked for thick noodles but got thin ones when it finally came out... apparently, there was a kitchen miscommunication and they gave me thin noodles by mistake. The waiter was quick to realize that and went back to the kitchen to get the right udon. When I got it the second time, it was the right thick noodles but the portion was much smaller (I asked for large), I finished eating my noodles in 5-6 bites. It was waaay less than my other friend who got an order of large thin noodles. I ate mine in half the time...even though I got my noodles 10 minutes later. I left the place feeling half full and a bit unsatisfied with my meal...so much for having a big bowl! I would still recommend getting the thick noodles since they're more chewy and I think taste better than the thin ones. You'll probably get more noodles if you order thin ones so keep that in mind! (or maybe I just eat too much..!).

In terms of the flavor, I don't recommend their tan tan noodle or the curry soup base, they weren't that good. My other friend got the new flavor on a separate menu, crab and mentai caviar ankake udon, and that was probably the best option out the 3 we ordered.

Overall, I didn't enjoy the experience due to the long wait time and that the kitchen messed up my order. I do recommend making a reservation before you go so you don't end up having to wait that long like I did! Food was just ok so I would not wait an hour (or even 30 minutes) to get it.
I order the sushi every time, it's amazing! The drinks are strong and delicious, I love trying a new cocktail with each visit and have yet to dislike any of them.

I really enjoyed this place. Deceptively large and very modern and sleek, you need to make a reservation to come here. My friend said it is the only one of its kind in America and they make their udon noodles fresh each day. We started with the spices tuna appetizer (think spicy tuna in a little cones) and it was quite good. I had the vegan option for the Sizzling sukiyaki udon (with thick noodles) and thought it was delicious. Great flavors and just the right amount.

These udon bowls are HUGE! And super tasty. I love the variety of udon broths that you can choose from. 

I got the wagyu udon and was extremely satisfied with my decision because the meat was so tender and the broth was very delicious. The udon noodles are freshly made and I love the chewiness.

This place gets super busy so make a reservation!

Great happy hour, beautiful space and wonderful warming food.  Plus top notch, friendly, attentive service. I had far better service here than from the most expensive restaurants in the city. We were sitting next to a raucous party literally SHOUTING at the top of their lungs and when we asked waitress if there was anything to be done, they made very effort to move us to a quieter table. Cheers to good food and customer service!
Quick service, nice staff, good food. I got one of those rice bowls and it was good, but I wish it had more flavor in it.

Saw this place on an insider video on Facebook and wanted to go immediately. Tip: make reservations online (you can keep also change the time last minute if you're running late lol) to avoid an hour long wait, which would not have been worth it. Anyway, after a rainy day, udon soup seemed perfect. We tried thick and thin noodles and thick udon noodles definitely tasted better. I also really liked the duck meat in my duck udon but the meatballs were just okay. Also the broth seemed like it needed a bit more of a kick-perhaps I should get the spicy one next time? It just seemed to be missing a little something, plus we paid like $18 for each bowl so I had pretty high expectations. you can also order a large and get extra noodles for free, which I definitely recommend. To conclude, not sure if it was worth $18, but definitely worth one try.

Had one of the best textured udon at this place and the soup varieties were also tasty. We had the deluxe, which was light and had a lot of varieties of seafood, and the truffle creme with mushroom and crab, which was heavy and creamy. The uni and seared wagyu sushi was also excellent. The lychee desert was also flavor-able. The water ball desert was interesting but per someone had it in Taiwan, did not live up to the original. 

Place was packed on a Friday night so reservation is highly recommended.

Never had udon before. Only had ramen for the first time in the last 18 months (but I've eaten at Ippudo in Hell's Kitchen, Tokyo and Yokohama since then.) So, call me a novice, or call me someone who's had the best and knows what it is. 

This Tsurutontan place? Awesome. So many choices it can be overwhelming. This will help. Get the Truffle Creme with Crab and Mushroom. See, that simple. Seriously. Get that one. As most all their dishes, it comes in a bowl big enough to make you think you might be able to slip in and swim in the broth. I would if I could. 

The truffle cream and crab and mushroom is just, wow kind of good. You won't be disappointed.

I love noodles in soup, but especially udon or ramen. There are plenty of ramen joints in NYC, but not too many that are solely devoted to udon. This place really does udon justice.

When this place first opened, the lines were insane, but now the hype seems to have died down a bit and you can actually get a seat around dinnertime if you're in a group of 2-4 people. Once you sit down, you're served pretty quickly, and the menu is highly visual -- which I LOVE! So far, I've tried the following:

Appetizers
- Soy Garlic Fried Tatsuta Chicken
- Spicy Tuna Tartare Cone
- Hamachi Carpaccio
- Creamy Spicy Shrimp Tempura
- Kuro Buta Pork Kakune
- Corn Fritters

Udon
- Truffle Creme Udon with Crab and Mushroom
- Tsurutontan Deluxe
- US Wagyu and Mushroom Sukiyaki 

My favorite of the appetizers would probably be the fried chicken and spicy tuna tartare cone. The fried chicken reminds me of a better version of the soy garlic Bonchon chicken, and the tuna tartare cones are just the perfect bites of spicy tuna goodness. I had all my udon prepared with thick udon, which is always the perfect chewy consistency! Of the udon, I loved the Tsurutontan Deluxe, followed by the Truffle Creme. The Wagyu one was good, but didn't feel like anything special.

Food was good but still really upset with the experience. I made a reservation for 8:00, got there early, and was told I'd have to wait 15 min from my res time. I waited for 45 minutes. That is absolutely ridiculous. And after asking them after a half an hour of waiting how much longer they said I'd be next to be seated- I watched 4 parties go in front of me after that

Came here on a Saturday night around 8pm. It is absolutely packed so I would recommend going online and making a reservation in advance if you don't want to wait to long. We ended up waiting around 20 minutes with our reservation.

When we were seated our server explained the menu to us and gave us some recommendations. We all ended up getting the spicy tan tan udon noodles. She told us that there we could get extra udon noodles for free so we opted for that. However all my friends didn't really notice that there were extra noodles there (the bowls are huge but the portion size didn't really seem that big). The noodles themselves tasted fresh and weren't too chewy. It really grabbed onto the soup base well. The soup itself wasn't that spicy. It comes with some pork bits but I wouldn't really recommend mixing it with the soup because most of it sinks to the bottom and is hard to fish out without drinking the entire soup base. Overall it was a nice place but not really filling unless you maybe order appetizers or something. My friends and I actually ended up getting more food at another place after.

Kara age is soooo good and the udons are also sooooo hearty. I love this place. The only thing is that the service could improve. Requests can be forgotten or slow. Also, it is strange that the drinks at the bar aren't available in the dining area and that you can't go to the bar and order it once you're seated in the dining area.

If you enjoy a good bowl of udon noodles, this is the place to be. There's nothing really fancy going on but they serve you bird bath sized bowls of noodles. 

We got the seasonal uni cone and the sea jewels which were great starters. The "regular" sized bowl of udon was big enough to share and the donburi was very satisfying. 

Overall I'd recommend this place. Do make your reservations because they can get packed.

I came here for a friend's birthday this past Saturday. It was very snowy so trains were delayed. We had a reservation for 11 people- 10/11 people were there however our hostess refused to sit us until our last person showed up. I thought she should have been more understanding- plus the 10 of us were making the place even more packed and uncomfortable because she wouldn't seat us. She was also just a little rude in general. 
Our waitress however, was very kind and helpful. The udon bowls are huge and you can get extra noodles for free which is nice. I decided to try the ikura udon since I love ikura- wasn't that impressed with it and I thought the noodles were a little over cooked...if I decide to come back, I will definitely try something else. Also just FYI if you want to bring a bday cake in it's $3 per person- regardless of how many people there are. I understand that there's a fee for bringing in dessert but I just thought it should be a flat fee.

This is a great shop for ramen and a very convenient location near union square. The ambience is luxurious but not stuffy and the food is delicious. Service is prompt and helpful and portions are generous. The only reason I did not give this restaurant five stars is because it is quite expensive for what it is, in my opinion. Ordering an udon main and an appetizer (or more, if you order a drink) will be at least $20-30 which is pretty pricey for soup.

Had some delicious wagyu udon here. The bowls are huge. Soup was flavorful, wagyu was delicious, and large udon portion. The tuna tartare cones were also delicious and fun to eat. The restaurant looks fancy and is pretty big. Menu has many options, with helpful pictures. They also have an interesting cocktail and alcohol list.

Waiters are very patient in explaining to you each of the bowls and types of noodles or dishes they serve. I was pleased by this as I knew nothing about the dishes on the menu. The restaurant itself has an urban and unique design. Lights are dimmed at night which makes for a good date spot. Best of all prices are good for that big bowl of soup you see in pictures.

This place is amazing! If you're ever in this area, definitely check it out. Don't let the crowd in the front discourage you. Pass right through them, request a table, grab a drink at the bar, and wait for your table. The host staff is super efficient and friendly! The bar staff is even better. I honestly love this place. The food, the staff, the atmosphere. Everything is a win!

This udon was heavenly. Absolutely Divine, with a whole big bowl that's mine. I've been to a number of food on places in lower Manhattan and I have to say that I couldn't name any but this one. Most of them have been overhyped and left me eager and sad, with the urge to find the perfect Bowl. Anyone who knows me knows that I much prefer Ramen to udon, but this place almost makes me reconsider. There's such a wide range of udon with large pieces of meat, or delicious bowl of fried shrimp and pork in a curry t Udon, there's something for everyone.
My only complaint about this place is the more than average wait times, and the prices are a little high, but still worth its value.

Overrated and felt like a tourist trap. My bf took me to this place to celebrate Valentine's Day because it had such good reviews. But after trying we thought the Udons and other food were just so so and over priced. We've been to many other better ones (hidden gems). We do recommend the lamb chops appetizer, it was pretty good. However we probably won't bother to come back again to try other food.

I really wanted to like this restaurant. I'm a fan of Japanese food that's not raw or fish related. But my experience here was really quite a disappointment. And to add salt to the wound, it was an hour and a half wait for two people. I wouldn't have minded the wait at all as it was my choice to wait, but the meal was just not good. To be fair, I think my choice of dish was off the mark.

So I got the truffle cream mushroom and "snow crab" udon soup and my friend got the tan tan one. He said his was okay, but it was too spicy for my taste. My dish was extremely...truffley. Truffle has a really strong flavor. But what I'm really upset about is that there was almost no snow crab in my udon. Which was the main reason why I chose to bare with the truffle. It was literally just crab crumbs in there (see uploaded pic). I kid you not. The crab picture that I post is the actual size of what I got. I had to fish for them for a good 10 minutes to make sure I didn't miss any. But I wouldn't have missed much even if I didn't. 

Definitely not worth the hype and super overpriced. I'll give an extra star because I liked the waiter and atmosphere. Oh and the crispy eggplant tempura was good.

I stopped by Saturday night with a friend. We were told a 45-50 min wait. No problem. We didn't hear a call or text so stopped by to check in. We were told it would be another hour, which is not so cool. We decided to walk around and wait. Suddenly, 5 minutes later we were told we had a table. We came back but the seats were at the bar. It was kind of ok to sit there so we opted for that rather than waiting again for a table. We ordered about $100 of dishes. The wait service folks were really nice. The presentation was lovely. However, I rate based on taste. We can comes filled with avocado and tuna, but the cones were thick and oily, overwhelming the delicate tuna taste. The cold noodles were gummy and the sauce was a creamy mess, totally off. (I do much better at home and I'm nowhere near a chef level, lol.) as for the udon, the broth was fine, the duck was all fat and no flavor, and was basically a meh experience served in a large bowl. Poor tasting food, which was unsatisfactory and expensive. :(

Been here twice and loved it both times. It's a huge restaurant, which is great when you want a yummy last minute meal, but I can see how it's off putting if you're trying to have an intimate night out. The restaurant is a good sound level, and the portions are gigantic. I've had the chicken udon and the pork tan tan which was SUPER spicy. The first time I went there was just a 5-10 minute wait, and the second time it was a 30 minute wait, so my friend and I just went for a walk around Union Square and it passed pretty quickly

this is def my fav noddle place!!! Every single dish on the menu is good!!! The onbeyonds is good too. The service is fantastic. My fav type of udon are those creamy ones. Truffle, crab, mushroom. Like the wagyu beef sushi, steak and tofu appetizer too!

If you know you're going to be in the neighborhood, make a reservation if you're coming during a peak dining hour.  I happened to be in NY over a three day weekend and I don't think the wait was as long as it would normally be. Plus, we opted to come before 7:00 in the hopes of aiding our cause.  We checked the website about making reservations and 8:45 was the earliest reservation.  

We took a chance on putting our name in and not having it be an exceptionally long wait.  We ended up waiting about 30 minutes.  It's a bit deceptive when you walk in as there is a fair amount of bar seating.  Only the first few seats are first come first serve, the rest are seated by the hostess.  The restaurant is bigger than you think.

We were seated at the communal dining table, which was fine by me.  They do pack the tables in, but I wouldn't say that you are sitting on top of each other.  Our server was extremely friendly and knowledgeable.  Since both of us had never been to the restaurant, she gave us an overview on ordering the udon bowls.  Wide noodles?  Extra noodles?  Add ons?  She covered it all, which was super helpful.  In addition to an expansive regular menu, there were a handful of seasonal options as well. 

We started with the shishito peppers appetizer.  They were excellent - I've had something similar at Mu Ramen which I thought was tops, but I think this place might have a better take on this appetizer.  I ended up getting a seasonal choice - pork belly and mushroom tempura udon.  I got the regular amount of noodles.  You end up getting a massive bowl of udon and broth, I'm not sure I could have eaten any more noodles.  

No the prices aren't cheap, but you get a ton of food and it's extremely high quality.  I think it's totally worth it.

We made a reservation for Saturday lunch thinking it'll be crazy busy but it wasn't too bad. The place looked small from the outside but the restaurant is pretty big. It's also a family friendly establishment - many tables were filled with kids. I mean, how can't it be when they have great service, and generous portions! 

We ordered the Spicy Tuna Tartare Cone and the Soy Garlic Fried chicken for appetizers. I felt like I was eating sushi on a cone. The cone is fried and filled with spicy tuna and avocado. It's served in a rice filled wooden bowl. You can't go wrong with the fried chicken here either! It isn't too oily and has the right amount of flavor.

We had the Wagyu Shabu Udon, Wagyu and Mushroom Sukiyaki, and the Hot and Sour Udon. They have so many choices we couldn't decide on what to order! Our server was very helpful and attentive. He gave us his recommendations and when we ordered, he asked if we wanted the large portion and big bowl or the regular portion. He told us it's the same price, small or large so we all went for the bigger bowl. For the price you pay, you definitely get your money's worth. The noodles are a good texture and all the broths are delicious! I had the Wagyu and Mushroom Sukiyaki. The mushroom and wagyu were perfectly seasoned. The noodles were chewy. I wasn't sure I'd like the sweeter broth but it was refreshing and tasted healthier compared to the other broths I've tried.

We took the Hot and Sour Udon to go because my cousin didn't finish it. We were talking and didn't realize how long they were taking to pack up the leftovers. The waiter comes back, puts her food down and apologizes. He said they accidentally threw away her food and he requested the kitchen to make her a new order! We were pleasantly surprised, especially considering she finished more than half of her dish. Thank you again for the pleasant experience! I'll be back to try their other udon dishes :)

Terrible taste and terrible food and terrible experience and there is a hair in the noodle!!
I don't understand why so popular! Never come again!!

Very nice restaurant. Lights are dimmed which creates a relaxing and semi-romantic ambiance. The noise level was pretty loud though. I would say this place is good for groups, friends or coworker hangout, and dates. 

Our waiter was attentive and our waitress was cheerful. My glass of water gets refilled almost without asking and I give them props for that on a busy Monday evening. 

The food was delicious! The uni Wagyu sushi was so good, I definitely need to get it again. It was $22 for two pieces of sushi. They ran out of Amberjack sashimi so I chose Blue Fin Toro sashimi for $21. There were 5 pieces of thick sashimi. The eel avocado for $12 was also very amazing. It wasn't even mine and I can't stop eating it. The beef udon is highly recommended. I ordered an uni ikura scallop udon for $32, which I would not get again. There's nothing wrong with the food, it's just that I learned that I don't enjoy cold noodles. Yes, it's cold. And something else quite amazing about this restaurant is that a regular udon and a large udon are exactly the same price. The difference is more noodles, unfortunately not more proteins like uni, scallops, or beef. 

I had my eye on the lychee dessert but I got so full after the udon that there's no room for anything else.

A very nice restaurant. The restaurant is pretty big. It's a good place for family, friends and coworkers dates. Our waitress was very friendly and attentive. This is our first time, and she explained everything to us. She makes sure we were okay with our food. The food came quickly too. 

I felt the food was average. We ordered a vegetable tempura skinny udon, shrimp tempura thick udon, and deluxe curry udon. The udon is pretty big. I felt two people could share one bowl of udon and it would be fine. The udon wasn't soggy and mushy. It was quite chewy and tender. The deluxe curry udon was heavy and creamy. In the curry udon, there was two shrimp tempura, one katsu pork cutlet, and beef. The tempura and katsu weren't crispy and crunchy because it was soaked in the curry soup.  It would've been better to place on a separate plate. The curry wasn't special; it was just plain Japanese style curry.We also ordered a crispy corn kakiage. Out of all the dishes that was my favorite. It's basically a fried corn patty. It was extremely crispy.

Overall, I felt the food was average. It wasn't especially tasty to my friends and I. The environment and service are good. Would I go there again? Probably not.

It was pretty good! Suggested by a friend. We got the sukiyaki one- I thought the broth was a bit sweet. I'd return to try another dish-a dry udon perhaps? I probably wouldn't be the one initiating unless I knew the other person had a sweet spot for Japanese/noodles.

We also tried the fried chicken and the buns. The buns were good, nothing mind-blowing. Meanwhile, the chicken kinda bombed. Dry, nothing spectacular. I'd rather save my money and calories for ice cream :P
Got the seafood broth option; it had weird consistency and the taste did not deliver either.

Horrible experience at Tsurutontan! My friends and I were recommended by my sister to come, and we were hoping to have a good experience. However, the server we had was horrible (chubby Asian male). We asked him to take a picture for us and he told us he is so busy that he can't. I mean...I'm paying for a $200 meal for a party 3, and the waiter can't even take less than a minute to take a picture for us?!? I think management should step up.
All the times I've been here I've been blown away by the service and the food. Huge portions of udon, perfect for cold winter nights.
Delicious!! Super friendly, courteous and attentive! I ordered the Duck Udon. It was extremely savoury. The atmosphere was very nice as well. I can recommend.

I've been here twice - once for lunch that was fantastic - which made me decide to bring a group for dinner - but this time it was a big let down. 

The menu is unique. The soup is definitely Asian style but in a kind of generic way. Lots of good high-end ingredients (Uni, duck, etc) but executed in a way that hides the ingredients themselves. 

Nice try, but trying too hard to pull it off in Manhattan.

This restaurant locates at the busy corner around Union square and we went here after a trip in the strand bookstore and felt starving. The whole ambience is definitely different from a typical japanese restaurant since it's big and the decoration is quite modern. We ordered three best sellers from the appetizer and two udon subcategories, one is beef udon and one creamy uni udon. To me the sushi as appetizer is pretty good, very fresh and good taste combination. The uni udon is very creamy and the soup reminds me of lobster chowder. The beef udon is definitely not my type, too sweet soup and very naive taste. The mushroom didn't go well with the sweet soup. 
The waiter is friendly. But one thing I personally felt not comfortable is that we waited the udon for a long time and he came to us to ask about do we want to refill the drink (11$) but rather than helping ask the food.
The price overall is quite reasonable if you don't order drink. For the Umeshu  we ordered, it's disappointing by putting too much ice and at the end the taste was very light.

One of my fav udon places- It has both traditional and fusion flavors! 
Udon flavors that I LOVE: Sukiyaki beef with mushrooms, tan tan, duck soup
I'm personally not a huge fan for cream-based soups but their best seller uni cream udon is def worth trying
Appetizer: tuna corns, uni soy jelly is a must try if you are as crazy for uni as me
Dessert: I must say their lychee sorbet wowed me. Really refreshing and came with fresh fr
Careful, they really serve huge portion, don't get overly greedy and order too much (like me) hehe:)

Super big bowl, im not a fan of udon myself but their chicken udon was alright.
The staffs were super friendly and funny! It has a cool bar before the dining area.
Such a cook spot overall

I've been here 7 times. The food is great. It's always packed whether it's the weekend or weekday - that's how you know it's good because people want it all day everyday. One downside is that they don't offer orders for pick up and no delivery. The seating hosts usually have a bit of an attitude which isn't a pleasant experience but the food is delicious so that kind of makes up for it. Also they changed the way they make their shishito peppers and they're not as tasty anymore but everything else is still delicious. Katsu Curry is my go-to.

I really love Tsurutontan. They make the perfect noodles to warm you up on a cold day. They can be really popular though so during peak times there is a really long wait. Atmosphere is good, with a lot of wood detail.

Coming here, I'm always torn between going for a dish I know I love and trying a new one. 

Favorites: 
- Sukiyaki Udon: The flavor of the sukiyaki is great - not too sweet, and authentic tasting. The dish is full of meat and vegetables. Personally, I think it's the most balanced dish I tried.
- Duck Udon: Really clean broth; good quantity of duck. Not as flavorful as the sukiyaki, but still a great (and simpler) choice. 

Didn't like as much: 
- Spicy Soondubu Jigae: Flavor was decent, but the noodles were too quick to soak up the broth. 
- Katsu Curry: The katsu was really crispy and well cooked, and the curry tasted delicious, but the noodles soaked up the curry extremely quickly and before you knew it, you just had a huge bowl of bloated noodles and it wasn't great to eat.

Love love love this place !!! It's probably my 4th or 5th time here and every time it's just as good ! Never disappoints me but always made reservations ahead of time. I love the spicy tuna cone and the uni cone(seasonal) and the uni creme udon ! Sooooo good. And also they have happy hour if you're sitting at the bar. Half price drinks and appetizers all night !

Great for casual dinner. The place is very loud, but the tables are a good size and nicely spaced. You don't feel crowded (at least where we were sitting)

Shrimp dumplings: the only disappointment of the night. Came lukewarm, half filled, not really worth it. They came with chilli oil, which saved the dish, complementing the shrimp stuffing well, and giving a nice kick to warm up your taste buds for the rest of the meal. It was okay, but I wouldn't recommend it, as there are better options.

Tuna tartare cones: amazing! And they have a deal on them when you order at the bar, while waiting for the table. Comes 4 in one order. Prominent tuna flavor, very creamy, with a perfect amount of spice. The avocado cream was layered in between tuna, and it was a great combination.

Sea jewels: it was my first time trying uni. It has a very strong sea flavor, which by itself was a little too overwhelming for me, but when mixed with the roe, egg, and soy jelly, it was very well balanced. The sea taste of the uni, came together with fresh sweetness of the roe, creamy yolk, and amazing saltiness of soy jelly. The soy jelly was so good and different that I will be stealing that idea for my future sushi nights!

Salmon and snow crab roll: just get it! My favorite dish of the night. 

U.S. Wagyu Shabu Udon: our favorite soup! After trying all of their creamy variations, we concluded that the clear broth is the way to go! The wagyu beef was very tender, and had a very nice beefy flavor. 

Spicy Tan Tan Udon: not too spicy, and I'm a white boy, who can't handle a lot of spice. The flavor was really good, but they put a lot of sesame oil. Every spoonful of this delicious spiciness was finished with a sesame aftertaste, which made it difficult to finish, unless that's your thing. 

Truffle  Cream with Crab and Mushroom Udon: share this with someone! It is definitely worth to try at least once if you love truffles. Crab flavor is not there as the broth is dominated by the truffle oil, and just like with the case with the Tan Tan Udon, the oil is what you taste the most. It's very creamy and heavy.

Good place for Japanophiles to check off their authentic Japanese cuisine experience.  
Fellow customer (lived in Japan before!)can give testament to the authenticity.  "The kurobata pork was right on point. Did you fly in the pork from Japan?!!" Was a question I overheard.   No, they did not fly the pig in.
Udon was ok, got shavings of oh so precious beef with sad bits of napa cabbage in a huge bowl.
Fantastic noodle place. Big portion of delicious udon noodles. Soy garlic fried chicken appetizer was great too.

Randomly found Tsurutontan while walking in the Union Square and glad we did! First, we had our 14 month toddler with us and were looking for a place that has sufficient seating and child seats. Second, we were looking for varieties and while the place mainly serves udon, there were plenty of other options ie sushi rolls, sashimi, appetizers and rice bowls. We ordered the grilled duck breast and they were pretty tasty and some may not like the fat but it's good! The beef sukiyaki buns are a must try. Our little girl loved the chicken rice bowl. The Waygu Mushroom sukiyaki udon Bowl was huge, could feed two. A tad sweet but very good. Couldn't really tell the beef was waygu though. We finished the meal off with the water cake. It's a fun dessert from a visual perspective.

Great casual dinner. We got the cumber salad and fried chicken as an appetizer followed by the beef udon bowl each as a main dish. 

Overall the ambience is great and service was good too. I just personally wasn't the biggest fan of this type of food...I think they have taken an interesting twist to the traditional ramen bowls you find all over NYC but it just wasn't for me. 

The bowls are quite large (note: the bowl is large - not the quantity of food in the bowl) and the broth was a bit more oily than usual. The amount of meat seemed a little limited too. Seemed worth a $12 dish as opposed to $18. Part of me wishes I had hopped across to Ippudo instead.

Having a big sweet tooth, I wasn't impressed with the desert menu either. A $13 lady M slice here is was more expensive than same slice at lady M itself...

Definitely a one time experience but again, this twist to the traditional Japanese noodle bowl just didn't speak to me...

Definitely make the reservation, especially if you have a group of people. 

It very insta worthy and the service was outstanding. All udon dishes are unique in their own ways, whether or not you crave creamy, savory, curry, sweet, hot or cold, you will find one that satisfies your cravings. The Bao and the fried chicken appetizers were also very good.  A bit on the expensive side but I think the food and the service definitely match its price tag. I've been here 4 times and I did not disappoint every single time. But you do have a strong urge to hit the gym the next few days haha

Udon noodles definitely has to be one of the top food out of my favorite foods list. This place serves you udon in gigantic bowls and they give you really big portions. I ordered the beef udon and my boyfriend ordered the tempura udon. He didn't really like the tempura udon because it got really soggy but other then that it was pretty good.  They also have really unique appetizers.  The restaurant itself is very cute and simple. The lighting for this place is pretty dim, I guess to create a relaxed vibe for whoever who goes here.

I had a sukiyaki udon and was very happy with it! I chose the thin noodle in a large bowl and so full afterward. (Initially felt a bit embarrassed to have a large bowl when the person next to me was male and having a regular size lol but I was starving) The servers were very attentive. I've seen the long line outside over the weekend so I'll come back my slow Wednesday lunch break again!

Came in on a Sunday for lunch time and had to wait about 15 minutes. I ordered the tan tan udon and a salmon crab sushi. The udon has bits of pieces of ground pork, was good but kinda of oily and for the price you're paying you don't get as big of a portion..The sushi was good as well, and also pricey. The total came out to be $47 for a bowl of udon($20) and sushi($16)

I really wish I didn't have to give it a 2 star... but I really felt disappointed with my experience here. 

I've planned for weeks to come here as a celebration after a big test. I saw Tsurutontan featured on Strictly Dumpling and what Mike had in the video looked delicious. I thought about the udon for weeks and weeks. After my seven hour test, my stomach was ready. 

To my disappointment, the udon that I got was nothing like what I anticipated or saw. In the video, Mike had a really creamy and gravy-like spicy udon broth. Mine was very much soupier and not as thick as it appeared on that video. I also ordered an addition rice bowl on the side (for $8), which I thought was pretty good. Sadly I thought the $8 bowl of ricebowl on the side was better than the $24 bowl of udon I got. 

Not to say the udon was bad, but it just wasn't very good or satisfying. I could tell from the first two bites that I wasn't going to like it or wanted to finish it. I felt really bad because I had to ask the waitress if I ordered the right dish. She was so very sweet and said she could talk to the manager for me. I really don't like to complain because I understand how hard it is to run a restaurant but it wasn't what I was expecting. 

With that being said, I didn't think the udon was very good. It wasn't very  flavorful (at least what I got). I thought it was kind of bland and lacking any real flavor. I don't know if they made a special one for Mike or if they just made a sloppy one for me today, but that bowl of udon definitely made my day more disappointing after a 7 hour test.

Move aside ramen, udon is the next big noodle craze! 

Tsurutontan is a trendy and spacious restaurant in Union Square serving up some tasty udon bowls, rice dishes, Japanese appetizers/snacks, and solid drinks. The ambiance is casual yet hip, great for dinnering with a few friends.

The entire menu is quite pricey but you do get a ton of noodles when you order extra. I ordered the cold Mentai Kamatama Udon with thin noodles and loved it. Slightly creamy with plenty of delicious spicy cod roe and the perfect oozy onsen egg. The thin udon noodles reminded me of angel hair pasta but with a softer consistency. I actually couldn't finish my bowl and the leftovers tasted just as amazing the next day.

FYI, regular and extra noodles are the same cost, and you can choose your noodle thickness (thick is recommended for soups and thin is recommended for cold noodles).

Try to make a reservation before you go - I was actually surprised how easy it was to make a reservation for 6 people about an hour before dinner, and once we arrived, the place was packed! Definitely make a reservation if possible. Note that your entire party needs to be present to be seated, but you can always stop by the bar for their all day happy hour menu.

This place is amazing. I'm usually not a fan of udon due to its slimy and chewy texture and it's usually hard for the flavor to stick with the noodle since udon itself is super thick, but this place totally amazed me. The first time we came here for a birthday party, after that we came back twice. The wait was insane here; make sure to call ahead for reservations, especially on weekends. The second time, we ordered:
 
Appetizer:
Lamb Chop with Spicy Miso ($22)
Soy Garlic Tatsuta Fried Chicken ($12)
 
Entrée:
Tsuruton Crème Deluxe ($24)
 
The fried chicken came first and it was freshly fried with the perfect amount of soy garlic. The lamb chops were cooked perfectly at medium, exactly what we asked for. The crème deluxe came with steam rising out of the giant bowl.  We ordered extra noodle at no charge.  The crème broth perfectly seeped into the udon, making the thick noodle super tasty. The broth was rich and creamy, unlike other places that only use MSG, they used a real broth that was cooked overnight. The bowl is a lot bigger than the amount of noodles that was inside, so one person can finish it, but if you order appetizers, probably should share a bowl.
 
The third time we came with another group of friends. We ordered:
 
Tsuruton Curry Deluxe ($24)      
(2) Tan Tan Udon ($20)
Tsuruton Deluxe ($24)                      
Akatsuki Mango Sangria ($13)
 
Not only were the foods great, the drinks were delicious as well. The mango sangria wasn't overloaded with mango syrup as you can still taste the wine in the sangria, yummy! The Curry Deluxe was very similar to the crème deluxe we has last time except with a curry broth instead of cream. The curry was rich and thick, with a light kick, just enough for you to feel the spice, but not too overwhelming. The Tsuruton Deluxe has a clear broth, very refreshing if you are not looking for something thick to spice up the noodles. Lastly the tan tan noodles were not as spicy as it looks. It had a very unique taste different than the other broth aside from the spiciness.
 
Service was great here and waiters were super attentive, always checked on us and refilled our water. Will definitely return.

This place was an adventure to be in - I'm pretty impressed with the number of options they have here.

I'm out here traveling for work and decided to swing by here since it's near the office. It's a good place for nice, leisurely sit down meal (although coming from LA, I must admit the price point for food in general is a bit high in NY, and I felt the same way for some of the udon here). But in general, this place is solid for the ambiance and everything was presented nicely and tasted great.

I didn't end up going all out with the set meals (though tempting as it was), and kept it pretty basic with a duck udon myself since I wanted to keep the meal light. Broth was light yet flavorful, and they did give a good amount of duck slices. I like the fact that you can add on a small donburi so that you can try a few more options. My coworker had the spicy tan tan udon and seemed to really enjoy getting a sweat out of that (in a good way).

Service was great and attentive, and I really appreciate how our waitress really took the time to explain everything on the menu in great detail to help us decide what we wanted.

The portions are massive- we missed breakfast and had lunch here and I couldn't really even bring myself to eat dinner. I got the curry udon without any meat (they replaced the meat with soft tofu) and it was pretty tasty. Our server was also super sweet! Four stars mainly because I think the taste isn't particularly special but the portion size makes it a unique experience.

Came here for date night on a Thursday and our overall experience was great! We waited briefly at the bar for about 15 mins as the place was busy! Francis at the bar took great care of us with our Moscow Mules which were delicious and refreshing! We were seated in a nice spot and was attended to by Marcos who was nothing short of amazing. He was friendly, engaging and fluid with his service. Food was good as the udon and sushi rolls filled us up. However, the service was really what stood out to us which is the reason why we will be back! A BIG thank you and kudos to Eddie and Amon the managers on duty that night that made sure our date night went well! Thank you Tsurotontan for a great experience!

Definitely one of the best ramen/curry joints in the city. They seated us promptly, the dining room had a modern Japanese vibe, and the service was excellent (waiters were extremely attentive and patient). Most importantly, the food was incredible. We ordered a snow crab sushi roll and I got one of the spicy udon dishes with beef and tofu.

Solid Udon, price is a little high but I believe still worth it. Atmosphere is great. Service and speed is also great. Not snooty, and very organized! Don't go out of your way if you aren't a noodle fan, but if you are, please go out of your way.

Simply tried the Nabeyaki and Sukiyaki Udon as well as a Bluefin Tuna special appetizer. Nabeyaki is good for those who enjoy a clean broth flavor, but honestly, I think most people would prefer a more flavorful broth. Sukiyaki was excellent if you're into it, sweet and salty, with a great profile of fatty from the beef. The noodles themselves were excellent. Tasted more "fresh" and had a much more lively texture as opposed to the normal udon you get in a cheap place. Would highly recommend ordering the apps and side orders, there were so many that looked good that it was hard for us to decide what to order! 

Place gets packed, so going during an off hour or making a reservation is ideal. Definitely going again.
Great udon noodle shop close to Union Square with authentic ambience and diligent servers. I've had a sizzling seafood udon pot. It was spicy and the soup was warming in the heart of winter.

My sister and I came here late for dinner like around 6pm and had to wait an hour but it was worth the wait !! I've enjoyed every dish we had.  First we sat at the bar and had some drinks while waiting for a table.  The restaurant setup is very cool and had a cool vibe to it.  They gave us menus to look at beforehand so we could know what to order by the time we got our table.  We ordered 4 appetizers and shared an entree together so it was just perfect for the 2 of us.  Everything we ordered was wonderful and I would highly recommend this place to anyone wanting good Japanese food !!

I thoroughly enjoyed my meal here. I came here on a busy Saturday at around 6 and waited only half an hour even when I was told it might be an hour and 45 min wait. So don't be scared by the estimated time guys cause it was definitely worth the wait. We ordered a lottt of food for four people and managed to finish most of it. The spicy tuna cone was one of my favorite appetizers and the beef bun was not bad, quite oily and messy but had a lot of flavors. The hamachi was only okay and the tofu I could have done without. Our server Annie was adorable! very personable and attentive, explained the menu and we all thought she was great. I ordered the uni cream udon and it was a bit too sweet for my liking but it wasn't bad for anyone who like uni, upgrade is also free so you can get extra large portions to fill those extra large bowls free of charge. My friend ordered the first udon on the menu the one with everything and I liked her soup base better than mine cause it wasn't as sweet. One friend ordered the chicken don? And he finished everything so it had to be good. The braised pork belly was a popular hit among the group and the highball was a solid drink for those who don't like anything too strong. ( how can you go wrong with club soda and plum wine?) This place was expensive but I will definitely be back!

FOOD: 8/10
SERVICE: 8/10
AMBIENCE: 10/10
RECCOMENDATION: seared salmon snow crab roll

Make sure to make reservations because this place is poppin and you wont be able to get a table if you dont. When i walked in this place, i immediately felt boujee af from how nicely decorated this place was. We ordered the uni creme udon with thick noodles and the seared salmon snow crab roll. The uni creme udon tasted like macaroni and cheese but a little better cause of the uni. i think if i come again next time, i will order the thin noodles instead. The sushi however was very delicioso. Overall i would say this place is pretty good and definitely worth a try.
The best udon place! I love the appetizers especially the salmon and snow crab sushi roll!!

I came here with four other people at 8:30pm on a Monday evening. We got seated very quickly. I got the Sizzling Sukiyaki Udon. It can be made vegan, or vegetarian with an egg yolk. It's in a hot stone pot, so the noodles get crispy where they touch the bowl. It smelled and tasted out of this world. I could only finish half of it, and I spent the next morning really looking forward to getting to finish it for lunch. It had tofu in it, was really filling, had a great diverse set of textures, and was just the right level of smoky. The noise level was nice for chatting with a group of friends.

I got the classic Tan Tan Udon and it was so DELICIOUS! It's a little pricey here but the portion size is humongous. They give you a giant spoon and bowl. Extra noodles are free! I will definitely come back when I visit New York again. They also offer a coat check in service which is very nice.

Standard random place for decent udon with a big chain vibe. I'm reminded of mall food in Asia, which is good enough for this transplant! The small dishes aren't worth getting for the price that they're charging. Sukiyaki udon is my favorite but it can get pretty salty.

From the ambience to the service to the drinks/food- everything was on par which made for a great date night! Loved the cute decor, the delish Moscow Mules made by Francis, and the service by Marcos (who might just be the best waiter I've seen thus far). Recommend the spicy tuna cones and the wagyu udon! 

And of course, a big thank you to the managers- Eddie and Amon who made sure our experience was nothing short of awesome. 
Will definitely be back!

Tsurutontan is my favorite udon place in NYC. I don't even remember the days when I didn't go here. The first time I went to Tsurutontan was when it had first opened - reservations were absolutely necessary. They are still preferable but on a Monday night I walked in for a party of two around 8PM and was seated immediately. 

The bowls are bigger than my face, which justifies the bigger price tag (approximately $24) for the udon. It also comes in a regular or deluxe size (more noodles for the same price)! Thick noodles are the way to go. If you don't eat much, then I'm not sure how you will finish this bowl. 

Since I've been to Tsurutontan numerous times now, I skip the appetizers because I want to save room for my big bowl of noodles. Udons that you can't go wrong with are the Tsurutontan Deluxe, Curry Deluxe and the Uni Creme. If you're feeling like you want something creamy - get either the curry (not spicy btw) or the uni. 

Either way, you must check out these humongous bowls of udon out! I leave extremely satisfied every time.

Food: 4.0/5.0
Service: 3.0/5.0
Value: 3.0/5.0
Decor: 4.0/5.0
Overall: 3.5/5.0

Good and heavy.  Who can possibly resist a big helping of udon served in a comically large bowl?  No one, that's who.

Two of my co-workers raved about this restaurant so a bunch of us came here last night for an early dinner (5:15pm). We made a reservation to ensure we wouldn't have to wait. Definitely do this if you want to eat here.

The Pros:
-Decor is very nice, clean and modern
-Love the glassware/bowls they serve with
-Great service everyone was so kind
-Extra noodle (large) is same price

The cons:
-Overpriced
-Food was good, but nothing special

Perhaps its because I ordered the Wagyu Sukiyaki udon, I thought it was good but tasted familiar and something I can get at another udon restaurant for half the price. $24 for a bowl of udon is pretty steep.

The location was easily accessible by New York subway system. Make a reservation if possible, but that does not guarantee a table once you arrived (the reason it was 4 stars). When you wait, you have to remind the hostess team your reservation and you're waiting. Otherwise, they will go through the waitlist and something skip over the reservation. Also, the hostess area is too small for a team of 3-4 hostesses to work together. This is the first impression for guests. The hostess area and team are very important. Let's get to the food. 

We ordered:
Negi Toro Maki
Tsurutontan Deluxe Udon
Tan Tan Udon
Uni, Ikura, Crab Donburi
Green Tea Crepe Cake
Water Cake

The Tan Tan and Tsurutontan Deluxe Udon were great in taste. Best part, you could ask for extra udon at no cost. So, when ran out of udon but plenty of tasty broth left, you asked the server for extra udon. The Negi Toro Maki was really tasty. We ate the maki with a minimum of soy sauce and wasabi. The Donburi bowl was great. It had plenty of uni with fresh Ikura. Again, we used a minimum amount of soy sauce. The flavor came directly from the ikura, uni, and crab. Overall, the food was tremendous. The server was very attentive too.

The two desserts were unique in its own way. The Water cake was a clear jelly cake. You need to add the brown syrup to it for flavor. The Green Tea cake was very tasty and light. The green tea ice cream was very heavy in flavor with a little bit of bitterness to it. Overall, it was good. 

Overall, I would recommend people to go try this place out. You will not be disappointed.

The place is very cool and this concept of extra large bowls of soup is interesting. For me their portions were too big and I felt like it was waste of food. Other than that, the taste was great, service was good and this location is always beautiful.

Tip:  As of this review, get a large because it does not cost extra!

Among my group of many friends, like many! I am the Japanese food connoisseur! (I hope I used that word correctly!) I am the know it all for all things Japanese slash food. All of them say, "You have the taste buds of poor royalty!" Kidding, I think that was during one of my daydreams.  

All jokes aside, I went to this place because of a close friend's recommendation, this one person from YouTube. And boy-oh-boy, the Spicy TanTan Udon was near darn perfect! Near because I do not have much Udon experience. I usually, do not drink all the broth of any soup base dishes but the soup was very savory and spiciness did not overwhelm the distinctive flavors of this dish at all. Therefore, I emptied and licked the bowl like a hungry newborn child. In addition, the noodles itself was perfectly chewy and not as slimy as it would be, which would constantly slip off your chopsticks.

The service was good, the decor was appealing, the other dishes were decent and I came out with broth splatter all over my dress shirt. Honestly, I can only vouched for the Spicy Tantan Udon, come here for that and you won't be disappointed. The softshell crabs and sushi were mediocre because I have yet to find one that tops a Sushi restaurant in Little Tokyo, Los Angeles; of course, except Japan. 

Pros, noodles and broth are almost perfect, service was timely, plenty of seating arrangements and the servers are always nearby, sometimes standing directly behind you. 

Con, the other dishes were decent, seating arrangement are a little tight so privacy could be something of an issue if you don't like listening to the romantic couples professing their eternal love for each. Or that could be you, to each their own. 

Come with friends, have a drink, eat some Udon or Ramen.

Best Japanese food I've had since coming to NY. Even my Asian Grandma and Aunt approved. Gorgeous interior too. 

Food: 4.75
    Taste- 5
    Presentation- 4.5
Atmosphere/Aesthetic: 4.5
Service: 4
Price/Value: 4

    
I got the shrimp tempura donburi ($18, comes w/ side of udon) and I wish I could eat it eternally. Sauces are just right, udon noodles are fresh to the max, and fried stuff tastes heavenly. We also got appetizers of sesame brussel sprouts, cucumbers, and fried eggplant. Fried eggplant was really good. 

The bowls are hand crafted, and you can definitely tell. Everything here feels meticulously selected. 

The servers are incredibly professional and kind! Quick and helpful, but not overbearing. 

It's definitely a pricier place, but the portions are so huge that you can split with a friend. They also have the option of getting a larger size of udon and no extra cost! 

Would definitely go here again. Multiple times.

I came here with my girlfriend because she loves udon and we saw a post about this spot on Facebook. First off, this place tastes way better than udon west. I ordered the tempura udon and the beef udon and they tasted way better than expected. I wouldn't order the tempura only because it gets salty but the flavors were still pretty good. I usually don't like beef udon from other places cause the broth gets too fatty but the soup from this spot want greasy at all. I recommend this spot for a date or dinner with a small group of friends. The also hav a bar with their own drinks, so it's would be a nice casual place to turn up too.

Great udon spot in the city. The udon noodles are the perfect chewy texture and the broth is flavorful. 

I ordered the Tsurutontan Deluxe and it was a delicious blend of seafood, beef, and chicken. The price may be steeper than you'd expect for udon but the quality of the udon makes it worth it. 

Also, you can ask for the large size at no extra cost. The bowl was so big noodles and if I had known how large I would have split it with a friend!

Make a reservation beforehand and your whole party must be there before you get seated. Be sure to not be late otherwise you will lose your reservation and the restaurant gets very crowded.

The food was great and the server was nice. However, the seating was too tight. We were close enough that we could hear all of our neighbors' conversations. I would go back again but during less busy hours.

Tsurutontan Udon Brasserie is certainly all about the udon. There are about 20 or so different varieties of udon you can choose from, separated into a few general categories. You can go with the simple dashi-based broth, or thicker curry or cream "broth". Or you can go with no broth at all and get a "bibimbap" style udon bowl. All are likely delicious. 

After you choose your style of udon, you get a choice of thick or thin noodles. Thick is better for brothy bowls, while thin is good for cold udon bowls. You can also get a one-time extra noodle, so if you're hungry, go for it! The portions are quite large already, though.

I got the seasonal special - crab and mentaiko ankake. It's basically a light broth thickened with corn starch with bits of crab meat and mentaiko. I enjoyed it immensely. The sea jewel appetizer was also delicious - what's not to love about a soft poached egg, uni, ikura, and gelee?

Overall, I'd say that the hype and wait are not worth it. The drinks were sub-par, the tuna tar tar cones were mush and textureless with mediocre fried wontons, and the udon soups were astronomically too large.
