The noodles were gummy and the flavor was monotone. We also ordered a mushroom appetizer with truffle oil, and it was just doused in a low-quality oil that masked any other flavor in the dish. While we might have ordered wrong, all the dishes and drinks we ordered underperformed and missed the mark. While nothing was terrible and the pricing was reasonable, I certainly am not rushing back. The only redeeming part of the restaurant was the service. The waiters were friendly and the food came fast. 

In sum, there are better Japanese noodle houses out there that are worth trying.

SHOUTOUT TO MIKE CHEN AKA STRICTLY DUMPLING for recommending this place on YouTube! 

I am so excited to talk about this place because (almost) everything was SPOT-ON. 

Let's talk about THE WAIT: 

I came here on Thursday at around 8 and there was a wait. 
So if you are planning on coming here, make sure to make a reservation beforehand. Especially if you plan on coming with a bigger group!
THANKFULLY, I am tend to travel alone when going on foodie adventures, so I only had to wait 5 minutes for a seat at the bar. 

Going straight to the point: THE FOOD
the only downside to eating alone in my opinion is that you most likely can't try a variety of dishes. I wanted to try a bunch of different apps but sadly, I was only able to try the SPICY UDON. Let me start off by telling you the udon comes in two different sizes : REGULAR AND DELUXE. I got the regular with thin noodles and that thing was HUGE. Like, 2-3 of my heads can fit in there. (I have an average size head)
As for the actual food....
.
.

SPICY, but not overwhelming. SILKY, PORKY, and RICH broth texture. It was so rich and because the noodles were thin, a lot of the broth was able to penetrate into the noodles, thus getting a burst of flavor in every.single.bite. 

I mentioned earlier ALMOST everything about this place noodles was spot on. The only thing I did not like was the beef in the udon. The meat was ground up beef and the texture threw me off a bit. You know when you eat meat and instead of delightfully melting in your mouth, it sort of just falls apart in your mouth?? That's what I was getting.
I know, I know, ground beef ain't supposed to be all melt in your mouth. But let me just say, I DID NOT enjoy the beef texture. Wish they put up a different meat. 

Other than that, my waiter was very prompt, they atmosphere is PERFECT for any occasion (date night! ;) 

I would definitely come here again, but next time I want to try a dashi broth instead of something so rich 

Xoxo @THEHUNGRYQUEEN

Very delicious noodle shop near Union square!

We were able to walk in without a reservation with a party of 4 on Saturday around noon. But on our way out after eating, the line definitely stacked up so come early!

The noodles come in a very large bowl, you get a choice between regular or large. Large gives you more broth as well as more noodles but honestly we couldn't tell the difference. You also get a choice between thin noodles and udon noodles - go udon for sure.

All the broths were delicious and flavorful, definitely not too salty like other ramen shops.

Prices were reasonable as well.

Great find in an area with little noodle choices!

The environment was cool and trendy.  Food was good, but it doesn't stand out.  Service was great.  It was a tad on the pricier end for what you are getting.  So probably won't be coming back not because it was bad, but because there are tastier options at the same price point.

Not usually a fan of Udon, something about it never really appealed to me. But I have to say, this place is all about Udon and they succeed on all levels.

Our waitress was very patient with our indecisiveness but everything we had was remarkable, particularly the soy chicken. The tuna cones we also good. not the best thing on the menu, but still yummy. Quite delicious, and it was crowded even though we weren't eating there during their busy time. We've been back a few times since and its been a mad house.

When we entered, we were told that it would take 20-30min but it turned out to be only 10min. 

The service was great as everyone was extremely helpful and nice. The waiter explained to us about you can get the larger size free of charge and which noodle they recommend. 

I got the seasonal fall item - crab and mental caviar ankake udon. The flavor was good but a little on the salty side. The one thing I didn't like was the fact that the crab was shredded and floating in the soup. You can't necessarily eat all of the crab because it's all over the place. The eggplant in it was flavorful and had nice crunchy texture. The udon was cooked to perfection and it was the right level of chewy. 

The bill for my bowl ended up being $27. Would I come again? Maybe. It is a little gimmicky with the huge bowls. And the actual amount of food (even the larger portion) was not a lot. Maybe I'll come back to try the popular bowls.

Came here on a really cold night, and I left this place satisfied and full. Both my boyfriend and I ordered a large bowl of udon and couldn't finish. We got the tsurutontan deluxe. Customer service was awesome, although we didn't make a reservation for seating, we were seated in less than 5 minutes. Everyone was super nice, and the waiters were always checking up on us to see if everything was okay. If you are really hungry, I would recommend this place because they let you upgrade your  bowl of udon for free !

I had the COLD udon w/ uni and the seared steak appetizer. Both were AMAZING. I'm still thinking about it and I left NYC a few days ago.

The COLD udon had uni, seaweed and shiso (other green garnish thing).  You have to mix it very well so that the shiso spreads evenly into the entire bowl of udon, because once you taste it all together, it's AMAZING. WOW.

I didn't mix it well so my first half of spurping was good but not life changing then I got to the part where the shiso was...and OMG, game changer.  

The seared steak appetizer was amazing as well. It was pricey at 22$ for 2 pieces but once I put it in my mouth, I was in heaven.

Udon is much better than expected in the dining area. The bar area is nice, but the service at the bar was beyond bad. It's very disappointing for Japanese restaurant. I would only go back for dining area for noodle.

Definitely a great spot to get a bang for your buck. I've been here quite a few times and they offer a great selection of udon noodles. 

*TIP* The portions are huge, and they even have free unlimited noodles if you don't get enough. Just a heads up, the large size is the same price as the regular size. 

The udon comes in a giant bowl, which makes it hilarious to snapchat. The menu has photos for every bowl so you know exactly what you're getting. I recommend any of the sukiyaki based bowls. The katsu curry one is good too, but heavy.

I ordered a truffle creme with mushroom and snowcrab udon. The only problem was that THERE WAS NO SNOWCRAB!!! I noticed when i got my receipt!!! I was a bit sad that i wasnt observative but what happened happened, it was a lot of food in the bowl anyways.

Onto my opinion of it, it had a very strong truffley smell. The first bite, delicious! I can promise to anyone who is a truffle lover or a creamy and thick-ish broth that this will not disappoint. Im just not used to the truffle-y taste so it kinda was too much for me so i swithced with my boyfriends udon which was a curry udon. It had beef cubes in it and i really liked the beef cubes a lot!!! I cant really say much because I only ate a little bit.

As for their noodles, their thick nooldes were oh, so, satisfyingly chewy!!! And their skinny noodles were nice and somewhat slippery. 

We also ordered two appetizers, it was the garlic chicken and i believe the pork belly with two hardboiled eggs. The garlic chicken was really good but it was a bit dry but not sooo dry so its good. As for the pork belly, it was just kinda too much. I suggest, if possible, to have them put the sauce for the pork belly in a separate little sauce dish or something because it was really salty. We almost couldn't even start eating our udon xD.

Lastly, their ladies restroom was soooo nice! It had a sliding door and it was a bit cramp but cute and super clean. I would like to see a bit more of a japenese, traditional decorations, or a bowl of dried plants or something to not only make the bathroom smelling nice but it'll also look pretty.

Overall, it was a very nice experience and it was a bit over my expectations.

Tsurutontan is pricey, but worth it. This is my third time coming here and I've always gotten the Sukiyaki Udon ($20). The portions are good - the soupy noodles come in a HUGE bowl and you can get thin or thick noodles and also have the option of doing EXTRA noodles for free. The only downside is that the soup is a bit too sweet for my taste.

Came here wanting more food after having drinks and food at another place beforehand. Since I was starving, that probably affected my judgement of the food here. I got the tan tan noodles which was good (but not mind blowing probably cuz I already ate beforehand). The cocktails were surprisingly great and something I'd recommend even tho I'm not the biggest fan of eating and drinking at the same time. 

Service was pretty decent. The waiter was nice and was able to help us out with suggestions which is always appreciated. Other than that, there wasn't anything out of the ordinary so there wasn't anything I could exactly give dings or kudos for. 

The decor is pretty nice here so don't be afraid of bringing a date here. Especially if she likes uni cuz the uni noodles are pretty impressive (even with my subdued appetite). I'd definitely come make the trip out here again on an empty stomach so I can properly enjoy it.

The decorations are beautiful.   Our server was friendly, attentive, and quick services.  Since it was our first time there, he explained the menu and told us we can get more udon without extra charge.  
We ordered spicy tuna tartare cone, soy garlic fried tatsuta chicken, shrimp tempura and blue crab roll, uni creme udon, Tsurutontan deluxe, and sizzling shrimp mushroom udon.   Spicy tuna tartare cone was ok, nothing really special and the box with raw rice they served in was a bit unappetizing.  All I think about is how many times that have reuse the box and rice.  Soy garlic fried tatstu chicken was too salty for me.  Shrimp tempura and blue crab roll was good but the picture on the menu looks different.  Uni creme udon's soup base was delicious, texture of the udon was prefect, but the amount of uni we got was not worth the price.   Tsurutontan deluxe was lacking of seasoning.   Sizzling Shrimp mushroom udon was delicious.  We asked for extra noodle but I don't feel the portion is that big,  the bowl was huge.   This place is pricey for a bowl of udon but it was a nice experience.

I will go to this restaurant once every week if I lived in the city, it is that good!

I love their udon and the fact that they have so many different ones, you can visit this restaurant and always order something different. The portion of their udon are huge for my appetite, I will always have to visit when I am super hungry. I have visited the restaurant around 5 times now and have each time tried something different. Out of those 5 times I think I was able to finish everything 2 times out of the 5.

Aside from their udon, their appetizers are amazing as well. I've tried their Spice Tuna Tartare Cone, which was absolutely amazing! You get the freshness of the tuna, and with the cone you get a nice crunch as well.

Honestly I love this restaurant and will always be my first pick to go when I am around Union Square.

Walked in at 9pm opening week! Food was excellent!

Went back last week and were told it was an hour and half wait. We waited 10 mins and they sat our party of 4 right away. Best udon!

I'd love to give a better review to this place, as the food is genuinely pretty good. Unfortunately, I've been waiting for more than 30 minutes to be seated at my reserved table, so I can't actually eat any of that food.
Excellent udon spot with a massive menu - it feels as though you could come back 10 times and still be having something new each time.

Best udon I've ever had. Portions are extremely generous and the noodles are made fresh- very thick and doughy. The sizzling udon is not to be missed! There are over 20choices of soups (both hot and cold options) with traditional and more contemporary flavors. 

Ambiance is fun and inviting and great for a date or groups. 

Despite having a reservation there seems to always be a long wait time but it's well worth it. Once seated, the service is fine.

The udon itself was good, not exactly like what I had in Shikoku, but it's good enough.  Then why a two star?

First, it was Saturday 2pm.  When I walked into the restaurant, there's a bunch of people standing there waiting. I saw that there are many tables empty, why not just let these people in?

Then I was asked how many people, I was dining alone so, 1.  And I still had to wait like 10 min.  The host did not ask my name to be put on the waiting list....I think it's a complete mess in the waiting system.  There was another lady also was waiting for a while and she was just seated 1 min before I got seated!

Anyway finally I got seated.  The menu is big. It's not like the usual udon joint in japan.... in japan the usual udon joint is a semi self serve place that you can order your noodles and get the fried food on the side.  And it is usually super cheap....

The server told me there's "thin" or "thick" noodles to choose from... and again, in an authentic udon shop in japan, you don't have a choice of the noodles as there are basically two different style and they won't sell both style in one place!!  The "thick" one is sanuki udon which is from Kagawa and the "thin" one is inaniwa udon which is from the Akita.

Anyway I got the sanuki style with uni. It was tasty.  Price for a regular and big size is the same.  I got the regular size as I have dinner plan.

Then when I finished, I noticed there is more empty tables and more people waiting outside, wtf?

I have an impression that this place is trying to create a lining up hype...........

Best udon in the area! Had this noodle shop bookmarked forever and it didn't disappoint. The noodles are served in a MASSIVE bowl with plenty of toppings - I got the Tsurutontan Deluxe and it comes with lots of chicken, beef, shrimp & veggie tempura in an egg drop broth. You can choose between thin  or thick noodles, and regular or large bowls. The regular size was plenty and we couldn't even finish that. Prices are a bit steep but the noodles are worth it!

The service here is fantastic, though we did not particularly love the udon. The deluxe udon had a particular flavor that seemed like a combination of too many things, and the tempura came soggy (it was in the soup, which was sad). The sashimi bowl was yummy though (the fish was fresh and the sushi rice was delicious), and we wish we had more of that instead of the deluxe udon. It's nice that you can choose to get either a small or large portion of udon, both for the same price. Our waters were always filled and our waiter was very friendly and helpful. The great service definitely stood out.
Huuuuuge portions but amazing food! Would recommend for a date night or w a group of friends.
The wait here is usually 20-30 min but the cocktail drinks are really well made. The udon presentation is the best I have seen, and they are really big which has left me full every time.

I grew up in Kagawa, so I know I shouldn't have expectations for udon outside of Shikoku. I thought this place was pretty average, but it's good enough especially if you're new to trying udon. I was able to only try 3 entrees for my visit: the maitake appetizer, the sukiyaki udon, and the nabe udon. The maitake was too salty, and you can barely taste the mushroom itself. The broth in my nabe was a tad too salty, and though I got 2 shrimp tempuras, it was already way too soggy when I got it. My nabe pretty much consisted of this- a bunch of napa cabbage, half a shiitake, an egg, and an enoki mushroom. I just don't think it's worth $20. The sukiyaki broth was also a tad too salty and sweet, my companion couldn't finish it. Everything was just too saline in my opinion. I personally think if the flavors were a little more subtle, I would have preferred it. Overall, however, it wasn't bad!

Pros:
Japanese-style customer service
Serving size
Quantity of noodles
Good variety of items on the menu

Cons:
A little too salty
Noodles not consistently cooked (some were a little overcooked)

Really leaning toward 3.75 stars.

I have so many mixed emotions about this place. I've eaten here at least three times, and I make almost the same mistakes every time.

They offer to upgrade you to a large bowl for free. The first time I came here, I was so blown away by the prices (they are high) that I wanted to make sure I was getting my money's worth, so I said yes. What a mistake! The bowl is already humongous, so to get a large serving only makes you waste more food. However, I no longer have the metabolism of my youth so I definitely can't finish as much as I used to. It's a BIG portion.

My second mistake is getting the curry udon deluxe (see attached). It's $24. I get this every time and at the end of every meal I end up regretting it! It's not that it's bad, don't get me wrong. It's delicious. It warms you to your soul. There's enough meat to go around. I'm just saying, it's a LOT. I've learned and thought about a lot from this bowl. You know how some things can be done, but they shouldn't be? Like the whole theme of Jurassic Park was like "we have this science to bring back the dinosaurs" but the entire theme of the movie/franchise was like "we're not ready to bring back the dinosaurs! we're just not ready!" Or how sushi theoretically could be rolled and served as a GIANT roll of rice and called a "sushiritto," but it shouldn't be? Same goes for this bowl: curry COULD be made into a soup broth, but it SHOULDN'T. It's not thick enough to be curry, but it's too thick to be a sippable broth! "Thick" with five C's and a Q at the end. 

Like trees, the bowls here have rings around their rims and I use that to distinguish how far I've gotten in my soup. I can only get the broth level to go down by two rings by the time I feel like I've stuffed myself silly of udon. It's truly tragic and a waste of delicious food. I didn't know you can get it to go because when I asked once, a waiter said they "didn't do that because it ruins the noodles," but I just saw in a review you can get leftovers. I probably have to agree with the waiter though, sitting in that broth probably does ruin the noodles. 

On a separate occasion, I fell into the trap that is the raindrop cake. I forgot what they call it here, but does everyone remember that? It was a Facebook/Instagram fad in like, 2015. It was a beautiful looking "cake." It's actually just gelatin or agar. I tried it here and it was meh. I was more excited about the ice cream it was served with. The jelly is tasteless, not even sweet, and you have to put it with either this Korean bean dust or a special sauce (I forgot what it is). The sauce had a weird after taste and I associate the Korean bean dust with Korean bbq. 

Overall:
Pros - delicious food, great service, beautiful ambiance. I'd recommend it as a date spot if you're bold enough to go noodle-slurping on a date.
Cons - I can't get over the prices. They're high. Like skyhigh. Like One World Trade Center high. I've never paid that much even for a bowl of ramen.  I've never paid that much for udon ever. 
Suggestion - my tip is to go with someone that has the same taste buds as you and get one bowl, LARGE. Then split it in two. It'll probably be enough. If you're worried about not being filled, get it an appetizer or dessert I guess.

Summary:
Environment: 4/5 

Waiting time: 3/5 crowded and popular for good reason. 

Drinks: Standard, no rating

Appetizer: 3/5 a bit disappointed with their famous pink sauce fried chicken, everything else is standard. 

Udon: 4/5 (had better other places, but this place still good)
Soup is lighter than you would think. 

Overall good, repeat? eh.. 

XOXO 
You know you love me
Gossip Girl

I LOVE THIS PLACE~!
If i could marry it I would. Seriously. The food is amazing and the ambiance is so sexy. The bathrooms are nice for creative selfies as well.

I've eaten here on several occasions and none have been a disappointment. If you have larger parties, try to reserve in advance. I some how luck out on weekends when it is myself and one other person just dropping in.

The selection of ramen is actually varied. There is something for everyone here. I've had my share of ramen in NYC and this is in my top 5!

came at an odd time on a Saturday - around 3pm and the place was still pretty full but the wait wasn't too long

The place is huge and seats a decent amount of tables- nice and clean, casual and comfortable which is great for groups but definitely plan ahead if you want to come here with a lot of people

My friends and I split an appetizer and each got an udon (upgrade to large for FREE) and the bowls were massive!!! Amazing for the price considering large doesn't cost extra but made me feel bad when I couldn't finish it all and seemed like a waste of delicious udon... probably should've just stuck with a regular size but I couldn't help myself haha I got the mentaiko caviar creme which I thought was warm but came out cold? Not sure if I ordered wrong or they gave me the wrong one .. my friends had the tsuruton curry and the truffle creme with crab and mushroom - all pretty good and super super filling

on the pricier side but considering the portions, they're definitely worth it

I've tried coming here a couple times for dinner but never made a reservation so always faced a long wait! I was finally successful when I came for lunch on a Friday afternoon. We were seated immediately, and the restaurant is larger than I thought! The decor is cozy and warm and dark (making it feel like it's nighttime even when it may be noon). 

The menu is extensive (cold noodles, curry, noodle soup, sushi, etc.) and I love that you can add extra noodles for free. The udon noodle soup comes in an ENORMOUS bowl--it's really amusing. I got the sizzling Sukiyaki udon which didn't come in a big bowl but was still a good sized portion. I would come again and try other dishes!

Love the ambiance and old school hip hop music they play here. But best of all the udon soups! Large size for around $20 that will fill you up. I had the wagyu beef which was good. I tasted the cream uni broth which was also flavorful. Had truffle sushi which is the first I ever had. I will be coming back.

We came here for lunch on a Saturday. We had a party of five and was able to make reservations online relatively easily the night before.

The restaurant itself is pretty large with a downstairs and upstairs seating. The ambience is modern and had cool wall decorations. Their service was good. Very attentive servers.

The udons here are excellent and I can't believe how large!  Asking for extra noodles is free.  I highly recommend the curry deluxe.  The broth is curry but not too thick.  Tempura chicken and shrimp was crispy.  The fried sukiyaki in hot clay pot was also amazing.  Very flavorful and different from anywhere else.

The tan tan udon was also pretty good. It does have a mildly spicy kick.  Meat is minced.  We also enjoyed the garlic chicken.  Bursting with flavor and moist  but not too greasy.

It's very easy to over order here. Because their portions are ginormous.  Great ambience, food, decor, and service what more could I ask for.  Big groups would do well here. I will definitely be back again and again!

I split an order of the beef buns which were really really excellent. I thought the buns were just a little heavy. . Also had the wagyu udon which was pretty good but not amazing. 

We were seated quickly and the service was good. Also worth mentioning is that the restaurant seemed very clean. Modern decor. I would be back any time.

This place straight up has Udon on steroids. Holy crap. It's definitely on the high end as well, considering their bowls range from $15 - $22. Their large portions cost the same as their small portions, but that's probably only the cause because the price is already so high.

BUT THE BOWLS ARE HUGE!!! Like, bigger than a toilet bowl. They recommend ordering thick noodles with the hot dishes, and thin noodles with the cold ones. 

We ordered:

TRUFFLE CREME WITH CRAB & MUSHROOM (3.5/5): I'm taking off a star because I wish there were more crab & mushroom in this dish. The cream broth was very brothy, and not as heavy as a lot of other Udon places make theirs. I personally wish there were more of a truffle taste as well. It was delicious on first bite, but the bowl started to feel more and more empty since there wasn't enough crab/mushroom. I wish the udons could be chewier and more al dente. 

SPICY TAN TAN UDON (5/5): I liked this one a lot better! The broth was spicy, but had a very rich aftertaste. The beef was really good as well. There was enough beef that my sister and I could share it and feel satisfied. Definitely would give this one a go!

The bowls are bigger than what you can imagine. It definitely was a great experience, considering the restaurant itself looked very cozy and comfortable.

I used to live in Japan and was a big fan of Tsurutontan when I was over there. I've been to both the branches in Osaka and Tokyo multiple times each. Needless to say, when I saw they opened a New York location, I was excited to go.

The udon noodles here are the best. The taste of the udon is almost identical to the branches in Japan and the portions are large. The service is quick and the atmosphere is classy but casual.

I highly recommend the mentaiko caviar udon (cold), the kitsune udon (with the gigantic piece of kitsune!!!), and the sizzling sukiyaki udon.

I heard this place by the insider food video and I had to try it out when I visited! When we first got there the inside interior was fabulous! It had this modern but Japanese culture feel to it. Our waitress was really nice and she explained what was the most popular dish they had and answered our questions.
The food was amazing! I highly recommend the seafood creamy udon, even though it's not the traditional udon, it is very delicious! They also give you options on what type of noodle you would like!
The price is the same when you get a large, and the large is huge compared to the regular size. But the regular is big as well so you get your money's worth!

Prices are reasonable, service is good, and the food is well made. I ended up ordering two dishes and loved one (Curry Katsu with thick noodles) while disliking the other...I forget the name but it was pork katsu, egg and rice and tasted very much like egg foo young from a Chinese restaurant. Decor is quite nice, though there are a few areas with low ceilings where taller people should mind their heads. Would definitely return here.

I've come here many times for udon, definitely the best udon restaurant in NYC.  They have the most variety of udon and they cook it perfectly every time I've come here.  My favorite udon dishes are the spicy tan tan udon and the sizzling shrimp/mushroom udon.  The tsurutontan deluxe is good too but they leave the tempura in the bowl is it's soggy by the time you eat it.  Also, the duck udon is good too but the duck is overcooked by the time you eat it.  I don't particularly like the sukiyaki udon since it's so sweet.  The prices are the same for small or large just like in Japan.  The udon is a bit pricey ($15-$22) but the ingredients are high quality.  Service is fast and attentive.  I'll be back when I'm in the mood for udon.
I thought this store was going to sell me a trumpet that was shaped like a noodle and I am highly disappointed

This is one of my favorite places to get udon in the city. The sukiyaki udon is very good. Full of vegetables and the broth is perfect. The appetizers are weaker, save your stomach for the udon. Their bowls are also enormous which is fun!

Hey boys: if you ever want to send me noods, you can start by getting me takeout from Tsurutontan.

Just kidding - please don't slide into my DMs. But if you do love noods- and udon in particular- Tsurutontan is one place you don't want to miss.

If you're like me, you've probably only had 1 or 2 different types of udon in your life. Tsurutontan offers 30+. Luckily, the servers are great at taking you through the different types if you're a complete noodle noob or just indecisive like me.

And the portions are comically large, so it's easy to share with a friend. Or don't! My wagyu and mushroom sukiyaki udon was so delicious that I wanted to keep it all to myself. The broth was subtly sweet and filled with all sorts of goodies, from several types of mushrooms to the succulent wagyu beef. I also ended up taking home leftovers that fed me for 2 days. 

You also have the choice between thin and thick udon noodles, and can even ask for a larger order of noodles at no extra cost (who knew?!)

If you're not an udon fan, 1. evaluate your life choices, and 2. don't worry! Tsurutontan's sushi offerings were also top notch. We tried the spicy tuna cones (can't go wrong here), the seared salmon sashimi (a little greasy - maybe pass on this), and two pieces of chutoro (melt in your mouth) for appetizers, and the salmon and ikura don for an entree. The fish quality for everything we tried was great, and the sushi rice was seasoned to perfection.

We also attempted to drink with our meal, but for some reason our beverages didn't show up until we were 3/4 of the way done. Womp. Otherwise, the service was just fine.

Make a reservation and wear some stretchy pants! I have a feeling I'll be back soon.

Be ready to drown yourself in a steaming delicious bowl of noodles. The bowls themselves are ridiculously large. I ordered the Sukiyaki Udon (regular size) and it came in an eye-poppingly large bowl. And though the bowl looks big, don't be deceived because the portion itself is manageable. You can also get a large portion for the same price! What a steal of a deal! 

The Sukiyaki was sweet, delicious, and top-notch quality in every way: broth, noodles, meat, toppings. Also, if you're feeling extra picky you can even customize your noodles. You can get them either regular or skinny! 

There is a crazy long wait, but surprisingly - they take reservations!!! So beat the crowd and get ready to do some intense slurpin'!

Food did not live up to the hype. First we had the fried chicken appetizer- it was not all coated in the sauce, not super flavorful. Tasty but not anything special.

The Udon: We had the uni cream broth and the sukiyaki beef udon. Uni cream was just a massive bowl of cream broth and udon noodles with a couple bites of uni. Very monotonous and kinda boring to eat. Nice flavor, but it needed more veggies or something for texture. It also did not come out hot. Like almost hot lol. Just not fun to pay 24 dollars for a boring bowl of Luke warm noodles. Sukiyaki was a lot better, but really sweet.

Service and ambiance are really nice. But the food was sub par, especially considering all the hype behind this place. Disappointed foodie here
Udon and the broth were great! Waiting 1.5 hours for it was less than optimal. But it's definitely good food and there's plenty to do in the area.

Made a reservation online on resy for dinner on a weekday at 8:30pm and the place was still really busy.  Large restaurant, good atmosphere and service.  

The udons are good.  yes, you can upgrade to a large udon bowl for free but I think the portion sizes are the size except the bowls are bigger for the large.  We ordered the chicken udon and Uni cream udon. Both really delicious.  Not super creamy and salty, just perfect.  We also order the corn fritters and chicken donburi.  Not outstanding but still good.  Pricing is good, not expensive for NY standards. 

I will probably come back again.

This place is my usual place to go grab some really good udon and broth but after my recent visit their service really needed to be improved. I brought my elderly grandmother and my mother to eat and were waiting for my sister, they didnt seat us which I understand and we would have to wait 30+ mins. Then I asked for a table for three instead as I didnt want my grandmother they still said no. There were clearly tables avaliable in both instances. After 30 mins then they announce they would seat us regardless if we were waiting for one more person, but then whats the point after that. They also didnt buss the table when the plates were stacking up. Perhaps I will revisit this place but I definitely wouldnt bring my grandmother here again.

Wowwwwww wowwww wowwwwww!!!!!! My long over due review of this place.

So I always thought that udon was ehhh and just too thick of a noodle, but after experiencing cold udon for breakfast in Japan my view on Udon totally changed!!! It has such great texture and is super chewy and soft and the slurping part is my favorite part!!!!!!

I only learned about this place through my friend who told me that the food was great and the portion size was pretty decent and that I should not over order, so what's the first thing I do??? I Over order by a lil........... ( a 4th person would have been a perfect amount of food for everyone). 

First and foremost, you have a choice of thick or thin udon noodle. 2- a regular size or a large size ( meaning an extra hand full of udon noodle) is all the same price. 

I don't quite remember what each dish was all called but the cone appetizer with tuna and guacamole was SUPER DUPER DELICIOUS!!!!!!! Now some may say that it's not worth it or that they can make it at home, I totally agree but I don't careeeeee!!!!! That tasted sooooooooo gooodddddd!!!!! So worth the money in my opinion! Though it disappeared too quickly

This shishito peppers with yuzu sauce and bonito flakes is a simple dish but it was more enjoyable because the peppers themselves were not very spicy and the yuzu sauce gave it the perfect amount of kick that you look for. 

The ocean jewels consists of uni, poached eggs, and Ikura, which is very high in cholesterol but hey I'm not visiting the doc anytime soon so I can afford that. So good especially it came with little cubes of soup jelly that matched so well with the uni and Ikura and the cream poached egg.

Then came the starssss!!! The udon BANGING noodles!!!!!!! The sukiyaki udon(hot) and the mentaiko Udon ( cold) and the Kaisen Don ( raw fish over rice). My goodness people u have to try their udon. For both the udon dishes we got thick noodles though the thin noodles would be best for the mentaiko udon. The sukiyaki udon was warm and delicious and was on the sweet side. While the cold mentaiko udon was salty and slightly creamy from the eggs and just a hint of spicy. It was sooooooo gooodddd I wish I had more of that bowl!!!!!!!! The Kaiden don was ur typical kind of raw fish on egg so no further explanation needed. It was good and it hits the spot when ur craving some sashimi.

Over all this was a very very pleasant nomming experience and I would bring family and friends here for dinner anytime and any day!!!!!

Can't say enough good things about this place, I truly enjoy it.  They have a super wide variety of offerings for udon, from chilled to hot, and every time I visit they change the menu ever so slightly with interesting options.  You can also choose to upsize your bowl for no extra charge.  You might say "then why wouldn't you just get the large every time?", but they give you a healthy serving for the regular order already, so you really need to be super hungry to be able to finish the large.  I've enjoyed every dish I've tried here so far, I cannot even list all the ones I've had as they do rotate the menu choices regularly.  All I can say is they're all good!

I have been to this spot twice and have enjoyed my experience both times. I tried different things and tried some of my friends' entrees as well... I'd have to say I have liked them all! I tried bits of the curry udon, the creamy truffle and crab udon, the spicy seafood stew udon, and was not disappointed. Though it is not my favorite spot for udon, there are interesting options for those that are more keen on trying new things. I would say though that they have fantastic service! From the general feel of their attentiveness on filling water before asking, clearing garbage as it appears, etc. to our personal server - could not ask for a better experience! Marco was absolutely exceptional and went above and beyond to get my unfortunately odd and annoying request, fulfilled and was more than happy to try and accommodate me. Thank you Marco for making my second time around an even more pleasant experience (who would have thought that to be possible!) The five stars is not for the food per se (though it is delicious) but more so for the phenomenal and kind service. I think its a solid spot for those that are not willing to make the trek out to the east village for their japanese food fix.

I went this afternoon with my boyfriend around 2 and was seated very quickly. I got the large spicy soondubu thick udon and my boyfrd got a large beef thin udon with an egg on the side. We also got an appetizer of smashed cucumbers. The cucumber was marinated very well with a strong hint of sesame. 
When our udons came out we were both shocked at the large portions. 
My spicy soondubu was quite spicy and a tad sweet which I think really balanced the spice out. The udon was al dente which I really liked. 
My boyfriends soup base was quite clear and his thin udon was a little softer than my thick ones, so if you prefer chewier udon, I recommend the thick ones.
Will definitely come back again for more!!

My go-to udon spot in the area. Lots of table space for groups, decor can be casual but still impressive if you bring guests from out of town! Also lots of space to just grab a drink at the bar. Affordable for the area. I dream about the sizzling sukiyaki udon sometimes

I'm not an Udon connoisseur, but I love this place!
Found out about it while walking back from a client meeting and got to try it during lunch time (they have great specials).  The specials are generous in size and allows you to taste enough dishes to make you want to come back.

My favorites after a couple of visits: beef buns for appetizer, sizzling sukiyaki udon and the tsuduton curry deluxe!

We tried many times to come here without a reservation and finally we got to taste what the hype was about. The 4 stars is for the flavor and generous portions. However, I think frankly it's overpriced noodles at the end of the day. You get a free upgrade to the large size, so I suggest you do so, since you're paying a lot for the entree! I got the tsurutontan deluxe with shrimp tempura and chicken. I thought it was alright. My mind wasn't blown or anything...My boyfriend got the spicy tan tan noodles and he liked it. We also got the spicy tuna cones as an appetizer. Again, good flavor but seemed small for the portion. I thought about bringing my parents here for a birthday celebration. Unfortunately, the loud R&B music would probably not be their vibe. This feels like an ippudo for udon - a place you have to try once but there are definitely more affordable and delicious places out there.

Interior 5
Service4
Taste 4
You can experience what is real Japanese udon. 
Even many Japanese udon shop using udon it content some kind of chemicals which gives you some Chewiness. This shop use" flour, salt, water" only. If you feel less chewiness, that's because you are too much used to chemical ones. 
Did you know disposable chopsticks are all bleached wood.  They use non bleached one. I brought back one to my house. This shop care about everything, I already went back few times with my friend. Put on my FB. Talk about this udon shop at least 40 people.

This place is a bomb ! I always love creamy noodles soup so this place is perfect for me. I've been to this place twice and still in love with it.  First time tried their Uni creamy udon. It was delicious ! And second time tried their Truffle Creamy Udon with crab and mushroom.  Oh my God ! So yummy n rich ! Next time I'm coming back for Mentai Creamy Caviar Udon.

I really like this place. First off, the decor is cute for a noodle joint and I felt like I was back in Tokyo. There are over 30 dishes one can try. After the helpful waitress ran through the menu with me, describing the various bases etc, I opted for the tan tan as I love sesame and it looked creamy yet spicy. I was torn though and really wanted to try the chicken parm creme and also the curry udon. The waitress explained that large was the same size as a regular portion and that I wouldn't finish the large. ( that's as a definite throw down). So I had no choice but the order the large to prove her wrong hehe. I have to say that while the bowl was large, the volume of food didn't seem that much to me. I mentioned this to my friend and she was agog. 

The tan tan was diving. The base was mildly creamy, balanced and had a nice spicy aftertaste. Yum. I had selected thick not thin noodles and they were great with the sauce but I wish they had been chewier. I wish there was an option to order more noodles like one would find in some ramen joints but nope. So after I finished my udon, I asked for the rest of the broth to go. It was actually a lot of liquid so I'll probably make udon at home and just add it to the soup/bits of pork I have left. 

My friend had duck udon and that didn't look yummy enough for me to try but she said she was pleased with it. I'll certainly be back to have the chicken parm because I'm curious about what it tastes like. It feels as though it could be awesome or terrible so I have to find out. I'd definitely recommend this place for at least a one off although the noodles I had were a tad over cooked. If you do go, I'd rec the Tan Tan for sure if nothing is calling out to you.
One of the worst Udon I've had. I ordered the udon chicken for lunch, no taste, no flavor and the chicken was barely cooked. Never again!

Unfortunately after SEVERAL trips to Tsurutontan where this happened every time, I will now be needing to take away my previous 5-star review. 

While the food is still great, the service is extremely lacking. The servers and kitchen staff DO NOT understand the concept of timing a table's food correctly.

On several occasions, we have ordered appetizers that came out much later than our entrees, and when we sent them back the servers couldn't understand why we didn't still want them.

Additionally, almost every time the entrees arrive mine comes out 10-15 minutes before the food of person I'm with. By the time theirs makes it to the table, mine is cold from waiting so long.

These consistent frustrations have caused me to rescind my past 5-star review.

A real find. You wouldn't know how chic this place is from the street. Inside it has great decor and even better food. There's an enormous array of noodles to chose from. They run the gamut from Chinese to Japanese with Korean and SE Asian mixed in. Service was great and attentive. I'll definitely be back.

This restaurant was packed on a Friday night. Thankfully we had a reservation, but we still waited a few minutes to be seated. We were seated upstairs which was nice because it was a little bit quieter. 

Our waiter was really nice and answered all our questions. Get the mushrooms for an appetizer!! I also had the sea truffle sushi roll. I love truffle so it was also great!

Fun place to meet friends!

Great udon place - albeit overpriced. There's almost always some wait time but fortunately the bar is quite good with extensive drink menus and great cocktails. Five star to the restroom (something I always include in my reviews

Man this place gets it all right in my book. Great ambiance, top service, and great food! If you're near union square do yourself a favor and eat at this joint. All their ramens are huge and so delicious. Got to sample them all thanks to group of foodies willing to share.

Wait times are long during peak hours, but you can make a reservation on their website and skip all of the lines.

Appetizers are on the small side but they are tasty. Udon bowls are on the big side, still tasty. The giant bowls are a bit gimmicky since they fill them to the 1/3 line, but it makes for a pretty cool instagram.

Nippon Old Fashioned was done very well. It'll get you drunk.

There is another review below complaining about food timing - while it didn't happen to my party, I definitely noticed the problem with other tables. Food was coming out 15-20 minutes apart and they just sat awkwardly.

Review to come. Just walked out.  Miscommunication from the young man up front, and indifference from the manager Supong will ensure we don't come back, and that I share my experience as often as possible.

I recommend making a reservation here. The line is crazy. There are a lot of tables for 2 ppl but not many for big group.
I took off a star because on the day I went, the hostesses did not know what they were doing ... We came checked in for our reservation and they forgot about us. We asked them 20 mins later and they said we never checked in......so many ppl were waiting and they did not know how to communicate the situation very well...

On a brighter note, the service inside was great! The waitress we had was on top of it. The food was also really good. 
I got the Deluxe savory udon. It was one of their top sellers. You can make it large for no extra charge! The broth was a tiny bit salty. But wasn't too bad. It came with lots of toppings and big portion.  I highly recommend it.
My friend got the truffle oil Udon. It was very strong truffle taste. I like my truffle on a lighter note but it's just my personal reference. My friend loved it!
The beef over right was also really good! 

The place itself was very clean. I will definitely come back

I don't normally care much commenting on restaurants but this time the service was horrible that I have to bring it up here.  What happened was, my friends and I, 3 of us ordered a bottle of sparkling wine and the waitress served 1.2 glasses of each. She put it on the ice basket behind the table but then the bottle fell into the ice water. One waiter saw it and told her that it fell down, but she quickly brought us a check to pay for the bill instead of coming to us say the truth. I asked her whether we have more wine left but she lied to us that there's no more left. I nicely told her that I saw what happened and Said you should've told us earlier before I ask for more wine. She realized that I actually know the situation and she said the truth that she slipped it- but still not a good attitude... she tried to cover her mistake and lie to us-  I think this is really a big problem working like that as an waitress. If she came to us and apologized right away, I would have said we were full already and it's okay. Her attitude ruined my night-

This is my 2nd time visiting this location. My friends and I went here for lunch this past weekend. I ordered the Tsuruton curry deluxe udon. You can choose between thin or thick udon noodles and the regular or large portion. No matter which option you choose it is the same price. I ordered my bowl with thin udon noodles in large size.

My udon came with shrimp tempura, fried pork cutlet, and beef. I wish they put the fried pork cutlet on the side or right before they serve it to you because the pork was not crispy anymore. Nevertheless, the udon was delicious! Although pricey, it satisfied my appetite!

I love the flavors and the variety of choices this place offers. The signature Udon with wayugi beef tasted really good and different. The quality of the noddle is fine--not the best but doesn't disappoint either. The most disappointing thing during my visit was the service. The server made two mistakes for our order. Both of them were minor. One was a missing topping for the Udon. When I brought it up after receiving the food, she simply said: oh I knew so I didn't put it on the bill.  

Also if you have ordered food at the bar while waiting for your friends, you will have to close the bill before you can get seated in the dining area. I'm not sure why so much trouble.

omg this place is amazing!!  had the special wagyu sukiyaki. I received a special tour about the three distinct areas the restaurant has. A loud and slurping area, a more refined area and an area more quiet for deep learning or meditative learning.  I was so happy with my time there. hopefully will be there later tonight!

This place = worth.the.hype.  I honestly wasn't a huge udon fan before eating here.  Game changed.  

I got the wagyu mushroom sukiyaki udon.  The beef was amazingly tender and flavorful.  The mushrooms were delicious.  The sukiyaki broth was perfectly sweet.  GET THE BIGGER BOWL (It's FREE, after all).  It's not as deep as it looks, so don't be super intimidated.

Can't wait to go back and try more.

The flavours were good and the portions are huge!! We should have shared one bowl! Sukiyaki was amazing and the tan tan udon with its spiciness. The soy garlic chicken was in flavour but nice and tender. Service staff extremely attentive and helpful.
Okay one of my fellow foodies put me onto this spot, which now if my fav fancy new udon spot. Cute nice decor and amazing eats........recommended reservations and be on time.

Food was ok. Don't see a reason of serving udon in huge bowls. I wonder what the "large" size bowl looks like. My drink was week and not spicy at all. I didn't taste the mezcal in it. 
The serving was not up to the level. The waitress didn't ask about the food, or if we needed anything during the meal. Luckily I had my water bottle. She was also eager to get the check while we didn't even sign it yet. 
Not going back, and not recommending this place.

I love this Japanese udon place! I've been here a couple times now and both times all the food I tried were all really delicious and on point! This place is always pretty packed so I would recommend making a reservation before coming in otherwise be prepared to wait for a table. 

Tuna and avocado cones (so good, a must order for appetizer). We tried the wagyu udon with truffle broth and also the dry udon sukiyaki, both delicious! But I think I liked the wagyu udon because the broth was so light but still very flavorful and the wagyu beef is SO good. Definitely need to order any noodle dish with the wagyu beef. 

The portions are pretty big for the noodles and you can also add extra noodles later (for free!) if you're not full. Love this place, will definitely be back!

This is my favorite udon restaurant in the city. I've tried both their hot and cold udons. I personally prefer cold udon and I've never seen such a large variety of cold udon. My favorite is the cold caviar mentaiko udon.

The place is huge on the inside and we did not have to wait for seats at all.  The udon was delicious Delicious udon noodles with very generous portions!  The staff was also very friendly and super helpful.  I will definitely be back to try the other dishes.

Great Quality
Great Quantity
Great Atmosphere
Semi Expensive Price
Good value
Definitely one of the best udon places in NYC but quiet expensive well. I got the Tan Tan noodles. Udon and the broth was delicious.

Fast service. Awesome cocktails. Good sized servings. But sushi fish  and scallop sashimi not top grade, a little mushy. Fried chicken they emphasize over quality. Sea urchin in the cold udon very fishy and bitter.

Great spot! Easy to get a reservation and able to get in without one. Usually have to wait ~20-30 minutes.

There are so many options on the menu all packed with flavor and spices. Definitely come hungry. The serving sizes are very large and you have the option to add more noodles if you can handle it. Spoiler alert the bowl is twice the size of your face.

Atmosphere is nice. The space is huge and bustling. Service is quick. Highly recommend this place!
Tsurutontan is a decent restaurant with good atmosphere. Make reservation before you go. There's a long line most of the time.

After numerous occasions trying to contact the owner/manager and receiving no reply I have to assume he has no intention of honoring the offer to bring us back and give them a second try. 

Absolutely horrible service. Lying management. Do not go here.
The udon is great the large portion might be too much if you co sider your self a small portion. The food is great and all but one thing to note there is no cell signal!

I had brought two guests and so made a reservation ahead. Otherwise it is usually a half hour or so wait. Personally I had the fried dumplings and cucumber salad. Both were good not great. My guests had udon wagyu noodles and the sizzler. Sizzling noodles was appropriately sizzling! Not a bad place for a nice lunch. Service was good and they did not rush us. Portion sizes for noodles is pretty good. Regular and large portions cost the same. It is not super cheap.

Great place for Japanese food with a wide range of options. reason for four star being I haven't found my "favorite" dish here..unlike other five star places where you could easily find some dish that you would want to go back to each time.

Go big or go home! No seriously you can get a large order of the whole menu for no extra money and it is amazing, hands down a challenge every time but you will leave fat and happy. Great broth, great noodles and the place is huge.
Only has two vegan options but very good! Definitely make a reservation as it can get very packed.

I had been to quite a few ramen places, but never to an udon restaurant. Tried a number of noodle dishes here at various times, and all were delicious. My favorite was the udon noodle soup with vegetable. Very satisfying, especially on a chilly winter evening! Love the layout of the restaurant as well. Has an intimate vibe...

One of my favorite Udon Noodle places in the city. You won't regret the options and especially, most importantly the flavors. Great ambiance and lighting. Friendly waitressing staff. Fantastic Old Fashioned

Came here for a spontaneous dinner meal after the movies this past Saturday evening on behalf of the suggestions of friends. I will have to admit that this place has a nice decor given that it is a brasserie located by Union Square. But it was also really dark in the restaurant and the possibility of hitting your head (if you're above 6ft tall) or falling down the steps is very high as there was very little lighting on the 4-5 steps to their lower level. 

In regards to the food, I had ordered their signature udon dish which was the Tsurutontan Deluxe with extra noodles. Upon receiving it, I was left very unimpressed by the bowl size's proportion to the food itself. The udon took about 60% of the bowl which makes me wonder why they would provide people with such big and heavy bowls when they could do much better with a smaller one that is in better proportion to the amount of food offered. The udon noodles were nothing special as they had a good texture but didn't hold any taste. The part of the meal that annoyed me was the shrimp and vegetable tempura offered inside the dish. I believe that tempura is most well-known for offering a light crunch texture but they just disrespected this idea by soaking the tempura in the broth. 

Overall, I would not come back here as the udon was nothing impressive especially given the price.

Good. I tried the kitsune udon w fried tempura. Udon was slippery and smooth. Shrimp well fried . Didn't blow me away though and don't thk I will be back. All that said, I am not an udon connoisseur and have not tried udon in Japan, so have really nothing to compare to. Give it a shot would be my recommendation!

Oooh, had this place bookmarked and when my group brought me here, I was pretty excited. They have a very big menu with a lot of delicious-looking options. I practically looked through the entire menu and did not know which dish I wanted the most cuz the pictures made everything look interesting and yummy. I wanted to try almost everything! Sadly, my stomach would not survive if I had ordered everything, but good thing one of my friends were willing to share something with me, so we both ordered a dish to share between ourselves. I was not too impressed with the salmon ikura donburi cuz the ikura had minor fishy taste. The udon we had, though, was a whole other story. It was unique for me and absolutely tasty. We had the mentaiko udon with the thin noodles. At first I did not realize that it was a cold noodle, but no regrets.
This is a spot I would like to return to. Large and filling portions.
My absolute favorite Udon restaurant in New York thus far.  My favorites are Uni Udon and Mentaiko Udon.  Get cold Udon to experience more flavor.

Tried this Japanese restaurant with a Japanese friend. 
We tried creamy uni udon and seafood tempura udon added a small bowl of donburi. I like the donburi the most. Creamy udon is not a traditional Japanese style, more like an Italian creamy pasta. The noodles tastes good soft and chewy at the same time. But I can not eat the whole dish as it is a little greasy.

Best time to go here is soon after they open! I went here sometime last year and wow, it really is good. I'm not sure if things have changed but I remember us ordering large udon noodles and it was a monstrosity. Really good and wished I could've finished it since they did not have take out containers at the time. I will go back one day!

REVIEW NOT BASED ON FOOD.

I had booked a table here for 10 people on a Friday night for a birthday dinner. Around an hour before, we'd had an extra few people join us, so I updated the booking to accommodate 14 people - seemingly no issues, great!

Note, the restaurant uses Resy to facilitate their bookings.

Upon arriving at the restaurant, I'm then told there was a "glitch" and that my table for 14 people cannot be accommodated, and that we'd need to wait an additional hr or leave. Bear in mind our booking was already at 9:45pm. Additionally, admittedly we were a large group, but telling us to (in a more polite way - im paraphrasing) "make a decision because your party is clogging up the host area" isn't really acceptable.

Whether or not it was an issue with Resy, or an issue on the restaurants side, I feel pretty hard done by - and as the face of the issue, I feel the restaurant could have done more to accommodate us - at least offer us some complimentary drinks while we wait to make up for the issue.

While certain this was an isolated issue, it's still Pretty disappointing stuff...

It's a cute concept of an udon specialty restaurant. I had gone into the store after a particularly rough and rainy day. As I was alone, I was promptly seated at the bar and given a menu by my waiter. 

I had wanted to try a cold udon when I first learned about this place, but considering the weather and my seat at the bar (right next to where the register and bar entrance was), I figured I would have hot udon instead. At the waiter's recommendation, I had the duck udon with thick noodle.

The noodles themselves did not blow me away. I love to make udon at home and the noodles did not feel different than nicer frozen udon noodles I could buy at the store. No special taste. However, the broth was delightful, not too salty (always my concern with Japanese food) or cloyingly sweet. The duck slices were tender, slightly chewy, and nicely charred. The meatball was surprising as well. It was soft on the inside and seasoned with ginger, which helped reduce the gamey flavor you can sometimes get with duck. I wish there were a little more of the negi and the spinach, as they helped cut through the fattiness of the duck. 

You can order regular or large, with no price difference. You supposedly get more noodles with large. I ordered the large and I felt like it was just enough to make me feel full (and I'm not that big of an eater either). So I would recommend going with large. 

It sounds weird but their tea was the best part of the meal... the complementary hot tea, like what? I expected some low grade green tea or jasmine tea you get at any East Asian restaurant around here but the tea was so good. It reminded me of a really nice oolong I had in China. I was this close to asking my waiter to tell me what kind of tea it was but I figured he already suffered so much watching me struggle taking pics of my food, get myself situated back on the tall stool, and pick away at this udon for like 30 mins.
Without a doubt the best udon in NYC. Just amazing. Really recommend the tuna tartare appetizers as well as the wagyu udon beef soup. Very reasonably priced and I 100% recommend.
Orderred the Uni with thick noodles. Yes it was a BIG serving but it just lacks the Uni flavor. Wasn't very pleased. I'm sorry but we're not coming back.

Ordered curry udon. I could taste a little delightful sourness in the soup, making the dish less heavy and oily. The place is big so even though three groups coming before us, it took about only 10 min to be seated.

I've been to their location in Japan and I was very excited to try their NYC location! We were there around 5pm on a weekday so we got seated right away. We ordered Deluxe udon and Spicy Tan Tan udon. The deluxe udon was had a really nice fish broth and we enjoyed it, but was it worth $24? ...I don't think so. The tan tan udon had some vinegary taste to it and I didn't enjoy it very much. I was disappointed as I had very high hopes for this restaurant. I will definitely go back to their Japan locations but not the NYC one.

*went by myself

I saw a video from Insider and this place and went. The place is very close to the Union Sq. Subway station which is super convenient. The light and the overall mood is relaxing and great for a slow, above-average lunch or dinner. 

I went in for lunch around half pass noon and I didn't wait long for a seat. I ordered a salmon lover lunch set and it's very filling, along with a lychee sorbet dessert with comes with the set. The food is awesome. No weird looks from other people or waiters when I'm sitting along.

I would come back alone or with my friends next time.

Bottom line here, GIGANTIC BOWLS of food. Alright, let's get back to my normal review style. 
My college buddy K.K. and I came here to grab some food after a failed attempt to get sugarfish down the block. We had heard about this place from a few Japanese friends who are fans of the chain in LA and in Tokyo so we figured it must be good. It did not disappoint!

So for starters, the menu has udon which you can get in small or large sizes for the same price. Naturally that meant we went for the largest size and ate ourselves silly. I got the Tsurutontan udon and KK opted for the wagyu beef and truffle udon. So their namesake udon was good, warm, good rich broth as you would expect out of any udon place worth their snuff. The tempura toppings on top were crispy but quickly dissolved into mush as you would expect if you didn't eat fast enough. KK, however, made a super amazing choice for udon that I will have to repeat the next time I go back. Super savory and extremely fragrant, the truffle and wagyu beef udon was everything a savor hound is looking for. Tender slices of beef and the fragrant smell of truffles wafting as you dip your head down to get another mouthful of noodles... mmmmmmmmm... I stole more of this from her than I should have haha. 

Ah, to finish we had the water cake dessert. Interesting in its own way, water gelatin with toasted toppings and ice cream can never go wrong with me. It was very light in flavor and something that you need to experience at least once. 

Four stars because I still have to go back and try a few of the appetizers and other udons. Also to be honest, I liked the udon and the portions were great but I like the broth at my favorite udon place better.

What's not to like at Tsurutontan? I am not an Udon fanatic but this place really makes good Udon and more.

It was already my second visit here. The first time I visited I tried the US Wagyu Shabu Udon with Truffle Dashi and it was so flavorful that I singlehandedly finished the entire bowl (they serve Udon in a massive bowl)
On my second visit I tried the Salmon and Ikura don, it was a Scottish Salmon and ikura caviar served with Sushi Rice and a small bowl of Udon.

I am really impressed with this place, just allow an ample amount of wait time if you're a walk in customer and note, they have happy hour at the bar that serves plenty of cocktail, wines and beer choices.

It was my second visit but definitely won't be my last, I'm a fan!

I am not kidding when I say that these bowls of noodles are the size of your face. My friend had the tan tan noodle and I had the sizzling sukiyaki udon. I think we were both more excited about the cute appetizer though - the spicy tuna tartare cones (hooray for a non-disappointing top seller item)! It's definitely more pricey than we had anticipated, so I'm not sure I'd come back for just noodles.

Edit update 5/19: made a reservation for 7 at 8:30 days before and were kept waiting past 9:15 with no eta. Groups of 6 were getting seated before us that arrived much later. When we asked if we could get some sort of update they told us they can do nothing about it even though similar groups were getting seated. Please fix your seating policies or at least let people know seatings were guaranteed past parties of 6 or something.

Nice Nice Nice Nice Nice. Enjoyed being there a lot. Amazing place to go hang out with friends. Easy to have conversations as the atmosphere is engaging but the place is relatively quiet and the food is delicious. Pretty much anything you order, you'll love. We got a few large bowls of thick udon and shared them, along with the tuna cone appetizers. Really yummy, staff is friendly and the service is quite quick! Favorite udon place in town up until now!

This place is amazing. The food is fantastic here, Ive tried to curry udon, sukiyaki wagyu udon, and the egg drop udon (Not the exact names) and none of these disappointed. You get the option to either get regular or large without any price difference so naturally I got the large and let me tell you it is super filling but well worth it. 
The wait can sometimes be long even with a reservation but I would definitely say it is well worth the wait.
Massive bowls of Udon, great flavors. I recommend the Sukiyaki Udon. Excellent decor and good service, a good lunch, dinner, or date spot!

One of the best udon places I have ever been to. Their big bowls will shock you, but the noodles are so good. This did not disappoint me and I even went during lunch time. I did not wait long, but if I did, I will still enjoy it the moment I sat down. They even have an option for thin or thick udon unlike some other places. In the end, it is a great experience, if you want to drop by.

If you want to impress someone, definitely try this place out. From the modern interior design of the bar display to the coconut wall, rope wall, and denim jean wall, Tsurutontan definitely is eye catching and creates a sense of sophistication. 

The staff are very friendly, attentive, and helpful to recommend and explain the menu items. The food is beyond amazing. For the price and portion, this place is a steal! If you order noodle soup, you can choose the regular size and large size for the same price, which means you can get extra noodles for free! Also, the presentation of the food is very instagram and Yelp worthy. Everything and anything in here will make you feel very elegant, even the sliding door bathrooms!

Loved the service and especially the udon noodles. They were so fresh and glad I was able to share t with a friend because the portion is huge!!! We had the uni one because we were both uni fans and definitely worth it :)

The udon was what we tried here and the outcome was...lack of for better word....below expectation.

For the price and the hype of the location, I expected more flavor for the udon soup but over flavored.

The sides were good though and that saved it from a 1 star along with the service being decent.

Probably won't be back.

*Made edit for the owner since he asked to include what we ordered*

I was excited to eat here.  I came here for lunch post doctor's visit.  I ordered tsurutontan deluxe udon.  I can't say I was impressed.  The broth with the egg reminded me of homemade egg drop soup. The other ingredients were nothing worth mentioning.  It wasn't bad but it wasn't great either.  At $20 plus tax and tip, I didn't think it was worth it.

The decor and service were good. The udon was average.

Udon is pretty popular here if you didn't realize it from the name. I have to say, the fresh housemade udon noodles may be one of the best udon noodles I have ever had. There were so many different broths to choose from. I do recommend the curry and sukiyaki. It is slightly different from the typical dashi broth people tend to get. Curry udon is not very broth-like, but it is very delicious though after awhile it can feel very heavy. Sukiyaki is usually paired with yam noodles, however, udon noodles definitely added something different to the light but sweeter tasting broth. The portions are huge (highly recommend getting the large) and the food was delicious. Duck udon was different but if you don't like smoked duck then this may not be for you. Overall the service, experience, and food were all very delicious and not disappointing.

We came here on a Saturday night at like 9pm and still had to wait 20 minutes because it was so busy. We were seated on a bench for two that was fixed to the ground. 

Interesting enough, they offer both the normal and large size as the same price, the only difference being more udon noodles. Large selection of hot and cold udons that I absolutely loved. Started with an order of asahi beer, which they were kind enough to split into two glasses. 

I ordered the tsurutontan deluxe, which was absolutely massive! There was an incredible amount of meat inside, making it a very well balanced meal. Plenty of carbs from the udon, yet plenty of protein from the chicken, beef, eggs, and shrimp. IMO, a very well balanced bowl of udon that I couldn't get enough of. The fried sesame leaf was a nice touch, but all I could really taste was the batter. 

Girlfriend ordered the mantaiko kamatama udon, which was a completely different style compared to mine. It had a light, creamy caviar sauce and also comes cold. Unique flavor that I've never really had before in a bowl of udon. It almost tastes like liquid sushi with the caviar and mantaiko mixed together. 

Absolutely stuffed after finishing the meal. I'm looking forward to my next visit to try out all the other bowls of udon.
Truffle udon was WAY too overpowering. Fried udon and matcha crepe were delicious. Comin back for more.
Forgot to add a review from 2 months ago, if i recall i liked it a lot, thick rich broth with udon noodles.

I've been here two times and it's been amazing. Will definitely come back with my parents. The staff there is so helpful and nice. The udon and broth were just exceptional. Thank you for the great experience and great location!

Delicious udon place. Good portion for the price. Modern atmosphere.

Will definitely come back.

Great portion - the noodle bowl is HUGE! Apart from their signature udon, I found their appetizers delicious and impressive too. For some, it gets a bit too salty and too much soy sauce after a while.

I tried the uni creme udon during my latest visit here and thought it was pretty tasty. The creme broth is thicker and heavier than the clear meat ones, but not overwhelmingly so. It also complements the tender uni well. Still, I think I prefer the beef udon that my friend ordered - the light, meat-flavored broth is better for big bowls like this - you won't get bored of it like I kind of did with the more monotonous uni udon (there were only a few toppings, which didn't quite offset the thickness).

As an appetizer we ordered the tatsuta fried chicken and liked it a lot. It's pretty dry, not as oily as fried chicken usually tends to be, and the sauce had a nice hint of tartness to it.

This import from Japan is definitely making waves in Manhattan! They have multiple locations in Japan and this is the first US location (with more coming to NYC soon). As a huge fan of udon noodles and seeing the Yelp reviews, I knew I had to check it out! 

I made a reservation in advance, which I'd recommend since a ton of people just stopped in without one. We had to wait a bit for our table, but it wasn't too bad - it gave us time to admire the surprisingly large restaurant. 

Once we sat, I had a super time narrowing down what appetizers and dish I wanted since EVERYTHING looked good. We got two appetizers, the spicy tuna tartare cone and shishito peppers. Both were absolutely fabulous in their own way. The shishito peppers were cooked in a soy sauce base that added so much flavor. 

For my main dish I went with the sukiyaki udon. The dishes looked huge and we had the option to add more noodles, but unless you're CRAZY hungry you don't need it. The flavor basically explodes out of the flavorful broth served with the udon. The noodles were perfectly cooked and the meat was tender. It was everything I wanted and more.  I'm already looking forward to my next visit!

This place was sooo delicious. Came on recommendations from other friends who have come here and raved about the udon. I had been planning to eat here since hearing about this, drooling over the pics and the menu. 

The only downside is that on Saturday, when we went for lunch, they didn't have the lunch option where you can add a small bowl of don for 3$. 

Hubby ordered the sizzling sukiyaki, which was bursting with umami. I think if we had gotten the broth, the whole thing might have been too sweet, but this one was just right. After having so much trouble deciding, I went with the cold mentaiko udon with poached egg and added a side of ikura. Omg. Soooooo good. My mouth was grinning side to side as I devoured this. We both got the large portion, and probably could have and should have stopped eating halfway, but we were gluttons and proceeded to eat the whole thing. The mentaiko udon was a little on the saltier side especially after adding the ikura, but I loooove fish eggs, so no complaints from me. We got the sukiyaki with thick udon and the mentaiko with thin udon. The thin udon isn't really thin thin. In fact, I thought it was really similar thickness to the thick udon. The thick udon in the sukiyaki was sooo tender and soft but with a nice bounce. Omg. Drooling as I write this review. The meal is a little pricey for udon, but I would definitely come back!

This is now one of my favorite udon spots in New York. 
When I first walked in, I don't know how the hell they can pay for all that retail space, but man, after trying their udon, I know why this place has been here for a while and are doing well. 
First off they have like 20 kinds of udon and they also have udon thats pan fried. We came as a party of about 11 and tried different ones and every single udon did not disappoint.
What's also cool is that they have a regular size and a large size. JUST get the large size man. 
Customer service is fantastic. I highly recommend the duck udon!

The uni cream udon was good. A very creamy broth flavor if you're into that. I love the thick noodles and the portions are huge! The Uni cone tasted really fresh and the lady M chocolate cake was amazing! However we waited for over 2 hours to be seated. I recommend getting reservations.

This is an amazing place! I came here and got a beef udon noodle soup. I loved it a lot. I got the small soup, but it was very big. Still, I finished my bowl. I loved the whole experience and I recommend this place a lot. I also got a black tea. That also tasted awesome. The soup had everything I wanted in it; it was perfect. They gave us a surprise: A desert. We did not have to pay for it.
Chic place for asian ramen with their delicious broth. There portions are huge. And I highly recommend their beef ramen.

This is a very busy restaurant, and even with a reservation on a Friday night, we waited 45 minutes for a table to open up. The food is worth the wait though. I got the Sizzling Sukiyaki Udon, which comes in a giant stone pot. The egg yolk cooks as the noodles sizzle in the pot, creating a really creamy sauce. For every dish, you can order thin or thick noodles, and order a normal or large size for the same price. They have some interesting cocktails as well, like a Matcha flavored one, which was very yummy.

This restaurant deserves their reputation on udon. They have their own soup recipe that will sweep you off your feet: natural sweetness, rich but not heavy. The portion is quite large so if you are a light eater or in a strict diet, maybe you want to share it with your friends. 

The restaurant design is cool and energetic!!! 

Definitely will come back for more.

Very yummy wagyu beef appetizer! The udon noodles had large portions and we weren't able to finish them all...but tasted great! However it's not worth waiting for more than an hour just to get udon. Their udon tasted great but not unique.

Uni lovers this is the place for you. I'm obsessed with their cold Uni udon. If you're trying to decide between the cold Uni udon or cold Uni udon with scallop and ikura - go for the former because one has uni puree in the sauce and the other doesn't. It's not all that clear from their menu. Their uni kobe sushi is the perfect complement. Surprisingly the Uni cone is just ok. The cone sort of overwhelms the uni.

After being warned by my friends, I brought another friend with me to Tsurutontan and we shared a bowl of large Tan Tan Udon. While the broth was satisfying and the noodles chewy, we felt that the portion was slightly smaller than we expected. Neither of us were full after splitting the the sukiyaki beef buns, the udon, and a Lady M matcha cake. The highlight of the meal was definitely the sukiyaki beef buns. I've tried the pork buns at ippudo but these ones far exceed them. I love he sauce and the softness of the buns. The meat was not overpowering and light. Overall a great meal, but the udon was slightly disappointing after all the great things I heard about their portion and flavor.

I've been here several times and the udon has never disappointed. My favorites are the sukiyaki with mushroom, the deluxe, and the spicy udon (forgot the exact name).

I made a reservation for my family and I on Saturday for 8:30pm. We arrived at the restaurant five minutes early and the hostess told us that it would be another ten minute wait. When we approached her again after that ten minutes, she then notified us that it would be another 30 minutes and that I would receive a text when they were ready for us. At around 9:05pm (35 minutes after our reservation), I received a text saying our table was ready. When we got there, the hostess hastily told me they weren't ready yet and didn't know how much longer it would be. The process was extremely unorganized and annoying because if our table wasn't ready, why was the hostess telling me it was and wasting more time.
