At 9:30pm, an hour after my reservation time, we were finally seated. The manager sent out some edamame and chicken because of our inconvenience which was nice, but overall the communication between hosts and guests should be less of a hassle. I think they've always had a problem with getting me into my reservation on time, but if you aren't pressed for time then probably shouldn't be a problem!

Their concept is really cool, but their thin noodles (which is yummy don't get me wrong) should not be cooked in soup. Because by the end of the dining experience (their bowls are huge) the noodles have definitely bloated and become mush.

My friend really likes this place so I have been here a couple times and did a few experiments. (All on the kimchi udon noodles, which has delicious soup btw)
First, eating it normally, the thin noodles will become mushy and all the soup will be absorbed by the noodles (leaving me with no broth)
Second, talking half the noodles out into an empty bowl. The fresh noodles were decent, but the rest of the noodles still absorbed the soup and were mush at the end
Third taking all the noodles out into empty bowls and eating noodle and soup separately. Soup is saved but holy shit the noodles became mush again even not in water!

Please change the composition of your thin udon noodles! It is delicious but why does it soften and become a ball of noodles even before finishing the meal?

Oh my so I really can't find anything wrong with this udon (except for price but I'm always a fan of paying less haha).  Definitely better than Marugame and I'm not sure if the larger portion of noodles for free is actually for free or a marketing consumer behavior gimic but always yes to extra food for "free"?. I was between the wagyu truffle and beef udon which the waitress said wagyu truffle is one of their most popular so I went with that. I wish I got the beef but I'm not unhappy that I got the wagyu truffle. I just think the truffle flavor can get a bit overwhelming as the meal goes on and especially the after taste throughout the day until you get to brush your teeth. Broth was on point, noodles tasty, meat delicious, and the bowl is yuge! Service was always there filling your water and there are reservations. Again, only thing I'd put as a negative is the price but a must try when coming to NYC.

So far my first visit is a 4+.
Had the cold dipping noodle w a side of tempura. Pretty solid. I hope my second visit is just as good. This time going in for for an udon dish.

Disappointed. The noodle and soup used to be pretty good. Sadly, I came bk for lunch and expected the good quality as usual, it turned out to be disappointed. The noodle was not well cooked,some of them were sticking together; and the duck was almost raw, even the soup and service is ok, I'm not gonna come bk or recommend to my friends anymore.
Great udon prepared in various ways. The place was perfectly crowded and the food was awesome.

Noticed this place had a happy hour going on, so made my way to the bar on a Saturday early evening where it was almost empty. The friendly bartender quickly hands me the menu as soon as I sit down...

Prices aren't that great considering it's supposed to be happy hour. Regardless, ordered the Kurosawa Sake ($7), Spicy Tuna Tartare Cones ($9), and Sukiyaki Beef Buns ($9). Sake comes out first, poured into a shot glass and served cold. Not great value for $7, but the item is remarkably smooth to drink. Food comes out shortly after, the cones are arranged in a wooden box and placed in uncooked rice. Good presentation and the tuna itself is tasty, perfectly blended with the avocado. The bun exterior wasn't as fluffy as I'd like, but the meat is supremely juicy and easy to eat. All in all, was finished within 15 minutes of sitting down.

Upon further review, I saved a couple bucks going for happy hour (though still expensive). Would like to try the udon for my next visit.

Let me say this: I'm not a fan of udon. The noodles never stay in my chopsticks, they flip and flop around, and they're sometimes kinda gummy okay? I just don't like it. Guys. You have to try this place. 

You walk in, and what's the smell that immediately hits you? Beef? No. Onion? No. TRUFFLE. I was so confused and intrigued at the same time. This location is incredibly upscale; we had to have a reservation for two at 5:30pm on a Saturday, and we definitely did need it, so make your calls.

We started with the spicy tuna wontons and they were so cute but honestly a little tiny. They can be eaten in 2 bites. One if you're feeling sassy. But guys, take a look at the pic I snapped of the wagyu beef and truffle udon bowl. The prices are a little high, but not for what you get. There is NO price difference between the small and regular, and there is NOT a charge for extra noodles. The Sizzling Sukiyaki Beef Bowl was delicious. My friend from Thailand thought the sauce was too salty, but my American palette was just fine.

And GUYS. THE NOODLES. DIDNT. SLIP. It must be something with the consistency, and I know I'm pretty good with chopsticks, but these are the easiest to handle udon noodles I've ever had. They're homemade which I'm sure has everything to do with it. So yeah, you'll spend a lot here, but you can honestly share a WHOLE LOT. Wonderful place.

It was expensive, but the food quality was worth it!

We got 3 appetizers, and I had the tempura udon, with one mojito.

The udon was served in a GIANT bowl, it looked so good on photo. The udon was hand sliced/pulled and was very fresh itself. Highest quality food!

The appetizers were all good too.

Quite a long wait ~ 1 hours on a weekend evening.

The mojito was below average though.

Quite expensive, over $50 for this dinner. I probably won't be able to afford many dinners like this haha.
What can I say. The place is a treasure on its own. The udon was amazing and plentyful. Bowls are HUGE and portions are just right. I'm definitely a fan and would be coming back often!

This udon shop is very hip and it has plenty of seating downstairs! (they turn up the AC quite high so bring a jacket.) also worth noting there's no reception downstairs

The food comes in LARGE quantities. They offer a normal and large size for every entree for no extra charge, but believe me when i say you probably don't need the large size. it's also not really that much value added, noodles and broth are cheap! 

Taste wise, it was just okay. nothing you can't make at home with dashi, mirin, and very basic ingredients. The service was very slow - it took us 30-40 min to get our food. 

Given everything, I felt like the food was extremely overpriced for what it is and with so many other options, I would probably not come back.

I love this udon/noodle joint! I frequent the Union Square location quite a bit last year to a point I pretty much tried everything on the menu! I always start with the spicy tuna tartare cone, it's tasty! My fav was the UNI Udon given I am a UNI lover. The Tsuruton curry deluxe is really good too. You can request extra udon (no extra charge) which come in a BIG bowl. The Big bowl is bigger than your face!

Terrible experience with the hostesses at the front today. We arrived before 7pm and were promised a 40-45 minute wait. She took my phone number and we returned at 7:45 to check on the table, only to be told it would take another 15-20 minutes. She told us we could wait at the bar where she said we could transfer our food to the table. The wait ended up being over 1.5 hours vs the quoted 45 minutes.

Once we got to the table, the hostess came to us to say that we had to close the tab first. I don't understand why she didn't make it clear in the first place that by saying "transfer", she meant just CARRYING the food over to the table instead of transferring the tab...

Once we left the restaurant, I then received a call from them claiming the tab at the bar was not paid off... (well... clearly we did the first time around... after being passive aggressively served with the tab, with some serious attitude, when we sat down at the table) Despite what we told her, she strongly insisted on our return to the restaurant... Not until we broke down exactly what we ordered. Apparently they had mistaken another tab for ours and didn't even apologize that they tried to get us to walk back to the restaurant to pay for someone else's tab. (Seems like we're not the only ones misled by the word "transfer"...)

The food is not bad. It's better if you get the more traditional flavors (traditional broth and cold noodle variety with mentaiko and ikura are decent; uni quality is subpar and non-tempura cooked shrimp is usually overcooked). But the poor experience with the hostesses tonight left us all with a sour taste...
Food was delicious!!! Portions are ginormous!! Everything was fresh and super flavorful :)  we love this place and have been here more then twenty times!!

Have been here a handful of times now and always enjoyed my experience. They are known for their udon, but they also have a sushi options and a growing menu, I saw pork chops and lobster last time I went. They are usually super busy on weekends, so try and go on a week day if possible. This time I got the Spicy Soondubu Jigae Udon, which I like because it is one of the spicy dishes. Normally I would try other dishes and just add hot sauce, but for some reason they charge for hot sauce. Service is ok, they are friendly but sometimes hard to get water refill even when it's not super busy.

OMG!!!! Such an amazing place for udon noodles!!! From all the beautiful photos posted on Yelp, we kind of expected good food but we were even more amazed when we left here. We love udon!!!! I love the texture and different types of options. This place definitely take your typical udon dishes to the next level!! First of all, this place is so beautifully designed and decorated. Modern with touches of Japanese transitions. We didn't make a reservation because it was a last minute decision to visit here. But we made sure to arrive just right after they open at noon. At 1215, there were already a small line of people at the front door. We got lucky to have counter seats right the way. Their menu has all the different styles and types of udon dishes. From hot light soy sauce based soup to curry sauce to spicy or shaved ice cold udon noodles. It was very difficult to decide what to order. They also have lunch set or rice bowls to make a lunch combo. I had their top seller, CURRY DELUXE with thick udon. The size of the bowl!! Wow! Bigger than my face! The udon was slightly chewy but still tender. Excellent quality! The beef curry was just right for the noodles, lightly coated as you eat the noodles. The shrimp tempura was good but the pork cutlet was so so. Overall, love the curry udon! Different than the udon I usually have. It can get heavy as you eat since the portion is pretty large. BTW, you can ask for extra noodles without extra charge! How generous!! My friend has their shaved ice BEEF UDON. It was sooooooo good! I love the thin slices of beef, light soy sauce broth with finely chopped green onions! Bravo! I can eat it all day and everyday!! The soy sauce broth was so flavorful with a bit of sweetness. Perfect! I also had a side of uni and ikura rice bowl! Didn't think it would come as sushi rice!!! Amazing uni and ikura just made the rice bowl into a great side option! I enjoyed everything here!! So amazing, you have to come and try it out!!!

Came to Tsurutontan based on a recommendation from a passerby, but it was a very lackluster experience. I came with a friend and we sat at the bar, but our bartender was pretty quiet and unenthused. Our drinks (Asian Pear Mojito + Mango Margarita) were also pretty watered down, and we couldn't bring ourselves to finish them. Granted, this restaurant is apparently known better for their Udon dishes, so maybe I'll be back to try the restaurant experience instead.

I actually frequent this establishment quite often since I work just around the corner and is a bit of an udon fanatic.  I am actually slowly working through the menu and have tried many of the udons that this restaurant has to offer. 

The host/hostesses are nice and welcoming. Because this location is in a pretty busy location, if you are dining during peak hours, I would suggest you make a reservation. If you decide to walk in, account for wait time. I've had to wait a couple times but you have the option of putting down your name and number and can browse the shopping area as you wait for a table to open up for you. In my opinion, the food is worth the wait. 

Decor is very elaborate and quite beautiful honestly. A little dark but I suppose it creates some sort of romantic ambience if you want to bring someone out on a date here. 

The udon is fresh and the broth is so rich in flavor. I literally can't get enough of the broth. If you're unfamiliar with udon or the types of broth itself, the staff does a good job of explaining the menu. The best part about this restaurant is definitely the large selection of udons (both hot and cold. The cold udon has been my go to so far since it's getting a little toasty outside. My favorite so far has been the Uni Creme Cold Udon). The portions are generous and for one price point you can either have a "regular" portion or a "large portion".

I have been here five times and often try different things! 

Things I've ordered:
Appetizers
- Seared Salmon Sashimi
- Spicy Tuna Tartare
- Creamy Spicy Shrimp Tempura
- Soy Garlic Fried Chicken 
- Silken Tofu

Entrees
- Deluxe Chicken Katsu
- Uni Creme Udon
- Tsurontontan Deluxe 

Literally the best udon I've ever had. It is soooo chewy and soft! Appetizers are amazing and so flavorful. All the staff are friendly as well and service is always attentive. Will always be my go to and such a convenient location around many stores!

The udon here is great - lots of variety, very well made. I've had the sukiyaki and the tan tan and both were great. Waiters are great, and service is quick (but not rushed).

The one thing that is not great is the host stand here has been a total mess every time I have come - even when we have reservations. There's not enough room to wait, the hostesses seem perpetually understaffed / overwhelmed, and parties often get seated out of order (e.g. walk ins seated before reservations). Only ding in an otherwise positive experience.

Don't get fooled...

Don't go by what you see in the pics...lots of yummy Uni....NO chance...just a little flabby brownish Uni

Some of the other dishes good...but There is NO WOW that was delicious!!!
Too much broth in the soups
Seats are sunken and they haven't fixed them...NOT comfortable 
Rushed...very rushed service
Little girl up front takes you to shitty tables and then has an attitude...actually she had an attitude since I walked in...and as the front person...how about a smile???
Delicious food and excellent service. Would get a reservation. Got the shrimp tempura udon.

I liked the service at this restaurant. Our server was very friendly and informative about the menu options and any questions we had. We ordered the wagyu shabu udon in truffle dashi, uni creme udon, and salmon snow crab roll. I really liked and recommend the truffle dashi broth; the truffle and dashi flavors go really well together! I did not like the uni creme udon.. it tasted very fishy and the uni was not very good unfortunately. It was not buttery and smooth as fresh uni should be. The roll was good though.

I am a udon and ramen fan, so I have been here a few times. Previously, I have tried the Katsu curry udon which I thought to be very filling. This tine though I decided to change things up. I ordered the Katsu Don. I was happily satisfied, but not blown away.

My dish took longer than my friends' udons to come out. But, I was pleasantly surprised by a relatively large serving of  pork katsu and rice. An added benefit was that the Katsu don included a small portion of udon. I was worried that by choosing a katsu don I would have to forgo an opportunity to try another great udon dish.

The katsu that came with the Katsu don was chewy, a little more so than I would like. The sauce though was really good. As a dish Japanese people often have before strenuous activities, the dish accomplished lived up to tradition: I was happily full after my meal.

I've been here a couple of times and it has grown on me. It's a solid joint and good enough for me to come back. It's not somewhere I get super excited about. Kind of like sweatpants, it feels good and comfy, but it's not your favorite outfit. I don't salivate in anticipation, or exclaim about the texture of the noodles. But I do love big foods (preferably bigger than my head) and this bowl is BIG. It is also pretty consistent as far as quality and service.

The ambience is nice, servers are attentive, and if you make a reservation, you don't have to wait too long. The udon noodle is decent but I feel like the texture is not quite what I crave, as I like a chewier noodle (personal preference). 

So far, the Ontama Toriten Curry and Sukiyaki Udon have been the best for me. The Shrimp Tempura Udon is middling and Tan Tan the least favored. I have yet to try a cold noodle so I am holding out hope that it might be an undiscovered treasure for me. The sushi is of good quality and the Kaisen Don is a decent alternative if you're with a friend who wants udon but you're feeling like some rice that day.

I've moved to NYC in Jan, and I've been to this restaurant 5 times in the last 6 months. That's how good it is! I definitely have strong cravings for noodles, and this place has excellent cold noodle udon. It's pricey for noodles, but the quality is worth it.

I've tried many of the udon dishes including the uni udon, sukiyaki udon, and the seafood jiggae udon. I've also been to both the downtown and midtown location. Both venues are huge, but there is typically a line if you want to go for dinner in the downtown location (midtown is open for lunch). Make reservations to be safe! One con is that I had made reservations for 5 people once, and we ended up waiting 40 minutes regardless. Typically I come with only small parties after that experience. 

By far the best udon dish I've tried is the mentaiko caviar udon with thin noodles (the sauce sticks to the thinner noodles more). Opt for the larger portion since it's the same price as the regular!

I've been to this restaurant a couple times and there's beautiful decor both upstairs and downstairs that leaves me impressed every time I walk in. I've tried both the hot and cold udon as well as the thick and thin noodles and I love them all! I recommend trying the spicy tuna tartare cones as an appetizer - portion-wise, they are a bit small but they are so fresh and crispy with a hint of guacamole! It's definitely a unique dish that you don't get to try everywhere, so share with friends!

I would recommend trying the duck udon with thick noodles - the broth is extremely tasty, the noodles are chewy but not soggy, and it's a perfect blend of flavor. The best part was that the broth was not salty at all. I loved the broth so much that I pretty much slurped up all of my boyfriend's soup!

This review is based solely on the terrible service we just experienced last night at dinner.

I've eaten here in the past and haven't encountered any real issues, but the service seems to get progressively worse and worse.

Our appetizers took 30 minutes to get to our table. Our food took even longer. Once we got our food, an hour later, we noticed one of the noodle orders were incorrect. We let the server know that we were not happy with this mistake and the time it took to get our food. They insisted several times they would replace the incorrect order, but we argued that we didn't want a replacement considering it would take another eternity to get it. After many times saying we didn't want replacement noodles, they brought it to our table anyway. It was clear they were doing this so they wouldn't need to comp their mistake.

At the end of our meal, they asked if we had room for dessert, which we didn't. They were again asking this so they could comp the dessert and not the noodles that were incorrect, but we didn't feel like waiting around for more food. Once again, they just brought the dessert to our food, even though we said no many times. At the end of it all, we were charged for everything, all of the mistakes, minus the dessert we didn't even ask for. 

So, no, I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone. My parents were restaurant owners and I've worked in the restaurant industry separately and this service was unacceptable. The manager should have offered to comp the noodles they mistakenly brought an hour later or even the $8 appetizer we had willingly ordered. They shouldn't have brought over a subpar dessert we never wanted to start with.

Not a fan at all.. 

I guess a big bowl of udon noodles seems really enticing but you have to make it taste good for me to finish the whole thing.. I mean I did, but that's only because I was hungry. And I'm not going to waste food; my mother taught me better.

The flavors were nothing special nor memorable.
I actually felt really gross after eating so much-- that's what you get when you have no self control 

There are way better places in the city so I would t recommend coming here.

I absolutely love this place. There's a sophisticated feel that comes from the simplicity of the decor. The food is delicious and beautifully presented. The service staff is knowledgeable and very helpful. The service itself is seamless and efficient. I must say these were the biggest bowls of udon I've ever seen in my life. I very much enjoyed the spicy tuna cone, the wagyu sushi just melted in my mouth. From the decor, to the house made udon, to the presentation I would say this place strives to bring an authentic Japanese experience to NYC. I will be back and I definitely would recommend.

Whenever I visit New York I always make an effort to visit this restaurant. They have a large selection of dishes on the menu that I always want to come back and try something new. The udon bowls come in regular or large, both for the same price! So obviously I'd order a large! Though it's impossible for me to finish, I always am very satisfied with my meal. 

For food I would recommend the the Sukiyaki Buns and the Spicy Tuna Tartare Cones for appetizers and for udon it's really comes down to personal preference. I've had the US Wagyu Shabu Udon which has a clear broth so it isn't as heavy as the creamier broths like curry. Curry is always good you can't go wrong with ordering curry. The Truffle Creme with Mushrooms is very fragrant with truffle oil so if you love you're truffles I'd recommend that. The udon noodlesitself is cooked to perfection.

Service was great. Our server was very attentive and made sure to keep our water glasses filled and our table cleared of empty plates. The manager even made an affront to come to the table to see how we were doing. 

I would 100% recommend this restaurant for anyone planning to visit New York.

Wow! Not gonna lie, i thought i accidentally stepped into a hotel haha it is so nice!! Now onto the rest of my meal. 

I came here with a party of 4 for lunch and everything was great. Our server, Annie, was attentive and sweet but not overbearing which i really appreciated.

The food was also amazing. You can tell they use really fresh ingredients. My group got some apps to share and we all got our own bowl of udon, as well. I got the uni creme pasta and boy, is it good! Can't wait to try everything else on their menu. A must-visit when you're in New York!

Chill Udon spot in the heart of Union Square.  Off of 16th street in a hidden fashion, but as you enter, the establishment opens up into various layers of a dining experience.

With ground level, subtle downstairs area, and an upstairs dining area, you are pleasantly surprised. 

The staff is helpful and will give you a run through of the many Udon options that exist.  Kudos to this place as they immerse Udon in regular broth, their version of a sweet broth, their version of a a curry/creamy broth, and various other broths.  They also serve cold Udon which is an interesting twist that may have me go back.

The Wangyu with mushroom was portion heavy and I definitely had to get the back half of my meal to go.  So an empty stomach is ideal for this dining experience.

An overall win to the evening and would definitely go back.

Wow, I've never had udon before but this really knocked it out of the park as my first entry into these types of noodles. I had the curry deluxe which didn't disappoint, and the portions were enormous. Highly recommend trying this at least once if you're visiting New York! I was told that they have another location in Japan that's very busy so I had high expectations as well.

I've been here a few times and the food never really amazed me, until I ordered the Sukiyaki udon this time. It was an explosion of flavors unlike the other udons i've had. It was a perfect balance of flavors, not too sweet not too salty. It was so savory. I would recommend the Sukiyaki udon to everyone.

I've been here more than three times and each with a new group of friends. The place has a great ambiance and decor. I especially love their non alcoholic drinks because flavor of the drink I had was refreshing and no overly superficial. I enjoy their enormous bowls of Udon and tuna tartare. Their tuna tartare is worth trying. My friend who was skeptical about the dish because of previous experience end up enjoying the dish very much.

Love, love their udon. This spot is so trendy and modern and their food is great! I was surprised by the sheer amount of space in this restaurant. I always crave uni but uni in the city is extremely pricey. The uni udon (thin noodles and not the creme one) always satisfies my craving without breaking my bank account even though it is still a bit more pricey. The big bowls definitely makes you feel like you are getting your money's worth, however I am still able to finish an entire bowl by myself.

This is a place near union square in which they provide different types of udon.  As far as I know this place is a direct import from Japan.  When it first opened the hype was really high and people had to wait for hours to get seated, but now I don't think you have to wait much at this point unless it is Weekend dinner. 

I think when we were there last time (been there 3 times I think), we waited for like 15 minutes before getting seated.  We ordered some appetizers (they are all decent).  Then we ordered different kind of udon to our likings which were all good.   In summary, this is the kind of place in winter time, after spending a lot of day time outside, you wanna come in for a noodle with warm broth.  A perfect place for it.  A little pricey, but still doable.
I went to this place with a friend without doing much research and the food was surprisingly good.

Came here with a friend for lunch. Make sure you get here before 3PM because it closes for lunch at this time. 

I ended up getting the curry beef udon bowl. It was $16 and it was very delicious. I asked for extra noodles (which is supposed to be free) but compared to my friend who didn't get the extra noodles, it looked to be about the same. I'm not sure what the deal was. 

The noodles themselves were quite delicious. The broth was also great. However, it was clear that the dish was mostly udon and there was very little curry beef in it. That was pretty disappointing. My friend got the uni creme udon. She let me try the broth and it was actually amazing. So creamy and delicious. However, it didn't seem as if she had much more than her noodles as well. 

The cool thing about lunch is that for a small extra fee you can get a mini donburi bowl. I ended up getting the spicy tuna avocado. It is quite mini but delicious. Also when they brought it out, it was missing the avocado! The place was pretty empty, so it wasn't like they were swamped in the kitchen. I'm not sure how they messed up so many things. 

Finally, I would just like to point out that there is happy hour all day every day at the bar. This means that there are some beers for $4. However, you cannot enjoy these deals at the table, which is pretty weird and whacky. 

Overall, definitely great udon. However, at the price point, the lack of meat / filling and the so-so service, I would have to think twice about coming back here.

overprice for udons. their broth is rich, it is yummie, but it is way overprice for the portions, i ordered the uni udon, again, the broth is rich but there were like "ONE" or "ONE POINT FIVE" uni in the big bowl. it is definitely swimming in there. 
i guess you really goes there to enjoy the atmosphere and the huge serving bowl.

This food here is always good and the restaurant has great decor and is very spacious.  It's a little bit pricey for lunch though (compared to others in the area) and service can be slow -- don't expect to be able to get back to work within the hour!

Not the best but a great hefty lunch spot. The ramen is decent and you'll never have the sinking feeling of fishing chopsticks through your bowl to find more noodles because you can just upgrade to a "large" portion that's massive enough to make you feel guilty in all the best ways.

Quick Summary:
- Large bowls and plates, so portions appear small (beautiful presentation however)
- Appetizer was amazing delicious
- Udon was chewy and thick! One noodle is a mouthful. 
- Air conditioning was on a subtle side, but it was enough to remain cool and comfortably eat hot noodles. 

We reserved our spot and entered the store a little bit too early, and we were directed to our seats at the exact time we reserved. 

The menu was vibrant and easy to see because it was covered in beautiful pictures of food. Each dish name had a description to explain the ingredients and the quantities. The waitress was very kind, and when we asked that it was our first time and we wanted to know the recommendations, she explained them in great detail. 

We ordered an appetizer, udon, and a dessert. The one thing we noticed about the appetizer was that the picture in the menu made it appear it had more portions. The bluefin tuna tartar arrived in a wide dish and the tartar lay right in the center, a fourth of the size to the plate. HOWEVER, the taste was out of this world. The sea urchin melted in the mouth and was sweet. The bluetin tuna tartar was also soft, and this all went well because of the delicious sauce. I would definitely order this again despite its size. 

The udon was also a surprise. It was a beautiful presentation with the udon noodles in the large wide bowl. Again, the plates and the bowl appeared larger to the portions, and looks was deceiving. It might also have been because of the hot weather, but it filled me up 100%. I ordered the dish with tempura vegetables and shrimp. The tempura was crispy (when it was still floating over the soup surface, and it was light)

Finally, the dessert. We ordered a water cake, which is what I have eaten before. It tasted exactly like it but I loved how the dark sugar syrup and the kinako powder wasn't overpoweringly sweet. My friend became a fan of the kinako powder, so I was glad I introduced it to her. It came with ice cream, so I mixed it with the water cake, after pouring the dark syrup and kinako powder over it. This was perfect for the hot, humid summer weather in New York. 

If I visit New York again, I would love to come back.

We came here for dinner on 4th of July and didn't make reservations so we ended up waiting for around 20 mins. 

The udon here didn't disappoint! We got the beef udon with thick udon and the duck with thin udon. Both were really good but I preferred the thick noodles, which had a nice chewy texture. Beef and duck were flavourful and not too oily. You also get to choose between a regular or large for the same price. I opted for the regular and thought it was a good amount already.

Overall, the Udon is on the pricier side but still worth trying!

Okay, I love this place and have eaten here a good number of times (like, once a month or so) but lately I have been getting sick the day after I eat dinner here. The last time was when I ordered the creamy uni udon, and my tummy felt so off the next day. Last night, my boyfriend ordered the tan tan udon (spicy broth with ground pork) and I had the spicy mentaiko udon (plus we ordered the tuna cones and wagyu sirloin to share). This morning, we both woke up with bad tummy aches and felt like puking :/ Not sure what is going on here.... the food is very tasty, but if it's giving us diarrhea then I will not come back ever again.

I came here with a friend on a Sunday night, and it took about 20 minutes to get seated.

We sat at a table, which was a huge plus. If you're bring a date, ask for a reservation at a table - the alternative is a bench facing a bamboo screen.

The portions here are HUGE. I got the Tsurutontan (shrimp and vegetable tempura udon) and the servings were twice what you'd get anywhere else.

The broth was spectacular, while the tempura and udon were average. I'd come back again, but try one of the rice bowls instead.

Ate there with a bunch of friends I hadn't seen in a very long time.  Menu is perfect, something for everyone. Would like to see more gluten free options but it was still great.  Service was awesome and was very accommodating.  Will be back definitely whenever I'm in the area. Very nice decor as well.

This place gets packed! Get a reservation in advance. I came in on a Tuesday with a reservation at 7 for 2. We waited about 10 minutes before we were seated (we were able to get some delicious cocktails for $9 each at the bar; the bar always has happy hour). My friend and I shared the Sea & Truffle roll as an appetizer. I was curious about the truffle oil used in the roll, but surprisingly it worked really well with tuna, salmon, and yellowtail. The truffle does not overpower the the taste of the raw fish. We then shared the Uni Udon ($24). The udon noodles were so delicious. Perfectly cooked to the right consistency. Usually with uni, you can either have uni that can taste like garbage or taste like a creamy sea breeze. Thankfully the uni here is the latter. To end our meal, we had the water cake. This was my first time trying such a dessert, although it's been around for a few years in the NYC dessert scene. The cake is more like a gelatin. It didn't have too much flavor by itself, but with the ice cream and kuromitsu it tasted good. Not the most amazing dessert, but it ended the meal well. I will be coming back to try the other udon dishes!
Good service, good sushi, beautiful bar and decor. Recommended.  Be seated downstairs for a romantic dinner.

This is one of the most classic udon spots in nyc! It's a really nice restaurant on the inside and they have a nice substantial menu. The udon obviously is what most people get and it's the same price for a regular sized bowl or a larger sized bowl (definitely get the larger sized bowl if you can finish it because it's really good)

My only complaint is that it is kinda expensive so it's definitely not somewhere I'd go often but I would definitely come back!

Good food, great service and generous portions. Been here a few times and everything has been consistent. Tuna "cones" are incredibly tasty as well as the signature rolls. Pork dumplings are delicious though I was not a fan of fried chicken. And the udon....delicious! You can upgrade to a larger bowl for the same price and its more than enough for 2 people especially if you are getting curry as its very rich. Very quick and attentive service so overall a good experience. (and thanks for 90s throwback music)

Came here on a Friday night for dinner and waited about 45 min which isn't too unreasonable for a popular place like this. 
The server was extremely friendly in guiding us through the menu for our first visit! 

Drink menu here is extensive which is great for anyone who likes sipping on some liquor with their meals. We had a glass of Gueissard Les Papilles rose and a Complices de Loire sparkling champagne, both were great and paired well with the Udon. 

Their Udon comes in a regular and large all for the same price! My friend got the deluxe while I got the shrimp tempura and both were delicious and tasted uniquely different from each other. The noodles were chewy and smooth and the toppings really accentuated the broth. 

For dessert we gave into the temptation and ordered their water cake and it was definitely worth the hefty price tag. The cake was light and refreshing and the toppings it came with added depth to the whole ensemble. 

Overall it was a great meal but due to the prices, definitely not an everyday dinner destination

I've always been a fan of Udon, but in USA there just not enough recognition for udon than for ramen. We see in recent years how ramen shops starts opening throughout major cities in the USA. And now udon restaurants are beginning to open.
There was first Marukame Udon open in Honolulu, and then in SF in recent months. But never a more upscale udon restaurant until Tsurutontan open. Tsurutontan was always a restaurant I wanted to go on my next visit to Tokyo, Japan. But since I am visiting NY for a few days, I took the opportunity to see what the NY branch has to offer.
Tsurutontan is very metro accessible, just a few blocks off the union square station. The host would only seat you if all your party is here, even if the restaurant is not full yet, so be sure to go together or be on time.
If it's your first time here, the waiter/waitress would explain to you about the menu in detail: what's popular here, hot and cold udon options, thick/normal udon or thin udon, and larger option for the same price!
There are just so many choices in the menu! and all of them looked very delicious. The price isn't cheap, most udon ranges from mid $1x to upper $2x. I ended up going with the deluxe bowl with regular udon, and 1 zaru thin udon (simple iced udon). Both were very delicious.
Their bowl and spoon are huge! And the content is a lot too if you order the large size.
FYI, large size and normal size prices are the same, but make sure you can finish it if you order the large one, don't want to waste food.

I came here on a Sunday night. There was no wait for table for two people. The two-people tables are structured in a unique way: they basically divide 4 people tables to 2 people tables: two of you sit parallel to each other and there are decorating walls separating you from the 2 people opposite. 

As for food, I like the sukiyaki udon that I got. There was generous portion of vegetables and beef. You can choose regular/large portion and thin/thick noodle, all of the same price. I had regular portion thick noodle, and was so full after eating. 

The dessert was ok.  The chocolate cake has nothing memorable.

My boyfriend and I came here on a Friday night around 8:30. It is located right by Union Square. When we walked in we were greeted and told it would be a 30 minute wait. Not that bad for a Friday night; so we sat at the bar and got a drink. When our table was ready, it gave us a nice view of the rope wall. The seating is like a booth. 

I had never been to a restaurant that solely focused on udon so the menu was a bit overwhelming, but what I really loved that they did was put pictures so you can visualize what you are ordering. Our waitress was very attentive and helpful with answering questions. I ordered the Tsurutontan Deluxe which was labeled as a best seller and he got the truffle creme with crab and mushroom. For our appetizer we got the yellowtail with scallion sushi which was incredible! I think the sushi here is underrated it tasted so fresh. 

My dish was so flavorful. Loved how they did the dashi broth. Before I came here I never liked udon that much but I am definitely converted. I got the thick noodles which were a great contrast to everything. The tempura shrimp was cooked to perfection. The beef and chicken were very flavorful as well. They do give you a large portion but overall I unfortunately do think it is a bit overpriced but it is New York so I kinda get it. Something that really turned me off was the fact that we were charged $6 for a beer at the bar and then $10 for the same beer at the table. I think they should make that clearer in the future.

Probably a 3.5 star for me. I had a reservation for a party of 7 on a Monday night at 7 pm (won't seat you unless everyone is present), and the ambiance of the place wasn't bad.

Hamachi Carpaccio ($14) and Tsurutontan Deluxe ($24) set me back a good amount. For the deluxe bowl of ramen, they offer you a regular size or large size (both cost the same amount of $). I was hungry so I went for the large, and it was fairly large, but a good amount for one hungry person. In hindsight, I would have gotten something where they don't put the tempura directly in the soup, making everything a bit soggy.

Their menu is pretty extensive - curries, sashimi, dry udon, etc. A lot to try. Quality is pretty decent, but a bit too pricey for me to frequent too often.

I love udon in general, so I was pretty excited to try this place out. A couple of us were late, but they wouldn't seat us (party of 3) unless the whole group was present. That's totally understandable if the venue is super busy, but it's a bit strange to enforce when your restaurant is close to half empty... Anyways, besides that small hiccup, on to the food!

- Wagyu Mushroom Sukiyaki Udon: we had the thick noodles with this, and the udon was outstanding; every mouthful was like biting into a pillow. The soup base was light, with a hint of sweetness from the sukiyaki, and I would order this again in a heartbeat.
- Tsurutontan Deluxe: the broth was very good and quite light, a welcome relief from all the greasy pizza and burgers we ingested in the past few days. We tried the thin noodles with this, and although it was still good, we definitely gave the trophy to the thick noodles. Our server said that the thin noodles are usually paired with the creamier, saucy bowls, which in hindsight makes sense. 

It was a bit of a mistake to order 2 bowls with the large portion of noodles (at no extra cost) for 3 of us - 1 bowl with the large portion would have done it, the portions were so generous! The thick udon noodles were some of the best udon I've ever had, and I hope to be back soon!

It is really big portion for sure. Big bowl, extra noddle no extra charge, but me and my friend ordered 2 different flavor both recommended on the manu. They surely taste not good. Th supple is not broth, but pure soy sauce with hot water, and the curry flavor is quite salty, I feel I can cook better flavor.

I was invited for lunch as the guest of friends.
Ideally and easily located at the fringe of Union Square. 
Subway is less than 400 feet walking distance. 

As I did not make the plans, I had no preconceived notions, no idea what to expect.
Arrived to find my meal already ordered for me.
Looking around, the restaurant is a long shotgun with a seemingly large seating capacity.
Bar is organized and sexy. Tables and booths provide a bit more intimacy.
Visually, designed to appeal to the American vision of Japanese culture, but neither cheap nor overdone.
Lots of wood and hanging paper.

Food arrived quickly.
Several enormous covered bowls. 
And, side plates of tempura.
Our server took off the covers from the bowls, unveiling deep, steaming broth with thick udon noodles.
Aromatically inviting.
Visually exciting. 
Each bowl with slightly different vegetables and proteins.
Tempura was perfectly crispy and full of flavor from the shrimp and vegetables, not the oil. 
The udon broth was complex, saturated with pork flavor but not fatty or heavy.
Thick udon noodles with the optimal amount of chewy texture, but exactly the way they should be prepared.
I'm a healthy eater, but there's enough in each bowl for 2.
I did not have dessert, but the water cake looked cleverly interesting and my friends definitely enjoyed mixing the side sauces and dustings to flavor.
The green tea cake also looked good and was quickly consumed.
Service was very good.
Prices commensurate with the quality and volume of food. 
Added to my list of places to return on my next trip to NYC.

Nice interior with friendly servers. Their udon comes in two different sizes, small and large but the price is the same. I had uni udon in large size. You can totally finish large size! It was pretty good but little salty.

Loved their Udon noodles! Here visiting a friend that is a local and this is her favorite Udon spot in the city. Fun fact: you can get a regular and large portion, and costs the same. The large portion could definitely be split between two people. Nice atmosphere and great service.

Great Lunch experience! The menu can get a bit overwhelming - who knew Udon can hold up into so many different preparations? - but we stick to the classics such as Tempura Zaru Udon (served cold) and Curry-style Udon, which my BF & I thoroughly enjoyed. You can choose either small or large udon, which I think the earlier works better on cold-based dishes, and opposite for the latter. Portion is generous, and you still have the option to upgrade into Large, which means you get more noodles! 

Very excited that Bostonians will soon welcome an outlet in town!

I come in with a friend to satisfy our noodle cravings.
Place is bigger than you think! 

With a party of 2, expect a table with a bench. Expect to also sit next to your partner. Luckily you can get the two tables that have chairs that actually face your partner. 

I got the bench inside the restaurant and the benches seem very tight to enter in. There is also not that much space to eat considering the big bowls you get. 

For food, you get the sushi special menu, the drink menu and the noodle/curry/anything else menu. 
The bowls are HUGE, that come with large SPOONS and a noodle-slurping bowl. I got the beef udon and my friend got the curry udon. 
The waiters will ask you for either thin/thick noodles.
The waiter will also ask you for either large or regular (more noodles or more meat). 

Expect a really huge bowl, a really intimidating (in a good way) bowl. Cus it was massive and I absolutely loved how ridiculously large it was. The noodles were nice and chewy. However, some noodles were still stuck to each other. The soup base was not as strong as I would like it to be, as I didn't get much aroma. But overall, okay noodles and soup base. 

Bathroom for men and women are completely away from each other. The men's bathroom is straight down when you enter to your right. The women's bathroom is to the left as you enter. 

Service was okay as well, and waiter kept apologizing for where we sat, as we clearly struggled to actually sit on the benches... that cannot be MOVED. Respect for the waiter as he sympathized with us as well. Overall, good food with awesome bowls and utensils.

my go to is always the tsurotontan deluxe! even though 2 sizes are offered, they are both the same price. i even surprised myself when i finished the large portion! highly recommend for anyone who loves udon or japanese cuisine!

While the food is good and consistent, their biggest problem is that making a reservation is meaningless.  Been here 4 times and every time they make you wait at least 15 minutes before they seat you after you check in.  What's the point of making a reservation if you're just waiting anyway?  Annoying.  This is for the Union square location

A group of ten for dinner, a mistaken reservation at a another location usually, and people running late usually spells trouble for a group dinner. That's exactly what happened to us with about half of us running late for a 6 pm reservation. I also made the wrong reservation for the Midtown location instead. However, the staff was very accommodating and allowed us to be seated once we cancelled the other reservation when we arrived at 7 pm. They also opened up an area usually reserved for special parties on the second level for us. 

As for the food, we all ordered the udon ( wagyu truffle, wagyu mushroom, and a few others) and a few appetizers to shared. We also ordered a red wine to share which we all agreed was delicious! The udon portions were quite generous and they give you the option to have a regular or large portion as well as thin or thick udon. We all ordered the thick with the exception of one from our party. 

Great place for parties and definitely recommend!

@TsuruTonTan
 
"Tsuru"--The sound of slurping noodles
"Ton"--The sound of kneading and shaping udon
"Tan"--The sound of cutting udon
 
These three sounds embody the spirit of the finest, handmade udon. The other sound was of my teenage daughter singing along to Whitney Houston while she slurped that entire huge bowl down.

The hostess was willing to seat the two of us without a reservation at 5:45 pm but she did not seem very happy. I don't know if something else bothering her. But our wait staff was the warmest and most professional person we could have asked for. Price was reasonable for the Union Square area.

This place is known for its extremely large BOWL of noodles and it caught my eye when i saw that they had truffle oil udon so we came spontaneously and we got the wagyu shabu udon with truffle oil and the uni creme udon. Im a big fan of truffle oil and i had to come here to try out the truffle oil udon. the atmosphere is nice and waiters were really attentive to explain and give you their recommendations. however i was disappointed when the wagyu udon was overly oil, it had me feeling really bloated. but i would still come back to try the other dishes that they have.

Spicy tuna tartar cones - very cute presentation of a delicious appetizer - tangy and tasty
Shaved ice sukiyaki udon - very hearty, delicious broth, delicious meat, and delicious noodles - and with the addition of ice makes this the perfect dish to have during the summer
Tempera Zaru udon - tempera for the crunch, udon for the chill and slippery(?) feeling - a combination that just spells out "oishi" ^_^

I love this place. It's a nice Asian fusion vibe. The udon noodles are amazing. They offer a bigger portion for the same price. The truffle sushi is also unreal. Definitely my favorite noodle soup I've had in the city. Usually a 45 minute wait.

Huge servings of udon with top notch service and delicious drinks like the mango margarita and Moscow mule. For appetizers we had the fried chicken and creamy shrimp tempura, and thoroughly liked both. 

Entree wise we had the tan tan bowl with thin noodles and curry deluxe with thick noodles. I have to say I preferred the thin noodles (which are still broader than ramen noodles) as the thick were way too heavy and chewy for me. 2 bowls were more than enough for 3 people. Order large size and take leftovers to go as the price for regular and large is the same. The chocolate cake is an absolute must have and the perfect end to a satisfying meal.

Service was okay. They left you alone, which isn't to say they were inattentive, but it didn't add any stars to this review.

Food was also just okay - a little pricy for the quality though the quantity was much much larger than I had expected. The bowls are huge! 
One thing I would actively encourage you NOT to get is their uni - which was not fresh at all, it wasn't creamy or bright yellow but instead a bit gray and chewy (I only took a few tentative bites because I was afraid it had gone bad).
We waited for 30 minutes and the waiter made the mistake of saying she called our name when she didnt.

Celebrated my birthday here with my coworkers for lunch.  Now I understand why there's always a line around dinner time.  This place is GOOD.  For appitzers you must get the Spicy Tuna Tartare Cones, Sukiyaki Buns, Soy Garlic Fried Chicken.  Shimp dumplings were just okay.  For the main course.  Everyone was happy with their order.  The biggest hit seemed to be Sizzling Sukiyaki Udon.  Also the best sellers that are listed were pretty good.  Spicy Tan Tan = Yes.  The Tsurutontan is HUGE.  That's easily 2 meals.  That was my dish and I enjoyed it.

Great Service.  Perfect date spot.  I'll be back!

I was so excited for Tsurutontan but was deceived by their exquisite interior design and atmosphere and typical New York pricing. Two things I really appreciated: free extra noodles (just like in Japan! or just order the large) and the interior decor was on point. Other than that, their extensive menu was not necessarily äuthentic with their Korean-fusion like spicy seafood jjigae udon, spicy soondubu jjigae and their Italian?! with snow crab, trufle oil and parmigiana reggiano. I ordered a Nabeyaki Udon and a Tsurutontan Deluxe without the beef (I don't eat beef) and was disappointed to find the broth very lack-luster. It tasted like chicken-scented water, very thin and flavorless. I asked for the tempura on the side so it wouldn't get soggy. I appreciate the large portions but it was hard for me to finish my dish not because of the size, but rather the quality of the noodles and broth I was eating. There are so many ramen places in New York and I was incredibly excited to have possibly found an Udon place for a change, but I guess I'll just have to continue on my search. This was definitely worse than Raku. On the fence whether I'm going to give this place another shot. Also another thing that bothered me was that our booth was right next to the stairs going down to another section of the restaurant and all the waiters/waitresses chose there to gossip and hang out.. really disturbed our dinner vibe and wish they would've moved elsewhere.

This was my first time eating Udon noodles and coming to this place. The ambient is super nice and the waiter was great! Definitely recommend coming here, they serve big portions for a very reasonable price.

I was so excited to try this place out and it definitely lived up to expectations!! I came for dinner on a Friday night, party of 2, and didn't really have to wait. 

We started off with their spicy tuna avocado cones which were small but really good! I had their uni cream udon with thick noodles and in the large size and my friend had the Tsurutontan deluxe with thick noodles and large as well. Both tasted really good! I almost finished mine but my friend couldn't finish hers. The uni cream udon doesn't have much toppings except uni which is probably why it was easier for me to finish, while the Tsurutontan comes with lots of different tempura and chicken pieces. Both were really good- depending if you want to go for something creamy or a regular dashi broth. 

So glad I finally tried this. I will definitely come back in the future!

Truly did not know udon could taste this incredible. So much flavor and texture with such a simple noodle. 

The portion sizes are HUGE - price is pretty high, but they give you a free upgrade to large so it's worth it. 

Ordered the truffle based udon and the spicy cold udon - both complement each other nicely as the truffle could get a little heavy at times, and the cold did lack the punch of flavor given that there is no accompanying soup. But the truffle udon was so savory - each bite was HEAVENLY. Highly recommend it! The texture of the noodles is perfect. 

All in all, highly recommend! Will drop by to try their other udon, as they have more varieties than you could ever imagine.

Came here on a whim on the weekend. 

The ambiance of this place is chill.  There's a lot of space here and you can enjoy your conversation in peace. 

For the food, the portion size is huge. There is Regular Size and Large Size.  If this is your first time here, go for the Udon. I went for the Wagyu truffle based with the thick udon and it was extremely tasteful. 

Perfect place to come for some good comfort food.
This place is retarded, won't sit us with two kids because one other party is a few minutes away.  What is the difference between 4 and 5?

Came here for the noodles but also ordered the sushi and it was amazinggg!! The noodles came in a huge bowl and I just couldn't finish it so I took it to go but my curry noodle was amazing the broth tasted so rich and creamy.

Don't get me wrong the place looks great. I guess most of the money was spend on the interior design and not on food. I order 4 dish with 2 drinks = $160

1- veggie with truffle : good truffle dish.  But they only gave us 8. YES. 8 small slice of vegetable. Really?

2- tuna tartare: unbelievable tasteless. Basically taste like grind meat. You suppose to diced the tuna because it will taste slimy. 

3- Wagyu beef: 6 small slice for $40. Good price if it's quality meat done right. they over cook the beef to well done. Really?? Plus there was tendon in the beef steak. I had Wagyu beef in Japan and other restaurants in NYC, it's suppose to melt in your mouth. Right? 

4 - uni noodle: the noodle was the other thing that was done right in this meal. Good bite with enough chewiness to it. Uni was ok. I guess they forgot to put a little sea salt to the uni to bring out the favor.  

5- two drinks : nothing much to praise about. 

Conclusion: Bill come out to $160 with tax and tips. Come out of the restaurant feeling hungry and tasteless. Don't think I'll be back.

I love this place!! 

HUGE, and I mean GINORMOUS, bowls of udon. I love the uni crème udon and the truffle mushroom udon. So flavorful and delicious. Free upgrade so why not get a larger one? Totally sharable too if you don't want to overstuff yourself.

Karage chicken appetizer is really good too along with some others. They also have some yummy drinks.

The food is very interesting to say the least. You're treated with good portions that will definitely be enough. The appetizers were okay (we got the chicken in the sweet sauce and the fried dough dumplings), and the entree was okay as well. I got the spicy beef tofu mix. I kind of wished the broth was less fishy though.

Dinning here was a fun experience, all of the food was tasty and the atmosphere was engaging. This would be a great place to bring parents or friends from out of town, it's right near Union Square--so it's a super convenient location. 

The restaurant is huge, with many different rooms, meaning there are a variety of atmospheres. In addition to standard tables for 2-4, there are large booths that would be good for group dining, and in the downstairs room there are low counters where you could sit side-by-side with a date. 

You can only order Happy Hour drinks at the bar, which I found annoying. 

The portion size on the udon is HUGE, we're talking a bathtub of broth... but hey, makes it a fun experience! I recommend ordering a "large" (extra noodles, same price as a regular), and sharing it with a friend. 


Food: delicious, huge portions. 
Drinks: totally fine/good, but expensive. 
Atmosphere: feels New Yorkey but approachable.

It's a beautiful restaurant in terms of decor and ambience. Location is also super convenient. Food is amazing and nice seeing udon making its mark as a delicacy noodle in NYC (I'm looking at you, ramen). I'm a big fan of their sashimi and uni rice sets but I wish the portions were bigger for the price.

We came here pretty late. Let's just say for the price you pay and the portion you get. It's definitely a bang for your buck kind of spot. The food, the service was amazing. You would think cutting close to the hr before closing. Most servers would rush the job or give you crap food. They were patient, and served us with a smile. It's definitely a great date spot! I would love to come back and try their other choices of foods!

Soo delicious. Udon over ramen any day. I haven't eaten a lot of udon and my friend suggested this place and it was amazing. Large portions and reasonably priced for location and food quality. Ordered as follow.

Spicy tuna tartere cones- amazing and great bite size appetizers. Delicious and crispy cones. Would strongly recommend.
Shishito pepper- I haven't found anyone who could mess this dish. This was a easy pick.
Uni corn- was good but not enough uni. Did you had to pick uni corn over spicy tuna cones, go with the spicy tuna cones.
US wagyu and mushroom sukiyaki- sweet and savory broth. So delicious and packed with lots mushrooms and nice slices of beef. Wagyu beef I hope. I ordered a regular siZe and it was more than enough.

Such a great place for dinner. Absolutely worth the wait if there is one.

I got the vegetable tempura udon (regular size, thick noodles). First of all, the udon comes in a bowl twice the size of my face - the portions are so large. Usually, vegetable tempura consists of 3 or 4 pieces of bland vegetables. This tempura was next level - not only was there a pile of tempura (maybe 7 or so pieces), they included items like shiso leaves, seaweed, and egg tempura, along with the classic vegetables. The tempura was well seasoned and full of flavor that complimented the clear udon broth. 

The restaurant is also large (enough for our party of 10, although expect a wait) with a great atmosphere and friendly waiters.
This place was great! Make sure you make a reservation as the restaurant is normally packed! If you can ask for JUSTIN as your waiter! He was so helpful, attentive and fast! I will be back !

One of my favorite udon spots in NYC because the food is delicious, service is attentive and friendly, great atmosphere, and you can make reservations! It's my go to spot to take my friends that visit. All the apps and udon that I've tried have all been really good. 
 
Items I have tried : corn karage, tuna tartare, truffle wagyu udon , scallop uni ikura udon, uni cream udon, wagyu nigiri 

Also to upgrade your udon size to a large is free!
The classic beef udon is the best udon I have ever had. I would definitely come back. Their thick udon is just amazing. Chewy and smooth. I would like to try their thin udon next time.

Huge portions, love the noodles and their chewy texture. Highly recommend, just a tad bit salty in the wagyu sukiyaki. Definitely left feeling super full and still had things to bring back to eat later. Come if you are an udon fanatic, because this restaurant will satisfy those cravings for sure! Try the hand rolls as well, I was surprisingly very satisfied with them!

Love the large large udon here! The soup is great! They also have a very large selection of appetizers and other non-udon food. The only downside is they get very busy, so it isn't a place that you can sit around for long to catch up with friends.

My family found this place walking around nyc and it is SO GOOD! I got sushi and it was amazing and my family all got noodle dishes and I tried them and it was delicious. The price for what you get and the quality is amazing and I would totally recommend this to people looking for a noodle place (or sushi place)! And the staff is so nice :) very helpful

Fortunately, there was no wait even on Saturday night...amazing! My party was 2 people. 

I got the sukiyaki udon and the corn kakiage. The corn kakiage was very crispy and just the right texture but it lacked a bit of flavor by itself. Fortunately the spicy mayo sauce it was served with improved the flavor but was a bit overwhelming for my taste. Overall I was still very satisfied with this appetizer.

As for the sukiyaki udon, it was very very flavorful. There was lots of meat and vegetables in a hot stone bowl. The sauce accompanying the noodles was very good and it was a fantastic mix of the ingredients. Would definitely recommend.

Service and atmosphere were very nice and no complaints.

I had my birthday dinner here with 17 people and it was fantastic. Service and food was great. There was a little hiccup and they brought out a free lady m slice of cake which was yummy! Will be back. Skinny udon noodles has made me like udon!

Our food was amazing as always however the service we received was extremely below par for a restaurant that serves $20+ entrees. Our food was brought to us as expected but our server never returned to check up on us. Not even ask if our food was good after we received it. My wife asked for her remaining meal to be boxed so we can take it with us. The server discarded it and never brought it back to us. Franklin, we were celebrating our wedding anniversary and could've gone to a really really expensive place but we chose to come to TsuruTonTan for dinner. Thank you for ruining our anniversary dinner.

Went again with friends. I still got my fav uni cream udon - still great.  Though this time's uni didn't taste as fresh. And meitaiko was a little less than before. This time we tried some dessert: green tea ice cream with lady M - absolutely yummy and water cake - very creative and yum! More like a traditional Japanese dessert.

Holy moly the sizes! Ordering a large is the same price as a regular size so I ordered the large and a BASIN is brought before full of delicious broth and noodles . Been here a couple times now and is always a good meal. The rain drop cake is also a fun dessert to finish the meal with. It gets very crowded and noisy during peak times (I try to avoid it then). Very tasty and love this spot, the appetizers and desserts look quite good too and will have to try them out in future visits.

First time here and food was delicious! Staff and waitresses are spectacular and friendly. Host Jackie was very friendly. Ordered the tuna tar tar cones and it was really good. We also had the hamachi, seared spicy salmon, corn fritters, and some kind of mushroom with truffle oil, the mushroom was also one of our favorites that night. Udon is flavorful and portion size is huge. Ordered the spicy seafood udon, and I couldn't finish it, had to pack it to go. Environment was unique and definitely worth the wait. Make sure to make reservations beforehand. Would definitely be going back again!

Best udon I've ever had, and amazingly good sushi. The truffle wagyu udon is as decadent as it sounds and even more delicious. Same goes for the truffle sea sushi. The spicy tuna cones appetizer was also fun and tasty. Be advised that the udon portions are HUGE!

The bowls are comically massive, as is the menu which is complete with pictures of each dish. Never thought I'd see udon made so many ways, but I'm definitely impressed by the good food and more elevated ambiance. For a party of 7 we waited 45 minutes on a Friday night at 8pm. The wait isn't too bad when you're in the heart of Union Square with tons of shops to kill time at. For each dish, you can pick thin or thick udon noodles (thick is the way to go!!) and small or large (same price, so why not go for large and pack up extras for a second meal?).

FOOD:
1. Sizzling sukiyaki udon 5/5: SO good and piping hot, plus you get some crispier noodles at the bottom. This makes for a comfort meal with really tender beef. 
2. Uni udon (cold) 4/5: My friend got this cold which doesn't come with a soup base, but nonetheless the uni is so fresh and I love the options for having cold vs hot soup noodles. I'd love to return to try the hot version. 
3. Curry udon deluxe 5/5: really hits the spot, and the thick udon noodles are consistently chewy. The bowl for this was MASSIVE and we got to pack the leftovers. 
4. Soy garlic fried chicken 4/5: The chicken was juicy and flavorful, though not a large amount for the price.

This place was one of the fanciest places I've been to for a noodle spot. As soon as you walk in, you are greeted by extremely nice waiters/waitresses that politely ask how many you are dining with and then proceed to take you to your seat. As you are walking to your seat, you should smell the fragrance of other noodles that should excite you for your food. The environment is very classic, with nice wooden designs and decals all over the place. The place is dimly lit and provides a very "modern" type of feeling. For first-timers, the waiters/waitresses briefly explain the menu to you in an organized and very clear fashion. You have drink choices of iced water, tea, and I think regular water for free. As for the main course, you can order large noodles and regularly sized noodles for the same price. To be honest, who wouldn't get the large bowl of noodles. Now there are speculations that only the bowl is larger, but why not? For the deluxe TsuruTsurusomething noodles (the $24 deluxe noodles), it was outstanding. The broth was very tasty and rich and alongside it were eggs, some chicken meat, two pieces of shrimp tempura, eggplant tempura, and so much more. Now I wish they had more shrimp tempura as that was extremely tasty, but if you want more tempura, you will get more with the shrimp tempura udon noodles for $17. In addition, the waiters/waitresses have very high-quality etiquette, they ask how's our meal often, but not too often to the point that you get annoyed by them, they refill your water when it's low and most importantly, they bring out your food in a proper manner. As for food wait time, I would say that it's very good for a large bowl of noodles, around the 5-10 minute mark (maybe even less). Some other notes are that the soup spoon they provide is very large (good for the bowl size), it's a bit pricey, and you should leave a tip for a place this "fancy". All in all, this was an amazing experience to have, the food was delicious, the staff etiquette was on point, and I would definitely recommend going here.

TLDR (too long didn't read): the food is outstanding, price above average,  very good and caring servers, good environment, and I would recommend the deluxe noodles/shrimp tempura noodles for first-timers.

Tucked away behind Blue Water Grill just off of 16th Street in Union Square, I stopped in to Tsurutontan with a friend who had highly recommended the place.  She was told to wait until I arrived before we were seated, which is fair enough.  However, once I did arrive and were told that it'd be "5 minutes" before we were sat, a number of other patrons who arrived after us were seated before us, instantly leaving me with negative feelings towards the place before I even took a bite of food.  After waiting approximately 20 minutes beyond the 5 of which we were advised, I mentioned something to the host, who apparently noted for the first time that the entire party was here, despite being told that 20 minutes ago.  

The interior of the restaurant is dark, modern, and somewhat busy with decoration.  The restaurant is much larger than the storefront portends, with a large basement seating area and another ground floor seating area deeper into the restaurant past the bar (I think).  The seating area was large enough to not feel cramped, which was nice, but the tables for two have you sitting next to your guest on a love seat, not across from them, changing the dynamic and ease of conversation somewhat (this is why coffee shops usually have laptop areas on bars against the window and reserve table tops for those wishing to converse).   

Our waiter was very engaging, and showed me some of the best and/or top selling menu items since it was my first time in the restaurant.  The menu is quite broad and anyone can find something they like to eat, from beef, to seafood, to rice bowls. I learned after I ordered that there was a special winter-fall menu, but I did not get a chance to look at it, nor was it brought to my attention.  

I started the meal with the popular Hamachi Carpaccio, which was fresh and tasty, though the grated daikon and avocado did not add much in the way of flavor or texture.  It was essentially a different presentation of sashimi from my perspective.  

I had the sizzling sukiyaki udon for dinner, and opted for the "large" which apparently comes with more noodles for the same price.  Served in a sizzling stone bowl with a perfect egg yolk on top, the sizzling sukiyaki made for a pretty and exciting presentation.  It was a simple beef, green onion, and vegetable mixture, with a slightly sweet sauce.  this dish was the highlight of the meal.  

For dessert, I tried the water cake, never having tried a similar dessert before.  Served with four components (the water cake, Kuromitsu syrup, kinako powder, and vanilla ice cream), it was never made clear how each component interacts with one another.  The syrup was similar to a molasses; the powder, though soy-based, had a slightly peanut-esque quality to it, and the ice cream was ice cream.  The water cake lived up to its name and simply tasted like gelatinous water.  The dessert left me confused, and I don't think I'd order it again, as it seems to exist more for the sake of pictures rather than sustenance or pleasure.

Given the price, the rather significant lapses in service, and the less than impressive food in a particularly busy area of the city, I think I'll opt for a number of other establishments before trying Tsurutontan again.

Union square is a rather funny area - it's famous for killing restaurants that can't hack the rather fickle habits of the millenials frequenting the area.  Between the anarchists selling "Resist" lapels on Union Square South, the Greenmarket on the north and the chain shops dotting the square, we've seen some serious transitions there.  Republic Noodle Bar was replaced by BarnJoo The Grain.  Union Square Cafe?  Gone.  Heartland brewery?  Done.  So during this entire cycle of birth, death and resurrection, there are businesses that tries to appeal to the millenials but have the soul of wallpaper paste (*ugh* another Dig Inn or Juice Generation?), and then, there are the weird outliers trying to break out, like Tsurutontan.  

First of all, if you are a frequenter of St. Mark's place (the street on the East village) or East 46th near Grand Central Terminal, you would've no doubt been familiar with Udon West.  It's a mini-chain that advertise itself as an Izakaya (which means that it serves hard liquor), but it's really an Udon specialist.  The noodles are typically around $12/order and it's fairly self-service.  Grab a pair of disposable chopsticks, mutter "itadakemase" and go to town.  The flavor there is fairly solid and it's a good place to feed if you need something sit-down that is fairly cheap.  

Now, take that same ethos and translate it to a high rent location on East 16th street next to the Blue water grill.  Now picture a more minimalist decor (a bit more elegant), a bigger bowl and arguably fresher ingredients - and you have Tsurutontan.  The pricing is of course more than the norm - it's Union Square, and this is a flagship location - about $20/bowl.  The clientele tends to be millenial girls in their mid-20s.  The buzz surrounding this place faded quite a bit in the past 6 months - what used to be lines snaking out the door is now decent available seating during a Friday lunch.  

Now, how's the food?  *Eeeh*.  It's not bad by any stretch of the word - the udon are well textured (that is, not gummy), the broth is savory without being too fishy or weird, and the toppings are ample and fresh, but it just doesn't grab my attention and made me want to return too often.  If I have to compare it to other Japanese joints that I frequent, it's not quite Sakegura (one of my favorite semi-affordable joints near the United Nations General Assemby) and it's not like,Yakitori Taisho (cheap and decent).  It doesn't have the vibe of Izakaya Raku (near GCT and have that Tokyo salaryman ethos).  It's more like Soba-ya, a buckwheat noodle specialist in the East village claiming fresh custom ingredients and matching pricetags.  It's not a bad addition to the neighborhood, but not something I would frequent - too damaging to my wallet.  It's good for once-in-awhile.

We initially decided to come to Tsurutontan to satisfy our uni udon cravings but left being blown away by arguably their better dish: the Tsurutontan Deluxe Udon Bowl.

Let's just start by saying that these bowls are simply massive. One bowl will be sufficient for two people and then some so do keep that in mind. That being said, we ordered a bowl of the Uni Udon and the Deluxe (our eyes are clearly bigger than our stomachs). The uni udon was a bit lackluster, while they were generous with the uni and ikura, the thick broth was rather un-flavorful and lacking in umami. The real star was the Deluxe: filled to the brim with tempura, juicy slices of beef, and perfectly al dente noodles. The broth was complex, and had much more depth of flavor than its uni counterpart.

We finished off with the Instagram famous "Water Drop Cake," which in it of itself is flavorless but provided a good textural vessel for the syrup and dried peanut powder that was provided as a topping - it was also served with refreshing mango ice cream. If you are looking for your udon fix, come here, but perhaps try something else besides the Uni Udon.

Easily made reservations (easy to change/cancel reservations too) through Resy off their website. Although we arrived a little before our reservation time, we were quickly seated upon arrival. 

Our waiter, David, took the time to explain the menu, dishes that paired well with thin or thick iron noodles, and even made sure to point out that extra noodles came with no extra cost (perfect for hungry folks).  

I ordered the Ontama Toriten Curry over thick noodles. The dish was not only HUGE, but it was also super flavorful and the curry was quite rich. Next time, I'd come back to try their cold udon!

The service here is wonderful! When my boyfriend dropped his chopstick, a staff member quickly brought over a new pair (without us even having to ask). The same staff member even walked me over to the downstairs bathroom when the first floor one was occupied.

A friend dragged me out of the office to introduce me to this place and it was some pretty good grub!  The best part is that their price for large portion is the same as the smaller portion... yup, you heard me right!  A must try place!

Didn't know you could make a reservation so we ended up sitting on these awkward benches that face another couple and you sit side by side with your partner.  I didn't mind but I'm sure others might.  

The service was above and beyond.  Incredibly nice and professional servers, very attentive, and clearly very proud of their establishment.  

The food is quite fantastic.  I haven't been to too many udon places in the city, but Tsurutontan hit the ball out of the park in my opinion.  Obviously you're not going to be getting udon as good as in Japan, but my god this was a delicious, plentiful, heart-warming second place next to the best of Japan.  The portions are massive, and while the price is the same for both the standard and large, the only difference is that the large has extra noodles.  We got the Tsuruton Curry Deluxe, the Tsurutontan Deluxe, and the corn fritters as an appetizer.  The sauce that came with the corn fritters made the dish, and complemented the crispy light corn patties very well.  The curry udon was quite heavy, in a savory, delicious way.  Absolutely fantastic curry, a bit sweet, somewhat thick, and it's topped with very flavorful donkatsu slices.  I was a huge fan of this udon despite being apprehensive about it initially.  The Tsurutontan Deluxe, or the most classic of the udons, was heavenly.  I loved that there was chicken, beef, and the traditional dashima-based broth in there.  It all formed together to make an extremely rich, complex broth that rushes through your body everytime you take a sip.  It's like experiencing anime food in real life basically.
