We got the thicker traditional udon noodles for the traditional udon and thin noodles for the curry udon to pick up the sauce, and it worked out quite well.  When I come back I will definitely be trying out some of the other udons, as they have many different kinds.  Perhaps try a donburi as well.

On the whole I was more than pleased with my experience here, and won't hesitate to come back again.  Most of my friends are more ramen fiends than they are udon, and that's probably because ramen has a stronger flavor.  I think some of them could enjoy this place as well, as the meat is plentiful and the broths are absolute umami bombs.  

9/10 
-1 for a bit pricey for what is essentially regular japanese udon.

It is my fault for continuing to come back here but the reservation system is terrible. Every time we make one, we still end up waiting at least 15 minutes but today we ended up waiting one hour with a reservation. In addition, the hostess was not doing a good job managing expectations of wait times. I think you need to be realistic with when a table will actually open up, instead of saying "15 minutes" to everyone who comes up to you, so people can decide to make other plans. On a good note, the food is always consistent.

The perfect bowl of warm soupy udon on a rainy NYC day!

Reservations can be easily made through their website and are recommended since by the time our party left at 7:30, there was a crowd by the door.

We got seated shortly after 6:30. Our waitress (don't remember her name) was very attentive and came by multiple times to make sure that we were able to make an educated decision given the EXTENSIVE menu. We ordered the:

Wagyu Truffle Udon - Beef was sooooo tender and the broth was nicely balanced with the truffle oil, not overpowering at all. The noodles were a good chew.

Creme Mentaiko Udon - Lots of toppings in this one and the soup was not too heavy. I liked it but I wouldn't be able to finish a whole bowl since it's creme-based.

They give you a FREE upgrade but tbh, I didn't think the portions were *ginormous* as some yelpers have said. It was also a little difficult to eat while hunched over the bowl lol.. For the price, I thought it was a tad bit expensive but I'd come again just to try the different flavors and broths.

It's also a really cozy spot with nice decor. Would recommend for a date spot to show off your udon slurping skills!!

Awesome Japanese noodle spot when you're tired of eating the same bowls of ramen from ipuddo look-alikes in the city. Plethora of options ranging from clear broth, to curry, to creamy options with uni or crab or truffle. On top of that, they give you the option to get the large sized bowl at no additional cost. Noodles have good firm mouthfeel and they definitely don't skimp on meat and other toppings. Would recommend making a reservation as they get fairly busy at times.

Tsurutontan was our first stop on our trip to New York last week. We landed at Laguardia at 7pm, dropped off our luggage and went straight to dinner here. We grabbed a drink at the bar and then got seated within 5-10 mins of our arrival. We ordered all the dishes to share between the three of us: 

[1] Soy Garlic Fried Tatsuta Chicken served with a shibazuke tartar sauce, crispy and savory with creamy sauce. 
[2] US Wagyu Shabu Udon - US kobe ribeye was so tender and delicious, this was the table favorite. 
[3] Uni Creme Udon - uni tobiko caviar, shiso leaf in an uni cream broth. Delicious, but imo not as good as Marugame Monzo in LA (for those of you that can relate). 

Just a heads up, you can upgrade your udon size to a large and it's free! The large size is great for sharing if you want to order different broths to share.

Cavernous space impresses. Food not as much.
Appetizers - Simmered eggplant wrapped in seaweed was okay and the Soy garlic fried chicken was average (more quantity than quality). Best was the Goma Kampachi.
Udon - Tsurutontan Deluxe was much better. Delicious dashi broth and thick chewy noodles were very satisfying. The toppings were plentiful with the silky egg and beef the best of the lot. The tempura had to be eaten quickly to avoid turning into a soggy mess.

I'd probably avoid any dish with tempura on my next visit, but the broth and noodles were the highlight. At $24, not a bargain.
Overall, the first impression is this a great choice for a date or nice evening out, but if you're all about the udon, Raku does it better.
Excellent service and big portion, great service, you can choose how much noodle you want for the same price, clean restrooms

Really nice atmosphere, huge portions with great presentation, price is pretty reasonable for the amount of food you get. Best part certainly is the udon, which has a lovely texture and can be upgraded in size for free! I've been here several times, enjoying the kasu udon, sukiyaki udon, and uni udon. All three are very good, with sukiyaki having a very savory sweet and salty broth (a little overwhelming). Uni is refreshing and of good quality. Staff is very nice and can introduce you to the way they serve (portions, udon size etc).

Ridiculous waiting time especially when you order appetizer. They don't put your entree on line until you finish your appetizer. And then you end up waiting for a whole lot more because it always get "backed up" with other orders. 

The manager keeps emphasizing on entrees should be brought right after the appetizer. However, it's more like 20 more minutes after we finish the appetizer. FYI, we've waited for the appetizer for a long time already. 

Considering the slow preparation, I recommend either notify the customers about it or hire more chefs please. The waiter who served us, on the other hand, was pretty efficient at bringing us water and checks. So appreciate that.

I really wanted to like this place. Came here Friday night around 6pm so the place was busy. A table for 2 eventually turned into almost an hour wait. Finally we got a seat at the bar and got a drink during their happy hour. Got a $10 mango margarita that had no taste whatsoever, so bland, wasn't even slightly sweet, the only flavor was the chili salt they used. 

We get to our "table" which turned out to be at the end of the bar, which meant we were sitting really high on some stools next to some random tourists. We order appetizers and drinks and find out the price is more than at the actual bar 4 feet over. What happened to happy hour? Apparently, it's happy area. The same exact items are less if you ordered at the bar, had we known, we would've done that and saved ourselves $20! I don't see how this makes sense, they should've clarified. 

We order the classic udon, the Tsurutontan bowl. I get a large and my friend gets the normal. Yes, I get it, the BOWLS are huge, but the serving is like a large pho bowl. Bowls come out and both our noodles are the same amount it seemed.. Ok. Not only that, they are giant bowls but they covered it with a lid. That means the tempura items in the bowl were all mush. What's the point of tempura if you're going to do that. It's supposed to be sitting at the surface. They tempura was soaked into the broth when it came out thus nothing was crispy. The soup has bits of tempura floating all over. That was $24 for a bowl. Someone wrote the tempura was "next level" and another said it was comparable to Japan's udon restaurants Lol.. Portion is large and noodles were good consistency but taste is nothing extraordinary especially if you've had noodles in Japan. Around $100 for 2 people

I had the deluxe udon soup. Was good but not great. A bit too eggy for my taste and way too much going on. It was basically solidified scrambled eggs in every bite and not much soup. And the chicken pieces were way too big for me to eat whole, so struggled to break them up with chopsticks. I think I just didn't order the right item. Would probably go back and try one of their other items next time.

For a 5 day visit in NYC, I came here a second time in one week because I loved it.
Last time I had the uni creme udon, this time i tried the uni udon. It is served cold and i figured it would be perfect for the summer heat. 
It was enjoyable but next time, i'd go back to the uni creme udon!

This place is an absolute NYC must! There are two locations, one in midtown and one in union square and both are equally good. I prefer ramen over udon, but I will haha to say that this is probably some of the best udon I've had in America. I really like how there's so much variety (spicy, dipping udon, tempura, Korean style, curry and dry udon). The ingredients are all fresh and portions are very generous. Great for any occasion, casual or a date spot even.

The wait time is too long. I came on a week day night at 6:34, ordered at 6:45 and my noodle didn't come until 7:30. We were starving over there.... Don't come if you are hungry and expecting something fast, it's wasting ur time.

Lots of expectations and hope for this place but was disappointed.
I got the Katsu Curry Udon- the udon noodles were springy, but I was disappointed in the katsu- it smelled like meat, a lot- those of you know what I mean will probably understand. Not sure if it was an off day, but I won't be ordering it again if I return.

The tuna appetizer was nice, and everything else, including the service was fine, but that Katsu left a bad taste in my mouth.
Delicious curry udon - enormous serving size, tasty broth, tempura and katsu still crispy (not soggy from the broth)

Service was pretty bad from getting a drink at the bar to asking the chef to accommodate a vegetarian (simple request - he refused). I brought a friend here for her birthday and was pretty disappointed. I've been here before with no problems and the food was great. We ended up leaving this time.
Deeply fails to capture delicacy of authentic Japanese cooking. Broth was basically soy sauce + water, salmon and uni were not fresh, bordering on foul.
Large bowel of udon, fresh sushi and great happy hour bites and alcohol selection. Long line on the weekend.

the sashimi are very fresh and tasty, but I am not a fan of their udon. the udon itself is pretty good, but I really don't like their broth, it's too sweet and heavy. (I tried 4 different broth since we ordered 4 different kinds of udon, but I don't like any of them.) there are better udon places in town. Will come back for their sashimi, but not for udon.

Came here at 7:30pm on Tuesday, my first official meal as a New York resident. Was quoted a 20 minute wait, but they took our number which allowed us to take a leisurely stroll around Union Square. 

Before sitting down, I could tell that the ambiance was great- tall ceilings and fully stocked bar with lively conversation everywhere. My friend and I ordered the beef bao appetizers, duck udon (for me), beef udon (for him), and two draft Asahi's. 

They give you a choice of thick udon noodles or thin noodles (which I imagine are usually for ramen?), but we both went with udon noodles. The beef baos were very tasty (shredded beef), the udon was served in a really large bowl and was quite a generous portion size. Wish the udon was more flavorful, but I've never been a huge fan of udon and the fact that I wasn't disappointed was more than enough for me. Plus, my friend paid as a "welcome to New York" meal. Can't complain when the food is free! Draft Asahi to go with the baos and udon was the perfect choice.

Given this is my first review as someone who just moved here, I think the main factor would be whether I would eat here again - and unfortunately I probably would not. Not a knock on the restaurant, I'm just not a fan of udon and there's too much other good Japanese food here!

Eh. I really thought it'd be better.

I really wanted to like this place from the moment we made reservations to when we came in and saw the modern and artfully designed aesthetics of the place. I ordered the Tsurutontan Deluxe ($24) while the friends ordered the Shrimp Tempura Udon ($17) and Uni Creme Udon ($24) with Poached Egg Tempuras as add-ons. 

We all got super excited when the servers came out with these HUGE bowls and lifted the lids with steaming udon underneath. But I was majorly underwhelmed after a few bites. Tempura in broth is a risky idea cause it's pretty much soggy by the time it arrives. The tempura poached egg in theory sounded like a good idea, but the insides were hard. My biggest complaint was the lack of flavor in the dashi broth-whatever I did end up tasting came out to be one dimensional. It reminded me exactly of the soups my parents made when I was sick (crack an egg, add some meat, seaweed, and noodles), cept I paid $24 for it. 

I tried my friend's Uni Creme and it was alright...tasted exactly like it sounded. My friend said the taste gets overwhelming as he consumed it and he got sick of it halfway through. 

Upside is the portions are BIG...none of us could finish ours although the Lady M desserts looked tempting. Also I can see the place being a good date spot with its tasteful decor and dimmed atmosphere.

This location is super fancy compared to the ones in Tokyo which was a nice surprise, very upscale feel to it for an udon place + full bar. They still have the signature huge bowls and the service was friendly and informative. I had the tsurutontan deluxe and my friend had the mentaiko caviar cream. It tasted good but the flavour was just lacking that extra 'umf'. Price was a bit steeper as well, or if you got something that was reasonably priced, it didn't have any toppings in it. Maybe I had too high of an expectation.

A must-visit-at-least-once kind of place! Surprisingly spacious, great interior, enormous plates/bowls/ladles (which are fun in itself), great food... It was quite an adventure from the moment we walked in. They have an interesting range of menu options for udon, ramen, curry alike... Their biggest hits amongst our group was their Truffle Wagyu Shabu Udon ($19) and their Sukiyaki Beef Buns ($10), which were absolutely delectable. Their beef was on-point and of good quality.

The only downside is that, as with many Japanese udon/ramen, they can get a bit greasy-tasting, especially towards the end of the meal.

Otherwise, this place was a thrill!

We had a reservation at 8 and were not seated until 9. I have experience this long wait between reservation time and being seated at this location once before, which I chalked up to bad luck that one time. It's clear there are systemic issues in place with their reservation system. The hostess asked the manager to talk to us about it but he just brushed us off saying he's "trying the best he can."

At 8:55, decided to order drinks because it was unclear if we would ever be seated. Of course then we were finally seated. The hostess refused to move our check at the bar to our table, even after making us wait so long. The bartender poured a white wine for someone who ordered a Rioja.

Our noodles didn't come out until 9:50, because the kitchen "ran out of noodles." When they did come out, one of the dishes had thin noodles when thick ones had been requested. The waited acted like "uhh, I guess we could fix this?" Rather then apologetically taking care of the problem. 

Finally, we ordered more drinks and were told happy hour pricing doesn't apply to the restaurant area. We ordered beers which turned out to be $8 each. Just after the beer arrived, the waiter informs us that there is in fact a happy hour in the restaurant, and the beer we ordered is now $4. We ask the waiter to change the order for beers on our check to the happy hour pricing, but he says "that will be complicated" and refuses. 

Overall, this is the most atrocious service I have ever received in NYC. The errors of hospitality occurred every step of the way and from every person we interacted with (hostess, bar, waiter, kitchen).

For all of these errors, we were offered nothing. What terrible hospitality.
I came here for the uni udon. The cold uni udon is just soso, but the cream uni udon is good. The uni cone is good but very little uni. The milky tofu is also just soso.

FILTHY!  Dirty outside...you can imagine what the kitchen is like!
This space was the former Union Square Cafe.  When they occupied the space, they scrubbed their sidewalk daily.  Since Tsurutontan Udon Noodle Brasserie moved in, they haven't washed the sidewalk once.  They drag their oozing bags of trash across their entrance. There are mountains of cigarette butts from the patrons left all over the sidewalk in front of the restaurant.  With this level of filth left to accumulate in front of their business, you can only imagine what their kitchen is like!  Stay away from this dirty place!  They are lousy for the neighborhood and lousy for their neighbors.  You can see how dirty it is in the photos posted on Yelp!  CLEAN IT UP Tsurutontan Udon Noodle Brasserie!!!

Best udon  place I know for now ... had dinner here a couple of time and today had the son here and he actually liked the food here and the desert was good too. Dinner here is great, love the udon noodles and the flavor and appetizers are great too. Family dinner here is great.

Had uni cream udon and spicy tuna cones (both highly recommended by my waitress) while I was visiting NYC for a business trip. Very disappointed and too expensive!!! I don't really understand why this place has such high reviews. If you're from LA, I recommend to try something else at this restaurant since we have a lot better uni cream udon and spicy tuna dishes available for less money where we live.

Come here for three things:
- the wagyu and uni appetizer sushi: two big splatters on a marble slab of the fattiest wagyu you've ever had, sandwiches between creamy uni and a bed of rice. UNSTOPPABLE.
- the uni udon soup: the broth is creamy but not too heavy and inflected with all these bits of shiso and some uni. Of course, I'd like more uni in it, but such is life. 
- the sukiyaki beef udon: the broth is the richest, best broth I may have ever had. 

Get here on the earlier side of dinner or lunch unless you're okay with a 30 minute wait. We strolled Barnes & Noble and that made the wait fly by.

5 Stars!!!!!!!
Huge, gut warming udon soup bowls with both traditional and crazy flavor profiles. The place is big, so you can always get a seat. The uni isn't good, but everything else is aces. Love this spot.

I stopped by with my cousin on a Saturday afternoon. We only had to wait about 10-15 minutes, which was fine since there was the Farmers' Market right down the street in Union Square. Inside, there is actually a lot more space than you would have expected and people can sit side-by-side on a little bench. Definitely had the Japanese interior down in here.

We ordered the Soy Garlic Fried Tatsuta Chicken to share - this was actually very good. Very well seasoned and had the perfect spice/sweet/tangy-ness to it. 

My cousin ordered the Shrimp Tempura Blue Crab Roll and I got the Tan Tan Udon. Hers was very interesting as it had some pink wrap around the roll, which we still could not figure out what this was. It was pretty good (in my opinion, hard to mess up a shrimp tempura roll) - although not sure it's worth the price. Surprisingly, my Tan Tan Udon came in a huge bowl (all the noodles do) and I actually really liked the visual of the dish. At first, I was not a big fan of the soup, but it ended up growing on me. It has a bit of a sesame flavor, not too spicy, but was rich. Not sure if I would order this again if I came back - but this is also due to wanting to try some of the other dishes. I would probably come back to see how the other dishes fare. I must say, the noodles were delicious though and I could tell they are handmade.

Second best udon spot in NYC. 

The bowls were massive - it was the bigger than the size of my face!
Portions were generous. You can choose either regular or extra noodles for no extra charge. 
Recommendations that I would get here:
+ US Wagyu Shabu Udon - can't go wrong with wagyu
+ Curry Deluxe Udon - curry base was on point and so was the beef
+ Sukiyaki Beef Udon - if you'd perfer a sweeter broth
+ Kimchi Udon - was surprisingly pretty good
Had the Shrimp Tempura and the Seared Salmon roll plus, Happy hour drinks! Great waiter and service. Will do again!

Hands down the best udon I have yet to have in nyc. The udon comes in a giant bowl with a lot of toppings such as cabbage and thinly sliced beef. The best part about this udon was the broth..there's nothing like it. It's slightly sweet and very savory. I also loved how the cabbage soaked all the flavors of the broth. Worth every penny :)

It's a nice restaurant. It's beautifully decorated and service was great. As for food, we had the deluxe udon and sukiyaki udon, and vegetable tempura and fried chicken as appetizer. Vegetable tempura was very good, but the fried chicken was just average, as it was not crispy enough. The deluxe udon was tasty. The sukiyaki udon was also good except that it was a bit too salty. I also had the lychee dessert and it was very delicious.

Been looking for a good udon spot and decided to try this spot while I was in New York.  And it did not disappoint.   They have a huge selection of different types of udon and the bowls are huge so you'll definitely leave full and content.  Had the sukiyaki beef buns and tsurutontan deluxe udon.  I would come back again and try another udon option next time in New York.

Good food, horrific reservation experience.  CANNOT be trusted for celebrations or business dinners.  I called midweek and made a reservation for 6 people on Saturday night at 8pm.  On Friday, I called to confirm the reservation and asked whether a 7th person could be added.  I received confirmation 7 people would be fine and that we were scheduled for dinner on Saturday at 8pm.  On Saturday at 4:28pm (3 and a half hours before my reservation), the restaurant called and told me, "Due to technical issues, we overbooked and need to cancel your reservation for 6 people at 8pm."  I explained: (1) this was a birthday dinner that will be very difficult to reschedule on a Saturday night with such short notice; (2) I confirmed the reservation one day prior; and (3) the reservation is actually for 7 people (not 6).  I was met with the same response, "Sorry sir, due to technical issues, we overbooked and cannot honor your reservation."  After I complained how unfairly I was being treated, the representative offered to move my reservation to the midtown location.  I offered to instead give them 30 minutes to figure out the logistics to honor our reservation at 8pm at the original location.  I was put on hold, and another representative answered.  He again told me "Due to technical issues, we overbooked and need to cancel your reservation for 6 people at 8pm."  I had to plead my case all over again (evidently the first representative was not kind enough to even update him on the situation before handing him the phone), and I had to again note it was for 7 people instead of 6 people.  When I called midweek, I would not have been annoyed if they told me they could not fit my reservation.  However, when a restaurant accepts a reservation and then tells you a few hours beforehand that they cannot honor it, that is very, very bad.  Weirdly, this seemed common to the representatives. 
 Ultimately, the second representative said he could honor a 7-person reservation if we moved our reservation to 8:30pm.  I accepted.

Due to the shifting time of the reservation, one member of our party had to rearrange his schedule and as a result arrived 15 minutes late.  The hostess refused to seat us until our full party arrived, despite us offering to order all food prior to his arrival.  This is an understandable restaurant policy, but waiving this policy was the one opportunity the restaurant had to right its earlier wrongs and avoid a bad Yelp review.  They weren't forgiving, so I most certainly am not.

Can you imagine if you were someone's assistant booking this reservation for your boss and his business associates?  Then receiving a call a few hours before the reservation to hear the reservation has been cancelled by the restaurant?  Don't trust this place.  They will just let you down.

I love this place so much.  So much.  I have tried a variety of things on the menu, and they were all delicious.  I have a favorite udon dish that I've ordered at least 10 times and it's always delicious.  I've brought parents, friends, larger groups and smaller groups here, and everyone has always liked it too.  I love that it's near Union Square, so I can pop in after getting off the subway after work.  So glad it came to NYC and changed my life with udon yumminess!

I love this Udon place. I'm not a fan of udon but I love their thin udon.
I ordered Spicy tuna tartare cone ($12), Soy garlic fried Chicken ($12), Beef udon ($16) and Salmon and ikura don ($24). 

Spicy tuna tartare cone 4/5 (good appetizer) 
Soy garlic fried Chicken 3/5 (too salty for me)
Beef udon 5/5 (my favorite, make sure order with thin noodles)
Salmon and ikura don 4/5 (fresh and comes with small udon) 

Overall every thing was good, but there is a long wait so make sure you make a reservation through online!

overall just a good place for Udon. 
Everything is 4 out of five. 


The big bowels may be too big for average eaters. Be aware and do not order something you cannot finish.

Tsurutontan is easily one of the best places in New York City to get Udon. This is why: so I came here with a friend and ordered the duck udon with thin noodles and a creamy uni udon with thick noodles. Both were delicious in different ways. The thin noodles were soft while the thick ones had more bite to them and were more chewy. The creamy broth could have had more uni but made up for it in the great flavor of it's broth. The duck came rare and cooked in the broth. We also ordered some appetizers which although pricy they were worth it. If you are celebrating something or have extra money to spend I suggest ordering an appetizer!

Great udon! I took 1 star off for the rudeness of the hostess. I walked in without reservation and put my name down for party of two. 5 mins later my other party arrived. The hostess obviously saw that we are all parties here but she didn't say anything to us. We waited another 7-10 minutes and then I approached her about how long the wait since we are on our 1 hour lunch break. With an attitude, she said i was supposed to let her know that we are all here and that it wasn't her job to keep track of who's here and who's not. Partially, I understand her point, but it was the way she spoke to us that was unacceptable. On our way to the table, immediately I noticed the place is half empty....smh! I know the food is good here but it could've been better if the hostess can be trained to be more courteous and professional. It does makes the dinning experience more pleasant...

I like the Udon their. So good.
But it's probably because the Halloween Parade, there's a lot of people even after 10:00 pm, so we waited for almost 40min to get our udon.

My favorite place to get udon! I usually come here on the weekdays for lunch. Most of the time, there's no wait. For lunch, you can order a large portion. The udon here is satisfyingly filling and there's so much of it in one bowl! Not that I'm complaining. The servers refill the water whenever it's a little low, and refill it frequently. The atmosphere is nice and relaxing.

Yum yum yum. Thoroughly enjoyed this gigantic bowl of udon noodles. Soup so savory! I got the thin noodles because my mouth can't handle the thickness but I loved loved loved my dish. The large and the small are the same price so basically go BIG or go home. I was stuffed trying to finish my big ass bowl of udon but of course got desert. The matcha green tea crepe was everything and one day I will birth soft green tea crepe babies. Come here, indulge and enjoy!

Great place for udon noodles! The place is very big and very nice, and the portions are huge! I only ate half of my plate. Also, the normal and big sizes are the same price, so you can ask for the big one and take the lunch for next day!

The bartender was a dick, he wasn't smiling and was serving people drinks with his sour face. Neither he was greeting people with grace. However, this didn't stop me from eating in here. 

You have two choice of noodles: thin or thick
You have two choices of bowl sizes: normal or large. Both sizes will be the same price except that medium you can get broth refill. Large size is a big bowl but it is filled up to 25% of the bowl, so do not get overwhelmed by the size of the bowl. 

I ordered the Tsurutontan Special. The food is very good. The broth is very tasty and yummy. The meat is fresh. I was able to finish everything in a go. 

For the appetizers we ordered mushrooms and chicken. They were both very good. 

I highly recommend this place and you will not be disappointed.
Excellent food with HUGE portions of udon noodles. The wagyu udon with truffles was an absolute delight

I love Tsurutontan! I work in management of a major airline and I would always go to the Tsurutontan in Shinjuku when I travel to Tokyo. I was so excited to bring my friends in NY to this Tsurutontan so that they know what I would always talk about! 
I made my reservation online the night before for 12pm although I know on a Tuesday afternoon it's not going to be busy.
We were seated immediately after arrival. The waitress was courteous initially and introduced us the menu just like the way they would do in Japan. However, it went downhill from there on. 
I initially ordered the salmon lover set introduce by the server, but I wanted to order an extra small udon on the side for my 1 year old. She said we don't do that, I said OK fine. She then introduce me to the kaisen don that comes with a small udon on the side, so I took her suggestion and went with the kaisen don. We also ordered steamed dumpling with chili oil for my baby with chili oil on the side. 
We waited 45 minutes for the appetizer to arrive and other people around us that arrived after us were already eating. The same waitress that took our order came to apologize and stated it was due to they put the chili on the dumpling instead of on the side. So then we told her she can serve all the sets including Udon all together, whatever is ready she can bring it out, she acknowledged but didn't bring anything out for another 10mins. This time the people next to us had finished.
When the orders came it was a massive confusion on who ordered what. Two orders came and one of the udon from a set came without the entree for my friend. Another waitress came and said I need to speak to the first waitress in regards to the order confusion. 
She came to my face and said that I ordered both the salmon lover set and kaisen don , but how can I eat 2 entrees the same time? I took her suggestion of the kaisen don so then that's it. She kept interrupting me when I was explaining myself to hear her out. She kept telling me how wrongful I was. I said but "you never confirm our order, that's the proper procedure as a waitress" she didn't acknowledge and walked away. 
Because of this behavior, none of us gave her a tip. We wrote comments on top of receipt and she ripped it in front of us. What kind of customer service is this? Definitely not the Japanese way of hospitality. I'm very disappointed! She is Asian with dark frame glasses in a pulled back pony tail, be aware guys. 
We go out to eat, catch up with friends and have a good time, not to get mad for no reason, totally unnecessary! I hope management of this establishment knows about this waitress.

We loved the food here! Great atmosphere and friendly staff. Our server took her time to explain the menu even though they were super packed. 
Appetizers- Spicy tuna tartare cone, grilled organic maitake mushroom. Both were great! 
Sukiyaki udon has the best udon broth I've had in NYC- loved its sweetness. 
Truffle Cream udon was also delicious but prefer the Sukiyaki.

I got a curry deluxe katsu udon and the portions were very generous. overall decor was also really nice. they also had some really tasty asian themed cocktails. if it's crowded i would recommend not waiting because people loiter here after dinner

I am an avid noodle lover and harsh noodle critic. Normally, I am not a fan of udon, but these guys knock them out of the park. 

My friend and I split two: Tsurutontan Deluxe and Tan Tan Udon (their top seller). Both were every udon lovers dream. We wanted contrasting broth flavors, and these two were perfect for that.

The Tsurutontan Deluxe had a light and delicate broth that was the perfect backdrop for all the meat and veggies that came with it. The shrimp tempura were perfectly crispy and crunchy (although they became soggy after a while so eat them quickly before they settle into the broth!) The meat was thinly sliced - not super flavorful but not bland either. 

The Tan Tan was equally good, if not better. It was the best udon I have ever had in my life (probably because I love spicy food). The broth was creamy and full of flavor without being too salty. The spice level was perfect (definitely on the spicier side). The ground pork was a bit dry, but still tasty. The two shishito peppers were a nice touch to the whole bowl, aesthetically and to the palette.

We ordered both with the thick noodles and large sizes (no regrets!) As good as the broths were, I think the noodles may have been the stars of the show here. They were cooked perfectly and did not get soggy or break apart during the entire meal. 

The drinks were great also. We both got the Matcha on the Moon. The matcha flavor was strong, and you could barely even taste the gin! We appreciated this :) 

I will definitely be coming back here again!

Great for large groups. Reserve your seats online via Resy.

Portions are big. Noodles come in 2 sizes: medium and large. Both are the same price. Noddles come in 2 types: thin or thick.

Curry deluxe udon: comes with pork katsu and shrimp tempura. good flavor, very filling but gets monotonous after a while

Tsurutontan deluxe: has a mix of different fillings. highlights are the crispy nori and shisho. Good.

Wagyu truffle udon: my favorite. Super truffley.I could smell the truffle from 2 seats away.

Soy garlic fried chicken: is ok. A little soggy, but good size.

Oyster mushrooms: my favorite. Full of umami flavors.

22 hours ago

Went here to have lunch yesterday. We had first stopped by Starbucks and picked up an iced coffee. When we approached the hostess to be seated, she advised that we would not be allowed to bring the Starbucks drink to the table. She said, "No outside drinks allowed. Shall I take this drink from you now, or do you want to finish it now?" Given that it was a brand new drink, we elected to leave to another noodle place, Toto Raman, where they did not object to us having the Starbucks cup. New York has so many great restaurants. Why put up with that kind of treatment?

If i have to summarize my udon experience, it will be bad ass. The large udons were served in a giant bowl that could easily bigger than your face. Everyone on our group seemed to enjoy the meals except for one which had the  Korean soondubu jiage (I'll stay away from that).

We started with grilled organic maitake mushroom which was really good. Really liked the truffle flavor on mushroom dish. The soy garlic chicken was juicy and crispy. 

I've tasted tsurutontan and curry deluxe. Both dishes are good. I would go for the udon deluxe as curry can be too much after some time. I've also tasted my friend's wagyu shabu udon broth which was so heavenly. The truffle flavor was so good. That will be my next dish next time.

Overall a very good experience but i must say that they have to do something with the bartender. He was so rude and had a gangster attitude. 

One tip is to order drinks from the bar as they are cheaper then. Once you are seated, you can't order from the bar anymore.
Great udon place with large portions! The ingredients were all fresh! We got the Uni deluxe udon and the Wagu deluxe udon. Love the broth!

Description: Great place for fusion udon. It lives up to the hype. Certain udons are far superior 

Service: It is very busy so it may be hard at times to flag down a waiter. They are super kind otherwise and quick to refill water 

Atmosphere: The inside is spacious with warm brown decor. It's hard to get WiFi if you're sitting further into the restaurant

Items Tasted:
- Tsurutontan Deluxe: This is the best deal here. The broth is amazing and it is packed with toppings 
- Duck Udon: This was good, but I think duck tastes better outside of a soup dish. It could have been better if the duck was fried beforehand so the skin would be crispy. A lot of the duck flavor was lost 
- Tan tan Udon: I was not a fan of this. It has a lot of vinegar in the broth which I was not expecting. Also, there's barely any ground beef
- Uni Creme Udon: If you like uni, get this. It has a lot of umami and the broth is very thick
- Curry Udon: This is amazing if you enjoy curry. The curry is thick, but not so much that you can't sip it. The katsu is fried perfectly
- Seafood Kimchi Jjigae Udon: This isn't a bad dish, but it doesn't taste like kimchi jjigae at all. The broth has some weird sweetener added to it. There are only a few pieces of clam, shrimp, and scallop. The best thing about this dish were the chives. I wouldn't recommend this at all compared to their other udons

This is actually one of my favorite places to go. It's one of those goto places been here over 6 times already with friends and mom as well. 

But came here yesterday and my friend came here two weeks ago it seems the quality just isn't as good anymore. Ranging from the noodles being just okay to the shrimp in my soup being over cooked.

We came here with local friends who live in New York. Oh my god ! all we had was great.
Their ramen was chewy with a nice texture, the broth was savory, smelled so gooooood, I finished it all . The only thing that i didn't  like is the line was way too long but i totally understand because they got great food.
Will be back when i visit new york !

I really like this place. I've been here twice and I haven't found any faults. Except maybe the portion size which is a tad big. But is it a fault? 
My favorites are the spicy tuna cones (no wonder it's a best seller) and the deluxe curry udon. Every time the server asks if I'd like the big size and follows with 'it's the same price as the regular' I'm always tempted... but I know there's no way I can finish it all. Hence doggie bags both times. Today I also got the water cake, which I've had many times before elsewhere but I just really felt like it so why deprive myself of it. The atom sphere is nice and the service is very attentive. My only recommendation is, if you're coming with a friend maybe just order one big udon to share that way you can get a bunch of appetizers. Or go nuts and just order what you want and take it home with you after.

My friend and I stopped by on a Saturday night. The atmosphere was great, our server was genuine and we had a great time.
We were in the mood for noodles because it was freezing out. We shared two noodle dishes.
Sizzling sukiyaki udon - this was really delicious. We got the thick noodles and upgraded to a large (free to upgrade). The broth is ok the sweeter side but you can get spice on the side or added. We added spice on the side and didn't end up using it much. This is more of a stir fry dish than a broth dish. 
Tan tan udon - we really enjoyed the spice that this one had. We also got thick noodles and upgraded to a large. This was spicy and tasted similar to an army stew that one might order at a Korean restaurant. This was more broth based and perfect for a cold night!


We will definitely be back!

Went here to have lunch.  We had first stopped by Starbucks and picked up an iced coffee.  When we approached the hostess to be seated, she advised that we would not be allowed to bring the Starbucks drink to the table.  She said, "No outside drinks allowed. Shall I take this drink from you now, or do you want to finish it now?" Given that it was a brand new drink, we elected to leave to another noodle restaurant, where they did not object to us having the Starbucks cup.  New York has so many great restaurants.  Why put up with that kind of treatment?

Absolutely phenomenal on all ends.

Got there with no reservation and they told us there would be a 15 minute wait. It ended up being just 5 minutes and we were seated immediately. Staff extremely nice and the food was served in a timely manner.

The udon noodles--PHENOMENAL. The broth and meat felt so fresh. The appetizers--the tuna carrot and the beef bun--were so refreshing and a perfect way to start the meal. They give you the option of normal or large, both same price, and thin or thick udon noodle options. For the price that it is for NYC, I would say it is completely reasonable. I didn't feel like I had to rush out and could thoroughly enjoy my dinner. There's a really nice ambience to it as well, making it very calming.

Came here on a whim with a friend since it was cold and udon seemed to be the perfect fix. It was a Saturday and we didn't have reservations so we waited at the bar for about 45 min. I had the Asian pear mojito which was pretty good but the lime masked the taste of the pear a little too much for me. 

We were seated at the lower level where we sat side by side and only had a few wood bars between the people across from us. The seating was a little awkward but we were too busy eating to really notice. I ordered the US Wagyu Shabu Udon in Truffle Dashi and we shared the Soy Garlic Fried Tatsuta Chicken. The chicken was delicious but could've been coated more evenly in the sauce. It was crispy and so juicy and tender inside. The udon also hit the spot on a cold night. The truffle flavor was subtle and not too strong. The broth was a bit heavy. Overall great experience!

DO NOT RECOMMEND !!!
Don't go here not nice at all to my boss and work colleagues from NYU. Had lunch twice in same week first time was good and waiter educated us on type of choices. This was by the bar and food was quick and tasty. So we went back and sat downstairs. I ordered same thing but colleague order appetizer cuz we were hungry. It took 1.5 hours to get food. When I asked they were more angry than me. Informed me food order doesn't go in till I finish my appetizer. Also got the wrong food. Ask to see manger to she if there was anything can be addressed. She was even angrier cuz I ordered appetizer and I was at fault for not saying I was in hurry. We paid over 100 for 3 orders with one appetizer and no drinks!

3 tables after us got food with appetizers. Manager woman downstairs was rude don't even waste your time!

When people talk about udon in Manhattan, this spot always comes up in discussion. And for valid reasons too! First off, the decor of the place is beautifully done. Lots of wood and metal highlights, the bar is minimal, polished and regal. The dining area uses good use of the space with an asthetic divider, and seats a surprising number of people. My friend and I came on a Saturday night, and we our wait was roughly 40 minutes so we took advantage of the bar.

The udon bowls themselves are massive. You can choose to get large or medium portions for the same price, so pretty much everyone opts for the large. Will satisfy pretty much anyone in need of a good meal.

Fried chicken: my personal favorite. The outer layer of the chicken soaks up the sweet and tangy sauce so well, I wish we had gotten a second plate.

Deluxe udon: I was a little worried when my bowl came, it looked like too much. I kept repeating that I wouldn't finish it but the broth was so good I ended up clearing my bowl 

I personally prefer raku's minimal style, but can see myself getting a craving for the deluxe again.

As it gets colder, there's nothing I want more than a giant bowl of Udon soup. Thankfully, Tsurutontan delivers. The few times I've been here, it's been packed for dinner, so definitely make a reservation prior. 

You get to pick here if you want the medium or large size, also if you want the thin or thick noodles. Both sizes are the same price so I always get the large. If you're not a big eater, medium is more than sufficient. The bowls are huge. Typically, I just stick with the shrimp tempura udon and it's delicious. I like simple, clear soups, so this is perfect for me. 

Staff has always been friendly so no complaints there. Will be coming back soon as we're getting to the cold winters again!

Came here to satiate my somewhat insatiable hot noodle fix during cold, windy days in the Northeast. I'd been craving udon noodles and saw this place featured on Mike Chen's YouTube channel Strictly Dumpling. 

We ordered the massive bowl of deluxe udon noodles as well as an appetizer of mushrooms. The mushrooms, now I don't remember what kind they were but it is a best seller and they were super umami and delicious. The portion was so small for a $13 appetizer but how tasty it was somehow made up for it. 

The deluxe udon bowl comes in a massive bowl but it's only really filled up halfway ish so it's actually probably appropriate for one person, or two people with small appetites. The deluxe udon is supposed to be a combination of various fillings like tempura and beef. The broth was great and soul-filling on a cold day. The noodles (we got the thick kind) were chewy and silky soft how udon noodles should be. I will say, I was disappointed that the tempura came already in the broth. I usually like my tempura on the side for udon so I can retain the crispiness (the best part of Japanese-style fried foods) till the last moments but the tempura batter was soggy and soaked in broth, which a lot of people like, but also a lot of people dislike. I think it would help for them to serve the tempura on the side for the deluxe bowl like they do for the tempura bowl so that people have the option to put the tempura in if they want to or leave it out if they don't. 

Otherwise the broth was delicious and the egg drop especially added a good heartiness to the dish as a whole. As a whole, this place is quite upscale and on the pricey side but an overall good experience.

I really wanted to like this place as a noodle lover, but they use low-quality ingredients and msg broth. 

Very dissapointed.

Waited for our food for two hours. Kimchi ramen came with barely any soup and when I asked for more soup, ramen came back way too salty. Uni ramen had a tiny piece of uni with watery soup. We were told the kitchen was backed up, but that doesn't mean we had to have inedible meal for the night.

This could be the worst ever place I've been. It takes literally an hour for the courses to come when it's only udon. People that arrived after us have their food first because "we have appetizers" according to the waitress. We ordered our food at 12:15 where we thought we could at least finish it by 1 o'clock. Guess what? We walked out with starving stomachs because the food takes forever to come. Moreover, the waitress give us a " I don't care" look when we asked when will the food come.

One of my favorite Udon spots in the city. The uni creme udon is one-of-a-kind, to say the least. The noodles are cooked to perfection, and you have a choice between thin or thick noodles (I'd go with the thick noodles, personally). The soup base is creamy yet balanced, with a sweet aftertaste that is leaves you wanting more.

Love everything about this place, from the different kinds of alcoholic drinks to pages of udon bowls. They serve the udon in hot and cold, in thin noodles and the thick noodles. You can also upgrade the bowl from a regular bowl to a large bowl, which is extra udon, at no additional cost. Dessert is served with Lady M green tea crepes cakes, and seasonal cake from Lady M which varies depending on the day or season, and you have to ask the server for the special of the day. When I went last night, it was Pumpkin Cheesecake from Lady M. This place is very busy, so I highly recommend making a reservation.

Really not that amazing. It's praised for its giant bowls of udon but most of it is broth and it's literally a giant bowl. It's great that they have options for a large and small bowl but they're both the same price so I'm not too sure what's up with that. The wagyu dashi is overwhelmingly strong and the sukiyaki is too sweet. The two need to find a better balance.

I would classify this place as bougie udon. Don't get me wrong. The food was delicious but it was a bit overpriced which is why they lose 1 star from me! Always very crowded but you can make reservations online beforehand. I got the regular sized curry udon with the thick udon. The bowls that come out are bigger than your head! The menu is a lot because there are so many appetizers and different combinations possible with udon. Great vibes and ambience!

Uni Creme Udon!
***
Locals 
This is a LOTTTT of udon, and a lot of options. Not authentic Udon, but they have so many different types of Udon and non-Udon options as well.
***
Travelers 
Definitely the place to go because there is nothing like them. Their Udon bowls are huge and are the size of a basketball. You could also ask for another serving of Udon noodles free of charge. They take reservations, and it's in the heart of Union Square, so this is the place to be!
***
My Recommendation : Order the Udon and get another serving of noodles! They are quick with their service, and the interior is beautiful, so you get an amazing experience.

IG: @foodisseur

The food here is very nice, and that's where it stops. If you do not mind being treated poorly as you sit down, and as you order the food, and it comes then by all means go ahead and gamble. As you leave and paid; they'll treat you like royalty and say "thanks for coming". If you come for the happy hour ... nothing too happy about that! The bartenders are dryer than martinis should be, have no sense of humor, and look completely tired of life. They treat you as if you owe them money and haven't paid in more than six months. You work customer service!!!! I should've gave you my words as a tip. PS don't celebrate a birthday here if you are a person that loves the singing and clapping, these folks don't cater to nothing but your leaving, for the next people to sit down.

The bowls are soooo huge. You can definitely get a large size and share! I tried the tsurutontan deluxe and the us wagyu shabu udon in truffle dashi. Both were great, but the latter was better imo! I tried a little bit of the uni and it was too creamy for me.
Wait was an hour despite an abundance of tables. Food was good but they took 15 minutes to bring out item number two so my food got cold. Not worth the $50.

If you want a special ramen/udon, I think this is a good place to check out. We made RSVP a little bit before arriving and waited less than half an hour before being seated. The place was busy during dinner time so don't be surprised if you have to wait. 

I had the wagyu beef udon with truffle taste in the broth. The beef was sooo tender and sliced thinly which how can you go wrong with that? I also love the taste of truffle! The portion was HUGE and I was so full afterwards. The downside of that was my head was barely higher than the top of the bowl (yes, I'm very short). 

My friends and I also had drinks here which were pretty good. Pricewise, it is higher but I felt like that was compensated by how large the portions were. I had a good time here and look forward to coming back!

This place has sooo many udon options, it's amazing! You have the option of choosing the thickness of your udon noodles whether you want them to be thick or thin. Also, you can upgrade your udon to a large portion for FREE! If you upgrade it to a large, you get extra udon noodles but I believe the rest of the toppings are the same amount you would get if it were normal.

I honestly recommend sharing if you don't mind sharing because the bowls are so huge! Even when I ordered the regular size because I didn't want to waste food, the bowl still came out in the same hugee size but I'm assuming they just gave me less noodles.

I tried the US Wagyu and Mushroom Sukiyaki ($24) and I enjoyed it, but the broth was too sweet for me and the others in my party who ordered it. I would only recommend this one if you like sweet broths. I tried a bite of the Tan Tan Udon and the Truffle Creme with Crab and Mushroom and both were good and tasty! I also tried the cold Uni Udon but I wasn't a huge fan of this one even though I love uni. There just wasn't too much flavor in it.

Overall, good udon spot cause their noodles are good. Friendly staff and they accept reservations online. I do recommend making reservations just in case because the times I've been here, there were always a lot of people.

Their udon had great texture and chewiness.  The bowls are huge.  You can definitely share this bowl and just grab some appetizers.  I got the curry bowl and it did not disappoint.  The curry was rich and flavorful.  The beef was only okay, however.  Probably sliced a little too thin and was overcooked.  Had a slight grainy texture, but overall, the dish was still pretty good.  

Come early, or make sure you have a registration.  I hate waiting an hour plus for food, as my general rule of thumb is, nothing is worth more than an hour wait.  We had an estimate of 45 mins...we didn't get seated for 1.5 hours.

Good thing we decided to make a short walk over to grab some buns over at Baohaus.

Been here a few times and it's pretty good. They have a wide variety of options on their menu, ranging from udon noodle to teriyaki to sushi and sashimi dishes. Both times I have come I have gotten the sushi, however, my friends always get the udon. PS: they give every customer the option to upgrade to a large portion when ordering noodles, free of charge. The udon is said to be flavorful, which is not surprising since they have some really interesting flavor combinations for udon (for example, they have one that has truffle / mushroom in it). The sushi is fresh and delicious. My only compliant for sushi would be that the plain 6-piece rolls (about $14 each) cost nearly the same as the special rolls ($16 each). Overall, good spot and would recommend. Ambiance is great.

One thing that's different about this place is it's size - you don't typically see a ramen place seat more than 15 people let alone have a second floor.

This place also has a huge selection of ramen options.  The top seller listed is the uni crème udon, but I have to say I like a lot of their other ones as well.  The thing that stands out about this place is how creamy the broths are, which really help you hit the spot in the winter time on an empty stomach.  The noodles and toppings are decent, but not as good as say Ipuddo or Totto, which is why this place won't overtake those two in my ratings.

2's - Naruto, Momofuku, Kambi

Places to Try: Shinshi, Ramen Ishida, Zen Ramen, Zundo-Ya, Niu Noodle, Nakamura

Tsurutontan is one of my favorite places to eat and a place I commonly bring guests from out of town. The portions are huge, the menu is extensive (with udon), and the space is comfortable. I also love how the servers often remind you that the large size comes at no extra cost!

However, I'm taking stars off because I have had some really terrible experiences with the service here. Once, I came with reservations - and we weren't seated until 45 minutes to an hour after the time we reserved! Another time, we were told there would be a short wait, but again - we waited almost an hour. During that visit, our server was not attentive at all (we had to flag him down several times to take our order, refill our waters, etc.) and he forgot to place my friend's order. So, I had mine first and we had to wait for her soup to get made.

Generally, the food is great here but the service is hit or miss. And, it seems futile to make a reservation to avoid the wait.

I loved this place! It's conveniently located at union square, it's large so it can handle groups, the drinks are creative, and the food is satisfying.

Food: The noodles selection was incredible along with the broth base. They even have uni ramen for the serious fans of uni.

I could have sushi if I was in the mood or a hearty dish of noodles.

Ambiance: creative walls - denim, letters, coconuts. 

I visited two nights in a row since they also offer a decent happy hour at the bar (all days, all times).

Probably my favorite udon place in the city. This place lives up to the hype!

Been here multiple times, and have always made a reservation online which is convenient. Menu is expansive, and you'll definitely find an udon flavor that will satisfy your taste. The udon bowls here are huuugeeee and the prices are super affordable. I'd say one of the best values in the city. Regular and large sizes are the same price - both are ample big, but I go large since I have a huge appetite. There's a bar up front that you can order stuff at while you're waiting for your table too.

Service has always been excellent. Came here for birthday once, and they were so accommodating in regards to storing the cake and bringing it out for us. Had to drop off a cake at 2pm for a late dinner and they told me no problem!

Highly recommend this place!

somehow even with reservations, once your whole party gets there on time they still make you wait for at least 15  mins before you are seated, multiple times.
Beers are really cheap during happy hours.
Udons are great, the creamy ones tend to be really filling. i'm a huge fan of the sizzling hot stone options

Haven't written a Yelp review in years. 

This place pissed me off. 

Biggest complaint is service was absolutely dreadful. From beginning to end. First, at the bar, the bartenders were sooo appallingly unfriendly and offensive and gruff. Our drink was very watery and they blatently ignored our request to fix it. Then, they brought us the wrong appetizer, and after we told them, they still charged us. And totally saw that we were uncomfortable with it and still no offer to fix. 

Next, at the table, the food took FOREVER to arrive. and when it finally came, the tempura was soggy and cold. Further the noodles were also astonishingly cold. Ok maybe a little warm but for an asian they might as well have been cold. 

Ok lets talk about the food. Soggy tempura is gross. Soooo dismayed.

Sushi rolls-- the rice was mushy. what the what?!  huge bad. No need to be more explicit.

Warm soup is practually sacrilegious in the asian book. Should be steaming hot.

Plus, the servers did not know which bowl belonged to who (all the same classic deluxe, but one had double noodle, one had no chicken, one was 'normal'). 

And toppings we're paltry, mostly soup and noodles. Speaking of chicken, chicken 'chunks' had no flavor. and why were they chunks anyway? it felt really uncouth to be dealing with. Kitchen seems knife lazy. Not an elegant bowl of udon, no way, no how.

But no one came to check on us, ever.  They just unceremoniusly dumped the food on the table and scurried off like mice and never reappeared. 

In sum, just a wholly upsetting and honestly outrageous experience. There are way better places to go in NYC that won't raise your blood pressure higher than the temperature of your overpriced, lukewarm soup that you practically have to beg for.

We were craving udon on a cold night. I knew about ramen places but didn't know much about udon. Yelp gave this as a suggested place so we decided to try it out. 

It's a high end udon restaurant. When we got in the host was very nice and we only waited around 10 minutes. 

We ordered an appetizer (fried chicken) and an udon each. The size of the udon was the size of my hands combined. 

The food quality was delicious and very tasty. 

The only thing is, I guess because it's a high end restaurant, it's a bit too pricy to swallow. 

I would recommend for date nights since we saw so many people making out at the tables around us.

My friends and I frequent at TsuruTonTan because of the how unique and tasteful their menu and delivery is; I pretty much always recommend it to friends visiting NY as well.

Unfortunately, it's always a coin toss about what kind of service you will have, especially when it comes to their hostesses and seating arrangements, and more often than not, it's sub par.  Specifically, the restaurant will irrationally be extremely peculiar about seating the party only when everyone has arrived.  I understand the business model but they often abuse it; numerous times we've told about how there will be a wait, even in the middle of the afternoon in a non busy weekday, when there is virtually no one sitting anywhere at the restaurant.  Having reservations doesn't change things much, resulting in irrational wait times and poor floor management.

Today, I came in with two friends and my girlfriend; we were eventually sat down in their bar/serve area in the corner and the - unbeknownst at the time, manager - Elle (?) swung attempting to situate us.  Since my girlfriend was in the bathroom, I told her we need four, no three, waters and she responded with appalling mannerism that we can't be seated without the full party.  She immediately turned around and stormed off.  Needless to say, this was completely unprofessional; we requested from the waitress to see the manager unaware that it was actually her.  For the remaining 30 minutes or so, Elle never showed up.  While I've enjoyed dining at this place, Elle and her unprofessional attitude tipped the scale and it is unlikely that I will return.

Found this Japaness restaurant open in the morning, come in and were asked to wait about 30mins, but turned out only 10mins wait, not bad! We ordered one uni udon and one delux udon.Uni udon is the best,  the delux udon is normal. They will ask you if you want a regular size or large, but it will be the same price. also the green stuff on top is stinky, I have picked them out and left them on the upper side of the bowl. I will definitely come back for the uni udon!

I've been recommended this spot a few times and finally got around to visiting last night. I was so glad I did, because this will definitely be a future staple for me in the Union Square area, especially on a cold winter night like last night. I was overwhelmed by the menu (in the best way) because there were so many things I wanted to try. I got the regular size sukiyaki udon and have a whole portion of it for dinner tonight. The udon noodles are the real star. Elastic, chewy, and flavorful. I can't wait to go back to try some of their other top dishes.

Cannot say enough good things about this place! Their Tan Tan Udon with thick noodles are a little piece of heaven. My mom loooved her Soy Garlic Fried Chicken. Service and staff were excellent and very friendly. Great place to go on a cold day for some hot noodles!

Don't get me wrong with the 4-star review, this place is definitely one of my favorite udon place in the city and one of my must-visit restaurant to my tourist friends (especially people who love Japanese udon). They never failed to disappoint me, from uni cream, clear broth, stone stove to curry, all flavors are awesome and authentic. You get to choose thick/thin noodles and extra noodles if you're craving for large portion of fantastic udon. 

I'd definitely recommend reserving a table online beforehand especially during the weekends cause people in the city recognize deliciousness lol It tends to get really, REALLY packed. 

The only thing I'd complain, but also understandable, is that this restaurant only seat your guests when all parties are present AND can only hold your reservation for 15 minutes. Pretty clear and totally respect the policy here, but all New Yorkers know how terrible (f**ked up) the MTAs can be during weekends, so last time one person of our group got stuck in the train, instead of seating us and allowing us to order on her behalf, they told us that it's the restaurant policy, which with all due respect, we totally understand, BUT she actively and aggressively asked us if we'd like to talk to the manager.

Well, I was really clear about the fact that I LOVE this restaurant. But it was a really awkward dinner experience with my friends visiting from other cities...we were trying to tell the host that we totally understand their policy but we can definitely take small spaces or even the bar area and order beforehand (we already ordered some drinks from the bar as well) but she just keep on repeating "would you like to speak with the manager instead?" while I was actually thinking about closing our tabs at the bar and just visit other restaurants nearby...

My friends have heard so many good things about this place from me and were all pretty excited about visiting here, but we definitely didn't want to step on anyone's toes, but awkwardly we did by telling the host that one of our friends was stuck on the subway and might be late for another 10 min...

At the end they allowed us to sit in a 4-people table and let my friend who was late to squeeze in with us. But funny thing was, when my friend finally arrived, thanks to marvelous A Train, the host gave her a weird look and asked her to walk herself in.

I mean...I'd still recommend this place to Udon lovers but 

DON'T BE LATE, ARRIVE EARLY, MAKE RESERVATIONS ONLINE BEFOREHAND!

You can thank me later for saving weird awkward moments waiting at the bar

Great place to get a grub with friends! 
I loved browsing their extensive menu, the prompt service, and relaxing atmosphere.

BUT... 

Their uni cream udon, which seemed to be the logical thing to order on your first time, was honestly a bit disappointing. 
In that HUGE bowl, they gave tiny portion of uni, so little that I actually asked for more and they did give (I think they felt bad it was so little) but overall it was just slurping down cream soup with super thick udon noodles with not too much other toppings in the way so I got kind of bored quickly. Wagyu & Mushroom Sukiyaki udon on the other hand, was more interesting with generous portions of sliced beef and mushrooms, and lighter broth. That too, was pretty salty pretty quick though. 

I couldn't shake the feeling that their udon bowls were way too big with too much portion. Why not just reduce the quantity down along with price just a little so people can actually enjoy your udon instead of getting sick of it halfway through? 

Appetizer and dessert were decent, but nothing to write home about.
I will give them another try - perhaps a cold udon with mentaiko, but yeah I won't be paying $24 for Uni cream udon again.

Came here with my friend and her cousin on a Saturday night.
I made reservations ahead using Rezy.  ( you will get endless emails and texts, opt out of everything)
I arrived 15 minutes early, however we were missing 1 person due to train delays. The hostess said they could only seat us if the whole party was present. 
When our company arrived 20 minutes past the rservation time, our table was given away based on their "15 minute hold" policy. -Annoyed- 
Luckily, the dinner rush was ending and plenty of tables were opening up so we were only waiting for an extra 10 minutes.
Our waitress was nice and knowledgable. 
The for a regular udon bowl and an extra large is the same.. 
Me and my friend shared an XL  wagyu beef udon bowl and were perfectly satisfied with the portion. Udon noodles were definitely fresh and perfectly made. 
I deducted a star because for the price of $24, I expected the beef to be plentiful and "melt in your mouth" tender. neither expectations were met.

Cousin had the same order and was completely happy with the entree.
We all had 2 drinks each and shared 1 dessert. 
Our tab including tip ended up 140.

There is only one single bathroom for men and 2 stalls for women.
hope you don't have to use it during a high volume time because its slightly inconvinient. 

Would definitely come again because the XL bowl is amazing but would like to try other spots.

As the weather continues to get colder, Tsurutontan will be your go to place. Oversized bowls of Udon come in two sizes (small and large) for the same price. I'd suggest ordering the large even if just to see how big the bowl really is. I've been here a few times, and I would suggest getting the Dashi broth. The curry broth was thick and heavy - I was full much too fast. Will return for sure.

Pretty good noodles in a lovely space. From the tables to the interior decoration, to the bathroom, to the bowls and plates, everything was very tastefully chosen and decorated. As with everything else in New York, the price-to-quality ratio is overinflated (the food was pretty good! but I wouldn't go as far as saying phenomenal either), but the price-to-quantity ratio is really good ($20ish for a bowl that's probably bigger than some sinks in NY apartments).

My main qualm was the attitude of one of the waitresses at the door. We had a reservation and our entire party arrived only 3 min after the exact time, yet we had to wait for fifteen minutes in order to get seated. Now, I understand things can happen and getting a restaurant up and running smoothly can be crazy, so I don't mind waiting too much, but the least she could have done is apologize and explain to us why rather than dish off a curt reply and dash off super rudely. When I asked what was up, her attitude felt super dismissive--definitely far from the best customer service I've gotten in this town. While I understand staff could be stressed and rushing, especially with the hype and the traffic of the restaurant, it didn't leave a super good impression.

Amazing experience. Ordered wagyu udon, uni corn and fried chicken.

I have been sick of uni since I have had too much of them. But the way they prepared it is so different that I still enjoyed it. It's wrapped in crispy corn which makes the strong rich taste of uni more acceptable. 

The udon is REALLY good, definitely the best I've had. I didn't quite like udon before because the noodle is too thick, making it hard for the soup to stay inside. But the thin udon here perfectly combines the flavor and the taste of the noodle. The bowl is huge...

Fried chicken is the second best Japanese style fried chicken I've had. (First is udon west) It's a bit too sour but still pretty tender and juicy.

This location used to be Union square cafe but they left due to high rent fees according to some articles so I was curious to see how a noodle restaurant was holding up. The place was filled with a lot of young people and was pretty busy. Interior is nice and was pretty big.

Noodles were okay. But it wasn't really anything different though. It was just udon noodles in nice big dishes. They said extra noodle was the same price as the regular size. It's good to try and they opened another one in midtown as well.
Over priced. Don't get anything deep fried. They don't use even fresh oil for that price.

This probably has to be my fifth time coming to Tsurutontan. I really enjoy their food and service. I prefer the seating large arrangements at the location in Midtown, but the union Square one does have a nice open bar seating area. I couldn't finish my food, and was hoping to pack the rest of my meal to go, but they ran out of containers :( the food was delicious though! I got the tsuruton creme deluxe and tried the tsuruton Hot and sour udon. I was hoping for more pieces of salmon and shrimp in the creme deluxe bowl, but the dish had a lot of chicken pieces... The broth is very flavorful and creamy for both dishes. The broth for the hot and sour udon was too thick, but the flavor was pretty good! 

Their vegetable appetitizer was okay. It was interesting to have a deep fried boiled egg in this appetitizer given that it was a vegetable appetizer.. The deep fried mushroom  and seaweed was really good though!

It seems like most people make reservations. We were seated a few mins after we arrived because we got there 5 mins after the restaurant opened. 

We ordered: 
Tsurutontan Deluxe, $24: udon with shrimp & vegetable tempura, beef, chicken, egg drop in fashion broth

Tan tan udon, $20: ground pork in spicy & creamy sesame broth with chili oil, topped with grilled shishito peppers 

Both noodle soup broths were outstanding. However, the noodles were overcooked and soggy to the point that it broke when chopsticks picked them up. I believe it was an off day for them as the other reviews do not point out this criticism.

Tsurutontan had a beautifully complex flavor of fish, kelp, but was also thickened a bit by the egg drop. The shrimp & vegetable tempura was perfectly crispy. I would have preferred the tempura to be served separately as it became soggy within a min of sitting on top of the broth. 

Tan tan noodles were mildly spicy. The creamy broth was absolutely delicious. The ground pork & shishito peppers paired together perfectly. I wish they gave more ground pork. 

They offered 2 sizes: regular & large (1.5x the regular size). We ordered both noodle soups as large and easily finished the bowls. They looked insanely large when brought out. Surprisingly, we didn't feel stuffed after our meal. 

We would definitely return to try other dishes. Service was quick, attentive & courteous. Atmosphere: simple, elegant decor. The semi see through wood divider down the center of the table provided some privacy from the other side of the communal table. 

Bathroom: super hot & cramped, but clean.

OVERALL: a solid udon place with really authentic flavors. Get the large size if you can, it's the same price as the regular size, and make sure to either make a reservation or get here at an unpopular time to avoid a long wait.

I came here with a couple of friends on Thanksgiving weekend, and a hot bowl of udon was definitely something that we were craving to save our freezing bodies. We got seated in around 10-15 mins, which was less than ideal given that we came at 3:30pm and also made a reservation. The place was pretty packed though, given the time, so I guess it was fine.

I ordered the large beef udon and was surprised at how big the bowl was. However, there isn't actually THAT much more food compared to the regular size I think - it's just more soup and a larger sized bowl. The first thing I noticed was how strong the dashi was in the broth. It wasn't necessarily a bad thing, just not what I expected. However, I thoroughly enjoyed my meal and finished all of it, despite it looking intimidating in the beginning. I would definitely come here again and try the other things on the menu.

First off, their menu is amazing- it's so organized and show you top sellers and have pictures with each one, so it's so much easier to pick. The ambiance is definitely cutesy and very Japanese like (I'm definitely bringing my boyfriend and my siblings) and plus the food is delish and service was great! 

Uni Corn ($31.50)- 4/5 Loved the uni and the caviar cones! They were delish and the uni seemed fresh and was slightly bitter but tasty. Although they're quite expensive. Originally they have a set for 2 pieces ($21) but they allow you to add so we added a third and it was about (~$11 for each cone). 

Uni Crème Udon ($24)- 4/5 Slightly pricey for udon but it's uni! And the uni was decent but kinda hard to eat in small pieces, but definitely good. Unfortunately they only give you one lonely floating uni lol, but I already expected that based on the reviews. The broth was quite nice and creamy and not too heavy. The thick noodles tasted great as well. Perfect on a winter day! 

Spicy Tuna Tartare Cones ($12)- 5/5 Yum yum! I never really had spicy tuna tartare in cones but it was quite cute and easy to eat (better and less messy than taco versions). It was slightly spicy as expected and towards the bottom of the cone they had avocado puree which was yummy! I would highly recommend this as an appetizer and it's good to share since it comes with 4 cones but they are quite tiny.
So attempting to contact Christian as I was/am plannings revisit to make sure they now honor reservation times...no luck!!!! What now ???? Wow!

Udons are incredible. I ordered a large one, cause I was so hungry. But recognized that the regular one is the large one comparing to the other restaurants. My large udon was really big that three people could have it. Appetizers were just ok.

Walked in past 1pm on Sat. We got to seated about 5min which was great! Udon was very tasty and good texture. Service was also great! Me and my husband sat down share table. Unfortunately It was very tight and we're hoping that we get a regular table next time. Also udon bowl and chopsticks were hard to use because of the odd shape and size.

This experience was a complete miss. The food although decent, left a terrible taste in our mouth at the expense of the " manger " refusing to eliminate an item that was sent back from the bill. The " top seller " Blue Fin Tuna Toro Tartare" was unsalvageable. The  Uni was pungent like rotting seaweed from the bottom of the sea. We did enjoy some of the items which were edible but not anything you couldn't find at any other sushi restaurant. The hostess was very kind in trying to accommodate us at the bar with our 1 year old. Nearing the end of the experience our one year old slipped out of the baby seat due to faulty straps in the seat ( not the restaurants fault ) yet when we were paying the bill - the " manager " argued with little to no acknowledgement about the FULL dish of Tartare that we sent back. It was unforgettably disgusting- out of principle we were not willing to pay for it. He continued to auto- reply like a robot without emotions or hospitality " I'm sorry " - stating it was policy to ensure guests pay for food that was refused by the guests. Can't believe this restaurant survives in NYC. We would've love to reach someone with more seniority or half a brain in hospitality to represent  what this experience could've been. That $28 dish I would've paid for again, only to spit it back out on video to capture my true disgust for it, and this establishment.

Hostess Vanessa was very rude and unprofessional. 

We understood it's always busy at this restaurant. We followed hostess's instruction and left my phone number, she informed me the table will be ready in roughly an hour and 15 minutes. So we left to walk around and came back at an hour and a half later. 

We did not get a text or call. 

Then I approached the hostess asked for the wait status, she stated that she called out my name when my table was ready in the lobby, I did not respond to her calling in the restaurant so they gave away my table. 

What's the point of following her instruction to leave my phone number if she's not going to text or call it when my table is ready? 

I asked her did she text me as it's the process she told me at the beginning. She said no, she did not text or call my number. She then stated, either way, my table has been given to someone else and I will just have to wait longer. 

She did not apologize for the mistake but rather said it's not her restaurant, she just works there. It's a shame to have this type of service. 

I would not recommend anyone to come to this restaurant and receive this type of rude service.

Awesome udon place. They have an "extra udon" option, with no extra charge!
