If you're a heavy eater, this is the place to go! the bowls are also extra large, like literally twice the size of your face. Fast service and good atmosphere. If you're having a bday party and have your own cake, they charge $3 per plate.

The hostess told us that it would be a 30 minute wait and my friend and I were okay with it so we decided to wait in the restaurant. After 10 minutes of waiting we were seated quickly and was able to order our food.

So the beginning went well. However, after we were seated, an older gentlemen took forever to take our order but since this was a "classy" restaurant we decided to be patient knowing it was pretty busy. My friend and I then ordered two sodas, hot sake, two rolls of sushi, and two large udons. Our sushi came out pretty quick so we decided to wait for our udon to eat it together. We purposely didn't eat the sushi so that we can take a picture with all of our food together for the gram. We waited about thirty minutes and our udon was still not coming out so i had asked our waiter where our food was and he replied by saying that he THOUGHT we wanted our udon after our sushi. Now, if it has passed thirty minutes and both my friend and I haven't touched our sushi, we thought it was pretty obvious we wanted our udon with it. But instead, he went on saying that our order is next and that udon usually takes longer to make so we should just wait a bit. At this point, everyone around us who were seated later than us was getting their udon (which didn't make sense because we all ordered the same udon so i... anyways). After ten minutes my friend got her udon and i was still waiting for mine. After another ten minutes my udon never came and another waiter asked me under his breath if i no longer wanted my udon. So i agreed and told him that i no longer wanted my udon because it was just to ridiculous to be eatting at this restaurant at that point. I asked for my check and he told me that dessert would be on the house. Really? Dessert before an entree? 

Not only will I never come back to this restaurant again for poor qualty in service, but my friends udon was cold by the time it came out because PROBABLY it was sitting out for too long.

I thought the hype had died down but I was wrong. I made reservations online for a party of 4 for 8:15pm on a rainy Thursday evening. I actually arrived early, at 7:50pm and checked in with the hostess. The bar area was packed. I understand it's a waiting area but they had a lot of people sitting at the bar who were not ordering drinks. I was able to find an empty bar stool and order a drink but my friends had to stand when they got there bc there were about 4 women sitting there just waiting for their table. Even with a reservation, we didn't get seated until 8:40pm. I came solely for the pink creme udon, with the thick udon and of course the large bowl. My friends got the uni udon and the beef udon which they both said were good. Definitely make reservations, they are always packed but the food is worth it!

a couple stars for the food. but negative ten billion for the service. brutal i know but it was the most frustrating service i've ever received.

service: just freakin ugh the service SUCKED. it took us over an hour to get our first main dish. and its not like all came at once, it came one by one, like we had to share each dish every time because it took FOREVER. we made reservations at 5, ordered by 5:05, didn't get our first appetizer til like 5:40, then 6, then got our first dish at like 6:20pm. it SUCKED. we were starving, and yes we asked for appetizers first, but that doesn't mean it should come in freakin 30 minute increments. dishes came out ONE BY ONE. not altogether. like what -_- we asked when our dishes were coming, and i guess our ticket goes in once they take our appetizer plates away which doesn't make sense. like were hungry. put everything in at once, and bring out the dishes in a timely manner, not forever. like cmon. and the waiter just never came by. the host staff wasn't friendly either. super disappointed. left really pissed. food was good but if you're pissed, doesn't really leave you a good impression, so i wouldn't recommend coming here at all. food is good, but people here sucks.

food: you can order a large portion for the same price, which is great, but no need because the noodles are THICK and the dish is pretty big. unless you have a huge appetite, but because the bowl looks big, it looks like you're getting a huge portion. we ordered the WAGYU UNI SUSHI (2 pieces per order. trust, its pretty heavy for a sushi piece, so one bite is enough), BLUE FIN TORO TARTAR (great light appetizer in a yuzu soy sauce type of thing. comes with a sliver of uni and a little dollop of caviar), CREAM UNI UDON (this tastes like a cream pasta. not fishy at all, and not overpowered by uni. not too heavy on the cream either. pretty light), WAGYU TRUFFLE UDON (this dish came out luke warm. it wasn't hot at all. i was so confused. i think it was supposed to be hot, but it was cold, but cuz the dish came out LATE, didn't bother to send it back cuz we were all so damn hungry), COLD UNI UDON (cold udon is lightly dressed in a sauce at the bottom, and just a little bit of uni. refreshing udon bowl), KAISENDON (all bowls come with a side of small udon in their normal dashi broth. great combo). all the dishes here are great. the noodles are super thick and chewy, and the big spoons are definitely needed for these large noodles. anything uni though, they give you like one sliver in each dish (even the udons). not worth for anything uni.

cute interior though
I don't understand the long wait time! There is nothing special about the udon noodles. The broth is alright..... I think it's just overpriced

This is a super nice restaurant, the interior was modern meet traditional. The staffs are professional and friendly. But I don't get why there always a wait, even though we get there pretty early for dinner, like around 6pm, the place was kinda empty but I guess they were preparing for the dinner hours. Anyway, we didn't wait long and get seated in front of the noodle bar. We ordered one of the very popular appetizers, I believed it's the sashimi cone or something and I ordered a wagyu beef bowl with thick noodle and my fd ordered the crabmeat bowl with thin noodle. Omg, they are super good!!!! The broth of the soups are absolutely amazing~ My beef bowl is sweet and tasty, I love it!! ( and I usually don't like sweet ) my friends' bowl was literally full of crab meat!! They are a bit salty to my tastes but my friend loves it! We both like our own noodle bowl so much! Not to mention about our appetizer, it's very unique and of-cause it tasted good too! We would love to try out more appetizer as they all seems very delicious but we wouldn't be able to finish our noodle if we order more... I will definitely come back again with more fds, so we get to order more stuffs to try out!!

The reservation wasn't too hard to make online. Resy. 

Great service. 
Great ambiance. Not too crowded even though it was busy. 

This was my second visit but first visit to this specific location. 

My wagyu beef sukiyaki was too sweet for me. I ordered extra plain broth to add to my sweet sukiyaki broth (+$3) which didn't do much.. so I added a little water which helped. 

It had a good amount of mushroom and beef.
I love the udon noodle! Nice thick chewy! In love!

The large portion is the perfection for me. 3 out of 4 girlfriends finished the large udon.

I really enjoyed my friend's truffle udon. The soup has a very strong truffle flavor!

Another friend's dan dam noodle soup was too salty for all of us. She also added the plain broth but didn't help much so also added water. It has been 5hours since we left the restaurant and she is still drinking water :p

The uni tuna roll appetizer was good. Nothing amazing for me. 

The lycheetini was very strong!! And flavorful :)

I will be back at the Rockefeller location because it's a bigger location and I just love the udon noodles!!!

This was my third time visiting Tsurutontan in the past 2 years. My 3 friends and I wanted to have a belated Christmas dinner to exchange our gifts, and the winner was this udon restaurant. I was excited because I wanted a soupy, noodle dish. My past visits were very good, but unfortunately, I was not pleased with this time's experience. 

My lovely friend was 45 minutes late, so we hung out at the bar for their "all-day" happy hour. I asked the bartender to make my lychee martini not as sweet since I don't like sweet drinks and gave me a look as if I was crazy. Apparently you can't make a drink less sweet if it contains lychee. I got the drink and it tasted a bit weird, but I sucked it up and had 3 lol I thought it was bc they put more alcohol in it. 

When my tardy friend finally arrived, we were seated. Based on my past review of this location, the younger version of me recommended the tuna cone and creamy shrimp, so we ordered it again. The tuna cone was still delicious! The creamy shrimp - not so much. The shrimp tasted very oily and there was not much flavor to it. I would not get this again. 

We got a bottle of sake to wait. The waiter recommended Hakkassan which was good. The bottle has about 8 glasses which was the perfect amount of drinks we needed. The waiter chilled it between pours which was nice, but I'd prefer to have an ice bucket of some sort at the table. 

For the entree, I wanted a spicy broth so my options were limited. The tan tan looked good but it contained ground pork which I do not like. I asked the waiter and he said it was not possible to substitute, so I decided to get it any way. The dish was extremely salty and had way too many tiny balls of ground pork with barely any veggies or anything else. You have an option to pick small or large. We all picked the large, because why not? There is also an option to pick thin or thick noodles. I love thickness, so that's what I picked. We asked for more broth to dilute the soup which didn't help. I had to add more water to it and they charged us for the broth. I drank soooo many cups of water, almond milk, seltzer when I got home. 

The finish, I got a serving of green tea ice cream which comes with two scoops. I thought the ice cream tasted pretty authentic, not too sweet and matcha-y. 

The bill was reasonable in my opinion, but I don't think I will be returning for a while.

The perfect place to go to on a rainy day - or any day, really. I've been here a few times and have always loved the ambiance, the service, and the food.

My go-to is always the wagyu and truffle udon; sometimes I'll make it a large (at no charge!) if I'm feeling extra hungry. I had the uni udon once and was disappointed; there was only one tiny slice of uni in the middle and the broth was under seasoned. After that I stuck with the truffle/wagyu and thicker noodles; it smells just as good as it tastes!

This place is simply amazing. My wife and I happened to passed by here and decided to try it. We didn't have reservations but was able to get a table within 30 minutes. And when we did. Oh boy. From our experience at the bar. ** thank you for our bartender whom was so nice that he help my wife by recommending a delicious mango margarita. 

To Our waiter who was extremely gracious and delightful. As for the food??? Omg. Absolutely delicious.  My wife and I have found our place for future date nights dinner.

Made a reservation for Friday night for 7:30 and it was really packed. The waiting area does get pretty hot and congested. We waited for around 15 min to get called which wasn't too bad because we were able to get drinks at the bar in the meantime. 
We got the spicy tuna tartare cone as an appetizer. It wasn't too special in my opinion for $12 but they're cute for aesthetics and for that Instagram story. 
For the udon, we got the tan tan udon and uni creme udon. You have a choice of skinny noodles or the regular thick udon noodles - so we decided to try both. 
The creme udon had a little smokey flavor to the broth and was interesting in a good way. 
I really liked the tan tan udon. It had a little kick to it and more of a ramen-type broth. 
Service exceeded my expectations considering how busy it was. They came over to fill water multiple times and were very polite. Food also came out very quickly.

Sad to say I had to knock down the rating from a 4.  This was my third visit and I chose to visit here for a special occasion.  Previous experiences were okay, but the most recent one just fell flat for me.

Made a reservation, the earliest time was at 9:45pm.  I understand usually weekends can be hectic so I booked this time.  Hostess told me to wait outside and she'll contact us when there's a table, but she never did...After watching other parties that arrived after me get seated, I went inside to inquire about it. Apparently she forgot I was outside.  Whoops.

I ordered extra udon once and it seemed exactly the same as the regular portion.  I wanted to really determine if there was really extra udon.  I think it was a bit weird when I asked for the extra udon to be placed on the side, the waitress said they don't do that.  

Took a while to get the check, it seemed the wait staff at the time was more preoccupied with servicing the tables and not the bar like seats.  Overall the udon is decent, my go to is the katsu curry udon. I just don't think it's a good idea to dine here when they're crowded/peak times.

We visited this restaurant on Sunday at 12:30 with no reservation. Even they said hi or welcome. Nothing. So I asked hostess for a table for 3 then she said is it okay with counter table. But she wasn't asking me really okay or not. Just mention it. I thought it would be a bar table where is near by door. We wanted to get a normal table so I asked her if we could have another one. She said "Counter table is not a bar table". I was so embarrassed and felt bad at the moment. Did she treat me like I'm an idiot? I don't know. Anyway our waitress was so cute and really kind. She was so nice. We ordered Oyakodon, curry udon, and shabu beef Udon. Shabu beef udon is too oily but other one was okay. I hope they check their host service again. The hostess doesn't know what's she is doing because the way she treated other customers was not good at all. Maybe she thinks she's professional but doesn't at all.
The udon noodles were great, as the tuna sashimi. Service was a little slow, so make sure to plan a little extra time / keep tabs on your server so things don't slip through the cracks.

Love love love! My family and I came here for lunch and were blown away by the soup bases and size of the noodle portions. It's definitely more convenient to make a reservation before coming here because the place gets full quickly and the waits are medium time. One of the signature dishes here is the truffle udon (I absolutely recommend after trying). The soup bases are unlike a lot of other restaurants in a sense that they are not salty. The portion size is great for the price (when I came here the small and large size were the same price so I was thrilled). The staff are also super friendly and attentive (but not over attentive). Will definitely be back considering this might just be my mom's favorite place!

Dinner
Wait: 1.5 hours
Ambiance: 7/10

I came in as a group of 5 and was at the top of the waitlist for 1.5+ hours. The place was jam-packed with many tourists and mainstream eaters. Definitely not the place you want to go if you want authentic Japanese cuisine. Place has calm lighting and nice accents but there is a lack of space for walking.
--------------------
Appetizers
--------------------
Crispy corn kakiage $8
Presentation: 3/10
Taste: 4/10
Recommend: No

-came with spicy ra-yu aioli (spicy mayo) with some hot pepper oil
-disappointed that the corn was bland
- 3 pieces were not worth the 8


Soy Garlic Fried Tatsuta Chicken $13
Presentation: 5/10
Taste: 7/10
Recommend: Yes

- the soy garlic sauce is tasty but didn't evenly coat the chicken as some pieces were dry
- there was a larger portion than expected so definitely one of the more worth-it appetizers
-chicken had the slight crunch, satisfying to bite into

--------------------
Main Course
--------------------
Ever popular dashi broth
(Large) duck udon w/ large udon noodles $18
Presentation:  7/10
Taste: 5/10
Recommends if you want some good meatballs. Otherwise, perhaps trying a different dish might be more worth it for the amount you are paying.

Note that the price for a medium bowl is the same as the large bowl. The large bowl is served in a comically larger bowl but the extent to how much more food is given to you if any is unknown. Duck was not the freshest duck I have had. Didn't seem like it had any flavor. However, the meatballs were very moist and flavorful. The udon serving was large however the broth is too salty for my taste (intended or not). Is a classic but for the amount I paid for the noodles, I expected more.

Service: 1 Star. There is no point in making a reservation. I made a reservation for 8:15pm. Checked in at 7:45pm with my full party. Did not get seated until 8:35 pm. 

Food quality: 3 Star. They give you a massive amount of food which is cool but the taste is sub par. Definitely a quantity over quality udon. you can get tastier udon for the same price or cheaper at Raku.

AtmospherCleanliness: 4 stars.

Been here multiple times and always enjoy their uni ikura scallop udon, but maybe not anymore. Had it again on 12/27/2018, and the portion of ikura and uni were just, underwhelming. It used to blow my mind and easily earned a place in my heart, now it's just meh and I probably won't come back again since the other items I have tried didn't impress me that much. (And this place is a bit pricey, which is why I always came here for that particular udon).

This place is pretty popular so remember to make a reservation.

I have been the restaurant many times in the past two years. And the quality of their food and service went down so fast. After tonight. I will never be back.
We made a reservation online at 6:30, and we got in time and checked in. After 15 minutes standing waiting, still nothing happened. I went to the girl who is hosting in front of the computer and tried to ask how long we need to wait more, and I saw she marked my name on seated section already and brought other people to seat on my name. I was like when can we sit now, and the girl quickly deleted my name on the seated section and asked me what's your name again? I was like I saw you put my name in the wrong place, that's unreasonable. She just stared at me and said, no I didn't, if u don't gave me a second problem u should talk to my manger. 
I guess that's how the restaurant in New York to train their staff to treat their customers. Shame of you. The original one in Tokyo was way more better. Also there r many other great udon restaurant in the city like Raku, why have to go to your place.
Ruin my night.

Still love this place as ever!
Affordable quality udon with huge portion~

This was my second time trying this location. It does get busy but the wait is usually 10-15 minutes.

Pro
- affordable noodle 
- huge portions
- fast service
- got tantan udon! it was good, but wasn't my style as it was very salty
- also got uni udon! the udon was good... but i was barely seeing the uni
- I will say just go for the original udon

Con
- spicy tuna tartare cone - this was okay. interesting, but I don't think I will order again as they are tiny $12. It was just cute
- stick with orginal udon as others can get a bit salty
- the second time I went, the udon was really overcooked so I couldn't use my chopstick to pick up the noodles lol

Found on Yelp. We both had the Sukiyaki Udon soup with beef and vegetable, it's out of this world and the bowl is humongous. Prepare to wait a little as it's a popular and trendy place. Loved it so much I will definitely come back here again!

Came here a few times and enjoyed it every time. Food is good and I like the variety of appetizers. Udon is soft and fresh. Broth is flavorful. The only thing that might be a bit deceiving is that they advertise the big bowls a lot but the food portion itself isn't really that big. But it could also be that i'm a fatass.

Definitely, the place to go to if you're craving udon! 

I went here to eat lunch in a party of 4. The store is quite fancy looking, with some steps leading down to additional seating. 

There's quite a lot of different food options to choose from, all with the same lovely high price tag! 

The male server who served us was super friendly and spoke in a well-mannered tone. We all shared 4 bowls of different udon, the thick noodle kind, and large size (which is the same price as a regular!). 

The bowls the food came in were massive! The Katsu Curry Udon ($18) had a sweet taste, as expected from Japanese curry. The Wagyu and Mushroom Udon was also pretty sweet and had a strong mushroom taste to the broth, which I didn't enjoy. But I sure enjoyed the fatty meat in it! The Sizzling Sukiyaki may not be in a fancy bowl like all the others, as it was served in the flattest looking dish. However, it was my second fave as the udon, soaked in meat and mushrooms, offered plenty of flavors. I particularly enjoy creamy types of udon, so I loved the Uni Creme Udon ($24) the most. We may be sharing but I probably ate from this dish the most! They also offered plenty of uni inside if you're into that. 

In the end, I spent around 20 something dollars. The meal definitely is pricey but I was able to try 4 different types of delicious udon. Best of all, the service was also fantastic so I definitely see myself going back!

Just as good as the Midtown location!! This place is HUGE, but I heard it can get busy especially on the weekends. I recommend reservations or call ahead and put your name down. Excellent service!!!!! Our waitress was very friendly and checked up on us often.

Food came out pretty fast. I got a tuna tartare, sea jewel, and a large uni creme udon to share with two other person, and it was the perfect amount. WARNING they are HUGE portions like BUCKET SIZE. Anyways, it was SO GOOD AND CREAMY. Very flavorful and filling. The appetizers were good, but no as amazing as the udon.

About an hour wait for parties of 2-3 on a Friday evening. Make a reservation!!

We ordered
Sashimi platter appetizer for one (3 pieces each of salmon, tuna, hamachi) - A++++
Fried corn appetizer (3 pieces with bomb sauce) - A
Uni creme broth udon - B+ (the noodles and soup were delicious, but the uni was sadly bitter)

You can choose between skinny or thick udon noodles, and regular or large portions for the same price!

Fancy Asian Fusion vibe
We took a Duck Udon - Large portion : yes the bowl itself is huge : there was a lot of broth, a lot of big noodles BUT not enough duck!
Also the broth is kind of sweet which is strange, a couple of green onion slices. It is disappointing.

Even our home made udon soup is better and more tasteful!

Music not loud - good point 
Not too pricy (I am not saying it's cheap)

Staff is Ok but they when they speak all together, you can hear the conversations : how much was the tip....

So the experience was Ok but not sure We will come back. I am sure there are other good Asian restaurant in this area. Someone told me about Oramen....

Keep following our adventures ;)

Had really high hope for this place since I love Japanese food and Udon is one of my favorites. The atmosphere here is nice - very different from the Tsurutontan's in Japan, but it fits in well in NY. The food though was subpar - we got the treasures of the sea appetizer - and it was not well put together. The udon dishes were ok - broth was pretty bland and my dish just had a ton of cabbage and not very much meat. All in all - I think they have some work to do to maintain the standards which we experienced in Japan.

My Yelp review for the restaurant:


We ordered the tuna tartare cones and edamame to share, and I ordered the Tantan Udon dish. The food was alright, the tuna tartare was like a blended paste (?) that they squeezed into a wonton cone and the edamame was served cold, which I was not a style of edamame I was a fan of. The Tantan Udon portion is HUGE! So that is a plus - also, the charge is the same whether you get the small or large size, the only difference being you get more noodles with the large size. However, the broth was just a little too heavy and felt oily. The flavor of the broth was alright but nothing to write home about. I got the thin noodle version for my dish. The noodles were soft and chewy but felt over cooked, again, wasn't a fan.

Service was pretty attentive but I felt rushed the entire time I was there. When I got there, 6pm on a Monday, it was relatively empty but for some reason I barely got 5 minutes to look at the menu before being asked what I would like to order, and if I paused for a second while eating, a server would come over and ask me if I was done. That happened like 3 or 4 times. Eventually, I just said yes because I wasn't a big fan of the broth anyways. As soon as they cleared my bowl, they dropped the check on our table and then hovered. After paying, we were asked to leave to make room for the next reservation. I think we had barely been there more than an hour. I would understand if this was one of those hole in the wall places where the space is limited and the food is excellent (i.e: Totto or Ippudo) but this was a big space with multiple floors! The whole experience was very bizarre and definitely left a bad taste in my mouth (literally). Don't think it will be worth it to go back again.

Only been here once. The food is decent. A small is the same price as the large. The service was annoying. My friend got her food and I got mine ten minutes later. We also took a while to just get the check.  This review is based on taste alone.
Absolutely the best!!  Always first stop in NYC!!  Pork udon extra spicy and tuna cones.

My boy friend and I were OBSESSED with this place and often time brought friends + family to join us. However, the last two occasions have been far from pleasant to the extent that we no longer will be coming back. Last week, I found a very long, curly black hair intertwined in my udon. I understand that happens sometimes and although it was absolutely disgusting, I was willing to let us slide. I was already originally the last to get my food so when the new bowl of udon came out, I ate then asked for a to go container. Subsequently, they "ran out" of to go containers. Furthermore, they didn't even have the common decency to remove the dish from the check. However, this did not entirely sway our opinion of this place and we went again yesterday with my boy friends family. Food was OK but not as hot as usual and they completely forgot one of the entrees we had ordered. We had already been waiting quite a bit for what we thought would be coming out so when our waiter let us know he did not put the order in, we decided to get the check and leave. Upon our departure, the table next to us found a disgusting material within his udon bowl. He thought it was an old tissue but that would have disintegrated due to temperature. Whatever it was - it was disgusting and the staff did not seem to be phased by it or apologetic. Needless to say, we are now on the hunt for a new udon place as we will no longer be customers of this p

I've heard a lot of good things about this place but had to admit I was underwhelmed. I'm quite picky with my udon since I've had my fair share around the city and Asia, and I felt like Tsurutontan caters to an American taste. Personally I thought the noodles were too clumsy, something about them wasn't quite right. The broths were also too unbalanced-one was too heavy and the other didn't seem to have enough flavor. The bowls were also unnecessarily large, and I also noticed that the crowd was also heavier on the Caucasian side than other noodle places I've been to. 

The service I will admit was very good, our server was very attentive and friendly, and also gave us recommendations very enthusiastically. Unfortunately the food just didn't really live up to the hype, and in my opinion in the New York landscape this just didn't really make the cut.
Great service from the staff, however, I found a bug in my food and lost my appetite after. I visited here with high hopes and did not expect this at all. All they did was offered to replace my dish.

Came here for lunch and got the Wagyu Truffle Udon. The noodles were perfectly chewy and the beef was sliced nice and thin so it just melted in your mouth. The broth was good and the free "extra noodles" are the way to go. Haven't had as much udon as I've had ramen, but I would happily return

Love the location off of union square but not very comfortable seating and all dependent on people around you. Loud "neighbors" make the meal experience a bit off putting because the center "bar" is really long and seating tight. Bowls are big - flavor so-so. A bit salty. Had veggie and a shrimp tempura udon.  I'm not sold on returning.

We ordered uni udon and hot & sour udon, udon were great! We love it! Kaiden don was fresh and delicious. Spicy tuna tartar come are good too! Service was nice. Everything was wonderful until we got the lady M green tea crepe cake  :( 
we understand it happened sometime, just feel funny and disappointed

My friends and I decided to stop by Tsurutontan for a weekday dinner. We got there around 6ish. We were escorted to the back section and seated right away. When we got there, it wasn't empty, but was definitely quieter. Around 7-8pm, those same empty tables that we saw around us were getting filled quickly, so we thought to ourselves that we chose a good time to come & avoid the long wait time. 

When we got seated, we got looking at the menu. I didn't know that they had such an extensive list of dishes/udons that I was kind of overwhelmed making my decision. There were a few standout dishes that I was deciding between, but when the waiter came, that solved everything. 

The waiter was so knowledgeable about the menu. She had everything good to say about every dish and noted out what makes them unique. She highlighted the most popular dishes and clarified some questions. She then went on to explain that they have the option between thin/thick udon noodles and even bowl size options. She mentioned that the larger size portion of noodle is a complimentary add-on at no additional cost. 

In the end, I chose the tsurutontan deluxe, which had various tempuras inside and opted for the thick noodle with the free portion upgrade. To be honest, the dish wasn't super impressive. But, I did enjoy that the bowl was huge and there was indeed a lot of udon noodle inside that I was satisfied and full by the end of it. The whole general experience was great.

Love the fresh udon noodles and all the creative and beautiful soups the make here. I had the creamy uni udon and beef udon. It was too die for. I count down the days to when I can come back here again.

Learned what the restaurant name means on the website:
Tsuru: sound of slurping noodles
Ton: sound of kneading and shaping udon
Tan: sound of cutting udon

Several things to note:
1) The bowls are huge!  You can order a bowl for individual eating (some folks finished their bowl and ended up being very full) or sharing (trying different options).
2) Any leftovers you have, there is no doggie bags or package to go.
3) The price is the same if you order the regular or large.  You can ask if the regular bowl can add noodles for free -- since it's the same price.  If you want additional noodles on top of what is in the large bowl, there is an added cost.

As you walk in the restaurant, there is a section for waiting area, a bar on the right side, and dining rooms are located on the left side and as you walk pass the bar.

We had reservations since we were a big group celebrating a birthday.  We were given the semi-private room (on the second floor that overlooks the first floor).  There are 2 two people tables on the same floor.

For appetizers: We shared 
corn kariage (didn't need the condiments), unicone (the uni was only on the top and didn't reach the bottom of the cone), spicy tuna tartare cone, sukiyaki buns, soy garlic tatsuta.

Entree:
Oyster Soondubu, Kaisen Don, Tsurutontan Deluxe, Lobster Tempura, Duck Udon, Wagyu Mushroom Sukiyaki

Dessert: 
Chocolate Crown, Green Tea Crepe, Lychee Ricotta Cup

The restrooms are located on the first floor.  The is 1 restroom for the Men (by the staircase to the second floor) and 2 restrooms for the Women (by the dining room on the left side) located in separate areas.

Overall, we had a good time, great service (constant refill of water cups) and quickly clearing of plates for the next course.  The menu changes according to the season so there is always something new to try!

Came back again for dinner and another birthday celebration...We sat upstairs again as we did the first time with a big party. Upstairs seating doesn't open until 5:45pm and they don't seat incomplete parties so make sure your party arrives on time. 

Great service and food here...they have expanded the menu a bit since I was here last year.  Always good to see new items. Happy hour specials at the bar... may come back for that as drinks are 1/2 price at the bar for certain drinks vs service at the table. 

Got to try some new appetizers as well as the usual favorites: 
spicy tuna tartare cone, uni cone, corn kariage, sukiyaki buns, soy garlic tatsuta (chicken) ...all were good!

Main course:  usual tsurutontan deluxe is the favorite, winter special - oyster soondubu, duck udon, waygu mushroom sukiyaki, lobster tempura (basically tempura lobster tail cut up in pieces), kaisen dan.

Dessert: chocolate crown, Lady M green tea crepe, and lychee ricotta cup. Love the green tea crepe with green tea ice cream.

Remember: order what you can eat as no doggie back to take food home.

Came here for a friends going away (although the receptionist was confused on how to seat us, we mentioned "together" and not separated a few times but she kept reasking until most of us got a bit annoyed). 

For udon of choice time, I had the wagyu shabu udon and it was sooo good! I still chose the large (same price as normal, just more noodles) with the thick noodles and I really enjoyed the wagyu shabu udon. It was a bit oily and after having enough of the broth it was too salty to me BUT that could be because I don't usually eat food with a lot of salt. 

Overall, the service was super accommodating for our 13 person party and I enjoyed my noodle dish!

IG: @phothegram

Make sure you reserve on a weekend night, feel the fusion vibe when you walk in. Refer to my pics, most of the tables are arranged as shared with limited single tables on the side (what we got and more preferred). There's a young, fast-paced vibe with tables turning fast. 

Got the following for the two of us: Sashimi combo, pork kakuni, large beef udon, uni creme udon. Like: sashimi combo and beef udon. In terms of sashimi quality, although it's a tad overpriced, it's on par with the standard. Really wanted to try the wagyu sushi, but backed off with the high price tag. The beef udon is your traditional (and pretty authentic from my opinion) Japanese udon with clear broth. Make sure you take extra udon option (with no additional cost, another strategy with the price tag already including the "extra" udon, the bowl was huge and good for your Instagram photos). However, I'd expect some better beef with a $21 price tag, but don't take me wrong, udon was decent overall.

Then here goes the dislikes: uni-creme udon and pork kakuni. Expect the kakuni to be similar to your usual Asian beef stew with a soy sauce based broth. However, the pork was really tough with very limited fat. The uni-creme udon was a huge miss.....ugh....I wouldn't recommend it at all and don't want to comment.....couldn't even find the uni when it first came up.....

Should have tried the sukiyaki and donburi instead.....

Service was good, on par with other restaurants with a similar price range.

Conclusion: worth a first try, but probably would only try the donburi and sukiyaki if I ever return. If you've been reading my post, you know that there are so many choices and it's hard for me to return to the same location unless the place is that good, couldn't find any of that anywhere, very very rare.

food 3/5
ambiance 3.5/5
service 3.5/5
value 3/5

TL;DR: huge portions that you likely won't finish. Delicious and a little pricy; wait can be long even at lunch.

The fact that I came here two days in a row says something about this spot. I love noodles and all noodle soups, and Tsurutontan hits the spot when I need something warm and filling. Most of the soup udons are delicious - I had the spicy seafood both times - and I was counseled to get the regular, not the large. If you're one person eating, the regular is large enough to be filling, with leftovers to take home. The large is the same price but with additional noodles, and I could see that being a good option for two people sharing. Otherwise, there's no way you'll finish on your own (and reheated udon gets soggy and gross). Total comes to a bit above $20, which is the only downside; this spot is a little pricy for a bowl of noodles.

Warning if you're trying to come here on a business or date lunch, the udon is very hot and you'll likely start sweating if you get one of the spicy ones. You will not look dignified and be slightly embarrassed.

I don't know how people can physically eat a whole bowl on their own. It's massive. There's lots of choices. Even If you come with a group of (picky NYC) people everyone will find something they like. It's really good and warms the soul. A different vibes from Raku which is equally good but is more traditional and simpler flavors. I would gladly go to either! Check out the massive bowl which is bigger than your head.

I fell prey to the hype but unfortunately don't know what the hype is all about?? You can choose between thin and thick udon for all their udon dishes - I personally thought their thick udon was a bit tough and not chewy like I've come to expect from udon. The thin udon was different, though it felt like essentially a combination of flour noodles with the consistency/texture of rice noodles. 

It's cool that the bowls come out so large, but really the portion sizes are okay. Cool if you come for the insta, but honestly it's pretty dark in the restaurant so tbh save yourself a wasted trip. It was also extremely crowded and busy on a random Thursday night so if you really want to check it out make sure you call ahead for a reservation! 

I don't quite remember the name of the clear broth (Nabeyaki?) but it was quite flavorful so I'll give them this. The seafood chigae one was very mediocre (tastes neither Japanese nor Korean) so I would recommend passing on it.

If you're in NYC, you have to go to Tsurutontan at least once for the experience.  You can choose to get the iconic big bowl of udon. It is a little pricey but I'd say it's worth the taste and experience. Other than the udon, my favorite appetizers would have to be the seared salmon sashimi and spicy tuna cones.

Authentic Udon. Excellent udon noodles. Very highly recommend. Visited the restaurant on 48th street back in July and had a similar, excellent experience. Great udon in a giant bowl. Had the blue fin tuna don as well. Enjoyed it all.

For the amount I paid the taste of the food was a disappointment. I got one of the caviar crab udon and it tasted bleh. The soup was thick pretty much tasted like something I could order from authenic chinese restaurant and tasted better.  Maybe I ordered the wrong item on ther menu. Don't think I'll be coming back here again but service is pretty good.
Udon heaven!!! Visit here!!! Definetely coming back....good food service a little slow

Came back here when my friend, the birthday girl, was craving for udon again, and I'm not complaining! There are so many different varieties of udon bases here that I knew I had to try something new this time around. My friend recommended us to try the Truffle Creme with Crab and Mushroom. I love truffle, cream based broth, crab, and mushroom so I thought this one was for me.

It was good. Not outstanding or anything amazing. Just good. The broth was overly saturated with truffle oil flavor, in my opinion, so much that the crab lost its own flavor. I'll admit, there were a great number of crab pieces in it, but it was a bit difficult trying to fish them out from the giant bowl filled with a cream based broth. The udon noodles were perfectly al dente and the mushrooms were good. It was more flavorful than the Uni creme udon I had last time, but the truffle oil was a little overpowering for me.

Overall, it hits the spot on a cold winter day. The wait was not that bad with a reservation, but it was definitely crowded on a Saturday evening. The portions were huge and the waiters were nice and accommodating. I would still love to come back and try their other udon dishes.

P.S. The lighting was very dim and the music was too loud. Good atmosphere for the bar, but not for the restaurant.

SUCH A YUMMY UDON PLACE ! I heard good things about this place and I wanted to check it out!! it was a cold rainy day that we went and honestly The broth of this udon just warmed me up! The interior is cute. The seating is a little tight and hard to get out once you're in sitting but the menu has such a wide variety and the bowl is HUGEEE! My boyfriend and I shared a bowl and it was so delicious. It does seem a little pricey but it is so worth it!

Very trendy type of Japanese restaurant.  Beautiful bar upon entrance and I enjoyed dining in the underground area where the middle was designated for individuals/couples eating in a more casual setting.

Food was really good!  After just returning from Japan, I was used to having bomb udon and sukiyaki at reasonable prices. The food here was just about on par.  They gave American-size portions, and had a lunch menu option to add side chirashi bowl dishes too. However, the $20 for the sukiyaki udon was just too steep.  I dont think I can even find dishes as these back in the SF Bay Area for that much. I understand all the hype behind these dishes, but it just felt like they were gouging us.  Funny because I'd probably come back again to eat these dishes and eat the price.  Very attentive service, besides the hostess who seemed to be in a bad mood, or just wasn't particularly friendly. All in all, great ambience and a very Japanese New York feel!

The portions here are huge! If you're near Union Square and in the mood for noodles or soup- this is it! There are so many options of flavors and styles of udon. I truly do think there is a dish here for everyone. 

They brought out our udon in huge bowls. You could easily fit your whole face in there. They ask if you want free extra noodles and I took them up on it and honestly it was enough for two meals for me. I had the spicy seafood udon and it was delicious- so flavorful. All of my friends ordered different styles and enjoyed theirs as well. 

The staff was so accommodating and took the time to explain the different styles of noodles since it was our first time there. I was seated in a semi private booth and it was so cozy and perfect for my group. The interior is stylish with long bench style seating downstairs and some booths on the main floor. I liked the ambiance there, it was chic. 

I had a great experience and I definitely will head back!

If you like truffle and creamy broths, get the crab and mushroom creme udon. You won't regret it.

So I heard of long waits at Tsurutontan, but I didn't expect a crowd THAT big when I came on a Friday night. Luckily, I had made reservations earlier in the day for 7:15 that night for my boyfriend and me, so we only ended up waiting less than 10 minutes (not bad considering we arrived early too). The waiting area was jam packed with parties waiting for tables -- it was a bit overwhelming and the huge crowd made me feel a bit suffocated. More than happy I didn't have to wait too long in it.

We were seated next to one another in one of the more communal-like tables. My boyfriend mentioned that he really likes the set up of the restaurant (he has a bit of restaurant experience) and that their layout is a smart way to accommodate crowds of just pairs or larger parties. Our waiter came over with menus and, after verifying that this was our first time there, proceeded to explain the entire menu to us. With every udon order, you can choose thick or thin noodles and regular or large proportions, all for the same price. My boyfriend ordered the uni creme udon while I ordered the crab and mushroom creme udon, both large with thick noodles (as recommended by our waiter).

For appetizers, we got the spicy tuna tartare cones and sukiyaki buns. Both dishes were great; I loved the crunch of the cones and the layers of tuna and avocado and the buns had such tender meat and flavorful sauce. Super yummy! However, I will say I feel kinda ripped off because the spicy tuna was only at the top of the cone. As for the noodles, my boyfriend loves uni but wasn't too impressed with his dish. He said the uni didn't taste as fresh as he would have liked it to, though he did like how it practically melted into his broth. However, because of this, he felt like no broth could go to waste! My dish, on the other hand, was pretty good. I do feel like they went a little overboard with the truffle oil (you could see it settle on top of the broth overtime which grossed me out a bit) but the flavors overall were still good. There was a decent amount of crab but there wasn't much of a crab flavor (probably due to the overwhelming truffle flavor), which was fine with me but may be disappointing to you crab lovers out there! I liked the noodles, but my boyfriend found it to be too tough for his liking. Even though we both got large, we had been starving for hours and managed to finish our bowls!

I personally thought prices were a bit high and though the bowls were huge, the amount of noodles and broth you actually get isn't as much as you would think. It's pretty much an optical illusion, but to me it is a decent amount of food (maybe not $25 worth, but this is NYC we're talking about). Service was okay, water glasses were kept full and there are a ton of servers. I had a slight issue with our order -- we had ordered the spicy tuna cones but our waiter misheard and brought out uni cones, to which he apologized and brought out the correct order. However, on our check, my boyfriend noticed we were billed for both and had to flag down a server to bring it up to his attention (an extra $21 yikes). The problem was resolved quickly and luckily my boyfriend checked the bill before we paid. I was so engrossed in conversation that I didn't even bother checking -- lesson learned: always check your bill!

Usually love this place however went today at 12:00pm when the place was pretty much empty and the front of the house staff was extremely slow at seating people down. It took them 15-20 minutes for us to be seated at the bar. Food was fine but the poor service really ruined the meal.

I have been to Tsurutontan 5 Times. 4 out of 5 times - excellent experience. It's unfortunate that I have to write a review like this because the food is truly delicious (I am a big fan of the tsurutontan deluxe udon), and the atmosphere is great.  However, my most recent visit with two of my colleagues left me feeling disappointed and wary of returning. Again, food was excellent. Yet the service was terrible. The server was unhelpful and accusatory. We ordered two tsurutontan deluxe udons, but we were served two tsurutontan curry deluxe udon instead. When we flagged the waitress to correct it, she told us it's because we pointed at the wrong photo while saying the correct name. If she noticed this, she should've clarified it but the more appalling thing is, we never physically pointed at the picture. As mentioned before, I have been here multiple times so I know exactly what I want. Hence I would not and did not point at an image on the menu to order. My friend also ordered same dish based on my recommendation. Instead of fixing it immediately, she chose to just stand and stare - expecting us to either eat it or order another udon, and pay for it again. We had also mentioned that one of us cannot eat pork and the curry udon has pork, and yet she still chose to assert that we have to either eat it or order and pay for the correct dish. In the end, another server did bring me the correct dish but my friend never had her's corrected. She ended up eating nothing that night. The waitress then still tried to charge my friend for the udon that she physically cannot eat, until a manager came by and modified the check for just two udon bowls and not three. The manager was helpful and calm which I appreciated. And yet, because of how long it took to fix this mistake, my entire party was late to another appointment after dinner. The waitress did end up apologizing to us - but it felt forced and I felt so terrible for my friend who ended up not eating dinner at all that night.

Worst service.
We were said to wait for 20-30mins when we got there.
We saw many available tables and seats though.
And we were said to sit on a tiny bar seat which is uncomfortable.
A bartender charged wrong price at first and asked if it's correct then brought fixed receipt without apology.
We wanted to order another beer but they said bar is closed.
We couldn't get Udon either.
It was freezing freezing cold Friday night.
There weren't much people walking outside.
Maybe they didn't work because they can't get good tip on the night.
My first Tsurutontan was such disappointing experience.

I was really craving noodles and soup and stopped by for some udon on a Saturday around 1pm with no wait even without a reservation. My friend and I were seated adjacently to each other which was kind of awkward for conversation since I had to angle my body to talk. 

We ordered a sashimi salad as an appetizer to share. There was a generous portion of sashimi (with two pieces of each so it was convenient to share!) on top of mixed greens and edamame. Wasn't a huge fan of the ponzu and sesame dressing cause the nuttiness didn't pair great with the fish. I also got the shrimp tempura udon (with extra noodles cause it's free!). Big fan of the broth - it's full of umami flavor and the noodles were soft and thick - very fun to slurp up. The tempura was as expected but I wanted a simple dish to test the quality of the udon. The portion was huge and I was able to make 2 meals out of the dish so very worth it. Next time I definitely want to give one of the more creative menu items a try!

Finally I got the try this udon in a huge bowl. Always remember to make a reservation or expect yourself to wait. I made a reservation so I don't know how long people have to wait but I did see a mop of people waiting while blocking the front door. I went there on Friday night so definitely the wait will be much longer. The interior design was impressive on all 3 floors(half, first and second floor). 
The waitress came over and gave us the menus and explain the different options of udon since this is my first time here. On the menu, there were appetizers, rices dish, udon And dessert. Since it was my first time coming here, there is no point looking at anything else except for udon. The udon came different kind of soup base and it is category into either hot(soup base) and cold(no soup, just sauce base). We got the uni creme udon($24) and wagyu and mushroom sukiyaki($24). Just remember one thing no matter if you get the small or large, it is the same price. I got large. For me it is a no brainer, I will always try to get my money worth. The uni creme was really creamy and heavy. It was really good at the beginning but heaviness and creaminess of the base really became too much after few more bites and I didn't feel like eating anymore. The wagyu beef and mushrooms sukiyaki soup base was sweet with a really strong rice wine. Very sweet at first but it tasted better afterward.  I recommend you share it with someone so that you can try different flavors as well as not having too much of any one of them. Overall it was good but due to the high price, I would like more service and food.

I come here a lot and just because of their appetizers not the noodles. I love the hamachi carpaccio (dont know why it's better than another place), the spicy tuna is good too. I have tried several udon dishes and only like the duck udon and the creamy uni. Steak here also good. Im glad that they open another location in eastside now, that is closer to me. 
Service is ok. One time when I came for the happy hour at the bar, the bartender gave me very uncomfortable service because he was too busy at that time. 
Overall is good!!!

Made reservations for 5 people at 8:15pm, my party and I went in and was greeted by a snobby hostes full of attitude like she doesnt want to be bothered. We waited for 45 minutes, standing in a corner. They didnt even bother to update us unless we asked. I asked one of the hostess and  caught her rolling her eyes coz I asked. The manager sees us and didnt even bother to say anything until we were seated 45 mins later. what a JOKE. These people were so overwhelemed. Bad service. IPUDDO is way better.

Udon is deep. I know that's not common knowledge but it is. The noodle here are served in mainly four styles: 1- hot 2- cold 3-Thin noodle 4-fat noodle

Amazing variation and high quality. Noodles are cooked perfectly-- deliciously chewy.

I usually order mentaiko or the shabushabu. 

You get to choose between normal portion and large portion for free too. 

Last but not least, great decor. Indigo, shibori patterned wall? Yes, please.

This place is definitely my favorite place for Udon in New York hands down.  I came here once for Sukiyaki Udon and another time for Wagyu Shabu Udon.  Both were tasty, but I didn't find the Sukiyaki Udon to be as filling compared to their udon with broth.  The service here is superb, and the portions are huge!  You can choose whether you want thin or thicker noodles, and whether you want regular or more noodles with no extra charge.  I got the   This place is quite popular , so be prepared for a short wait.

Great food and nice drinks. Creamy soup udon are really good and water cake is a must try dessert. Art inside the restaurant is great !!! Except the guy did not give my udan dish to go and instead threw it away . Bar Menu is really good and great service .

I keep editing this review, but I am just extremely disappointed. Until this place,  I had never experienced poor service in a Japanese restaurant.

They completely ruined a friends birthday with their terrible service. Please make no important plans here if you wish to enjoy.

All I have to say is this is the worst experience I have ever had in NYC. The customer service was atrocious,but at least the food was good.

Do yourself a favor and never come here. I will never return. One star is far better than this service deserves.

Living in Boston, I don't have an access to Tsrutontan. However, I know that there is in NYC due to local Japanese paper published in NYC but delivered to Boston. I was determined to try this when I was in NYC. The restaurant is pretty crowded so reservation was necessary. I had tatsuta chicken for appetizer and Tsrutontan original for main. Chicken was authentic and the "tare" was good.  Udon bowl was really big! Filling. Shrimp tenpura is authentic and good. Overall I was satisfied.

Always make a reservation! It takes all of two seconds and I've never gotten a table from just walking in off the street. 

I've now been here five times. Once for lunch and four times for dinner. I've tried all the udon soup bases they have and they're all delicious. The curry is much thicker than you would expect from udon noodles and the creme is so rich you might die before you finish. That being said it would be a happy death. I love the thick chewy noodles that are perfect coming in from a cold winter night. Or the cold udon with the thin noodles that are perfect during a warm spring lunch. 

The rice bowls are very cute and tiny, but I recommend if you're getting a cold udon for lunch. The cold udon soup base is very salty and the rice offsets it nicely.

Tsurutontan is a super solid udon destination. I have come here and few time and every time it's been a good experience. The most recent time I came I had the curry katsu udon and it was delicious! I was skeptical of a curry udon because it's tricky to get done right, but this one was really flavorful and the taste of the curry complimented the noodles and the katsu. The pork katsu was crispy and super tasty. I think the soup noodles are more worth it than the stir fried udon - the stir fry udon seems much smaller even though they're about the same price. It seeeems smaller but it's still pretty tasty for stir fried udon!

People aren't kidding when they say the bowls are huge! You definitely get what you pay for at this restaurant! 
For appetizers, my friends and I shared the Spicy Tuna Tartare Cones($12) and the Seared Salmon Sashimi($14). Both were delicious, although quite small in portion. For my dish, I ordered the Mentai Kamatama Udon ($18), which is a cold udon dish. It was creamy and had plenty of mentaiko caviar on top. The egg added a nice flavor and egg creaminess to it. A large bowl costs the same as a regular bowl, so obviously I got the large. I ordered the thick noodles, which I highly recommend because they are chewier and have a better texture. Overall, I would say that this place definitely won't let you down in terms of portion and in flavor. There are so many different udon dishes to choose from, you'll have to come back multiple times to try them!

I LOVE Tsurutontan. Everything here is delicious. I especially love the buns to start with, and the curry with thick noodles as a main dish. The Lady M cakes as dessert are also so good - the matcha green tea cake is so spongy and soft and melts in your mouth. The atmosphere is also so cute and fun, and the wait staff is so, so friendly. The only minor downside is that when I make a reservation, the table is never ready on time. However, the food is always worth the wait!

Im not a huge udon fan but I've enjoyed eating at Tsurutontan! I've been to the location in Hawaii and recently ate at their union square location for the first time.

First off, their menu is super extensive with quality photos so you know what you're ordering. Besides just udon, they also have rice bowls, sushi rolls, sashimi, and a number of appetizers! For the udon, you can order either small or large portion of noodles (same price!!) and either thin or regular udon. I ordered the sizzling sukiyaki udon with thin noodles and it was really good, especially since I'm not normally an udon person. The only downside was that there wasn't much meat

Overall, I'd probably be back to try other things on their menu! The prices are not terribly expensive (esp if you get the large portion) and they also have late night happy hour drink specials starting at 9 pm

Delicious! Entree portions are huge. Appetizers are meh.  

For those who care, THEY USE MSG. I asked the downtown location as well as the midtown. I was told that just the sushi dishes and the sizzling sukiyaki don't have msg. Everything else does.

Besides the grand entrance of this restaurant, the food is pretty great. The ramen is flavorful, extremely large, and might be impossible to finish in one sitting. During lunch, this place is packed and in the later dinner hours toward the end of happy hour, it's so hard to get a table but the best time to truly get here is around 5pm. The happy hour is just starting and all of the appetizers are great. I personally recommend the truffle sushi roll!

What's the point of making a reservation if you can't get seated on time? Made a reservation for 5 but had 1 person missing and was not allowed to get seated even though we all knew what we're ordering, both for appetizers and entrees, and was going to help the last person order. The restaurant was empty and no one was sitting or waiting for our reserved table. Really annoyed. The hostess said she'd ask her manager if we can get seated and she blatantly did not ask. Used to like this place and recommend it to everyone but this policy is ridiculous and completely unnecessary. Very disappointed.

Came to this Tsurutontan location for my birthday on Thursday evening after having a reservation for 6 people at 8 pm. Although I enjoyed the US Wagyu Shabu in Truffle Daishi that I ordered, the portions seemed small (it did not seem like we had gotten the extra noodles we had ordered....) and my friend's vegan sizzling sukiyaki udon was burnt! This in and of itself would not lead to a 1 star rating (I really hate giving those out), but our experience with the staff left a taste in my mouth worse than the burnt noodle residue.

Due to complications with people's work schedules, we had to change the reservations several times since they have a policy that you can't be seated unless your entire party is there. I have no issue with that policy, but I do have a problem with the attitude and pretentiousness that the wait staff had in treating us. By 8 pm, we had finalized our party to a party of 5 people, but they sat another group in front of us. Around 8:30 pm, I ask why we still had not been seated, and they said, in a very condescending manner, that since it was 15 minutes after our original reservation, they had to give away our spot. What baloney! First of all, we were on time for the original reservation, and secondly, none of this was communicated to us. I had to ask the hostesses repeatedly before they answered. I understand that it's late, they're tired, it was annoying to change the reservation, but it does not give them the right to be so rude! Our waiter was lovely, though when giving us the packed leftovers, he accidentally switched my order with my vegan friend's. Just overall, not a great experience and honestly, so unfortunate. I will not come here again.

If you have a big appetite and love udon, this is def a spot you should hit up. All those pictures of huge bowls of udon floating around instagram are all from here. Aside from the big portions of food are also actually great tasting broths and perfectly cooked udon. 

My friend and I tried the uni corn which is a thin fried wafer filled with caviar, avocado and fresh uni. I was impressed with the uni but i was disappointed to see that they filled a majority of the cone with avocado. It was just a little upsetting because it wasn't written anywhere that there was avocado in the cone. However it was still really good. I don't think I'll be getting it again but it was a great experience. For our main course, I got the uni creme broth with thin noodles and my friend got the truffle wagyu broth with thick noodles. Both were really good. It was so comforting and tasty. Each bite or sip filled our mouths with flavor. For the uni creme broth, there were only a few pieces of uni on top of a chicken creme broth. It was a better version of Campbell's cream of chicken soup. The wagyu-truffle broth was exploding with the truffle aroma which I loved. You can taste the truffle in each bite. However, you did not actually see any truffle shavings in the bowl. 

Each bowl of udon is gonna set you back roughly $20, but the portion of food you get for this price is well worth. We both left feeling extremely full and satisfied. I can't wait to come back and try other broths on the menu.

Terrible service! The food is good but they overbook so reservation times don't mean anything and they were disorganized as well as unapologetic....we had a terrible experience for a friends birthday dinner! If you want to have a nice dinner for a special occasion don't come to this restaurant!

Just an average bowl of udon in New York City with a big space filled with plenty of seatings and a stylish decor for an udon restaurant. Tsurutontan Udon Noodles is originally popular establishment in Tokyo, so visiting Japan before but not being able to try this place while we were out there, I was quite happy to hear when they first ever opened. Now I been here two times, second time was to give it another go and to try other things on the menu, but both times did not make me love the udon here... and normally I love udon noodles. Do they have a great large selection of udons and other Japanese food items on the menu? Yes. Are the bowls more ginormous than your head? Yes. But don't let that fool you, it's still the same portion serving as any other noodle shop in town but just in an unnecessary large bowl size.

Given the price point, this restaurant falls short in getting me to come back for the food here. The price is just not really worth it. Even the a5 wagyu sushi with uni isn't great. The wagyu was a super small thinly sliced beef with the teeniest skimped portion of uni I've ever seen in my life topped on a wagyu beef. For the bowls of udon, it's okay but something about the udon bowls here is missing a wow factor in their bowls. Just go to Raku or Udon West, yes their menu isn't as extensive nor fun looking but Raku will actually serve you very quality udon and Udon West is half the price of Tsurutontan but just as good maybe even better.

I came with a party of two and got seated fairly quickly. Our waiter was very helpful and informative about the extensive menu. I loved the ambiance of the place.

I got the duck udon. Noodles were well made. Portion size was generous (can ask for a regular or extra noodles... Same price). Duck pieces were not too fatty which I really appreciated.

I also had their salmon & blue crab roll, which was SO GOOD. I could be biased because those are my two favorite seafoods, but my boyfriend said the roll was good too so ...

I tasted my boyfriend's food. He got the curry deluxe. I was worried that the tempura would get soggy sitting in the curry sauce, but it stayed crunchy till the end of his meal. He also got karaage, which it was good but not my favorite.

Overall had a good experience.

We are regular customers and enjoy the meals.  The Udon dishes are fantastic.  However, we were absolutely disappointed with our last dining experience.  We asked for small soup spoons, but were told that it was against restaurant policy to supply small spoons for the soup bowls.  When we asked another waiter, we were told the same despite telling them we never had an issue previously with this request.  The poor customer service will prompt us to looks elsewhere as there are so many good alternatives in the neighborhood.

Got seats on crazy busy Friday. Could still chat with friends!

Went after work Friday night when everywhere else had 2+hour wait (its NYC, understandable). Surprisingly big space, so we put names down and went to the bar for 45 mins. Fun tasty cocktails. Despite how busy we could still hear and chat with friends!

Only meh for us was they couldn't pack our leftovers--they ran out of lids (??) for their boxes. Our food wasn't soup, it was the stir fry udon. We had half our portions left (which is a decent amount) and had to throw away. Kind of feel like a place that big with so many customers should've figured something out to rectify the situation. I wish I'd insisted they just give me 2 bottoms, foil, and plastic bag... I would've rigged that up myself! oh well. Would go back though.

* I updated my review but I hate hate how the manager responded and instead of address the issue and asking who was our server or what happened he brushed it off saying they will work on it. So are you implying all
Your servers suck...



I was really excited to try this place. The food was great but the experience in terms of service was horrible.

The hostess wasn't a very pleasant person given we came early but she just spoke in this tone that really agitated me. When someone says you will be seated in a couple of minutes I expect quick not asking us to go to the side.. which whatever I was also hangry so time felt slow. But even my friend who is very passive was annoyed by her demeanor it just wasn't a good start.

We sat down and the place is beautiful I'll give them that. When the the waitress came over she asked if we wanted to hear the story of the menu and we said no because well we already knew whet we wanted and she essentially made the executive choice to walk off and not let us tell her we were ready to order.

After she took our order she never checked on us nothing. She literally deserved a tip of zero I wish I just tipped the busboy who was clearing our table and trying to create a good experience.

I was excited for the tuna tartare cones you can pass on those.

I do recommend the sea jewel and the wagyu beef with uni.


I had the spicy mentai udon it was great you have a choice or the type of udon you want.

My friend got a creamy udon broth with uni the broth reminded me of clam chowder so meh.


If they did take out I would get it all the time because the food is great but the service leaves a lot to be desired for
Great restaurant! Reasonable price at Union Square. Recommended all appetizers. Also basic udon is really nice!

A one-of-a-kind udon place for sure! The bowls are HUGE and the portions are extremely generous. The noodles have a great flavor and texture. The broth was flavorful and comforting. We got greedy and ordered the large portion instead of the small and non of us finished. We suggest staying with the small portion unless you are starving.

FYI: Upgrading to the large size is free. Just do it.

WHAT I GOT: Sukiyaki Udon

PROS: I gotta give a shout out to this amazing broth. It's honestly one of the best things I've ever tasted. You really get a full umami experience without any of the heaviness that's usually associated with it. It's clear and it's super warming. Absolutely delicious. The udon noodles were cooked perfectly. You get a choice of thick or thin but definitely go for the thick. The chewiness makes the experience a lot better. The texture of the noodles were amazing, as well as the texture of everything else in my bowl. I waited to eat my egg at the end so I could pop the yoke in my ladle (yeah, they don't give you a normal spoon), and dip the rest of my noodles in it to coat them a bit in that flavor.

CONS: This isn't really a con, more like a heads up. So these bowls are HUGE. We talkin bigger than your head huge (see photo for reference). Like a small dog could probably fit in one. The upgrade is free but I honestly wouldn't upgrade unless you come in starving and this is gonna be the only thing you eat that day. Cause it will knock you out. In every possible good way.

Terrible service. the bartender named Henry was hitting on my girl the whole time. 
The soup was cold. Terrible wine. Overall a bad experience.

Such a unique menu here! Came here on a Friday night around 6:45pm with a friend. They told us the wait was ~30 minutes, so we sat at the bar and each got a drink. 

We got seated 45ish minutes later. Because I'm such a sucker for uni, I ordered the uni udon noodle soup, and my friend ordered a beef udon stir fry. We shared the seared wagyu sushi with uni ($24 for 2pcs). 

The wagyu/uni sushi came out first. It looked incredible -- the slice of beef was generously cut, with a small piece of uni on top and what seemed like a piece of broth jelly. I *love* seared sushi, and this was pretty good, but the beef itself was a little difficult to chew. I didn't think it was worth $12/piece.

The uni udon was amazing. It was a creamy broth with 5 slices of uni on top, masago, and shiso. I LOVED the combination. Definitely a dish I'll remember!

They serve you the ramen in a huge bowl with a huge spoon -- this is interesting at first but ultimately the actual portion is pretty normal.

Service was great as well. All around a solid spot that sushi/noodle lovers should try in NY.

I'd like to start by reviewing the food, because it was SPECTACULAR. Armed with solid advice from a friend who recently came for dinner, I ordered the L version of the Wagyu beef with truffle broth and the thin udon noodles. The broth was divine, the beef was tender and melt-in-the-mouth deliciousness and the noodles were magic. Oh, and don't skip the tuna sashimi app that everyone raves about - that too, will make your tastebuds sing. If I were reviewing the food alone, it would be 5 stars. 

...also the green tea cake slice + green tea ice-cream was the perfect way to end our meal. 

Now for....the less loved bits of my visit. When you walk-in, you may wonder if you've stumbled onto a club and not a restaurant. The loud pounding club music (which gets louder in the bathroom, weirdly enough) and the very loud + very drunk customers at the bar on a Thursday night, might throw you off. The bartender (at least) was nice enough to warn me that I nearly ordered a $68 glass of whisky (say, what?) and I opted for another, less expensive version. 

Then we were seated in a booth, where the cushions were completely sunken in, so it was hard to get comfortable. I also wanted to order a 2nd drink, and the server told me to wait 20 mins until happy hour - and he never came back to ask what I wanted. Then we switched servers and he seemed more obsessed about clearing dishes than asking if we wanted to order anything else. 

Come for the food, and if there's any option to be tucked away, where it's quieter (so you're not yelling at your friend to talk), I'd highly suggest it.
Highly recommend the US Wagu and Mushroom Sukiyaki!! Got 2 large bowls of udons and shared it with 3 people. The broth was super delicious drank the whole thing!!
Great udon. Clean place. Giant portions.  Has the Tsurutontan udon, and some spicy tuna to start the rice with the tuna  was the bomb. The udon wa great. Ill be back.

Hands down my favorite udon restaurant in New York. Upon entering with another friend, we were greeted by friendly staff who sat us down within 5 minutes. The space is quite sheik, modern, and clean. The waiters were extra generous and explained the menu to us and made recommendations based on what most people like. You can have your udon hot/cold, thin/thick noodles, and either a small/large portion at no extra  charge. I decided to get an udon with wagyu beef and truffle oil (small); the broth was so refreshing, noodles were perfectly tender, and the amount of food they give you is just enough to get you satisfied. I haven't tried any stir fried or cold noodles yet, but I will definitely be coming back to try more!

i first went to the midtown location which i really liked too. 

this one is also just as great! but i love their lunch special here. my husband and i came for the lunch special. now, i am a huge salmon sushi lover. HUGE. so when i saw that they had a salmon lunch special with udon i jumped at it. 

salmon lunch special: SO WORTH IT. i left feeling so full and satisfied. the sushi was so fresh and the udon hit the spot. it all was just a perfect lunch. 

katsu curry udon: great classic taste of curry and udon.
This place is great! Very good design, spacious, we didn't have to wait long though we came during the "rush hour". The food is amazing and the portions are huuuge!

Amazing noodles and price. Totally worth it. Can't even describe it. TRY IT NOW! It was about $19 for a HUGE bowl of noodles and you can tell the noodles were hand drawn. The noodles alone had very great flavor and texture, not mushy and chewy, nor hard and stiff like packed ramen. The bowl came with lots of meat and vegetables that would leave one unable to walk out of the restaurant, yet unforgettably tasty! I do not regret inhaling this 10,000 calorie meal!
Favorite udon place in the east coast! Every thing on the menu is authentic. Noodles are so chewy and the broth is amazing. Uni udon is the best.

The place is overrated. What surprised me is that it's actually not a traditional humble udon place. The decor is actually kinda nice. And they play fast pop music, which is kinda loud. First of all the bowls are huge, you have to sit up to eat, which could be tiring. The food portion is on the large side, but not actually that large. The sukiyaki broth is too sweet. The beef is like a little ball instead of thin slices. It's just a very simple dish. Not much to it. And the spicy tuna cone, not sure why it's so popular. It is just ok. Ps. There is avocado on the bottom. And it's 20+ for udon, kinda pricey. If you care about Decor, go. If u just want good, real udon, go to raku or udon west.

Tsurutontan Udon is DELICIOUS. Let me tell you about the uni flavored udon. It was so creamy, tastes like the ocean (acquired taste not for everyone), and rich with flavor. I highly recommend it if  you love seafood as much as I do. The depth of flavor that the noodles absorbed was just delicious that I couldn't stop eating. If you have the stomach for it I definitely recommend trying more flavors and definitely get the extra noodles!

Really wanted to check out this place after watching Mike Chen's udon noodles video.

I came here with a friend who says she loves this place. First off, we both noticed that the service was exceptionally slow that night for whatever reason. The wait time was about 30 minutes and our noodles took forever to arrive as well. 

To start off, I had an asian pear mojito. I don't think this turned out so well as there wasn't very much mint flavor and basically zero asian pear flavor. It basically tasted like lime juice with alcohol and a little sugar thrown in.

We ordered the soy garlic fried chicken appetizer, which came out promptly. This was sooooo delicious -- the chicken was hot and crispy and had a nice salty, garlicky flavor. It came with some tangy sauce which I thought really accentuated all the flavors.

I also ordered a large Tsurutontan Deluxe. The size of the bowl is actually a bit intimidating, although I surprisingly managed to finish the majority of the noodle bowl. I think I was a bit underwhelmed by the udon noodle bowl, not that is was particularly bad, but there was just a little too much going on flavor-wise. It was also a tad on the sweet side for me. I also didn't like how the tempura was completely soaked in the broth, which kind of defeated the purpose of frying it in the first place. 

Overall I'd give this place a 3.5/5, and I'm only rounding up to 4 because the fried chicken appetizer was so good.

I love coming here, it always hits the exact right spot..... and more often than not, I'll need a two-hour nap to help digest. They offer legit udon noodles in a variety of broths; my go-to is the curry udon deluxe, thick noodles, small amount. This is usually more than enough, but if I'm feeling fat kid status, I'll tack on an extra donburi (for only a few bucks more!). Usually the yellowtail. Or the fried chicken. Mostly yellowtail actually.

Kinda pricey but what do you expect, they occupy the same space that priced out Union Sq Cafe.... so don't be surprised. 

I'm here for lunch weekly, if that vouches for anything. I'm actually here right now awaiting my aforementioned choices.

Come alone, sit at the counter, drool over Yelp user photos of the food. Be a cool kid like me.
