Made us wait at the bar for 15 minutes and then sat down when there clearly were plenty of tables. We ordered and then the waitress told us last call before our food even arrives. So did they think their food was going to be perfect? 

Ordered the sizzling pot which was way too salty. We asked if they can modify and they said they couldn't because the kitchen was closed... 

We also ordered the chicken don. This was also way too salty but we couldn't tell them again, could we? 

Anyways horrible experience.

The food here was pretty good. We ordered the spicy tuna, tan tan udon, salmon garlic sashimi, sashimi salad and some snow-crab salmon roll.  Udon broth was superb!The large was huge and good enough to split into 4 small bowls. I usually dip my sushi pieces in spicy mayo, but I didn't even have to with that roll. 

The only downside was if you order at the table your not allowed to order anything at the bar for happy hour and they also charge $1.50 for a side of spicy mayo.

Came here last night with a friend and left happy. I ordered the wagyu-truffle with thick udon noodles and my friend ordered the uni creame with thick noodles. The broth for the wagyu-truffle was super flavorful and the udon noodles were chewy, perfect for slurping. My only complaint is that I wish the dishes came out warmer. 
My udon came out room temperature and was cold by the time I was close to finishing. Will definitely come back again to try!

First time here;  menu on-line is not quite the same as in the restaurant.  For instance, seared wagyu sushi is on the on-line menu but not on the menu in the restaurant.  Also, ordered the uni ikura hotate udon and on the menu it looks like it has multiple pieces of uni, which I was really looking forward to.  However, it came with only a single tiny sliver of uni, so the menu completely misrepresented the dish.  I was saddened since they charge so much for it.  Broth was too salty, too.  Another member of my party ordered the donburi;  we're used to donburi coming with warm rice, but here it was cold.   I guess that's a small thing compared to the uni.  Overall a bit disappointed, though.

Do you like udon? Do you like toilet bowl sized portions? Then you'll love Tsurutontan.

Nevermind the higher end prices, the bowls are huge here. Only opt for large since "regular" and large are the same price. Anyhow, this here is comfort food taken to a fancier level. You can do thick or thin noodles but I say thick for hot and thin for cold. Any of their "top seller" udons are good but their wagyu and truffle udon is definitely a must try. The wagyu beef practically melts in your mouth and the soup is amazing. The tsurutontan deluxe is just a hodgepodge of everything so it's a safe option if you don't know what else to try. 

All in all, it's a solid option for udon if you're willing to pay $20ish for a bowl and even if there's a wait, there's union square to explore and walk around so it's not all that bad.
Very average and overpriced. Do not get the tuna tartare - it was not fresh, super fishy and $28! I told the waitress and she did not care or acknowledge.

Uni udon is so good. I am definitely going back for that. They have small or large portions for the same price, which I think is a cool concept. I split the large with a friend and we also had a roll. It was weekday lunch happy hr so we each got a draft beer for $1.99.

I went there with a friend and we both loved the food.  Also, I found my favorite cake there - green tea crepe cake.  Everything's a bit over priced but it's NYC.
4 /5 because service was a bit behind... overall, great experience!
The ramen was huuuuuuge but they are so good. I got the curry deluxe - exactly what I was looking for on a cold winter day. Appetizer really fresh and nice too

For New York, this place a is a solid 4 stars, but coming from Boston, this place would have been 5. We were warned that the wait would be long, but I guess we just got lucky. We were seated once we entered, although it was pretty late for lunch (around 2pm on a Saturday). But even if there was a wait, it would have been worth it. Their udon noodles were perfectly chewy, and you even had the option to choose between thick or thin noodles. They come in deceptively large bowls with giant metal spoons, but honestly, it wasn't that much food. It's filled probably halfway, and there was a lot of broth. I got the wagyu beef udon with truffle, and it was so flavorful. The truffle flavor was strong but not too overpowering, and the beef was soft and tender. I personally prefer thin noodles, and these udon noodles were soo good. I definitely recommend trying this bowl, or the Tsurutontan Deluxe that my friend got. At some point, my bowl felt like it was just too much meat, but the deluxe had a good variety of everything - tempura, veggies, etc. If we had the stomach, we would have tried some appetizers and the curry udon too, but I guess we'll just have to come back the next time we're in NYC.

Honestly this place is not that special.... their udon taste like regular udon . It's just served in a huge bowl. But the worse part is ... their larger bowl still serves one person portion but you pay more than the regular bowl... super disappointed .. too hyped by the media!!
But I like their appetizer, the pepper dish was nicely done.  But I'm unlikely to visit again

Like the food here, the udon is good and they have my favorite oyako don but what is the point of having reservations when they make you wait for your table for an excessive length of time? Every time I've gone I've had a booking but I'm never seated right away. Last time we waited for our 3-top for 45 minutes. It's ridiculous.

I waited 'til coming here a second time before writing a review just to make sure that this place, which floored me the first time around, was in fact a 5 star experience and it sure as heck delivered again.  I knew before I even went the first time that it was gonna be good because my sister, who never goes to a restaurant twice, agreed to have dinner with me here. Let's get to it then.

The service was timely and respectful, and the space was generous yet cozy.  There a lot of different nooks, that you could be seated in which gives you a sense of privacy where ever you're seated. They take reservations via Resy (you need an account), but definitely worth doing it as it gets busy during prime time.

Food: I wanted literally everything but my stupid human body would never allow that.  Yes, the bowls are big, and yes the you get the same bowl whether you get regular or large but they do fill up the "large" order more than the regular in the bowl.

Here are the things I've tried ranked from best to not as good:
- Hot and Sour Udon ($22): Holy heck such a perfect combo of hot, sour, savoury and richness, decked with beef and mushroom.
- Pork Belly Spicy Tantan Udon ($24): So decadent with such a generous helping of pork belly. I couldn't move after devouring this. 
- Braised Eggplant ($8): Yummmmm, savoury yet slightly sweet with a soft, almost buttery texture. Highly recommended.
- Maitake mushrooms ($11): I think they added extra truffle flavoring, they MUST have. Such umami, such char, much happy.
- Tsuruton Deluxe Curry ($24): So rich, so tasty. I know you'll want to drink all the curry but don't. Really. Your stomach will thank you for it.
- Seared Salmon Sashimi ($14): I mean, you can't got wrong with seared salmon slices.
- Water Cake ($8): It was fine. Fun to try at least once given how unique it is but, it's nothing to write home about.
- Corn Fritter (sp?) ($8): Forgettable.

I found Tsurutontan on the Seated app and am so glad I gave it a try. I got the sukiyaki udon and it was soo delicious. You can opt for a bigger or smaller portion and it will cost the same so naturally I got the bigger portion of noodles and was able to take some home. I definitely can't wait to come back and try some other stuff on the menu!

We went here on a weekday around 5:15ish and there were already a lot of people. We got seated fairly quick. The service here was excellent. This was my first time here so the waiter explained everything and gave several suggestions. Upgrading to a large bowl of udon is free so I suggest that a hungry person should get a large bowl.

I got the large spicy tan tan udon and the soy garlic chicken. The soy garlic chicken was ok, but a little too salty for me. The tan tan udon was delicious. It wasn't spicy to me as I love spicy food. The large actually had a lot of noodles. I couldn't finish the entire bowl. 

Overall, this is a great restaurant for udon. I would recommend people to come here for udon and come hungry since the large bowl is very filling.

Man. I really didn't want to have to write this review but  here goes nothing.

There was a bone in my sushi. I ordered the salmon lovers lunch special and the first sashimi I eat has a bone in it. I didn't feel like eating the rest of it because I didn't want anymore bones! I now have a fear of getting bones in my sushi, thanks guys.

What was really upsetting was that I complained and they didn't do anything to help me. They gave me ice cream which already came with the set. It ruined my entire day! I didn't eat like 50% of my meal! I really wish this was handled differently.

It's a shame because what I did eat was really good and I was enjoying my meal before I bit into the bone. But there's no way I'm going back.

Delicious but here's what happened in one hour: spilled beer all over me with no acknowledgement from the staff and foil in my soup. They replaced it but no acknowledgement of that as well. I hate this place right now.

This is my go-to udon place in the city. The noodles never disappoint, flavorful broth, amazing texture on the udon, all served in a ridiculously oversized bowl. Recently I decided to try the thin noodles, and I have to say I might like them more than the thick noodles. The thick noodles have a good bite to them, so go for that if you're looking for traditional udon. If you're feeling like comforting broth with noodles that take a bit less work to get through, the thin noodles are great. I liked everything I've tried on their menu, but the wagyu truffle udon is my favorite. Highly recommend if you're in the area and looking for a hearty, steaming hot bowl of noodles.

Been here 3 times now and have to say that the udon is delicious. Do not get the thin noodles. It's udon you want here.

My all time favorite is the curry udon with tempura shrimp and katsu. It's a huge bowl of food that will keep you satisfied for 24 hrs. You probably shouldn't eat the whole thing but sometimes I just can't help myself. A couple of my friends have gotten the creamy udons such as mentai and truffle but have said that it's a bit too much.

Last night I came here for udon but found out they had happy hour. $1.99 Sapporos from 9-close! You really can't find that anywhere these days. They also have some great app deals during happy hour. We got the hamachi sashimi which was delicious. We also got the soy garlic karaage which was nicely fried but a bit salty. We got the spicy tuna cones which were good. The fired corn was a lot of batter so I could only eat one. The edamame was a nice palate cleanser. We ended up taking some food home because we couldn't finish it all. You could easily have a huge meal here during happy hour with drinks for ~$60. Great deal!

Service and food was sub standard. I asked for hot green tea and got lukewarm hoji tea.  Their karaage chicken was a rip off of korean fried chicken chain, KyoChon but no were close to the taste.  But the most disappointing part of the meal was their udon.  They got the noodle texture close to right but the base was overly salty and could not taste the bonito base and ruin the whole meal.

Came here again the other day and it's just as good as I remembered it to be! Literally no wait time on a Monday around 130 pm. They offer set lunches but I just wanted a nice big bowl of udon in broth. I got one of their top sellers: Spicy Ton Tan Udon (Spicy and creamy sesame broth, ground pork, and chili oil) for $20. There's not much topping - just the ground pork but the broth was amazing and the udon was the perfect texture. For the same price you could ask for a bigger portion but the regular was just perfect for someone who can't eat a lot.  My friend got the regular Tsuruton curry deluxe ($24) and she had to take a third of it home cause it came with a lot of toppings.

This review is for the unauthorized charges to my credit card by this restaurant. I ordered both at the bar and at the dining room when seating opened up. Attached is a screenshot of both charges as they appear on my credit card as well as paper receipts of the customer copies I saved. The amount for the bar tab was correct but I was charged over double the amount for my dining room tab. KEEP YOUR RECEIPT AND CHECK YOUR STATEMENT. I am now going through a dispute process with my bank.

Edit: The management from the restaurant reached out to me to refund the incorrect amount back to my credit card. They explained that they had made an error when entering the tip amount and added an extra digit. I appreciate their response to correct the issue.

This is my #1 happy hour spot in the area. Awesome drinks specials ALL DAY and very reasonably priced happy hour apps. My go to is their strong and refreshing $4 lychee martinee (until 6pm/8:30p-close) and their plentiful serving of tasty fried soy garlic chicken for $9.

The venue has tons of bar area seating for the happy hour. It is classy enough to go with friends, clients, or romance. The servers are a bit thin at the front so dont expect fast waiter turnaround during a happy hour rush unless you seat directly at the bar. So far thats the only qualm I've had. Otherwise the waiters and bartenders are very nice.

Great food, amazing happy hour drink prices, and good service. I cant wait to go for dinner. This place is a winner in my book.
I order the cold noodle becuz I were craving with Udon! It is really authentic, fresh, and sooooo yummy

My first experience eating here. The place has a great atmosphere. I ordered the lamb and organic mushrooms amazing. The place was busy. The reason for only
Three stars. My French Martini was not served in a proper martini glass but a small gimlet glass and was
weak. The service was mediocre at best.
My dry stir fried noodle was heavenly. Chicken sukiyaki buns were awesome. Service was excellent. Waiter was especially helpful in recommendations especially when I was with 2 kids.

I think of this place on rainy days or when I feel under the weather. What better to soothe my insides than their hot creamy udon broth? They have many new additions to their menu and will accommodate really any taste bud. Pick from their wide variety of appetizers and of course udon. Their sashimi appetizers are very fresh and very delicately put together. Their udon variety is very impressive and even offers two types of noodles - normal thick (thicker than normal udon noodles I'd say) and thin (almost like Shanghai noodles which thicken the soup more than normal thick noodles). I absolutely love the Spicy Pork Belly Tan Tan Udon. More than the pork belly itself, I love the scent and depth of the pork belly flavor in addition to the spicy tan tan broth. I've had the regular Spicy Tan Tan Udon in the past and it was quite not up to par. I love the ambiance of the restaurant and the staffs are very professional. On busy days or peak hours, I'd recommend making a reservation in advance.

Everything about this place is huge. Huge menus, huge selection, huge bowls of udon. Although it is incredibly filling because of how gigantic the servings are, the food quality is pretty average. 

You can choose between thick and skinny noodles and regular or large portion of noodles (same price). They recommend skinny noodles with cold broth. Even if you get the regular portion of noodles, it still comes in a big bowl.

I got the seafood jjigae udon which came with a couple of shrimps, scallops and clams. The broth was quite spicy! It was a reliable and good bowl of udon but not so amazing or unique that I would wait a long time for.

Surprisingly wasn't blown away by this Udon place (contrary to the hype from Youtube vloggers who raved about it). I got in for a late lunch around 3:30PM as a party of two and there wasn't a wait. The servers were attentive to us, quick to take our order, and kind enough to explain how you can upgrade to the larger bowl at no additional cost. I got the Nabeyaki udon while my friend got the Sukiyaki udon; we both chose to get thick noodles and larger bowl upgrade. Looking at the menu again now, I realize they didn't actually put in the Anago (eel) in my Nabeyaki udon! I only had a few pieces of the chicken, two shrimp tempuras, and some mushroom. The egg was hidden below the noodles. I would say taste-wise, the udon was solid/average and the texture of the noodles are commonplace. The bowls that are served are HUGE along with the spoons, but it didn't feel like I had an insurmountable or even "extra" serving of food.
Lovely food would definitely come back for seconds!! The portion sizing was big and good for a warm dish. I was able to enjoy food and drinks for happy hour!

Came in early for dinner during their happy hour which finished at 6pm, ordered appetisers which we don't usually do but because it was cheaper we did and very glad we did! We had the pork buns which were delicious, and the shrimp dumplings which had just the right amount of heat punch! I had the Lycheetini which was very nice and quite strong. The duck and meatball Udon with the larger noodles was absolutely delicious, glad we got the Large at no extra price!! The atmosphere was very nice for our last night in NY and the decor was very very nice too! Would definitely go back if I had the chance!
Fantastic noodles and ramen. Great for family events or lunch. Reservations are done on Resy. The biggest spoons and bowls I've ever used. Good sushi too.

I'm sad because of their services and staff, not because of their food. 

I ordered beef bun, cucumber salad, and US wagyu sukiyaki udon. 

The cucumber salad was fine, nothing to comment. It just cucumber. The beef bun was cold, i should I should be a hot beef in the bun, but it was cold. Maybe it should be like this? IDK 

The Sukiyaki Udon has a great taste. BUT! BUT, I got a bug on my poached egg! I told a waitress and I would like a full replace of my noodles. She only took the egg away, and gave me a new egg. I was like: what?! 

Isn't that normal for restaurant if you have Themis kinda of issue, you would either replace the full dish or cover the price?

The food here is great and this is one of the places I always take my friends from out of town when they visit. Not anymore. The manager was completely unprofessional to my group of friends and she purposely made our experience there uncomfortable. They would not give us her name except that some initials of AL or EL. 

We came with a big group of friends for a reservation and 4 of us came late. The group sat down first without us. We in no way were excusing our tardiness but it's NYC, things happen. There was a four top available next to our group of friends but they were insistent in placing us in a completely different section. When asking the manager why we couldn't sit at the table or even in the same section next to our friends, she could not give us a good answer. We knew something weird was going on and finally just had to ask her if she was punishing us for being late. She said yes!! Who in the world does that? What happened to customer service? She did not care about us having a great experience there at all. It was so unprofessional and we have never been treated like this at any restaurant in our lives! We had to just leave. They lost us as customers and we will never take our friends here again.

My favorite udon place. The broth is amazing, it's light and flavorful. Free udon upgrade.

I will definitely come back here. You can come here everyday and have a different type of udon.

Amazing meal here! Found the spot on Yelp when I was looking for a great noodle spot. Their udon dishes are their specialty! You can even pick whether or not you want thick or thin udon, and they do small or large size dishes for the same price. I went ahead and did a large w/ US wagyu beef. Super flavorful. And the chocolate cake was great too

I was brought here by a couple friends as a celebration for getting a new job. the food here is great! the atmosphere and ambiance are also very nice. will definitely bring people to come try as well. I got the uni cream udon and drank all the soup!

I've been eyeing this place for a while and finally got to try it recently and I loved it! I love the price, the amount of food, and the quality of it as well. First of all, they give you the same price for udon noodles for small or large. So of course, you go with the large! Also, they have happy hour times so you can score a few discounts on some select appetizers like we did. The spicy tuna tartare was very yummy and had a good kick - only $9 at happy hour price ($12 originally). The tsurototan deluxe had a bit of everything in it - chicken, assorted tempura, etc. The broth was excellent. The creamy uni udon could use a little more uni flavor in it, but I must say the broth for that was great too. It isn't too thick and creamy where you can't drink it as you would think. The uni itself tasted okay and they really didn't give you that many pieces. I've had creamy uni udon where I actually can taste a lot of the uni, so this sorta failed my expectations in that regard. However, it was still good and I enjoyed it! They also have $4 lychee martini and $2 sapporo beers during happy hour so take advantage of that! 
Their restaurant is also pretty huge, so I don't think you'll have to worry too much about a long wait or anything. They're also on Seated (an app to make reservations on and receive cashback) so take advantage of the cash back they offer there!

Yo, this is a good udon spot. I was skeptical at first because it seemed like a fancy restaurant that expanded past udon and served small plates and alcohol, but I stand corrected. My friend and I ordered the wagyu beef and truffle oil udon, and we both loved it! (Well, I think she loved it. I definitely loved it.) It started with a fragrant truffle aroma when the ginormous bowl of udon arrived at our table. Taste of the truffle was initially subtle but gradually started building on top of each other, and I left really happy because of such a fantastic bowl of flavor. The beef was cooked just right - you still saw hints of pink when the bowl arrived. Amount of noodles for the regular sized bowl was just right for me. Our server kindly informed us that the amount of noodles is included in the price, so if you want the large size (aka more noodles), sure why not. Texture of the udon was also great, not too chewy but also didn't fall apart when I ate it. Definitely craving some right now...
The bowls are bigger than your face.  If you're an exception, I'll need proof please.  Maybe they should also sell bowls...

I came here for lunch with a friend. The place seems fairly big. There were couple of people waiting even though they were empty seats...maybe make a reservation just in case? I'm not sure how it changes for dinner but for lunch there were several combos and sets that looked nice. The wait time for the food to come out was a bit long. I loved the cream udon. It wasn't salty or too creamy. It was perfectly my style. People were nice, the place was clean, the food was good.

Excellent weekday sit down lunch option. Service was quick, food was delicious and there's plenty of space so not a huge wait to get seated. Lunch menu offers their most popular udons at discounted prices. 

Note that they are really strict with the policy of not seating you until the whole party is present. It seemed a bit unnecessary to make the three of us wait by the door for the last person in our party to show up especially since we arrived when the restaurant opened at noon and literally every table was empty.
Best ramen I've had!! Love the tantanmen udon so spicy and flavorful!! The portions are huge and you can get more noodles for free if you prefer. I would make a reservation, if does fill up quick!

We got to restaurant at 8:30pm. They finally took our order 20 min later.  Sushi was brought at least 40 min later.  Followed by a cold udon soup that was supposed to be hot.

We also ordered a wagyu beef uni sushi which was brought out completely raw and inedible.  Please see photos.

Management is terrible. We nicely complained and nothing was done.

Stay away or go to ippudo.

Came in for dinner and was given a very uncomfortable table.  Politely asked the waitress to be reseated and was told by the hostess "take it or leave".   

When my udon finally came it was cold.  I guess the waitress decided to take revenge.  Complaining did absolutely nothing.  I was told that the udon is served at that temperature, while i observed everyone else's soups were steaming hot.

Absolutely worst food and service ever. Stay away.

This is a great restaurant. The interior is unique and the ambiance is perfect for any occasion. The menu has photos which is super helpful when ordering. Also the happy hour is insane - $3.99 lychee-tinis!! So tasty. I would advise to make a reservation. I came here for dinner on a Monday at 7:30 pm with a party of four and the restaurant was nearly full. They don't seat you until the whole party has arrived. We ordered sushi which was delicious and my other friend ordered a beef noodle dish. Note that the regular sizes of the soups are HUGE! I would come here again!

This place will be packed on the weekend, so definitely try to make a reservation before coming. My friends and I had a reservation here on a Saturday night recently. Despite how crowded the restaurant was, service was still pretty fast. 

For an appetizer, I shared the spicy tuna tartare cones with a friend. They were delicious! The tuna was fresh and the cones were nice and crispy. Sort of wish I just ordered a bunch of those instead of the duck udon I got for my entree because I thought the duck udon was just average. My friends who got wagyu shabu udon in truffle dashi really enjoyed their meals though. Even though we all chose the "large" option for our udon, the bowls were only half filled, but it was enough food anyway. 

Taste | 4
Atmosphere | 4
Presentation | 3.5
Service | 3.5
OVERALL | 4

It's hard not to like Tsurutontan! The extensive menu has something for everyone, and everything is pretty good to boot. I've had multiple dishes  and the standouts were the pork belly spicy tantan udon and the U.S. wagyu and mushroom sukiyaki - both in the signature gigantic bowls of course. If you come with a group, it invariably turns into a contest of seeing who can finish their massive bowl of udon and soup.

The Union Square branch is located in a huge space, so wait times are usually on the shorter side. Take advantage of the happy hours if you can!! A ton of the (still extensive) food menu is reduced, but you can also get $2-$4 beers, $4 lycheetinis, and $8 cocktails! DRINKS FOR EVERYONE!

Came to this restaurant on a Sunday afternoon and was disappointed. Of the 6 plates on our table, 3 of them were dirty with a sticky substance. When the waters came out one of the cups was really dirty and we sent back.  They allow you to pick your noodle size, and they're prices are the same with a large and small (small comes with a side). They brought out bowls for us and 4 of the 6 were dirty. When the food came out, it was mediocre, the soup didn't have much taste (kinda just tasted like water), and the noodles kinda bland.

Came here to try the uni udon - got both the creamy one and the dashi one. We also got the mushroom truffle cream. The cream broths are a little on the heavy side so it was hard to finish the whole thing. I like the thinner udon more than the thick. The thin udon in the dashi broth was perfectly chewy and light but a little on the salty side maybe because of the ikura. 


We also made it for happy hour while we were waiting for our table. We ordered hotate sashimi (super fresh and sweet), corn tempura (not that great), Hamachi carpaccio (nothing impressive), and fried oysters (good). We got $4 Asahi drafts!
Tried the wagyu and truffle udon. Soups good. Some of them a bit salty. But not something to write home about unfortunately

Had the grilled maitake mushrooms and the Wagyu Donburi. Both delicious! Very friendly staff, and got our meals fairly quickly considering how busy it was. Recommend getting a reservation for late night seatings. Also, watch your head if you're sat downstairs, hahaha. I wasn't as careful

Being from Florida, I was freezing in New York LOL so udon sounded amazing to help warm us up! 

We came during a special where they were doing $4 lycheetinis which were both yummy and strong! 

I decided to get the curry udon, which I enjoyed! But wowowwww portions are huge. And how can you not order a large since it's the same price?! 

Everyone seemed to really like their dishes! And we all rolled ourselves out of the restaurant after we finished our meals LOL

Note: kitchen doesn't open til 5pm for dinner! We came here around 4pm and got some small bites and drinks while we waited. They have all day happy hour prices on the appetizers, but that menu is also available in the main dining area. 

At the bar we got: scallop sashimi, wagyu, and sukiyaki buns. Everything was delicious, although I would probably pass on the sukiyaki buns because the sukiyaki meat was just OK. The wagyu and uni combination is really good but the wagyu meat was very oily. 

For dinner we split the large version of duck udon. Especially after the apps, we were absolutely stuffed and couldn't finish the bowl! The soup was incredibly flavorful - maybe the best I've had for udon. There were a mix of duck meatballs and slices of duck meat in the soup.
Good restaurant to go. Donburi udon is astonishingly large. Skinny udon is good for yaki soba, fried noodles. But it's too weak for broth udon.

Big bowls of Udon caught our attention from our Facebook YouTube vloggers. 

We tried to fit this in to our crazy NYC weekend food schedule. So we had this at around 5pm for "dinner" right before our flight. 

I guess it didn't help that we were kinda full and also in a rush.  To be fair the Udon was pretty good but for the price  I expected a bit more. 
Also service seemed a bit slow but I think it was the time of the day that threw the server off. 

So I ordered the duck Udon in thin noodles and the wife ordered the curry Udon in regular size noodles. Her curry was really flavourful and the Udon had a nice chew to it. My duck was pretty good too but I didn't get too many pieces. I guess the noodle bowls allowed for a nice photo moment hah

Came here on Memorial Day weekend. No line at 1pm so we went in right away. The food wasn't as good as it first opened. The portion is smaller than before. The service is not as good as before as well. The waitress just put down water loudly on my table for no reason. When she introduce the menu for my sis (first time comer), she just recited her line without any passion. We will not come back for sure. Sad :(

I would love to give this place a good review but the waiter was so obviously told to sell, sell,sell. He even told us that something wasn't on the menu because it was less expensive than what he showed us. It gets to be too much and then takes the pleasure out of eating st an expensive restaurant.

It's good but it's not as special or amazing as I expected with all those great reviews. Convenient spot with some subway lines at walking distance (union square). The service is good and staffs are all generally really friendly and helpful. They are also very attentive and the food didn't take too long of a wait even with all those people. The plating of the food is okay, the tastes are good, quality decent but could be even more detailed. Nice bites and satisfying but if you are looking for a high end Japanese place where you focus more on the texture, tastes, and visual experience as to a decent and filling meal this will not hit the spot. If you are craving udon or Japanese food that's more home style with a bit of creativity but nothing crazy, you'd find this place pretty wholesome. Decent prices and good amount of selections for food and drinks. Some desserts as well. I'd say it's a cool place to check out. Good for family, kids, or a date but it's not going to be my go-to spot. I don't mind coming back again to give other things on the menu a try but it's definitely not my favourite and nothing too memorable. Personally, the interior is nice and atmosphere is good but in an artistic point of view..as nice and modern as the interior and decorations are, it's just doesn't fit the whole experience and atmosphere right. It's fine if it's a bit modern and a bit traditional (lots of places are starting to do that and it's a genuinely cool concept) but some decorations or the furnitures the choose is more western and the other side of the room is not modern Japanese style with a hint of traditional sense. The staffs and whole feel is more traditional so it doesn't match all that great but that's just me being particular about my interior design fitting with the whole atmosphere. Otherwise, there's nothing wrong with it and I know from some reviews..people actually like the decorations and interior design

I decided to come here with my friends after my friend Eva, recommended it for the $3.99 lychee martinis for the anniversary special. Y'all, they have $3.99 lychee martinis and $1.99 Sapporo drafts ALL DAY Saturday/Sunday at the bar! They also have happy hour specials after 9 pm at the dining room. Definitely worth it if you guys are nearby. 

Anyway, we made a reservation for 7:15 on Saturday evening for 4 people (also easy to do through Resy). The service was decent, and the food was pretty decent as well. They have the same price for both the regular and large bowls. So...definitely recommend the large bowl for people who can eat a lot. I ordered the #1, the Tsurutontan special that comes with tempura--I got the tempura on the side since I don't like my tempura soggy. For $21, it's a lot of food. Recommend sharing a large bowl with 2 girls and maybe getting an appetizer. I eat a decent amount of food and couldn't finish my noodles or all of the tempura. Would come again to try out some of the happy hour appetizers/small plates! They also serve sushi but I didn't have anything other than the udon bowl so not sure how their sushi tastes. Also they have dessert of Lady M crepe cakes and various other stuff if you guys are into that.

I wanted to celebrate my birthday here, but it was a complete disaster and turns a happy day into a stressful one. 

I emailed the restaurant a month before my birthday and reserved a table for 20. The day before I called and updated final count to 17. At the time of the event, at first they said there wasn't a reservation (apparently one manager didn't talk to another one). Then after I showed them the emails I had with one of their managers, they refused to show us to our table unless the full party was there. It was ridiculous. For a large party like this, how could they expect every one to arrive exactly at the same time? It was very chaotic. After almost everyone texted me that they were there, I spent another 10 minutes going through the crowds at the bar, on the street, near the entrance and calling to find everyone. 

Finally after grabbing all 15 people standing right there next to the hostess, she said she still couldn't give us the table because we are 2 people short (they were supposed to join late). She said we had to wait until those two people get here. I told them they were going to join us a little later, but we can started ordering immediately because we were all very hungry (at this point they already caused a 30 minutes delay after our reservation time). However, she just wouldn't let us in. I said this was ridiculous, she said, "It's not my fault that your friends are late." 

It turned out to be very hectic night. It didn't have to be. The hostess/manager was very rude. Clearly they don't value their customers. I will never come back.

This was supposed to be an enjoyable birthday dinner for my girlfriend surrounded by friends, but unfortunately, the restaurant wasn't on the same same page. 

I arrived early with other friends and we were waiting a few minutes for the rest of the group to get there. The host told us that they were unable to sit us unless all 17 people were here. A large group us had arrived and we were missing only 2 people. Yet the manager/host snapped back and insisted that everyone had to be present. She rudely refused to explain the situation to her, and refused to honor the email between my girlfriend and another manager of the restaurant when she made the reservation. We were finally seated after much pleading, and we were told that she made an "exception" for us. Exception for us?? My girlfriend made this reservation a long time ago and had her credit card charged for this reservation; there was no need for an exception. 

If you plan on hosting a large gathering here, think twice. And if restaurant service is about hospitality and friendliness, this is the exact opposite. It's a pity, because the food and drinks are very good.

The manager on duty on Friday night May 24 was extremely rude and needs a refresher course on customer service. My friend was celebrating her birthday celebration and reserved a table for 17 people. The manager refused to let us sit at the table that was reserved a month prior because only 15/17 people were there. Now we all know how it is, we plan for everyone to be there at a certain time but life happens and people join things late. It happens, it's NYC! Imagine being fired for coming in 5 mins late because of a train delay... listen it's NYC people are late to things... Anyways, I was dissatisfied with the fact that the manager profusely refused to work with the 15 people that were actually there. The table was set up already... I don't understand what the problem was?!?! Customer service 101... sit the 15 people down. Offer them drinks from the bar. Let them mingle and then take food orders when everyone is seated. It's really not that hard to make people happy and coming back for future events at your establishment. Unfortunately due to the lack of professionalism and human courtesy I will not be coming back. I highly advise that anyone planning to come here with a large group take their business elsewhere. Please avoid a headache and the need for 3 drinks after dealing with their management.

Def my go to udon spot! If you love udon noodles and big bowls, this is the place for you. Service was a bit slow but that might be just cause I went during dinner time. Udon lovers should definitely try this place. Would recommend and come back

Great quality Asian food selection
Recommend to make a reservation before showing up is quite popular. 
Family and I love it.

I ordered US Wagyu udon, kinda pricy, so I have high expectations, but I was disappointed. Because Im a meat lover, however, the amount of meat is so little and most of them is tiny slice...Also the cabbage is bitter for some reason..

Decently large restaurant with plenty of dining tables and high ceilings giving off a spacious dining experience. Good for large groups and can get quite loud. Despite the large space, there is practically always a wait for dining and reservation is strongly advise. It is mainly known for their udon ("master of udon"), but also offers a variety of other Japanese food such as sushi, sashimi, and rice bowls, as well as different Japanese appetizers. Appetizers are delicious but small portions, probably enough for one bite per person if sharing. 

Onto the udon, there are plenty of broth choices to choose from so there is something for everyone (hot vs cold noodles; sweet, savory, spicy, creamy or light, etc). Price is the same for a regular size or large size bowl (so why not opt for the large?!). Don't underestimate the amount of noodles. If you are not a big big eater, one large bowl of udon is enough to share between two people with room to order appetizers to try. Also, there is the option to choose thick or thin noodles. Overall, nothing spectacular but it is a decent bowl of udon- homemade noodles with well made and flavorful broth. Come here if you like udon or Japanese food. 

P.S. Currently, they are offering an Anniversary special, $3.99 for Lychee Martini at the bar. I believe this special has been going on since March 2019. Not sure how long it is going to last, but definitely take advantage before it's gone!

The Udon at Tsurutontan is good with a nice chewy quality, just maybe not the best the city has to offer. I appreciate that you are able to choose the amount of noodles you get with no extra charge. The duck or Wagyu Udons are satisfying and even if the portion of meat is small it does not break the bank with such high quality ingredients.

I'm pretty sure my friends and I got food poisoning after eating this but the taste was worth it. Do I regret eating the Wagyu&Mushroom Udon because I almost pooped my pants? No. The soup was extremely flavorful and the noodles were perfectly al dente. Ask for the large size since its the same price for the regular.

Ohohohohohoh if you are reading this and thinking about coming here to eat, stop thinking about it and just do it. I came here with a party of 6 after watching Strictly Dumpling's YouTube video on the beat using in NYC and I actually think he's wrong. I think it's the best udon in the country (we have some amazing udon in LA but this tops all of them!). The broth is so rich and the toppings are good, too. But what we loved the most were those thick, chewy udon noodles. Wow they were really just delicious, and they picked up the delicious broth so well! I like to use a spoon to get soup when I eat noodles but this time, I forgoed my spoon and just slurped those noodles. 

You can choose between thick noodles and thin noodles. Get the large portion because it's the same price as the small portion. You WILL eat them! Yes they are that good. 

I recommend the tantan noodles. Even though it doesn't have as much toppings as some other noodles, I felt like the soup was the most flavorful. This is comparing it to the deluxe egg drop noodle (which was kind of overwhelming with toppings but the soup was not as rich) and the uni soup noodles (creamy, tastes like chowder). 


And how can I forget to mention how fun the huge bowls are!! We had fun taking photos of the food.

TLDR; I've been here 5+ times since they've opened. Used to be good but now it has inconsistent quality (uni creme is sometimes watery, sometimes thick). Also cannot seem to manage a wait line or even seat parties appropriately in an EMPTY restaurant. 

--------------

It's 530pm on a Sunday, the restaurant is empty, reservations are completely open. They seat our party of 3 at a table meant for 2. They had to pull a third chair up to the table. We ask to switch and were told it's against their policy to sit 3 people at a 4 person table.

To add insult to injury, they sat a party of 3 at a table for 4 right after us.

The tables around us and reservations for 4 online stayed open during the entirety of our dinner. 

????? 

Perhaps this is what happens when restaurants rely solely on a table management system instead of common sense. 

Their quality isn't super consistent especially for the uni creme udon. The broth in that one should be more of a sauce but it comes out watery a lot so we stopped ordering it. 

Photos of the empty restaurant the entire time we dined attached.

Will not be returning anymore, unfortunately. It was a good run, Tsurutontan.

This was my 2nd visit and last. I went there with my family with table of 6. We all ordered udon and appetizers. After my second bite of my udon, i discovered 2 strand of hair in my soup. I immediately called the waitress, i showed her the hair and she immediately took it away( trying to destroy the evident). Next, i think he was the manager that came. He didnt not introduce himself. He just asked do you want me to take it out from the bill or replace it. Hello! I am not going to sit there while my family eati.  I said i want a different kind of udon, i was thinking if the hair was inside the broth the whole batch would be contaminated. He took my new order but the whole entire time did not apologize or i will not charge you for the new bowl. He never showed up again. I did not even mentioned the service was bad. When the waitress brought out the food she just told my son to pass it down to me and she dropped it down on the table so hard. Terrible customer service! Food was ok not even good. One star would be too high rating for this place.

All the ways to have udon. Curry, kitsune, sukiyaki, etc. Lots of other stuff to eat but whatever. 
They give you extra udon for free if you want it. It's crazy! 

Come here because it tatsed great and udon is life.

Enjoyed the food until these giant pieces of plastic were in our soup. Gross. Hopefully not the normal and just a random occurrence but after seeing so many good reviews can't possible give this place more than a 1 Star.

This place offers happy hours at certain time of the day. The drink are a good deal during happy hour. The appetizers and ramen were yummy. We Didn't Get to try the uni dishes but we will definitely go back to try other items on the menu. This place definitely get packed and busy. However they do take reservations and I definitely recommend it if you have a large party.
The food is good, between $$ and $$$, but the waiting time is way too long!!!! I waited for at least one hour for my udon. I won't come again, this restaurant just waste too much of my time.

When it isn't busy, waiter and waitress flirt with each other. Bar intenders look like yobbos. Food mediocre. 

Lack the professionalism and intensity that all great japanese restaurants have.

Enormous restaurant- hence so many reviews- -feairing overbooked rubbery shrimp, over-salted noodles, too sweet sukiyaki, ambience ruined by loud music. Rigid customer service: we were told that was told that the restaurant would accommodate a guest's wheat allergy by leaving the sun out of the sukiyaki "this time, but don't ask again." No problem - we won't be back.

I love the amazing ambiance of the restaurant. Every dish or noodle entree is amazing. Wanted to try everything. Will come back for more... I will say you must make a reservation or there will be a very long wait time.

Well worth the time to come here. Interestingly enough there is no difference between a medium and large bowl to be prepared to eat! The udon here is quite good and the noodles taste fresh. I got some of their traditional deluxe udon but the tempura fry was good and the medley of meats and flavors were almost overwhelming but this place makes it work! We also got some silken tofu and spicy tuna hand cones. My friend got lamb chops which were also quite good but somewhat small. C'est la vie. My other friend got the traditional shrimp tempura udon. All of the broth was clean and flavorful. Personally I really wanted to try their uni cream udon but it wasn't meant to be this visit. I'll be back soon to try!

I ordered the Sukiyaki Udon, crispy corn, and spicy tuna cones during the happy hour times on the weekend. The discounted appetizers ars absolutely worth it! The spicy tuna cones are super fresh and not too spicy, and come with guacamole in them, which was a pleasant surprise. The crispy corn was battered corn into a mini cake shape that came with a spicy dipping sauce that was extremely flavorful. Finally, the Sukiyaki Udon was incredible and the sweet broth was unlike anything I've had before. The thick noodles were soft, chewy, and wonderful. The vegetables in the udon soak up all the broth and makes them especially delicious.

Highly recommend this restaurant and the portions are enormous. Service was great as well, and happy hour at the bar has great prices!

I'm a frequent visitor of this Tsurutontan, and not sure if it was a one time fluke, but my last experience here was definitely disappointing. 

We ordered their Tantan noodle. First, the noodles took forever to arrive (at least 40 min) and the waitress apologized because they had apparently put in the wrong order so had to re-make it. Mistakes happen and it was a busy Saturday, so my friend and I were happy waiting.

But when the noodle came, I was so disappointed. The broth was so salty, and the noodles were all clumped together! For a restaurant that prides itself on the quality of their udon, this was really unexpected.

Overall, Tsurutontan really fell short of expectations this time. Really do hope it was a one time miss.

great decorations great vibes and very welcoming staffs. the spicy tuna cone is a must-try while cucumber salad and silky tofu r good-to-haves. the curry deluxe is very tasty especially with the thick udon. the thin udon is good too but pairing it with mushroom wagyu beef broth can be a bit too salty. good serving size so skipped the dessert session this time

Great HH prices here at the bar and for the drinks. $2 Sapporo and $4 Lychee-tini was an absolute steal. 

The wait is horrendous without a reservation. You must 100% have a reservation or expect to wait at least an hour for a group of 3-4.

Overall, the truffle shabu was good. The soup was not as hot as I thought and it was a bit warm, which negatively impacted the taste. The truffle was strong in smell, but weak in taste (truffle oil). The meat was tender and abundant, but because of the temperature of the soup, it felt cold.

Overall, I had a good experience, but not great. Would be open to try it again in the future.

The mentai kamatama blew my mind. I love noodles, I love pasta, and I think this was hands-down one of the best noodle dishes I've ever had. Maybe because I used to eat sushi that had globs of spicy mayo on it but this was like spicy mayo noodles with crunchy tempura bits, green onion, and a super slow-cooked egg. Plus, I really enjoyed eating out of a bowl that was the size of a basin you could bathe an infant in. 

Our waiter was also one of the best parts of our meal. He checked in on us often and when I dropped a cucumber chunk on the table and moved it over, he quickly swiped it away. 

The not-so-great parts: 
(1) The Friday night wait. I don't even understand how people could have gotten in without a reservation. They herded everyone who did have a reservation into this tiny waiting area near the bar and, every time a spot would open, would holler the person's name. Then, when we sat down at the long table with the divider, we noticed a ton of two-tops that were empty. Huh?

(2) It was incredibly loud. To the point where my friend and I were sitting this close to each other and I still had to shout. 

(3) We were by the bathroom and there were occasional wafts of toilet smell. You know what I'm talking about. 

(4) The $3.99 lychee martini lived up to its price. It was like guzzling lighter fluid with the barest hint of lychee syrup.
The bowl of udon here is huge, and great flavors too.  Would definitely recommend!  Would definitely come back

Likes:
- Getting an online reservation was quick and easy.
- The thin udon noodles had a great texture and the Daishi broth was absolutely delicious!
- Free refills of the udon noodles, we didn't take advantage of this, but sharing seems to be common here!

Not a fan of:
- The thick udon noodles were a tad mushy, although still delicious compared to the frozen varieties
- Wished the Happy Hour menu was a bit more straightforward. HH prices apply all day if you sit at the bar, otherwise, on the restaurant side, the prices only apply at certain time slots depending on whether if it is a weeknight or weekend. 

I came here with my work friend and his wife. The 3 of us ordered 2 large bowls of udon plus a side of smashed cucumbers, given that we weren't too hungry from our food hunt at the Chelsea Market. 
- Tsuruton Curry Deluxe (USD$24) - This came with a decent sized pork cutlet, 2 pieces of shrimp tempura and some beef slices. We ordered the thick noodles and as mentioned above, the texture could have been slightly more chewy. The curry broth itself was flavourful and overall, the protein tasted pretty good.
- Shrimp Tempura Udon ( USD$17) - This came with shrimp (2 pcs) and vegetable tempura, served on the side. I really enjoyed the dashi broth, although it would have been even better if served piping hot. The broth itself was clear and had a distinct flavour. I make daishi broth from scratch at home regularly, but their combination is definitely much tastier! The tempura on the side was decent, but nothing special.
- Smashed cucumbers (USD$8) - This was noted as one of their top sellers on the menu, so we decided to get some extra greens. The cucumbers were fresh and I enjoyed the light dressing, it was fragrant from the toasted sesame seeds, with a nice balance of sweet, savoury and tanginess. I would have preferred the cucumber chunks to be cut smaller and portions to be bigger at this price. 

Overall, I enjoyed my experience here. They are good at what they are known for, their udon noodles and daishi broth! Both were tasty and I am definitely looking forward to re-visit this place and try new items the next time I am in NYC!

This place is absolutely amazing! We made a reservation about three days before we actually went and once we got there we were seated right away. I would say if you were looking for something very flavorful this is not the place to go although it is very authentic Udon. The bowls are so gigantic so I definitely think it's worth every dollar you pay.

We loved loved and will be back! Prices are decent, portions are large in terms of entree/udon. We went in on a Saturday around 830 and waited for 10 minutes (projected 20-30 min)! Service was great and our server was upbeat and helpful. Ambiance is nice, you can tell that large parties go so it's a nice place if you have a large group. We did not sit in the communal seating (not my jam). Food was tasty and drinks were cheap! Yay 2$ beers. WILL BE BACK

This was my third visit to tsurutontan! Blown away once again. I got the lunch combo with the curry thick noodles and the fried chicken rice. The food was good as always, I would recommend the lunch combo if you are sure you can finish it. I'm a big eater and I had about half the bowl of rice remaining. My only dissatisfaction is the lack of vegetarian or vegan options. My vegetarian friends were limited to the veggie tempera udon. I wish there were one or two more options for them to choose from. I will be back again soon!

The food is so good. The staff is very kind and efficient. I brought my mom who is visiting from North Carolina and she could not stop raving about it. Catch happy hour! The drinks were amazing as was the sushi. Love this place.

This place is great! I got the small bowl of seafood udon (the small is substantial & chocked full o seafood, and, for some reason, the same price as the large). The meat buns were also good as was the service, matcha egg white cocktail, vibe & aesthetic. Other than feeling overly carb-full, this place is cool by me!
Great noodles and VERY healthy portions.

I have been wanting to try out this restaurant for a while now after a couple of my friends raved about it when they visited NYC. Therefore when a couple of friends suggested we come here for dinner I was very excited to try it out. 

I came here on a Thursday night with three other friends and the place was bustling. Two of my friends had arrived before me and another friend so they put their name down. We arrived around twenty to thirty minutes after and once we stepped in we were told the wait would be around 5 more minutes. But after 1minutes our table still was not ready and people in similarly sized groups who had come in after us were being seated before us which was a little bit frustrating. And even though we had confirmed with the hostess three separate times that our group was all present she still kept forgetting. 

However, after the long wait, we were finally seated. As soon as we arrived our server (who was absolutely wonderful) came over to give us our menus. The menu was impressively organized, every item had a photo associated with it so it was easy to see what the items look like and to choose the right item for your meal. 

I chose the Tsurutontan Deluxe and loved it. The giant bowl that came out came quickly and turned out to be an amazing and delicious meal. The tempura and delectable broth was such a great compliment and had such a great selection of ingredients. 

Finally, the decoration and appearance of the whole restaurant was wonderful. And definitely a warm environment for a great meal. 

Although there was a bit of a hiccup in the beginning the rest of the experience and meal more than made up for it. Additionally, there were also lots of appetizers and other dishes that looked absolutely amazing and that I would love to come back another time to try.

Was looking for a noodle place with my friend around Union Square and decided to try Tsurutontan out! Immediately thought the inside looked really nice and had a cool modern vibe with wood and lights 

Ordered the regular tan tan ramen because it was noted as a best seller

(+) ramen bowl is huge!! (See my photo for some hand to bowl comparisons) 
(+) udon noodle texture was great! Soft but still a little chewy
(+) flavor of broth was very good 

(-) though the broth was yummy it was quite oily on top
(-) the portion's are huge as I noted (I ordered a regular so I can't even imagine how big a large is) - it'd be nice if there were even smaller personal sizes

Tips:
1. Come for happy hour during the week, they have a lychee martini and beer special
2. Lunch special during the week - $10 for a ramen set
3. If you know you're not super hungry, share 1 ramen with 2 people

Their udon is solid and I think it's a great place to bring visitors too, especially because of their free upgrade with the giant bowl. I've been here twice, the first time I ordered the tan tan ramen but felt like it was too oily for me. This time, I ordered the tsurutontan deluxe and I absolutely loved how comforting it tasted.  Make sure that you request for the tempura to be on the side so that it doesn't get soggy! 

I think their lunch specials would be even more worth it. I'd also recommend the spiny tuna tartare cones, those were really delicious, the tuna was fresh and the cones were super crispy (also a good price during happy hour). Make sure to make a reservation too so that you wouldn't have too long.

I have been here several times for dinner and each time have been unimpressed with the quality of the food for the price. Many of the deluxe noodle options are well over $20 for dishes that may be served in large bowls but have small quantities of the premium ingredients. The prawns used in the tempura are quite small and the sea urchin in the uni creme udon and other dishes are not plentiful. Even a large portion of noodles, which are admittedly top notch, is not all that large by US standards. As an aside, this location also lacks the subtlety and calm that are in my opinion integral to the success of the Tokyo Roppongi location and other higher-end noodle places in the city.

Udon in soup. Broth was tasteful. Udon was cooked just right. They offer small and large bowl for the same price. As well as thin and thick udon. Udon is a bit pricey. Roughly in the 20s for a bowl, however it is filling and worthwhile to try. No need for reservations.

Omg the service here is just god awful. Waited forever for someone to take our order. Then 10 minutes later she comes back asks us what we ordered.

Food is ok but expect 2x longer than you would expect a restaurant to bring you the food. And this place is not cheap either so at least have service with a smile versus walking around as if the customer is burdening you.

Fix your service issues because you are losing customers. It's gotten progressively worse and worse each time I come here

UPDATE: been over half an hour and still no food!  And the place is not even that packed. I think they don't have enough servers and waitresses. I only see one waitress who looks like she is overworked and hates her job

The two tables next to me just left after sitting waiting for 15-30 mins and no one came to take their order. The waitress looked at them as she walked by without saying a word as they asked for their orders to be taken

My new favorite udon place  Although a bit pricey, the dishes are quite large and filling (medium and large are same price so might as well get a large) I really liked the matcha cocktail and tune cone too. & I ordered the truffle wagyu udon that was so delicious. It got a little heavy towards the end but I still couldn't stop eating it.

This is my third time here, and I really want to like it but I just cant. Tsurutontan is a Japanese chain now in NYC (similar to ippudo, ichiran, ikinari, etc) and this chain specializes in udon. It's taken over the old Union Square Cafe space.

Food - the most important criteria for a restaurant. It's an udon restaurant so there's a respectable variety of different types of udon and you can get a bigger bowl (more noodles) free of charge. Tried the beef udon, uni creme, wagyu and mushroom sukiyaki and duck udon. All of it is better than average in NYC with some chewiness to the noodles. Appetizers here are a little underwhelming, especially the quality of the raw fish (quality seems to have gone down over time). They also serve rice bowls.


Service - the service here is to be desired for. They're rushed even when it's not that busy. And stop trying to take away my udon that I haven't finished. The biggest qualm? They don't let you pack the noodles and broth separately. As an udon shop you should know better. Who wants to eat soggy noodles!? I offered to pack it myself - somehow also against the policy. The manager came and explained that it's a rule that upper management set and they don't know why and other customers have complained. If you're going to make strict rules that don't cater to your customers' needs, at least have an explanation. Or change the rule. 

Restaurant is large, with a bar at the front, though I would avoid the cocktails. 

Price here is fair for this area, with an average udon at a hair under $20. 

You can do better at Raku, which is not that far away.
Definitely delicious Udon. Their recipes are unique! I love the uni cream Udon so much , I ordered it every time.

Went there with my family since we were craving Japanese food - we ordered a large variety of different udon dishes including the curry, Dan Dan/spicy as well as the veggie tempura as well as sushi rolls for good measure. The spicy udon was very spicy which I didn't mind but the flavor was rather flat and I expected the broth to be somewhat richer. Service was prompt and The portions are huge so you can share and you'll definitely be full but I doubt we will return as it was an expensive meal for a mediocre experience

Great place to go if you want solid food and big portions for cost. 

We got some beer (Asahi $7, Sapporo $6), appetizers (Shishito pepper $9, Soy garlic tatsuta $13), and large udons (Sukiyaki $20, Wagyu Mushroom Sukiyaki $24, Uni Creme $24). 

It's not the best udon but again portions are big and there's a lot of seating. The big bowls make good social media fodder so Tsurutontan is still pretty popular.

This may be my new favorite udon spot. The bowl of noodles is so flavorful and hearty. You can get extra noodles for the same price. Might as well take advantage. I saw a couple share a bowl of noodles. Smart. Don't break the bank and still enjoy the food. 

My friend loved the service we received. Staff was so friendly and helpful. There is a wait to get a table. But it's not terrible. I think we waited around 20 minutes around dinner time. I'll return again to try more from the menu.

Choose thick noodle. 
The noodle is the best in NYC. I really like how sticky and density of the noodles. I like this place, but one time they forgot tempura from tempura udon. Also, plz do not keep asking whether I am done or not lol

wonderful restaurant. i loved the ambience and the decorations. happened upon this place and will totally be returning. i went with two friends and we each got different dishes & everything tasted so flavorful and different. i got the simple beef udon soup. the noodles were a great texture and portions were huge. the options at this restaurant are diverse and there is something for everyone here b

I've been here twice and will probably return in the future. This previous visit, I was feeling sick, so I ordered the chicken udon and some green tea. The chicken udon was a bit bland, but it was perfect for me because I was sick and it totally hit the spot (do your taste buds even work when you're sick?!). My husband ordered a tuna roll and the caviar udon noodles. His udon bowl was sooooo delicious. Very savory and unique. We arrived after 9pm, which is their 2nd happy hour (the first is from 5pm-7pm, and the 2nd is 9pm-11pm - I think). Because of the happy hour, the roll was only $7 and his Sapporo draft (12 ounces) was $1.99. I mean, you can not get a better beer cheaper anywhere (well, maybe in Japan or the midwest).

The first time I went, I ordered the sashimi plate and from what I remember, it was fresh and delicious.

This is a Japanese chain, so you're not going to have a completely mind blowing, culinary experience, but you will get some good udon and decent deals if you hit up their happy hour.

I believe they just introduced their takeout option, and unfortunately it still needs a lot of work. 

I ordered takeout via Yelp at 6:44 on a Thursday evening and walked in at 7PM as shelter from the rain and also hoping that my food may be early ready. I let the girl at the front know that I was early and that it may not be ready, and she immediately responded with "it's not ready." She didn't bother asking for my name or order to go check on it. 

I ended up waiting for the full time estimate that Yelp gave (another 25 minutes) before asking someone else who looked more in charge if my order might be ready. 

I was never instructed that I needed to stand in a specific place to wait on my takeout order so that the hosts would know to check in with me (apparently there was). I understand that it's a busy restaurant, but I really wished she had checked on my food when I initially asked. With 4 hosts, I'm sure one of them could've gone to the kitchen to check. I wouldn't have minded waiting if I wasn't so caught off guard by the immediate shot down by the first hostess. Disappointingly rude. I definitely don't recommend ordering takeout here unless you feel like waiting an hour for food.

Wagyu Sushi. Flavor is good, but Wagyu is too raw for us. 
Seared Salmon Sashimi: salmon feels like not too fresh
Spicy seafood jjigae: worst spicy seafood korean soul i've ever had
Truffle Creme with Crab and Mushroom: tastes ok. Too much alfredo no crab

I commute all the way from DC for this place. Quality udon, freshly made, every time. Tasty broth, reasonable price, and nice ambiance. I really like that you can get an extra bowl of udon if you started off with a regular size. Definitely won't walk away feeling hungry! Strongly recommend. 

Area for improvement: faster service would be welcomed.
the presentation of the noodle was impressive, but the soup was a little bit too salty for me and the texture of the udon did not taste like hand-made one.

Amazing udon! absolutely loved the noodles here and the staff are so friendly. The portions are huge so make sure to come with a friend to share or even order multiple to try out different options! The appetizers are also delicious. I can not recommend this place more. I did have to wait for a bit, but it was well worth it! Come here if you're craving udon, you can't go wrong.

Quality and service have gone down. Loved this place initially, but recently the food is inconsistent and service is poor. 

Note to staff: please start thinking for yourself. A lot of complaints are just common sense.

We got there when it opened at noon with plenty of room, but for some reason it still took them 10-15 mins to seat us so they need to fix their system. We almost left but we were glad that we didn't because the food made up for it.

The lunch special is a great deal- $11.99 for a bowl of udon and you can add a beef or tuna rice bowl for $3. We shared the Tempura Udon and the Curry Udon. The noodles were very good, comparable to udon in Tokyo. The broth was delicious and the tempura was served on the side so it didn't get soggy. However, the curry was waaayyy too thick. The Sukiyaki Beef Rice Bowl on the side was very good. Service was good too. Overall, very good Udon and reasonable lunch prices for NYC standards, just don't get the curry.

I love Udon noodles. The glutonous texture of noodles is delightful. Curry udon noodles was my favorite here. It was moderately spicy. I had the ontama toriten curry udon. Chicken tempura in it was excellent. US Wagyu and mushroom sukiyaki was not spicy enough for me. Wagyu, mushroom and udon was excellent, just the flavor was not something for me. Overall my recommendation is to go with a curry udon.

Come in at 5:05pm when they just open for dinner, they make us wait for 15 mins when the restaurant is empty!!!!  Because we don't have a reservation. Have been here in the past years and it never happen to me..... they need to work on their system. Unfortunately I'm not coming back. Nothing wrong with the waiting time. It's about the attitude!!!!

The noodles were pretty good. Can't really complain. The only reason why I give 4 stars is because the last time I was there which was at 2pm, our check came right away after our food had only been delivered to us within 2 min. Our waitress wanted us to pay immediately. We haven't even started eating... she told us to "take our time" but we felt rushed out of the restaurant. I think she mumbled to us that the restaurant was going to close at 3pm and open up again at 5pm. So she wanted to finish her shift and get her tip before leaving... I was really annoyed with that. Other than that, the food was pretty good.

I was there three weeks ago. The ambiance was very comfortable. You have a lot of noodle options to choose from. Great big portion. The price is a little high but you do get a big bowl of noodle soup.

After watching a video of the place and their huge bowl of noodles a while back, I finally decided to try this place with a friend. I went with their shrimp tempura udon ($17) while my friend chose their wagyu beef udon ($21). The waiter asked if we'd like the big or small portion, in which both cost the same price. It was a no brainer that we'd opt for the bigger size. However, we unfortunately confirmed my suspicions that it wasn't that the portions were huge, but the bowls that the noodles came in. My shrimp tempura set came with vegetable tempura too, which is nice that it wasn't just shrimps. Thankfully it was tasty, but the portion for the price was a little disappointing -- especially the way it's advertised and phrased. I felt hungry after finishing the meal and think that maybe the cost is what it is due to the appeal of the huge bowls.
Good food, perfect location right next to the train station. But they give a huge share of food we were not expecting that.

I'm a big udon fan, and it doesn't take much more than some bonito broth (I'm a bad vegetarian) and some thick noodles to please me. To satisfy those cravings in the future, I will continue going to Udon West nearby.

The food here wasn't bad, but everything was distinctly lacking in flavor. We ordered the vegetable tempura udon, and it seemed no one thought to add seasoning to the panko crust. Maybe a little dashi on the side would have saved them, but the soup broth was not enough to uplift these mediocre tempura. Same went for the eggplant tempura app that started our meal.

If you told me the silken tofu appetiser was made with store-bought tofu, I wouldn't be surprised. I was expecting fresh, luscious homemade tofu and was disappointed.

Texture of the noodles was good - no complaints there.
The Beef Udon is amazing. I absolutely loved the broth and the handmade noodles!! I ate here in the summer but I imagine this place would be even better when it's freezing outside. Will return!
Do not come here! We reserved a table for 10 but were seated in a table for 8. The restaurant manager asked us to squeeze in instead of providing additional chairs. The food was truly overpriced.
Literally my favorite restaurant in the world. Posing this review so I never forget the magical noodles I cannot find anywhere else

Cold uni non-creme option with thin noodles was the perfect choice for a hot summer night. Was quickly seated on a weeknight around 8pm. 2 seaters sit next to each other on a bench, and tables of 4 or more have more traditional seating. Will come back and try more!
They have the best HH specials at the bar. Tasty drinks and the yummiest noodles! Great modern and chic vibe.

Horrible!!! For what i saw tonight -.- 

OMG!!!

Busboy set up the table, he dropped chopsticks on floor, he put it pack to the paper wrap setting. I signal him, and even call him over and told him it's dirty. He came back later tried to explain he put on  the side of his hand. And what, it went back to the setting table where only chopsticks and plate on it. He didn't put directly inside the chopsticks setting but leave near by. Definitely he will wait after i leave to put it back. I hope the owner or manager must check the camera and see if it's really went back to use again. It's around 10:15pm on Sat (aug 10th) night in main dinning room. This is unacceptable for this kind of place!
Definitely you'll lose a regular customer who come there once twice a week. 
Last few week i had been ignored for half hour by a new lunch server. A girl server there know I'm a regular and kept apologize for the new guy. Even told me don't have to leave tips but I know it's tip pool so i still leave it for other staffs. I've been back many time after and didn't see her, may not same shift she works.
After today, i don't think i will be back if i don't get any feedback from the management team!
Very disappointed

I have been here multiple times and have decided that the uni udon is probably my favorite. However, this time I tried the truffle wagyu udon and was disappointed by how overwhelming the truffle flavor was. It overpowered everything else in the dish and definitely overloaded the umami taste buds to a point of heavy reluctance. Overall it is a nice restaurant to get udon if you are craving!
Some of their food is definitely top notch. Others are average. Great date spot or pretty great for groups with reservation.

5 stars all the way for udon quality cause of how bomb the uni creme udon was!!! 
The uni might not look cute and it's small BUT LISTEN, SAVOR EVERY BITE YOU HAVE OF IT!
When I (accidentally) slurped it up, the moment it entered my mouth, the uni taste was a slap to my face. Jesus, I've never had this kind of flavor in my 21 years of life and now I feel enlightened. 

I could not believe I swallowed it all in one bite and that was my biggest mistake. Probably is the reason why the udon cost as much as it does even though there isn't much in the dish.
The cream of the udon isn't heavy at all which is wonderful especially on summer days when you have that craving for something creamy. I got the thin udon noodles which were like spaghetti thin so it didn't have the bite like normal udon noodles. 
The price is same for normal or large size (which means more noodles) but even the normal size is quite big.
I liked the uni creme udon more than than the mushroom sukiyaki udon. 

One star off for the slightly disappointing customer service. It was good when we first settled in and ordered but after that, the waiters were harder to flag down than taxis in NYC. Most of them busily walked by us with customers or stuff in hand and the waiter who initially was serving us just disappeared after refilling our water once. Even after getting a different waiter to give us our bill, we waited awhile for someone else to receive it. Would have also knock off half of a star for slightly uncomfortable table seating but the food completely overpowers that minor issue.

The place is small but nice and confortable. People is nice and kind and service is good. Dishes are very good and they have for all tastes. Brebajes are good too. The bowls of noodles are enough for one person but that is the only thing you will eat. You pay what you eat, procedente are excellent.

Got the uni creme udon. It comes in Regular and large portion size with no difference in price ($24). The noodles also come in thick or thin. Got it with large and thick and I'm stuffed wow. 

The udon is bouncy but chewy. The soup is reminded me a lot of a great Alfredo but without the thickness of one. It was watery in consistency but still creamy. The flavor is hard to describe. Kind of reminded me of instant Mac and cheese but much better lol. 

Uni is floating on a shio leaf to prevent the broth from cooking it (which is only mildly successful). I got the feeling that the uni varies in quality a lot from fresh and salty to bitter and kind of gross. Granted, I'm not the biggest fan of uni. But you do get 4ish pieces which more than enough.
Food was too salty, slow!!! Service consider not bad!!! Please let your management know it is time to go buy new bowl or new plate. Using a broken plate is actually very dangerous and ugly!!!
Very filling and large portions, wait can be long, food is not bad, typical of what you expect for udon

In My Opinion Only. 
To me the place was not all that.
My noodles came out mushy and not bouncy like an over cooked instant Ramen. Broth sucked. I thought I could not go wrong with their most popular order. The tempura was soaked and soggy by the time the noodle got to me.
We had a party of 8 and all 6 got Udon with the deceptively looking giant bowl which was properly the same amount as the regular size bowl with a little more broth. Such gimmick. My son loved Ramen and Udon, he said thought it was the worst broth he tasted. 
But the Sushi was good tho...

If you ever wanted a bowl of udon the size of your face, you've found it! And if you're really feelin' it, you can upgrade to an even more gigantic bowl for free!! The interior is sleek and modern and seating is a little tight but totally manageable. The Mentaiko Caviar was creamy with just a lil bite--absolutely delicious. And the Duck Udon is perfect for those who may be craving a classic with a more unique protein. All in all, delicious!

The food here is excellent. 

For appetizers, I recommend the garlic fried chicken, beef buns, and shishito peppers. Favorite entrees are the sashimi salad udon (delicious sesame dressing) and tan tan udon (thick noodles!). Lastly, for dessert you should go for the Lady M. cake- I don't even like cake but this was tasty!
