I usually do the happy hour after 9pm but they also have it earlier in the evening. Very smooth sake and you can't beat the prices on the saketini and Japanese beer. 

4 stars instead of 5 because the service is average. I keep coming back for the food!

This place blew me out of the water with their udon. I am a huge fan of udon but it's hard to find noodles with the right consistency along with a broth with good seasoning. Look no further than Tsurutontan. The udon noodles are house-made. They have the correct thickness, chewiness, and how the flavor from the broth grips onto the actual noodles is amazing. The sushi was refreshing and had a good ratio of rice to fish. The tempura was hot, flaky, and crunchy. With my sushi lover lunch combo I received chrome, eggplant, sweet potato, mushroom, nori, and parilla leaf tempura. The lunch special combos here are really a bang for your buck. You get so much food and not to mention it's great quality. If I lived in the city I'm pretty sure I would eat lunch here everyday haha.

I am truly, genuinely baffled by the good reviews as this was one of the worst meals I've had in a very long time. I would never recommend this place to anyone nor come back; you'd be better off just setting your money on fire, at least you'd save yourself from the nauseating experience of having to eat their food. 
My friend and I got a sushi roll as an app. It tasted fine, but was very loosely rolled and falling apart. The waitress took our plates away, even though I said: "But we aren't done eating," and there was still food on our shared plate. This was all a little inconvenient, but ok...
Then came the horror of the actual udon. My friend's dish must have had a pound of sugar in it, it was simply inedible. She picked at it and was left very nauseous afterward (we had to ask for her plate to be removed to avoid the smell). Mine wasn't exactly delicious, but it was edible; I ended up eating a fair bit of it, but was left with stomach cramps as a result. 
Ailments aside, it's overpriced "designer food" presented in a flashy, trendy fashion for people who are out trolling NYC for fake clout and don't know nor care what these dishes should actually look or taste like. My friend eded up apologizing profusely to me for suggesting this place (totally don't blame her) and I'd like to spare you the experience. Again, genuinely confused by the other reviews here, there's so much great Japanese food in the area

We're tourists... wandering around NYC and suddenly starving. We came upon this place and it sounded really good. It was a very busy lunch hour but they seated us right away. They have 4?5? menus so that was a bit confusing but everything had a picture next to it so you can see what you're ordering which is nice! Literally everything we ordered was amazing! So good! But ORDER THE LAMB CHOPS. There were 5 small perfectly grilled chops that were literally melt in your mouth tender, with the perfect amount of charring. Omg I could have sat there and ate those for hours. The staff was super efficient and polite and the food came out fast. I would definitely eat here again!!!

Honestly you are paying for the noodles. They give you lots of noodles and nothing else. 

If you ask for veggies it's not cooked. It's worse than the way Ootoya would cook them. It's like a salad: raw cabbage. 

I ordered the truffle wagyu and the wagyu was rubbery. It could not be chewed. Way gamey than their duck udon. 

Ordered their eggplant appetizer and it was way too soaked in dashi....

You're better off at Ise for their soba. Sorry but their soba wins hands down. 

Service was pretty bad. I had to find the waiters. I won't be back to this franchise.

Hmm.. Did I get unlucky? All the raving reviews is what brought me here; however, I must say - this was sadly the worst udon I've ever had. I had the Sukiyaki Udon, which was on the "bestsellers" menu and is what the waitress recommended. I'm well aware that sukiyaki is cooked with sugar and is a sweeter dish; however, it was bad.. I could not taste anything but the sweetness.  I tried, I really did, but I ended up just leaving it - I couldn't get through half of the bowl.  

The Good: The place is big and is probably great for larger groups.  The decor is awesome - the first thing you see when you walk in is a huge beautiful bar. Maybe good for drinks and apps, but I came for UDON, and I will not be returning.

Very good food. I had the udon and uni. Very interesting and tasty combination was a cold udon. I recommend trying it. Our daughter had this cold udon and liked it very much. 
My wife had a spicy sea food udon was very good. I tasted it and liked it too. We also had the iqura rolls and toro scallion which were great. All very good quality but not inexpensive. We paid about 145 dollars without the tip. I would go back.

Coming in: 
Busy restaurant during peak dinner hours. There are booth and tables for seating. The tables have a wooden divider the makes you sit next to the person you are eating with instead of having people become face to face. It is definitely more intimate due to proximity but I think I would have preferred a booth. The aestetics were nice and felt like a fancy Japan store. 

Restrooms:
They don't have a men's bathroom. They have a gender neutral bathroom. Good thing I only had to pee. I would suggest adding more bathrooms here. The women's from what I heard at least had their own bathroom with 2 stalls. 

The time that you have been waiting for - 
Food!!-
Sukiyaki Udon - I ordered a Large(it cost the same) my noodles were thick and it just felt right having thick noodles. The broth was very sweet to the point that I was confused. It was super delicious. The veggies were a little bitter but due to the sweet broth it was fine. I definitely enjoyed how rich the broth was and how it was so delicious. I brought home left overs and ate that for lunch the next day. 

Pricewise- very much $$ but it was a good place to go to in the City. 
Remember to order a Large Bowl, doesn't add cost and you can bring left overs home.

Sushi is 5-star!! The tuna tartar cone and the negitoro roll were delicious and made the meal all worth while (it was crowded, friday night happy hour!) Came quick and was melt-in-your-mouth

Udon is what didn't hit home. Both the broth and the stir-fry were waaaaay tooooo sweeeeeet it was almost overwhelming. The noodles were good, but that was about it. Good for those with a sweet tooth.

Service is great, waiters were attentive and speedy.

I've worked across from this place for years but never ate here. There are multiple menus: set menu, happy hour menu, udon menu, drink menus. A ton of choices! I had the curry udon set with spicy tuna rice ($14.99). My husband had the tempura udon set with sukyaki rice bowl. Both sets were beautifully arranged and presented. The udon was freshly made and just so incredibly delicious and long (length)! Think Lady and the Tramp where they slurp one noodle on each end. The curry was spicy and creamy-so tasty and filling. I had to eat very slowly to savor every bite. You won't find another place like this in Manhattan that gives you a hearty meal for a great price. We also tried the sukiyaki bun-the beef was so flavorful, but I wish the bun was served warm. The service was friendly and helpful. The decor is funky with cavernous ceilings and has 3 levels. It's quite spacious. Unlike Ichiran, they give you extra udon noodles for free-although I'm not sure who would need more. The large has plenty of noodles and is the same price as the regular size. So go for the large and if you want more noodles then ask for it. I was stuffed after my bowl. 

We will be back!

PS. It looks like they have a great happy hour at the bar that is available all day until 6pm. This would be a great place to meet friends after work or for an early afternoon drink. For their 3 year anniversary, a glass of Sapporo beer is $1.99

My wife and I went here on a Saturday night after having a long day roaming around New York as tourists.

The restaurant was excellent. I enjoyed it a lot. There was a very short wait, we got in right away. The food was very good and the atmosphere was very pleasant. Service was nice very respectful and quick.

-My Stars-

Restaurant
* Atmosphere: Excellent. I don't know how authentic it actually was. But going inside the restaurant, and after going downstairs it felt like I was in a real Asian establishment. There were some nice decorations, and very good lighting. It was clean, including the bathroom. Everything smelled good.
* Service: Outstanding! We were treated very well. We were quickly seated, and the servers seemed to know exactly when we were ready to order, when we finished etc. During the meal, I did notice one employee standing as a sort of sentry, and just waited for people who needed a water refill, or when they started looking around for someone who might need help, or had a question. 

Food: I ordered the House Dish. A large bowl with noodles, tempura shrimp, dropped egg, chicken, pork, and beef (I might have gotten that wrong).
* Presentation: Excellent. My meal came in a large bowl. Noodles at the bottom, meats on that, and the tempura veggies, shrimp, and some sort of fancy leaf on top. It was fun to pick at it for a minute, before stirring it up. The colors were pleasant, and everything was nice.
* Taste: Very good. I enjoyed my meal very much. Everything had that good blend of flavors. While the various ingredients were sort of dumped into a soup bowl together, they each still had a unique flavor, and the combined mixed flavors of the other ingredients.
* Texture: Good, with a catch. Each of the ingredients were obviously put in right before being delivered to me. The tempura hadn't gotten soggy. After a few minutes it did, but that's ok. My wife's tempura came on a second plate. Very nice. The meats were not low quality, and it was all very pleasant to eat. The noodles are out of this world. I felt like a kid, slurping them up.

Wow what an amazing Bargain for New York City ! 

Stopped in for lunch and was amazed by the selection of food options.

Location is great, right next to Union Square and just a quick walk from the 33rd metro/path stations. Interior was spacious and modern with a really cool vibe.

Staff was friendly courteous and attentive. Especially when I asked about the menu items they were knowledgeable on the offerings.

My meal was fabulous. Large portions of udon and tempura. I definitely did not go away hungry. The tempura was light and crunchy. And the soup base had a slight tinge of miso scallions and Bonito. But I came here for the handmade noodles which were perfectly made and fresh.

Well done ! All in all a fabulous experience.

$1.99 for a Sapporo Beer.
14.99 lunch special sets.

Follow me on Facebook, Twitter, YouTube and Yelp. @ NoodleSoupReview. As I search for the perfect bowl of noodle soup.
Delicious - large selection of different udon soups and very substantial portions. Friendly staff / nice ambience

All the udon are excellent. Either the thick udon or the skinny udon tastes great and the flavor really gets into it. The soup is delicious. The rolls are fresh and nice, got seasoned well, and plated beautifully. 
The dining environment is well designed and quiet. 
Order any udon here and you'll be full and satisfied!
Waited one hour and was told 'our noodles will be ready in 10 minutes'. Absolute disaster. Left hungry and angry.

Wayyy over priced and poor service. Also not enough bathrooms for the size of the place. It does however have a cute atmosphere. 

Basically paying $30 for soup. Only other options are tapas type foods with tiny portions. 

Our food came out at very different times, making an awkward dining experience that we are paying a lot of money for. The waiter also does not come by often so if you're hungry make sure you have your order ready as soon as they greet you.  

Everything is very pricey and they still charge an extra $1.50 for hot sauce.

Went during happy hour on a weekend (which starts at 2pm) which included Lychee tini for $3.99 and beer for $1.99. We ordered a Lychee tini which was stronger than expected. 

The interior is beautiful with a mix of tables and booth like seating. Service was great and attentive, always refilling our water and removing the plates. 

Appetizers: 
Dashimaki egg omelet (cold dish) with a hint of sweetness coated around it. 
Soy Garlic Tatsuta with mild spicy-ness but it is a good amount served. 

Udon (Large): Wagyu mushroom sukiyaki (sweet soysauce broth) balanced well with mushroom and cabbage (slightly bitter). The Wagyu was a bit on the tougher side though. Big enough to share with two.

The udon noodles were delicious and the salmon quality was great. Something to watch out for- the portion sizes are huge, so maybe bring a friend to split the food with you if you can't eat a lot. Definitely plan to go again!

WOW.

OUR ORDER
-Uni Créme Udon: uni, Tobiko caviar, shiso leaf in uni créme broth
-US Wagyu Shabu Udon in Truffle Dashi: sliced US wagyu ribeye, truffle oil

Wow. No words can describe how delicious these two bowls were. For the uni we did a thin noodle per the recommendation of our waiter and I was so happy with how they turned out. I highly recommend doing one thin noodle dish. The broth in both of these dishes was another level and the wagyu slices were perfect and all of portions of each ingredient were perfect. I want to go back in time right now to eat this again. Highly recommend getting these two stunner dishes. We also got some cold cuts to start

Same price for either regular size bowl of noods or LARGE!? Can't forget to mention their all day HH at the bar. $4 lychee-martinis! I was there two days in a row, oops

Solid spot of sushi and appetizers but to get the best bang for your bucks, grab a big bowl of food.

Their truffle broth options are wonderful. They aren't cheap on the truffle oil. Either the wagyu beef or the crab and mushroom udon are delicious! A favorite of mine is the uni creme udon! My preferred noodle is the thin one since the ratio of noodle to broth is better in one bite. I've tried a few other broth but nothing stood out more than the ones I've mentioned. But definitely will come back for many other things on this huge menu!

Was so excited to try this restaurant. Came on a Sunday afternoon and was quite disappointed. It seemed like everyone around us who came after us had their food first. Also, our waiter came around and asked us numerous times asking what we ordered again and again... Don't quite understand the reason why.
Our udon noodles came out very soggy and overcooked. Soup was also on the salty side. But for an establishment where it's known for noodles, I don't understand how they can make such a mistake.
Later, the manager stopped by our table but only had excuses for the noodles's quality. She stated that they cannot control to be state of the noodles.???
Really chill spot, service is great! Seating is clean and fast; theres definitely a feel of privacy. Food was delish.

HUGE PORTIONS!! Best part is that the large is the same price as the regular. Pictures don't do it justice. Japanese fried chicken is good. I got the cold dipping noodles which looks super japanesey and aesthetic. Only thing is I got sick of the flavors easily. Maybe I'll try a don next time

The 4 star is for the ambiance, service, and food. 

Ambiance: beautiful and unique decor. The restaurant is a great place for a date assuming it isnt too busy. We went for dinner and it was a bit busy so we were seated near another couple. The seating is tight so a 2 seater really feels like 4 if you have someone to your right. Perhaps 6 seater if you have someone to your left AND right. Otherwise the restaurant is beautiful. 


Service: great service. The waiters all seem very informative and tries to help give suggestions if needed. Friendly and tentative. I was very happy with the service. The waiter wasnt overly annoying either, he didnt constantly come by to ask if everything was ok while my mouth was stuffed with food. 

Food: the creamy yellow ramen with thin noodles was amazing! So flavorful, not too salty, and just delicious. The best seller appetizer which looks like 4 cones wasnt great. That wasnt worth trying and I didnt feel like it was particular special. I would skip that and focus on the meals. The meals all look amazing and definitely taste great. The dashi rice bowls are so delicious and filling. The meat is tender and nothing was overly seasoned or dry. We left feeling full and happy. 

Tight seating and soso appetizer was where the 1 star was dropped. Definitely recommend for a date night

TLDR: This is hands down my all-time favorite udon place! You really can't go wrong with anything you choose here and the portions are HUGE. I'd recommend getting a large duck udon to share between 2 people!

Food: 10/10
I've never had such amazing udon before. We got the Duck Udon and the US Wagyu and Mushroom Sukiyaki to share between 3 people. Both broths were so flavorful and unique! The duck udon had a almost indescribable broth, bursting with umami flavors, while the mushroom sukiyaki broth was sweet! Both had generous portions of the toppings and meats. Personally, I loved having both udons, since the broths contrasted so perfectly.

Price & Portion: 10/10
Wow these bowls are HUGE! Like bigger than my head!! Each bowl is about $20 and definitely splittable if you share a large with someone. 100% a bang for your buck.

Service: 8/10
Be sure to make reservations because it gets pretty busy! We came here for dinner on a Monday and only waited about 10-20 minutes for a table of 5. Our server was super nice and attentive! Definitely love this place.

Ambience: 8/10
The lighting is dim and definitely romantic! The chairs are SO comfy and the decor is really just so trendy. It's perfect for a date or just dinner with friends.

Been there so many times and while food and your waiter/waitress services are great - you have to get pass that horrible front desk reception service/ area first.

I frequent here a few years already and always find the reception area and service serious lacking if not off-putting. You can never tell/know if the receptionist is going to help you coz they aren't really that responsive. And if the space is a little crowded (say maybe 5 customers waiting?) good luck coz there's no control of streamlining. U can't tell who's been help, who's waiting for our name down, and the front desk just handle what she is handle at that moment without checking the whole scene. A few times we felt it's so ridiculous and out of control we just left coz no one would even acknowledge us. That's why I take two points off coz they never improve on this for years.

But again, once I manage to pass 'phase', all thing are good.

I really like the spicy seafood jiggae! I've visited two times and I liked it so much that I got the same thing the second time I came as well. The soup is flavorful, the bowl is huge, and definitely delicious.  Also a plus that the menu has pictures for reference!

First time here came in with a party of 13 no problem seating at opening time. We got the spicy tuna tartare, the cucumbers, and the beef sukiyaki udon. The appetizers were very tasty the tuna tartare has guacamole inside which was a nice surprise. The beef sukiyaki udon was delicious. The broth was extremely flavorful and sweet which can be a bad thing sometimes. The nice thing is you can get a small or large udon for the same price and get free extra udon. Definitely one of the best udon I ever had

This is definitely my favorite udon place in nyc. Great food and nice environment. Remember to reserve a spot especially if you plan to visit on weekends, otherwise you will be prepared to wait in a queue cuz people really love this place!!! Ordered udon pon dumplings, eel and ricotta roll, and stir fried sukiyaki udon, and they are all amazing! I would definitely recommend this place to the world.

Disappointing, to say the least. Our waiter told us that there was a smaller bowl and both would be the same price. I asked for the regular, assuming it wouldn't be the smaller he mentioned. I believe I was given the smaller portion... 

The noodles were okay, but there were exactly two tiny cubes of pork belly in my pork belly spicy tan tan udon. At that point, I just didn't care anymore. Not sure if I'll come back to try something else.

came here for lunch with a friend on a friday and even though we made reservations, there was pretty ample seating left. 

we sat down in the downstairs area near the bathrooms and it had a weird smell it almost turned me off. almost like a smelly cheese mixed with bathroom that was very offputting but i eventually got used to it.

we started with a spicy seafood udon and a wagyu mushroom udon with a side of fried chicken rice bowl. 
- the spicy seafood udon was very good, reminded me of jjambbong except i thought it was weird there was tofu in it. 
- the star though was the wagyu beef udon; the flavors had such depth and the beef and the mushrooms were so tasty
-the fried chicken rice bowl was decent, needed some type of sauce though since the rice on the bottom was just white and flavorless even though i mixed the bowl around. 

our server was nice but a little strange; my friend offered to pay for my lunch even though i kept telling her not to and the waitress kept looking at me to say, are you sure you don't want to put your card in and clearly my friend had won the battle by paying for lunch but the waitress wouldn't walk away with her card. so i awkwardly grabbed mine and she kept trying to grab it while my friend was screaming at me. eventually she walked away with my friend's card but she was mouthing something to me i couldn't understand. i thought it was weird how involved she was getting

all in all, the udon was decent and thought it had good prices! i would definitely come back to try the other udons

Favorite Udon place.The ambiance is very contemporary.Great selection of food and drinks.The portions are huge. The broth is very tasty.The udon are perfect and has the right amount of chew to it.Definitely recommend this place

Good food but the service was SO slow tonight. We waited about 20 minutes for our beers, then probably another 15 minutes for sushi, then another 10 minutes just for edamame, and then another 10 minutes for our noodle soups--so almost an hour for the main courses in all. Twice I noted to the waiter that we were waiting a long time and he brusquely and unapologetically replied, "There's a line in the kitchen." Don't think I'll return, at least not at a busy time of day. I expect better service for these prices.

Wow. I got the udon with pork belly and the regular size is the same as large size so might as well get the large. I thought it was good but to be honest, I've had better udon elsewhere. Here's a photo to depict how large the udon bowls are!

Fantastic upscale Japanese spot specializing in Udon! 

Overall: 4/5 
Food: 4/5 
Service: 4/5 
Decor: 4.5/5
Value: 4/5 

We had the sea and truffle roll ($16), silken tofu appetizer ($7), and the cold Uni Udon ($24). The silken tofu was just ok, I feel like it was a little plain and also the sauce was pretty much soy sauce so having a special sauce would've been nice and more interesting. The roll topped with various slices of sashimi with truffle oil was quite delicious - wanted to eat much more! It's like 8 pieces for $16 which is not bad and was quite good. The Uni Udon was delicious, but only had like 2 pieces of Uni... it's also an enormous bowl they serve it in so was expecting it to be a super large portion but it wasn't like exceedingly plentiful - definitely a good size but wouldn't say it matched my expectations. Overall a nice upscale spot, would highly recommend reservations!

Love the food
Good prices
Happy hour is awesome and really good prices


Def would come back
Overall is good but the udon was a little bit salty and pricey

Got the spicy seafood udon noodle soup. It was delicious, and ambience is very cool. Not a 5-star because the chopsticks they have were weirdly too skinny to be of much use for the thick udon noodles, which made them difficult to use, and the spoon for the broth is this huge spoon made of metal, which is very heavy. I couldn't enjoy the meal 100% because of the actual physical effort it took to eat it. But will definitely come back!

Great spot for dinner with friends. Their location is huge so its good for large parties. They have a wide selection of noodles and soups so you'll definitely find something you'll enjoy.

I ordered the beef truffle udon and the curry udon on two separate occasions. These noodles come is super large bowls with a shit ton of food so if you eat a lot like I do its a great place! I recommend the beef udon people who try it for the first time, and the curry if you really like curry!

Yes! Yes! Yes! Seriously, this was the best udon I've ever had. This is a great location right in Union Square (easy to get to!). There is a lot of space in the restaurant (there are various rooms with seating). The specialty is handmade udon-- both thin noodles and thick noodles. I had the hot and spicy chicken udon with thin noodles. It was in an egg drop broth. It had a kick but not too much to be uncomfortable. My friend had the fried tofu udon with thick noodles and she loved it. The serving sizes are HUGE (but, admittedly, I ate almost all of it).

I often go here on Sunday afternoons with a big group of friends (10-12 people). They're always very accommodating to big groups! Really appreciate this  Last time I went I ordered Spicy Seafood Jigae Udon and it was really tasty! The portion is definitely huge because I can't finish it and have to take it to go. The noodles are very fresh and chewy. Also, the dish is not that spicy (so don't worry for those of you who's worried it might be too spicy). So would definitely would recommend this place!

This udon place is awesome. I especially love their $2 beer happy hour special. Inside has a lot of seating, and the staff is pretty attentive, given the number of people they have to serve. Price-wise, very reasonable for the portions you get: medium or large at the same price. Of course, I got the large.

Tsuruton Curry Deluxe: Thick udon noodles, marinating in flavorful curry broth and surrounded by loads of beef, chicken katsu, and shrimp tempura -- a lot to love here. The broth was an excellent base; I came hungry, and this broth definitely helped fill me up. All of the meat was tasty, especially the beef -- tender and bite-sized. The chicken katsu was definitely good, but it would have been better if some of the slices of "chicken" weren't just fried batter -- a minor complaint. The shrimp was also very good. Overall, this dish was great. I would get it again, but there are too many items on the menu to try first. 

Price: 4/5
Quality: 4/5
Quantity: 5/5
Service: 4/5
Atmosphere: 4/5

This is one of my frequent visit ramen places near school. So I took my family here during their short stay in nyc. Usually the server would introduce the menu to you or at least ask if you've been here before. But this time the lady didn't ask any questions before order which was a little bit disappointing. The food was good as usual. Love the wagyu beef sushi! And surely we ordered the large ramen bowl, which this place is most famous for. My mom ordered sukiyaki ramen; she thought it's a bit too sweet in the end. So don't order it if you think you can't accept Japanese sweet flavor. The desserts were really nice; they had lady m cakes and water cake.
The seats they arranged for us was under the staircase, so it was a bit dark.

Great place for udon noodles. We walked in early on a weekday evening without reservations and got a table right away. The seating decor is  partly done in bamboo Japanese style and it's very nice. There's 50% off on all drinks if you hit the happy hour which is before 6PM and also sit by the bar I think, not sure about that part. 

Coming to the food, we ordered seafood udon large and spicy pork belly udon regular. The latter had two small pieces of pork belly for $24. I am highly dissatisfied with the portion of protein in the udon. I do not recommend this dish, if you don't want to feel shortchanged like me. I have had $15 udon with better portions in malls.

The theme of Tsurutontan would have to be their HUGE udon bowls. The large size here is definitely one of the biggest servings of udon I've seen! Here you can get a regular or a large size for the same exact price. This is reflected in the pricing, as each bowl will cost around $20 or more. 

We had the wagyu truffle udon and the tuna tartare cones. Not only does their udon come in large offerings, but the flavor is great! The broth is a 10/10 to me, as it's very rich and flavorful. The noodles are of excellent quality, and the toppings are tasty. I do recommend avoiding the tuna cones though. It's a pretty bland tasting dish for the price.

The service here was excellent and attentive. I also enjoyed the presentation of the food. It's not crazy fancy but it really does elevates Udon. The menu can be a bit overwhelming as there is so much to choose from, but luckily they highlight their best sellers and even dedicate a whole page to them. 

Overall, as a lover of Udon and huge portions, this place does it right. The servings here are can be really big, but you're getting quality and not just quantity. Be prepared for a bit pricier dinner than your typical udon restaurant, but if you're dining with someone else, a large bowl can easily feed two. I would definitely recommend Tsurutontan.

My go-to udon place. A fun place to bring friends or family or dates since they have huge bowls and huge spoons (great for cute pics) food itself is so great, noodles are never overcooked. Their happy hour menu is offered at great prices too and so far haven't come across an appetizer I didn't like.

The ambience was pretty good
Service was great 
The uni creamy udon noodle, however, was too heavy and sweet...
The truffle wagyu thin noodle was pretty good but the beef was SO chewy and greasy... doubt if it's real wagyu 
The spicy tuna roll was pretty awesome tho 
The proportion was big but it was 90%noodle and 10% of actual ingredients foods. 
Price should be a bit lower considering the quality of foods

Bathroom 1 Service 0 Food 4 Average 1.66.

Bathroom was pretty bad. Long wait there was 1 bathroom for women and 1 bathroom for unisex. So men had to wait for the unisex one. The traffic is unbelievable you'd think they have more than 1 bathroom. Its also noisy. I don't know why it has music blasting louder than it is outside the restroom. It's dirty from constant use because one bathroom serves around 50 people. There's an air drier. Thats a plus.

Service was pretty horrendous. One of the worst. We had a reservation at 8pm and we were sat at 9:10pm. Also got one of our orders wrong and the person got the food when everyone else finished theirs. The server left in the middle of the dine-in as well so we had no waiter for the last 30 minutes. This was top 3 worst service of all time in nyc.

Food was good. Its worth the hype a little I guess. I had the uni creme udon. Really heavy and good. All the udons were good. Not worth dying for though. Also appetizers were good. Had fried chicken and tuna wraps.

I hope they get their things together. This would be good if they actually had a system and an actual bathroom.

Amazing udon!! The restaurant looks pretty small from the outside, but it goes deep to the back, and there are upstairs seating area and a side room. We got a reservation online just 30 mins prior to showing up, and that turned out to be a good idea because there were parties waiting to be seated when we got there, but we were seated within 5 minutes. 

I got the US wagyu and mushroom sukiyaki udon, and it was undeniably delicious!! I got the regular size, but it was enough to share with 2 others (who had already had burgers before we went to this restaurant). The broth was perfect, and the meat was great! The mushrooms went surprisingly well with the udon! We also ordered drinks and the Lady M layered matcha cake! For drinks, I highly recommend their matcha drink - the matcha flavor hides the alcohol flavor so well! The old fashioned was good too. I got the mezcal negroni, but I wouldn't recommend that one unless you really, really like mezcal. 

The matcha cake was to DIE for! When I saw the cake on the back of their menu, I knew I HAD to get it - after all, matcha is my favorite dessert flavor!!  it comes with some azuki bean paste, mochi balls, and matcha ice cream (with super rich taste!), so it was spectacular - almost stole the show from the udon!

If you love udon, definitely try to come here if you're in the area. The consistency of the noodles were great. They were firm and thick. But to be honest, the main star of the dish was the broth. I got the sukiyaki udon. It was the perfect balance between sweet and salty noodles. My party had arrived before opening time and there was already a waiting list. Granted we had a larger party of 12 but they were able to accommodate to us by splitting up our party intro two smaller groups but sitting us close to each other. Our server was very kind and welcoming. She answered any questions that we had with a smile and was very attentive. Just a PSA, there are two bathrooms for women. If you go down the stairs, there is an additional bathroom but it is only for women. The ambience was very modern, and aesthetically pleasing. It was a very lit up restaurant which can be an issue for certain restaurants. Overall great experience and can't wait to be back!

Horrible customer service. I asked for my Tan Tan Udon to have no pork and add an egg. It came no egg with pork. My waitress took it back, came back 10 minutes later with the same bowl, with some pork picked out and an egg on the side. I didn't want to wait another 10 minutes when my party was already half done with their meals so I ate around the pork as best I could. Then I asked the waitress if I could order some sushi to go, she said they don't do that, but I was able to take my udon leftovers?  I asked to speak to the manager, who was very  rude, and she said the same thing. So I guess I should have just order the sushi, not eaten any and then would have been able to take it home! The food was good besides getting the wrong order twice, but I'd only go back for takeout!!!!!
Overrated noodle and horrifying service. Waited 40 mins with a reservation - if you can't guarantee seats then do NOT allow reservation then. Also the noodle is just average.

Made rsvp via online for 3. We still waited abit when we got there, but it wasnt bad being that it was a saturday night. The decor of the restaurant looks nice, kind of reminds us of DomoDomo.

We were seated and our waiter was Bruhan. There were a couple of things throughout the night that kind of resulted to me giving a 3 star review. The food is good. Udon noodle soup was very flavorful and came in a huge portion (mainly soup), sushi was also very fresh and unique taste to it..

However, their menu stated happy hr was every day starting at 9pm, but our waiter told us he found out that they were not doing it this evening. Well im concerned cos its noted on ur menu. What if people came for the happy hr only? But meanwhile, the table next to us, their waiter allowed them to order from the happy hour menu with NO mention abt them not doing happy hr tonight. Hmm.

Food came, but our waiter took away our small plates.. and couldnt find him so we had to ask the bus boy (kudos to him, he might as well be a waiter) to get some for us. He also filled up our water when we asked.

Then desserts came, again we had no plates.. at this point we jus didnt bother anymore.

Food was good, but service really sucked.

I came back with my family and they all loved it! We tried the crab egg drop udon (hot), the wagyu and truffle udon (hot), the duck udon (hot), the deluxe (hot), and the sashimi salad udon (cold). Also the yellowtail sushi rolls. I know I said the sashimi wasn't the best last time but I think it was because the wintertime didn't offer the best selection. In the fall, it's soooo good and worth it! Trying thin udon noodles in cold soup is a must. I think the only thing I was iffy about was the wagyu truffle soup-- it was definitely too strong of a flavor for me. Everything else was delicious and fresh and our waiter Mike made us feel so welcome. He spoke Cantonese to my Chinese grandma! Hopefully we will come back soon.

Recommendation: The mentaiko cream udon is the best i ever had in life. The cream soup is so good that every time i come here thinking "I'm gonna get something new" but always ended up ordering this! My boyfriend ordered the tempura udon as always, which is really good too!

Wait time: 
Highly suggest you make a reservation ahead. If not, the wait is pretty long especially during rush hour.

Service:
Great as usual. Hot tea is served for free (not green tea) the noodles comes in 2 kinds: thick & thin. I personally prefer thin noodles. The size comes with 2 options as well: regular & large (for the same price!) I usually choose regular because the large is too much for me.

Also-- they don't have the option to take out the noodles you left if you don't finish them. Not sure if you can order and takeout.

Probably the best udon in the city -- the noodles have a nice texture that doesn't go completely limp or disintegrate five minutes after you start eating it (I'm looking at you, Udon West). I've probably been here about 10 times since it's opened and there's a reason why I keep coming back. 9 out of 10 times I've gotten the katsu curry udon; the one time I didn't, though it was nice to try something else out, I felt like I missed out. The spicy tan tan udon was nice, if you like cilantro. The curry broth, however, has a nice Japanese curry flavor and packs a bit of heat that is pleasant and not painful at all. Raku has a comparable curry udon option, I think theirs might be spicier but Tsurutontan has a better and bigger location (well suited for groups). 

The price is steep especially for a bowl of udon but it's well worth it and an upgrade from Udon West in terms of quality of the noodle and the broth.

Hands down one of the best udon spots in the city. Creative and sophisticated comfort food options served in huge portions. The hot and sour udon (fall/winter special) had tender thin slices of beef and assorted vegetables / egg in a spicy broth with citrus tones - absolutely unreal. 

Cool wooden aesthetic and great customer service as well!

Disappointing Udon experience - might go back to try the Uni Udon (if they don't run out of sea urchin again...).  

FOOD // They ran out of Uni the day that I came for lunch, so I ordered the Corn Kakaige and Sukiyaki Udon (one of their signature dishes). The Corn Kakaige had a nice texture to it, but it was SO bland. The sauces it came with helped, but I think GOOD corn kakaige should be able to taste good on its own and not with the help of a sauce? (maybe that's just in my opinion) I ordered the Sukiyaki Udon with thick noodles and large size (it doesn't cost more for large). The udon broth was very sweet and maybe I'm not used to how sweet it was. The noodles were well done and nicely chewy. However, there was a FRUIT FLY IN MY NOODLES, so I couldn't enjoy my noodles. Maybe I was being picky, but I didn't have time to wait for another bowl since I was catching a flight.

SERVICE // I made a reservation before showing up, but they took a while to get my table ready. The service is average - servers and hostess were not particularly friendly, but you're not really here for exceptional service. I did appreciate that they removed the udon off my bill since I didn't even eat more than a few bites before noticing the fly. 

ATMOSPHERE // Modern udon shop, sort of what I would expect in Japan. Nice decor, felt quite authentic. 

PRICE // It's a bit on the pricey side, but if you order a large portion, it's about right. 

I MAY come back to try the Uni Udon, but if they don't Uni again, then this place is going on my U-don't list.

Thick and Large! That's how I like my udon. First off, the menu was well organized. I could easily differentiate the dashi udon from the curry udon and from the stir fry udon. My party of 6 each ordered their own bowl and WOW were the bowls huge. You're given the option of thick or thin noodles and either a small or large portion (large meaning extra noodles with no extra price). 

The party's overall favorites were the Curry Deluxe and the Tsurutontan Deluxe. Both came with tempura. 

Tip: move the tempura out of the bowl when the food is served so your tempura batter doesn't get soggy like mine did. :( but the shrimp was still good.

Only downside was that all the seaweed, egg plant and other sides that came in my Tsurutontan deluxe were battered and soggy since they were sitting in my soup. 

Food: 9/10
Service: 8/10
Ambiance: 9/10

Love love love this place. It's basically ramen but with udon noodles!! I got Tsurutontan Curry Deluxe ($24) which comes with two pieces of shrimp tempura, pork katsu and a beef short plate which almost tasted like brisket. The broth is real thick - yum yum. The pork katsu was so flavorful and crispy and when slightly dipped into the curry broth, it was basically instant nut. Note that the curry broth is beef-based as an fyi. Absolutely delicious and huge bowl. The bowl is larger than my face and the noodles are perfect for a cold day in the city 

They also ask if you would like thick or thin noodles, but I personally would prefer thick udon noodles since the broth is thicker and it matches better with their soup noodles. I feel that the thinner noodles are more for the dry stir fry noodle dishes.

Additionally, the ALL DAY happy hour is straight up amazing (might have just been an anniversary special). I got Sapporos for $2 at about 16 ounces per glass which is sweeeet. Service is also great and my server (Nicha) was so helpful and kind.
Came here Wednesday night with my friends but no one was at entrance area and it took 5min to take a seat even though not enough customer.

AH-MAZING udon here! The only issue is that it is really hard to come here when it is during busy lunch or dinner time, but otherwise a great place for good value especially during their happy hour or lunch hours. Their seats are actually not comfortable either. The udon is where it is at and very filling!

Dependable udon place for big groups. They take reservations online, which makes it easier for a big group.

I've been here a few times and see that they have changed their menu. The most popular dishes are in the center pages and they didn't disappoint. I had the beef hot and sour soup udon, it had mushrooms, eggplant, thinly sliced beef and eggs like the ones in an egg drop soup. The curry udon is much heavier but a great choice for a cold winter day.

The deluxe versions have more toppings on top but it comes out to be about the same portions. They don't have the adding extra noodles option anymore but you can choose the thickness of your udon (i prefer thinner since it soaks up all the soup flavors). If you're looking for something lighter, the duck soup is great as it's the dashi base, which is the more traditional clear soup.

We got a side of uni rice bowl ($9) but you only get 1 small piece on top. It's also too much food on top of the udon. Will want to come back and try other flavors.

Tsurutontan has long been on my list of places to try as their giant bowls of udon have been all over social media.  This chicly decorated restaurant is huge with plenty of seating, but I recommend making a reservation.  With a resy, we still waited 15-20 minutes for a table for 2 as folks were slow to clear out.

My friend and I started with the chicken karaage which was a well sized portion for the price and very nicely cooked.  Then we shared a large bowl of tan tan udon with pork belly and thick noodles.  The bowl was disappointing.  It is really just a large bowl with a normal portion of noodle.  The noodles tasted homemade but it felt like a marketing gimmick.  If we had not ordered the chicken, we would have left very hungry.

Tried Tsurutontan again tonight in hopes to have a better experience, and left incredibly disappointed. My previous visit my food was incredibly slow to come out (and only came out when my friend and I asked for the check to leave after an hour). Tonight was the same issue. We ordered a spicy tuna roll and cucumber salad. The cucumber salad came out after the tuna roll was finished. Then we waited another half an hour for our food. When we asked the server for the check without our main entrees, which never came out, our dishes magically show within a minute this. I won't be returning to try this place for a third time.

The first few times I went I remember this place being pretty good but I went again recently and was disappointed. I would recommend getting udon-tempura/nabekyaki. Last time I got the sashimi which was ok, the fried chicken- overcooked, a roll (forget the name but it had jalapeño in it)- p good, uni cream pasta- this was very underwhelming. The uni cream pasta soup tbh tasted to me like a canned soup- very watery, lukewarm, it did not even go well with the uni. I would stick to getting sukiyaki or nabeyaki.

Don't you just love Resy? 
Located in Union square area
Plenty of people started to line up but hopped on Resy 2 days before.

Modern and chic inside. 
Feeling myself in the building type of feel. 
Tons of options of udon you can never go wrong.
Wagyu with truffle?! hell yes please very indecisive  due to either wagyu with curry flavors or uni?? so thank goodness my foodie friends ordered all different things that way I was able to test try.

Portions are large and you can add more noodles for free but I felt like will be eating a lot later. Results of 3 different soups- bold and delicious flavors. I was impressed and kept bitchin why don't we have these options in the bay for an affordable price? 

Ps there is more than Udon, I want to come back and try thier sushi and bao's.
Don't care what else you eat here as long as you order the maitake mushroom appetizer. I don't want to over sell it. Just try it. Trust me.
Not impressive at all. Big bowels make it look worth the price, but the taste of the soup and noodles are just average. This place is overrated.

First I will say this is a very popular place with cool interior design. It was busy!  The reason for my 2 star rating is that I am a new vegan and there was only one entree that the waiter said was truly vegan, the Udon noodles with vegetables and tofu. Fair enough, but it was really a plate of noodles with a few mushrooms and pieces of tofu without many other vegetables . A very oily sauce with a ton of sodium. Just not a very healthy or satiating meal though the flavor was nice.

A bright spot were the appetizers of the veggie roll with avocado, the edamame and the crushed cucumber salad. Good and healthy.

Overall if your vegan you can find many better options in NYC.

Udon here is still very good, but the bathroom was a little messed up.  I was there at like 3pm and the bathroom looked like nobody checked it for 3hrs during lunch time.  Properly managed restaurants check bathrooms every 30 minutes or so to make sure it's not messed up.  It seems like there's no management oversight in regard to that and that makes me worry what may be happening in the kitchen too.

One dish sold me! Truffle Creme with Crab and Mushroom. So good. The appetizers are good. The place has a good vibe and energy. Nice size, and it's really simple. The night I was there it was packed. We had reservations for a table, and the servers were still on point. The food came out promptly time. I was just impressed, because of the number of people there I was expecting a long wait. I recommend checking this place out.

I've come here a few times and had great experiences. The first time i came i didn't realize how large the plates were and ordered too much. However since then I always share with my dinner mate. Cocktails are decent but the noodles are delicious. Here on a cold winter night? You'll love your experience. The hot noodle cuisine will only add to the warm intimate setting that will induce coziness upon your entrance.
We went there for the first time last week. Great food, price, service and ambiance. Would totally go back.

I love the variety they offer on the menu. My personal favorites are the curry udon and the wagyu shabu udon in truffle dashi. 

It's also nice how the small and large portion are the same price, but only get the large if you're feeling REALLY hungry, because it is a huge portion. 

The only reason this place loses a star is because most of the times I've been here it was really hard to get the attention of our server, and the staff aren't always friendly.

A place to go if you have an insane noodle craving. They give it to you in really big bowls and to me it's a pretty large portion (I can never finish it). 

The noodles are chewy and good quality. Not mushy!! And I've tried the truffle mushroom one and it was really rich and creamy. I recommend this! It is a bit expensive though.

I haven't been the best at leaving reviews but this one, I had to make it a point to share with the cyber universe that I had the best bowl of udon noods for lunch today! I had the fried chicken in curry with thick udon noodles--so damn good! The ambiance was great and the decor was beautiful. I will definitely be back.

Love me a good big bowl of noodles and soup. Tried a few things here but the most recent one was:
- the curry deluxe 10/10: i looooove curry with noodles and the katsu and shrimp tempura on this was just perfect. 
- the mini salmon don 6/10: its really small and quality is just alright, wouldn't recommend for $6
Excellent customer service. Love the atmosphere of the place pretty big. Food was exceptional and had a very good time. Great for date night

Had a reservation for about 10 people for a Friday night and we weren't seated for almost two hours later. We hung out at the bar to pass the time where they have all day happy hour prices so pretty cheap and the drinks were actually good. Our waiter gave us a few plates of complimentary soy garlic chicken which were delish to make up for being seated so late. You have the option of getting udon or ramen noodles and doing a larger size for no extra cost. I got the wagyu truffle udon. Broth was super flavorful and definitely a good amount of truffle. The meal itself was a little too meaty for my taste but all in all solid dish. Our waiter knew the menu thoroughly and easily answered all our questions and gave us recommendations. Also, the accidentally threw out a couple of my friends' leftovers so they gave both of them another entree each on the house.

After an insanely long wait, 2 round of drinks with mouth watering soy garlic tatsuta chicken at the bar  we were finally seated. Our group of 3 each had a version of the the udon with beef or duck. Next time I'll get the thin noodles. Happy Hour kicking in again after 9p was a plus. Our server Marco was an absolute delight. He was the topping on our evening.

The udon was great. There are so many varieties that I had a hard time deciding what I wanted. However... the service here wasn't so great - my friend and I arrived at the restaurant 15 minutes after it opened and were told there will be a 10-minute wait. The 10-minute wait became 30 minutes. When we were finally seated upstairs, there were at least 5 open tables. Then it took another 20 minutes to get someone's attention to take out orders. A little reluctant to come back again.

The sushi looked nice. I should've gone with that.

Instead I ordered the lunch special which was a GIANT bowl of... something. It looked like brown mustard and had the same consistency, with noodles, and it was the largest bowl of anything I've ever been served in my life. It wasn't great, and I felt like I overdosed on sodium and carbohydrates. 

If I ever return here, I'll definitely be ordering a different dish. 

The ambiance was nice, and the service as great, too! It was "OK."

I wouldn't say this place serves the best udon but it is up there, considering I haven't tried many places specifically for udon. Listen, the regular and large bowls here are the SAME price. Regardless if you're hungry or not, the best way to go is get the large bowl!! If you don't finish it, you can bring it home and enjoy it then! It is quite an experience to get a large bowl and trust me, the bowl is SO BIG; it's like a pot instead of a bowl! The portion however isn't as large as the bowl. You should definitely get an appetizer or sushi or just another dish because you definitely won't be completely full with one bowl (at least I didn't!!) Make a reservation beforehand, it gets busy!!

The uniqueness of the menu makes this my absolute favorite udon restaurant.  I've been to both NYC locations once with a large party and once with one other person.  The midtown location has a shorter line in my experience. The combination of a sleek, modern atmosphere and great happy hour drinks makes it the perfect place for dinner.  

The menu is initially overwhelming, but the servers were patient and helpful in recommending options we might like.  The spicy tuna tatare cones seemed so strange at first glance, but it was delicious.  The creativity in the presentation and flavors was fantastic to experience.  Highly recommend exploring the appetizer and happy hour menu because there were so many other interesting options we wanted to taste.  I ordered the uni creme udon (not pictured), and I cannot praise it highly enough.  The richness of the broth was unlike any udon soup base I've ever tasted, and they give you a decent portion of pure uni on top of the noodles.  I think my friend ordered the spicy soondubu jigae udon, but I can't be completely sure.  I just remember it also tasting fantastic.

The presentation of the noodles was beautiful.  Each udon dish seemed crafted, in the sense that all the ingredients were added/placed with care and not thrown into the dish haphazardly.  The bowls were bigger than the size of my head.  Interestingly, the price of a small or large udon is the same; both come in the same size bowl, but the large has more noodles.  My friend and I both ordered the large, and we could finish just over half of the udon.  The portions are HEFTY.

I would 100% recommend this to anyone looking for modern restaurant that serves creative udon dishes.  I'm usually one to explore new eats, but I keep coming back here.

I come here at least twice a month with my girlfriends for 2 reasons:
1- Bar has Happy hour all day
2- Food is pretty tasty and inexpensive - just be AWARE they received *GRADE B* (eewww)

Now lets move on to the NOT SO GOOD part -

Bartender is the grumpiest/ slowest person alive (or at least in NYC!). Bar is ALWAYS empty and still takes him about 10 - 15min to take our orders and he always place our drinks all together in front of one of us (we are usually 4 people!!) leaving to us the job of distributing

You are probably asking why do we keep going back right? Answer is pretty simple, we go to the gym next door and is just a lazy option for us to grab a cheap drink/ catch up before heading home.

Very good chance this place will be closed early next year. Take advantage now.

Odd seating system, often the restaurant is less then half full but they still make you wait 10-15mins, this has happened most times I've been here.

There was no bartender for 10-15 mins, as in zero bartenders at the bar. When he got back and we got a drink our table was ready. 

That was the bad, here is the good

Food has gotten crazy cheap. After 9pm they have $4 draft beer, $8 Japanese Whiskey Hi-Balls, $7 Lychee Martinis, $6 rice bowls and discounts on this huge happy hour menu, $10 lunch special. The value is huge.

Service by the servers/bussers is friendly and fast (bartender is terrible)

Overall the restaurant is way too big for the amount of business they are doing. Too many service failures at the front door and bar. If they ever reimagined this place at 25-30% of the size it would be great. As of now I can't imagine we will see them around too much longer.
Best noodles in NYC. Great flavor profiles combined in to a classic Japanese form factor -- sea urchin creme udon, I'm looking at you.

I get it, trendy place and food. Don't waste your time and money on unorganized management, rude staff, mediocre, overpriced food.

We waited 45 minutes with a reservation. Had an extremely rude waiter. Lastly, the udon was overcooked.. Three strikes in my book. Won't be back.

Convenient location with an extensive menu! I like the dark interior and overall environment as well - great for either a casual meal out or a nice dinner. 

All of their udons are tasty! It just depends on what broth you're in the mood for. The bowls are pretty rich and the portions are huge. Unless you're extremely hungry, one order is enough to split! Their rolls are good as well - the fish (and other ingredients) are fresh. 

The service was a bit unorganized and I had to go out of my way to grab our waiter's attention several times. Other than that, a go-to for consistently good food!

Really delicious curry udon here! Service was fast,  touch stand off-site, but really good! Wasnt too spicy, but very, very flavorful. Go with the deluxe size because its same price, but different portions (strange notion). The katsu was tasty and so was the beef, the deluxe bowl was very good! Definitely try to avoid the rush because they very much dont seem equipped to handle a lot of people coming and on the weekends, lots of kids around so if waiting for a table for 2 with screaming kids is your thing, come on in. Wish they had more than one bathroom on a floor, with the amount of people eating there, you'd think thered be more facilities. Anywho, the food was good and I'll probably re-rate when I do eventually go back.

Have come here many times as it's my local. Lots of udon options, some traditional and some more fusion and most taste good. The servings are big but the bowls aren't cheap but large is the same price as small. Could be large pricing but giving you large for the same price makes you feel as though you're getting something for free.

What irks me about this restaurant is the host lady at the front. She's never friendly and often gives me attitude, either that or she just ignores me. She really needs to change her attitude or be replaced with someone more welcoming.

I was so excited to try this place but was kind of disappointed! The service wasn't great. It seemed like only one server was on a Saturday. The udon was good. They had a nice bite. Surprisingly the price of a regular bowl and a big bowl of udon is the same. We ordered a couple of appetizers as well. The mushrooms were good but a tad on the salty side. The pork belly was a little dry. The dumplings were average. Hubby ordered a rice and we waited almost an hour for it because the waiter had put a hold on it for some reason before he clocked out. When he finally got the rice he wasn't hungry so we took it to go. Hopefully we just went on a bad day and will try the place again.

This is my go to place whenever I'm craving udon. I love the many options there are but no matter what you get, it is delicious!! I've gotten soups in the past but this time I decided on a stir fry and there were no regrets. Tsurutontan has a taste that is uniquely theirs. I came home with leftovers and without asking, my husband already knew where I got it from. The restaurant itself is pretty spacious but even with that, it's usually busy no matter what day in the week; it is definitely worth the wait though. If you're craving udon, definitely give this place a try! Also, extra noodles is the same price as a regular amount of noodles  so if you're feeling like an extra noodle day, it doesn't have to be extra on your wallet.

I got the stir fry udon made vegetarian so it came with tofu and mushrooms. It's one of the yummiest things EVER. It's so flavorful and decent sized. You can get a larger size for no additional cost. My boyfriend got the same but with beef. We got the cold udon dipping dish to share. It was really good and the chilled noodles were refreshing. They have so many greats apps as well. I would only give it a 4 stars because it is a bit of a pricy place.

My sister and I had high hopes for this place as it has high Yelp reviews and we both like udons. However, we could not have been more disappointed... While they have great interior design and ambience, their udon... was mediocre at best. Served in a giant bowl, the udon tasted little different from the kind of udon I can make myself from instant noodle packages sold in Asian grocery markets... Taste and quality did not measure up to their high price. Way too disappointed and will never come back.

I love Tsurutontan! great atmosphere, large portions, and tasty ramen. A bit on the expensive side but I have never once been able to completely finish a course from here. Always wind up taking some home for the next day. Im particularly a fan of the spicier Ramens there, but I did however come here one time and there were shells pieces in my Crab ramen, which explains the 4/5, thankfully they let me get something else.

We ordered Spicy Tuna Tartar from the Happy Hour Food Menu. There was a purée of avocado, as well as the tuna tartar, then the "cone" holding the tuna tartar was very hard, it didn't pair well with the tuna. 

The Spicy Paprika Chicken Wings. They definitely lived up to the name of Spicy Paprika. It was a bit of a kick, and paprika has a very peculiar taste. The breading and chicken ratio was off, the chicken was okay, it wasn't something that was memorable. 

The Hot and Sour Udon. Definitely made the experience much better, the udon noodles itself is 5 out of 5. It's absolutely delightful, I could eat the noodles for breakfast lunch and dinner. As for the soup base, it was a bit thick, so it was hard for the noodles to get the flavoring of the soup. 

Overall, definitely go for any dish that has the udon noodles in it!

I got really excited when I found this place because I had such an amazing udon in Japan the previous year. I ordered a couple of appetizers to share with my friends and uni creme udon and mentaiko udon. Appetizers like mushrooms and chicken karage were ok. Nothing special. The noodles were chewy and had its own taste, but yet very bland. Noodle itself was very good but it did not go along with creme or sauce of the udon entrees. It felt like I was eating plain noodles and sauce separately. It was disappointment, but maybe I had too high expectations after Japan trip.

Went for lunch on Sunday and though the place was busy our party quickly got seated. We ordered 3 different dishes all of which were very flavorful. The duck udon that I ordered had a very balanced broth that wasn't too salty. They have regular and large size which is the same price and the quantity of noodles is the only difference.

Always a good choice! No matter what the weather outside is, you'll have a noodle option. Cold? Get a warm duck udon or wagyu beef udon to warm the soul. Summer days? Get the uni, ikura and scallop udon that's refreshing (while the fish itself is super fresh). The mentaiko udon is always a good option, as well as the curry!

Portions are plentiful and for the same price, you can choose small or large portion of noodles. Get the large. You also have a choice of thin or thick udon so I love that you have preferences. There's never not something you can get and think of. Staff is super friendly from hosts, to the person who seats you, to the waiters.

A little overpriced, although the portions are great. I don't love the ambience or location. Compared to Raku....it just cannot compare. There are  A LOT of udon options though. I would go if I'm in the area, but nothing that special.
The seat was super sunken ( the cushion was too used or something) and it was so not comfortable. The waiter didn't change our seats after all, horrible horrible experience.

They changed the tip amounts by themselves. The food was just ok. The service was not good at all. The host lady at the front has a huge attitude problem. She seems can not talk in a friendly way. So disappointed.

Update:
I took the customer copy with me and wrote the total on it. I am in my twenties so I think I can remember the exact number I put on the merchant copy. I know it's a hard question to clarify. You can say I changed it by myself. It has already happened and I don't want to stick to it. Hope you guys can fix the host problem as soon as possible.

Stopped in on a very rainy Sunday for a hot bowl of soup.  Second time trying this place out, but this time invited company.   Appetizers were amazing, came out fast, tasted fresh, and full of flavors.   Very large selection of noodle bowls,  one of the largest I've seen here in Mid town.  The portion sizes are more than enough and you'll always have left overs.  The reason for 4 out of 5 stars,  they charged $4 for flat soda.  We had 4 sodas so $16 in for bad soda.

We went there on the recommendation of friends. Nice little restaurant tucked in the side of 16th street. Food was good and service was pretty good too. We went early, around 545pm so didn't have to wait to be seated. Overall, was a good experience.

Menu has a wide selection of various udon noodles sorted by clear broth, creamy broth, cold udon, and customer favorites. They also have a nice assortment of sushi and sashimi. Separate menu also had several specials. 

We ended up choosing the salmon ikura roll, pork belly spicy tantan noodle, shrimp tempura udon in clear broth, and creamy uni udon. 

Salmon ikura roll was delicious. Rice had a nice texture and was topped with a nice helping of ikura. The udon is made fresh in-house and you can really tell the freshness with its nice el dente texture. Noodle comes in wide noodle or thin noodle - wide is what we normally see when we order udon. The bowl size comes in regular or large (large gets an extra helping of noodles so is good to share). 

I really enjoyed the porky belly spicy tantan - I wish there were a couple of extra pieces of the marinated pork belly. The broth is very rich and the spice really adds a kick. The noodle also had a few pieces of eggplant which helped break up the richness of the broth and spice. Great bowl of udon.

We didn't have any room left for dessert but we will definitely be going back to try more dishes there.

Go-to place for Udon. Lots of variety, tasty, and filling. Tried the cold sea urchin udon and the Tsurutontan Deluxe with tempura, seafood, chicken, beef, and egg. Someone next to us ordered the truffle dish which smelled so tantalizing it kept distracting me from my conversation.

Cozy, upscale atmosphere, plenty of seating room, efficient service, and solid food.

I fully intended to visit just for the stir fry udon and the maitake mushrooms, possibly the spicy tuna rolls for the photo. Went with some friends and accidently ordered a bunch of things.

The stir fry was excellent, very satisfying and not dry like some stir fry can be at times. The egg didn't really do much to elevate the dish, but I guess it made it seem more creamy. 

The corn was ok, not sure if this was worth it, but the sauces it came with were delicious. 

Spicy tuna rolls spoke for themselves, although there should have been more of them, perhaps 6 instead of 4 for the order. The rolls had a nice crunch to compliment the tuna.

The mushrooms were outstanding. Maiktake mushrooms had a lot of flavor and a wonderful meaty texture that other types lack. It's worth ordering a second dish for both the crunchy bits that the mushrooms sit on and of course more Maitake.

The water ball was an interesting dessert, I don't think I'd get it again, but it was an interesting experience to have all the components together in 1 spoonful.

Excellent food! Has made me an udon convert and now I crave it! You get a large portion of udon for your money. And if you happen to come for a later dinner, having the happy hour start back up around 9 is a big win!

Wagyu truffle udon!!! Need I say more! Hahaha!
This place is only open certain hours. Please be sure to check before you come. To be safe, try to call in for a reservation. The restaurant is the fanciest udon place i ever seen. Really cool place for a date! 
Just a heads up, these udon bowls are huge so I highly recommend adding extra stuff like extra wagyu and mushrooms!
The broth is so delicious and perfect for those cold nyc winter nights :)
I really wish this place exist in SF!!!

Surprisingly large number of small tables as there's a second floor with tables tucked at the back. I only tried the uni scallop and salmon roe udon with thick noodles and the large portion which was a hefty $32. The scallops were okay but a little lacking in flavor. The roe got a bit lost in the broth which was soy and dashi based but too salty. The udon noodles themselves were perfect. The uni was fantastic and fresh but the portion wasn't huge. If I were to do it again, I'd have the uni udon, which seems to have an uni based sauce rather than a broth. That's $24. Both are in the cold noodle section. Service is efficient and attentive and friendly. I'd definitely come back.

Seems like this place is set up to make lots of $, but wasn't feeling any love from the food. My large Deluxe curry ($24) was uninspiring. Bland sauce, bland shrimp, huge chunks of meat.  The udon noodles were good.  Servers were nice, but it really feels like generating profit is more important than anything else.

This place seems to get pretty packed so I would suggest making a reservation. But we did arrive at 6oclock on a Friday night and overheard a party of 4 say the wait was about 30 minutes so it doesnt seem that bad.

The ambiance is great. Lights are dim but bright enough of you to see the menu. The area looks small but they do have rather large seating areas and even a smaller 2nd floor where we were seated. I think the waitress was really nice and she asked if this was our first time and spent some time going over the menu with us. There was an appetizer menu, a main menu, a drink menu, and a seasonal menu. She went through all the sections and explained the different types of broth and sizes of udon. I really appreciated that she took the time to do that 

The appetizers were amazing. The fried chicken was delicious, though it wasnt what I expected soy garlic to taste like. It had a sweet, spicy, tangy sauce so Im not even sure I ordered what I wanted, but it was great to no complaints. The shrimp tempura was fried and you can taste the freshness. The tempura was curled, unlike most places that fry their shrimp tempura straight. Thought that was interesting. It comes with spicy mayo which was added to a great component to the flavor.

Main courses we got the curry deluxe and uni creme udon. The uni creme udon only came with 3 small pieces of uni, and they were pretty fishy. Not the best uni I've had, but that broth, oh boy. The broth was so delicious. It has a slight sweetness to it and it is not too thick to make it heavy but it was still very creamy and smooth. I ordered the large thick udon with it and had no problem finishing it. My girlfriend ordered the curry deluxe and it comes with pork katsu, shrimp tempura and beef in japanese brown curry. The sauce was very flavorful and savory. After having some of her broth, it completely overpowered the uni creme broth. Weirdly enough I liked her order more and she liked mine more.

Dessert. Always room for dessert. They serve Lady M cakes here but we opted for the chocolate sponge mousse cake and the water cake. Both came with vanilla ice cream. The frozen raspberries that came with the chocolate cake were very tart so do not eat those by themselves, but its a fun prank to pull on your partner by having them eat it. The water cake was interesting. It is some sort of gelatinous ball that comes with soy powder to give it some texture and some sort of honey/syrup to give it flavor. Reminds me of herbal jello that you need to add syrup to to make it yummy.

I think this place was great. Everything looked delicious on the menu and my only problem was that I wasnt able to try more things. Will definitely be coming back.
Fantastic broth and udon noodles. Very nice sushi too. Big portions. Great service. 10/10 would recommend. Book in advance (can do it on the same day via app), it gets busy!

The decor is really nice. The place looks tasteful and a great romantic place to take a date. The lighting is dim and feels good. Soft lighting and warm heat makes this place inviting. The spacious waiting area is a nice touch. There is 3 levels of dinning area, but they are mainly using the ground and lower levels. There is plenty of seating, but the restaurant chooses to make people wait. It could be a staffing issues. If you want fast food, this is not the place. Service is a bit slow, but hopefully the food is worth the wait.

 The udon noodles was ok. The soup bar was way too sweet. I'm not sure how much sugar was put into the soup bar. I needed to drink a lot of water to dilute strong sugary taste. I would not order the udon again. Also, the udon was served in a huge bowl with a huge serving spoon. There portion was enough for two.
  The sushi was delicious. It was fresh, light and tasted great. I highly recommend the sushi.

Really really great udon. I've been here more than a handful of time and never been disappointed once. They have great udon noodles (great portion too ! Always go for the big portion). 

I've had the udon with tempura, the duck  truffle udon, curry udon these past months. If you're into curry flavor - definitely recommend their curry udon. 

Great happy hour price and selection, though never really been here specially for happy hour. Will try that next time!

My friends who recommended this restaurant raved about the uni udon so much that I thought uni udon is the only thing they serve - until I saw the menu with tons of different flavors of udon and a wide range of appetizers and other dishes. 

We had a group of 11 so we tried a couple appetizers: fried oyster, hamachi and grilled duck breast. All of them are on point. Fried oyster is juicy inside which I loved. Hamachi is totally refreshing and grilled duck is tender and delicious. 

I got the uni creme udon and my bf got the sukiyaki with Wagyu beef and mushroom. The soup of uni creme udon is very rich but not too cloying. I chose the thick noodle and it was pretty good. I wasn't particularly impressed by the sukiyaki just because I felt it tasted similar to what I could make at home myself, and the soup was too salty for me to keep having it.

However, I have to say that if you are going to get uni udon here, Get the one with the cold noodles!!!! It is THE BEST!!! My friends got the uni udon cold noodles and it tasted so much better!! A small tip: get the thin noodles if you are ordering the cold noodles! They're chewy and got the full flavor of the soup!

I didn't vote for 5 star because I didn't love every dish we had, but I'll definitely come back for their uni udon with cold noodles!!

Just OK. I definitely prefer Raku for udon, as their noodles have a better QQ texture and their broths are more multidimensional, but Tsurutontan will satisfy the noodle craving in a pinch. The space is HUGE! Also the menu is extensive, and looks like a good happy hour too.

I came in on a Wednesday weekday night and this place was already filled to the brim! I had come with two other friends and they require that you have your full party there prior to seating. I left my name down while waiting for my friends and when they arrived, I updated them that my full party was present. They quickly got us seated despite the heavy traffic of people and it seemed like they were pretty efficient with the turnover of people. We did however sit at the bar which was not too bad as we could still talk to one another easily. I ordered the waygu beef udon with truffle. Apparently you can choose to get a regular or large with most udon dishes with no additional cost so I chose the larger option with more noodles. I was taken aback with an initial reaction to the potent aroma of truffle with a taste of the pure broth. With the noodles though, the flavor ends up being a lot more subtle which nicely coats each bite. The meat was amazingly tender though limited. With the large size, I was mostly content by the end of the meal. Overall, I was generally satisfied by the food quality here and would want to come back again to try some of their other options.

Do not recommend the tempura here. The corn tempura had too much batter. The fried oyster also had a thick coating and came with a strange cross between mayo and egg salad. The tempura that came with my udon was the worst I've ever had. Greasy and the two shrimp were thin and mushy, the vegetables were a piece of seaweed, a thin sliver of eggplant, enoki mushrooms (from the look since there was no taste but grease), an almost normal slice of pumpkin, and possibly a shiitake mushroom. My husband said the ankimo (monkfish liver) was the worst he ever had. I thought it was ok but agreed it tasted oddly like tuna. He got the spicy udon with thin noodles which he said were mushy.  My daughter ordered the chicken udon with thick noodles.  I also ordered the vinegar cucumber with bbq eel. The cucumber was more garnish on top. We sat in the lower dining room (lunch on a weekday) which was very loud. The decor was nice with dynamic use of wood and modern elements. Too bad the food was such a disappointment.
Long wait time and charge $27 dollars for holding my friends birthday cake and was not provided good service

We came here for a friends birthday, party of 9. Asked the staff to store our cake for us, staff said it's going to be $3 per person. Total of $27 to store a 8inch cake in the fridge for 1 hour. What kind of scam are you running? This isn't my first time here but it WILL be my last.

I came to this place with a friend on Friday December 13th for happy hour. The hostess was a rude unhappy woman, the hostess is the first person you see when you get a restaurant, hiring friendly patient people is a must!  The server was great but when we received our bill  prices were not the same as in the menu, the menu said $13, the bill said $14, an appetizer was $9 but the bill said $13. We ordered all our food before 6 pm to get happy hour prices and still prices were different. We said something about this but  supervisor sent a server to tell us that the quality of what we received was better than expected. 
I do not appreciate small unclear and dishonest  "mistakes"

Amazing! The udon really did not disappoint and their bowls are huge. The variety is the thing that gets me because it is almost a fusion with their jigae options and my favorite udon is definitely the jigae udon. The udon's texture is so yummy and is absolutely my favorite udon noodles in NYC hands down. The service can be hit or miss though, and it is definitely on the pricier side for a bowl of udon.
