However, like I said, it's my favorite place for udon so that is all overlooked. It's a blessing (for my stomach) and a curse (for my wallet) to be close to the midtown location for lunch. Both locations have great quality food.

I don't know if I can say enough good things about this restaurant. First of all, the dining area is beautiful and well set up. The dim lights are great for the mood, but bright enough that you can see your dining companion and the menu just fineEven on a fairly busy night we only had to wait about 5 minutes for a table. 

The menu looks intimidating but if you ask the waiter to explain it it's actually very well set up and categorized. We started with the seared salmon sashimi and the smashed cucumber salad. Both were light yet packed with flavor. I'm not usually even a cucumber fan but whatever they were seasoned with with delicious. We got happy hour pricing which made the appetizers totally reasonable $12 and $6 respectively. 

Something to note, the udon bowls are HUGE. You think you know how big the bowl is and you're wrong, they're bigger than your head even with the "regular" portion. They're absolutely amazing. 

I got the Katsu curry and I can honestly say it's one of the best things I've ever eaten, I'm taking last meal kind of awesome. The broth is silky and flavorful and not too spicy. The katsu is crispy and tender. I got the thick noodles which were everything I wanted, they had the perfect texture, and really held up to the curry broth. $18 for the dish, which may seem high but for the portion and how delicious it was that's a steal. 
My friend got the Shrimp tempura udon which has a much lighter broth. The tempura comes on the side so it stays crunchy. She loved it!

We accidentally stayed a few minutes past close and they were really nice about it and didn't try to rush us out. 
12/10 I seriously can't recommend them enough!

AMAZING UDON. A restaurant that specializes in something and does it right. The process of getting seated is a very hectic process even before dinner rush (small waiting area at the front, people pushing and shoving to get inside). The interior is pretty spacious, but I would definitely make reservations even if you have a small group. The place was super busy at 5:30pm on a Wednesday night.

Loved that they have Happy Hour even though it is a very limited time (most of the dishes offered on Happy Hour are $2-5 off normal prices). Happy Hour is 5-6pm, 9pm-Close Mon-Fri (please double check). 

I ordered the Fried Oysters (5/5- fried perfectly, decent portion to share), and the Spicy Scallop Roll (4/5- a bit too much rice to fish ratio, but it was HH price so can't complain). I then ordered the Uni Ikura Scallop Udon ($32, cold dish). Even though the thick noodles were wonderfully chewy and had a decent amount of fresh seafood, I didn't LOVE this and wished I had ordered another udon dish. Don't get me wrong, it was still good but if I come back I wouldn't re-order this. Just wasn't the right udon dish for my personal taste (a bit too salty with the amount of Ikura).

Overall, an excellent place to get super chewy Udon. I will definitely be back to try the other dishes.

My friend recommended their udon noodle which is very delicious. The server told me I can upgrade to a large portion at no extra cost; however it is still much smaller than usual lunch meal at $18. I wonder if its really an upgrade or they just say that to make customers happier. The place is huge, good for large party.

Hands down best udon I have ever had. 
Service was a top notch, food tastiness and portions were also stellar. 
Interior of restaurant was moody and elegant! Love this
place!
The food is amazing and has good prices. Only downside that we had reservations and the made us wait 20 minutes. I would definitely go back but not at peak hours.

massiiiiiive bowls-super delicious udon! We got the spicy seafood jjigae udon which has shrimp, clam, scallop, kimchee broth and the duck udon which includes udon with duck meat, meatballs and green onion. Both were really flavorful and the udon was chewy but not over or undercooked. We went during happy hour so we got the soy garlic fried tatsuta chicken for $9 (regular price $13) as an appetizer. It's just fried chicken pieces drizzled in a soy garlic sauce- pretty good! Also got a lychee tini for $3.99 bc of happy hour as well.

I have been to this restaurant three times and LOVE their food! However their service needs to be improved, specifically their host. I had a dinner reservation for 2 yesterday and our table wasn't ready in time. Immediately we were annoyed, but we thought waiting a few minutes wouldn't hurt. Fifteen minutes pass and more people had been seated. My partner and I grew more hungry and impatient, so I go ask the host about our table. She apologized and guided us to our table. It had been set for awhile and I believe she forgot to call our party. Despite the poor host service, the food never fails to deliver.

A hot bowl of something is always good to have on a cold, chilly Christmas time Saturday night.  Stop #2 on the food tour was Tsurutontan because my bestie has a deep love of udon, and this is conveniently located close to the Union Square holiday markets.    

If you plan to walk-in Tsurutontan without reservations like we did, you will more than likely be asked to sit at the bar, which actually declined.  Yeah, we could've been seated faster, but we honestly wanted to be seated to better enjoy our experience.  I kinda felt the bar would've been a decent alternative if I was dining alone, but when you have friends visiting, you want a more relaxing vibe.  The wait time was 40 minutes to an hour, but we were willing to wait to be comfortable.  It looked like other customers made reservations in advance, and most groups were 4 people plus.  Most of the patrons were Asian, so I further felt that we stumbled upon a well known gem of a place with magical noodles.  I'm thrilled!

We finally get called, and we walk into the left and step down a few stairs to a seating area with a very clean and simple stick wall to separate a long table of patrons.  It created a very nice illusion of privacy, but not completely; I really liked the concept.  We sat on a couch kind of a bench together side by side.  It was a little tight, but we made it work.

For starters, we got the spicy tuna roll in a fried wonton wrapper cone, and they were absolutely delicious!  We easily could've had another order, they were that good.  Definitely understand why these are a crowd pleaser.  For the entree, we decided on the spicy pork belly udon, with a mini bowl of sukiyaki.  The sukiyaki caught me by utter surprise as to how much it tasted like a bowl of Japan.  The flavors screamed Tokyo, and I was getting so many good flashbacks.  The udon broth was fatty and definitely spicy, in a numbing good way.  Highly recommend this amazing duo for sure!

I'll be back that's a guarantee!

I went in on a Monday afternoon for lunch and waited about 20min before being sat, which was expected due to the popularity of the restaurant. Once we got sat though, it took forever for the server to greet us or even just acknowledge us. 

I understood it was the week of Christmas and decided to wait patiently. However, she took forever to greet us, forever to take our orders, forever to bring us our food, forever to bring us our checks, but were so fast to clean our table and get us out. 

I'm not sure if they were understaffed for a busy week or if they're usually like this, but I did not appreciate their service what so ever. 

On top of that, in the midst of our meal, we heard a woman scream and get up off her seat because there was a cockroach crawling on her table. It was so big we could spot it from the other side of the room. 

The food was good but no extraordinary. And because of such terrible experience we had, I don't think I'll be coming back anytime soon.

Was craving udon and a friend recommended this place. We arrived early on a weekday evening, so we didn't wait long at all. 

There are a lot of options, so be prepared to deliberate. I ordered the Tsurutontan Deluxe, which came in an almost comically large bowl with an equally large spoon. The broth was light, warming, and full of good things like pieces of chicken, tempura vegetables, and shrimp. The udon was perfectly cooked with great texture. Even though the bowl was really large, it was the perfect amount of food. My only comment is that the tempura was served in the broth, so it began to lose its crunchy texture pretty quickly (which I didn't mind too much). 

Even though business started to pick up towards later in the evening, the staff never rushed us and continued to refill our waters. All in all a lovely place for udon.

Not great. This place was heavily hyped up. And they kept pushing our wait time. I remember asking an update on our wait time and the woman basically chewed my head off. I thought I had asked nicely enough, but I did not expect the venom I recieved. The food wasn't bad, but it certainly wasn't anywhere near the hour plus wait. I've had equal food and even better for virtually no wait.
They asked if we wanted dessert we said no and they asked us to leave. We weren't rowdy or anything. They just were trying to chip at the wait-list. Which I get, because the wait was ridiculous, but it was not the restaurant experience that I was hoping for at all. I'm all about time is money, but we had barely finished our meals. I will not be going back and I will not be recommending this place.

We arrived for lunch on Christmas eve, and even with a reservation, the wait time was long - but it was SO WORTH IT. The portion size is gigantic, big enough for two people to share. Our waiter was so friendly, and was really helpful with his recommendations and explanations of dishes. 

I'm looking forward to the next time I eat here!!

Was desperately, DESPERATELY in need of sukiyaki. And wouldn't you when it's freezing outside? Having not had sukiyaki in over two decades, I was ready to settle for a mediocre bowl of that sweet and salty mix, but Tsurutontan refused to compromise and delivered one of the best bowls of sukiyaki I've ever had. At the very least it delivered the BIGGEST bowl of sukiyaki. No but seriously it was enormous, and apparently every bowl is enormous regardless of what you order. I got the thick noodles to pair with the soup, and they were perfectly cooked. The broth, simply sublime. I slurped. I laughed! I fell in love. It was a religious experience. 

My friends also ordered the uni creme bowl. We both love uni, but the creme was a smidge too heavy for us, though the first few mouthfuls were truly heavenly. If you're feeling in a creamy mood (and don't pretend like that's not a thing, it's definitely a thing), then this is for you. The uni wasn't overpowering, and it's not like a giant heap so uni lovers, temper your expectations.

Bad policy! When you have a customer that wants to sit at a table not bar, you don't say I can't sit you there
Especially when the place is only half full. Maybe the food is good ? Will never know attitude is more important to me. Poor

5 stars for food and portions. So far I've had the spicy seafood jigae, duck udon, wagyu truffle udon, beef sukiyaki, and a few random sushi pieces. Flavors were robust and I highly recommend the food. Service was fine. Definitely can get busy so be prepared to wait in line.

-2 stars for not even able to place a take out order on the spot. Was told I have to go through seamless even though I was right there....now sure how that makes any sense at all. Not sure how this is different than placing an order at the bar? 

Also the seamless menu is limited so I wasn't even able to get the noodle dish that I wanted (the spicy seafood jigae).

Tan Tan Udon soup is cold, pork belly is icy cold.  Curry udon is Luke warm.  We ordered four appetizers but only three came.  We finished the udon and finally the salmon came.  Service is a bit rough.  We asked to warm up the tantan udon.  It came back 15 minutes later.  My sons are regular at this restaurant and they said regularly the food and service were good, not like today.  it's probably New Year's Eve and the regular staff is off.

I initially liked it here so much since the food is amazing.  One of the rude Asian waiter just destroyed of all my good impression about this nice restaurant.   We were dissatisfied with the seating arrangement one day, and kindly asked one of the mal sissy Asian waiter to see if we can switch.  He arrogantly said he couldn't help and said If we would like to change, we have to get up and speak to the host.  Then we r like fine, not a big deal.  Later on, since I couldn't find my waiter, I kindly ask this sissy arrogant Asian waiter If he can bring me a spoon for my soup, and he just said "oh, you have to wait" and of course the spoon situation never happen.  I think the restaurant should carefully evaluate waiters qualifications before hiring.

Came here on a busy Saturday and this place was completely packed. Wait was over an hour so my group and I decided to get drinks else where prior to sitting down. We ordered the curry deluxe 24, beef udon, small order of uni and salmon roe, and also the spicy tuna rolls. Wow these bowls are massive and packed with so much broth and udon. The Japanese curry was mild and rich in flavor. You want to eat the katsu and tempura rather quickly as they do get soggy. The beef in the udon comes out a little rare and you'll want to dip it in the broth a lil longer for it to cook. The small sized uni and salmon roe was perfect with our dish. I was really please with the service here. We felt like we had 3 servers at all times. The restaurant has a cool dark ambient feel to it. Extra comfy leather chairs and plenty of sitting for large parties. I really enjoyed my experience here. Flavors were on point and the massive bowls blew me a way. Highly recommend this to anyone that loves udon and authentic Japanese cuisine.
Service was friendly and efficient and the udon noodles were fresh and delicious. We had the katzu curry and duck udon. We also liked the $3 Sapporo after 9 pm. Yum!!

Overrated. Even though the udon noodle was made in house, it wasn't super bouncy like the one we tried in Boston's Porter Square. Maybe it's because I don't like sukiyaki broth or maybe the broth was just okay, there was no WOW factor. Luckily, there was no line or else it would have felt like I cheated my stomach on something substandard when there's so many other good restaurants in NYC.

This place is big, has a lot of seating and is conveniently located in Union Square. The food is alright, but if you charge premium prices, they really shouldn't serve their food with chipped bowls (this leads me to believe it is a Chinese operated establishment, proper Japanese people would never do this). The udon was good but soup could have been hotter. Bowl was also humongous compared with the regular portion, I guess they use the same bowls whether you get the regular or large portions.

One of my favorite places for udon in Manhattan. The self made udon noodles here are perfect every single time. I usually go for the wagyu udon. For me, the sukiyaki is too sweet and the truffle overpowers the rest of the broth, but I know others who love it. The happy hour is good for sake and appetizers, as well!

Definitely come for the lunch menu as it is so much more worth it. 

I came in with a friend and waited 5-10 minutes to get seated. We assumed it was because they were busy but realized it wasn't busy at all and a lot of tables were empty. We asked for a booth but it was apparently reserved ahead of time which I would recommend because in the end, the server seated us next to each other which made it a bit difficult to talk while eating. Our server was very knowledgeable about the food and warned us the curry udon was heavy so we didn't get it. 

I got the spicy udon (I believe it is called tantan udon if I recall correctly) while my friend got the beef udon. Boy, the spicy udon isn't spicy spicy but it made me cough several times because I didn't expect the kick. "It hits your throat" as my friend said. All in all, it still felt heavy in the end and I wished I just got regular instead of extra noodles (free upgrade) because I couldn't finish the rice that came with the lunch special. If you just want to check this place out, come during lunch special. Our total came out to about $26 before tip (2 large udon + 2 bowls of rice) which is a lot cheaper than regular price (I think $20 for one bowl of udon).

Best udon noodle I have had, the soup was not hot enough.  

We tried the fried chicken hot and sour soup and the Waygu sukiyaki noodle.

Neither was hot enough.  The place was busy, and service was decent.

It's about 3.5 stars.  For a noodle soup it's pricy.

The bowls were made to be posted on the gram.

But my bowl was chipped.

The service was not its usual. A regular  for their awesome HH specials! Staff is awesome here but our waiter was short tempered  and just was in a bad mood. I took a friend here and he did not have a good dining  experience!

Get the large portion of noodles!!! You can never have enough  noodles. And that truffle roll o0oo so delicious!

Been here a few times .. I loved it when I first came here but now it's okay at best. The ambiance is really nice which I can appreciate but the food is only meh. I came here with my boyfriend and two other friends, and they've never been here and they just were not impressed. 

I got the shrimp tempura udon because I wanted something simple ... the broth had a fishy taste and what I disliked most was that the broth just wasn't that hot. Room temperate at best. Now I love my food steaming hot usually more than most people .... but this didnt even have any steam! None of the broths did. 

My boyfriend got the wagyu and truffle udon and he said it had way too much truffle and tasted like uncooked ground beef. Wouldn't recommend!

If you're craving udon - go to raku. It's a much smaller establishment but worth the wait!

Let me first start off by saying that I am in no way an udon connoisseur. However, my experience here was mediocre at best.

I went here on a Saturday night with my girlfriend and two friends. We had a reservation so the wait wasn't too bad.  Aesthetically, the place is nice. Dimly lit, average noise, and modern decor. 

We first started off with an order of their Spicy Tuna Tartare Cones. Honestly, we couldn't taste the tuna at all. The mayo was incredibly over powering. 

I ordered the US Wagyu Shabu Udon In Truffle Dashi. First, the broth just wasn't hot enough. Second, maybe there was too much truffle oil, but the taste of the broth was just not good. It tasted like the smell of ground beef. Weird, right?? Third, the broth was way too oily for my liking. 

However, our server was 5/5! He knew the menu inside and out and was very quick and responsive to our needs.

If I ever get a craving for udon, I'll stick to Raku in the East Village!

The first thing I noticed was that there are so many menus and options and their bowls of udon are ginormous!!

I came here for lunch with my friend and we were overwhelmed with options. It took us forever to decide what we wanted to eat because there were so many different types of udon and lunch menu special combinations. 

I ended up getting the basic udon and tempura lunch combo with sukiyaki over rice. Everything was delicious and their noodles were amazing, but to be honest I liked the sukiyaki over rice the most haha. To be fair, I'm more of a rice girl and udon is a newfound noodle I just started liking. 

I would definitely go back to try the other udon!

If you love Udon, this restaurant is for you.  Huge variety of udon soup bowl, cold or hot. The soup bowls come in 2 sizes, large and small.  The large is ginormous!!!!  You will not walk out hungry.  Appetizers were really good.  Restaurant is usually crowded.  Service was okay.

Must go to if you're in NYC and looking for amazing Hot Udon noodles. Whether you want your noodles in curry or broth they will both taste fresh with great flavors.  The portions are great and the meals are at a great price point. Also, the menu is sizable so you have a lot to choose from. 
Cons - Messy and not the best seating. In some instances you have to sit across from people and you can see and hear everything.

Divine. Died and went to noodle heaven. 
Forgot what the appetizer we had was called but it was delicate perfection. 
For entree I went for the Creamy Bacon Truffle udon from the seasonal menu & heard angels sing at first bite. No, seriously. 
I went for the larger size, since it is same price as the smaller portion. Serving is massive & I couldn't finish it but took the rest home & it was just still super delicious reheated. So trust me on this, just get the big one, it's worth it..
Finished with the Lychee desert which also did in no way disappoint.
I will return many times for sure to try lots of other things on the menu as well. 
Service was great, place is nice. Upscale but still a casual feel. 
We weren't seated right away, we had to wait for a table but not long (party of 2) & it was worth the wait.
A++++ every single time. Huge fan of their mushroom and cream and also seafood udon noodles. Highly recommend

NO NO NO!! OH MY GOODNESS. Around 8 pm, we were greeted by a welcoming host and seated soon after. After dining and enjoying our dinner, my friend asked one of the waitresses for a check. 

We received the check, and I soon after placed my card. We were planning to split the check, but my friend realized that the check was gone- the waitress had only taken my card. We turned to the waitress and informed her of how we planned to split the bill, and how we were unaware that she took the check because she did not tell us - no conversation, no nodding, no eye contact, NOTHING.

BUT... as soon as we informed her, she started yelling at us. We did not expect uncomfortable yelling and eye rolling. As we  received our second check after she took both cards again, she sarcastically left our checks on the table saying "Thank you SOOOO much" and grunted a long "ughh" as she rolled her eyes and stormed away.

My friend and I were baffled BAFFLED. Nothing like this has ever happened to us before and we really thought it was so unnecessary.

The ultimate problem is that the $80 from the first check is taken out of my debit card.

Very yummy udon spot! Go for the larger portion because it's the same price as the regular portion. One of their signature dishes is the uni cream udon which I enjoyed. I prefer the thinner noodles. The spicy pork belly udon is also tasty, but be prepared to sweat if you don't have a high tolerance for spice.

Very very delicious udon! Their menu is pretty extensive, but because of the restaurant's name, the best choice would be their udon. I came in later on a Friday night around 9:30pm, and there was no wait. I ordered the seafood jjigae udon, and it really hit the spot. The soup comes out piping hot so be careful! The flavor profile for this dish was really on point and captured the right amount of kimchi and seafood. This is definitely a bit spicy so beware if you're sensitive to spice! I ended up not finishing the entire thing (probably had about 1/4 left) since it was so big! 

I would definitely come again and try their other udons. Really great option especially if you're looking for something warm on a cold day.

Service was great food was delicious.  I def could've had two orders of the shrimp dumpling appetizer. I ordered the Sukiyaki Udon w beef on the stone hot plate and my friend ordered the Pork Belly Spicy Tantan Udon and we loved both. Would def come back again.

REALLY BAD EXPERIENCE FOR DELIVERY. I had been to tsurutontan two times and I did liked the Udons and salmon.
Good portions for the price.
Then I have ordered a takeout of the same dish and i am extremely disappointed. 
I have spent  72$ for a lunch worth 25. The portions were less than half of the dIsh and didn't have all  ingredients. 

VERY DISAPPOINTED  I WILL NEVER ORDDER DELIVERY AGAIN

So this place is probably the Best location to eat authentic udon noodles. The sukiyaki udon platter is my go to dish at this restaurant. Also the Tokyo mule Is a great cocktail drink! The restaurant can get a little pricey but definitely worth the money!

Delicious udon. Stick with the more traditional ones, like the nabeyaki udon (chicken, shrimp tempura, cabbage). The sukiyaki udon is very sweet for a big bowl of udon. The service was very nice, and we were seated immediately (we walked in at 5:30 pm on a Saturday). The menu is quite extensive, and would recommend trying the appetizers.
The environment inside this restaurant is claustrophobic with a terrible layout. Food is mediocre and expensive for what it is.  Disappointing and frankly a rip off.

the hostess there was the absolute sweetest, took care of me and made me feel welcome. food was nice and the environment was friendly. i loved where i was seated, felt like i was given priority and made me feel valued. im def coming back again soon.

TERRIBLE SERVICE!! We went during the holidays in December before a Broadway show nearby. We were one of the first tables to sit at 5 pm. However, the food took FOREVER! We saw tables who had seated later than us get their food first! I had to keep asking the server where our food was, and eventually had to tell them, in no uncertain terms, that if it didn't come in 5 minutes, we had to leave. We had waited at least 40 minutes for food. Finally, he came back with our food, but it was clear the serving size was wrong, as we had ordered the larger udon, but we barely had enough noodles for each of us. We were so rushed we didn't have time to ask for more and just paid quickly and left. We still gave a tip but in retrospect, they didn't deserve it as the service was terrible, and the quantity was clearly less than it should have been. They probably threw together it quickly in the back kitchen. It was clear he had forgotten to put in our udon order. As a courtesy, the server could've waived some cost or thrown in a dessert. Nothing. Barely even an apology. Disappointed in the service and not worth the trouble.

Stopped in for some noodles and sushi to warm us up on a cold winter day!

The interior is warm and there's ample seating in the restaurant. Service was a bit slow and they forgot a few sides requested, but the noodles were absolutely delicious. 

Would recommend calling ahead to make a reservation especially on the weekends when it can get a bit busy. The menu had a little something for everyone which is exactly what we were looking for.

I LOVE udon noodles. I love its bounce, chewiness, and texture. Udon noodles is one of those things I think one can screw up easily: overcook it and it's soggy; undercook it and it's rubbery. Tsurotontan mastered it, and I've been addicted since. In fact, we actually got ENGAGED after dinner here, with a massive bowl of udon sitting in our bellies.

Nevertheless, we actually first came here years ago when it first opened, and LOVED it. The bowls were MASSIVE and they had a steady cult following as the chain is originally based in Japan. We've tried a lot of things on their menu: their duck udon, their uni udon, their curry deluxe. You name it, we've probably had it. Each dish was flavorful but not too overwhelmingly salt (ok maybe the curry one was, but does that surprise anyone?). Definitely suggest upgrading to the extra noodle option if you can handle it, but, warning (!), it's massive. It looks like, in recent years, they've expanded their menu to include sushi and other miscellaneous items which are equally good, but I still go back to my homeboy: the almighty udon bowl. You can also try going to happy hour to score more discounted pricing on their appetizers.

Overall: Highly recommend if you're in the area and, heck, I would even travel to get it. Get it in your belly, now now now!

This place is phenomenal. Have been here on several occassions and have never been disappointed by the staff or by the food. They have a variety of different udon noodle bowls so that way you can always try something new each time you go, and each one is filled with delicious, chewy udon noodles, a warm and flavorful broth, and of course toppings. Their small sushi bowls are usually a go-to appetizer for me as well and those are also always delicious.

Tried them a couple of times. I really like their deluxe udong and their happy hour deals are very good. I enjoyed them until I visited them for lunch. I ordered something from their lunch menu and very disppointed.  The noodle was not cooked well and the soup wasn't warm enough. Tempura wasn't crispy and portion wasn't worth for money. Will still go back for dinner but def not for lunch menus.

Beautiful restaurant eith excellent service. The creamy mushroom udon soup was very flavorful and a great vegetarian option. We loved everything we ordered except for a sushi roll - it did not have much flavor. The pork buns, cucumber salad, spicy tuna appetizer, and dumplings were all delicious. Highly recommend this place.

My all-time favorite udon place in Manhattan! Their portion sizes are perfect, the soup base is unbelievable, and the interior design is dim and cozy. I have been there 4 times and every time, the service is great! Still currently trying different noodles, but the sizzling gyudon is my favorite by far!

I ordered tantan with pork belly. Soup was JUST sour and spicy. It was not thick and rich enough. Pork belly was not tasty. Nothing was special. Other udon that my friends got was too blend as well. Tuna corn was okay. 

Shiso cocktail tasted like vodka. It said kettle one, shiso, cucumber, and some sake. It tasted like a martini with kettle one. 

 Service was also two stars. Everything was below average. Our server barely came to the table. 

I wouldn't recommend this place to my friends

The udon is good but the service is no bueno. I made a reservation for my family here and the hostess not only gave up our table when she *thought* only half of the party checked in (coincidentally she has no recollection of rudely dismissing my brother when he informed them our party was complete), but when we followed up 20mins AFTER our reservation she accused us of lying and took no responsibility whatsoever. For one thing, I've never been to a restaurant (or any establishment) where I was accused for lying. Second, she had the gall to share her frustration with her manager and other servers of the accusation IN FRONT OF MY FAMILY. And lastly, made no consideration for the additional wait time and rude behavior.

I liked the udon the first time which is why I brought my family but after that experience I refuse to return or recommend this to anyone. Dining in a restaurant should be equally about customer experience as it is about the food, and in my case the former just tarnished the latter.

3.5 stars if there was an option....
Came here for the second time for dinner with my group of 5.

Service: honestly I wanted to give them 3 stars because of their service.
Made a reservation for 7pm originally for 6 people. I had told the hostess that it was one less person which wasn't a big deal. However, I don't understand as to why I didn't get seated until at least 15 mins after my reservation. If the table wasn't ready yet then they should've mentioned it to me. I felt like the hostess wasn't giving us the updates that she should, but instead she sat everyone else who came after us which honestly was just rude. 

Once we ordered our food, not once did the server came to check on us and asked if the food was good. When we finished out dishes the runners came to collect the dishes and instead of asking us if we were interested in their dessert menu, we were handed the bill, which honestly was quite unacceptable. I was not very pleased with their service here at all. 

As for the food:
I used to think they're good but I feel like they're quite mediocre. I had ordered the sizzling beef which didn't even sizzle and looked like it has been sitting in the kitchen for some time. It was also quite salty in my opinion. It was good at first but once you started eating it, it just gets saltier and saltier

As for the other dishes 
They were good but also mediocre.

Tip:
They offer same price for their regular and their large size .
HOWEVER I don't think there is actually a difference in portion although they tell you there's more soup and noodles. They just give you a a bigger bowl to make you look like you got a bigger portion.

This is  one of my sons favorite restaurants. So it only made sense to give him a  surprise birthday party here. It was my first visit. It looked small on the outside but it's a large space.  I was totally impressed with the decor. The  waiting area was packed so I decided to grab a drink at the bar with the alphabet wall. The bar is well stocked and the mixologist are  great. 
Once our entire party arrived, we were  leaded to the lower level of another well decorated space. 
We were a party of 16, we ordered the salmon, corn fitters and edamame appetizers. Our server helped us newbies order our bowls.  The bowls are large enough to feed two people.  The staff was very attentive and the food  
was very delicious. 
Negative: they charge to cut personal cakes. 

I will return!

I've come back a few more times since my initial visit, and find myself for the first time updating one of my reviews.  

Tsurutontan Udon Noodle Brasserie at this location is seriously great.  The vibe is still fun and hip, the food is still amazingly delicious, and the service is fabulous.  I'm going to say it - I think my first visit was just a one off and the entire service staff from the host/ess, the bussers, and the wait staff are great!

I've come back both on weeknights and weekends, as well as happy hour and every time since all of my visits have been wonderful.  There aren't many yummy udon establishments that will satisfy your cravings if you've had it in Japan, but this chain (from Japan) will definitely do the trick, and on top of their udons, all their sushi is yummy too!

DO NOT EAT HERE. I would give this place 0 stars if I could. I've never experienced worse service in my life. We came here for dinner and my friend was still on her way from outside the city and they REFUSED to seat us without her. We had assured them the 4 of us that were there were ready to order and would start getting drinks and appetizers and they still refused to seat us and refused to hold our table. They were extremely condescending and rude and told us we could wait outside... in February....PC was the manager that night and he was extremely unhelpful and just kept repeating it was policy and said he couldn't trust we would actually order if we sat down??? Extremely unprofessional and a terrible customer service experience. There are hundreds of places just like this in the city, DO NOT GO HERE!!!!!!

I came here with a friend on a Saturday night, and I had made a reservation. The place wasn't too full when we arrived, and we got seated upstairs which was empty. It filled up as we were there, as did the restaurant but it wasn't full when we left. Anyway, we were seated and given menus and water, and the menu is super extensive. There are so many choices! We got a brief rundown on the menu, although I would have found that helpful before I started looking at it. I ended up going with the curry udon just because I love curry (although I wanted to try their dan dan also because it's spicy), and I got a large (which doesn't cost extra) with thick noodles. The food came out a few moments later, and it was quite delicious! The noodles were chewy although I could've done with maybe a minute less of cooking, and the curry broth was very flavorful. I was given (Japanese) red pepper flakes which added the kick I wanted, and I enjoyed my meal. My large seemed to be an appropriate amount of food, so I wonder what regular would be like. In any case, aside from being a bit pricey at $16 pre-tax for a bowl of curry udon that didn't have much aside from the udon itself, it was quite a good meal!

There is a great selection of udon here (cold, creamy, spicy, dashi) as well as appetizers and sushi. While my noodles had a great texture, it was obvious that they were cold and had been plunged into the lukewarm broth. The tempura was on the greasy side, and they kind of skimped on the vegetables - it was mostly some kind of fried parsley and radish.

Supersized bowl. I was afraid that I can finish it lol. But I did cuz it's super tasty. 

Definitely good California Uni they used for the dish. So amazing .

Don't get the hype. The flavors are way too strong that you get sick of them very quickly. And the flavors are pretty boujee like truffle and uni. Others definitely appreciate the sickening strength of these flavors (given the number of positive reviews here). But if you don't love that kind of thing and just want a good traditional bowl of noodles, this is not your place to go. I never want to come back.
Thanks Tsurutontan!

Delicious noodles! I particularly enjoy the stir-fried udon but all of it is great. Not a ton of vegetarian options, however. Very good spot to grab dinner with friends. Note that you should definitely make a reservation if going for dinner.
Love the menu . Very creative . Been there 3xs and always a good experience.  Good service and reasonable price

We had reservations at 5pm on Saturday and were seated promptly. But once we got seated, it took forever for our server to even acknowledge us. Service was just extremely slow; we had to ask for waters 15 minutes after being sat and food came out so slowly. One of our appetizers came out at the end of our meal so we had to take it home. But they were fast to bring us the check and clean our table. 

Onto the food--food was good, but it's not something to rave about. I got the wagyu truffle udon; broth was flavorful, noodles were slightly overcooked which was fine, but the meat was very, very chewy. Also, we each got the large size but it seems like it's with normal portion of noodles, just in a larger bowl. My friends and I left hungry.

A dependably good bowl of noodles. 

They have such a large menu that you probably will want to come back again and again and again. 

I come here every so often when I'm craving one particular dish, and that's the mentaiko caviar udon. I've always been a zealot for Japanese mentaiko pasta. It can be found in some izakayas in New York, but the quality varies greatly. I was skeptical about mentaiko udon at first, but this honestly has replaced regular old mentaiko pasta as my new favorite. The way Tsurutontan does it is by giving you a great fat dollop of caviar. They do not hold back. If you mix it into your noodles you get a really spicy, flavorful dish that is refreshing and pungent. It does fireworks in your mouth. 

The noodles themselves are perfectly el dente, and they make them in house so it's always fresh. A customer-favorite idiosyncrasy is that they ask if you want regular or large in terms of noodle portion, and the large is the same price as regular. I've always been a little skeptical just how much larger is large... the two sizes don't seem that different to me. But hey, wallet-wise you've got nothing to lose by going large.

We came in for a weekday lunch with a group (and fyi, if you plan to do so, make sure your whole group is there... they weren't very accommodating to our stragglers) and while I left very well, it was an average meal. They do have several lunch specials which is nice as otherwise it's a bit price-y for lunch. I settled on the curry udon with a spicy tuna bowl side and honestly, I enjoyed the tuna side better than the main dish. While the noodles in the curry udon were thick and cooked well, there wasn't much meat (or anything else) in the dish and the curry udon is a bit too rich to be slurping up on it's own. Perhaps the spicy broth would be a better option, as it looked thinner and more like a broth you'd get in ramen or bun bo hue. Service was fine once we seated and our food came out quickly which was appreciated.

I am in love with their udon noodles. The best I've had in the US hands down. I got the thick noodles and they tasted so fresh and chewy. The bowls are huge! My boyfriend and I were full from sharing 1 large bowl (same price as the regular bowl but comes with more noodles). I really want to try the uni one next! This is a must place for the next time I visit nyc!

I got a similar combo a couple months ago at the Midtown location: a double order of an udon bowl and the small yellowtail rice bowl. I was able to share this with my friend while we were starving at get full. However this time the large portion felt like a regular one and the yellowtail bowl deceptively only had 3 pieces of sashimi. I remember in the picture and last time I ate it there were maybe 5-6 pieces. Anyways it was almost too small to share with another person. 
Now I'm not sure of the variability across the two locations. I may just go back to the Midtown one.

Honestly, the best udon I've had. We had the pork belly udon bowl to split between two people and it was more than enough food. Perfectly spiced broth, al dente noodles and the pork belly just fell apart in your mouth. I dream about it, it was amazing. We also shared the soy garlic fried chicken and it was great as well, good fried chicken and very garlicky.

I will definitely be going back!

They have giant bowls of noodles here, and you can choose between getting regular size or large size (which has extra noodles) and they are the same price. Even getting the regular size though is a lot of food.

I got the uni cream udon, and while it hit my uni craving for the day, for the most part I though it was just average. It was more cream than uni, and so besides the piece on top, you couldn't really taste the uni throughout the udon.

The udon itself was well made though, and it was still pretty tasty, but I prefer the udon at Raku if I was going to go get udon myself.

Tsurutontan has a wide variety of udon choices with numerous broth and and topping choices. Tip: always upgrade to a larger size, it's the same price and you get a larger portion! I got the wagyu beef with truffle oil. I wish there was more beef, but it's on par with the prices in proportions in NY overall. The truffle oil was a good accent but didn't retain too much taste once it combined with the big bowl of soup. The udon was cooked to al dente and the broth was rich and flavourful. I would come here for the lunch combinations since they have pretty good deals. I shared this udon with free size upgrade and an additional bowl of chicken karage rice (+$5) with a friend and it was a full meal for both of us!

I ordered from here because they advertised discounted prices on uber eats.

I'll let the picture speak for itself.

Curry udon with 1 tiny block of dried beef. My gf had the same dish with only 1 tiny block of beef as well.

Is this normal? If not, you should not advertise cheaper prices and give less food without letting the customer know.

Go to spot, always packed so be sure to plan ahead. You can reserve a spot online. Always worth the wait. There isn't one thing I've tried that I don't like. It's the perfect spot to hang out, have a heaping bowl of udon and a cocktail.

Placed a family meal via UberEats. It was $59 for a whole lot of food:

- edamame
- cucumber salad 
- 4 miso soups
- 2 beef udons
- fried chicken 
- Fries
- 8 mini sausages 

All came well packed and also fresh which was a nice bonus. 

The cucumber salad was so nice and crisp. I would have that again. The fried chicken was also nicely marinated and crunchy it was pretty enjoyable.

Servings were pretty generous for our family - ended up with a fair bit of leftovers. 

I would definitely order the meal deal again at some point - pretty good value in my opinion.

Went to this place with my mom, and ordered the beef udon ($16). You can upgrade to a large size for free, which I did. It was delicious! Noodle texture was soft but chewy, and the broth was also amazing. Highly recommend.

Take out wasn't up to par...the tuna cones were incredibly oily. Sushi rolls were falling apart. Was disappointed with the delivery service. Got some other noodle in my order, I ordered beef and got creamy chicken. I ordered through GrubHub which charged me some ridiculous service charge. Tsurutonton website offered 50% off noodle $11, but then the difference was charged through service charge. Real bill came from The restaurant charging me $16 per noodle soup.
So disappointed. Delivery was on time. That's a plus. 
But on top of tax, tip and service charge it's at least $20 on your meal. Don't trust grub hub on their secret fees.

I've been craving sushi during the pandemic. Since I was nearby I ordered takeout. Got the tuna & salmon tekkadon & shrimp dumplings. Everything was delicious & well packed. I'll admit it was a bit pricey but it satisfied my craving. I'll try them again sometime.

Told 45 minutes wait for party of 5, waited 10 minutes and then they had a dimly lit table for us. The bartender was a bit rude while we were waiting. The highball seemed to have no alcohol.
The Bowls for the noodles are crazy large and the portions are decent. You get a choice of thin or thick udon in regular or large portions. The regular and large size are same price!
The truffle is udon is great, while the Curry and uni udon are just ok. 
Noodle texture is a bit overcooked, soft, and slimey.
Also, the Happy hour apps are worth it.

Delicious and huge portions. I've gone here in person several times and always had a great time. Ordered delivery today and there was a mixup with a few of the items so I called the restaurant. The host was very apologetic and sent me the entirety of the order again! Can't wait to go back in person when it reopens and until then I'll continue enjoying their udon and donburi from home.

Tsurutontan is a solid Japanese restaurant for me in NYC. Their portion sizes are huge, quality is pretty good, and they take reservations! The prices are a little high, but could be considered normal for NYC. The good thing is that they have a great happy hour menu though with many of the appetizers, drinks, and sushi discounted. 

When I come to Tsurutontan, I always usually go for their sukiyaki udon or their chirashi bowls. The udon bowls are huge and you can ask for extra noodles at no extra cost. They give you a selection between thin or thick noodles. I prefer the thick noodles, they have a lot of the chewy texture and flavor inside them as well. The broth in the udon is also always really flavorful. In terms of the fish they serve, they are all pretty fresh which is nice. I also liked their spicy tuna cones (comes with 4) with some avocado at the bottom. 

Would definitely recommend booking a reservation for this place. They do have a lot of seats, but the walk-in waits can add up, especially around dinner time. Just call ahead and get a reservation to save you some time!

Curry udon here is among my favorite curry udon bowls in the city! It's always busy at whichever NYC locations of Tsurutontan you may go to. But, the wait time is never long because of the amount of seating they have, along with quick service and food serving times. I never feel that I'm being rushed to leave, either. Soooo many noodle options (with a menu that's friendly to English readers), but somehow I keep being drawn to the beef curry udon. The mentaiko udon bowl is a close second though. So. good!!! Def check em out, if you're craving and looking for a Japanese udon noodle soup bowl.

Too many incorrect items not just first time. This time, there was 2 missing (incorrect) items. They asked me to come back to the restaurant with all the items I received. 
But They still charge one roll which I ate before I found this problem. 
I wasted my time for extra round trip. 
Never never.

This spot has always been one of my favorites. I'm so sad that I haven't visited due to covid! I make it a point to try someting new every time I go and have NEVER been disappointed. I highly recommend!

The food here is, *chefs kiss*

Literally love eating their food, it's tasty, there's a balance of flavor for all types of clients. I also love my food very spicy, so it's wonderful to have an establishment that meets those standards. Some people might argue that it might be pricey, I personally don't see it, but I'm also a food junky, so I don't mind spending coin on my food. But, like, also have you seen the portion sizes?!?! In my opinion, you're getting your money's worth.

Tried this place out after seeing the promotions on social media. Super weak udon even for $8 and $11 which is a discount. The chicken udon was literally noodles, bland broth, and few pieces of chicken. No vegetables or flavor. The stir fried udon was basically pricy beef lo mein but with udon noodles. On top of it all the prices in the ad were less than what was listed when ordering so it was the classic bait n switch. No need to come back here.

(2/14/2020)
Surprisingly the place was not fully booked by the time we made a reservation (for a party of 3, we booked few days in advance). Upon arrival, we had to wait a bit for our table to be ready but that was not a big deal.

They had a Valentine's day special menu but we opted for their regular menu. Tried their spicy tuna tartare cones, sea and truffle roll, uni creme udon, Tsurutontan deluxe udon and US Wagyu shabu udon. Ordered all udon bowls large (price is the same for the regular and large size). The bowl was so big, it came with a ladle for the soup. All broths were really yummy and noodles were perfectly cooked. At first we thought it was a lot of food, but it was sooo delicious we finished everything!

I would definitely come back, service was great, food came out fast and it was beyond our expectations.
Easily my favorite city spot. Never will find a better udon spot, and the most generous portions. Happy hour deals are also great.

Service was great.
Outdoor seating with view of a Union Square made for great ambience.
Giant bowl of Spicy TanTan Udon was impressive. 
The broth was good, as were the noodles.  Not enough ground pork.  Otherwise a simple bowl of udon where the broth was the star, albeit not sublime enough to carry the show on its own.  But for 20$ I wanted to be wowed and the only wow was for the size of the massive upside down samurai helmet bowl in which my soup was served.  Also for 20$ I wanted more, not less.  No egg, no corn, no nori, no scallions or onion chips or garlic chips, no mushrooms, no bamboo shoots. 
Overpriced good, but not great bowl of soup.
3.5 stars.
Amazing udon- especially love the curry bowl.  Spicy yellow tail and salmon sushi is great also and they have nice lychee martinis and mojitos. Will definitely be back!
Seriously, how dare you charging people $9 extra for this? Is this uni? 20g? This is so ridiculous!

I work around Union Square so I always was thinking to stop by to have lunch so today was a day there's outside seating area but if you decide to have lunch on your lunch break don't take a chance only one server that take forever of you do ask for water don't expect any refills it takes forever but one thing that makes me mad is when you in the rush they try to over charge you so when I realized that I was charged not for lunch prices but regular I asked to fix it he came back saying that everything is fixed but again it was regular price I have to go inside to look for him and confront him and explain on my fingers of course he was wrong so if you don't want to get aggravated pick something else other wise you loosing your time and money

I could eat noodles every day for the rest of my life and be happy, and I wouldn't be mad if the noodles were from Tsurutontan. They specialize in udon, the rounder, chewier cousin of the flat rice noodle. If your experience with udon has solely been from the serviceable but not amazing udon stands inside most Korean-american delis around the city, I'd implore you to try fresh udon for yourself, which is in a league of its own. The texture is silky smooth, and has a bouncy chew, a texture asians have dubbed "qq." Noodles are nothing without their qq, and the udon at Tsurutontan has this in spades.

I've dined inside this sprawling, multi leveled complex of a restaurant many times, and each time am always surprised by how much space there is behind the non descript storefront off Union Square. Right now they have plenty of tables set up for outdoor dining, spaced out and with plastic shields installed between tables. Their super long menu has been pared down, but there is still plenty to choose from. Most recently I had the uni creme udon, but in the past I've enjoyed their shrimp tempura zaru udon (not on their shorter menu as of late September) and their panko fried curry udon. The enormous, seemingly bottomless bowls are really fun to eat from and the portions are large enough to sate even the largest of appetites. I don't remember ever having to wait too long for my food and the speedy service during my recent outdoor dining experience with them was no exception.

They've changed their hours during the pandemic so be sure to confirm their hours with them before you visit!

Another place where those thrillist FB videos overhype.

I went with my friend and I would say the only thing going for them are portion sizes for the udon (and maybe... decor...) 

You know when something's so salty that your lips start to tingle and burn? That was the soup. It was so salty that it was undrinkable and I debated pouring some water in there. We also got an appetizer- the tofu. As my friend quotes : "headasses deadass charged me $7 for a piece of plain tofu". And indeed it was flavorless.

I'll give it two stars for a benefit of the doubt since I only tried the one type of udon (the signature one)

Definitely a big let down... I mean the noodles weren't the worst, but would I come again to over spend on udon? Nah.

Dine in service was not thAt great. The woman so called manager was disgustingly unprofessional. Did not handle the dine in or out situation correctly. The waitress was barely speaking English well, was having difficulty explaining no
More menu items. It was the WORST dine in experience ever in NYC restaurant experience. Over all food was not so bad but the service and manager's behavior was disgusting and disappointed.

Excellent spot for lunch combos.  Udon and other main dishes are great together.

Today I had the Spicy Udon + 3 Sushi Roll Combo.  $21 plus tax.  I selected the Mentaiko Roll, the Hamachi Roll and the Scallop Roll.  All three were excellent, with the mentaiko being the salty item, hamachi with a neutral vibe and the scallop bringing a savory umami flavor.  Comfortably feeds two.

I've had delivery and pickup many times because there are just so many options that you will never not find something to fill your craving.

This is a spot I keep coming back to. Their udon is very good, especially since it's starting to get cold out. I've had the pork katsu curry udon as well as the deluxe and both have been great. Definitely a nice spot to go to if you're craving something warm

This was a cool looking spot but we were greeted with a "oh you don't have a reservation...there will be a lot of people coming *soon* so we cannot seat you" Meanwhile there was only 3 parties eating and the place was pretty empty. We agreed to sit outside but they did manage to switch us inside at some point. I was still confused because there was barely anyone eating inside so I don't know why that was being said. (Even with COVID restrictions, there was still a LOT of empty space and tables to spread out).

I was expecting a big portion as everyone said in the reviews...it's literally a normal sized noodle portion in a huge bowl...I was not thrilled to pay $20+ for that. I prefer something like Marugame instead. Was interesting to check out but wouldn't come back for overpriced udon.

Had my first Tsurutontan experience at this location and have since been to both locations in NY and one in Ginza Tokyo, I would rate the overall experience in Ginza a 10/10, midtown NYC location a solid 8/10 and the Union Square location a 6/10 ; I was initially amazed by their food portion. Although we know by now it's the size of the bowl that gave the illusion of an exceptional size but they do offer free large noodle portion option. 
Truffle cream w/ crab, mushroom udon was amazing 10/10
Gyoza, it's nothing spectacular but decent at 7/10
Soy garlic chicken, not great, lacking taste and the seasoning is not well balanced, 4/10 for at least not being dry 
Blue crab California roll, amazing at 9/10 but a bit on the expensive side for 1 roll
Deluxe udon, a taste of everything and all is nicely balanced at 8/10
Wagyu mushroom sukiyaki udon, very sweet but had a nice umami flavor at 8/10

Visited here mid September and ate indoors. Prior to being seating we had our temperature checked. They did a really good job at spacing out their seating and there as basically a table per corner. 
It was really comforting to eat their bowl of udon, the size made it perfect to share and the sushi tasted very fresh.

Pre-covid - Been to this restaurant multiple times and never get tired of their food. They have a fantastic deal where you can add extra noodle for free! No additional price! You can choose between 2 types of handmade udon- thin noodle or the regular thick udon. I prefer thin since the thicker one is harder to chew haha.  I had a few of their popular udon and all were good. Their appetizers and sushi are great additions. Especially the spicy tuna tartare cone. This is a chain restaurant and there are two locations - union square and midtown. Went to both locations and both are big. Def check this place out if you can.

Absolutely one of the best ramen spots in town for me. Staff are welcoming and very attentive, food is hands down authentic in flavor and the ambience of a modern bar resto feel is something I would always go for.

Hopefully, I can write this review to the best of my ability. I've dined in twice and ordered takeout once. The dining environment is definitely high quality, with very nice ambiance. My first time here was definitely my best experience. They have a variety of menu items to choose from, from sushi to their famous udon and noodle soups. Though, with COVID, I think the menu shrunk a bit. When I dine in, I usually order a large amount of items with friends and family but for takeout, I only ordered their Wagyu Truffle Udon, which is discounted right now! It's such a good deal for something that's usually $21, but is now $14. 
Highly recommend as a cute date spot!

Offered outdoor seating and they were focused on being 6' apart! I appreciated that. The udon was amazing here! I recommend the special. We loved it so much that we have ordered take out from them for the past month haha and they currently have a great promotion on the beef udon of 2 for $14!!!

Right now they're doing a 50% off deal on a lot of udons and dishes, which is what pushed me to a 5-star! We ordered a Wagyu Curry Udon, Vegetable Tempura Udon, and Cucumber Salad and the total came out to around $27, which is awesome for the portion sizes! The interior is super nice and big with trendy design, so it felt like really good value for the price! The service was amazing as well, with people caring for us a lot and food coming out quickly.

Their famous huge bowls are indeed huge, which is fun to eat out of! My only con was that the broth for my udon was a bit too salty, and tempura a lil oily.

I came here this past weekend for the first time and had a delicious meal. I was with my friend and we ordered a cucumber salad, hamachi carpaccio, shishito peppers, A5 wagyu truffle udon, and the truffle cream with crab and mushroom udon. The cucumber salad was solid, as were the shishito peppers which are not on the menu but they'll serve upon request!  The hamachi carpaccio tasted fishy but our waitress was kind enough to take it off our bill. 

The two udon dishes that we ordered to share were really good. I prefer the wagyu truffle over the truffle cream because the broth is not as heavy. The udon is solid but not as good as the udon at Raku, but the broth here is wayyy better than Raku's.

Our waitress was so nice and helpful. She was super accommodating and understanding when we told her that our app didn't taste right. She also recommended the cucumber mojito, which is super refreshing!

Never been to a spot that specializes in udon before, but I see why this dish deserves a dedicated restaurant. The udon I had here was next level. We started off with some Edamame and Spicy Tuna Cones. Edamame was Edamame, but the Spicy Tuna Cones seem to be the trendy appetizer here and for good reason. Very crunchy on the outside and almost creamy on the inside with a good kick. For our udon we got the Tan Tan Udon and Tsurutonan Deluxe Udon, both of which were very delicious and very filling. The bowls and spoons are HUGE, to the point that the spoon is ladle-esque. There's a small 5'3" lady included in the Tan Tan Udon photo for reference. We also ordered drinks, a Tokyo Mule and some matcha-infused alcoholic drink, but both left a bit to be desired and were pretty light on the pour.

Lacking service. No water refills. Waitress rolled eyes when I asked for hot oil and it never came. Quite hurtful to someone that was so excited to try your restaurant. 

I feel that I need to request this first for the Udon noodles.....provide tongs to serve the noodles!!! So messy. A huge spoon is provided but not tongs. We had clearly said we were sharing and due to COVID-19 putting our chopsticks in the same bowl is probably not the best bet. 

Udon soups were good. The vegetable udon was sweet, noodles cooked well. The fried vegetables to accompany were very greasy and lacked flavor. It would have been an added bonus to have vegetables added into the soup - maybe sprouts? 

The crab truffle udon was very tasty. I wanted to add extra hot chili flakes and when I asked the waitress rolled her eyes and never brought them. It was disappointing. It had a cream of mushroom feel. The crab was not fishy. 

Appetizers were fresh and the cabbage dumplings were cooked to perfection and the cucumbers were refreshing. 

I am grateful for the experience and had a wonderful evening out with my friend. I just wish we weren't forgotten about outside. It's important not to forget about the outside people dining - especially during COVID-19.

Made it to Tsurutontan to take advantage of their AMAZING 50% off deal this month !! we made reservations online for outdoor seating, and we're pleasantly surprised when they were still willing to seat us even though one member of our party couldn't make it. their seats were also more than 6 ft apart, which made us feel much better about dining! also, the servers were very sweet and got us warm water to keep us from getting cold! 

I got the cold uni udon ($13). you might think I'm crazy for ordering a cold dish while dining outdoors in november in nyc... but it was SO worth it!! the dashi uni broth had such a strong uni flavor and coated every strand of udon with a taste of the ocean! i originally wanted to get the thinner noodles cuz heard they were chewier (but forgot to specify) but the thick ones were still SOOO chewy, as if they were perfectly "Al dente" for udon!! the uni itsself was mixed, some were buttery, some nutty, and some kind of bitter. i thought the freshness of the shiso leaf added a great touch, but didn't love tempura flakes... too heavy for the dish and seemed misplaced! overall tho, this was definitely the best noodle dish out of the ones we ordered!! sooooooo good, would def get again!

My friends got the duck udon ($9) and beef sukiyaki udon ($12). The duck udon was smokey and had an iron-y taste, which i liked a lot, and the beef sukiyaki was sweet and rich.

For apps, we had the soy garlic fried chicken ($6) and the grilled maitake ($6.5) the serving sizes for these was huge!! the chicken was super tender and crispy, with a very complimentary sauce! such a great app. the mushrooms had an ok bite (a little on the hard and snappy side vs bursty and juicy side) but i think it's because they weren't super evenly cooked. the truffle flavor was strong at first then died pretty quickly. there was a bunch of fried crispy stuff under that were fun to pair with the mushrooms !! overall i really loved this app because I just love mushrooms!

Ordered take out and it was very tasty! Def recommend - satisfying and hit the spot for any Japanese food cravings. 

* eel beef bowl: A+! 
Really liked the vinegar rice, and had a hint of smokiness. There were 5 or 6 pieces of bbq eel, so delicious. The seared beef was thinly sliced and flavorful too. It was beautifully presented in round bowl with ginger and wasabi. I would order again!
* small side of doshi udon: A! The broth was perfection, very comforting. It was still warm! And the udon noodles has perfect texture, soft and nice bite. 
* app Seared Mushroom: A, it was very flavorful, loved variety of mushroom. The crunchies are a nice touch. When it arrived, it was cold :( but I guess that's just delivery.. every thing else was still warm.

This spot has a 50% off the menu deal right now for the month of November. I came here on a chilly weekday afternoon. They offer both indoor and outdoor seating so we chose to dine indoor away from the cold. They highly suggest you make a reservation but they also welcome to walk-ins. We had a party of three so we were told that we only had an hour time limit. Upon entering the restaurant, temperature checks were required. 

Inside the restaurant, the lights are dim and background music is softly played. The first floor shows a bar with alcohol lining the walls. To the left, there is a short staircase leading downstairs to the main dining area. 

We ordered soy garlic chicken for appetizer - it was very unique and I had never tasted anything like it. It reminded me of karage. The sauce was a bit sweet and tart, with hints of soy sauce. It was topped with green onions as well. The uni creme pasta was very rich and savory, uni was presented in the middle of the huge bowl. In comparison, the cold uni udon had a stronger taste of uni. This one was refreshing and the umami flavor coated wonderfully in your mouth. The truffle crab and mushroom udon was very filling - you cannot be disappointed with the notes of truffle in this dish.

This was my first time here, saw this amazing 50% deal on instagram and just had to come and try it at least once. Servers were really nice. I made a reservation on resy and I got seated immediately didn't have to wait. I ordered the wagyu sushi, shrimp tempura & a us beef wagyu truffle dashi, for a first timer it was absolutely delicious. Service was quick, my water was never empty, always got a refill after I finished my cup. I would most likely come back for a round two. There was definitely social distancing inside as well where they spaced all the customers out. The dining environment here is pretty high quality, definitely deserves a recommendation to all my friends.
I went there for a lunch so I had a curry udon. I liked the atmosphere and it was an enjoyable lunch.

Food is good. BUT SUPER STRESSED OUT dinning in. Due to the discounted price they limit customers to dine in at a limit of 45 mins which is understandable. However, we were reminded FOUR times of the time limit during the 45 mins. Waiters also mentioned that food should not be shared. We order two entree, one appetizer, one shushi roll and a bottle of hot sake. I think instead of saying food should not be shared, they could have specified that each customer should order one entree at least. There were multiple tables available and no customers lining up while we were reminded of the 45 min limit when the waiter ask if we would like the check. On a Sunday night, it was a very stressful dinner experience.

I went for their special promo 50% off udon and other items on their menu. The price was honestly the only incentive for us to go, as I've been here before and it's pretty expensive for what you get. The chicken app was good to start, but my Uni udon was over cooked and broth flavorless and too creamy that it was so underwhelming to eat  I got takeout another time after that a few days ago for the Dan Dan udon and it was even more disappointing...wouldn't pay full price or even half price anymore

I came here with a few friends on a Saturday night. Reservations are needed if you do not want to wait. They seat every other table and all staff members were wearing masks. The staff were all really friendly.

They are currently running a promotion with 50% off certain items on the menu. Please note that items that are not on the 50% promotion menu can still be ordered but it will be full priced. 

We order a few appetizers (soy garlic fried tatsuta chicken, french fries, crab croquettes, and unicones), udons (sizzling sukiyaki udon, cold uni udon, and tsurutontan deluxe), and sushi (seared salmon snow crab roll, shrimp tempura and snow crab roll, and the eel avocado roll). Everything was really good and fresh. I would recommend the sizzling sukiyaki udon! It does come with a raw egg but it will cook once you mix it into the noodles. This dish does not come sizzling but the noodles were still hot and they gave a good amount of meat.

They are currently not offering thin noodles and additional noodles will cost an extra $3. If you are getting a drink and want something sweet, I recommend the Nagashima Ice tea. Don't forget to ask for light ice as they fill the cup to the brim with ice leaving little room for the actual drink which was sad :(.

I was pleasantly surprised by the quality of their prime beef and broth! I got the truffle dashi soup base which had an umami flavor that deserves a chef's kiss - and to top it off, they were having a 50% off at the time! Will
definitely have to be back to try the other udons! 

They are currently opened for both indoor and outdoor dining. All the indoor dining tables have dividers in between each table and the servers are quick to take your order. They do have a indoor seating time limit of 1.5 hours I believe.

The cold uni udon here is delightful! Ordered to-go and my order was ready within 20 minutes. I got the cold uni udon and the spicy tan tan udon. Both were delicious but I enjoyed the uni one more because it was more unique and refreshing. The noodles have such a great chew and I loved the cold broth paired with the creamy uni on top. I also reallly liked that they added wasabi to it because it coated the noodles in such a great kick! The spicy tan tan udon is another great choice if you're looking for something spicy and rich. Portions were decent and we had tons of leftover broth to save for later.

Thank you Tsurutontan for staying open this year!! I don't know how I could've survived this year without your handmade udon noodles, flavorful broths, and fresh sushi.

Here's a photo of my wagyu beef with truffle oil udon and salmon lovers combo. The delivery was so fast I think it got here in under 30 min.

On top of that, the packaging was seperate to ensure the meal was delicious on arrival.

Please support this business if you can afford to dine out!! Happy New Year!

New Years I didn't expect they open but they are! Also they have 50 percent off special BOGO) and combo special! Wow great to star this year. Usually I thought little skeptical because I usually choose ramen but I saw deal menu I'm in!! Udon and soup separated and pour soup( but if I live around I will make cold noodle myself and keep soup for another day) any way noodle is not little soft ( yeah I know it's take out) sushi is also good! I don't know when they will end this deal but if they have good to try!!

I ordered takeout from here I got the bogo deal and by the time I got home it was still really good. Packaging was packed really well, packed with beef and the udon noodles were nice and chewy! Husband loved it and so did I. Will be coming back for more takeout soon!

They have really good deals during COVID if you're looking for quantity over quality! The bowl is HUGE!

Cream udon - It was recommended by the waiter, but my friend and I couldn't finish all of it. It was too creamy and not flavorful either. 

Shrimp tempura udon - It wasn't the best I've had... a little oily and the broth was not flavorful but salty at the same time. 

Tan tan men - My sister had this one and she said it was one of her favorite dish in NYC!

Warabi mochi - Kinako and kuromitsu came separately with ice cream! It's good if you like warabi mochi :)

For a generous helping of specialty udon, this is the place to go. My favorite, uni udon with a more than creamy broth, will satisfy the wanting palate. The bowls themselves a Goliath size provided to satisfy the famished. 

Once a place where there was a 1-2 hour wait, unfortunately had been reduced to a skeleton of what it was by the pandemic. The place offered 50% to reinvite regulars back in; and now many BOGO options for pickup and delivery. 

Appetizers and sushi sides also keep with their standards.

The interior design comprises of a beautiful earthy vibe with an accent wall of wooden letter art to feast your eyes upon. 

We hope this place will quickly regain its former glory.

My absolute favorite udon place. Such great broth and appetizers. Makes me feel so warm inside especially on a cold day. I absolutely love the truffle crab cream one. And the soy garlic chicken is so amazing. I miss their indoor dining so much- I can only hope they create a heated outdoor dining.
Great food, and they're doing a BOGO special which is extra nice. I received my order in a timely fashion and everything tasted great.

The wagyu beef truffle udon was pretty good! Very rich and tasty broth, and not too overwhelming either. The noodles were also done right, not soggy and not too hard. It's such a shame that their service wasn't better.

We came as a large group (~7 people) to order takeout. Originally, we hoped to get their buy-1 get-1-free promo for outside dining, but learned that it's only for takeout/delivery. Only one of us had put in our order, before the cashier left and went straight to the kitchen. Meanwhile, another staff member (manager maybe?) was sitting toward the back doing something on his computer. After waiting for about 15 minutes, we tried to get his attention so that the rest of us could order, but he told us that the previous cashier would come back to take our orders. Odd, because it felt like we were just sort of brushed off.

Eventually she did come back to take the rest of our orders, but the whole process to get our food took about 45-50 minutes because of the ordering setback. They seemed like nice people, so I'm not sure what happened, but maybe opt for delivery or something.

When we first entered the restaurant, there was a mouse under the bar. And they packed my sushi straight, so my sushi got smashed shown in the photo. Most importantly, there is a small fly on my sushi !!!!!!

Satisfy your udon (or noodle soup) cravings with Tsurutontan's enormous bowls of thick noodles and flavorful broths. If you come during their 50% off deals, you really can't beat this place for a dinner date or honestly anytime dinner. My boyfriend and I each got a bowl of udon and shared two appetizers, which was more than enough for the two of us, but we couldn't resist trying more items given the 50% off deal. Considering the quality and quantity of food you get here, I would say the food is worth the original prices as well, but would consider it to be a special once-in-a-while type of dinner. We loved both of the appetizers we got (fried tatsuta chicken and creamy spicy shrimp tempura) and were pleasantly surprised by the generous portions. The sauce that came with the shrimp tempura was unreal and really the highlight of the two. We tried the spicy tantan and wagyu beef with truffle oil udon which were delicious in their own ways. However, I started out feeling like I couldn't get enough of the wagyu beef with truffle oil broth because it was so flavorful, but as I ate more, the truffle got a bit overpowering. Just keep this in mind if you're not sure what truffle tastes like, because the truffle flavor as 110% there!
Covid review: food is good as always but they don't have heaters and the outdoor seating is awkwardly on the sidewalk. I think take-out would be a better option.

The restaurant should not even deserve to get one star
I've ordered dinner since Caviar estimated it will 45 to 55 minutes to be delivered.

However, the restaurant didn't confirmed my order for over 30 minutes, so I contacted Caviar customer support, then when the support rep contacted Tsurutontan, they said my order is being prepared and my dasher is at the restaurant waiting for my order to be completed, so I waited.

Even after additional 40 minutes, the status was the same though I got one text message update from dasher, saying 'still waiting for my order to finish cooking'.

Additional 20 minutes, no updates, so I decide to contact Caviar customer support again. Once Caviar rep reached out to the restaurant, Tsurutontan just cancelled my order.  

After over 90 minutes of waiting with fake updates from the restaurant that my order is being prepared?

Tsurutontan does not treats customers right, lacks professionalism and integrity as restaurant.

If Tsurutontan is so incompetent, cannot handle the orders, why didn't the informed me before making me wait for over 90 minutes?

What is worse is that Caviar re apologized but not Tsurutontan. Such an arrogant and incompetent restaurant.

If you cannot even operate at the minimal standards, maybe you shouldn't be operating the restaurant anmore.

Stumbled upon this place when the BOGO promo was on my UberEats home page and ordered the Beef Sukiyaki Rice. The portion is HUGE because it's a family sized box, and with the BOGO promotion the 2 boxes lasted me about 6 meals and stayed tasty all throughout! I'm a huge sucker for a rice bowl but the rest of the menu looked pretty good too. Would order from here again.

The food here is a decent value since everything is basically half off during covid, but not worth the effort for the terrible service. I came to pick up an order and when I arrived was told that the order had been cancelled for no reason, and I cannot make another order as the kitchen is closing in 5 minutes. There was a crowd of people in the lobby to whom the same thing had happened. They were not apologetic at all and started yelling at the customers basically telling us to go away and stop bothering them. This is shocking behavior from a service industry trying to survive in a pandemic. You would think that if they're desperate enough to offer their whole menu for 50% off, they would at least try to be nice to their customers. Will not go back ever and hope they shut down soon for good.

Tried their udon couple of times already and every time the experience is good. 
The time we tried the combination from NY restaurant week. 
The Uni udon with sushi is really impressive to me. Their sushi is fresh and delicious. 
To my surprise the uni soup is creamy yet light and pair with the udon well. Super recommend!!!
