Great buy for the restaurant week special.   Udon is chewy and bouncy.   Truffle beef Wagyu udon is rich and have good portion of beef.  Creamy uni udon do have uni flavor.  They do offer a lot of buy one get one free offers.  Definitely will be back once the indoor is allowed.

Restaurant week order last Saturday was a nightmare. First, you can't get through the phone because they were overwhelmed. I only saw two staff working the front. Anyway so we went to the restaurant since we only live two blocks away. We tried to order but it was a mess, no 6 feet social distance since everyone is trying to pick up their order. This is where it's management issue, there were about 20 bags of order on the bar but they are not organized by alphabetical or by order number so the staff had to look through every order for each customer! What kind of management is that. You complained about not having business due to the pandemic but when the business is there you just can't handle it. As a consumer this is a horrible experience. And that's not it, so if you look at their restaurant week website offer, it's omakase  choice of beef, chicken or tan tan udon with 8 piece of sushi. Oh well, manager say it doesn't matter what's there, that's not what they're serving. It's only small plain cold or hot udon with 8 pcs sushi! I'm done with them. I like to give business to those who deserves it. Will not be back, there are many places for udon and ramen all over the city.

[pre-pandemic dine in]
There's unlimited noodles?? I wish I had known. Even so, one serving was filling enough. The beef udon broth was light and perfect, the fresh noodles was bouncy. 

[restaurant week takeout]
Amazing deal during restaurant week, I got full on the sushi alone and had to eat the udon for a different meal. I wasn't expecting a lot out of sushi from a restaurant that specializes in udon, but I was pleasantly surprised.

Well packaged for takeout.

[Review specifically for current pandemic time takeout] 

I've ate with them pre-pandemic and food and service was phenomenal. Therefore when I saw the nice deals and combos, decided to order from them even though we weren't interested in the restaurant week deal but we wanted to order the other combos.

Like some other reviewer said, take out process was horrible starting with them not picking up the phone so no way to order. Looked at their grub hub and uber eats pick up option but the delivery/takeout menu prices must not have been updated. So we decided to drive over to order in the restaurant to order. When we got there, there were tons of delivery people waiting to pick up grub hub or uber orders and the guy manning the front orders were super overwhelmed. We waited ten minutes for waitress to come take our order. Since I was picking up for different people, I asked to have three orders placed so I can bill them back accordingly . The waitress told me no, only one order.  I asked her what she meant I can't if I'm picking up for four customers and my boyfriend was with me. She goes so you have three credit cards? I wasn't planning on using three credit cards and since there was so many people there, I didn't want to make a scene so just ordered. 

Order included:
1) Buy one get one sizzling sukiyaki beef udon (no soup)  for $22 
2) Salmon Lover set with full size choice of udon (plain hot with soup or plain cold udon) for $20 upgraded to the US Wagyu Truffle Udon for +$5
3) Deluxe Salmon Lover with full size choice of udon (plain hot with soup or plain cold udon) for $25 upgraded to the Tsurutontan Deluxe Udon for +$7

Order took ~35 minutes and when I finally got the food home, we were not pleasantly surprised. For the first order that was for two different people, they put it in one box with "2 serving" written on the side. The order barely looked like their usual one order when you normally dine in. The "full" size udons with the other orders had like a few pieces of udon in a small container so can't imagine was a half size udon order would be. The soup container was some weird medium sized container vs the typical larger container that usually comes with noodle soup orders. 

The food tasted okay. The sushi was good. The udon ended up being surprising as some of you may know, at least for those that ate for dining in or outdoor, they're known for giant size udon bowls. While I understand it's takeout and the pandemic, the pictures and descriptions on their menus are very deceiving especially if you say BOGO and basically just halved the serving size to then equal one for two orders. It's very dishonest to people ordering from you based on pictures and descriptions and being surprised like that. 

Honestly, I'd rather pay the regular price and know what I'm supposed to expect vs finding all the orders halved in portion. I still think that dining "in" would still be good but I wouldn't recommend take out. Honestly They also need to staff the place better or have some sort of system to take care of orders including placing them and picking them up.  It was just a mess and a poor overall experience.

Came to pick up lunch because their bogo is too hard to give up! I tried calling but the calls do not go through for takeout so I actually ordered through Yelp which is via Grubhub. After having read reviews about the long wait, I placed an order close to 40 minutes before I'd arrive so I wouldn't have to wait too long. Ordered two different udons and fried chicken. ALL were part of their bogo. I got to their right on time and my order was ready so I was happy- the wait time for me from placing to receiving order was about 30 mins. At first look, the portions of the noodles seem relatively small but after you eat it, it's actually the perfect amount, for myself at least. The food is great and for their promotion, I think it's really worth it! The winner though is the fried chicken- also part of their bogo but they put both orders in one box. For $13 you get A LOT of chicken and it was really delicious. We ate it too fast I couldn't catch a photo but if there's anything you don't you want to miss out on from this deal is the fried chicken- quality and quantity is all there! I think their promotion is a great way to pull and lure customers in! Will be back soon if I am in the area!!

I came here when there was 50% discount and it was amazing. This was when there was still indoor dining. I called for a reservation and was seated right away, staff checked our temperatures and they were wearing mask at all times. We ordered 3 bowls udon, 2 appetizers and two rolls of sushi. The total bill was $75, and we each paid $25 and left the restaurant will a full stomach.

Restaurant week deal was great! Didn't expect much of the sushi considering it's an udon shop, but it was pretty good! Nothing too fancy, but hit that sushi craving right on the spot. Truffle wagyu udon (+$5 supplement) was delicious. The order was on time for pickup and everything was packaged perfectly for takeout.

I ordered a uni, ikura and crab meat donburi as well as their restaurant week special Omakase sushi set. The sushi set came with and 8 piece Nigiri set (Bluefin Tuna, Salmon, Yellowtail, Seared Salmon, Spicy Tuna, Unagi, Tobiko and Inari sushi and a side of udon soup. The sushi was fresh and the flavors were all there. The quality reminds me of the good times indoor dining, when it was a thing. 

The donburi on the other hand was not as good as I had expected. The uni wasn't fresh which was disappointing considering how go everything else was. The ikura and crab meat (this was actual crab meat not imitation) was better. Overall, I really enjoyed their sushi set, but their donburi set needed some work.

Edit: they're still have restaurant week deals until the end of February because there's no indoor dining at the restaurant.

Still as good as the first experience years ago. I wanted to try a few spots for restaurant week. This time around they had an 8 piece nigiri with a side of udon of your choice. I chose the cold udon. The sushi portion was pretty good. Everything was fresh and the sushi rice was well seasoned. The side of cold udon was bouncy, fresh, chewy and was complemented well with the dipping sauce. Overall I thought it was a nice well rounded meal.

The lobby was a little hectic while we were waiting for the orders. Lots of walk ins and lots of people waiting for pickup. They had a sign in sheet for pickup orders and they literally asked me like 15 times what's my name. They aren't opened for indoor dining yet, but they have extended the restaurant week to end of the month

The noodles were standard udon. Dashi broth was decent, noodles weren't too soggy.
But the SUSHI set (during the restaurant week deal) was AMAZING. Great assortment of fish- definitely the highlight for me!!

Last night we ordered the the udon and sushi take out special.  Everything was delicious.  We both ordered the kake udon, as we are both pescatarian and it was amazing.  The noodles were perfectly chewy and broth was delightful.  The sushi was fresh and all in all it was a great value.  I highly recommend!

We called to order 3 orders of $20.21 Restaurant Week Omakase for pick up. It was a great value and surprisingly good quality, especially for the price.  The udon broth was tasty although nothing extraordinary, packed separately from the noodles.  The sushi was fresh and delicious.  We would definitely order from Tsurutontan again!

Support your local businesses!

very very good experience! if you've ever had the sukiyaki from ootoya, the taste is remarkably the same but slightly more oily as the beef itself has more fat. 

wagyu sukiyaki: super flavorful and very sweet - i loved the meat chunks and the egg in the middle that adds another layer of flavor to the mix. noodles are cooked just right and tons of mushrooms! 

duck: very clear and light broth, not as flavorful as the sukiyaki but perfect for those looking for a lighter taste, but def not as many ingredients in this one
I ordered a few dishes, including the tan tan and chicken appetizer. Everything was ready on time (and even a little before). Tastes great.

1. Clean bathroom that's said a lot of thing for me u know? Since we all know it's Covid-19 Era. 
2. Great hospitality, love our Japanese server and the manager both are very attentive.
3. Udon noodle is very soft and different texture. In a good way. I think they might have made them in the house. Broth is super testy I finished the whole thing.
Spicy scallop roll is so fresh I wish I have more room to try their sushi. But the soup is ginormous, very generous portions.
Always been my fav spot to have udon, they recently have many happy hour deals selected udon are 4 bucks off. Got to try something new this time. Food came quick and very consistent quality.

I've visited this restaurant twice and I'm embarrassed to admit that I've never tried their hand made udon. I will make sure to try it out next time. But I have tried their entrees and apps and their fusion dishes are scrumptious. This is a great place to hang out with your friends and enjoy a wide range of Japanese cuisine for lunch and dinner. It's fun to order a bunch of items and and share amongst your friends.

The restaurant itself looks really modern and chic and they have outdoor seating available.  

However,I was more interested in the BOGO deal that was going on and that was through take out only through grubhub or ubereats.
I've tried the spicy tan tan udon, wagyu beef truffle dashi, and the tatsua fried chicken. The spicy tan tan udon soup base was pretty flavorful and because it was take out  I was able to add vegetables into the soup at home to make it a more filling meal. There was very minimal minced meat and I'm not sure if this is the usual serving size or they did a reduced serving of the protein due to the BOGO deal. This is the same comment towards the Wagyu beef truffle dashi. The Tatsua fried chicken was pretty crispy and had enough salt to bring out the flavor but I would be a bit disappointed if I had paid full price for the single amount. The udons were both nice and chewy even on the next day.  The wagyu beef wasn't really anything special and it was very mild in flavor. I'm not sure if I would pay full price for the amount and quality  but as for the BOGO it is worth it.

Tsuru Ton Tan has amazing udon, sushi, and rice bowls! Located right next to union square it's really accessible! 

I ordered the Oyako Bowl with chicken, onions, an egg, and rice. It's a wonderful savory dish and has a creamy texture to it. The addition of the yolk on top really does it for me. I added a small Spicy Tan Tan udon which comes with ground pork in a wonderful broth. I love these udon noodles and think it's amazing perfect for slurping. Lastly I ordered a truffle roll with tuna, salmon, yellowtail and a little truffle oil. Honestly I wouldn't expect the truffle oil to have a profound impact on the dish but it did. And for the better. It's an amazing roll. A better experience than I had the last time I came, definitely will be back

Great Service
Great Food
Delivery deal during covid is a good deal!!! The portions are huge and tastes great! Highly recommended!!!

Sorry, Tsurutontan, but the service has been extremely lacking.  The last two to three times, our order has come with full spillage.  Attached are photos of how messy it has been.  You clearly need to work on the packaging and I hate to leave a negative review, but ruining at least three of my dinners has caused me to leave this review.  I no longer enjoy ordering from your restaurant and better care needs to be placed on how you package meals.  Attached are photos of all the damaged meals that have arrived.
Good place good appetizers good udon. The truffle crab udon is a must have!! Ordered 4 appetizers all super delish. Love the food here!!!

Been to the one in Roppongi, midtown, and now this one in Union Square. Was expecting the same quality of udon and it did not disappoint. 

What was disappointing was the hostess who came by our table at least 3 times, with a blank stare on her face, and looking at her watch. She was obviously trying to indirectly tell my party that just spent $600 on dinner that we need to leave. Funny because I didn't see any one waiting for a table as we left. The polite thing to do would have been to ask us how much longer did we plan to stay. 

The udon was great but the hostess left a bad taste in our mouthes. Won't be coming back here.

This place is opened for indoor dining! I ordered the uni cream udon and my sister ordered the beef sukiyaki. The udon texture is fresh and chewy but I wasn't the biggest fan of the uni cream udon for the price. I tried the sukiyaki udon and it's very flavorful and highly recommend this one!

Horrible service.  8:30pm Friday night reservation and as soon as we sat down they said kitchen was closing already at 8:30. Well, then don't take 8:30 reservations if that's the case and then try to rush people out.  8:30 closing on a Friday night in NYC. Really??  Food is good but we had to be in and out in 40 minutes as they were rushing us out. If we wanted fast food then we would have gone to McD.  We used to love this place but service and management have gone downhill.  Not coming back.

Their Udon is amazing as usual. The staff is friendly and the services are nice. 

However this recent visit is a mixed experience, I hope it's an honest mistake, that the check didn't reflect the happy hour price (which is all day), the server corrected for us after we noticed the price difference. So, just double check the check we you receive them.
Food was good except I had a hair wrapped around my wasabi.  I ordered a ottoro sashimi and it came with hair on my wasabi.

Fast take-out during COVID. They separated the noodles and the broth so you can get it fresh. Their 2 for 1 deal is amazing. We ordered fried chicken appetizer and the portions were massive. Still thinking about how good that fried chicken appetizer and the noodles are.

The udon was pretty huge but very delicious! The service was very slow though they took a long time to come take our order and bring the food. It was covid safe, everyone was wearing masks and socially distanced inside

Came for late lunch/early dinner so it was naturally quieter and no need to worry about social distancing. 

They have happy hour pricing all day Mon to Thurs and until 6 Fri to Sun. I forgot the exact prices but since the pandemic started they seem to keep changing the menus and prices - annoying. 

I kinda miss their seafood deluxe cream (?) udon but haven't seen it in a while. Didn't like the truffle crab or curry. Don't want to eat the wagyu beef again. I settled for Tsurutontan Deluxe. It has a little bit of everything: beef, chicken, shrimp tempura, shiso pepper, and egg drop. 

It was disappointing. 

The udon arrived lukewarm.

I don't appreciate how their tempura items aren't placed in a separately because it's impossible to not be soggy upon arrival. What's the point of eating this sit down vs takeout if it's soggy anyway. 

Chicken and beef pieces were intertwined with the egg drop. The chicken can be more fresh, not saying it's stale, but can be better. Slightly drier than I'd like. Beef was normal but wished there was slightly more considering proportion with other ingredients. 

Udon noodles itself, when I first ate it they seemed too soft. The more I ate, it either got stiffer or it was never cooked properly to begin with - the outside was mushy and inside was a bit tough/stiff. 

No one really came to ask how's our food but then again I probably won't mention all these details in person. Also I must say that not all eating sessions are about the food. 

One more comment that I've had since day one, the regular udon spoons are soooo heavy. My fingers get sore while using it and I must put it back down every so often.

Food was good here but waiter and waitress made people to rush out. I told them we are still working on food but they kept asking us every 3 minutes if we are done until we left. Total eating time was 35 minutes. I'm wondering if we stayed that long. We ordered 1 appetizer for share  and 2 udon and sake so we need some  time to eat. Next time if I ever go this place, I would tell them I'll let you know when I'm done so they don't need to checking on us every minute.

Went on Friday at 430 pm.

Service 5/5
Ambience 5/5
Food taste 5/5
Quality ingredients 5/5

I got US Wagyu shabu curry udon. AMAZING. I'm a snob when it comes to curry udon, but dare I say this is top 2 (#1 is still Murakame in Oahu). Broth is thick and delicious and flavorful.

Husband got tricolor dish with uni cream udon. They couldn't substitute the yellowtail, even tho he's allergic which I thought was weird, and I don't usually like yellowtail... But when I tried it, it was omakase grade!! Yummy and buttery! The uni cream was just as buttery without an overwhelming fish taste. 

Would recommend and DEF coming back!

This place has great ambiance.  Fancy and beautifully decorated indoors! However, the udon was pretty average. I was disappointed by the Wagyu beef & mushroom udon. 

Notes: 
Thursday - Sunday happy hour ALL DAY!!! (Udon / sushi discounted) 

Udon price: $16 - 24 

I ordered the Lady M dessert too, $13. 

Each person is required to order an entree***

Food: 4/5
Given that happy hour price is absolutely reasonable, we were satisfied with the quality of the food. Surprised by that uni was in such a good quality. Nothing extraordinary, but I wouldn't expect that like would in high end fine dining. Better than expectation. 

Beverage: 2/5
Few options were not available. Rose was either opened for far too long, or have failed the temperature management; unless it was a different one from what listed. Draft beer tasted VERY watery. 

Service: 2/5
Staff didn't know which items are N/A. She had to come back and forth only to tell us items were not in stock. Rose we refused was remaining on the receipt, along with the price error on the other item. They fixed it. 

Overall: 3/5
My wife visited here at the other day for a lunch, and told me she had a great time. We decided to pay a visit which was just in time for a happy hour so lucky us (there's no HH for drinks, btw). Beer came in, watery, with server asking my wife any substitute for her drink. Appetizers came in, enjoyed. My wife asked for a rose, which went wrong as described above. Gigantic udon came in. Good. We felt a bit uncomfortable for having it due to the presentation but acceptable. We were just so underwhelmed by the beverage program entire stay. I don't want to hurt or offend anyone, but hope they fix the issue. Food is a great value.

Tsurutontan knows udon.  They make their udon from on a special recipe daily.  You can definitely tell the difference - more flavorful than the average udon and perfectly chewy.  Lots of hot and cold varieties ranging from the traditional to exotic.  Everything is good.

Insider'sTip: Extensive Happy Hour menu
This was my first good dining experience in nyc and it set the bar pretty high. The udon comes out in huge bowls and the truffle sushi was amazing.

4 to 4.5 stars for food, 5 stars for ambience/atmosphere

UDON ORDERS:
--spicy seafood jigae udon: my favorite
--wagyu udon: wagyu is really good
--curry udon: average

OVERALL:
The menu is extensive with many flavors of udon available. Option to do regular or large size. The interior is spacious and relatively more upscale compared to your typical local ramen shop. Prices are reasonable given the location. They're more known for udon and not necessarily their nigiri or donburi.
The udon noodles were amazing honestly you have to visit this place if you are ever in NYC I will be going again

YUM!! I came in thinking I would not finish a whole boneless of udon by myself but alas, I devoured the whole bowl. We made a reservation on a Friday night at 7pm for 7 people since they close early! We were able to be sat down right away. 
I ordered the Sukiyaki Beef Udon which came with beef, an egg, and various other toppings. If I thought other udon places around me were good, my standards have just raised higher from this meal. The bowl is huge with lots of soup but the noodle portion is standard. 
They have so many different udon noodle soup options as well as items like omakase and cold noodles. The waiter we had was so knowledgeable of everything on the menu and helped me figure out what to order. My friends got the Duck Udon and the Wagyu Beef with truffle and they all loved it!  I will definitely come back and bring others to try!

This is my second time coming here to eat. The first was probably when they first opened many years ago. I feel like the taste was a little off than what I remembered it to be the first time. The service now is also a little bit spotty (the waiters messed up an order and forgot an item). I came during happy hour and ordered the spicy tuna tartare cone ($9), beef tataki ($7), tsurutontan deluxe ($20) and tsuruton curry deluxe ($22). 

The spicy tuna tartare is a must try here, especially during happy hour (its about $3 cheaper). It is filled with avocado and spicy tuna in a fried cone. The curry deluxe was not too bad. The flavor of the curry was amazing, however, the katsu was a little disappointing and had a funky taste to it (something I can't quite put my finger on) 

The tusurontan deluxe was alright, however most of the tempura was submerged in the bottom of the soup and was soggy by the time it came out (I wonder if it is possible to ask them to separate the tempura onto a plate). 

The beef tataki has a citrus/ponzu flavor and is very unique and refreshing.

Tsurutontan does udon right! If you're jonesing for an udon dish, this is one of the best places to go in the city. I had the spicy tan tan udon, and it was amazing. Perfect level of spice, great broth that wasn't too heavy or watery, and udon noodles cooked to perfection. Plus the portions are MASSIVE, so come prepared to eat.

The Union Square location really impressed me too. From the outside it never struck me as anything noteworthy, but the interior is really well done. Clean, modern, and lots of seating - for groups and for individuals. I can see myself popping in here solo for some udon once in a while!
Great food, great presentation, and happy hours even on holidays! Happy hours discounts were applied to food and there were seats for parties of all numbers! Will be coming back here soon
Huge portions! Happy Hour makes this restaurant even more value for the price. All the udons are very delicious.
I got the three roll and soup meal for lunch. Very good sushi and the udon bowl is HUGE! Makes it fun. We also tried to soy garlic fried chicken and it was the best thing we ate!

If you're looking for a comically large bowl of noodles to take a photo with, this is your spot.

Came here for lunch based on all the wonderful yelp reviews and this place did not disappoint. Fresh udon, delicious sushi, large, clean establishment -- what more could you ask for?

What we got:
Lunch/sushi combo (forgot which it was called specifically, but it was the one with super premium fish, but it was $25):
- The udon in sukiyaki broth was amazing! Definitely homemade udon, definitely delicious. The meat in the broth wasn't too fatty or overly lean, just perfect. Big plus: it came in a comically large bowl that will intimidate just about everyone
- Combo sushi platter: This was also a pretty impressive array of fish - scallop, tuna, salmon roe, salmon, uni, etc. These were also very delicious, sans the uni.  The uni had a verrrrry verrrry fishy taste to it. So much so that my sister also got the combo, had a quick taste and quickly rejected that piece.

Other than that, the waitstaff and people are very attentive and nice! Solid place to go for lunch
My favorite ramen spot in Manhattan. So delicious!!! And such big portion with reasonable price!!! And the vibe is PERFECT! Love it.
I ordered beef udon and it was amazing considering the price. Would definitely do it again for a quick night meal.
Good place for fast lunch break. Reasonable price. The quality of udon can be better. Sometimes fish in maki smells

Finally got the opportunity to go back to this popular udon restaurant again. We got there in the mid afternoon for lunch. There were a few tables with umbrellas in front for outside dining. Upon walking in, the restaurant was very empty compared to pre-Covid. Safety precautions like recording names & contact numbers, temperature checks, masking, and hand sanitizers were in effect. Tables were isolated using plexiglass. 
I ordered my favorite Curry Deluxe which consisted of a pork Tonkatsu, shrimp tempura, and sliced beef over an udon curry soup. My soup was a bit thinner than normal but just as flavorful.  I always get my order with the larger portion of udon. What normally would be no extra charge is now $3. I can understand this being post Covid recovery and it's still worth the extra price paid.
My friend order the beef sukiyaki udon lunch special which came with choice of two sushi rolls. The beef sukiyaki udon came with an abundance of sliced beef. Soup was rich in flavor with a hint of sweetness. We ordered both dishes during the happy hour (HH) special which saved us $3-4 per order; HH is all day (Sun-Thurs) and limited hours for the rest of the week. Staff was friendly and service was fast. Overall, this was a enjoyable afternoon lunch.

Love the udon soup and sushi. Been here several times and always had a wonderful experience.  Came for lunch today, missed the lunch menu by 1 minute, no problem.  My friend and I ordered a combo soup and sushi to share. There were 18 pieces of sushi and a bowl of udon soup. It was alot of food. The waiter said that he could not give us another set of chopped sticks and only ONE napkin because we had to order our own meal.  Really?? So my friend had to eat with her hands. Then I asked the waiter if he can please pack up my soup to take home. When I received the bag with my soup in it, there were TWO sets of chopped sticks and FOUR napkins.  Now, why would he give us all of that to go when he would not give it to us for our meal??? Did he feel bad or was that a dig or maybe he was just having a bad day.  I will be back but will be bringing my own chopped sticks and napkins.

Jun 2021 eat in experience: they changed the menu and now have sushi combos! Three sushi rolls and a small Udon for $20. I got the udon regular (large) size because thats what I was craving. Noodles are made in house and is so chewy. Made reservation and was seated in 5 min on a Saturday night. Be careful with resy- they have times up to 9pm but the kitchen closes at 9!!  Street parking only.
So I haven't been back to the restaurant but I have ordered delivery at least three times. The bargains on the menu and good portions has changed my review for this place. I highly recommend.

Did you know that happiness comes in the form of a bowl of udon twice the size of your face?

Now you know.

Pair that happiness with a pint of beer and Tsurutontan's lounge vibes, and you've got yourself a solid evening dinner that doesn't hurt the wallet too badly - especially if you go in during their happy hour!

Service is attentive and efficient (and waiters may or may not make killer sake recommendations). Both locations usually have dinner reservations available online a few hours ahead in advance.

Tldr: delicious broth and noodle in huge portions

(Old review from pre-covid I forgot to post, but I've gotten takeout from this chain throughout covid and quality is still top notch.)

I wish I knew about this place sooner! Chewy noodles: check, fragrant broth: check, loads of toppings: check, portion to value ration: right on the money. I came here for lunch with a friend and got the Tsurutontan deluxe udon. 

I literally cannot find anything negative to say about this restaurant.

Love this place before covid, during, and after!

Quality is always amazing and quantity as well.
Great for dates and good price for family as well because of the size of the dishes.

Their curry udon is amazing and sushi is also amazing too. I always have a great time!

Service is always amazing too. One of my go to places that can never go wrong in Union square that doesn't break the bank but still fun and yummy!

This is a review of my experience here pre-pandemic.

I always felt like this place was pricey so I never really was interested, until my coworkers mentioned to me one day that the bowls and spoons were bigger than your head. Well, that certainly got my attention. I love places that have cool selling points like that, lol. About 8 of us came here for lunch on a cold, windy day, and I'd have to say that the lunch menu was really reasonable! The inside of the restaurant felt spacious and a bit upscale to me. I ended up ordering a mini sukiyaki don combo (which came with a full size udon). I chose the spicy tan tan udon with my sukiyaki don. Both were flavorful and exceeded my expectations. The menu is pretty extensive consisting of udons, sushi and donburi, etc.  Ended up having to take my leftovers to go because, well just look at the size of that...

One thing to note is that while they do let you take your leftovers to go, they did not allow me to order an extra udon for take out (for my coworker), and said that if I wanted to take out I'd have to order through Seamless. Felt pointless to be honest, since I was already there and could pick it up. But besides that little hiccup, my experience here was overall satisfactory!

No wait at 1:30pm Friday. Appetizer came quite quickly and the udon also comes shortly after.

There's a no share policy so each person needs to order at least one main item.

The udon and the broth is really good. They come in very large bowls although the portion is probably just regular if you put it in a normal bowl. Overall would recommend!

My go-to udon spot in Manhattan. First visited their location in Roppongi and the NY locations do not disappoint. I have been to both the Union Square and the Midtown locations. The restaurant's design is elegant and sleek. This time i tried the Salmon Lover Set ($28)  - so generous I had to take some sushi home! The spicy tantan is rich and the noodles are chewy.

Definitely a good bang for your buck!

I work in the Flatiron area and I am always on the hunt for affordable and delicious eats.

The udon portions here are pretty big, and the lunch specials are competitively priced. I wouldn't recommend eating here on a day where your work day is particularly busy, however. The food portions can be relatively heavy on one's stomach throughout the day. 

Taste-wise, however, this place is pretty hearty and the broth is definitely savory and delicious.

Udon and lunch specials here are more suited for a Friday type of lunch.

Service was extremely bad, was seated in the smallest corner table when we had three people, the entire restaurant was empty but every single seat was apparently reserved. Not reserving nonetheless is on us, but onto the food. The udon all tasted extremely old, and my girlfriend immediately felt sick after eating and threw up in their bathroom, and if you get a soda they'll give you a glass full of 75% ice and 25% soda, and the glass itself is a skinny glass which probably doesn't hold half a can. All in all my experience was terrible I wouldn't recommend.

This place was almost empty when we got there (6:30pm on a Thursday) but made like 10 of us crowd in the foyer to wait to be seated until all of our parties were there. The service was very slow, and we had to keep flagging our waitress to order more drinks or even get our food order in. Our waitress (when we could get her attention) was very friendly.

The food came suspiciously quickly, and unfortunately was ho-hum. My friend got a beef stew udon, and I got a stir-fried udon with tofu (their only real veg option). All their broths are apparently made with seafood but they have very few seafood options - lots of beef and so on.

 My drink was ok, but my friend's cocktail was too sweet and so she switched to mine after she finished. I had to ask multiple times to get our water glasses filled, and after we paid our bill, we asked for another glass of water and they didn't want to do it which was weird. And we thought we were the last ones there and that was why - they were trying to get us to leave - but then it turned out there were other patrons around the corner. Anyway I wish we had gone somewhere else.

This is a review for an experience Pre-COVID.

Came in with some friends to finally try Tsurutontan! We made reservations in advance but ended up having to wait a little bit before being able to be seated. We grabbed some drinks at the bar and patiently waited. 

The portions here are generous. And they have some great combo specials.

For appetizers, we had...

Grilled Maitake Mushrooms
Cucumber Salad
Shrimp Dumplings

For my entrée, I had the simple Shrimp & Vegetable Tempura Udon. 

The mushrooms were delicious. The other appetizers were good.

My Udon noodles were so fresh and chewy. The huge bowl of broth was flavorful but a little too salty for me. Tempura was perfectly cooked and served on the side, as it should be!

Dessert we shared Matcha Crepe Cake. Yum!

Reminded me of Japan!

Prices are reasonable, especially for the portion sizes.

Service was excellent.

It's my flavor spot for the udon.   They are bounce and chewy at the same time and they have so many choices of broth and meat/ vegetables/ seafood... combinations.  Love the mini beef sukiyaki on rice.  The buy on get one free menu is good deal if you can go with your friends together and share the bill.  You can taste more dishes in one visit.

Be aware that the Bogo and the regular priced udon is the some size. I ordered the bogo and an order of a regular udon the udon is great and tasty I just don't get it with the "bogo"since it's the same and not a bigger container

Tsurutontan was such an amazing experience! Their quality of food is top notch and their staff is also great. My family and I came here on a weekday evening for dinner. Our party was quite large, but they kindly accommodated us to all sit together and our waiter, Tony, was very friendly and played along with our little banter.

Right off the bat, we were blown away by the appetizers. 

Spicy scallop roll (5/5) - the roll was delicious and fresh
Grilled organic mushrooms (5/5) - highly recommend!! You definitely want these bad boys. They were so flavorful and buttery and delicious 
Grill duck breast (4/5) - was also delicious with all the components provided, I was surprised the wasabi went so well with it 

After the appetizers, we were stoked for our udon entrees and they did not disappoint! The bowls were literally larger than our heads! 

Sukiyaki beef udon (4.5/5) - I love everything about the udon except for the actual sukiyaki broth itself which is purely because of a personal preference. Sukiyaki is sweeter than a typical broth. My other family members loved it, but I personally found it a bit too sweet for me. I had a taste of the normal beef udon broth and I absolutely loved that. Everything else in the bowl was perfect cooked. The beef was tender and delicious, udon noodles were the perfect chewy texture, egg was nicely soft boiled. You can't complain!

When I'm in Manhattan again, I will definitely be making a stop at Tsurutontan.

Stopped by for lunch on Mon, July 5th and noticed a BOGO menu (18 items) for takeout/delivery. Not sure how long this has been running but we decided to get (2) Sukiyaki Beef Udons (2go) and ate at a table in Union Sq Park just down the block. "BOGO, free of the same, no mix & match"

Gourmet udon noodles with good portions and excellent flavor.  Happy hour prices also made the meal prices more manageable (happy hour is all day Sunday to Thursday and limited hours Friday and Saturday). But you get what you pay for. Just a unique experience with flavorful udon and broth. The broth wasn't salty and was light flavorful and among the best broths I've had.

3.5 stars.

Tsurutontan used to be one of my favorite places in the city but my recent visit was quite disappointing. I stopped by during the lunch hour on Saturday, just walk in. We were seated immediately. No line. 

First, the seats were assigned weirdly. They were seating all small parties in a round bar table in the middle of the dining room that had pixie glasses in the front. So when you walk into the dining room you see huge empty space surrounding the bar table. Idk, to me that gave a weird vibe. I actually liked the bar table but it would have been nice if people were more spread out and they made better use of the big space. 

Another perplexing thing was the menu. For Saturday lunch, we were given a menu with (1) dinner specials which was basically their set/combo menu, and (2) happy hour menu, which was basically their lunch/discounted menu for a la carte... Given this menu, It was unclear which menu to look at: Why am I given the dinner menu during lunch hour? Is there a separate lunch menu? Or are we supposed to order from happy hour? 

We ordered a combo menu plus sukiyaki udon as a la carte. The small udon that come with the combo comes with no toppings (toppings for extra bucks), and the 3 rolls were mediocre... I don't think the combo menus are worth the money. 

I recommend just ordering a full size udon with toppings -- this is their specialty! They used to ask for the size of the udon, but seems like there's only one standard size now. It was still huge and I left with full stomach.

This food was HEAVENLY. I'm usually not a big fan of noodles because I try to limit my carb intake, but this udon was such a treat!! I got the sukiyaki beef udon with the salmon lover set and it was the best thing I have put in my mouth in a while. The flavors were so rich and there was a nice amount of beef in the bowl too! The sushi I thought was pretty good too, especially the sushi rice. I liked how it was flavored and there wasn't a lot of it-- the fish to rice ratio was really good and I appreciated how I wasn't eating a huge amount of rice like at some other sushi places. I thought the fish itself was good but not the freshest fish I've ever had, which was fine because I mainly came for the udon (again, so so good). 

The pricing is pretty awesome too. For my sushi and "small" udon, it was just above $30 after tip and tax. I think this is a huge steal for how much I enjoyed this food. This place is highly recommended by me and I will definitely come again!
We had 3 rolls with cold udon, 3 rolls with creame udon.   Delicious and the size was great !! Come hungry!!!

Pretty good deal for sushi and udon combo! I had the sushi set with assorted fishes with sukiyaki beef udon($25) and another set similar to the sushi set but with just three kinds of fish and sukiyaki beef udon ($20).  The sushi was so fresh and delish and the udon was tasty and bouncy! Def must try and good deal for the amount of food it comes with!

I came here for restaurant week and got the premium omakase set, which was $35 dollars and included a sukiyaki udon. The menu said it would be a small udon, but the size of the bowl surprised me and was honestly very filling and delicious. The sushi itself was less impressive. I felt like each piece had too much rice but the fish was decently fresh. 

Another qualm I had was with the uni, which was the only difference between the premium and the medium-tier restaurant week choice. When it came out, it looked a little "melted" as uni does when it sits out for a while. Nevertheless the taste was good, just texture was slightly off. The ikura also wasn't as fresh as I expected as it was sticky and stuck to my teeth when chewed. The whole set was super filing and definitely worth the price - though I'd probably skip the uni and just get the medium tier one. 

The service was also nice and friendly. It was easy to secure a reservation and location is just a quick walk from the 14th & Union subway station.

Love the food hate the service. Just tried ordering for pick up on the grubhub app and would not allow for pickup. Claims their kitchen is "too busy"  so they closed it off but yet they are still taking delivery orders. 

One of my go too restaurants but now not so much.

This place is a really great deal in terms of prices and the amount of food you'll get!

The taste is pretty great :) but nothing out of this world!

Pro tip is to go during either their happy hour (Anytime sunday-thurs) for reduced prices OR order takeout/delivery to snag their BOGO deals which make their udon around $7 to $10 each! :o

I got the shrimp tempura and really loved all of the tempura! I also liked how soft and squishy the udon was, and the broth was fine.

My friends got the Beef Wagyu and Sukiyaki with the Restaurant week sushi set for $21. All around plenty of good food at a great price :)

If you had asked what my rating for Tsurutontan was before my visit yesterday (7/22/21), I would have said 5 stars, hands down - amazing food, good prices, big portions, great service. Unfortunately, my visit yesterday was a big disappointment. I have been to this location once before and their midtown location twice and loved it each time. This was a VERY different visit. 

When my party of 4 put in our food orders, we were told the sushi May take a little longer than expected, we said that was fine. While the appetizers were brought out in a reasonable time, we ended up waiting over an hour to receive our meals - so long that at 45 minutes, I actually went inside (we were seated on the patio) to ask when our food would be ready and I was met with apologies, being told they were very busy, no time estimate of when the food would be out, and being told to "give it another 10-15 minutes" and we would see from there. 

When the food did finally arrive, the sushi came out first, and the udon came another 5-10 minutes later- which made no sense since we were warned that the sushi would be the hold up. The udon was not hot (like it had been sitting) and there was far less broth than usual. I asked for extra broth, since it seemed low, and was told it would be an extra $3 - no offer to just waive the fee since the wait was so long. It also took about 20 minutes for the extra broth to come, at which point I had almost finished my bowl of udon despite deliberately eating slowly in hopes of the broth coming soon. I also ordered the same dish I had ordered previously but it was far less tasty this time. We had asked for the drink menu for a second round of drinks, and it was never brought. 

The restaurant was busy, but no busier than the other times I had been there with very positive experiences. This was also a weeknight, bit a weekend where longer waits may be expected. There was no compensation on the bill, there were some verbal apologies, but no real explanation for the issue. If this had been my only experience at the restaurant, I would not return or recommend it to anyone else. I can only hope that this was a fluke and that others' experiences are better.

i was originally only going to give this place an overall rating of 4 stars again, but the prices and quality of the food truly deserve the 5 stars. 
-my family and i decided to come for lunch on a saturday afternoon for restaurant week. we didn't make reservations beforehand, which was a big mistake. they were especially busy on this day because their kitchen was backed up. so, we ended up waiting for around 45 minutes for a table after putting our name on the waitlist. the waiter told us that it would take a longer time than usual for them to prepare sushi orders (with no time estimate). we ended up waiting only 10 minutes for our appetizer, and around 25 minutes for our omakase sets after ordering. 
-the service here honestly isn't bad. i think they were just having an off day with the wait time, but they were still very kind to all the customers. 
-they're available on grubhub, caviar, and ubereats.
-both cash and card payments are accepted. 
-they have a decently large outdoor dining set up on the sidewalk with around 5-6 tables. you can make indoor or outdoor reservations through resy.

7/24/21
-soy garlic fried chicken: we ordered this appetizer because we were already really hungry by the time that we got seated. one order comes with around 10 pretty large boneless pieces of fried chicken. it had an amazing flavor and was fried just the right amount. during happy hour, this is priced at only $11; during dinner hours, it's $13. it's a very reasonable price either way, since it's a shareable dish. (4/5)
all four of us ordered the restaurant week omakase, which is a set of 8 pieces of nigiri, a tuna roll, and a choice of a small udon. you can choose between cold, sukiyaki beef, or soy dashi soup-based udons. they also have the option of some other udons (ie: wagyu, curry, etc), but it would cost extra depending on which one you order. in terms of price, i definitely think that it was worth it. the meal was extremely filling and i have no complaints. i loved the nigiri sushi options that the omakase set came with (bluefin una, yellowtail, salmon, seared salmon, spicy tuna, tobiko, unagi, and inari); they all tasted very fresh and so delicious! i'll review each of the different small udons that we decided to order. 
-uni cream udon: i decided to choose the uni cream udon, which costed $8 extra. i haven't had uni in anything besides sushi, so i was looking forward to trying this. needless to say, i wasn't disappointed! the cream broth wasn't too thick, but it was quite salty. the portion of uni was fair imo, considering how expensive uni is in general; it tasted super fresh and i was a big fan of the presentation too. (5/5)
-sukiyaki beef udon: this was one of the options that wouldn't cost any extra money. there's a big reason why this is one of their more well-known udon dishes because it's absolutely fantastic. the broth and beef were so flavorful! it's very similar in taste to their stir-fried sukiyaki beef udon, which doesn't come with a broth/soup. (5/5)
-chicken cream udon: this was basically the same as the uni cream udon, except there were pieces of chicken inside instead. of course it still tasted good, but it wasn't anything super special. i'm not sure if it was worth the extra $4. (4/5)
-soy dashi udon: this was also one of the options that didn't cost extra. it comes cold in a soy dashi broth. my mom thought that the dashi flavor wasn't strong enough, but i personally enjoyed it a lot. it's definitely the more refreshing option on a hot day! (4.5/5)

overall, this authentic japanese restaurant is a great place for a super filling, yet affordable meal. i could totally see myself coming back in the future! my favorite dishes that i would recommend you must try would be their sukiyaki beef udon (stir-fried or soup-based) and uni cream udon. their sushi is also extremely good.

Udon noodles were overcooked. Broth was good. Sushi rice was above average (surprising).

Cold noodle was the only one that had decent noodle consistency. I'm a noodle lover. Won't go back.

Avoid this place until they are better equipped to handle patrons. Seems they are short staffed and having food supply issues. Walked in during lunch on a Saturday afternoon. Place wasn't too busy. Sat down, ordered sushi, waited over one hour and no food. Asked the server when our food would be ready. He apologized, went into the kitchen and said that they are backed up and "couldn't predict when the food would be ready." Our number was called at the Harry Potter store and we couldn't risk not making it there during our timed ticket. Walked out, and noticed other tables were doing the same. I understand restaurants being short staffed, but at least give people a heads up that food can take 1.5-2 hours to come out. Avoid this place until they get their act together.

Come for the restaurant week. They do not have uni so I order the basic set. Nice sushi and udon soup. The regret is the udon itself. The inside part taste like flour. Besides, the waiting time is beyond my expectation. Both for waiting to be seated and waiting for the food.

I got the beef udon and it was good. However, I expected a bit more pazazz given the price and chic interior (maybe some egg drop, bean sprouts) but the udon was literally noodles and meat with broth, garnished with some green onions. The portions are large and the noodles are super soft and chewy, and the broth was flavorful because of the meat juices and fats. I wasn't blown away but I would come again if I'm craving udon in midtown.

I loved this place and came here often. Today 7/28/21 I went for late lunch and it was so off. The noodle was not mochi mochi (bouncy?) like usual and it was cut thin and brittle. The last time I went was on 7/8 and it was still awesome. 
I am very sad if this place goes down but if the noodles don't make a come back, it will. It was restaurant week and I'm so sad that this is what the first-time-TsuruTonTan goers will taste...

If I could give negative stars, I would. Customer service was abysmal and I was just picking up an order. Front hostess doesn't even deserve to work at a McDonalds with her attitude. 

I waiting over 45 mins, yet she had the audacity to get chippy with me because she "doesnt work in the kitchen". You get paid to deal with my frustration (which was nothing, just asked what was the hold up), I don't get paid to deal with that b.s.

As someone who has enjoyed their food, the hostess alone soured my taste for this place.

This place was underwhelming, they give you such a big bowl but the amount in it is small and the broth was not hot. I found the beef sukiyaki to be much better than the wagyu beef udon in broth because it had way more flavors and the noodles were chewier. This udon place is well-known so I thought they would have mastered this craft but I was wrong. The cucumber salad was pretty refreshing but on the salty side if you get too much of the sauce.

Amazing deals -- the food is great. Sushi is quality. I think this is one of the most bang for the buck places I've been to in NYC. 

The waitstaff is friendly too!

Waiter recommended a great sake to pair with our food! Staff was fairly friendly and the amount of food- although I thought was small at first- ended up being a lot for one person. We went with sushi and udon set and I would definitely recommend that if you are looking for a deal! I had the cream uni udon- to be honest I didn't love it but I think that's because I realized I don't love uni so I don't blame the restaurant. If you like uni, I'm sure it'll be fine

I came on a rainy Saturday and came back again few weeks after on a Sunny Saturday around 12-1pm. I needed to wait on line to be seated for both times. It's best if you reserve to save yourself some waiting time. 

There is Happy Hour ALL DAY Sunday-Thursday, 12-5pm on Friday's and 12-6pm on Saturday's. 

Appetizers:
1) Uni Wagyu sushi - This came in two individual pieces. my favorite appetizer of all time here. It's so delicate and perfect. I highly recommend it

2) Crab croquette - This came in 3 pieces. This had a crispy and crunchy exterior and an insanely soft interior. I was blown away by the contrast from the crust and insides. It was very good.

3) Soy Garlic Fried Chicken - It was a big plate. This was a miss. It was dry. There wasn't a lot of flavor. 

4) Crispy Corn - This came in 3 pieces. This was a bad choice. The corn was burnt and hard. I didn't enjoy this one at all. 


Udons: The bowls it came in were massive!!!
1) Wagyu Deluxe Sukiyaki - The beef was so tender and juicy. The broth was amazing. It's umami with a bit of sweetness. The vegetables soaked all that delicious broth, making it irresistible. It had an onsen egg in the middle and when you mix it all, the flavor is unbelievable. You MUST get the Sukiyaki when you're here. I loved this dish so much

2) Cold Uni Ikura Scallop - This is a great dish for the HOT summer. The ingredients were very fresh. The udon was tougher for this dish. So it was alright, but I like the scallop the most. 

3) Curry Deluxe - This was alright. It came with shrimp tempura, pork cutlet and beef short plate. The tempura food were fried perfectly. I didn't have any burnt or overcooked pieces. It went really well with the curry too. The curry was mild. The heat level is low, almost nonexistent.

If you like a restaurant that tells you what you MUST eat (as opposed to what you WANT to eat), this place is for you!  The place was at about 25% capacity.  We sat down, ordered a bottle of wine, four items  from the appetizer menu (Spring Rolls, Shrimp Dumplings, Tempura Shrimp and Veggies, and Ginger Garlic Fried Chicken), plus a bowl of White Rice.  That's when the waitress informed us restaurant policy required we EACH order an entree (none of which appealed to us).  And that's when we left.  Thank you Tsurutontan Udon Noodles, because otherwise we wouldn't have gone on to have the best bowl of French Onion Soup and best Bread Pudding (with caramel sauce if course) in NYC - not far away at Mustang Harry's Irish Bar.  Extraordinary food, drinks and service (at Mustang Harry's).  Not so at Tsurutontan Udon Noodles. Our last night of a seven day stay in NYC - it was the worst of times (@ Tsurutontan Udon Noodles), and the best of times (@ Mustang Harry's).

the us wagyu beef with truffle udon was the dish I got and it was great! I would've preferred more meat in the dish but the udon and broth were both excellent. my friends got the sushi tasting for restaurant week and honestly weren't that impressed. if you go here, I would recommend the udon and drinks, not the sushi!

I usually love this place precovid, but the last service experience was so upsetting. We arrived around 5:30pm on a Tuesday and it was their down time. After 15 minutes, my sister had to walk up and ask the host for our server to order and we had to wave another host/server to ask for our server for the check since he was no where to be found (she called another server to come over). We were done eating for 20 mins and was trying to find our server to get the check. He also forgot our nephew's (2y/o) roll. He claimed it's coming but came after everyone was done eating which was sad cus he has allergies to a bunch of stuff and french fries + eel/cucumber roll was his dinner. The tip left was mainly for the busboy since he did all the work.

$35 Dinner set during restaurant week. ($38 with the spicy tantan udon) WARNING: Don't get anything with uni if you want to be safe. I should have known better because it looked way too watery.. but ours was a miss, I might go as far as to say it was spoiled which we relayed to the wait staff. I hope no one else will have to experience that lingering gone-bad fish taste, lemme tell you fresh uni does not taste like that. Although it was a deal I would not eat the sushi here again, woke up the next morning with my stomach churning (mind you this is without swallowing the uni sushi...). In fairness it isnt a sushi restaurant, it's a restaurant that specializes in udon noodles, so I would recommend sticking with the udon dishes (sans the uni cream one) to have a better experience. I wish I had just ordered a full bowl of udon instead.

I came here for weekend dinner with a couple of friends  (party of 7). We The decor is very nice - a trendy restaurant perfect for an intimate date. 

I ordered the curry katsu udon. The bowl that they serve it in is huge and shallow. I think it can be a bit misleading because it looks like there's very little inside but there is a good portion in there.

The curry katsu udon was delicious! Lots of noodles inside with tender pieces of katsu. I would definitely come here again to try the sushi/sashimi.
This Omakase was a GREAT deal for Restaurant Week at only $21! The regular deals also looked great. Delicious sushi and udon and it was more than I could even finish.

I've wanted to try this place for a while, and with the added incentive of the Restaurant Week specials, I decided to come by for lunch on a Tuesday. My friend and I had reservations for 1pm, but when we arrived, the dining room(s) was quite empty, and we were immediately led through the elegantly-designed bar to a small, cosier room to our table. I quite liked the chic, trendy aesthetic, and thought it was generally a really nice environment to enjoy a meal in.

We started with a soy garlic fried chicken to share - it was excellently seasoned and perfectly fried. The garlicky soy sauce (as the name would suggest) was nice, but way too salty in my opinion - as we ate our way through the plate, the chicken just got saltier and saltier, having been marinating in the sauce longer and longer.

For our mains, we both ordered from the Restaurant Week menu - the deluxe omakase for me and the premium omakase for my friend. Both come with a bowl of udon - we both chose the sukiyaki beef - 8 pieces of nigiri (the specific fish varied), and a negitoro roll.

The nigiri and roll weren't bad - a little too much rice per piece for my taste - and while the fish was certainly fresh, it wasn't spectacular in either taste or texture.

Sukiyaki udon was the highlight of the meal. The noodles were well-cooked and delicious, and the broth was amazing - rich and flavourful, with just the right juxtaposition of sweet and savoury. I had actually only expected a small bowl of udon as a 'side', but the portion sizes were really large, and I was so stuffed at the end of our meal.

Anyway, especially for this Restaurant Week special, I thought this meal was such a great value for the price point (despite the mediocre sushi), and from browsing the menu, I think even without these promotions, I'd still love to return to try one of the countless varieties of udon (in their well-known extra-large bowls!) someday

Great service & food! I got the cold uni udon. Wanted the uni, scallop, ikura udon but they ran out of ikura . 
Uni was fresh & udon was cooked perfectly. I would come back here again!

My friend and I decided to come here because they had a restaurant week special and it did not disappoint! The sushi was incredible. The udon noodles were good but nothing spectacular. Which is the only reason I didn't give it five stars. I would definitely go back and try some more noodles and the sushi is a must! I'm not sure if their menu was only restaurant week because it seemed like they had a lot of other deals on noodles and sushi that I think anyone would find something they'd want to order and should give it a try!

I have been going to Tsurutontan since they opened. 
Have been to the one in Tokyo as well where I got to know them. 
Now, I am sad to say that I'll not be going back there. 
Today was my worst experience. I even had few take out during the pandemic so that I can support their business somehow. 
Well today, the tables were so close together that you barely have space to pass through which still kind of makes you feel uncomfortable. 
Fruit flies all over where we were, customers next table were trying to kill them... omg. 
Their menu changed a lot, no more choice for thin or thick noodles, no more double portions... 
A lot is sushi. Why??? 
Anyhow, it's sad and disappointing.

My husband and I stopped by here with my in-laws recently and were disappointed by how the quality has gone down. 
Not that we're picky people but from the beginning the menus they handed us were pretty tattered and dirty. I got the spicy wagyu tofu udon and there was no tofu in it whatsoever. The broth was also on the sweeter side so it made it hard to finish. My husband ordered the creamy snow crab udon and we found one piece of crab in it the size of my fingernail. Broth was good but for the price we'd had like to see more crab in it. My mother in-law ordered the premium sushi set but what came was clearly different from the picture. The uni sushi was basically liquified and the tuna was bloody so it made the rice red. They didn't have roe that day but didn't tell us and replaced it with a random sushi I guess. 
For apps we got the corn fritters but it didn't taste like corn. It was more so a flour pancake with burnt corn on the outer edges. We also got the dumplings but they were made poorly so when we got the dish the dumpling wrappers were open and the fillings all fell out when we went to grab a piece. We got some kind of sautéed or grilled mushroom dish as well but there must've been 4 pieces of mushroom and the rest of the dish was some kind of fried filler, maybe potatoes. It was just oily and not good. 
Service was great though but I don't think we'd come back for the food here anymore.

First time coming and decided to pick Resturant week. Sushi plus small udon, well worth the trip. Only downside is the location isn't good for parking cause of union square and weekend they block off streets so it's even worse. Food wise lovely stuff. I got their sukiyaki beef udon which taste exactly what it is with very thick and good chew udon noodles. I also had their uni udon which was creamy base with uni on top. Not my type of dish but over all tasty. My recommendation is come on happy hour just to save a little bit of money but worth a taste. The rock shrimp appetizer was prob the best bite. Definitely come back

Got take out and it was pretty good! I got the three roll combo with cold udon! I enjoyed the sushi and the udon was good! I like being able to get both for such a good price! My friend got the truffle udon and it was good! Definitely good for the price you are getting! Good choice for a quick and cheap meal!

Our server told us only after we ordered some appetizers and stared to eat that they had this "restaurant policy that each customer had to order one main course" of udon or sushi + udon set. I would totally understand it if they have quality food and better services.
Bad service, terrible attitude. All the bad reviews say the food is good but service is rude. How about firing the manger because she is sooooo rude.

Such inexplicably subpar udon/ramen for the city. Ordered the spicy wagyu -- broth had ZERO flavor & was not spicy at all. The "wagyu" was also major fatty & tasted old. And they charge $4 for a watered down draft ginger ale... literally what. GO TO IPPUDO HONEY and thank me later g'bye

I came here for dinner with friends. We ordered drinks and I got a spicy tan tan. My orders were good and correct, but the drink my friend ordered contained roach. We asked for a replacement and a refund, but the manager said we could either get a replacement and pay the price for one or get a refund. This explanation was not without attitude and unprofessionalism on the manager's part. My friends and I will not be giving our service to this place from here on out.

Amazing service. Came here with my friends and the hostess was super kind. They requested to see proof of vaccination and thankfully we all were. Besides that, the ambience in the restaurant was super comfortable and chill. They have a nice bar and the drinks all looked so yummy. You see the bar right when you walk in. I got the lychee-tini which was delicious. They have an amazing all day happy hour (for appetizers)  and I think they have happy hour (for apps) on weekends too. We got so many appetizers and sushi. We all got our own entrees - you're not supposed to share entrees which is what they told us which is fine because we were all starving anyway. We got the premium omakase (one of my friends and me) and our other friend got the sushi rolls with udon. the combo entrees all ranged from 25-35 but it was such a good deal. there were also just sushi or just noodles by itself as an entree. I was shocked and amazed how good of a deal that was with omakase sushi & a sushi roll with udon... I was stuffed! The food did take a little longer to come but it was fine because it showed how much work they put in while making our sushi! I will definitely be coming back here again. My friends and I enjoyed the food and the service so much. We all thought the food was great. Our server was super friendly and helpful with the menu and had a good sense of humor. Everyone was always helping out pouring more water for us, getting rid of our dirty plates, and kept checking up on us. One of the servers that was helping out accidentally threw out my friends food  instead of packing it to go that they made their entire order from scratch to bring home to because they felt so bad! How awesome was that! The food was 10/10, service was 10/10 and this is perfect for date night or casual hang out with friends. They also have outdoor seatings. This was super close to the Union Sq station!

Ordered delivery from DoorDash for dinner since they have BOGO deals on udon / rice dishes right now and I was craving something soupy and warm. I got swayed by how good of a deal $16 for two udon dishes was. The order somehow took 3 hours because the restaurant said they didn't get the order request until 2 hours after I placed it :( 

The actual udon was just okay. I got the chicken udon and gave the other free bowl to a friend; neither of us were that impressed. I enjoyed the warm broth but the noodles themselves tasted like standard grocery store udon, maybe even those instant udon bowls. If you want an actual bowl of GOOD udon, I would highly recommend going to Raku in SoHo / East Village. 

A good deal for the BOGO right now but if they didn't have that deal I wouldn't recommend.

I came here for the restaurant week and was pleasantly surprised by how giant the portions are. The RW deal that I got included a small bowl of udon, a sushi roll and 8 pieces of sushi for just around 20 dollars, which was a steal. The udon was pretty tasty, and the fish was more fresh than I thought. When you come to tsurutontan, you know that you're getting solid udon for a good deal, which is my favorite part of this place. However, do NOT get the lychee martini - I was so excited to try it, but it is not at all sweet and tastes just like straight vodka. 

However, I do have to dock off a star for the service. We came here while it was raining, and the ceiling had a hole that started leaking rainwater down on our heads. The staff half heartedly offered us a change of table, but the new table wouldn't have fit all of us comfortably. After doing so, they offered no other solutions despite a small flood former on the chair. Regardless, any meal at tsurotontan is a great deal, and I would definitely come back on a less rainy day.

The whole time I was basically trying to shoot away fruit flies. There was so many of them flying around our food :(  we got the a couple of different appetizers and 2 sushi and udon dinner set. The fish wasn't fresh but the tan tan spicy udon was pretty good. We had 4 different waiters coming to check on us but one of the guys was very pushy and took our plates in a hurry. I normally never complain about service in other restaurants but this one had to be mentioned. SRRY:(

Got here at 1:30pm and it is now 2:08. Waitress was rude and when I asked about the different pricing on the online menu and in-restaurant menu she rolled her eyes. I thought the lunch combo was $17/$18 and the dinner was $25. I went for lunch and paid $25 so I was trying to clarify since I've been there for lunch before and paid $18. Also, a group of 3 came and they got their food way before us even tho we got there first. I've been to the other location that has better service.

From the reviews, this place looked promising but execution-wise this place did not deliver. We got the beef udon and 3 type sushi combo and another order of the Tan Tan udon. The 2 udon were not bad but the sushi was what brought down the stars. It was clear the fish was not fresh and quite warm. Maybe it was an off day or the weather outside was in the 90's but I would recommend another spot for sushi.

Went here for a nice dinner at the union square location. We ordered the tempura plate for appetizer--squash was delicious, wish we could have had more pieces than just the one! For the main course we ordered the sizzling sukiyaki with beef and the salmon lover combo with soy dashi udon. Salmon sushi was high quality, which was a pleasant surprise as this place is known for its udon. Sukiyaki did not come in a broth (nor did it come in a stone bowl as advertised), but was still delicious and a great option for someone who is not in the mood for soup. Udon noodles were delicious, and staff was very gracious when we noticed they made a mistake in our order. Will come again to try more udon!

They have bogo for certain udons and they also have deals for a sushi roll and udon that are pretty good! I got beef udon for takeout and i got bogo and I thought it was really worth it! I also tried the sea and truffle roll which was pretty good!!

I got the beef udon (marked as one of their best sellers). The best part of the dish was definitely the broth. Besides that, everything was good but nothing spectacular as I've definitely had better elsewhere. However, still a great bowl of udon! However, the beef itself wasn't as flavorful

Since we were in the neighborhood, we couldn't let this one slid. All I wanted some fried oysters and a mug of cold beer. Somehow the fried oysters were not available then I switched to sautéed mushroom$8, Bluefin Toro Sashimi$22, and my chilled Sapporo was $6.
To main courses: Mini Sukiyaki beef Rice Donburi Set $12, Uni Ikura Scallop udon $30.
For the sake of huge serving bowls, I would definitely go back!

I popped in today for lunch because I knew Tsurutontan has great lunch specials. I and many of my acquaintances had been regulars of Tsurutontan. My last visit was about 1 week ago and it went great. 
Today's experience is one of the most terrible dining experiences I had in NYC. When I arrived, the hostess doesnt seem to know how to accommodate incoming guests. She straight up led me to outdoor dining when she didnt even ask my opinion which was I wanted to sit inside. I corrected her right away and it was just a small glitch. I didnt think much about it because I think she was new. I would let this whole thing slide by if not for the terrible service and overcooked noodles.
What mainly led me to this two star review was the server. She was distanced and indifferent. She wasnt even polite. There was no greeting nor conversation. She went straight up asking me what I want. This is the first sentence she initiated to me. She even seemed cold when she brought the udon to me. The second sentence she even conveyed was "here you go" when she brought back the check for me to sign. Yes, she only said two sentences in total and also in cold tones. 
Another factor contributing to this review was the udon noodle. It was obviously overcooked because the noddles were soppy and the texture were squishy and almost disgusting. 
I didn't feel welcomed so I finished my bowl really quickly to get out of there. I will go back to Tsurutontan in the near future.

Somewhat underwhelming. There were some components that were good but overall mediocre. I went here with a friend for restaurant week and got the omakase which included 8 pieces of nigiri, tuna roll and a small bowl of udon for $21. At first, I felt pretty hyped because I love sushi and I love udon so win win right? Sadly that's not exactly how it panned out.

The sushi rice was extremely sticky and took away from the nigiri experience. The fish was fresh but nothing too special about it. Usually nigiris melt in your mouth from the flavor and texture of the fish but that did not happen here. The inari was actually not good and I struggled to finish that single piece. As for the udon, they offered soy dashi, sukiyaki beef, cold or to upgrade for other proteins for an additional fee. I upgraded to $3 beef but now that I think about it, seemed unnecessary considering my friend got sukiyaki beef (for no extra charge) which also came with beef so mildly confused?? Also, like other reviewers have mentioned, my broth was also lukewarm when I got it. Granted, I waited 3-5 minutes until my friend's order came but doubt that should have resulted in it being cooled significantly. I will give it to them on their udon though because that did taste good.

Service was mediocre for the price point you're paying to eat here. When bringing 1 of 2 omakases to the table, we asked which one that was and the server didn't know himself and had to double check. Would possibly consider coming back to get their udon on their regular menu. Wouldn't recommend the sushi.

If you're looking for a restaurant with a killer lunch menu and happy hour, this is the place!

I ordered the 2 roll special. It came with a full bowl of udon and two sushi rolls. My order was the cold udon, avocado roll and mentaiko egg roll. Since it was happy hour, I decided to also order crispy corn tempura. Their select appetizers were half price! All of this came out to $25 plus tip! What a steal, right?!?!

The food was absolutely incredible! The broth for the udon wasn't too salty. I learned I wasn't a fan of cold broth. It wasn't the restaurant's fault - it was more so my preference. The crispy corn tempura was amazing! It was extremely crispy. The sauce tasted delicious. I'm not too sure what it was, though. Both of the rolls were nothing fancy but still enjoyable!

The service was a little slow, but I have no complaints. Just be aware when you come in :)

3.5 stars. Tsurutontan lost some of that wow factor for me since they first opened. The first time I came here, I was shocked by the portion sizes - there was a generous serving of udon, and it wasn't just a giant bowl. During my most recent visit, it seemed like the portion sizes have gotten smaller. The dashi broth for the tempura udon is yummy, but I managed to finish all the udon and still felt a bit hungry. I could never finish an order before. I remember the udon being silky with a nice bite to it but that seemed to be missing this time around as well.

Would probably still stop by once in a while for my udon cravings. If I'm paying ~$20 for udon though, I would like to at least feel satisfied, if not extremely full.

- food was about half an hour late (Ordered for a particular time)
- no utensils included

This has always been my favorite spot to eat everything BUT the Udon's lol 

I've always found the udon a bit on the sweet side, it's good, but not my things. 

I've always love the other food, such as rice bowl, sashimi, appetizers, drinks, desserts. 

Though, after the pandemic and shutdown, I think all the chefs changed, the food the doesn't taste the same.
Especially the shrimp tempura, ekkk nope. I used to order it all the time. 
Not I won't be back for a while... sorry
The first time I wait for 20minutes to get my dishes. The second time , though food was prepared faster, they said they don't accept Apple Pay.

Decent curry udon -- pretty identical experience to the Midtown location, though miles behind the og Osaka location. Big udon bowls are so fun even if the contents are a tad salty & the waiters never refill our water promptly.

Sukiyaki udon - so flavorful. it comes in a huge bowl! totally recommend the lunch sets which are affordable and filling
Salmon - delicious 

I want to come back to try other dishes as well!

I personally do not like Japanese food because I generally feel like the broth is too oily and lacks flavor. However, I've made an exception to this spot. Went on a coworker's recommendation and loved the food and ambience. They open at noon but there were 4 tables waiting to be seated. Felt safe with the covid regulations and food came out in relatively good time.
Broth was savory and delicious, ingredients tasted fresh and wait staff was very attentive.
Would suggest tgat you go there early because by 1 PM it was pretty packed.
Option to sit outside if you're unable to prove vaccination.

A place devoted to Udon? Ok wow. Big wow. And sushi?? The portions are MASSIVE. Service was pretty fast, a pretty cheap lychee martini too for downtown. They have a combo sushi udon deal that was also huge.

I went here during lunch and ordered the 2 roll combo with Eel Avocado & Spicy Tuna rolls and Sukiyaki Beef Udon. The bowls are HUGE. The photo on the menu does not do it justice! The quality of the rolls were great and fresh, the udon was yummy. I will  definitely be coming back to try more items from the menu!
However, I will say the food took a long time to come... I would say coming here to dine in on a lunch break would be stretching it. Order takeout!

Came here for dinner - had the supreme omakase and the lychee Tini; both amazing ! Will definitely come back to try new dishes. All the food was fantastic; the only downside was the seating. We sat upstairs in the doorway of the kitchen... had a lot of people walking past and it was annoying

The udon is pretty decent and the portion size is pretty large. The udon comes in a huge bowl that is half filled, but still a decent amount of noodles. Really filling especially if you add an appetizer.

Pros are that they have a wide range of unique fusion-y options and large wuantity. However I prefer the quality, noodles, and execution of more traditional places. Might go back if very hungry or craving a particular dish

What happened to you???
Came in around 14:30 today (Sunday).  
I've been coming about once a month to this location for almost a decade for two reasons; the excellent service and great food, but today unfortunately both were totally disappointing.
