Were greeted by the host and gave us the "bench" table, I looked around and saw there's at least three four tops so I ask if we could have one of those table by the window instead, he said no they're only for more people (it's was just my husband and I), I didn't want to argue by saying that the place is practically empty but he saw my hesitation then he suggested if we want we could wait for the two tops booth to open up, I said yes.
My husband and I waited at the bar, he had a drink while we waited.

Not a long wait until we were seated and the server came to take our order.                                     I asked the server if I could have soba noodles instead of the udon and without missing a beat, she said "this is an udon place, we don't have soba" as her fore finger tapping the front page menu where the word UDON is.  Baffled, out of word and mildly offended I said "ok".  Yes, we New Yorkers do sarcasm very well, but in the service industry, sarcasm in the absence of humor is just rudeness.  Btw sweetheart, with that logic you should not have any sushi or any rice dishes etc.

Food:
-Uni Creme udon; taste like dry mix cream of corn soup with a hint of dashi, temperature was barely warm.
-Tsurutotan deluxe: taste ok, temperature barely warm.
Our food came at awkwardly separate time.

I asked the food runner/bus person for shichimi togarashi and when I realized that he didn't understand what I was asking for, so I said to him red pepper powder, he came back with it and said that he couldn't understand me because he doesn't speak Spanish, neither do I...I was speaking in English.
As we were eating, we overheard the host telling another guests that they're going to have to move when he needs the table I guess they don't like the bench either), there's still four tables open on that floor!
What are you going to do?! Tell people to stop eating and move!?!  and did I mention there's four open tables and oh the bench area were also open!
My restaurant pet peeve: when they give you the check before they cleared the table and yes the server saw that we were finished eating because she asked if we want anything else, we said no thank you and she walked away without trying to take any of the dishes and came back and placed the check on the table between the dirty dishes.

If this is Tsurutontan's training issue, you can do better(I've seen it) but If this is a personality issue, than maybe service industry is not what these people should be doing.
 I'm going to end this review with a positive note,
both bartenders were courteous, especially the  older gentleman at the bar and he didn't even serve us, I appreciate you!

Came with a friend for a late lunch, so we made for happy hour. Overall, it was pretty empty so seating and such was not an issue. Plus the place is pretty large. Our waiter was pretty sweet. When there was a minor mixup with our order, she apologized and got it fixed pretty quickly. 

I got the US Beef Wagyu Truffle Dashi, which comes with some of the meat cooked and some not completely cooked (but it cooks as it sits in the hot broth). It seemed like there was a lot less compared to the other that my friend ordered. Not a big issue, as I was content by the time I finished mine. Overall, it was a decent bowl of udon but I personally did not think it was particularly special. Maybe it was the particular udon I got. I don't necessarily see myself going out of my way to come here again...at least for the udon. They do have a bunch of other things that looked appetizing as well, and the happy hour prices were solid. I can see it being a solid selling point. I just wasn't hungry enough to order more than the udon. So if I come back, maybe I'll try a different udon or something else on the menu.

My husband and I had lunch here on our vacation. Although I realize this isn't directly attributable to the restaurant, it was really a treat to be in a dining space where everyone had been vaccinated. The space was sparkling clean, the food was delicious, and the staff took good care of us.

This place's food is good and it has large portions. The only complaint I have is that they took 15 minutes to take our order and then 30 minutes to bring the food out. I still frequently visit here and would probably still recommend to anyone that doesn't mind the wait.

Got their BOGO for takeout, and got the katsu curry udon. Beware that the items on their menu online are not always available on the different delivery apps. 

The curry udon was really good, and the katsu was solid. I also got the chicken BOGO which was a big hit. They were soaked in sauce though so not as crispy as one would expect. Overall super worth for the price, especially in NYC!

I celebrated my friend's birthday on Sunday night for dinner. Reservation must be made. We got seated in a corner. Unfortunately, the food tray is so big that it couldn't fit 3 trays on a table. We moved to a 4 seated table instead. We ordered drinks and I got the kyoto perfection light cocktail. I really liked it! 

My friends and I each ordered the premium omakase sushi combo. I got it with the spicy tan tan odun noodle soup for additional $3 and bluefin negitoro roll for another $3 which comes out $41. Warning! The spicy tan tan is really spicy. It hit the back of my throat and I was coughing up the storm while drinking water until the spices went down. My friends got the spicy tuna roll & US wagyu udon (additional $5), apparently the most popular. 

Overall I enjoyed the foods. The service was decent. I would say you feel a bit rushed while dining. They have 2 restroom locations. Be aware the lower leveled restroom is unisex with two stalls and one shared sink.

I ordered the salmon set with the beef udon. 

First of all, my water cup was really oily and the cup was dirty so I asked for a new cup and it seemed like the same cup was returned to me. The waitress grabbed the cup with her entire palm from the top so she was touching the entire rim of where you're supposed to drink from. Already feeling bad that I had to ask for a new cup, I didn't say anything else and just didn't drink my water for obvious sanitary reasons. Next, the food came out and it looked really good--I was so excited to have your set. I was so disappointed with the quality. The salmon was weirdly sweet and super thin plus didn't seem fresh at all. The rice underneath the sushi was hard and kept falling apart so I ended up taking out all the rice. The rolls were covered in the same hard, stale rice and I had to take some off as well. The udon had soggy noodles (which is usually not like that because I eat at your restaurant quite frequently) and the beef was all fat. And just to top that all off, I was still eating and the waitress took away my food. I was too exhausted and annoyed to even ask for it back when I came back to the table so I just paid and left. This was a really frustrating experience and I feel like my time and money has just been wasted.

I'm not entirely sure why this establishment has such high ratings but I had an overall terrible experience. First of all, when you walk in there are customers standing around because none of the staff is acknowledging or helping get people seated. People who arrived on time for reservations hadn't been acknowledged or helped for over 10 minutes. And when you did try and ask for help the response you would get is "a host will come soon." When I finally did get sat, my waiter was great but the food not so much. I got the lunch special Sukiyaki Beef udon and sushi combo. My order arrived incorrectly twice. The first bowl of udon that arrived had been sitting there for a while before it got to my table. The noodles were way overcooked and the soup not even hot. There was a difference in the second bowl they brought out. The meat used in the udon seemed like it was cheap leftover meat. The sushi was incorrect both times it arrived. I asked they add cream cheese to a salmon avocado roll. The first time they brought out a salmon cucumber roll with cream cheese. The second time it was again a salmon cucumber roll with a side of cream cheese. It felt very passive aggressive and the person that brought my food gave zero explanation as to what the lump of white stuff was since I asked for the cream cheese to be in the roll. I will not be coming back here.

I've been coming here well before the pandemic and I've had fantastic experiences each time. My go to is the US wagyu udon, and wagyu sushi. However, I decided to order some nigiri this time, I have a salmon allergy so I asked if I could substitute for another kind of fish in their combo. My waitress abruptly said "'no." So warning to people with food allergies, Tsurutontan will NOT accommodate you. It's a pity because I really like this place for udon but I will be looking for other options from now on. Also.. they didn't check my covid vaccination card before I dined inside.

We had a group of 15 for a birthday dinner, and you can see some of the things that we ordered in the picture. The reason for three stars is that we had to wait until everyone was there to be seated, which I understand is relatively standard for many places, but we were missing only one more person and had to wait 15 mins for it. I wish the restaurant were a little more understanding. Another reason is that we found a bone in one of the Sushi dishes we ordered. They were quick to replace it with a fresh dish. 

The food was not top of the line and nothing out of the ordinary. But if you're expecting just good comforting Japanese food, it won't disappoint you.

HUGE bowl of udon and soup. So many varieties in this bowl too. You have tempura, chicken, egg drop, seaweed, beef. No MSG in the soup and it's not salty nor heavy. A choice that will never go wrong. A little expensive probably but I think it's so worth it.
Good udon but bleh soup base. Just want a simple chicken stock but have never been satisfied. Good appetizers and nice setting. The midtown location is better than the union sq one.

Do not sleep on their weekday lunch/dinner specials!! I came here for Tsurutontan on a Friday afternoon with no wait. The staff checked my COVID vaccine cards and IDs and we were seated pretty spaced out from other guests. My friend and I decided to share the 3 roll (salmon avocado, eel avocado, and shrimp tempura) and the beef sukiyaki udon (regular size), which was ~$20. The meal was delicious and very filling for two people. Definitely recommend checking this place out if you're looking for a value meal!

Great spot for both udon noodles and sushi. I came for dinner and ordered the Tri Color from the dinner set menu, which included tuna, salmon, and hamachi nigiri, spicy tuna roll, and sashimi as well as a small bowl of udon (I chose the sukiyaki beef udon). The sushi tasted fresh and the udon was nice and chewy, while the beef in the udon soup was tasty too. For all of this, $25 seems like quite a good deal.

The restaurant is tastefully decorated with somewhat dim lighting to create a more intimate atmosphere. There are two levels of seating indoors, with the top level being smaller and cozier. The service (speed and friendliness) were fine.

Overall, Tsurutontan might've not knocked my socks off, but it is certainly a nice spot if you're an udon fan and even better if you like sushi too. I would definitely recommend the dinner set menu options if you make a visit.

3.5/5

Second time here, and still not the biggest fan. When they first opened, I really enjoyed their thick, chewy noodles, but wasn't too impressed by the cream based broths.

Before I get into the food, I did want to mention that I was a bit put off by the seating arrangements. Came on a Saturday a little after lunch so it wasn't crowded at all. This is a fairly huge place, with a lower level, the first floor, and even second floor seatings (it was closed off though). Considering it was no where near full house, I was very surprised when the hostess seated us directly next to a couple. Again, there were a lotttttt of other seats available to ensure that diners could be distanced. Even though they asked to see proof of vaccination, if possible, it would be nice to stay further away, right? Especially when the space allows for that.

Later on, as we were finishing up, they again seated a party of four on the right of us, when it was practically empty on the lower level (this I saw as I was exiting the restaurant after paying), and another couple who expressed not wanting to be so close and was given an alternative seating that wasn't any better, so they chose to sit on our left instead. 

Ok on to the noodles, which had definitely lost their charm since opening. Still fat, but no longer chewy - aren't the noodles supposed to be the star?

Crab Truffle Udon: I'd forgotten that they serve their udons in these huge ass bowls, yet only fill 25% of it. Aesthetics. Lol. Despite that, it's actually a very good portion as we were immediately full. Just that as we kept eating this bowl, it was starting to taste more and more like clam chowder, but with limited crab. So that's a bummer

Wagyu Udon: got a small size and mmm this soup is very very good. Quite shocked that this stole the show for me, loved the super beefy broth and the meat. Gladly will drink more but don't give me these soggy noodles again, man

Salmon Deluxe: their salmon nigiri is all rice, the salmon slices are so thin, but the other rolls were decent. Again, a lot of food for one person so it's very shareable

Tastes like Japan.

The wasabi tastes as if it's actually grated from the root. Fish is on point as if it was swimming only just moments before. Sukiyaki udon makes you want to just finish after the first bite.

There is no short of happiness I had from eating the hearty meal presented in front of me. I only wish my tummy could expand so that I could inhale more!

From a bang for buck perspective, you are definitely getting a good moneys worth. For premium Omakase, believe it is around 38. The otoro that they use can easily be 5-7 bucks as a single order, they include Uni as well in the mix!

Finally, the drinks are okay though, they pair well but are not astonishing...! 

10/10 would be back again to get my fill on udon and sushi!

I think the waiter was having a bad day, we went to eat something but she was rude from the beginning that we decided to eat somewhere else. We had better attention from the busboy he tried to explain the difference between ramen and udon unlike the waiter.

It would be 5 stars if the music was better, pretty awful today. It's a cool elegant setting especially upstairs, but the music was bad teeny bopper. It didn't really fit with $25 udon and $22 toro which were really good!!!
Food was good, environment is 5 stars. Just little pricy, ordered beef udon. Soup was perfect, udon was good, but very tiny slices of beef.
Great service and food! Lots of space and tables open. Made it easy and low-maintenance to make a reservation

This isn't a review of the food, because i didn't get to eat any. My friend was running 25 mins late so i wanted to take a seat, order an appetizer, etc. but no, their policy was no seating till whole party present. I can understand that for a busy restaurant, but this was 2pm on a Monday and it was empty. Went to ootoya instead. Yum.
Solid udon place with lots of options! Service was great and decor is cute for date night or casual night. Come for happy hour all day Monday - Wednesday!

I am giving this place 3 stars instead of 2 because the restaurant isn't a total dump.  What is a dump is the food.  The udon was absolutely terrible. So disappointing after having many an amazing udon in NYC.  The issue - its loaded with sugar.  All sweet, no savory, and nothing Japanese about at all.

I guess it's a cool venue but the semi defrosted dumplings and sugar poisoned udon were pretty much inedible. Also what is with the viking sized bowls and spoons, I thought this was a Japanese restaurant.

I ordered a delivery and the soup container was completely opened. Everything spilled and destroyed other items too. This is a upon place they should be more careful with the items with soup. Either using different containers or wrap it more carefully. My lunch is ruined. Probably never order again. Be careful who wants to order from this restaurant

Food took over 40 minutes to arrive and we had to ask the server to get our food. Food was so-so, the fish from the sushi roll had a not-fresh odor and the sushi rice was too chewy. However, the udon was good. I also was charged 1 cent for a mysterious, unexplained "House SM Suki" item.

As usual Tsurutontan serves massive portions. We ordered the triple roll combo that comes with the sukiyaki udon. We had a spicy tuna roll, salmon avocado roll, and a shrimp tempura roll. And all three rolls were to our satisfaction. 

The other dish, however, the truffle broth udon, with snow crab and mushrooms was a little polarizing. Rozena who loves mushrooms was a big fan, while I thought it was just okay. The mushrooms were plentiful and overwhelming, while the snow crab was almost non existent. I suppose that for an affordable dish like that which features normally expensive ingredients one couldn't complain much about that.

Cool modern low-light atmosphere.  Wide choice of interesting broth flavors (I got the wagyu truffle).  Noodles were a bit overcooked / soggy, but still tasty.  Their soy garlic fried chicken was pretty solid as well. 

The biggest perk of this place is that you can make reservations online through Resy, and it's much easier to get a table compared to Raku.

I just love the idea of getting a large bowl of udon during the winter of New York. It is adapted to all kinds of Asian flavors, including curry, Korean style, westernized creamy broth, and other traditional Japanese flavor as well. Take your friends with you and they will always find something they like!

Perhaps it was the company. 

But their tuna cones are superb, fun to eat and delish. 

My udon was gigantic and not lacking in meat broth richness while his uni ikura crab bowl is nothing short of amazing- but how could anything w that trinity be short of stellar? 

Drinks were strong and perfect for the occasion. Atmosphere was intimate & service decent. Definite revisit.

So delicious. Best Udon I've ever had. Their happy hour prices are fantastic! 

Will be back for sure.

Been really wanting to try out this place and finally had a chance to have a quick dinner date in the car. Yes in the car ! Being constraint with time and difficulty finding parking, we ended up order an Uber eats delivery to the car. Aside from that, they had many generous take out and delivery specials including buy one get one and up to 50% off select items. We ended ordering sukiyaki beef udon noodle soup and a mini spicy tuna rice bowl. The sukiyaki beef broth was so delicious ; however, as we continued eating we felt that it was getting saltier and saltier. The mini spicy tuna bowl was disappointing tho. Perhaps the tuna got cooked when it was confined in a take out container, but it was bland with very little tuna and a lot of rice. Overall, I need to make a trip to dine in the restaurant and experience the hot bowl of udon by itself.

Delivery service of the Japanese style fried chicken...tatsutage. The chicken was rubbery and hard. I was surprised because usually Japanese places have a light crisp on the outside and tender and juicy chicken in the inside. I was a little disappointed.

Udon on a cold day - yes please! 

Pros: 
-spacious layout 
-diverse offering of udon types 
-rich broth in the wagyu udon. Get it if you like mushrooms as well 
-handmade noodles (softish and not bouncy) 

Critiques: 
-music is slightly loud if you're sitting next to the speakers overhead 
-California roll was $14.00 for small portion, however the crab is "blue crab" 
-greasy tempura 

Our server provided awesome service. The udon comes in super large bowls - unique presentation!

We take time to support local business in NYC, most especially during the pandemic.

We went in to try experience the food that has gathered rave reviews. But in the five minutes we were there waiting for a table, we met the rudest hostess: we saw her tell a group that they have another 15 minutes before they lose their table and be put back on the wait list; we witnessed her just wave off another group to check the menu instead of cordially showing them; then, when it came to us, she said we have an hour and 15 minutes to eat because we did not have a reservation.

How can you enjoy a meal when you are on deadline? Trust that New Yorkers know about setting their limit and we had kids with us and it's not like we were going to socialize for hours. 

Then I look around, there is easily about 40-50 if not more empty seats, before we sat and upon our departure. Our server did not come to our table for another ten minutes. Is that part of the hour and 15 of our precious time?

Relax - your own story on your own website mentions "hospitality." There was absolutely none of that today. People eat out to have a good time and to savor the food and the few minutes at the top of our experience with this hostess has affected that very experience. 

What. A. Shame.

I don't even want to give this restaurant any stars.

The place is cute and service is nice and fast. The udon itself is not the best I've ever had nor the best sushi... but the large size of the udon was worth it for the laugh. Seriously the biggest bowl you'll ever see lol

came here with my friends from chicago because they were craving udon and found this place online. they had reservations but honestly we were early and they seated us before our reservation that was nice. the service was nice and quick, the space was big and clean, and there were dividers to separate each party. but honestly the food itself was just medicore/poor. my friends got the udon and yes although the udon comes in a big bowl, the udon itself (depending on what you get) just wasn't quite hitting the spot... the beef broth was a bit salty, the curry tasted a bit watered down, and the creamy udon was more on the watery side than creamy. the sushi deluxe was also very poor and didn't taste too fresh.. overall not worth the money or time :/

Probably the worst service I've had in my whole life. Extremely long waits for every item. Servers are incredibly rude. Food's not even good.

1/5

Excellent sushi and udon! They were accommodating of our last minute party change of adding one person. We had a to wait a little when we had a reservation. The deals for sushi and udon were incredible. I opted for the the 3 roll combo getting tuna avocado, salmon avocado, and eel cucumber rolls along with soy dashi udon. It was my first time having udon so I'm not a great judge, but I found it slightly more watery and less flavorful than ramen, but I ordered a simple udon. The sushi was fresh and perfectly made! Service was great and again the prices can't be beat (I had leftovers too). I will be back!!
Just fantastic - udon was amazing, sushi was great - Nippon old fashioned was nice too with a sweet finish.
I had a really good beef udon here during happy hour for a great price! will definitely be coming back!

OMG the portions are enormous.  The udon can definitely be shared.  We ordered appetizers and that alone will fill you.  The udon was super delicious but so much of it was not touched because we filled up on the appetizers.  Took the balance home and was able to have it for another 2 meals.  Seriously, the size of the bowl is no joke.  Come with an appetite but share the udon if you want to enjoy the appetizers.  Coming again before I head home to CA.

Very disappointed especially when we were looking forward to a nice dinner out.  Instead we had ok food and had a poor overall experience .

Udon was ok at best.  Served in this giant size bowls but certainly did not have giant portions.  Shrimp tempura was oily and soggy.  Waste of money.  Sushi was not fresh.  To top it off, while eating the udon, felt something hard and a little sharp in my mouth, pull it out, turned out to be one of those thin tinfoil.  Could be the ones used to tie a bag.  Pointed it out to the waiter, was offered another bowl which we were not interested especially not comfortable with the chef knowing we pointed it out.

The bathroom was gross.  Paper towels were all over the floor.  Garage cans were overflowing.  Unacceptable!

Gave them a 2 star since they might be having a bad night, short of staff and etc. 

And yes, I paid full price for food that contained thin tinfoil!

Quality going downhill!!! I have been there many times and previously had really good experience. Went there last night, the sushi combo with noodle came out looked so sad!  Whoever is managing the kitchen needs to step up! The two star is for the nice service at the bar!

I came to Tsurutontan with a group (6) on a Saturday night. We had made a reservation beforehand and were seated when all our party arrived, which is pretty standard practice in the city. The place is massive- don't let its narrow exterior fool you! This place seems to go on for miles. 

We ordered a round of Lychee drinks which I think was a special for that day. I remembered it was really reasonably priced for NYC so that was pleasantly surprising. I ordered the Katsu Curry Udon, and I think if you order a large there is not extra charge and you just get more noodles so we all went for a large. The udon taste wasn't mind blowing (good noodle texture, curry was okay seasoned) but the size of the bowl/portion was truly something to write home about. I think if I had brought it home I could have survived on that bowl of udon for a solid 3 days. There was just THAT much udon and sauce. The pork katsu was nicely battered and fried. A smaller piece of meat but I wasn't surprised. Everything looked small in comparison to the massive bowl. The curry seasoning was okay- a little too much onion in my dish for my liking and I had wished there were other vegetables. However with the price, I don't think you can beat coming here for a quick fix meal. 

I would rate it 3.5/5 rolled up for the portion sizes. If you have a group that can eat a lot, this is a nice alternative without breaking the bank on a cold winter night.
Overall just an average udon place. Udon was salty and even with a reservation it took them another 40 minutes to seat me and friends.

Please take this review with a grain of salt - it was weekday dinner and we got our order in with the literal last order. Staff were probably busy with closing - 

Food (5/5) but price (2/5)- came here for dinner and the menu was super confusing; happy hour pricing supposedly goes til midnight and would have paid 20 for my meal but wound up spending up to 30?

Got the sukiyaki udon, the portions are gigantic. Soup was just the right amount of sweet, and the scallions were a nice touch. Egg was perfectly poached, ramen noodles were not too overdone (and the soup was still clear!) and the right thickness.

Ambiance (3/5) - well decorated and super cozy! Not too crowded though very efficient use of the space - but the place is not well insulated; the door kept getting propped open and for a nyc winter night this was not ideal.

Service (3/5) - slow, and a lot of simple things were overlooked, like we didn't get one of our ladles with our noodles and chopsticks with the other.

Despite all this I would definitely come again especially for the happy hour menu; want to try a lot of the ramen / noodle choices!

Modern decor, comfortable seating, attentive staff, excellent food
Always a great stop for amazing udon
The cucumber salad is nice and fresh with a splash of sesame oil
The tuna cones are good, not the most amazing take on raw tuna in a crispy shell, but something I always order anyways
We ordered the creamy spicy shrimp tempura for the first time - delicious, delicious sauce on top of a well fried shrimp with tempura style batter - the shrimp is not the typical elongated jumbo shrimp
Udon is delicious, many options to choose from whether you want savory, sweet, or creamy
The Uni Crème is a favorite of mine, but it's not for everyone - extremely creamy broth, surprisingly not too fishy with the roe and Uni.

The service was pretty good for how busy it was and the food was great for the price. 

There were some things that were a bit off that takes away from a perfect five stars. My party and I had a reservation so there was no wait time for a table. When we were seated, though, We waited a pretty long time to get our water glasses and silverware and to order. 

The salmon lover set is a great deal and the salmon nigiri was fantastic. The rolls were not my favorite, especially the one with crab in it. It tasted like chapstick. Of the three of us that ordered the salmon deluxe, one liked that roll. 

The spicy udon could have had more flavor and meat but the sukiyaki beef udon was delicious. Great amount of meat and good flavors. 

The sizzling sukiyaki was the best. Such good flavors and a huge portion. The meat was a bit fatty but overall it's a dish that you can't go wrong ordering. 

The fries were standard, the Mayo they come with is really good and usually I'm really not a fan of Mayo. 

Would come back! Getting different items though

Came here with my friend based on the reviews and we left disappointed . I ordered the beef wagyu truffle udon noodle. The bowl was huge but the portion size was small. There was barely any noodles . It contain basically just few pieces of beef and udon noodles. My friend had ordered Katsu curry udon noodles and it never came . After I had finished my food , we kept waiting for my friends order . When I finished , I asked the server how come my friends order hasn't come out yet , she said oh I thought you didn't want it cause you asked me if it was with rice . However , my friend never asked her that question. I remember my friend specifically told her he wanted to order the Katsu curry udon. It doesn't make sense for my friend to ask if it's rice when he specially pointed to the Katsu udon under the sub heading udon noodles . He knew it wasn't with rice ! My friend got upset and left with an empty stomach. To sum up my experience , Service sucks and food sucks !

I've gotten both the restaurant week deluxe omakase set and the udon before, and think the udon is wayyy better hands down. The sushi/omakase is rather underwhelming and not worth the price, but the udon is huge (you will be shook by how big the bowl is) and delicious. I got the sukiyaki deluxe udon since it was one of the most popular, and was not disappointed. There is so much flavor and the noodles are cooked perfectly. I can't wait to come back and try one of the creamy udons. Service can be a little slow at times though.

Sushi very good.
As was the noodles.
Also drank some sake.
Everyone else couldn't finish their food, so I finished their food.
I ate too much.
Recommend this restaurant.
No further comments.

Came here for an early dinner with my family. I had the sukiyaki udon before and wasn't a fan because it was so sweet, salty, and oily. But this time I had cream udon with premium sushi set and it was great! Highly recommend getting the two for one. The amount of noodles in one bowl is way too much for one small person normally. But the set has a perfect amount of noodle/soup and a large amount of sushi, perfect for one person and sharing! The quantity is huge and the space is nice for meet ups with friends and family.  The unagi was also very good, I enjoyed the shiso leaf with the udon.

How hard is it to get a delivery order correct that's just one order of noodles. Careless. You're a restaurant in the business of food. Get it right, at the very least. 

I ordered sukiyaki but got a beef udon instead. Would've been alright if it tasted okay. The beef is flavorless and tough and basically all fat. No vegetables. 
I sprinkled on a bit of spring onion and cilantro I had in my fridge. Udon noodles were not fresh, maybe cause I placed my order right before they closed. 

The experience eating at the restaurant I remember was a decent one, so thought I'd try ordering in. But eh.

Ordered the Sukiyaki Beef bowl. When it came out, it was super fragrant and beefy, and when I tried it, it was tasty but a bit too sweet for my liking. We also ordered the Salmon lover's combo, whose sukiyaki udon on the side was even sweeter than the sukiyaki bowl by itself since it didn't have the mushrooms and vegetables found in the standalone bowl to balance out the sweetness. Everything was priced reasonably, but coming  in on a Tuesday during their happy hour also helped with the bill. A nice satisfying meal overall, especially on a cold winter evening.

First of all, I love the ambiance and setup of this location. It's modern and great for a date night or gathering with friends and family. Making reservations online was easy. They do have outdoor seating but it's right on the sidewalk uncovered with no heat. It's pretty clear that they did not put too much effort on that part.

I came for the Wagyu Beef Truffle Dashi Udon which I first had in their midtown location years ago and still dream about. I remember it being heavenly and rich. Unfortunately, this time it seemed a bit more diluted which was disappointing. Next time I think I will try something else.

We also ordered the Soy Garlic Fried Chicken to share. If you are expecting it to be Korean-style, it is most definitely not. It just tasted like karage with soy sauce to me. I wouldn't recommend it.

First time here and it was delightful. Got here at the tail end of lunchtime on a Saturday. Starving after walking through the Union Square Greenmarket with one of my best friends. 
So four stars for two reasons. The first is that my waiter didn't write down our orders and forgot my soda the bar. He had to come back to confirm our appetizers. I think we came in between shift changes because it wasn't until after we were in the middle of eating that a different person asked if I had ordered a soda. I confirmed and she brought back a glass that clearly had been sitting for a while with pathetic melted ice in it. Been there but come on at least put some fresh ice in it- lol. I guess the tip was going to the guy that left. Second, was that the bar table set-up didn't social distance patrons or care how many folks were in there. I'm vaxxed and boosted but sheesh.

Pleasantly surprised by the food being more to satisfy a Japanese pallet than a typical Japanese restaurant that I come across. That said, it's got enough twists that that anyone would be happy to eat here.

Soy Garlic Fried Tatsuta Chicken was more soy than I expected and not much garlic. Personally, I think a drizzle on top and sauce on the side would be better since the garlic flavor is barely there. The delicious thigh meat made up for my expectations. Fried but not crunchy. So if you like the Korean kind, this is not it. Still worth ordering, though!

The shrimp appetizer had a mayo mixed with sriracha kind of flavor. I could've eaten the whole thing myself but my friend was the one who ordered it  
Expect gigantic bowls with enough food for one person. For aesthetic maybe? Unknown but I was grateful not to get any soup splashes on myself due to the high rim.
The soup of my katsu kare udon was great and exactly as I expected Japanese dark curry to taste. 
I was impressed with the shrimp because it was not the over battered kind that you get at most places. I'm usually peeling it off. My friend on the other hand was in mourning because that's the part she actually likes.

I noticed that the person sitting next to us at the bar-type table got katsu curry, too, but on a bowl of rice (donburi). It came out in a normal donburi bowl. 

The stranger across from us got the sushi platter but ate all the fish without the rice. Weird but helpful to see. The sushi had the right amount of rice so the sushi chef knows what they are doing. The salmon also looked quite fresh, too.  I think it must be their most popular dish because there were more combos with salmon than anything else. Sadly, no natto maki to be seen. 

Oh the tempura appetizer is mostly veggie with one or maybe two shrimp pieces. Ask what's in it before you order. I thought it was delicious but my friend was not too keen on the enoki. I forget what the other pieces were but it was also not what most Japanese restaurants serve. Not a bad thing at all because it sets them apart but I could see folks expecting carrot or sweet potato or something. 

Best to make a reservation if you want a table, need physical accommodations, are going at happy hour, lunch or dinner. Place was poppin' when we got there and then started building up again around 4pm.

Ambiance is modern but not a first date kinda place in my opinion. Bring someone you already know and someone who doesn't mind a meal experience lovely but not over the top. Or someone who likes gigantic soup bowls.

Gosh I love this place. I have been here so many times!! I have recommended this restaurant to so many people. If you feel like having a delicious bowl of udon - with curry, with cream sauce, with broth, this is the place to be. 

So far I have tried:

Wagyu Truffle Dashi - wagyu beef in the most savory truffle dashi. It is simple, comfort food and smells so good. I love this one

Wagyu Sukiyaki Deluxe - this comes in sweet soy broth with lots of wagyu, veggies, shimeji, maitake, shitake mushrooms, and a poached egg. It is delicious and filling. I recommend this if you're hungry.

Crab, Roe, Uni Donburi - expensive, but worth it if you are an uni lover.

There are more but I wrote this review like 3 years after I started going so I can't remember them all. Henceforth, I will be updating as I try more udons.

Please enjoy!

Also, although there is usually a line out the door, it is a pretty spacious place so it's not too bad of a wait. At least not the last couple times I went.

Wanted to try this place for a while and finally did it!
Came for a weekday lunch and surprised by the good ambiance and decoration of the restaurant. So pretty and chill!
Went for the wagyu deluxe sukiyaki.
At first, I was so surprised by the size of the bowl lol, HUGE. Same with the spoon that came with it haha
About the soup, happy that it actually came with lots of veggies, udon was really good and beef tender.
4 stars because the soup was way too sweet for my taste. So, although i had an overall good meal because of the ingredients, the soup was too much.
Service quick and very accomodating with my stroller!
The Sashimi Salad is the best way to get back to shape post New Year Celebration. Pair with a shot of sake.

Came here with some friends and we all loved the food! The udon was good, broths and curry were flavorful and sushi was fresh!
Definitely will come again!

Summary: great price, great food, great portion, good seating.

Now this, my friends, is a treat. In comparison to its neighboring udon places, tsurutontan gives a great picturesque udon bowl and affordable sushi on the side. I'd recommend heading in around opening time because like all other great restaurants this place can pack in quite a short amount of time. 

Udon bowl may look intimidating, but the noodles are firm to the bite, the broth is warm and a great compliment, and the rolls are fresh. 

Now, get this, around $20 for all of that! If you have some time, there's also a Uniqlo nearby! 

Cheers

Legit one of my favorite spots to eat in the city. This place is not a cute mom and pop shop where the owner hand makes the noodles and broth and serves only one type of dish on the menu. Just the opposite. Tsurutonton is like this vast, well oiled machine that can seat you pretty quickly and give you a menu that can pretty much satisfy someone who wants to keep it light or go really heavy. You can't really go wrong with the menu.

If you feel like something light and refreshing:
- The cold uni is a perfect summer dish. You get this really nice clean broth and briny uni that you can have alongside chilled udon. This is one of my favorite dishes here.

If you want something heavy:
- The Wagyu Beef Truffle Dashi and the Wagyu Deluxe Sukiyaki are bold and packed with beefy flavor. If you need to fortify your strength for a long day of walking around the city, this will do it. Or put you back into a couch for a long nap.
- If you just want creamy broth, the Truffle Crab Cream, the Uni Creme, and the Mentaiko Cream dishes are what you need to have. It's a lot though, if you plan on drinking all that rich broth. Don't underestimate it!

Donburi:
- A rice dish at an udon place. But... you get udon on the side. The Uni Ikura Crab is a hidden gem on this menu. It's a lot of food but damn, if this isn't one of the best dishes here....

This place has easily become one of my favorite places to eat lunch at in Manhattan. The sushi is always so fresh and delicious, and on top of that, the udon is so hot and savory. The sushi pairs really well with the udon. On top of that, the interior of the establishment is incredibly friendly and casual, and I always get such an amazing vibe and ambiance from here. You also can't beat these prices in Manhattan, the dishes are very affordable.
Came back and got the shrimp tempura udon. Excellent choice!!! I'd definitely say in order of goodness: udon, nigiri, sushi rolls. Yummm it was also nice to sit at the bar and have a casual dinner.

Truly enjoyed this meal  
Lights were dim, service was good, not too many people, was seated immediately, and music was good and not too loud. 

Would def come again!!

We visited for dinner as a party of 3, for restaurant week. I ordered the middle item ($29) with sukiyaki udon.

The udon (small size) broth was warm, hearty, and sweet. I would come back for this on a cold day, although it did feel a bit too sweet towards the end. It did cost $3 extra to "upgrade" my udon to sukiyaki udon.

The sushi was disappointing. Fish wasn't very flavorful, but more so than that the rice felt over-seasoned to the point of overwhelming the already mild fish, and I felt that each sushi had way too much rice compared to the fish.

At the end, I did spend around $40 including tax and tip, and I felt that it was kind of a fair price, but definitely not a bargain considering the quality of food.

First time having uni udon, best udon ever! So creamy and delicious. The sushi was good, but not the best sushi. Definitely go for the udon they serve huge portions I got the combination so it was smaller.

Oh my goodness. I was so excited to go in for a good hot bowl of udon.  I couldn't believe how bad the udon was.  It was as if I took a pack of frozen udon, put it in some hot water and flavoring it was not enough flavor packets.   Truly, it blew my mind.  Secondly, I find the restaurant's pics totally deceptive as the portion that comes in a huge oversized bowl is tiny tiny.  It's almost a joke and I wonder if it's meant to psychologically affect your impression of the portion size.  Since the food was awful, I didn't mind the small portion too much.  Justing adding the details fyi. Lastly, I should stress that the female host who brought us to the table only pretended to check our vaccine status as she didn't bother looking at my phone app after she went through the motions of asking us.  Not good.

Came here on a Thursday night for dinner. Three people, spent over $300. After we paid the check we were immediately asked if we wanted to move to the bar to continue talking and drinking. We were told by the manager, 'Bass' that there was a reservation waiting. Meanwhile there was a table across from us that could fit six people. Extremely disrespectful, rude and only trying to make money. That being said. The food was . The chefs should find somewhere else to work.

I got the Shishito Pepper as an appetizer and got Uni Crème Udon as the entrée. 
Shishito Pepper as an appetizer was a good choice and it was delicious. The Uni Crème Udon was not really what I expected. As you can see from the photo, the ingredients like shiso leaf, tobiko caviar and uni is not enough to represent the dish. The price for this was $24 and the value wasn't there. However, the flavor was good so I gave 3 stars. I fell in love with Tsurutontan in Tokyo, but I'm Afraid that the food quality did not translate the same in NYC.
This place never disappoints. Great food, great value. Both their udon and sushi are great, whichever you end up getting. The service is also very good.

I used to frequent the Midtown location whenever I could get out of the office for lunch, but never got around to writing a review (oops!). Caught up with a few girlfriends at the Union Sq location recently, and I have to say, the OG branch is much nicer.

Pros: 

- Affordable sushi & udon combos, especially during Restaurant Week, that will net you 8 pieces of ngiri + 3 pieces of sashimi + one 6-piece roll + a bowl of udon soup for $28. 

- Lovely, modern decor with ample, spacious seating


Cons:

- Service with an attitude. The bartender couldn't have been any more stuck-up when we asked him where the host was--since there was no one manning the stand. The host himself was also rude and stuck-up.

- Flavorless salmon sashimi/ngiri that made me wonder how long it had been chilling on ice or soaking in water to be THAT bland.


All in all, an okay spot if you're in the area, craving soup and on a budget. I don't know if I'll ever make it back to either Manhattan location again, but I'm not too sad about it.

Stopped in with a friend for Restaurant Week 2022, so we ordered off of a pre-fix menu that isn't available the entire time. Here the RW menu included different levels of a sushi omakase platters and a small udon bowl that you could pick. 

On top of the pre-fix menu, we also ordered a shrimp and vegetable tempura app. Everything was fried to perfection. I loved all of the fun veggies that I've never had tempered before. Very traditional, it came with a sauce but it also came with fresh grated radish.

The sushi was so incredible! Very fresh, amazing fish. We went with the middle tier, so lots of tuna, some salmon, other white fish and some fun extras like salmon eggs and eel. It also came with a tuna roll. 

For the udon, I went with the US Wagyu option. Sliced wagyu pieces and truffle oil. It was delicious! With all the sushi the small bowl was a perfect addition to the meal. My friend got the Katsu curry, she loved it, thought it wasn't too spicy and ate the entire thing. 

If your looking for a drink to have the lychee martinis ($9 all night!) we're very tasty, just a bit sweet. They are made to order so we asked for a little less pulp, if your not a pulp fan in drinks I would keep this in mind. 

Can't wait to come back and try more from the menu!

I checked out this spot as I was craving hot udon noodles to combat the cold and snow in NYC this weekend. I tried the deluxe restaurant week omakase with beef udon noodles and it was amazing. The sushi tasted incredibly fresh and the udon noodles were rich and savory, not watery like I've had at other places. The price point is hard to beat - $29 only due to restaurant week, check them and other participating restaurants this NYC Restaurant Week!

Super consistent food all the time and if you're craving some udon noodles this is a great restaurant. The happy hour prices aren't THAT much of a difference and we got seated pretty much instantly on a Sunday afternoon.

My go to order is the katsu curry udon. The portions are kind of big so usually I can't finish it all. But overall great food!!!!

My partner and I were in the vicinity recently and stopped here with my partner during restaurant week. 

It's a younger vibe here with music to match.  It was around 2pm on the weekend and the lunch crowd was thinning, so we were able to get a booth seat.  We started off with some water and a bottle of dassai 45, which was huge, around 750 ml, and took a while to finish off. 

We each ordered the restaurant week omakase set, mine was the premium and she had the deluxe because she's not a big fan of uni.  The premium also came with whole scallop sushi that was able to be split.  Both sets also came with a tuna roll and a bowl of udon, on which we added sliced wagyu ($5 extra). 

The cuts of fish were well portioned and each type was fresh and savory.  Our favorites were the bluefin toro, which was delicate like butter, and the salmon, which had sufficient fat and texture.  Also, there was also plenty of wasabi and ginger! 

Overall, the quality of the food is above par.  We peeked at the regular menu and the prices are respectable.  Additionally, the selection of wines, sakes and beers is not extensive, but good enough and makes your decision less complicated.  We definitely would return!

I have a love/ hate relationship with Tsurutontan. I love their bowls of udon noodle and a lot of their apps but I hate the wait at times. I've been back twice since the pandemic and it wasn't too bad of a wait both times. I go to is always the Tsurutontan Deluxe because it has all the proteins - best bang for your buck in my opinion.
Ordered food from them for me and my family they messed up the order and gave the incorrect amount called three time just to be put in hold or hanged up didn't even bother helping and vas very rude

Very well priced. We went here for New york restaurant week and they had 3 omakase options - Standard $29, Deluxe $34, Premium $39. I got the premium one which came with udon of choice which for me was Katsu Curry. I enjoy them both separately but together it felt like a lot of food. I meant I can't complain. The bill was so reasonable for this quality of food. The service was quick too.

It was pretty average udon for me. I went in for restaurant week and got a nigiri combo and the price was pretty good for the food, but i wouldnt go again unless a friend asked to come along. 

Had higher expectations with the yelp reviews i saw, but i think raku's is better. 

The building is really clean and nice though. Didnt have to wait although it did start filling up after we got in.
This restaurant perhaps worth 1.5 stars. Its noodle taste sort of weird; maybe still Asian but not very Japanese. Perhaps the only thing positive is that they added some Japanese pepper.

My friend and I came here for Feb 2022 NY Restaurant Week. We got the Deluxe Restaurant Week Omakase, which included 9 sushi and small soy dashi udon. It was really filling, but I didn't think that the sushi tasted that fresh. But you get what you pay for. 

Service was great, but also if you are a small party (mine was a party of 2), you might get seated in the middle where you will not be facing each other, but be facing a glass/plastic divider where you'll be able to see the people across from you. Not sure how we felt about that. But overall ok experience.

Great spot in the city! I made a reservation for a Saturday night and got seated right away. I ordered the grilled mushrooms and the vegetable tempura udon. Both were delicious. I'll definitely come back here to try more dishes!

seared Salmon Sashimi Creamy Spicy Shrimp Tempura bıth of them tastefully , Shishito Pepper was soury and delicious, best udon is Sukiyaki Beef Udon,Udon Pon Dumpling likes a shangai style fried dumpling,Wagyu Sushi is the best sushi...
I waited a to go order for 40 minutes. Can you believe they took 40 minutes just to make some sushi? Ridiculous.

Prices fair for the area. Food and service were sub-par and fell under expectations. I've ordered delivery before and don't remember it being that bad. Weren't greeted very warmly, felt like the servers were trying to get us in and out as fast as possible, which I don't usually get even in fuller restaurants. It was pretty empty as it was between lunch and dinner. 

@ Spicy tantan udon (part of omakase set)- pretty disgusting. Expected udon to be okay, but noodles were overcooked to near mush (similar to previous delivery order although I thought it was the delivery time ruining the udon). Noodles (not the soul surprisingly) had an odd bitter flavor as primary. Spicy, but not too appetizing. Okay if you haven't had udon before I guess.

@ Omakase dinner set (basic) - came with eight pieces nigiri, one tuna roll, and small size udon. Overall quality is average, doesn't live up to omakase expectation. The seaweed was soggy and chewy, weird it wasn't roasted. The sushi pieces were messy as shown. Worse yet, I found multiple scales in the pieces, something I really can't stand. It shows how speed and mass production is grossly prioritized over the food quality and presentation. 

@ Grilled mushrooms - very yummy. Wonderful grilled flavor with truffle oil and crispy batter pieces. Nice chunks of mushroom in a flavorful appetizer. 

Someone messed up on both the udon and the sushi we got or I'd have to conclude that the food quality is just as we experienced, under average relative to the prices and quality in the area. 

tl;dr grilled mushrooms had good truffle and grill favor, try your luck at the udon and sushi but be wary of being disappointed. Quick service with hawk eyes, huge seating areas.

I went on a Friday night with a group of my friends and it was a great experience. The ambiance was amazing, with the dim lighting and upbeat music. I got the 3 roll combo which comes with 3 rolls and a mini udon and it's only $28. The sushi was good and I recommend the mini beef udon. Honestly I've had better sushi but the vibe of the place and the combination of the udon+sushi makes it unique.

While I am not an udon person, the aesthetic beauty of the restaurant makes it a choice destination for a meal around the Union Square area. Ever since Republic closed its doors back in the day, USQ feels a bit empty in its diversity of restaurants until Tsurutontan came along. Slightly hidden away from Union Square Plaza, it fills the void left by Republic with an robust menu that's very reminiscent of the Sapporo East and other Izakaya spots no longer around these days. My go to is the Tsurutontan Deluxe, end of story. Wouldn't say any one item stands out, but the staff is really great, while cleanliness and convenience can't be under estimated.
Crab truffle udon- sauce is not too thick so I liked it the most. Wagyu beef udon- average. Shrimp tempura udon- just the basic but mainly fried veggies and 2 shrimps

I love Tsurotontan, specifically the union Sq location, and I'd been wanting to try this location since I work closer to this one, but my takeout experience was absolutely hellish. I ordered at 11:45, for a 1:15 pickup. So they had all this time to prepare, and I got there at 12:50pm  but the host said 10-15 minute. Sure, I'm early for my scheduled pickup time, so I understand. 

But it isn't until 1:50pm I finally get my food. Someone else before me had also been waiting for nearly an hour too, and multiple delivery workers were congregated in the tiny waiting corner. I was supposed to be getting back to work, and there was total disregard of people's time. I ended up an hour late back to my office, I probably would've finished sooner if I sat there and ate (I watched as people who came in after me were sat and started eating ages before I got my own food). 

The host was no help at all, not apologetic nor gave any explanation or time updates. If I knew it was going to take an hour, I would've gone back to work and come back. I was infuriated, but when someone else had complained, all they said was that it wasn't their fault, it was the "people in the back". I didn't want to take it out on anyone who wasn't to blame, but as I finally walked out, I just wanted to cry at how awful their treatment felt. Never going to this location again.

Also, the food wasn't even that good. The udon was okay, simple but tasty, but the sushi was bland, rice wasn't seasoned enough, and they included fillers like cucumber in their spicy scallop roll, which was not stipulated on the menu, which made it just take like cucumber. If they wanted to be stingy, they could've just turned it into a makizushi roll (nori outside), at least it would've still tasted good. Sticking to Yama Ramen next door for my Japanese cravings.

I have mixed feelings about this place. Maybe my hopes were too high from the rave reviews? 

This place was on my list and I've heard great things. I will say, it's a great deal for the sushi set combos. The combos come with a small udon, a roll, and sushi. Everything can also be upgraded. I opted for the deluxe sushi, the shrimp and crab roll, and uni udon. 

I felt the sushi was subpar and could have been a little more fresh. I was super excited for the uni udon. However, it was difficult to get through. I knew it was a cream udon, but it ended up being overwhelmingly creamy and salty. It felt wasteful given it was an upgraded item. 

When it came time to pay, we noticed an extra charge for one of the combos. When we brought it to our waitress' attention, she didn't really give us a reason why which we thought was kind of strange. 

Overall, the food is decent. If you're looking for a good value meal, this could be an option.

Honestly, the udon was a let-down. I got the truffle snow crab udon, and while it was tasty, the actual udon noodles were disappointing. They felt like they were overcooked. They were really soft and didn't have that chewiness and bounce that made great udon noodles great. If you can't get the udon noodles right at an udon house, something is wrong. 

I also ordered a tuna roll, which was surprisingly delicious. The fish tasted really fresh. I enjoyed the roll more than the udon. 

Overall, I would give 3.5 stars if I could.
Delicious, flavorful, you're in for a slurpy time. It might've been the second time I got Dan Dan noodles that week but I made it and it was delicious and worth it.

Better than the location in Midtown. Like it better than Raku so I'm an outlier.

I was debating to give it a 4 stars cause the host tried to seat us at the bar saying it's a half hour wait but then sat us in 10. (But I forgave due to the food and service.)

They've cut down on their menu since I first tried their food 3 years ago. My go-to's are Spicy TanTan udon and salmon carpaccio. Instead of the carpaccio, they have the seared salmon which tasted delicious too. They don't let you choose noodle type and bowl size anymore but it doesn't matter to me since I always go with the default options.

Not something to eat everyday but great once in awhile.
Love the atmosphere and decor. Very trendy and upbeat. The food was very good and for the most part seemed reasonably priced. I will say the $8 cucumber salad was a bit small though.

We came in for dinner and ordered a variety of food, the beef udon, sashimi, sushi rolls and wagyu donburi. Based on the mostly wonderful reviews my expectations were perhaps too high and I found the food to be good but not that great. The sashimi and sushi were very fresh. The flavor in the cooked food was just not that great in my opinion. My friend is a regular here and loves it and she told me that the food was as great as usual so perhaps they had a bad night. We loved our lychee martinis. I'll need to try this place again and see if I'm blown away by the food and this was indeed an off night.

My husband and I were visiting NY and dropped into this location. We didn't have reservations but were able to sit at the bar. The food was outstanding. I ordered the salmon lovers meal and the salmon was mouth watering. The noodle I got, I added the curry to and they were amazing. Cant wait to find another or go back. YUMMY
They had very good curry--highly recommend it. Sushi was mediocre and not worth the price tag in my opinion. The place is a good environment to dine out with friends
I waited two hours for delivery then they canceled my order. I don't trust this business.

I went to the location in Hawaii before and really enjoyed the food there so I was super excited to find out there's one in NYC! The interior is pretty spacious despite how it looks outside and it's super nice. They have happy hour prices all day on weekdays and they also have some really good lunch sets! I ordered a 2 sushi roll combo that comes with a regular sized udon (btw their udon bowls are HUGE). You can choose from a list of sushi rolls and also choose from 3 different udon. I tried the salmon avocado, yellowtail scallion, and sukiyaki udon. The food is super yummy and the portion is pretty big for one person. Definitely want to come back again to try different combos and some appetizers
Great service and great food! We loved the ambiance. Extremely clean for the city. Reasonable prices as well.
one of the best udon i've ever had. HUGE bowl. cheap prices and great happy hour offers... must have experience

I remember when Tsurotontan had just opened in their Union Square location and how good it was, but unfortunately it has gone downhill since then.  First, the prices went up.  With inflation and all this is warranted but it went up in addition to the portions getting significantly smaller.  The prices will go up, I totally get that, but don't get the need to give a deceivingly large bowl with quite a small portion, that's not fooling anyone.  There was also a lot less meat in the ramen as well.  As an appetizer (which we got after eating the ramen which wasn't filling), my friend and I got the chicken karaage.  Chicken karaage is quite hard to mess up on yet it was soggy here...how can you give soggy fried chicken...what...I get that it's deep fried in oil and all but it should still be crispy.  The only reason I didn't give one star is that our server was quite hospitable.

I hate giving bad reviews but serving your customer rotten brown avocado tuna roll is unacceptable. I paid over $40 for my meal and was expecting it to be at least edible. See the pictures of the tuna avocado. Very disappointed.

Visited for lunch which ends at 4! We ordered from their lunch menu, which is super affordable. Everything was under $30 for a noodle dish and a sushi dish! 

I had the beef udon with 3 sushi roll combos. My friend had the beef udon curry version and some pink rolls. Both were delicious! The regular beef udon soup was so addicting!! The three sushi rolls I got were delicious! It was also very filling. 

The ambiance was nice and the staff were kind. All I have are positive words!! Will definitely be visiting again!

Came on a Monday and super excited that they have all day happy hour for Monday - Wednesday!! They also got the large upgrade back again (they had it prior to covid but took it away). 

Ambiance - 5/5 
The area was so clean and spacious. I loved that they offered tables that were further away from other customers so that each table had their own privacy. 

Service - 5/5 
Our server assisted us with whatever we needed and always with a smile on his face. Always happy to help and answering all our questions!

Food - 3/5 
Honestly felt that the food slacked and smaller than usual. Their wasn't a lot of flavor in the Spicy Tan Tan, but we also ordered the curry katsu which was pretty yummy!

Was told that this udon place is a must try. They do have a wide selection of udon, but my friend had difficulty finding an option that didn't have beef or pork. So this place is not super suitable for people who have that dietary restriction.

My friend and I wanted to split the Truffle Creme with Crab and Mushroom, but each person needs to order a dish in order to dine in. This was the case even though we went in at 3:30pm on a Sunday, and the restaurant was not packed at all.

Therefore, we ordered the Soy Garlic Fried Chicken as well. This appetizer tasted mediocre. Not the best chicken I've had, but also not terrible.

The udon smelled EXTREMELY truffely, but thankfully did not taste like how it smelled. I would have preferred if the udon was a bit more on the firm side. They also didn't put a ton of crab in it, which I guess is expected. The broth was on the sweet side and was creamy. Not a type of broth I would want to just drink down by itself.

Overall, I had a very mediocre experience here. I would come to this place again if it was my only option, but I think there are many other restaurants to check out in new york.

The restaurant itself has a very nice setting - very cool, calm, and relaxed setting inside. The food is great! I came here for dinner with my family, and we had 4 different types of the udon - the wagyu, the crab, the tantan, and the uni cream. The tantan we got with the omakase sushi set. The udon bowls are huge! 

The crab udon was my favorite - it's creamy but not too strong. It has a rich flavor and it really complements the udon. If I went again, I would get the crab one again.

The tantan was not exactly would I thought it would be like. It's not so much spicy as oily - the red seems to be from a spicy oil, but it's really not that spicy. There was also minimal pork inside so was a little sad about that.

The wagyu was ok - it's what you would expect from a beef soup with noodles. It was perhaps the most traditional tasting udon dish. 

The uni cream was what I was eyeing, but it was a little too creamy and sweet for me. There were some pieces of uni included that were soft and tasty - but I think with the cream I was not able to appreciate the cream as well. 

The sushi tastes very fresh! I normally don't like tuna sushi that much, but theirs was very fresh and did not have any fishy taste.

I ordered delivery, and they delivered to us sushi with dirt and rocks. It clearly had been dropped in the kitchen/on the restaurant side because our delivery was completely sealed when delivered. What kind of judgement was exercised here?

Read Pamela L's review on this place and couldn't wait to get here.  Came here 6pm on a Monday, first meal in New York City, after landing at JFK airport 2.5 hours earlier.  Place was empty.

They have happy hour prices all day Monday thru Wednesday, and 12pm-5pm Thursday and Friday.  

The $5 edamame was served cold, with minimal oil.  I prefer an oilier version heated.

The $9 steamed shrimp dumplings came with 5 dumplings, over a small pool of mildly spicy chili sauce to give it some added kick.   Regular price $11.

Wife loved her $30 Tricolor set of tuna, salmon and Hamachi nigri.  the seafood was very fresh, and even the rice was warm in the spicy tuna rolls.  Regular price $38.

The $13 beef udon came in a huge bowl, large enough to wash your hair.  Unfortunately, it was only half full, mainly beef broth, with rather soft udon noodles, and beef resembling Yoshinoya's famous beef, sliced razor thin to make it appear large in quantity.   Delicious, not too salty, but nothing outstanding.  Would have preferred more meat and noodles.  Regular price $17.

Whatever you do, make sure you use the restaurant bathrooms before making the half mile walk back to the timeshare condominium, as the hot broth goes lightning quick through the system!

And no hairs in the huge bowl.

This used to be my fav restaurant but last time I saw a tiny mouse running around in it, the waitress saw it but didn't say/do anything about it. Not sure if it's common for nyc restaurants, just giving u guys a heads up.

They have a ton of reservations open but can only be seated with everyone there. Ordered the Wagyu udon with the truffle broth and it was so delicious. Love anything with truffle it was so flavorful. Also ordered the tri color set which is such a great deal and upgraded to the katsu curry udon. I thought the curry udon would be north bright but it was quite thick and more curry than broth. The katsu was perfectly cooked and so good with the curry
Beautiful space with decent udon. The presentation is grand, udon is served in a giant bowl. The overall taste was good but had better.

I've been here a few times and this time around went with the soondubu spicy Udon which I hadn't seen on the menu before. It was fantastic. I love the tangy spicy flavor of a good bowl of soondubu and I've never had it with udon noodles before. 

These are some of the better udon noodles you can get in NYC, on par with Raku and hanon. They are chewy and a great compliment to a complex broth. The soft pieces of tofu and abundant varietal mushrooms added lots of textural interest. I was very impressed with the quantity of mushrooms in the soup. 

Obviously the portions are quite large. Certainly worth the price if you can finish it all.

The meat is a little tough and grisly. Definitely not my favorite part of the bowl.
Terrific lunch specials.   Tasty chicken udon and fresh sushi.  Hip looking space. Reasonable prices!

Honestly these udon bowls are HUGEE but you know what they say, the more the better. Me and my friend came on a cold NY winter which was perfect for a nice warm bowl of udon. This is hands down one of my favorite places to eat udon of all time! The vibes are nice and chill but the food is also delicious. We ordered the curry udon and the wagyu sondubu udon which both were really filling and the broth was amazinggg!

REALLY liked this place -- was surprised at the quality of the sushi/sashimi given I thought it was just an udon spot. I got the truffle roll, toro sashimi, and the sukiyaki udon. Presentation was excellent -- they put the sashimi over ice in a nice wooden box and the udon in a huge bowl. I very much enjoyed the truffle roll and sashimi, but my boyfriend thought the truffle overwhelmed the roll so heads up if you're not a truffle fan. The udon was interesting -- the waiter gave us a heads up that it'd be sweet, and it was definitely good but I don't think I'd order that particular one again. Boyfriend thought it was way too sweet. Service was good (a tad slow given it was only about half full) and the waiter had very good knowledge the menu. Definitely will be coming back and hoping to bring my parents here!
I was so thrilled to find a place that specializes in udon and It didn't disappoint. Ordered the cucumber appetiser and curry udon. Simply satisfying! I'll be back!

Yato is extremely disappointed in this place. 
Yato came in on a whim because Yato thought, "hey, let's try a new place." 

McDonald's is around the corner, you're better off there. 

Walking in, there is a young lady who guide Yato and his 3 guest to the bar when there were many tables around. Heck, even single people were settled at tables but Yato and his party were brought to the bar? When Yato asked for a table, the young lady whispered that Yato was an "asshole." 

What a joke the hostess is. 

But the food was just okay. The sushi was pretty good but the udon and the broth lacking in taste or flavor. Not good at all. 

The sodas were warm and small but expensive! Refills? Sorry, no free refills, even if you're only given a half can of soda in the first place. Sodas are left at the bar opened and uncared for. Yato sadly observed this as he left the place since a fly buzzed above the sodas. Disgusting. 

So would Yato recommend this place? No, no way. Don't go here. The food was blah, but the service? Horrible.

Yato has never said this before but the hostess needs to be fired. Never has Yato ever had such a horrible hostess before.

Absolutely delicious, huge bowls of udon. Everything was so tasty, warm, and flavorful. The prices were very reasonable for lunch and had many combination options available. 

We also got their strawberry gimlet - which was very sweet and light, and not too strong. A good balanced drink (leaning on the non alcoholic side)

Been craving udon and a group of friends and I all went out here to try the place out. (A group of 6.) 
Almost regretted our pick at the door since we were greeted by such an attitude packing hostess. 
She has such a nasty personality on her. I'm sorry you're at work? My party and I had been polite from beginning to end and she was rude the whole time. 
Judging by the reviews here, a lot of guest have had problems with this hostess for a long time! How does she have a job here? 

Overall the food was also lackluster. No flavor. My group and I all had different items and sampled one another's dishes and everyone agreed that the food wasn't good. So disappointing because the display was great. 

Overall, I would have tried this place again if not for that nasty hostess. I don't know if this restaurant reads reviews but they should; many guest have had issues with this hostess and it's the reason I refuse to give this place a second try.
A must! The serving sizes r very generous and down to the broth, it is well worth. A few cocktails to go with it and you're good for a cute dinner.

Came here yesterday for a meal as I was craving for some curry udon katsu.

It's always busy here as people just love their udon. I always told myself that I wanted to try their sizzling sukiyaki udon but I always go to udon soups. It's just that good! I sat at the bar counter and read my book while I waited for my meal. I did noticed it took abit longer in between courses (from appetizer to entree) but chalked it up to the busyness. 

Ordered:
Katsu Curry udon + mini Sukiyaki Don
Spicy corn tempera for appetizer

My only negative feedback: I wish the poached egg was warmer. It is always served chilled.

Just yum. No regrets. I want to come back already as food is always amazing. Thank you for the meal and service.

The food is excellent. Server is very friendly. Host today she was so friendly and accommodating to what we want 
She even gave us the bigger seat knowing that we didn't have reservations 
Overall very friendly and great experience. Definitely will go again
Delicious soup. Appetizers are great. The noodles are springy and chewy enough with enough types of broths that you wouldnt find elsewhere.
Delicious dinner! It was pricey, but it's Manhattan, and it's high quality fish. I really liked the udon soup that came on the side. I couldn't finish, so I wrapped it for later. Better deal!

If you like sushi and ramen, lunch at this restaurant is both fantastic and inexpensive. Treat yourself to two or three rolls and a bowl of ramen for less than $25 in a beautiful restaurant with lovely service. I particularly like the eel and avocado roll, and the katsu curry ramen bowl. Lunch is served until 4:00. I heartily recommend it.

This place is amaaaazing! My bf got the 3 sushi roll combo and I got 2 sushi roll combo. So worth it! Sushi was so good especially the Toro Roll. Udon comes in a huge bowl and it was really good too. Highly recommend!
My friend introduced me and I immediately fell in love with the massive pots. Presentation is a A HUGE bonus here. The broth is also flavorful. Make sure to try the tan tan noodles!

HORRIBLE SERVICE. I was catching up with a friend so we decided to come here. The waitress forgot about our table and I had to find someone to help. The waitress then took our order and was very rude. I was asking about ingredients due to dietary restrictions but she was annoyed and had an attitude. She also left in the middle of me asking my question. I asked 4 times for extra silverware and soy sauce but she kept ignoring and finally I asked someone else twice and got it. I was surprised that they have no vegetarian options. I had to ask for something custom and luckily I was able to get that. Very bad service. Do not recommend.

80% of my diet consists of udon noodles, so it's safe to say I love udon and eat it regularly but for some reason this place just didn't hit the spot. To be fair, I ordered delivery so it may not have been as good as it would've if I dined in. I ordered the tsurutontan deluxe, which I did heat up the stove, along with two rolls: cucumber avocado and spider roll. I thought everything tasted quite bland. The broth of the udon wasn't very rich, and the toppings weren't flavorful. The rolls also weren't my favorite. The cucumber skin wasn't cut off and was quite hard. Spider roll was ok. Overall a very subpar meal.

Delicious udon, sizeable portions. I had the value omakase and upgraded the udon to wagyu. The udon noodles had that delightful bounce and bite of a quality udon. The broth was light and flavorful with a delectable umaminess.  The sushi was fresh. My husband had the cold uni udon. Unique way to eat udon that we hadn't tried before. You gotta love uni to enjoy this dish - thorough uni flavor throughout. My husband enjoyed it and I did too with the couple bites I tried of his meal but I feel like it may be borderlining on too rich of a dish overall just cause it was such a huge bowl with such a powerful uni sauce. 

FYI - No happy hour on holidays including holidays observed (we went on 6/20 - Juneteenth observed). Neither the hostess nor our waiter informed us of this but luckily we overheard the waiter tell a table near us so we weren't surprised when the bill came.

The ambiance of the overall restaurant was cool, but I didn't particularly enjoy the area where we were seated. They had a ton of space and open tables yet we were packed in this little area of 2-top tables that were squeezed in so tightly that you literally grazed your butt on the table next to yours to squeeze through to get to the inside seat (the seats with the backs to the wall). I know restaurants are backing off their COVID protocols now but this scenario was just a bit strange since the other areas of the restaurant still had the COVID plastic table shields up to separate the parties, yet here we are in this particular section grazing our butts on the adjacent tables.

Ordered the deluxe wagyu udon and it was really good! Waitress was a bit overeager and asked if we were ready to order very quickly after we sat down but otherwise very attentive. My egg in the udon was very very underdone (I dare say almost raw) but due to the setting of udon it worked out.

AWESOME portion sizes, very solid lunch/Happy Hour deals, and delicious food. I have thoroughly enjoyed both of my visits here, and would be happy to return. Be warned! The udon bowls are VERY large -- almost comically so -- so consider sharing or ordering less!

Everything I've had here tasted great. I had a salmon donburi bowl, which was lovely. The standouts in my opinion are the bowls of hot soup (cold noodles are good too but I prefer hot!). The menu is expansive with tons of options. I would bet that each and every one is delicious. They have awesome weekday deals so I recommend checking those out! The main thing I would say is that the portions of soup are HUGE. The photos on the menu do not do them justice. Be prepared! Enjoy!!

Dang their udon bowls are HUGE.

My friend and I split the torched salmon as an appetizer, which was good but otherwise pretty standard.

I got the curry deluxe and it was fantastic. Rich curry broth that was not overly salty, crisp tempura, and plenty of noodles. Simple dish, but definitely hit the spot!

If you're craving udon and sushi, this is the perfect place for you! They have a lunch and dinner menu where you get both for such a great price. The original sets only come with two types of noodles, but for a few dollars more you get to change the noodles. The noodles and sushi here never disappoints. You can always make a reservation ahead of time. On weekends, they serve dinner special all day (no lunch special menu options).
Came in off the street for some drinks and sushi with a friend, Natalie the bartender was swamped but was still personable and attentive, and made for a fun night

I have had a few meals here the past few months and it is still a solid place to have Udon.
