The menu seems to have shifted to highlight both udon and sushi which likely caters more towards the general audience.  The udon still remains the star as well as the many broths.  We have had the simple dashi which is good until the last drop, the sukiyaki is wonderful and deep in flavor and the curry has just the right spice.  Recently we had the salmon and ikura donburi bowl, another star.

I wish this restaurant focused just on udon, but even with the expanded menu, it has stayed true to its roots!

This udon place has such a variety of udon noodles, you HAVE to check it out. My boyfriend got the truffle one and he loved it. I got the uni one and it was so creamy and delicious and actually had a decent amount of uni on it. The service was quick and we got our noodles fast. Definitely recommend checking this place out if you're craving some udon noodles!

Biggest bowl of udon I've ever seen - it's also free to upgrade to a large portion of noodles. Love the variety of broths but also some of the non-soup options like the sukiyaki. Have gotten take out too and they have some pretty good deals (1 for 1) and some good set meals with sushi.

If you don't know what you're ordering, avoid this place. They'll serve you with cheaper fish. I wish I could give them No Star. They served us with a lot cheaper fish than it says on the menu. We asked to explain why the fish is different. The manager came and told us that's the correct one, hamachi. No it was. Then, the sushi chef came out and said he made with cheaper fish because they had a lot of them. What?? That's not what I pay for. The sushi chef then gave us the correct sushi hamachi saying here is Hamachi on the menu so everything is okay since you guys now have the right sushi on the menu. No apology but just gave us what we WERE SUPPOSED to have at first. What a scam? And udon was terrible. I paid extra for special Udon but if was just power chicken soup flavor Udon nothing special. Avoid this restaurant if you can't tell what fish is what because they'll serve you with similar color cheaper fish sushi. Photos are what they fooled us. Made with kind of Bass then said it's Hamachi. Admitted they purposefully made it with Bass because they had extra bass without letting us know. If you've rated high at this place, it's either you ordered Salmon/ Tuna (anyone knows what they look/taste like) or you can't tell the differences among white fish. Staff are rude and disrespectful. Worst service ever despite the fact that here is not $ restaurant. My party ordered 3 main dishes. All of them were far below average.

Came here on a Saturday, just at opening hours for lunch with my gf. Having been to their Midtown location, I had a general expectation and what I wanted to order again, which was their US Wagyu Udon Noodle dish with that delicious truffle oil.

We decided to order the 3 Roll Combo Lunch Set ($24) to split between the two of us. We selected the Eel Cucumber Roll, Shrimp Tempura Roll, and Sea & Truffle (+$5). We also upgraded to include an udon dish for an extra $5. We got the US Wagyu Udon, which was what I was looking forward to. The sushi rolls were good, especially the Sea & Truffle because truffle oil. Notice the pattern here? I don't need to comment on the US Wagyu Udon dish because you already know my take on this.

I also ordered the Mango Chili Margarita. A blend of that tequila, lime, along with mango flavor with a salted rim as well as some sort of chili powder to spice it up. Really makes you feel like you're on a beach in Mexico.

The service is one thing I had a complaint about. At the beginning of our experience, we had one server who took our order. As the day went on and the restaurant got busier, it seems like our original server got reassigned? So that left this one other server to take care of an entire section of about 20 tables? The point was, it took forever to get my check and pay the bill. I'd say a good 15-20 minutes, which is unheard of. Management needs to be better with this.

So good!  Came in for lunch and did the combo 2 rolls with Udon.  Plenty of food for $22, really good deal.  Everything was fresh and delicious.  The ambiance was chic/modern, the service was good, not amazing.  Give it a try!!!

We were walking around the city and decided to try here for a late lunch. We were seated quickly at the bar but service was a little slow. I got the mini spicy don and my husband got the lunch special. It was good but it wasn't anything special.  My husbands gluten free and there was any other type of noodle available for him. My lunch was $15 so for the price it was worth it.  I don't know that I would say the same for my husbands special which seemed small for the price.

I thought the sushi menu was limited and bland. Of their two more interesting rolls, "sea & truffle" and "salmon and snow crab" I really only found the "sea and truffle to truly be unique. I'd go back but it's not as good as I expected hence the 3 stars.

Surprisingly excellent udon and sushi spot in the heart of Union Square. The restaurant is actually pretty big and spacious, and basically spotless. They have a bunch of different dinner sets for if you want sushi, udon, or a bit of both. I got the salmon lover set which came with nigiri, a spicy salmon roll, sashimi, and a bowl of dashi udon. The quality of the salmon was noticeably amazing and buttery, and the dashi udon broth was delicious. The sets are also very affordable for Manhattan and offer a lot of variety. I would highly recommend this place and will definitely return!

Food 6.5/10
Decent udon for a decent price, gets the job done but nothing too grand or amazing. A little salty for my taste, but the bowls are HUGE so that's a bit gimmicky and what they're known for. I always get the thinly sliced beef udon. The broth itself doesn't have too many layers, but there's a lot of meat in each bowl they provide, and the udon is bouncy. 

Atmosphere 6/10
Kind of dim and low ceilings, pretty big on the inside though and location is not bad. 

Service 7/10
I remember nothing but no bad memories so it must've been decent.

Really enjoyed my first meal at Tsurutontan! My 3 sushi roll combo was extremely fresh and tasty and a pretty reasonable price. When we were ordering the waiters mentioned that due to the popularity of their restaurant week menu the sushi might take longer to come out, but I am glad I took the chance because my sushi actually ending up arriving before my friend's udon which was somewhat odd. Another thing to note was there was some small gnats or flies buzzing around by where we were eating so hopefully that was a one time thing. However I would definitely come back especially if I am in the mood for noodles since that's what they're known for!
I was ecstatic to discover a resto that serves authentic udon, and it didn't disappoint! Even without prior reservations, our gregarious server furnished us a bigger seat to boot.

Was in the mood for some udon and rolls so headed out to this restaurant. Looks small from the outside but a lot bigger inside. Enjoyed my dinner combo. Rolls were freshly made and filling. Downside was I had to wait about 30 minutes for a table for four.

Been going here ever since moving to East Village, but tried out their restaurant week promotion this time!

Basic omakase set $30 + $5 US wagyu promotion add-on:
The sushi sets always comes with an udon side (Soy dashi or beef), but they seemed to downgrade it to soy dashi or cold udon. Maybe for restaurant week or forever. Kinda sad about it, but very glad it forced me to try something new--the US Wagyu!!!! Would very much recommend paying the extra $5 for one of the best udon broths I've had in NYC. Sushi, on the other hand, was subpar. Refer to photo for the selection, but overall would say that it was nothing special. If you're on the lookout for great sushi, go to an actual omakase place.

Premium omakase set $35 with soy dashi udon:
It's good. Slight upgrades from the basic e.g. real caviar, scallop, slightly fancier tuna seaweed roll. Again, udon was the highlight of an omakase set so I'd just say stick to the noodles here.

For folks easing into omakase/sushi, this is a great place to go for a value meal and introduction. For omakase fiends, would pass and stick with the giant bowls of udon. 

As always, Tsurutontan is a beautiful venue. Love the decorations, and workers are very attentive and nice. Sometimes they will rush you though. Oh also, apparently if you don't finish your wine, you can take the bottle home, which is unlike most places!

Taste: 4/5
Ambience: 5/5
Value: 4/5

For extra udon lovers: they basically always have BOGO on delivery apps! Secure for two bowls of udon delivered

This is a quiet restaurant nestled near Union Square. We had two different type of udons and their schtick is that they have these oversized presentation bowls, but the amount of food is a normal portion. 

Taste wise, everything was executed nicely. Good amount of heat on the spicy udon and curry flavor was on point for the other udon.

Delicious! Fantastic food, service is ok, I don't understand why they refuse walk-ins when the place is half empty, but I guess it guarantees reservations are kept. In all honesty, I have eaten my whole meal while those empty tables remain empty, they should review their policy, but you can't go wrong with the food!

I used to come here before the pandemic but my recent visit made me feel that the restaurant doesn't care about the quality of food they serve. The appetizers were good but the udon that we ordered are all either over cooked or according to the waitress " another supplier ", I think they used to have the ingredients shipped from Japan and now they get it from other places. Honestly the udon noodles is worse than supermarket quality....

Tsurutontan has a plethora of udon options to fulfill your udon cravings. 

What first caught my eye was the huge bowls served at each table as we were led to our seats. 

I got myself the mentai kamatama udon - a cold udon topped with creamy mentaiko cod roe, a slow cooked egg and tempura flakes. It was a great summer dish that was refreshing, and something unique I would not normally find. Usually when I think of udon, I think hot with soup - but this was a welcome take on the hot summer day I walked in. The bowl for a sole udon was huge - but portion size it was less than what I expected from such a huge bowl - it was perfect for me as I came in a little less hungry and since we ordered a sushi roll on the side. Our shrimp tempura and crab roll was good and plated well - but not one I would likely be craving again.

For $28, I was able to get three rolls of sushi and a side of udon. It was honestly a great deal and by the end of it I was really full. Definitely not the best sushi I have had but the udon was good, and the service could have been better. The original waiter spilled one of the water glasses while setting our table and took the glass and the menus, cleaned it up but never replaced the menus or water and it was annoying to ask multiple times.

This review is mainly for the service and not the food. I used to come here when I was without kid and it was good. However, today I came in with two kids, my sister in law and my brother, and our waitress was so rude. Firstly, she put us in the back next to the restroom which is fine, but we were practically forgotten or dismissed. Every meal we tried to order she couldn't accommodate for us. I got the omakase premium sushi set and it comes with noodles. For one of the noodles We asked if she does not put curry or spicy oil in it so we can give it to the kids and she refused and said it's not possible. My sister in law was like just don't put the chili oil, and she just kept saying no. We tried to explain to her that the noodles were for the kids and they don't eat curry or spicy because they're 3. She then replies that the restaurant doesn't have a kids menu, basically telling us the restaurant doesn't accommodate to kids. Wtf. So rude. Then I asked her if I can just purchase a separate small bowl of soy dashi udon for the kids and she said no they can't and that I have to buy one of the udon soups on the menu which doesn't have plain soy dashi udon on it. So basically for me to get the soy dashi noodle i have to order another entree?!?! Wtf! How can you provide it as a side but I can't purchase one separately?!?! Then she comes back with small plates for us but there are 5 of us and she only gave us 3 little plates. The whole time we were trying to order and just get plain broth with noodles she was rolling her eyes and telling us they don't have food for kids here. All I wanted was a plain broth bowl of udon for the kids, and they couldn't even accommodate that when they do serve it as a side when you order entrees. She then proceeds to give me my small bowl of soy dashi udon that I give to the kids, but she gives me the wrong sushi platter. The bottom line is this place isn't kid friendly and they won't make simple accommodations for you. My two tods basically starved and just shared one cup of French fries and a tiny bowl of soy dashi udon. Never again. Absolutely rude, stuck up behavior. The udon is good, and the sushi was ok, but the service is terrible. As a parent, I cannot recommend this place for families. I think that is what the restaurant wants too, so that's how they will behave especially when restaurants are struggling post-covid.
Udon as big as your head.  You will not leave hungry. Food is always amazing. Service can be hit or miss but it's fast and delicious!!!

Time square like circus. Comically loud inside and out. This is a young persons spot. ~20. 30 tops. 

Food is good for the price. Service is incredibly fast and friendly. 

Restaurant is two stories. Huge. Modern. 

Did I mention the music and chatter is insanely loud? 

Bathrooms are communal. 

This is for the casual young diner or the young tourist.

I've been here a few times before but this time it's my first for restaurant week here. I got the deluxe restaurant week menu dinner item for $35 and added the wagyu for $5 extra for my udon. Everything was pretty good and fish tasted fresh enough. Udon was satisfying as well. I've never gotten their sushi here before so this was a pleasant surprise. For $35 it was a good deal. You can tell the chefs tried to make it more presentable so I appreciate that.
I went here two times. I like the place however the salmon sashimi slices are getting thinner and thinner.
Came here for restaurant week and for $35 you get so much food. Service was ok but the food makes up for it! If you're in the mood for a filling meal go here!!
Delicious!!! Loved the spicy noodles and the sushi. Great restaurant week deals too. Super spacious and lovely ambience. Got seated right away on a Friday at 6:30pm!

Known for its large noodle bowls and diverse combos, Tsurutontan serves a little something for everyone. 

What attracted me the most about this restaurants were the combo meals. Almost as if they knew I couldn't JUST have noodles or sushi. You can adjust your portion sizes to your particular appetite upon arrival so don't be shy. 

We ordered from the dinner set menu that includes a small udon bowl (sukiyaki beef) and 3 roll combo + a large Tsurutontan deluxe udon noodles because why not. Both were great! Not the best sushi around but nicely made and freshh. Noodles were better in my opinion. Broth held the flavors of the ingredients marvelously. 

Plenty of seating, good service and looks like they have pretty sweet lunch deals too. Will likely return once it gets a little more chilly out.

We happen to pass by on our way somewhere else when we saw the menus outside. The lunch specials looked too good to be true but we tried it anyway and now I can't think of any other place I would rather be! It was my first time trying udon noodles and they were house? made an absolutely delicious. The sushi was so fresh and everything was so well presented. I live in Texas so when we got home this place was all I could think about. I wish we had one here, and I have been trying udon places just trying to replicate the freshness and chewiness of those noodles, but alas I cannot find anything close enough. When I go back to New York City I will definitely be eating here again.

So came here for dinner and booked only a few hrs in advance. Was seated right away. Havent been here in a long time. The last time i was here was years ago. Definitely miss the spicy tuna cones. Me and my friends got the set of sushi and udon. Udon was still good as always but the sushi was mediocre. The sea urchin in my plat was the worst. Very bitter. Over all was ok except cold and very dark. Needed  to use flashlight to read the menu lol.

Went for lunch today, was quiet in the restaurant. We had the kamatama cold noodle and Waygu|Eel donburi  with spicy tan tan side noodle.  The udon is consistently good, nice chewy texture and the portions are quite filling. The rice bowl was ok, the portion of beef and eel was minuscule over a large amount of rice. I probably would not get this again at this high price point.  Spicy Tan tan has a nice spice to it. 

All in all food is solid, and service is very good.  A couple of little things, water is room temp, not pleasant. The bathroom is a sliding door with 2 stalls, it's a little claustrophobic.  There is an unpleasant scent by the hostess bar, like dirty water rag... not sure what it is, but aside from that, definitely go for the food!

Returned in July 2022 and I have decided that this is an underrated sushi spot. I always get the udon, but this time I changed it up and went for sushi and I'm so glad I did.

The spicy tuna roll is amazing, as is the eel avocado. Edamame and spider roll are also solid. Enjoyed the Lychee bouquet cocktail as well.

I have not been here since before pandemic.  It seems they have more items in the menu.  But what I definitely miss is the dessert I used to order when I come. That Japanese sphere with light brown powder sprinkled on it.  Totally out of the menu.  I was disappointed.

But they do have sushi now more than they did before.  If they did - I do not remember.

My sister and I enjoyed our meal.  We ordered the delicious wagyu slice with uni on top.  Maybe we will come back for more of this.

The shishito peppers were also done well with bonito flakes on top.

I picked the udon with tempura shrimp and vegetables - that was very good as well.

One thing we were disappointed with was the corn fritter.  We remember what we had in Japan where you can see lots of corn kernels.  This had a mixture in it that tasted like corn but could not see the corn kernels like their picture and like the ones we have had in Japan.

Overall, it was good.

We had the pleasure of eating at their bar tonight. What an authentic Japanese experience. The host and our bartendress exemplify great hospitality. The laminated no-frill menu is unassuming and on-point. We had the premium sushi plate with wagyu beef truffle noodles and the uni cream udon, both were fantastic. The fish was all very fresh, better quality than some of the "premium" sushi spots I've been. I especially appreciated the uni and the scallop nigiri. Both noodles were 4.5/5. The wagyu beef broth was elegantly uplifted by truffle fragrance. I suspect they skillfully used truffle oil just right, because I didn't see any actual mushroom chunks. The wagyu beef for me was flavorful but can be thinner/more tender. The uni cream was unique and fun, the broth so thick and the soup spoon enormous. It does has a subtle creamed corn flavor that I'm not a big fan of because it tastes a little artificial and kinda random considering it's a uni cream. But maybe melted uni after being heated tastes like corn?? What do I know about molecular gastronomy. The bottom line is there are few heartaches that a bowl of hearty broth and silky fluffy udon cannot cure, or at least make hurt less.

My friend and I came after an exercise class so I'm pretty positive we would have eaten absolutely anything which may be skewing my view, BUT I can't deny a satisfying and filling meal when I get one. I definitely think lunch is the way to go here, and I ended up getting the 2 roll combo with Avocado Eel and Shrimp Tempura rolls, as well as an udon. It honestly can't be beat and is kind of unheard of for the price that it's at. 

The sushi was sushi, neither bad nor to die for, but my friend did say that the rice on this sushi was much better than the last time she was at a Tsurutontan. She went to the midtown location and recommends that anyone who comes here go to this location instead. 

This place is known for their big bowls of udon, but y'all we need to raise our standards because what is the point of the big bowl if it doesn't actually equate to a big bowl of udon. It's a regular amount of soup served in a larger bowl. The broth had that sweet savoriness to it from the soy, but it was oddly lukewarm. When I get served soup I want that soup served HOT. Blowing on your soup and then burning your tongue is all part of the Soup Experience, and I missed it. Where it suffered most of the loss was the noodles themselves. They weren't as chewy as I hoped they'd be. When you bit down on the noodles, they kinda just squished into your teeth instead of requiring multiple chews. IF YOU KNOW YOU KNOW. 

If I were to come back, it'd be for lunch again only because I can't resist a good lunch deal.

Someone told me this was one of the best udon spots in NY so I decided to check it out! It was easy enough to get a weekend reservation but it's a very large space so you could just as easily do a walk in as it wasn't very crowded for a Saturday evening. We started off by getting the garlic fried chicken app- would definitely skip this. The chicken had kind of a weird rubbery texture and didn't have a good crunch or juiciness to it. I got the creme uni udon and I actually liked the flavor of the broth- it was very rich & creamy which was what I was hoping for. It also had tobiko in the broth which I enjoyed! My main complaint is that the noodles came out lukewarm. Like someone else mentioned, I usually want to risk burning my tongue when I get soup dishes and this dish came out very lukewarm which in turn became cold pretty quickly and ruined the experience for me. I might stop by again if I were in the area to give it another chance, but don't think I'll be going out of my way to come by.

Tsurotontan is still the reigning queen of udon!!
My friends and I came here for dinner and loved dining in the grand restaurant. I ordered the Truffle crab cream udon. There were a few crab meat pieces but many more mushrooms in the dish. However, it still had an intense crab flavor and the noodles basically glided down my throat. To this day, I marvel at how silky, smooth and luxurious the noodles taste. The truffle flavor is very prominent as well. I would love to have this again, in the same portion size. The bowl was enormous, it's contents enough for 2 meals.

this place is one of my favorite places to eat at in NYC. i think it is genuinely SO much value to what you pay!

the bowls are huge, you can get $4 beers, and their sets "salmon lover" is my favorite. you can literally pay $30~ and get a huge bowl of udon of your choice, and sushi and then have enough for a second meal. 

I love udon, and i think the quality of the food is so good as well. really genuinely happy with this restaurant!!!!! warning: they do have chains, and i do feel like the quality is not consistent across the chains. IE, like the boston one i think is a solid 4 or sometimes 3.5 stars.

Man, I don't give bad reviews often. In fact I rarely do. But this udon just felt... so MID. I was so excited since it seemed so well acclaimed but I was left so dissapointed. 

We got a few different udons and the fried chicken starter. 

The fried chicken starter was literally a 1/10. It wasn't hot, tasted like it had been sitting under a heat lamp for 3 days. It was dry. Hard. Totally totally skip. 

I got the 3 roll combo and I believe I did spicy tuna, spicy yellowtail, and eel cucumber. It was OK. I got the mini cold regular udon and that was also OK - the broth tasted so sweet and reminded me of tempura sauce.

My mom got the tempura udon and I believe my dad got the wagyu and they were good, but nothing to write home about. Just huge portions and over cooked noodles. Not a lot of depth in the broth.
Love the udon and sushi combos. Sashimi was so fresh. Udon very flavorful. Waitresses and waiters were not that nice but hostess was very friendly. Would come back because of quality.

So many options to choose from! I would recommend getting the cold noodles over the hot ones. The noodles in the cold dishes are a lot chewier compared to the hot dishes. I got the cold spicy tan tan noodles and the truffle wagyu noodles. Both were very flavorful, but I prefer the spicy tan tan over the truffle wagyu (I personally think that the truffle did not go well in the broth). 

Service was very good and the restaurant seemed to be well kept (clean bathroom!).

Really solid udon place at a decent price point for the quality of the food. I got the curry udon and it was very good; Noodles were the perfect texture and I really liked the curry flavor with the udon. The portions are perfect as well.

Pre-pandemic / 2017-2019, Tsurutontan was one of the best udon places in NYC. Their large bowls of chewy and bouncy udon were all over Instagram and the line was out the door. When I went years ago, we waited at least 40 minutes each time and the udon was so satisfying. 

During the pandemic, they started having a lot of great unbelievable 50% or BOGO deals. I thought it was just because it was the pandemic and the fact that I got my order to go or delivered, but the quality definitely went down signifcantly.

The noodles are no longer chewy and bouncy, but more so soggy and your normal super market grade. The broth is one dimensional and a hit or miss. The curry udon broth was watered down and oily and the suyaki beef was way too sweet... The suyaki beef udon also comes with thin slices of beef that are supposed to cook in the broth, but I think because it was a delivery order, it failed to cook and gave me an upset stomach, TWICE. 

At this point, they're just a meh option for cheap food. Don't be fooled by the 50% or deals that you see. If I paid the normal price for the food quality, I would not be happy.

Yum! 

Uni crème udon was bomb! The udon was served in a giant bowl and portion was large. Udon was cooked to perfection, not too chewy and texture was just right. We also got the uni rice bowl and it was so good. 

Would return again.

Horrible portions, broth is lukewarm by time it comes to table. This place is not worth it at all, i had the wagyu truffle and the uni creme. Uni creme is legit one piece of uni and the broth is disgusting. Tasted worst than clam chowder out of a campbells can. Avoid this trap, you are better off going to a legit ramen spot and substituting the noodles with udon.

Always a fan of the Wagyu Beef Udon in Truffle Broth! The beef melts in your mouth and the truffle broth is rich. 

You can never go wrong with their sushi sets. The fish is high quality and super fresh!

I've been to both this location and the midtown one a few times before the pandemic. Im so happy they were able to make it. The service was great. The fried shrimp, the three different rolls, and the tsurutontan noodle were all good. The fried oyster was delicious. The fried chicken was dry and uni udon was too heavy for my taste. The lychee ricotta dessert was refreshing and the lychee smelled so good. Overall, great dinner.

I recommend coming during restaurant week, but I also had an enjoyable experience all the times I have been here. If you love udon  get the curry Uson or the traditional beef one. Not a huge fan of the flavor of uni, personally so I would not get that again. But, hey you love and you learn. There sushi is okay, but udon is the star and there are of course much better sushi places if that's what you want.

Food was good, but they pulled a fast one on me. Here they had 18% tip suggestion as $8 which is actually 50%. After slow service, I signed quick and tipped more than expected without realizing. It's not about the money, but the principle.

We rolled up on a Friday night at 7:30pm with a party of 16 and no reservations (a pre wedding party not well planned). We asked if we could sit outside. After recovering from a moment of surprise from the request they said yes. They put all of the tables together outside and scrounged up chairs from inside. Despite having an unexpectedly large party, our service was prompt and they were very helpful and welcoming. Our food actually came out quite quickly even though the restaurant was somewhat busy inside. The food was fantastic. If I could give them 6 stars after that experience, I would.

Picture 1 stained bowl. I ordered a beef sukiyaki udon but found a fish roe?  On the edge of the bowl.

Picture 2 sukiyaki bowl with a small crack on the bowl. The crack didn't bother me much but I won't be happy to recommend my friends coming here if they like taking food pictures.

Food is OK. Wait staff was reponsive. No other complaints about the service.

Crab and Mushroom Udon 
Was good but not much crab for price but not bad fast service

Mediocre udon but service was bad, They were trying to rush us out as fast as possible. Only positive is that they were able to push out food in a timely manner. Got the deluxe sashimi set, the sashimi were cut paper thin, I'm 100% truthful when I say you could see the shio leaf through a salmon piece. For a party of 10, they charged 25% mandatory gratuity, which I thought was a bit high considering the fact that service sucked.

Curry Katsu udon: 10/10 so good. If u like curry katsu and udon u will love this. Got a side of rice to eat with the soup and it was great. Def recommend and will be coming back for sure. Service was quick and great!

One of the most famous Udon chains in Japan! They offer a wide variety of noodle/rice/sushi dishes, and more. We tried shrimp tempura, Uni Crème udon, and sizzling sukiyaki with beef, all were delicious. The shrimp tempura consisted of meaty shrimp pieces and flavorful sauce, easily exceeded expectations! 

Also, even though the store front does not look grant, the inside is more spacious than it appeared.

I can't stop going here. I usually get the beef curry udon and I'm never disappointed. The bowls are wildly large, letting you put away noodles with reckless abandon. Modern and stylish decor and lighting. Pretty enough for a date spot (consider getting a reservation), but casual enough to drop in from a winter day to warm up with the power of udon. The variety of offerings is a bit intimidating, and the menu layout doesn't do a great job of differentiating the soups from the plates, but they have to pack a lot onto the page.

There is a surprising amount of space in the restaurant. Potentially good for big groups, but the limited range of vegetarian options might be a challenge.

We tried tantan and uni udon. Food is neither good nor bad. Just not impressive. Personally I don't like the huge bowl concept, I think it would be more enjoyable to eat Asian food in their way--small bowl but flavorful.

First time here o  a somewhat chilly day so the warm broth was perfect. Full of flavor and huge portion, prompt service and friendly and attentive staff made our lunch awesome. Would love to go back and try some of the other menu items

A delicious and huge amount of food for the price. I love how busy it was inside -- despite being a chain, you need a reservation because this place gets busy!

My favorite is the curry udon. I'll be a regular here when the weather gets colder and I could use a cozy meal to warm myself up.
What a unique twist to ramen! Order the dipping ramen! The noodles were so chewy and the broth was so flavorful! I was so full afterwards but so happy!

I remember this place being great, top tier service and good food. I'm disappointed to say it's changed, service is now slow and overall not good. The waiters are friendly and very nice but that doesn't make the level of service acceptable. The quality of food has severely decreased, dishes come out cold for what seems to take an hour to make, from what I can tell  it was sitting there for quite a while. It took about 30-45 minutes give or take to bring out an order of the wagyu sushi. Upon eating one piece I could tell it was definitely sitting there for some time. Very disappointed being from my memory this was a top dish which was absolutely amazing. Other times food is bland as per the Katsu curry and doesn't live up to the reputation tsurutontan had, or once had.

Absolutely delicious and so worth the money!!! So much delicious food for such a good price! Not complaints here. HIGHLY recommend this place!

The salmon lover set was perfect for a salmon girlie like me. All the salmon pieces (nigiri, sashimi, and rolls) were so fresh and flavorful. The side udon was also so good and a perfect size for a side noodle bowl. It perfectly suited all the salmon/sushi!

The interior is so cute and I love the architecture of the restaurant. I love how they had seats for people to sit next to each other as well as tables for sitting across from one another. Fast service too! Will definitely be going back!

Tusurutontan Udons a solid choice of udon in NYC - great with coworkers since it's so close to Union Sq offices. I was pleasantly surprised that they do happy hours!

My friends and I ordered a round of udon, and they came in bowls the size twice our heads. There was a plentiful amount of meat and udon noodles. My sukiyaki broth was great and not too overpowering. 

They seem to advertise a truffle oil udon, which my friends got. However having tasted their broths and seeing their inability to finish it, the richness of the truffle seems to contrast heavily with the lightness of the udon broths. Definitely a gimmick and I would personally steer clear unless you have some truffle craving.

Like the name implies, Tsurutontan specializes in udon noodles. Yes you can have sushi here and as a combo add a bowl of small soup, but I would opt for the giant bowl of soup with noodles. I opted for sukiyaki deluxe and my friend had the creamy snow crab.  Sukiyaki was spot on in flavor and noodles have a perfect bite even if sitting in hot broth while you eat.  Beef was a bit chewy and I would opt for a softer wagyu cut next time. The egg was perfectly soft boiled.  My friends creamy crab soup was a bit too creamy/ rich for me but he liked it.  All in All not bad but not wow for $30 each . If you want more classic ramen vs udon plenty options in the city that execute better in that regards

The food, ambiance and service was all amazing. I got the udon with sushi combo, high quality sushi, amazing broth and udon. Great value. The service was really good, they let us relax and hang out without feeling rushed. I would highly recommend if you're in the mood for Udon and sushi.

I'm a fan of their Hawaii location, and thought I'd stop by the nyc location as well. Review here is for the sushi. I tried their Omakase sushi and while presentation was reasonable for a mid tier place, overall flavors were just so so. For $39 perhaps it was reasonable for the price point.. but probably would recommend the udon here instead.

Ambiance and service were solid, and I found the noodle-esque decor to be pretty interesting. 

I'll be back at some point to give their udon a taste test and see how it compares to Hawaii.

I would have happily given this place five stars for the food and waiter except I am a single grey haired woman who walked in on a Tuesday lunch. The young seating hostess tried to sit me in an inside room "bar" facing glass two feet from my face, like a quick lunch counter at a takeout deli, and i asked to be seated a a small table for one.She said the two available were reserved. i preferred to sit at the front door bar where there were around 16 seats but she attempted to seat me right next to the only person sitting there, another older white woman, at which point I ignored the hostess and sat a few seats down. Not sitting a foot away is a safety holdover from covid, which should have been common sense. Then i noticed next to the bar a second dining room filled w small tables and lights on but no one seated yet. The hostess then quickly packed in two more single women at the bar attempting again to put them right next to me, but they, like me, chose to sit at a six foot plus distance refusing to be right next to anyone else. During this time she started seating men in the next room, never coming close to filling it. The uni dish i ordered showing three pieces of uni on noodles in the pic on their menu came w two pieces let me add. in any case, this hostess absolutely was choosing to be a sexist in her manner of seating and let me add selectively racist (a bevy of asian women were put at a large table next to us and not forced to sit at the corner of the bar) and though some still think this is how to treat single older women who have the gall to walk in alone to a restaurant for an early lunch, I will never walk into this place again..plenty of other excellent japanese places in the area where all are treated like gold. And let me add, the last woman this hostess tried to put next to me was sniffling. I didn't bother finishing my tea.

The ramen bowls were enormous and daunting at first, but I got used to the size. The food was delicious. The sushi was incredibly fresh. Absolutely recommend this place. Make sure you get a reservation.

Super giant portion sizes if you get the bowl for 2 (meant for sharing)!

One of my top spots I revisit whenever I need a hot bowl of udon. Their apps are also not to be missed. It's on the slightly finer dining side but not over the top.

What a fantastic spot! I came here upon recommendation from a friend who lives in the city, and it definitely did not disappoint. I was able to make a dinner reservation for the day of, so when we arrived we got seated immediately. The interior initially looks super small, but we were led down some stairs to a whole new seating area which was massive. The entire vibe of the restaurant was super cool, with dim lighting and a chill ambiance.

We ordered the salmon lover combo and wagyu udon to split between the two of us. The udon bowl was absolutely massive! I've never seen a bowl that large before. The texture of the udon noodles themselves was amazing -- chewy, yet extra soft in comparison to the ones you usually get. The wagyu beef was also extremely tender and the broth was delicious. I also loved the salmon lover combo -- the fish was really fresh tasting, and I'm a huge fan of raw salmon so this one was up to standard. The spicy salmon roll was also delicious.

For NYC prices, this wasn't even too extreme. All the food was delicious, portions were quite generous, and I thoroughly enjoyed the entire meal and experience. I highly recommend this spot!

I found this spot based on the reviews and did not disappoint. Very nice and cozy ambiance and the decor I'd just right.
The food is amazing, we're got several dishes and loved them all, the service was very good and even though we came on a Friday night without reservation, only waited around 15 min.
Definitely will be coming back.
Awesome food and great service. highly recommend if you want Japanese food. Our server Justin was great and efficient.

It's a nice a cozy place with a decent Udon. We ordered the Wagyu truffle Udon and and Cold Uni Udon. The taste of both Udon were good. However you have to quickly eat the hot soup dish before the Udon got soft. I would say the Marugame Monzo in LA is still my favorite.

Service is horrible - from the host to the waiters. The host cherry picked people to sit in different tables and lied about those tables were reserved. And the waitresses were hardly available. Took forever for the food to come when the place was half empty, and Food is Mediocre. Wont come back again.

Got the value omakase which I really enjoy. Least favorite was probably the tuna roll (lacking flavor/texture imo) but the other pieces of sushi made up for it. The fish is very fresh and have a great bite. I upgraded to the spicy tan tan but it wasn't that impressive at all. It wasn't spicy at all and the soup was really thick so it's hard to consume a lot. My friend for the cold udon and that was very refreshing and will get that next time instead. The spicy tan tan was not worth the 3 dollar upgrade. Second time here at the union square location and will probably come back in the future.

Went here with my team on a Tuesday afternoon. 
Their lunch specials are pretty worth, imo. I ordered the Sashimi set with beef udon. The sashimi was fresh and the beef udon was really good. The place was pretty packed during lunch hour, so I suggest making a reservation just in case..
This chain serve humongous bowls of udon and ridiculously affordable sushi. The happy hour prices are excellent for students and the servings could last one the entire day of walking around the NYC.
Very disappointing unfortunately. Neither of the dishes we had were good, nor the tea. And to cap it off the service was very slow.
Great ambiance. Sushi and tan tan udon were fresh and tasty. The service was very attentive.
Food hit my taste buds, I honestly sometimes want Japanese noodles pulled. Service is very nice, they cook the food in front of customers. Ambiance is cool. I ate the food after a bad break up.

This place serves huge bowls of udon (taller than my water glass and bigger than my head!). They also have sushi/sashimi options, donburi, and combo sushi + udon sets. Some items have HH pricing too. They also a few cocktail options and sake & beer. We opted for the nigiri sets, which come with a regular sized udon (soy dashi or cold soup), but you can upgrade for an additional price to get like your udon with beef, wagyu, curry, etc. The nigiri + udon set was super filling and a great price (~$25-$30 depending on which set you pick). The sashimi was fresh and tasty, and the udon was pretty tasty (even without anything in it, we opted for the default no frills soy dashi udon).

We had come by during lunchtime on a weekday with no reservations and were seated immediately, perhaps not true if it were at evening time or on a weekend. There looks to be plenty of seating, though the tables are all fairly close together. They have a contactless pay process (scan the QR code on the bill), so its a pretty seamless checkout process.

Excellent lunch special and portion sizes. Been here numerous times, and my favorites are their beef udon and sushi lunch specials. I've also ordered delivery from here (they frequently have BOGO deals on Uber Eats), and it comes pretty quickly and is still hot. I would also recommend the truffle udon for truffle flavor lovers. I still prefer Raku to Tsurutontan, but Tsurutontan does provide more value.

I would highly recommend their lunch / delivery specials. They also have a happy hour which seems very popular.

I remember my first time coming here back in my first semester freshman year. the food here is always good although I remember a couple years ago they gave the option to order a regular or large for the udon at no additional cost. It doesn't really matter much to me since it's more than enough food for a meal but something to note. I really wanted to try the #1 bestseller which is the wagyu truffle udon but they ran out of wagyu that day therefore I ordered the sukiyaki deluxe which was good but I felt like the broth was too salty and didn't have much depth. Compared to the tsurutontan deluxe which is the one I think I've always ordered in the past, the tsurutontan broth is less salty, more umami, and overall more comforting

Just don't come around dinner time, the restaurant is clearly short staffed in servers and back in the kitchen. And the seat settings make the servers hard to see you if you want to order or check. I tend to only give ratings based on food, but definitely not with Taurutontan this time.
Speaking of the food, it is not the best traditional Udon you will find in the city, but definitely one of a good place for various soup noodle, or Creative Udon I would call it. And the portion is great, which is definitely a plus.
Overall, I would say the service failed its food.

Where to start?  Let's just say happy winter. Udon in broth warms the heart. I've passed this place many times on the way to a local PT appointment. Today I was extra early and I stopped in for lunch. Excuse? Using chopsticks is like hand PT, right? Well, in sum, authentic and delish. I skipped the sushi and went right for the sukiyaki and udon. You can get a lot of good sushi around New York, but I find getting really authentic and delicious udon is harder to find. This is it. I will be back. They have a wonderful sake selection too. Sake before PT is a good idea too, right? The place also has a cool vibe, something you would expect in the block off of Union Square.

I've been hearing so many good news about this place and have been on a seafood/noodle frenzy. 

The interior design for this place is inspiring, it's a minimalistic restaurant that feels like it has been eroded into the space; a portion of the ceiling is concrete like we were in a cave.

The service was top notch 10/10 server, waiters and greeters were extremely kind and attentive. I ordered the Nippon Old Fashion to start, it was amazing a very spirit forward drink with minimal presentation. It was my 1st time trying Japanese whiskey, I was under the presumption it was bourbon at first. If you're looking for a strong yet calm drink this is it. My date ordered the Aki cocktail which had yuzu, passionate fruit and rum. We ruled that mine was the best... hers was a bit salty bc overpowering Tajin. 

I stuck with ordering a three set roll special which included the shrimp tempura (10/10), spicy tuna (3/10) and the fried oyster/blue crab California roll (7/10-taste like a California roll price as $18). I personally thought the sushi was mid (4/10) outside of the shrimp tempura. At $14-$18 per roll even if the special was $34-$38 total, I expected a few more artisanal rolls than your average restaurant. 

My date ordered the Wagyu beef truffle dashi... I was jealous, I'm not a big fan of Udon noodle size but I LOVE TRUFFLE. This bowl was sweet yet rich in flavor, when you eat the noodles you get more of the truffle oil and the wagyu beef was tender and a great edible experience. 

Outside of the minimal ratings on my end I still would recommend this restaurant, the music is interesting-- feels like techno but you're still able to speak over it. Would love to know what you guys think! 

I also want to see different offerings that match the design of this restaurant!

This place has great deals for takeout and I love their union square location. There is ample seating and a great happy hour on both food and drink. The servers are so kind and make sure to give you space while catering to your every need. I love this place, definitely recommend!

The service was slow, we were waiting for sometime. We ordered two sets of sushi and a set of three different rolls. They brought rolls we did not order! Miso soup was late and they never brought the salad. Fish on some of the sushi was of low quality. They are there to make a quick buck. It is not about the quality!
The best udon I have ever had in my life. Me and the wifey always split the udon and 2 rolls of sushi and always leave full and happy.

Solid spot for lunch/dinner. LARGE udon portions- the bowl is huge! For the price (especially during happy hour), there's a generous amount of protein, chewy noodles, and rich, tasty broth. The Wagyu beef upgrade is worth it.

We split the soy garlic fried chicken appetizer. The chicken was crispy, but could use more flavor. This was just so-so for me and not a must order.

Lychee-tini was good (not overly sweet and pretty strong).

Nice atmosphere and wait staff was attentive. Didn't feel rushed at all. The lighting is quite dim though (almost hard to read the menu if you're not sitting directly under the light). It looks like a small restaurant from the outside, but once you get in, the space opens up to a lot of seating.

Great place to bring friends, a date, or to dine solo. Recommend making a reservation for large groups.

This place is amazing! I love the huge bow of udon noodles and the combos you can choose from. I had the uni udon with sashimi- all the fish were very fresh...and it came with a huge bowl of white rice..I love Japanese rice.. I finished all the sashimi- yellowtail, tuna and salmon- just something about the combo with the big bowl of rice that made me want to eat a generous portion of rice...more than I would normally eat. I was actually too full too eat most of my udon. I took it to go and had it the next day- still very tasty! We started with fried oyster app and it was nice and meaty with a nice oyster flavor. The regular udon is a staple and you can't go wrong...very tasty as well..we got this with 3 rolls...again...fresh and delicious! I'm definitely coming back when in the area.

One of my favorite restaurants in nyc. Spectacular lunch special, super tasty foods. Would highly recommend for anyone visiting the city. 
Literally anything on the menu is so good and plentiful but I particularly love the uni udon and the wagyu udon. Chicken karaage is also great!

Katsu curry udon was slightly cold when served. They didn't even refill any water or check up on us. Service mediocre at best. They also added an UNAUTHORIZED extra tip to my bill. I already tipped 18+% per the receipt guidelines and rounded up to the nearest half dollar. Yet I got charged for 20 extra cents. I really don't care for the additional cents added but I don't stand for the poor ethics of that server. It really reflects badly on the restaurant and I do not think I would go back due to this. Plus the food really wasn't that good but I give it two stars because I had good company.
Delicious! We usually get their udon soups and some sushi pieces as appetizers. Everything is super fresh.

I've been here several times and the food is delicious! This is the place to go if you want either sushi or udon or even both. 
The restaurant is very clean and spacious. It is beautifully decorated. The staff are all very friendly. However, I will say that the service is pretty slow. The first time I went here with my friends, all of my friends got their orders and I was still waiting for mine. When I asked our server where my order was, it turns out it was just sitting in the back and they didn't bring it out. Another time, because we were seated in a corner of the restaurant, our server didn't come to us often and I found myself having to walk up to her by the counter to ask for the bill.
Besides the service, I really enjoyed the food. I've had the value omakase with katsu curry udon as well as the spicy tan tan udon. There was a good variety of fish in the value omakase. The servings are big so you can definitely split an order into 2 meals, but also, it's really delicious so there's never any leftovers. I did enjoy the katsu curry udon, but my favorite is the spicy tan tan udon. It has just the perfect amount of spice and tastes amazing. Don't be shocked when the udon arrives - the bowls are ginormous.

I came here with a friend on a late afternoon, probably right before dinner started, and we were seated right away at the bar. Inside, there was a small table for 2 that was empty until we left, so I believe if you want those non-bar seats, it is better to make a reservation. It was hard to hang thick jackets on the bar seats and it was a bit crowded, so harder to go in and out. I tried the wagyu sukiyaki udon, which was delicious and tasted just like I was having sukiyaki. It came out at just the right temperature and did not turn cold quickly. I really recommend this udon dish on a cold winter day. I liked how the egg was cooked (refer to photo). There is also a nice selection of nonalcoholic mocktails and alcoholic drinks to try. I cannot comment on the other dishes, but udon is what this restaurant is known for. The prices are a bit on the pricier side, which seem to be the norm nowadays in touristy areas of Manhattan... You can also ask for hot water instead of cold water if it's cold like in the winter.

After I had put my name down and all parties arrived, I was told the table will be ready and we would be called soon. However, we saw other parties who came after us were seated first, so apparently my group was forgotten. We had waited about another 30 minutes or so to be seated. Not a fan of the service but food was great.

This place is awesome! I love the atmosphere and vibe this restaurant gives. The servers are very attentive and friendly. They make sure we are enjoying our food and that we are comfortable. This places gets pretty busy during dinner time so reserving is a good idea. I always order the salmon lover roll and it's always delicious. The portion is big and it is filling. This is a great place to go with you friends.
We went for dinner and were seated immediately. The food was delicious and perfect after being outside in the chilly weather all day. Everything was made well, from the udon to the meat to the broth.

Bowls are so huge. You could literally fit your face in the bowl. It makes it feel like you're eating a lot. I highly recommend getting a reservation here. It definitely gets very busy, but it is also a large establishment so it could fit a lot of groups.

The udon is amazing here. One of the best I've ever tasted. They were perfectly chewy and thin enough, but not too thin that you'd question if it was udon. Definitely need to get an udon dish here.
.....

SIZZLING SUKIYAKI: 5/5
amazing sweet and savory flavor coated on the noodles and the vegetables, not too dry and the sauce is not too liquid-y

This popular udon place has quickly made it's way toward the lower half of my NYC foodie list these past few years. I used to recommend Tsurutontan to everyone because the quality, quantity and accomodations were outstanding. Sad to say that all three of those aspects have nearly vanished. 

They increased the prices and cut the portions. It's funny and ironic how little food they give you in their ridiculously gargantuan bowls. 3/4 of the bowl is literally just broth. The part that upset me the most is that they got rid of their thin udon option (the single thing that set them apart from other udon restaurants). My favorite dish, the Zaru Udon dish, is an absolute abomination now that it's served with thick noodles. No sane person would ever want thick, hard udon for cold dipping noodles. Just take it off the menu at this point. 

Tsurutontan, you have failed me :(

BEWARE 

Went to the restaurant at a slow time 2:30 in the afternoon.  Food was good, but less than 1 hour after leaving the restaurant I received a fraud alert on the credit card I used.  Thankfully they were flagged and didn't go through. 

I called Saturday night to speak with a manager but no one picked up.  I called again on Tuesday to speak with the office.  The person I spoke to was less than helpful.  Basically said he trusted the staff and it couldn't be the waitress.   He said he would investigate but never asked for my bill number and didn't give me a way to contact him if I got more info from the credit card company.  Then asked why I didn't come back that day (I was already on a train home).  And asked why I didn't file a police report (because no charges went through).  Basically blaming me and accusing me of acting improperly ... as if I had anything to gain.

I went to several places in the city that day this is the only place I surrendered my card.  No other cards in my wallet had charges on them.  

So food is good, location is great, service was a little slow and in my opinion criminal.  Lots of noodle places to go to in the city, I would recommend a more honest establishment.
Their BOGO deal is unmatched! Such a good spread for an affordable price. They have this deal to go too which is nice

Went during early dinner time on a weekday, we were seated side to side when there were plenty of tables (which didn't get filled even as we left). Food was generally salty, we got spicy tan tan noodles and sukiyaki beef donburi, both flavorful but so salty. We asked for more dashi broth to balance it out but it tasted weird, ended up adding hot water which made it tolerable. Fried chicken and spicy tuna appetizers were decent and the staff was friendly but they didn't have knowledge of the food served or how to tend to customers. Quality of this place definitely changed over the years

The food here is absolutely delicious, and I was able to make a reservation easily on Resy. Huge bowls of perfectly springy udon noodles in well-seasoned broth with nicely cooked mushrooms and scraps of thinly sliced beef hit the spot perfectly on a chilly January afternoon. HOWEVER, I was so disappointed to learn that the hostess refused to seat my parents when they arrived a few minutes early for our reservation. They are 85 and 76 years old!  I know many places have a policy of not seating incomplete parties, but a) we had a reservation, b) the place was half empty, and c) they are OLD PEOPLE. C'mon. Really not okay, and I am not sure I can go back.

I was in the area and felt a craving for Udon, so I quickly found this place on Yelp and popped in during their happy hour. The Udon menu was extensive, although happy hour deals were not very impactful given the higher end price point (over $20 each.) I made a last minute decision to get a premium sushi set that includes a small udon, after seeing the uni, triggering a craving for that, as well. I realized this was a mistake after trying the Udon. It was excellent and exactly what I came in there for, but the sushi set portion was significantly smaller than the regular bowls... which I saw were huge and very impressive. The sushi was fine and reasonably priced but the udon felt special and was very memorable. I look forward to returning to try more of the diverse variety. The decor is also very beautiful which I wouldn't have expected from just walking by.

Second time eating at Tsurutontan and it is delicious! was seated immediately. I tried the creamy uni udon and I thought it was worth the extra $8. I came during restaurant week so was able to get a small bowl of udon, tempura and sushi. The sushi tastes fresh and was excellent. Giving it 4 stars because my friend had the chicken udon and it wasn't as flavorful as other chicken udons we have tried.

The lunch price is very affordable for broke college students. Some of the waitresses are rude and ask for a big tip when they have been acting rude. The food takes long so be prepared but the food is good and fresh.
Everything tastes good, but a bit pricey for lunch. The place is pretty nice with good seating options. Service was good and everyone working here was very nice.

First of their bowls for noodles are humongous at least to look at but the amount of noodle soups is for one person. Tan tan, beef udon and spicy tuna roll. Spicy tuna roll was decent. Noodle soup were nothing incredible but it was good to eat. Service was fast and quick. The ambiance of the place is dark and yet too loud for a restaurant. We ended up asking to make sure that we are sitting at a place where the sound was somewhat limited. The manager agreed that the music was loud and he did mentioned that e aren't the only one.

That Uni Wagyu was truly phenomenal!!! We all agree that was the Best bite of the night! Came here to celebrate my sister birthday and this dinner made it perfect. Sea & truffle + seared salmon sushi were amazing as well. Among 3 of the udon, my fav goes to Uni Creme. It was on the heavy and creamy side which I like, the bursting red caviar in the broth made it even better. All the drinks were really strong on alcohol, adding syrup doesn't help much either so if u r not a fan of alcohol share it with your friend before getting ur own drink.

The place is def a vibe. Cute for a night out with friends or a date. It's half a block away from the 14th St. subway station, so very easy to get to.

There is a bar area and then the dining area. We came on a Wednesday evening around 8 PM and there was a 30 minute wait. 

There were a ton of options on the menu, but I loved that they had photos for each item. Super useful! I personally ordered the three sushi combo; Hamachi Shishito, yellowtail scallion and sea & truffle. I enjoyed all the rolls. The sea and truffle was a bestseller, and that one was also my favorite. It did cost an additional $4 to add it onto the combo. I also decided to add a side of Katsu curry which cost $8. it comes with udon noodles, but I substituted it for rice. The Katsu curry was OK and flavor. The portion was decently sized. The inside of the meat was dry. I will not get this again. 

They have many cocktail options as well, even mocktail drinks which I appreciated.

NYC Restaurant Week 2023 

$52 8 pcs Omakase Set (Comes with 8 pieces of nigiri: tuna, salmon, hamachi, scallop, unagi, ikura, uni, spicy tuna, as well as tempura and your choice of udon)

The 8 piece nigiri tasted very fresh and melted in my mouth. Also, a plus 'cause I think the wasabi was grated, as opposed to the paste.

Spicy Tan Tan Udon (extra $3). Wasn't the main but was so good I would come back for a full udon bowl. I also can't handle much spiciness, but this was just right for my liking. 

At some other restaurants, tempura feels like a filler, as in it's made without much thought and put to look like more food. This tempura was not like that at all. The batter was thinly coated and it tasted so light and crispy. Also paired well with the dipping sauce. 

Overall, everything I ate felt like it was prepared very thoroughly and made with passion. 10/10 would come back again!



P.S. They have a very high-tech paying system where you can split the check by choosing and paying your own menu items and tip!

I think this place is over reviewed and over rated. The bowls are HUGE portions which is really nice, but I think their food is not nearly as fresh as it should be.

The highlight of the meal was the shrimp tempura appetizer. But the katsu in my curry was really not fresh and the noodles were over cooked. I likely will not return as there are plenty of other Japanese places in this neighborhood with higher quality.

Their udon is wonderful. The reason for 3 star is just based on sushi and wait staff attitude. I used to give them 5 stars pre-pandemic for good quality sashimi but nowadays it's hit or miss, and one couldn't enjoy dining there when you happen to get a wait staff who has an attitude.
Nice place for ramen fan and some sushi too , I'm so surprise my noodle came with huge bowl and huge spoon , food was yummy, definitely will come back

Stopped by for lunch on a colddd Thursday afternoon. Was very excited for my Mom to try this place so she can see how it compares to Raku. 

The female host directs us to the back of the first floor. She offers my party of 3 to sit at the communal long table that extends past the bar while the WHOLE back section was empty. I asked if we can sit in the back because there were 10 empty tables and she hesitatingly seats us at the table diagonally across from the bathroom. If anyone knows me, my pet peeve is eating next to or being within direct vicinity of the bathroom. MIND YOU, there were 10 empty tables around us. We were the first to be seated in this section. I kindly ask our waiter who is Justin (according to our bill) if we can switch tables. He went to check with the front I believe and gives us the OK (with a slight attitude). The host was in the midst of seating another party and she sees my table getting up to sit somewhere else and IMMEDIATELYYYY stops us and tells us we absolutely can not do that. The waiter then tells her it's okay and she walks away. Why am I this stressed out before even ordering any food??? 

Moving onto the food, the lunch sets aren't a bad deal for sushi & udon for the area. Udon has good texture however arrives to your table lukewarm. If you are looking for a warm bowl of comforting soup noodles to warm you on a cold NYC day, this is NOTTT it. There was absolutely no steam coming out of the "hot" soup. Not even a slight wisp of steam. Very room temperature at best. The regular beef udon was mehhh. Beef quality & flavor was not good imo. Sushi was mediocre as well. 

As for our waiter Justin, he was NOWHERE to be found our entire meal. Thank god for the kind bus boys who I asked for sharing plates, soup spoons, bowls, and napkins. Justin seemed to ignore our table meanwhile serving everyone else around us and checking up on them. However, he did seem to notice us when we were finally paying the check. That is the only interaction we had with him the whole meal. 

All in all, horrrrible service even on a slow lunch rush. I can't even imagine when the place is absolutely slammed. I knew I should've stuck to Raku - way better food & definitely better service. Never returning again!

Their food is like ok greasy but a bit pricey for the taste. Service is not excellent but friendly. The place is casual use, maybe not for business dining at night. When Japanese staff were here for opening, the service was much better than now but nowadays, I see places gets tired.
Hostess does not understand the concept of a reservation, and only seats reserved patrons after the walk ins.  Then she proceeds to argue with the customer.

Food: 4/5 | Service: 4/5 | Experience: 4/5

Came here with a friend on a Thursday night and were lucky to be seated immediately at one of the counter bench seating. This seating is quite cramped, but not too bad for just the 2 of us. We ordered the toro to split, but wouldn't recommend. The fat veins in some areas were quite thick and chewy. The udon bowl was great though - the noodles are fairly well cooked and the portion was great. It was very simple with clear broth, udon noodles, meat, arugula, and onions. Their non alcoholic drinks are good, but they are sugary. I would come again because overall the food was good and the portions are great.

What we ordered:
* Non-alcoholic mojito
* Blue fin toro sashimi
* US wagyu beef truffle dashi

Things to know: 
* Off peak hours dinners for small parties usually don't have much wait
* Bar seating available
* Suited for large parties, but make a res
* Pretty large portions

Food: 2/5
Service/Speed: 3/5
Price (college student budget): $$
Ambiance: Large space, fitting for all occassions.
Would return & recommend? 1/5

Low rating primarily driven by the food - seriously nothing impressive, with one dish in particularly detracting from the experience. We tried the drinks, apps, sushi, and cold uni udon (which we normally love) - all of which was just simply underwhelming or so-so in quality. Value isn't there for the price here.

Had to find a quick lunch place nearby for me and my clients from Asia; happy to have found a noodle place on a cold day; I'd say everything was pretty decent but the udon broth can definitely be hotter (temperature). Toppings were tasty but tempura pieces gotta be a little more crispy. Overall 4 stars.

Still doesn't disappoint! This used to be one of my favorite restaurants pre-COVID and recently went back this week. I thought the food was perfect for this cold weather and it definitely didn't disappoint.  The portion sizes were just as I remembered with bowls the size of our heads. The flavors were still hearty and savory. I went as a group of 4 and we ordered 2 Tsurutontan Deluxes (my fave), 1 spicy tantan, and 1 Wagyu Beef Truffle. 

The Tsurutontan Deluxe was great! The broth was light but savory with plenty of flavors from the vegetable tempura, beef and egg. 

I tried a taste of the other soups and thought they were tasty as well the spicy tantan was a thicker, heavier soup with the spice of chili oil. The Wagyu Beef Truffle had a considerable amount of truffle flavor in it was slightly sweeter than the tsurutontan deluxe. 

In terms of cost, the prices of the udon had gone up $5 from what I remember before COVID. Also, the extra noodles option which used to be free, are now +$3. 

We also ordered a round of drinks:

Lychee Bouquet - DO NOT RECOMMEND. It tasted like a very watered down lychee martini. 

Osaka Garden - refreshing and light 

Aki Passion - Totally recommend. It tasted like drinking passion fruit juice. Could barely taste the alcohol 

Kyoto Breeze - I'd compare this to a jolly rancher vodka. 

Tokyo Mule - The yuzu was very light. Pretty much a ginger beer vodka.

Honestly I've been here a few times now and I like udon but it didn't blow me away. We were seated at fixed seats where we had to sit next to each other as I believe you need a reservation to sit at a table. I got the wagyu udon which was solid but it didn't have a lot of umami flavors to hit the spot. My girl got the sashimi and spicy udon set menu and it was just alright. Honestly my favorite thing was probably the mushroom appetizer that we had. I'm not sure why I don't enjoy it that much however, maybe it's because I remember this place being hyped up over 5-6 years ago and now that I've had it again after all this time I feel like I don't need to come back here again. Service was quick and the hostess was friendly though. Definitely worth trying but not coming back.

I've been to Tsuru Ton Tan a few times, and every time, it's been just okay. I like that they have a lot of options and sides so I can almost always find something that I'm craving. 

I arrived for early dinner and was seated promptly. It wasn't that busy. It was restaurant week, so I ordered the combo while my partner ordered a normal udon and maitake mushrooms. 

My favorite dish was definitely the mushrooms. I got a spicy pork udon and the sushi combo. The udon was so oily that I couldn't finish it. The sushi was just okay, but some of the pieces didn't taste as fresh as I'd hoped. If you look at the photo, the uni had practically melted. 

Overall the food wasn't horrible, but unfortunately I didn't feel great after this past trip.

There's something fun about being served a noodle bowl that's twice the size of your head. I've been here multiple times now and the food is always tasty and fresh. They also have several drink deals, though I would stick to the beer and sake rather than their cocktails - a little too sweet for me.

Tsura Ton Tan is a nice spot to go to if you want to try a variety of udon. It is pricier than the average udon in Manhattan so it wouldn't be a regular spot but it is something that is  worth going to on occasion.

The staff was very nice and very fast, they were always there when we needed something. The seating was a little tight but not too bad.

I had the value Omakase with beef udon on the side , the  Omakase was ok but not that great, but the udon was delicious and had me craving more. Next time i will avoid the sushi and go for the udon and apps only.

Great big bowls of udon! It's always kind of entertaining when they bring over the giant udon bowl. That being said, the amount of noodles, broth, and toppings always feels just right. And it's all delicious to boot. I got the beef sukiyaki udon, and it was very satisfying. 

The space is also quite large, with good seating arrangements for single folks, couples, and large groups of friends.

Frequent here many times over the years! Food and service is solid and I always find myself wanting to come back. This place has truly made a name for themselves in my heart and as well as others. Come here with friends or a date - you won't regret it! Love the noodle dishes, but don't sleep on the rolls and sashimi.
Prettiest udon restaurant in ny . The interior is beautiful and the food is amazing.  The udon dishes are huge.

The service was good the food took a good 15-20 minutes to come. The flavor of the udon was a bit bland I got the best seller. The sushi was great though which my friend got. I would just recommend getting their rice bowl and sushi if you want stronger flavors. The udon is mid for me. Thanns

So... I went to this place in good faith and I should have kicked myself in the backside!  Order the lunch special for $26, and a soda.  Time became an issue and I decided to take out the food.  When I ordered the special I swear it said the Udon came with 2 Sushi rolls.  As I waited for the food I drank the soda and got the bill.  $32.66 (or whatever the change was.). So the soda came to $4... see pic!  Yup, I was shocked too... but no big deal.  My take out bag was given yo me and I left.  Everyone was wonderful, friendly, and the place was nice.  On the train home, I look in the bag. My two Sushi rolls, with miso soup and salad.. nice.  But I saw no Udon.  I open Yelp to get the restaurant number to call and low and behold.  There is a pic of my order, 2 Sushi rolls special with Udon on the side... except
The title reads.. **** Udon Not Included ***.  So for $32 dollars I got 2 sushi rolls, a side salad and soup with soda.  Yup, a $12 special in the Bronx..... I feel cheated!!!  Moral to Story:  ASK QUESTIONS!!  Now to add insult to injury- no napkins, fork, spoon, or shop sticks!  Damn!

Grabbed an early dinner before a play here with three friends.  Loved the atmosphere upon arrival and the service was prompt.  Food came out faster than we anticipated and was tasty.  Ordered the Sizzling Sukiyaki w/beef and it was very tasty.  

I've been to the one in Hawaii as well which both were consistent in the quality of food.

Went back after covid, udon doesn't take like it used to be before. Noodle was over cooked and not as springy as it used to be. Bench seats were uncomfortable. You can find so many better places to eat at the price range.

Very solid sushi rolls option with udon as a bonus!  The combos are the best deals to get here as they come with the option to get a small udon at an incremental charge.  My reco is to upgrade to the uni cream udon for $10 and then add an extra bowl of noodles. You get basically a large udon for half the price. The 3 roll set is my go to with a spicy scallop, salmon ikura, and seared salmon and crab roll - the seared salmon and crab is definitely one of my favorite rolls here. The textures and flavors just mesh incredibly well. 

The service is very barebones as they appear to be quite understaffed but the food does arrive pretty quickly so no complaints. They also have the BOGO offers for delivery and takeout which are quite solid. 

Worth a visit if you are craving rolls and/or udon by Union Square.

Food: ordered the spicy udon. Great presentation with a huge bowl and giant spoon. Flavor was a bit oily but might come back if I'm in the area to try something else. 

Service: service was quick. No complaints  here. 

Ambiance: underground sitting area with not much on the wall. Weird tables in the middle with clear plexiglass separating the sides.

First time dining for lunch & thought it was great! The sushi & sashimi were both delicious & fresh. I ordered the 2 roll combo w/ Udon & assumed it would be a small portion of soup.. I was wrong.. it was HUGE!! The wagyu truffle udon was flavorful & a great option. 

The restaurant  is a huge space with full bar on one side, and with a very chic look. The service was great & very patient with us first timers! I must try!

Excellent service. Nice presentation for the shrimp udon with the main ingredients served on a separate plate. Broth was tasty. Also ordered the fried pork dumplings which were prepared in a way new to me. Tasty but a bit dry side. Will definitely go back.

The first time (Before the pandemic) is alright.  The second time (After the pandemic), it's not up to the standard.  Sashimi is thin, and the noodle is just greasy.  I will remove it from my eat again list.  : (

Food was good, service was great, ambience was cute but most importantly, I need to know when that TALL BEAUTIFUL ASIAN waiter is working so I can be there every time he's scheduled! He was SO beautifullllllll!!!!

This Udon bar is nestled below ground in a dim lit but spacious dining hall. There's a pretty extensive menu, but if order noodles you must go for the udon. We went during happy hour which has really good deals! On average $3-$5 off a bowl of noodles. It was really delicious, but nothing too memorable. Fast service, so I would go again for a quick bite.

I tried this place for dinner with some friends, and this place hit the spot! Service was overall quick and reservations were readily available - I made a reservation the night before. The portions were absolutely huge, and everything was delicious. 

Cold Uni Udon - 5/5 This dish was probably my favorite if you're looking to try a cold udon dish. It was flavored perfectly and the noodles were a perfect texture. 

Wagyu Beef Truffle Dashi Udon - 4/5 This dish was delicious. The truffle flavor was really prominent, but not overpowering. The wagyu was cooked well, and soup was well flavored. The portion was huge, but I still managed to finish the whole bowl because it was so good. I do wish there were other toppings aside from the beef to give it more dimension though. 

Mentaiko Cream Udon - 4/5 This dish was pretty good as well. It was served cold which made the dish super refreshing. The noodles were also cooked well, it was creamy, and the mentaiko flavor was there but didn't make it taste too fishy.

Overall, I thoroughly enjoyed all the dishes we ordered and would recommend this place if you're craving some udon!

Love Tsuru! It is the only restaurant in the city that makes the udon in house and it does makes a difference!

I do like this location much more than the rockerfeller one since that one is more crowded, less food, and more expensive but that may just be my preference.

Always likes to order their sukiyaki soup udon since that gives me both the soup and the udon two in one which is great. The happy hour deal is also great so if you can, go before dinner and you will get it for a few dollars cheaper for a dish!

It's only a block ish away from union square so very convenient to get to as well! 

Will definitely be back!!

The food and service from the waiter/ waitress were great and friendly, it is a little bit pricy but the food was yummy and seems like it'd be worth during happy hour. 

My two stars off is for hostess that was rude, stand off-ish and unaccommodating from the very beginning and it gave us an unpleasant rest of our experience. The restaurant wasn't full nor did it look like it was going to be especially when we were going at prime dinner time so it didn't make sense why she gave us such an attitude about changing tables/ table size as we had someone who last minute wasn't able to make it. (The restaurant also wasnt busy later anyways lol) Overall unsure if I'd come back because I felt like we weren't welcome, which is unfortunate since the rest of the staff were great.

Absolutely not, never again, would rather have eaten at home tbh - this is only about the AYCE sukiyaki, we haven't tried their udon bowls or anything else outside of the AYCE menu. 

Food: I would 0/10 pay $60 for their AYCE sukiyaki again. It was absolutely not worth it, regardless of whether or not they make their udon in house.
