Next time I would probably just get a bowl of udon, but honestly I probably will not be back at all. For the starting order, you're allowed to order 6 items each, meat included. I did enjoy the gyoza, seaweed salad, tuna and salmon rolls! Probably should've tried more fish, but I wanted to focus on the sukiyaki broth and udon. After the first round of ordering you can order 2 items per person. Sauces are on the table for you to use. 

There was also a $120 menu for wagyu, but there is no way I would be able to eat $120 worth of meat to make my money's worth. 

Pricing: Spent ~$155 including tip for a meal for 2, probably would not do it again at that point I'd rather get some omakase.

Location: a couple blocks away from union square, super convenient location, walking distance from a bunch of the trains, about a 10 minute walk from the 14th St/Union Square station. 

Service: meh. We had a reservation for 7:30 pm, we arrived on time, checked in with the hostess, and still had to wait 15-20 minutes. There were walk-ins that didn't have to wait (also for AYCE sukiyaki) so that was a little strange. Meh. Waitress seemed uninterested when we were ordering, and 2-3 things we didn't order/want showed up, led to some food waste. It seemed like the waitress was literally putting in whatever she wanted or thought we wanted. Also seemed like she was in a hurry even though the restaurant wasn't full by any means. 

Overall, AYCE sukiyaki was hyped up by TikTok for no real reason, apparently I am easily influenced. Would not be back.

We had a reservation for 7 people. The service was abrupt and unfriendly. Then the hostess came and told us we had to leave immediately as they had another group who needed our table. When i told her it wasn't appropriate to ask us to leave she literally said well this is America and we can. Strangely , the restaurant was mostly empty.

Reading some of the other reviews, it seems we were not the only ones to encounter the incredibly rude hostess.

tsurutontan just launched their brand new AYCE shabu shabu menu in NYC so of course i had to try it. although i wouldn't say it's so much all you can eat hot pot - you get to choose from a lot more appetizers and side dishes than traditional shabu shabu items, and they let us choose 3 rounds with 3 items each time per person? and one of those 3 have to be a meat dish? weird but okay, i didn't really get why they're advertising it as AYCE but whatever. it was fun times regardless, and i enjoyed being able to choose from such a large menu/item selections..

the AYCE experience runs for $60/person if you opt for the "normal" meats like USDA prime striploin, premium pork, and chicken. but you can choose to get A5 JAPANESE WAGYU as an option for $130 instead. noting that the $130 price point also "unlocks" another half of the menu you can choose from, which adds a ton of sashimi, seafood, and specialty sushi rolls to your meal... also uni sheesh. also huge shoutout to our server, justin, for being a homie and explaining the menu to us!

what we ordered * = my faves):
- $60/person AYCE menu, including all of the below
- sukiyaki broth*
- veggies, tofu, mushrooms
- udon noodles*
- onsen egg*
- USDA prime striploin*
- premium pork
- eggplant tempura*
- sweet potato tempura*
- crispy corn tempura*
- karaage fried chicken
- avocado salad
- sausage
- salmon avocado roll*
- yellowtail shishito roll

the onsen egg made for THE BEST dip for the high quality beef and pork, highly recommend! i loved how perfectly runny it was. the sukiyaki broth tasted super authentic & delicious too. and the best part of the entire meal was when we let the udon noodles soak in the broth so they absorbed all that umami goodness.

legit all of the tempuras we tried were top notch... my favorite of the 3 have to be the crispy corn tempura that came with the most elite spicy mayo/chili oil sauce i've ever had... my friend and i were dipping almost everything in that LMAO. the sweet potato and eggplant tempuras were also fried to perfection.

The decoration of the restaurant was pretty nice and felt warm. When I walked in with my guest we had made a reservation but they didn't know about it until later. Regardless they let us in. 

We decided to try the all you can eat for $60 each. We could get anything under the $60 menu and eat for up to an hour and a half. Overall the food was good but the udon got pretty soggy in the broth. We got the chicken lemon broth and the sukiyaki broth. Both were good and yummy. The drinks were also good but I was surprised they weren't included in the price.

Honestly I love this place. For the price that you can get and the quality of food it's definitely great in NYC. I absolutely love the sea/truffle sushi roll here, please get it (I'm also just a lunatic for truffle) and their udon can be a little salty but that could just be me. I upgraded for the uni cream udon, I'd say it's not entirely worth it and just go for rather the a5 wagyu one, but again that would be personal preference.

Waste of time and money.

Arrived as they opened and no one was at the hostess stand and no customers were in sight. I had the temerity to step forward a few steps in front of the stand to see if anyone was around and the hostess appeared, admonishing me to wait to be seated in a condescending and self important tone.

We ordered an eel roll and two tempura udon. The waiter did not ask what we wanted to drink.

The roll arrived and was tasty. Then the udon was served in the most ridiculous large bowls with a shovel for a  spoon. The tempura came without dipping sauce-- had to ask for it.

The noodles were firm, the soup reminded me of Japan, and the tempura vegetables were excellent. The shrimp not so much -- pre-made? 

The biggest disappointment was caused by the huge bowls that the udon was served in. Within a few slurps, the noodles and soup were cold. It's called entropy. The size of the bowl is important so the soup and noodles stay hot.

I stopped eating mine about 2/3 through and waited for my wife to finish. The waiter cleared my side of the table (experienced waiters know not to do that) and dumped the tempura sauce into to my unfinished udon, (we were only given one to share), even though my wife still had tempura.

The only thing my wife (who is Japanese) and I liked was the sushi. Will never return.

Visited this place twice and both experiences were very pleasant! 

Came once for the happy hour deal - got some drinks and the special udon combo with salmon and rice (around $18? I think) the udon was very bland nothing special but this was a plain happy hour deal. The drinks were delicious!! Not strong at all and stayed cold the entire time due to the tin cups.

Second time I got the truffle wagyu and it was so good. The truffle flavor was very strong, at times it was way too strong but it was a lot pricier around $27-28 so definitely worth it at least once. 

Overall place was well set up, didn't feel too cramped, although some areas the ceiling was super low. But overall solid spot definitely better than udon lab in ktown.

6/2/23 -- my friends and I ate sushi Friday evening and were satisfied and full from our order. The miso soup was $4 and a good size portion for what you pay for. The restaurant is beautiful inside and has a bar area and dining section. The only thing we felt a little discouraged by was the wait staff we had. It  wasn't crowded, many seats were empty. However, it took a while for the waiter to take our food order. I would still go back again though because it might have been an off night and the food was good!

My friends and I came to try the ayce hotpot and we made a reservation in the hot pot dining area for this. We were intrigued since this was a new concept they were rolling out and thought the $60/person menu would be enough; however, I believe since we got 2 hotpot broths, our pricing increased. The sukiyaki broth we had was a little too sweet for my liking but the spicy tan tan was good. There were many appetizers to choose from, but we felt a bit limited in the foods we could put in the hotpot. Ambiance in the restaurant was nice and service was quick, but I'm not too sure if I'd ever come back for the ayce menu again; it was a good one time experience.

When we came to this restaurant, we did not have a reservation and was fully prepared to have to wait close to an hour on a busy Saturday night. However, to our surprise, the host was very patient with us and even sat us within 15 minutes! Location wise this restaurant is on a side street right off union sq park, so it was definitely slower foot traffic, but the ambiance inside the restaurant was very home-y and welcoming. 

For the food, we ordered the sashimi platter to share, which consisted of salmon, tuna, whitefish, fresh ebi (shrimp) and uni. It definitely felt like we were getting fresh fish for a great price. Next, for the entrees we got the beef & unagi over rice (donburi) and the cold uni udon. Both had very distinct and memorable tastes. 

It wasn't our first time at this restaurant, and it definitely won't be our last because it has an enormous menu to fulfill many different types of cravings, ranging from the most popular udon options to sushi, rice, and many appetizers as well!

always my go to udon place. everything is always delicious and served to us very quickly. their menu and prices are a great deal!

*beef udon with sashimi combo: was always my favorite order because I got to have yummy sushi along with good udon

*sukiyaki beef bowl: this was my friends order and he would get it every time we visited, very good and always sizzling hot

*my recommendation: the spicy tantan udon noodles are by far my most favorite udon to order and the lychee martini is good as well. 

*my tips: reservations are available but are not necessary, did not have one but was seated very quickly. would still recommend you to reserve on resy. 

would I go again? HECK YES

This place is solid. It is a bit expensive for what it is, but the portions are large and there are plenty of options for everyone. Worth a shot if in the mood for soup and noodles but don't go far out of your way

Terrible service. Server told us they could give us food scissors or knife to cut food. Female server later told us they only have one set and it was no longer available. What a liar and unhelpful. Only one knife in the whole restaurant? Also would not let us add on a second udon even though we ordered three large udons and sushi combo and drinks. A small gesture would have gone a long way. Don't recommend at all. For the prices, the portions are mostly noodles and not much meat. Only good if you want a carb heavy meal.

I think you can come here expecting a solid meal. The interior lighting is on the darker side and it's a bit loud, so I wouldn't recommend coming here for a relaxing environment. However, the udon here was pretty good and I would recommend prioritizing this over other dishes. 

I came here with a group of friends and we all ordered our separate dishes, but you could definitely share one bowl among two people! There are very large portions here. I would recommend the sukiyaki udon -- the broth was a bit too sweet for my taste, but overall a very comforting dish. 

The service was a bit hit or miss for our table. Our waitress was attentive enough to make sure to refill waters and make sure that everything was going well, but she was way too fast and a little unwelcoming at times.

Fancy. I was surprised when they brought out the huge bowls and huge spoons to match. I ordered the Salmon Shrimp Cream udon and it was pretty good. The shrimp was huge and the salmon was alright. The cream wasn't too heavy though the dill flavor was strong, but still good to say the least. 

The server was kind enough to pack up the leftover cream I had so that's a plus :) 

Would I come here again? Maybe on a rare occasion as a lil treat I guess.

There are a lot of seats. Bowls are huge. I tried the Umeshu Highball, Green Tea Daiquiri, fried gyoza, and tantan eggplant udon, the second bestseller. The servers were nice. The green tea daiquiri had strong matcha flavors that you enjoyed. They have happy hour everyday. The tantan eggplant udon wasn't too spicy, and it was tasty. It was a bit too oily besides the chili oil.

LOVE the new hotpot (only available at Union Square) - this is probably the only AYVE Japanese hotpot place I know of in NYC. 

Vegetable selection was great along with delicious udon. The meat was satisfactory, the appetizers heavenly (highly recommend the wagyu sushi). 

AYCE Premium Shabu, with add on surcharge of extra $3 per person for split pot with two brothers ended up being around ~$60 post tax and tip. Service was aite.

I like the udon here than most of the udon I have tried in my life. The truffle udon was soooo good, beef was tender and the truffle oil definitely made it way better. Also the bowl was huge! Come for happy hour which is usually after 8-9PM

Have been to this location a few times and it never disappoints. The location is easy to find and I love the atmosphere and dimmed lights. The service was great as usual and this would be my go to place for Asian food. Got the fried chicken and fries with my entree and boy, i was stuffed. The food is so delicious and its worth my $ for the big portions for the price

Firstly, our waiter Carlos was attentive, friendly and gracious. 
As a raw food vegan great delicious veggie options and my wife loved her tempura and said the cold noodle broth is the best in the city!

This spot is in Union Square, right next to the biggest Barnes and Nobles in the city, and my friend and I came after a book signing, and let me tell you, best decision ever. It was late at night so we opt to get sushi there, but we saw it's also AYCE hotpot spot! We decided to get the combo sushi where we get I think 3 types of sushi we wanted, with the addition of a miso soup and salad. We also got dumplings on the side! All for 35 bucks! The price was actually not bad for being in NYC! I am always afraid that I'll be hungry afterwards, but I was so full!! Servers were so calm and patient with us, even after I broke a wine glass trying to reach for the dumplings lol! Definitely recommend and the aesthetics were on point! The ambiance and feel of it was very nice and I had a great time with my friend there! Gotta try the hotpot soon!

First time dining in the restaurant since after covid. Service was very slow and non existent. The food was good. We ordered the sea and truffle roll which was marked as a best seller on the menu and it was probably the worst roll we had. The truffle oil have the roll a chemically after taste. 

We had to flag someone down to order
The food took forever to come, about 30 minutes and it's really not that packed at all. The ambiance is dark and romantic vibes. 

I'm not sure I would eat in but ordering take out is probably the way to go. I wouldn't order the truffle roll again tho. Service was quite lacking

we go there to celebrate my grandson birthday we have 12people bring a small birthday cake. the group of waiters say will charge of that small cake for $3.50 for each person. we give the rest for $500 business. it's so crazy even the manager still says the same. so we talk to them no more visits for future. bad service

Food is awesome! I ordered a sushi set with udon for o my $34 bucks, couldn't finish all by myself, good portion to share with a person. My friend ordered a beef udon, super yummy, very flavorful and huge portion! 2 people could not finish everything, we had to take some left over home! Over all, food is awesome! Service is pretty decent, welcoming and nice. Ambiance is dark and moody, so, would come back often for comfort food!

We ordered 2 cold udon, the noodles are perfectly cooked with such a bouncy, springy, chewy texture!!! The udon texture totally won my heart!!!! Just typing this review make me miss the udon already! It is indeed a tad pricy for a bowl of udon, but the portion is huge and I'd gladly pay again. So stuffed afterwards!! (I finished 95% of the noodle, I tried my best)

~ Cold Kamatama Mentaiko Cavier Udon (4.5/5) ~
There is a generous amount of mentaiko, and they are fresh, flavourful with a hint of spiciness, tasted just like what you would normally get in Japan. The mentaiko cream is not too thick or heavy. The onsen egg yolk oozes out beautifully and add some more creaminess to the sauce. This dish is such a delight to eat!!

~ Cold Uni Udon (3.5/5) ~ 
Maybe because this is a uni dashi sauce, the sauce is not as creamy strong as I hoped, and the uni flavour is quite weak, I'm a bit disappointed. But the big piece of uni on top is fresh and creamy, with a slight seawater taste. If only there is another piece of uni on top, just 1 piece is not enough for the entire bowl!

Will I be back? Yes
Perfect udon texture, and the flavours are simple yet beautiful and effective. Will always say yes to authentic Japanese flavour!

what we ordered:
ayce $68 - sashimi, seafood, prime beef tongue, prime strip loin, vegetables, appetizers, sushi rolls, noodles, etc.
.
one of the best spots for all you can eat shabu shabu. they have so much variety of meats and they include sushi as well as appetizers too with the deal!! appetizers includes karaage, fried dumplings, and more! we got the upgraded version one which came with sashimi and seafood. the fish were all so fresh too. you can definitely taste the quality of everything. overall, really great spot and you should definitely try it out! treat yourself

Stopped by to celebrate my birthday with some AYCE Wagyu and was not disappointed! 

The Wagyu was buttery and delicious, and the udon was an excellent addition. It also came with a good AYCE selection of sushi and sashimi, which we took advantage of. 

The contemporary decor added a splash of elegance to the ambiance, and the warm house sake was worth noting. The service was good when we received it, but the restaurant tended to get very busy, and our server kind of just disappeared frequently.

Overall, we did encounter some slight discomfort, such as the hotpot being unable to heat up for a long time which cut into dining time, and the kitchen forgetting some of our orders. 

Still, considering the quality of food and the wide range of AYCE menu options, it was definitely worth it, and highly recommend trying it out.

I booked a dinner for 10 at 7:30. 8 of us showed at 7:30 and the table was not ready. They told us we had to wait another 20-25 minutes. Super unprofessional. And the hostess was giving us attitude for inquiring why the table was still not ready. He claimed the people are still eating. We asked to look at what was happening and it was clear there didn't even bother to keep the reservation there. What was the point of making a reservation? Very loud atmosphere. I would not do another group event here again. Why charge an automatic tip for a group event when they didn'f bother to honor the time of the reservation. The service was also very rushed. For instance, they took our drink menu away before people ordered.

Maybe come here as a party of two. Anything above that number do not expect them to keep your reservation. Service horrible.
Everything comes with a giant bowl of noodles so make sure you come very hungry. The food was delicious. It was just a little too much for me.

I am a repeat customer.  We had reservations and were seated immediately.  This restaurant gets crowded quickly during lunch, and thus, I would recommend you make reservations. 

My daughter and I had the Sashimi lunch set ($26) with sukiyaki beef broth (+$5).  The sashimi was incredibly fresh - salmon, tuna, and whitefish.  I do remember the slices being thicker the last time I was here.  The broth was flavorful, and absolutely delicious.  The beef in the soup was very tender.  

Employees were nice and quick.  Restaurant was clean.  I will definitely return for another visit when in the Union Square area.

This is for NYC restaurant week - August 2023
I came on a Thursday with a reservation. You need to have the whole party there to be able to be seated

They have a special menu - $60 AYCE for a wide variety of rolls, sashimi, udon bowls, etc. and a time limit of 90 minutes
You can upgrade to $80 for some nicer sushi but there's a limit of 2-3 items per person per visit.

I would recommend coming with a bigger party for the restaurant week deal because all of the food comes in normal portion sizes and if you want to try a lot of things, you definitely want more people to be able to help eat it all!

Some dishes and things worth noting:
Uni crème udon- served warm, the uni was not sweet and had a strong flavor that wasn't my fav. The crème tasted cheesy, but good
Wagyu truffle udon- this was delicious, broth was really nice 
Salmon sashimi- it comes with 6-8 pieces
The rolls- seared salmon and blue crab was really good

I was even able to get a happy hour deal sitting at the table.

The staff was very attentive. And though we can't wrap anything up because it's ayce, we tried hard to eat everything- our eyes were definitely bigger than our stomachs! I want to come back just to try more food.

I had the $60 all you can eat sushi for restaurant week. We ordered sashimi, sushi, and special rolls. It was fresh and very worth it. I can't wait to
Come again before it the deal ends.

Food was fine. Lunch special is worth it. Def get u full. Fries were fine. Service was a bit slow. Not much option for happy hour drinks. It was not worth it. 
Lychee martini was great but very small. It was strong though! $9 during happy hour for restaurants week. 
Other drinks from the happy hour cocktails basically doesn't have any alcohol in it & is not cheap. Would go elsewhere for happy hour.
AUCE deal for Restaurant Week was $60 and totally worth it! They had very fresh sashimi that melted in my mouth!

Dropped in on a Friday with no reservation but was seated at a fantastic bar top with amazing service.  The service was fantastic and the gentleman behind the bar gave great recommendations.  
The top 5 choices are listed and I had the 4th most popular and was not in the least disappointed.  The sushi was great as well and I will definitely visit again
The food was some of the best I've ever had. The waiters were so incredibly nice, and the fancy feeling I get when I walk in is so nice. This restaurant is so under appreciate, go here!

Sushi was good, especially the two restaurant recommendation ones! Definitely get those. The udon was ok, not bad, but also nothing special. 
Staff friendly, bathrooms clean. Inside feels very modern. Able to seat large groups. Close to time square.

If you are in search of a great lunch special this is the place. The atmosphere was very cozy. We ordered the salmon lover lunch special which came with 8 pieces of salmon sashimi and a huge udon soup. (We customized it to make it spicy). Service was quick and our waiter was super nice.

The service was below my expectations. People there are nog attentive and seems not happy. 

Food wise it's okay. Unless you like the presentation there are better noodle or ramen places.

The flavors of the broth were really well seasoned and had unique flavors. The restaurant is really big and clean. We have it 3 stars because our udon noodles were super over cooked to the point where they were mushy and not chewy like udon should be. We also felt really rushed towards the end because the waiter kept asking if we were done, even though there was no one else in the restaurant except for 2 other parties lol.

Excellent service by Jennifer.  The bowls could be large, 3 of them actually fit on the two top, lol.  

Tsurutontan been to a few locations, Honolulu I remembered had thick and thin noodles, I prefer thin and that's what this nyc location had only.  And I like cold and it was perfect Al dente chew and very cold.  

Jennifer packed our leftover katsudon and added two chopsticks and napkins, good thinking for us not asking, very sweet!  

Will be back!

I haven't been here since pre-pandemic, came in for a quick lunch with a work colleague. I'm basic so I just had the chicken udon but it was enormous serving, delicious broth, and perfectly cooked chicken thigh.

They have happy hour lunch prices for noon-6pm, so this was $17.

I love the dining area, the staff are friendly, and service is quick.

This Monday around 6:00pm, I went to the Union Square location. I was told to go down to the lower level space, and as soon as I stepped on the stairs, I slipped and fell down so badly. It was extremely slippery!!! After that incident, NO ONE asked me if I was okay, instead they just brought me the menu and asked me if I'm going to order! They acted liked it didn't happen! I was extremely upset by their attitude. 10 minutes passed, a guy fell down at the same spot! They still didn't clean up or put any warning sign. What if it was an elderly person?? They could easily break their bones. I could not believe how unprofessional they were to both of our falls. I'm still in a lot of pain and have a big bruise. I exchanged phone numbers with the guy who fell in case we experience further complications.

Excellent nigiri and sushi. Everything was done with a high attention to detail. Loved the uni in the lunch combo. The udon was nice and chewy. The seared salmon had a lovely texture and crispy roe on top. Very delicate and flavorful.

A bit on the pricier side but not bad considering the level of quality!

Never had food so bad I didn't feel like finishing it. The portions are huge, but that doesn't really matter when the food is inedible is it?

Started out with a hot house sake that was probably the worst sake I've ever had, no flavor harsh and just tasted like cheap alcohol.

I ordered a pork katsu donburi, but the pork was way overcooked, and the crust was soggy, not crispy at all. The rice and udon were over cooked as well. The sukiyaki udon broth was very salty. My friend got the wagyu udon and he said the hot pot meat from supermarkets were way better than what he had.

Such a huge disappointment, this was worse than mall food at 3x the price. Might be a bad day since we came on a night where it was pouring, maybe their chef called out, but holy.... never had such bad food at a restaurant.
Food was top tier! Udon and sushi was definitely amazing! I didn't like how they were being pushy with try to get us to do the shabu-shabu deal, but apart from that, the service was really good!

I've been to Tsurutontan in Tokyo twice, so I was really excited to try their NYC location and they didn't disappoint. Despite the steep price, it really brings the authentic taste of Japan to the States. The interior is classy, spacious, and suitable for group dining. If you are a big eater you will certainly get satisfied with their big portion.

＊ Mentaiko Caviar Kamatama
As a huge fan of mentaiko, I was 100% satisfied by this cold mentaiko udon. It was topped with a big scoop of raw mentaiko ball, making sure you could wrap every udon with plenty of mentaiko in every slurp. The yolk of the onsen egg was gloriously oozy, soft and runny. It tasted wonderful over the cold udon. It was also sprinkled with some tempura bits, which added a nice crunchiness against the chewy udon. Overall the udon was punched up with a range of exciting textures and flavors for summer. 

＊ Uni Cold Udon
My friend ordered this -- obviously one big piece of uni wouldn't satisfy her uni cravings. We both agreed the uni tasted fresh and briny with a prominent umami flavor. The cold udon was tossed with nori and uni dashi sauce, but it was pretty one-note. I'd suggest adding toppings or sides to serve with this bowl. Like the mentaiko udon, their udon noodle had the perfect springy texture.

A friend highly recommended this place due to having had it in Japan already and wanted to compare the states quality to the one in Japan. Obviously it was a lot better in Japan but it still sufficed here. The price was not necessarily too expensive for Union Square and the portions were pretty decent. I think they were pretty known for their udon in such a big bowl with a large ladle as well.

The food quality was good, service was attentive and food came out in a timely manner. The waiter also came by a couple times to refill water & check in on us. The spicy tuna over rice was delicious and the fish in the sushi definitely melted in your mouth. 

The location was pretty big on the inside although it looked smaller on the outside. There are multiple seating locations and tables that could accommodate larger groups. I will definitely want to return to try their shabu shabu. If not, the udon & sushi is definitely worth a trip to come back for as well.
Fabulous spot for udon n sushi. Who wouldn't love this?  So good!!  Enjoy a fabulous meal with anyone here
I'm not buying a $50 sushi meal just to get a small udon bowl. Also the sushi roll was $18 and I got 6 pieces
Great service and delicious udon noodle soup. The sautéed udon was a bit salty but the sushi, apps, and udon broth are always delicious.

The bowls are big!! I was surprised that the portions within the bowl are pretty normal, as I finished my entire bowl aside from the broth.
I was surprised to see how large the restaurant is! There is a lower level, which is where we were seated.

The sushi rolls - we got 6 pieces for $12 - is not worth it here. Very expensive, yet mediocre. However the Udon soups were good. My boyfriend and I tried the Beef Wagyu Truffle, which was really delicious. We also ordered the Sukiyaki. It had a very sweet broth. It was good to take tastes of both alternatively, because otherwise it would be too much of the truffle taste or too much of the sweet broth.

Service is good here, and staff was quite friendly. I give this a 3/5 because I didn't love the food here, although I'm glad I gave it a try!

I really, really, really wanted to like this place, but the broths had a very off-putting smell when I visited for dinner and got the all-you-can-eat deal. They have 3 tiers of AYCE: $48 for the prime strip loin tier, $68 for wagyu shortrib and beef tongue, and $130 for A5 wagyu. Each tier also comes with a choice of broth, sushi, other shabu shabu meats, and Japanese appetizers/snacks. 

I got the $48 AYCE with the shabu shabu flavor broth to start with, as well as three different sushi rolls, and a beef bowl. The sushi and beef were pretty average tasting, and I had high hopes for the udon. However, the broth had a really strange smell that I told my waiter about, and she very nicely swapped it out for the sukiyaki broth. Although the flavor was different, it had the same smell, and sadly that prevented me from eating more. I hope it was just a one-off since the other reviews are quite good. Other than the food, I liked everything else. From the beautiful ambiance, to the friendly and helpful service, to the generous portion sizes, I would definitely come back again to confirm my feelings about the food.
Love it. Appetizers and little dishes of variety of foods best accompany alcoholic drinks

Brought a friend here on a Saturday evening. It was busy but we had a resy and were seated right away. Our waiter also greeted us quickly, took our drink order, came back with the drinks, then took our dinner order. Our giant udon bowls came quickly and we took our time to savor every delicious mouthful. The veggies, meat, and broth were all superb!!! This is such a great place for delicious, comfort food! I HIGHLY recommend!

This place is decent for what it is.
Giant bowls of udon, with a lot of different options. 
I stopped here for a quick bowl of noodles and broth and it didn't disappoint.

huge portions of soup here that is totally shareable!

i thought the broth for my truffle oil wagyu udon was delish. it was super flavorful and dimensional. just divine during the cold weather. 

i would only visit during happy hour. while the portions are big, i think udon is rather simple, and easy to make. for $22 @ HH periods, its still unreasonably pricey for a solo bowl of noodles.

they charge $1.50/serving of chili oil here--which i thought was preposterous. chili flakes however, are complementary.

delicious looking cocktails too.

Varied menu, large portions - something for everyone. They could have more vegetarian options, but the vegetarian in my party felt the choices were adequate enough. Good place for a crowd, and they tolerated small children.
Solid choice.

Went here with two friends and got the spicy eggplant and wagyu udon and the portion size was huge. I really enjoyed the food. The ambiance of the restaurant was really nice and the place had a lot of space. While the food was good, the service and experience was a complete different story. We ended up waiting nearly an hour for our food which I was not too concerned about since the whole place was packed. My 2 friends who were vegetarians ordered potato rolls sushi and the server brought out the eel and avocado rolls and we didnt even know it had eel in it (never had eel before) until after we got our check and it said we ordered "eel avocado rolls" which was like $13 when our potato roll was suppose to be 7. 

What actually didnt click with me was that I told our server that we never ordered the eel avocado rolls and he told the other server to remove it from the system, when the other server took my card for payment, he didnt even remove it and still charged my group for those rolls. I had to explain again that there was no way we ordered the eel rolls because my other group were vegetarians so then after an extra 7 minutes, our check amount was correct. Funny enough, we never even gotten the potato rolls.

Not sure if I will ever come back to this place after this experience.
Really good lunch special. Come for lunch w coworkers a lot. Rlly nice staff, yummy. Not a fan of udon tho

This place was amazing! How did I not find this place sooner? The happy hour is 12-6 pm so stop by and grab some food and drinks! The servers are so friendly and knowledgeable about the very extensive menu!  The noodles are udon noodles and the portions are massive!! The seating areas are amazingly spacious and stylish. I didn't expect that from this place!  

I highly recommend this place over other restaurants in union square.  It is adorable and spacious.  The crowds are a mix of
nyu students, tourists and us regular folk looking for an adorable bite in union square!

Super yummy, been here twice, fast service and generous portions. If you come during M-F they have lunch specials from 1-6pm! There beef broth udon is so delicious the broth is so tasty! Def love coming here in the union square area. Eating with the HUGE spoons is always a little comical.

Wonderful ambiance, friendly staff and huge servings. Notwithstanding the size, the flavors were delicious which makes it all around an excellent dinner when in the area. Thank you Maria for a wonderful dinner.

We had no reservations and waited about 20 mins on a Thursday at 7pm. 

The bowls are so big! Bigger than you've seen. However, don't let that deceive you. The food amount was just the right amount to get you full. 

I got the sukiyaki beef udon bowl. My friends got the truffle udon bowl and the curry udon bowl and we all agreed mine was the best in terms of flavor. 

The flavor was there but not too overpowered for the sukiyaki bowl. 

The truffle flavor was too strong and you definitely got tired of eating it after a few bites for the truffle bowl. 

The curry bowl tasted like japanese curry but the broth left over was just curry so you couldn't really drink it after.

Stopped by for lunch on a weekday, was pretty busy but was able to get a table for 2 without a reservation. Service was fine. They have many good lunch deals, I got the udon + mini sukiyaki bowl for $18. The udon was simple but noodle texture was great! beef sukiyaki bowl was not warm but flavors were yummy, so would order this set again!
Came back again for dinner on a weekend (the restaurant was way busier), which was a much worse experience. We were disappointed as the batter on the pork tonkatsu was not cooked through, and they forgot about our salad order until we were done with our meal. The deluxe udon was very good, lots of chicken, veggies and egg in it! The agedashi tofu was one of the worst I've had, the tofu was dipped in too thick a layer of batter. The avocado salad was good except that it came after we were done with our meal.

Food: 3/5 | Service: 5/5 | Ambience: 5/ 5 | Value: 3/5

This review is based on the Udon noodles. Came here for a late diner with a couple of friends after a long day and it being super cold so noodles sounded like perfection. The bowls are massive!  My friends and I decided to share three bowls to try three different ones. We tired the Curry Udon Thick Noodles, Shrimp Tempura with thin noodles,  and the Wagyu Delux Sukiyaki with thick noodles. I honestly was not wowed by the broths as much as I had hoped, especially for the price. I think the best one was the Curry one which is one of their best sellers. The Wagyu one is their other best seller too. 
The service was great and everyone was so kind. The space was also so beutiful and intimate while being very spacious.

I first came years ago and the food was so good. I'd literally daydream about their mentaiko udon. I went back recently and I'm quite sad that the quality seems to have gone downhill. Prices went up, qualify went down :( 

It's a nice, very large place and the service is always great. But pleaseeee bring back the yummy quality food!

Had a reservation for 5pm and was expecting to do the AYCE but we were told that it was sold out for the day. We opted for the udon and some appetizers instead. The wagyu nigiri was really juicy and melts in your mouth. I got the wagyu beef udon and the broth was not heavy at all. For such a big bowl, I expected the serving size to be a big bigger but we were full after ordering two orders of karage and nigiris. Service was a bit slow as they didn't have that many people working but I would still come back next time to try the AYCE.

Soft shell crab is a must! So delicious! Udon is pretty good too. I had Wagyu Deluxe Sukiyaki Udon. The broth is on the sweet side. Wagyu is pretty good. 

Nice decor and comfortable seating. It also has a bar area. Service is great.

It's hard to give a proper review of this spot. On one hand, during restaurant week, they had an absurdly good AYCE sushi/sashimi special with two options, which also included appetizers and some of their udon. Now, it's replaced by an option that is almost double the price pre-tax (so over double the price with the tip) that primarily features hot pots with a much middling sushi selection compared to the old selection. I hope they re-add the ayce option for sushi/sashimi/mini udon. Even if it was $30 more, it would be worth it. On the other hand, I personally think their udon kinda sucks. The noodle texture is just not good compared to multiple other spots having an odd chew, and I find their broths mediocre. The uni/scallop dish I had had a weird overly sweet broth (same for the sukiyaki udon) and the regular udon broth just isn't that good either.

The fish from the salmon to the tuna to the yellow-tail to hamachi were all great. The eel was perfectly good, and the rolls ranged from alright to good to very good. The beef wasn't bad either or the fried stuff. The uni and scallop udon had pretty tasty scallop, alright quality uni, and the udon broth was just not that good like normal.

It's a mid 4 for their sushi/sashimi ayce and around a 2 for the udon. I'll stick with a 3 then I guess but this would be a 2 if I was reviewing their "normal" offerings.

Came here for the AYCE hotpot + sashimi and ordered Tier 3. The waygu was good but I preferred the Tier 2 meats better. The sashimi platter was soooo good - their toro rolls were great! Celebrated a birthday and we had such a great time because our host, Pinky, was so attentive and helpful! Her service was really great, but it seemed quite busy on a Friday - would definitely suggest a less busy night. The bill was rather expensive but definitely worth the splurge for a special event.

I came here couple times with friends and decided to take my family here to celebrate my daughter's birthday. I was told they charge $3 per person for cake. Then I was told I had to pay additional $3 per person for two pots since 5 people is considered a small party. My mom can't eat beef and how is 5 people considered a small party if gratuity is automatically added? After the fuss, the waitress said fine, she won't charge for the additional pot. But my mood was already dampened.  The waitress became nicer later on so I let it go.

But at the end, the waitress slapped us a bill for 4 adults and 1 senior. My youngest is 11 and when I told the waitress for the correction, she didn't say anything and just grabbed the bill to changed it. ATTITUDE!?  

Please don't nickel and dime your customers. Also please confirm the children's age before you decide what age they are. Your AYCE menu is not cheap compared to others and there are a lot of options in NYC. Other restaurants value their customers.

This is an "update" review. I've always liked Tsuru Ton Tan. The sushi is at least decent, if not good. The place is nice. The service is ok. To be more precise, I think the udon is generally always very good. The tan tan udon is great and the soy dashi udon is also great (maybe the udon was a bit overcooked today, however). The salmon, scallop, and blue crab sushi are great. The tuna was a bit subpar today (a bit too "iron-y" for me). The fish generally tastes fresh. 

My issue is with the prices. Look at the menus over time and you can easily see what I am talking about. The prices have gone up about 20-30% in the last 3 years. That seems certainly more than inflation. I remember the "old days" (less than 3 years ago!!) when the udon was reasonably priced and they offered a "small" and "large" version for the same price. Yes, I remember that. I also remember less than 6 months ago when the sushi combos included soy dashi for free... the sushi combos have gone up by about $6 and then you have to pay another $4-$5 for the basic soy dashi udon. That's $10 more for the same dish.... Which was about $26 before and is now $34. So that's $8 dollars more and does not come with udon. I am not talking about the happy hour menu. In the happy hour menu, both prices (before and now) are lower... the price difference between before and now is still too much.

Let me add that Tsuru Ton Tan used to have more people all the time... the reviews also used to be better. I don't know what happened. They weren't making enough money? I am guessing they are still not making enough money. I am certainly not going as much as I used to. 

I will keep checking prices in the future... for now - not a good deal in my opinion.

One last detail... the staff is also a bit more pushy to get people to order more... makes the experience less comfortable.

The food was not the best, the menu didn't really show what the food had. The service was fine but not the best. The inside looked nice and promising. I just wish my visit was better than I expected. When I ordered something it didn't say it had mushrooms but then the whole thing was filled with mushrooms, I was really disappointed. And also, my friend got soup and there was a piece of some white/grey hair in it.

We had a reservation at 8:30 PM and it was almost new year and New York was super crowded  in where I live. It took me 45 mins to get to the restaurant because of the bad traffic.  we ended up being there 14 minutes late than our reservation and the waitress told us we cannot enter the restaurant because their kitchen is going to close in 1 hour. We told her we usually eat fast and won't even take that long and she still said no, we were not allowed to enter because we arrived 14 mins.  Worst experience ever

You can't really go wrong with this place when it comes to noodles and they give you a lot. For the first timers, be ready for that.  My favorite is anything with beef.  It's worth it

Service is always on point and I do like the decor. 

I haven't tried other items such as sushi here because I'm always there specifically for noodles

Tried this place a couple of times on several occasions - in store and delivery and both times were just ok. The sukiyaki broth taste like it was full of MSG and we all felt extremely thirsty and couldn't even finish the bowl. The chicken udon was slightly better but there were no toppings other than 5 pieces of chicken.

Came here for a group dinner with a reservation and were seated immediately! I ordered 3 roll combo dinner set and got a miso soup & salad on the side - it was sooo good!! The portions were great and I left VERY full and happy!

Fantastic udon that comes in a comically large bowl. Only issue is the seating -- you literally feel crammed like a pack of sardines. It was so loud on a Monday night I literally couldn't hear my friend who was sitting 2 feet in front of me. The people at the table next to us had to move our table out of the way just so they could exit.

We came here for lunch on New Years Day and enjoyed a wonderful meal here. The food comes in gigantic bowls and their portions are quite large as well. Specializing in udon, we ordered three of these and a chicken karaage as our starter. 

Chicken karaage - very crispy chicken, well flavoured and chunks were not too fatty either.

Tsurutontan Deluxe - this is one of their most popular and special udon with a variety of toppings including tempura, beef, chicken and egg dropped in broth making a nice swirl. We really liked the addition of the egg and the soup itself was very flavourful without being salty. The best part was that the noodles were perfectly al dente and toothsome. There was also a lot of seaweed bits for texture and flavour. 

Tonkatsu Curry Udon - Very thick and flavourful curry with a large portion or pork tonkatsu. Although the pork was a little bit less crispy after being in the curry, the noodles and curry sauce itself went perfectly together. This was a very filling dish but enjoyed by our entire table.

Sizzling Sukiyaki - a stir fried udon noodle with beef, vegetables and of course, their wonderful udon. This dish was a surprising hit because the sauce was again, not too salty but very flavourful. It also came with an abundance of veggies and not too oily either. 

Overall, we really enjoyed our meal here and left stuffed to the brim! Great udon texture, soup flavours and overall experience.

this place has gone downhill. 

delivery review: 

i order from here from time to time and i let slide some of the times ive had a bad dish, but today was the straw that broke the camels back. i usually get the bogo deals, which, if the food was edible, would be a great. look at the tan tan noodle that came today. it was all mushed up like someone threw the meat in a blender. it was INEDIBLE. gritty, powdery even. 

i also ordered the sukiyaki and the broth was so greasy and the meat is dont even know how to explain it. like they were lapping it in warm water for 10 min. i swear the workers would probably not eat these dishes themselves. the absolute worst thing is ordering expensive food that you cant eat. my dog wouldnt even eat it. 

consensus: waste of money. youve been warned.

One of the best udon in the city. I've been coming to Tsuru since high school and I've never had a bad meal. The portions are super fillings and the bowls are pretty cool since they're so large. The sushi is really fresh as well and I really enjoyed my salmon avocado roll. 

I got the duck udon which is very fragrant and light. My friend got the katsu curry udon which was also delicious, but a bit thicker since it is curry. 

Stop in for a quick bite or a nice dinner! This place is great for groups and they have an expansive udon, sushi, and drinks menu!
bad environmental, staff didn't wash her hands after using  toilet paper. She also had badly cough without mask. After that I didn't want to eat anything.

The hostess promptly welcomed me, and the service was swift. Opted for the sushi set - 3 rolls (2 eel avocado and shrimp tempura avocado) with dashi udon as an add-on. The udon was okay, but the noodles were slightly undercooked. In addition, the rolls seemed overpriced for their quality; the eel was unexpectedly cold, and excessive rice affected the overall flavor. The rice-to-sushi ratio was uneven, giving it a budget grab-and-go taste. Unfortunately, I personally wouldn't recommend this place to friends or family with the food being overpriced and low quality dishes.

Came here on a Friday evening for a group of 5. Thank goodness we made reservations because the restaurant was packed! Typically they'd want the entire party there before seating, but we were only waiting on one person, so they gave us our table.

We ordered the Fried Blue Crab to start and it came with a lemon to squeeze and yummy tartar sauce. We also got their Yellowtail Scallion Roll and it was good with fresh fish. I ordered the Sukiyaki Beef Udon, which had an abundant of toppings and a nice sweetness to the broth. My friend initially ordered the Wagyu Truffle Udon, but found hair in it! Of course, the servers were kind enough to replace her order for something else.

Highly recommend making reservations, especially for dinner, and to specify whether you want their Hotpot offering or regular dinner. Overall, spacious restaurant with multiple levels, so it's perfect for large groups. The udon keeps you full as well. I'll always return for a yummy warm, casual, noodle-y meal in the area!

I haven't explored much of the udon around the city, but this place has me sold!

They have such interesting items on their menu and udon flavors that I have not really seen before. The layout and atmosphere of the restaurant is very nice and clean which I appreciated. It felt very spacious even though there was a lot of people. 

I decided to try out 3 of their udons, and you get a choice between thin or thick noodles. Here's the 3 I got:

1. US Wagyu Truffle Dashi Udon - This was my favorite udon that I got to try here! The truffle added such an interesting umami funk to to the broth and it was delicious. I found myself going back for more and was only sad that I ate it all so quickly. The wagyu was tender as well and I can definitely see why this is their number 1 seller! 

2. Uni Creme - I love Uni and decided to try this but unfortunately it wasn't the star dish for me. I know that uni is expensive so I could understand the portion size for the price. I felt that the sauce was sort of missing some flavors to be honest. It was pretty salty and I feel that some greens like scallions would've been nice, or if there were some mushrooms in there. It did all sort of taste the same at one point and wasn't as exciting towards the end. Thick udon noodles would be the way to go for this dish. 

3. Tsurutontan Deluxe - I decided to get thin noodles for this one and honestly I enjoyed it and I really liked how the tempura wasn't overly fried or overly battered. The broth was pretty salty but there was more depth to the broth that I couldn't find in the uni Creme. 

Definitely check out this place if you enjoy trying out different flavors of udon! It makes for such a nice date night or gathering.

I came here on a weekend lunch hoping that their special of all-you-can-eat shabu shabu was still available but unfortunately, it was not. We still got a seated very quickly and the waiters were all very attentive. 

I ordered the Seafood Pink Creme Udon which was essentially fried salmon and shrimp in a creme-based udon. Although I think mine was the best-tasting one out of everyone at the table, I thought the udon was just okay - the noodles weren't particularly chewy and I thought that the flavors of the broth could've been more intense. I did appreciate the fried shrimp as it was fried to perfection. The salmon, however, felt a little bit overcooked for me. Also, they serve the dish in a very impressive-looking bowl although the amount of food you receive does not match that.

Overall, okay place for lunch. Not sure if I would come back again, still on the hunt for better Udon!

Giant bowls of udon? Signed me up!

We didn't make it to HH but the prices weren't too bad especially for their portion size! I love and crave Uni udon/pasta and this place was right up my alley. I forgot that it was in my booked list to visit when my husband and I got hungry after walking around Time Square and lo and behold it was on the strip! Good timing or coincidence?

We were seated downstairs away from the bar and it was semi secluded like a little Japanese patio ambiance. I liked it.

Anyways, we got the spicy ton udon and uni cream udon! I'll keep it short and sweet, simply delicious! I would definitely come back.

Went here for lunch and food was solid but not great. We ordered karaage as an appetizer and it was really tough to chew and dry. I've had the tan tan udon before and it definitely tasted better last time than this time. My friend got the wagyu sukiyaki and couldn't finish because she felt the dish was starting to get too fatty. This place is not cheap either so I was expecting a bit more! However, the waiter was super informative and kind.

The Spicy Tuna Cones are off the menu - for now. When I heard this I shed a tear. I was continuing my birthday festivities and had come here just for this tasty appetizer. The server assured me that the dish would make a return quite soon. I am counting the days. Dejected, I  ordered  a salmon avocado roll. It was soft and I could eat it nicely. The interior was quiet as there were few people eating. A ladies restroom has two cubicles and a sliding door to enter. The bar area had more customers.

A perfectly decent noodle spot. Nice interior with a bar. Got the scallop/uni/ikura cold udon once and it was pretty tasty but not exceptional. Like the uni wasn't sweet but scallops were quite good. Got the wagyu beef another time and it was hearty and had great flavor. Beef was just good tho, not great. Also got some sashimi and that was perfectly okay.
Best udon noodle ever. Don't miss out on this. Appetizers are good, but noodle is large portion.
Very generous portions! Udon noodles are tender and flavorful, especially recommend the curry udons. Ambiance is very nice and the service was fast and kind as well. Would definitely come back!

One word: DELICIOUS!! We came during lunch time and each got one of the lunch specials. The regular udon was sooo good. Thick, bouncy noodles in a sweet, fishy broth. I would baptize my newborn in this broth it was that good. The beef sukiyaki udon was also delicious with the signature sweet sukiyaki flavor. The sushi and salmon bowl were also fresh and great. 

The service was great and the interior is beautiful. I can't wait to try one of their speciality udons next time!

I just ordered delivery direct from the website. I ordered 1 chicken udon buy one get one free and it showed a total of $25. As soon as I entered my card and completed transaction, a new total of $52 came up. I called the restaurant to tell them there was a mistake and they told me I needed to call Uber Eats! I was VERY confused as I ordered directly from their website and NOWHERE, even throughout the checkout, did it mention this was going through Uber Eats. They refused to cancel my order even though I called within 30 seconds of it being placed, refused to let me speak to a manager, and said my only recourse was to contact Uber Eats and hung up on me. It was not my choice to engage in business with Uber Eats nor was it disclosed on their website that this would be a third-party order. This is extremely dishonest and manipulative.

My husband & I went during happy hour and the drinks & food were great!  We had the lycheetini & mango margarita .For appetizers & dinner we had the pork fried dumpling, chicken teriyaki, truffle fries and bowl of rice

On our way to see a show- this food is amazing.  We had Spicy EggplantBeef.  It came out in a trough!!!  It was a perfect blend of spices.  Service was good.  Restaurant was lovely.  Excellent musical choices.   Lots of Asian families with their babies, so very family friendly.  Beautiful kids!!  Great food.  Huge portions.  Prices below expectation.

Went for an early dinner on a Saturday evening. Relatively quiet when we got there but the restaurant was buzzing by the time we were done.

Love the variety of udon, sushi and rice dishes they have especially in being able to combine a couple of dishes in their combos.

We had the Salmon Lover Dinner Set with a Sukiyaki Udon and a Katsu Donburi Ruce Bowl with a U.S. Wagyu Udon - both excellent.

Friendly, efficient service.

service was fine but food took at least 45 minutes to come out and udon was so mid and salty i couldn't finish, tempura was extremely oily as well (which i expected but it felt gross eating) portions are big but  they better be for the price you're paying :/ this was so mid and expensive sorry

Came in on a Saturday evening with a small group of friends and was seated quickly without reservation. 

If you're craving a *huge* bowl of soup and udon, this is your place. I was super shocked that the ladle they gave was meant to be the soup spoon - that's how big the bowl is! There are many varieties of udon here but I opted for the duck  - the soup was good and came with an adequate amount of duck breast and toppings. We also ordered karaage which was lackluster compared to the soup but paired well together.

I will definitely try out other types of udon next time I am here!

Came on the weekend it was pretty empty, the weekend doesn't offer and lunch deal or happy hour: the price gets quite expensive. 

The bowl are ally large for all the regular udon options. The toro sashimi has 8 thick pieces. But the fish doenst seem not fresh, part of the fish are grey not even pink. I had the duck udon the broth has more a sweeter taste to it. 

Recommend to come on the weekday lunch, much affordable with the same amount of food

Came on a Saturday night and got seated immediately. Missed happy hour which is 9 to close on Saturday. The food was delicious and the portions were substantial. They have a full bar and mood lighting. This would be an ideal date spot but beware of the music volume which can make it difficult to hear.

I walked in, and I was promptly greeted by the manager on duty( kaya)She was very kind and pleasant and walked me to the bar. The bartender ( Ariel) explained the menu and made me a great lychee martini and suggested some food items for me. I tried the blue crab, and the yellow tail scallion , which I will return and enjoy again thank you for your hospitality .

I came with my friends for Saturday dinner and were able to easily make a same day reservation. The restaurant is pretty big and I loved the vibe. The noise level was also perfect to be able to chat with friends. They had some 'April special' menu items so a couple drinks and food items were discounted. From that menu, a friend and I got a lycheetini for only $8 - and it tasted pretty good and was surprisingly strong. 

As for entrees, there are so many things on their menu, it literally took us so long to decide. Eventually I decided on the katsu curry udon while my friends ordered the mentaiko truffle udon, eggplant wagyu udon, and a beef cold udon. When we got our food, my friends and I were utterly in shock over the unexpectedly massive bowls of food in front of us. Everything looked absolutely delicious and tasted great too! I had a generous portion of katsu that was also still nice and crisp despite marinating in a bowl of curry. The udon was also great and the perfect texture. I tasted some of my friends udons as well and they were all great especially the eggplant wagyu udon which I would love to come back and try again. Overall, the food was delicious -- I think I'd opt to share an udon bowl with a friend (esp if I'm not feeling super hungry) and try one of the sushis or other apps. I think the udons with soups are especially filling and hard to finish if you aren't feeling super hungry whilst the udons without any are a good portion/entree size for one.

Salmon Shrimp creamy udon with extra crab meat- very creamy and delicious 

Grilled Maitake Mushrooms- very crunchy 

Sausage - very juicy 

Avocado salad - very fresh 

Service is great 

Place is clean

Good food, super loud, food served within 20 minutes. There were 3 of us bit they would only take 2 credit cards so we couldn't split the bill. Silly and avoidable inconvenience and lots of other more accommodating so will find a new spot.
We ate soft-shell crab, udon and other delicious stuff.  It was quiet so perfect for conversation.  Service was excellent.

Overall:  Went here for a friday date night.  They had last minute reservations available.  The food portions were huge and pretty solid.  It won't be my go to place, but it was solid, available, and a good value.

Food: 4
Drinks: 4
Service: 3
Value: 5
Atmosphere: 3 


Food: The food ranged from decent to pretty good.  We ordered the Spicy Tuna Roll, Tuna Avocado Crispy Rice, US Wagyu Beef Sukiyaki, and Katsu Donburi Bowl.  For the apps, the crispy rice very nicely cooked and warm while the tuna roll was just average.  The Sukiyaki was the best dish of the night - it was enormous and came with a nice portion of beef.  I was disappointed with the Katsu Donburi - the pork was soggy and the dish was mostly white rice.  The quantities were nice but some dishes could have been higher quality.

Drinks: My girlfriend got a cocktail and I got one of the happy hour hot sake's.  The sake was a good value and was plenty for the full meal.  They had plenty of other options as well.

Service: The restaurant seemed understaffed and it took a while for a server to take our order.  Food was quick once we got started, but the waiter mostly served to take our order and drop off food, there wasn't much else.  But overall nothing to complain about.

Value:  The prices don't look particularly cheap, but the food portions (particularly any sort of udon dish) are massive.  The bowl might as well be a bucket.  Its a ton of food.  We also got lucky with the late night friday happy hour starting at 9pm.  None of the deals were amazing, but they shaved $3-4 off of most dishes.  We ordered too much food, but the value here is pretty good.  

Atmosphere: The interior was nicely decorated and brightly lit.  There were some Asian design elements and some cool bar like seating int he middle.  We had a small table off to the side.  Tables were reasonably spread out and since the restaurant was only half full it felt like we had plenty of space.  The atmosphere didn't add anything special, but it was a nice place to grab dinner.

I've dined at TsuruTonTan a couple of times in midtown, but this is my first visit at their union square location. My friends and I arrived right before closing on a Tuesday night. We were seated in the main dining area on the left and started off with a pitcher of beer. Each of us ended up ordering their top customer favorites, like the wagyu beef truffle dashi, wagyu eggplant tantan, Tsurutontan deluxe, and sizzling sukiyaki. We also opted for their kaarage and truffle fries as an appetizer. Since we were probably the last customers to order, we got our food pretty fast. The kaarage was crispy, but the French fries were undercooked, which was disappointing.

All the udons with soup came out with extremely large bowls. I was very pleased with my wagyu eggplant tantan. The wagyu was thinly sliced and extremely soft. The soup broth with the minced beef was so flavorful and filling. Most importantly, the texture of the udon noodles were chewy and very pleasant to eat. The eggplant was also a nice addition to the dish but not the star. I struggled to finish my bowl since I was so full but eventually ate everything since it was so good.

Overall, Tsurutontan is a solid udon spot. I would definitely go back for their tantan, but I typically go for their curry udons since they are harder to find elsewhere.
Food, i felt the katau curry udon was bland, and the uni udon was also on the blander side. Both could be better seasoned.

Dinner set was tasty! Pretty standard Japanese food. Sushi was fresh and udon was nice and chewy. Good restaurant to have in your back pocket when you don't know what to eat. The "mini" udon bowls are actually pretty sizable! I was totally full by the time we finished.

Food (5/5): Very delicious food. We got a variety of sushis and udons. I got the three roll combo with scallop, avocado eel, and salmon ikura plus the sukiyaki bowl. We also shared some of the premium rolls. They were all delicious! I particularly enjoyed the premium rolls which were salmon and crab combo.

Service (4/5): The servers are friendly but for bigger groups the food can take a while to come out. They were helpful and friendly.

Ambiance (5/5): This is a beautiful restaurant with a nice upscale interior. The wall decoration is super nice and impressive.

Came here with my family and had amazing service as well as amazing food. Everything was super yummy and the ambiance was excellent! I highly recommend coming here. Especially with our server, Jorge, that took care of us! Everything was great, very happy.

Have been wanting to come to this place ever since I went to the location in Tokyo. They are known for their ginormous plates. The location is cute and cozy, but the tables are often so close together that you were unable to get out without putting your butt into someone else's table lol. 

We started with the edamame and fried chicken, both were seasoned well and a good starter. For our main courses, we got the classic beef udon and the Katsu curry udon. I had gotten the same in the Tokyo location, so I knew that I would enjoy it. The beef udon was savory but light at the same time. It was a perfect blend of saltiness and umami. my favorite part was drinking the broth at the end. The Katsu curry was heavier but still was very good and had a great curry flavor. The Katsu was cooked to perfection.

Can't wait to come back again! I find it so funny how big their bowls are and I would come just to eat out of them again.
really great vibes! drinks were amazing and not watered down at all. sushi rolls were ok but the star was the tuna volcano.

Enjoyed our Yelp! Find just a stone's throw from Union Square - we went to Forbidden Planet, The Strand bookstore and Max Brenner and hung out in the Square for street music and enjoyed being outdoors in the great weather!

Searched on Japanese food and since we were meeting near after our daughter's college classes, found this fun place! Waited up front and had some drinks as they don't sit incomplete parties.

But, once sat (in very close tables), we ordered quickly and got our food and drinks quickly as well! The draft Sapporo was delicious and the kids enjoyed their virgin cocktails: cranberry Lime and Mango mojito. My Tokyo Mule was icy cold and delicious (and pretty!).

The decor and vibe were chill and upscale, but the prices were very reasonable. We all enjoyed our udon meals, but the standout actually was the fluffy and perfectly sauced Oyakudon (rice bowl with scrambled fluffy egg), and the sizzling wagyu beef and chicken udon. All the options were really large and we would've taken some home, but we walked so much, everyone was really hungry! For our family of 5 the bill game to $208. Glad we came!

Food was good and the lunch price is pretty ok. The bowl and spoon are too big to eat comfortably though.
The waitress did seem to be in a big rush to clean up. I was literally scooping rice into my mouth when she asked if she can take my tray away, I didn't say anything because I was scooping rice into my mouth. She said I can take the rice as she took my tray away.

She then came back and asked to take my friend's tray away, my friend said she's still working on her sushi. Waitress said my friend can keep the sushi, she'll take the tray. No problem, but she also took the soy sauce and the little soy sauce bowl. So my friend just had plain sushi. 
No soy sauce not a big deal, it's the fact that we are literally still eating, putting food in our mouths, and she wants to clean up.

It was not rush hour at all, there were only about 5 tables full.

Although the bowls are huge here, the serving size is not that much as they're not filled all the way. That being said, we split two bowls of udon for the three of us and were satisfied. The duck udon was fine but didnt blow me away. The truffle cream crab and mushroom however was definitely a standout!! There's a decent amount of crab and mushrooms and the cream sauce is amazing. We were scooping up every last bit!

Came here on a weeknight and there was no wait! 
Portions were not that big, but the food tasted not bad. 
I love udon, and tried both the soup udon and the stir fry udon. The soup udon was very good, although I felt the broth lacked some flavor. The stir fry udon was ok, it was a pretty standard udon. 
The decor and interior of the restaurant was nice. 
Overall, I would probably come back again if I was craving udon and in the area. 
Otherwise, I prefer Raku for some fresh udon (although this restaurant is a bit more budget friendly than raku).
The service was amazing, the atmosphere was nice, and the food was great. The best part is happy hour is from 4-7PM. We'll be back for more.

This place offers some really good sashimi, along with impressively large portions for the Udon bowls, which made for a satisfying and hearty meal. We stopped by for lunch on a Saturday, and while it was quiet when we arrived, it started to pick up a bit as we finished. One thing that stood out was their unique Happy Hour timing--it runs from 8 or 9 p.m. until close. It's a bit unusual, but I can see how it might appeal to the student crowd or anyone looking for a late-night spot to unwind.

The food overall was enjoyable, though I did find the broth for the Udon to be on the sweeter side, which may be a matter of personal taste. That said, the atmosphere more than makes up for any small preferences. The place has a high-end, sophisticated vibe, complete with a large, stylish bar that showcases an impressive whisky collection. This setup definitely explains why late-night Happy Hours are a popular choice here--the ambiance is perfect for a relaxed evening with drinks.

If you're in the area and looking for a spot with quality sashimi, generously portioned Udon, and a chic, upscale setting, this place is worth a visit.

Food:
Food was good with lots of complex flavors working together! I got the Truffle Wagyu Udon, which is something I haven't had before. However, I think the truffle flavor strongly overpowered the dish. Not sure it tasted like udon anymore bc of it. Regardless, tasted great. 

I love the Tuna cone! It was perfectly crunchy. It's layered; it has tuna on top, guac in the middle, and tuna on the bottom. It was a nice, refreshing taste to have the guac in the middle! 

Service:
Servers were kind and attentive! I loved to hear their advice

Tsuru Ton Ton has two dining area, and I was pleasantly surprised to get a seat right away without a reservation. The ambiance was peaceful. I also discovered their were many Happy Hour food options from 4-7pm, which was a nice bonus. The udon was definitely Instagram-worthy, and I enjoyed the flavors--it wasn't overly salty, and the noodles were handmade. However, I did notice that a few noodles got stuck together, which led to some waste. Another downside was that they didn't refill our water, unlike most other restaurants and toilet was clogged.

Overall, I had a good experience and would consider returning.
Delicious food. Excellent service. Looking forward to the next time. Highly recommend.

We came to Tsurutontan a little after 12pm on a weekday, and were one of the first customers. Ordered the Fried Dumplings from the Happy Hour menu, and 2 lunch specials (10pc Nigiri Set with Soy Dashi Udon, and 3 Roll Set with Spicy Tan Tan Udon). Happy hour is from 12pm-6pm.
Fried Dumplings ($11) - The dumplings were tiny and the sauce carried this appetizer! I can't imagine having to pay normal price for this.
10pc Nigiri Set with Soy Dashi Udon ($38) - Includes tuna, salmon, hamachi, albacore tuna, shrimp, surf clam, scallop, unagi, ikura, and uni piece. I liked the scallop and unagi pieces the best. I enjoyed the soy dashi broth with bouncy udon.
3 Roll Set with Spicy Tan Tan Udon ($31 + $5) - Ordered the yellowtail, unagi, and spicy tuna rolls. It wasn't anything special. My partner enjoyed the Spicy Tan Tan broth.

I started with the yellowtail sashimi which were nicely portioned. I've had fresher raw fish. The noodles are served in an oversized vessel and were chewy and tasty. Uni was delicious but seemed tiny portioned compared to the noodle soup. The service was friendly although spotty as more customers arrived. Ambiance was pleasant and the crowd was young. I am curious to try the other dishes here and will return.

I got the premium nigiri lunch set with shoyu udon ($21). It came with 6 pieces of different types of nigiri. The cuts of fish were pretty fresh. However, the highlight was the udon. Honestly, I was so surprises by how bouncy the udon was despite eating it 15 minutes later. It wasn't soggy at all and the broth was so umami. This is probably one of the best bowls of udon I've ever had. 

I love the aesthetic of this place. It was easy to get a table for lunch on a weekday. Generally, the staff won't seat you unless you have everyone in your party present. Overall, staff members were attentive and nice when serving us! 

I'm definitely looking forward to returning to this place and getting another bowl of udon to warm myself up this Winter!
Always delicious food, fast service and friendly staff. Great variety from a broad menu. BOGO deal is fantastic!

Nothing like hot Japanese noodles on cold evenings, right? We weren't the only ones in this mindset as we had a moderate wait (15 minutes or so) at TsuruTonTan before we were seated. But this gave me ample time to admire their Christmas tree adorned with sushi ornaments! 

Location: This udon restaurant from Japan is right by Union Square Park and across the street from Sweet Chick. There's another TsuruTonTan in Midtown. 

Seating: We were placed in a strange central section where many other parties of two were dining. You sit alongside your companion and stare through a clear wall at strangers eating across from you. A tad awkward, especially since the bench appeared bolted into place, requiring some shimmying and sliding. I envied those sitting in the wee booths. 

Food: The grilled maitake mushroom ($9) appetizer was terrific, though it featured truffle oil (not mentioned on the menu while "white ginger soy" is) which I could've done without. And the TsuruTonTan Deluxe ($25) udon, true to its name, arrived in a massive bowl topped with tempura galore, complete with a battered shiso leaf! Needless to say, I was stuffed by the conclusion of the dinner. 

Service: Carlos had a great attitude and regularly checked on us. 

Restroom: The bathroom was toasty and tucked away off to the side, hidden by a sliding door. 

Reservations: TsuruTonTan is on Resy if you'd like to make a reservation beforehand. This is recommended since the host asked about our reservation status.
Food was fantastic! The restaurant looked well decorated. The service was ok, we waited for a check for awhile but overall a good place to eat for the price.

Best udon in NY!! 

We ordered the US Wagyu Beef Truffle Dashi & the US Wagyu Beef Deluxe Sukiyaki. 

The noodles for both dishes were amazing: very long and thick, making slurping them very satisfying. & the soups for both dishes were also very delicious, but obviously very different for both. The truffle Dashi is a bit saltier than the sukiyaki and definitely has a strong truffle flavor. Meanwhile, the sukiyaki is bit sweeter than the Dashi. It felt a lot healthier though b/c it has a lot of veggies. & the US Wagyu for both dishes were immaculate. You can't go wrong with either one! 

Good ambiance too. Definitely very lively w/ good conversations all around us. Plus, HUGE portions! Would definitely go back.
